        overflow: auto;
        padding: 2px 18px 40px 4px;
        font-size: 13.5px;
        line-height: 1.62;
      }
      .docs-body h1 { font-size: 19px; margin: 4px 0 12px; }
      .docs-body h2 { font-size: 15.5px; margin: 22px 0 8px; padding-top: 6px; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); }
      .docs-body h3 { font-size: 13.5px; margin: 16px 0 6px; }
      .docs-body p { margin: 8px 0; }
      .docs-body ul, .docs-body ol { margin: 8px 0; padding-left: 22px; }
      .docs-body li { margin: 3px 0; }
      .docs-body pre {
        background: var(--console);
        color: var(--console-ink);
        padding: 10px 12px;
        border-radius: 8px;
        overflow: auto;
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 12px;
      }
      .docs-body :not(pre) > code {
        background: var(--panel-2);
        border: 1px solid var(--rule);
        padding: 0 4px;
        border-radius: 4px;
      }
      .docs-body blockquote {
        margin: 10px 0;
        padding: 2px 0 2px 12px;
        border-left: 3px solid var(--rule-strong);
        color: var(--muted);
      }
      .docs-body table { border-collapse: collapse; margin: 10px 0; font-size: 12.5px; }
      .docs-body th, .docs-body td { border: 1px solid var(--rule); padding: 5px 8px; text-align: left; }
      .docs-body th { background: var(--panel-2); }
      .docs-body .md-link { color: var(--accent); text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px; cursor: pointer; background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; }
      .docs-body .md-ext { color: var(--muted); text-decoration: underline dotted; text-underline-offset: 2px; cursor: pointer; background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; }
      .docs-body hr { border: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); margin: 18px 0; }
      
      /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ device -- */
      .card {
        border: 1px solid var(--rule);
        border-radius: var(--radius);
        background: var(--panel);
        padding: 14px 16px;
        margin-bottom: 14px;
      }
      .card h2 { font-size: 13.5px; margin-bottom: 6px; }
      /* Same box as the Build console (border, bar, dark pane), but with a height of
         its own: this pane scrolls through cards, so flex: 1 has nothing to fill. */
      .device-logwrap {
        flex: 0 0 auto;
        min-height: 0;
        height: clamp(200px, 36vh, 320px);
        margin-top: 10px;
      }
      
      /* ------------------------------------------------------------- last build -- */
      /* Folded away: the window should open on the buttons and the log, not on a
         list of what an earlier build produced. It opens itself when a build has
         just finished, and is one click away otherwise. */
      .out-fold {
        margin-top: 12px;
        border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
        padding-top: 8px;
      }
      .out-fold > summary {
        display: flex;
        align-items: baseline;
        gap: 10px;
        cursor: pointer;
        list-style: none;
        padding: 3px 0;
      }
      .out-fold > summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
      .out-fold > summary::before {
        content: "▸";
        color: var(--rule-strong);
        font-size: 10px;
        transition: transform .12s var(--ease);
      }
      .out-fold[open] > summary::before { transform: rotate(90deg); }
      .out-summary { font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--ink); }
      .out-fold .out-list { margin: 8px 0 2px 22px; }
      
      /* ----------------------------------------------------------------- config -- */
      /* One row per setting. The switch is the `#`, the value box is the right-hand
         side of the `=`, and the ⓘ is the comment block the file already had. */
      .cfg-fields { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; margin-top: 12px; padding-right: 4px; }
      .cfg-sec { margin-bottom: 18px; }
      .cfg-sec-title {
        font-size: 11px;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        letter-spacing: .08em;
        color: var(--muted);
        padding-bottom: 5px;
        border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
        margin-bottom: 8px;
      }
      .cfg-row {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: auto auto minmax(150px, max-content) minmax(0, 1fr);
        align-items: center;
        gap: 8px;
        padding: 3px 0;
      }
      .cfg-row.is-off .cfg-key,
      .cfg-row.is-off .cfg-value { color: var(--muted); }
      .cfg-row.is-dirty .cfg-key { color: var(--accent); }
      .cfg-on {
        appearance: none;
        -webkit-appearance: none;
        width: 30px;
        height: 17px;
        margin: 0;
        border-radius: 999px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        background: var(--track-base);
        position: relative;
        cursor: pointer;
        flex: none;
        transition: background .12s var(--ease), border-color .12s;
      }
      .cfg-on::after {
        content: "";
        position: absolute;
        top: 1px;
        left: 1px;
        width: 13px;
        height: 13px;
        border-radius: 50%;
        background: #fff;
        box-shadow: var(--tick);
        transition: transform .12s var(--ease);
      }
      .cfg-on:checked { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); }
      .cfg-on:checked::after { transform: translateX(13px); }
      .cfg-key {
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 12px;
        color: var(--ink);
        overflow: hidden;
        text-overflow: ellipsis;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      .cfg-value {
        width: 100%;
        padding: 5px 8px;
        border-radius: 7px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule);
        background: var(--panel);
        color: var(--ink);
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 12px;
      }
      .cfg-value:focus { border-color: var(--accent); outline: none; }
      .cfg-row.is-off .cfg-value { background: var(--panel-2); }
      .cfg-info {
        width: 20px;
        height: 20px;
        padding: 0;
        border-radius: 50%;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        background: none;
        color: var(--muted);
        font-size: 11px;
        font-style: italic;
        font-family: Georgia, serif;
        line-height: 1;
        flex: none;
      }
      .cfg-info:hover:not(:disabled) { color: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); }
      .cfg-info[aria-expanded="true"] { background: var(--accent-soft); border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
      .cfg-info:disabled { opacity: .3; }
      .cfg-info-text {
        grid-column: 2 / -1;
        margin-left: 28px;
        margin: 2px 0 8px;
        padding: 8px 10px;
        border-left: 2px solid var(--rule-strong);
        color: var(--muted);
        font-size: 12px;
        line-height: 1.5;
        white-space: pre-wrap;
      }
      
      /* ---- addons -------------------------------------------------------------- */
      /* The overlay cannot do these, so the pane says what does: each row is a
      
      [read_files: showing lines 200-599 of 1230. Use code_search to locate the part you need and read a window around it, or call read_files again with offset=600 to continue.]
      
         Settings value the module writes on the phone, with the value it would
         write. The control is small because the sentence is the point. */
      .addons-intro { max-width: 76ch; margin: 0 0 14px; }
      .addons {
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        border-radius: 8px;
        overflow: hidden;
        /* The pane is a flex column and the list is a flex item: with overflow
           hidden its automatic minimum height is 0, so in a short window it shrank
           and clipped the last rows instead of letting the pane scroll. */
        flex: none;
      }
      .addon-row {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 18px;
        padding: 12px 14px;
        border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
      }
      .addon-row:first-child { border-top: 0; }
      .addon-row.is-dirty { background: var(--accent-soft); }
      .addon-main { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
      .addon-label { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; }
      .addon-key { margin-left: 8px; font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 11px; color: var(--muted); }
      .addon-tag {
        margin-left: 8px;
        padding: 1px 7px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        border-radius: 999px;
        font-size: 10px;
        letter-spacing: .06em;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        color: var(--muted);
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      .addon-summary { margin: 4px 0 0; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--muted); }
      .addon-side { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; flex: none; }
      .addon-side select { max-width: 140px; min-width: 96px; font-family: var(--sans); }
      .addon-switch { display: inline-flex; }
      .addon-default {
        font-size: 11px;
        color: var(--muted);
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      .addon-default[hidden] { display: none; }
      .addon-state { font-size: 11px; color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; }
      .addon-state[data-diff="true"] { color: var(--accent); }
      
      /* ---- match property ------------------------------------------------------- */
      /* The card sits inside the Overlay activation section, between the rows and the
         next heading. A wrong match condition is invisible in the built module, so it
         gets more room than a normal setting. */
      .cfg-match {
        margin: 10px 0 4px;
        padding: 10px 12px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        border-radius: 8px;
        background: var(--panel-2);
      }
      .cfg-match-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
      .cfg-match-title { font-weight: 600; font-size: 12px; }
      .cfg-match-head select { margin-left: auto; max-width: 320px; min-width: 200px; }
      .cfg-match .hint { margin: 6px 0 8px; }
      .cfg-match-summary { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 6px; }
      .cfg-match-summary .muted { white-space: nowrap; }
      .cfg-match-row {
        padding: 7px 0;
        border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
      }
      .cfg-match-row-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
      .cfg-match-prop { font-size: 12px; }
      .cfg-match-eq { color: var(--muted); }
      .cfg-match-val { font-size: 12px; color: var(--accent); }
      .cfg-match-row-head button { margin-left: auto; }
      .cfg-match-badge {
        font-size: 10px;
        letter-spacing: .04em;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        padding: 1px 6px;
        border-radius: 999px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        color: var(--muted);
      }
      .cfg-match-badge.trust-high { border-color: var(--ok); color: var(--ok); }
      .cfg-match-badge.trust-medium { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
      .cfg-match-badge.trust-low { opacity: .8; }
      .cfg-match-why { margin: 4px 0 0; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); line-height: 1.45; }
      .cfg-match-risk { margin: 3px 0 0; font-size: 12px; color: var(--warn); line-height: 1.45; }
      .cfg-match-rejected { margin: 4px 0; font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); }
      .cfg-match-error { margin: 0 0 6px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--bad); }
      .cfg-match-warn {
        margin: 0 0 8px;
        padding: 7px 9px;
        font-size: 12px;
        line-height: 1.45;
        border-left: 2px solid var(--warn);
        color: var(--warn);
      }
      .cfg-match details { margin-top: 6px; }
      .cfg-match summary { cursor: pointer; }
      @keyframes cfg-flash {
        from { background: var(--accent-soft); }
        to { background: transparent; }
      }
      .cfg-row.is-flash { animation: cfg-flash 1.4s var(--ease); border-radius: 4px; }
      
      /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ device -- */
      .adb-form { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 10px; }
      .adb-form input {
        flex: 1;
        min-width: 0;
        padding: 7px 10px;
        border-radius: 8px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        background: var(--panel-2);
        color: var(--ink);
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 12.5px;
      }
      .adb-values { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-end; gap: 10px; }
      .adb-values label {
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        gap: 4px;
        font-size: 11px;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        letter-spacing: .07em;
        color: var(--muted);
      }
      .adb-values input {
        padding: 6px 9px;
        border-radius: 7px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        background: var(--panel-2);
        color: var(--ink);
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 12px;
        width: 150px;
      }
      /* The device picker: the same field as the inputs above, wide enough for a
         serial, repeated on the tabs that probe a phone. */
      .adb-values select,
      .device-pick select,
      .cfg-match-head select,
      .addon-side select {
        padding: 6px 9px;
        border-radius: 7px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        background: var(--panel-2);
        color: var(--ink);
        font-size: 12px;
        max-width: 320px;
      }
      .adb-values select { font-family: var(--mono); }
      .device-row { margin: 10px 0 4px; }
      .device-row > button { align-self: flex-end; }
      .device-pick {
        display: inline-flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 6px;
        margin-left: 10px;
        font-size: 11px;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        letter-spacing: .07em;
        color: var(--muted);
      }
      
      /* The answer Detect gave, with its caret over the codename box it filled. */
      .detect-note {
        position: relative;
        margin: 12px 0 0;
        max-width: 440px;
        padding: 7px 10px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        border-radius: 8px;
        background: var(--panel-2);
        font-size: 12px;
        line-height: 1.45;
      }
      .detect-note::before {
        content: "";
        position: absolute;
        top: -6px;
        left: 18px;
        width: 10px;
        height: 10px;
        background: var(--panel-2);
        border-left: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        border-top: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        transform: rotate(45deg);
      }
      .detect-note p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); }
      .detect-note code { color: var(--ink); }
      /* Drawn as a button, not as a link: it is the way out of a wrong answer, and
         the thing it sits next to (the codename) is a field, not prose. */
      .detect-note .link {
        display: inline-block;
        margin-top: 6px;
        padding: 3px 9px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        border-radius: 6px;
        background: var(--panel);
        color: var(--ink);
        font-size: 11.5px;
        font-weight: 600;
        text-decoration: none;
      }
      .detect-note .link:hover { background: var(--accent-soft); border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
      .presets { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }
      .preset-group { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 5px; }
      .preset-group h3 {
        font-size: 11px;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        letter-spacing: .08em;
        color: var(--muted);
        margin: 2px 0 1px;
      }
      .preset {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: minmax(170px, 260px) minmax(0, 1fr);
        gap: 10px;
        align-items: baseline;
        text-align: left;
        padding: 6px 10px;
        border-radius: 8px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule);
        background: var(--panel-2);
      }
      .preset:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); }
      .preset code { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--ink); }
      .preset .why { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--muted); line-height: 1.35; }
      .preset .advice { color: var(--warn); font-size: 11px; margin-top: 2px; display: block; }
      
      /* Output of a preset, directly under the command that produced it: the answer
         is read where the question was clicked, not at the top of the pane. The rule
         on the left ties the panel to the button above it. */
      .preset-out {
        margin: -3px 0 6px 10px;
        padding: 2px 0 0 10px;
        border-left: 2px solid var(--rule-strong);
        animation: preset-out-in .16s var(--ease);
      }
      .preset-out-bar {
        display: flex;
        justify-content: flex-start;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 8px;
        padding: 0 0 6px;
      }
      /* Real buttons, not links: Copy is the one worth reaching for, so it wears the
         accent. The base button rule already supplies border, radius and hover. */
      .preset-out-bar button { padding: 4px 12px; font-size: 11.5px; }
      .preset-log {
        margin: 0;
        max-height: 220px;
        overflow: auto;
        padding: 0;
        background: none;
        color: var(--ink);
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 12.5px;
        font-weight: 650;
        line-height: 1.5;
        white-space: pre-wrap;
        word-break: break-word;
      }
      @keyframes preset-out-in {
        from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-4px); }
        to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
      }
      
      .adb-form kbd,
      .hint kbd {
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 11px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule);
        border-bottom-width: 2px;
        border-radius: 4px;
        padding: 0 4px;
        background: var(--panel-2);
      }
      
      /* ------------------------------------------------------------------- files -- */
      /* Two panes, like the Docs tab: the tree is the clone's src/ (what the build
         reads), the right side is whatever file is open. Disabled files stay in place
         in the tree, greyed, because their location is the thing worth knowing. */
      .files { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: flex; gap: 16px; }
      .files-side { width: 330px; flex: none; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; min-height: 0; }
      .files-tools { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; }
      .files-tools button { padding: 6px 10px; font-size: 12px; }
      .files-target {
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 11.5px;
        color: var(--muted);
        overflow: hidden;
        text-overflow: ellipsis;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      .files-target code { color: var(--ink); }
      .files-quick { display: flex; gap: 6px; }
      .files-quick button { flex: 1; padding: 5px 8px; font-size: 11.5px; border-radius: 7px; color: var(--muted); }
      .files-quick button:hover { color: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); }
      .files-tree {
        flex: 1;
        min-height: 160px;
        overflow: auto;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule);
        border-radius: var(--radius);
        background: var(--panel);
        padding: 4px 0;
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 12px;
      }
      .files-tree.is-drop { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); }
      .files-tree:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; }
      .ft-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 2px 8px 2px 6px; transition: background .12s var(--ease), box-shadow .12s var(--ease); }
      .ft-row:hover { background: var(--panel-2); }
      .ft-row.is-target { background: var(--accent-soft); box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--accent); }
      .ft-row.is-selected { background: var(--accent-soft); }
      .ft-row.is-selected .ft-label { color: var(--accent); font-weight: 600; }
      .ft-row.is-off .ft-label { color: var(--muted); font-style: italic; }
      .ft-main {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 5px;
        flex: 1;
        min-width: 0;
        padding: 1px 0;
        background: none;
        border: 0;
        border-radius: 5px;
        text-align: left;
        font: inherit;
        color: inherit;
      }
      .ft-main:hover:not(:disabled) { background: none; }
      .ft-caret { width: 9px; flex: none; color: var(--rule-strong); font-size: 9px; }
      button.ft-caret {
        width: 14px;
        padding: 0;
        border: 0;
        background: none;
        color: var(--rule-strong);
        font-size: 9px;
        line-height: 1;
        flex: none;
      }
      button.ft-caret:hover:not(:disabled) { background: none; color: var(--accent); }
      .ft-icon { width: 11px; flex: none; color: var(--faint); font-size: 10px; text-align: center; }
      .ft-label { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
      .ft-meta { font-size: 10.5px; color: var(--faint); flex: none; }
      .ft-off {
        padding: 0 5px;
        font-size: 10px;
        line-height: 15px;
        border-radius: 4px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        background: none;
        color: var(--muted);
      }
      .ft-off:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); }
      .ft-badge {
        flex: none;
        font-family: var(--sans);
        font-size: 8.5px;
        line-height: 13px;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        letter-spacing: .06em;
        color: var(--muted);
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        border-radius: 999px;
        padding: 0 5px;
      }
      .ft-empty { padding: 10px; color: var(--muted); font-family: var(--sans); font-size: 12px; }
      
      .files-main { flex: 1; min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; }
      .files-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
      .files-head .spacer { flex: 1; }
      .file-path {
        font-size: 12px;
        color: var(--ink);
        background: var(--panel-2);
        border: 1px solid var(--rule);
        border-radius: 6px;
        padding: 3px 7px;
        max-width: 56ch;
        overflow: hidden;
        text-overflow: ellipsis;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      #file-editor {
        flex: 1;
        min-height: 240px;
        padding: 12px 14px;
        border-radius: var(--radius);
        border: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
        background: var(--console);
        color: var(--console-ink);
        font-family: var(--mono);
        font-size: 12.5px;

> _Reasoning_
> Now I have full picture of app.css. There is already a motion section. The user wants the app "FULL OF ANIMATIONS". Scope decision: add a richer animation layer across the desktop GUI — entrance animations for panes/cards/rows, animated tab underline, button press/press ripple, chip pulse, log line fade-in, progress shimmer, switch knob spring, config row flash, dialog pop, toast/status slide, expand/collapse for details, tree row stagger, docs content fade, and a "running" pulse on active build. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

      'use strict';
      
      /* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
         The window is a thin client over the handlers in server.go. Everything it
         can do is one of build.sh's verbs, so there is no build logic here: it picks
         a verb, ticks flags, and renders what the child prints.
      
         Three panes talk to the phone or edit files — config.env, adb and the src/
         workspace — and all of them go through the server, which owns the parsing,
         the path rules and every write. Nothing here touches the disk directly.
         --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
      
      function el(tag, cls, text) {
        const node = document.createElement(tag);
        if (cls) node.className = cls;
        if (text !== undefined) node.textContent = text;
        return node;
      }
      
      const FLAG_HELP = {
        '--with-vendor-hals': 'include src/vendor/ in the module',
        '--allow-unknown-resources': 'build even if a resource is missing',
        '--force': 're-pick the resource dictionary',
        '--all': 'also remove config and device files',
      };

      let checkedFlags = new Set();
      let running = false;      // the build console
      let adbRunning = false;  // the device console, which has its own stream

      let adbSeq = 0;

      // adb console each draw their own in place.

      // Where the current adb run writes: the <pre> under the preset that started it,
      // or null for the console at the top of the pane.

      // preset id -> the panel under that command, kept across the re-render every
      // finished run triggers so the answer stays where the question was clicked.
      const presetOut = new Map();
      let currentDoc = null;
      let statusTimer = null;
      let refreshInFlight = false;
      
      // A run that stopped for a sudo password keeps its verb here, so the retry is
      // exactly the same command. sudoPassword is the answer; it stays in this
      // window's memory for the session and is never written by the page.
      let pendingRun = null;
      let sudoPassword = '';
      let sudoPromptOpen = false;
      let sudoDeclined = false;
      
      // config.env: the form keeps only what the user changed, so a poll that lands
      // mid-edit cannot repaint the row they are typing in.
      let cfgEdits = new Map();
      let cfgRaw = false;
      let cfgRawDirty = false;
      
      // --------------------------------------------------------------------- api --
      async function api(path, opts = {}) {
        const init = { method: opts.method || 'GET', cache: 'no-store' };
        if (opts.form !== undefined) {
          // Multipart upload: the browser owns the Content-Type boundary, so no
          // header is set here.
          init.body = opts.form;
        } else if (opts.body !== undefined) {
          init.headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
          init.body = JSON.stringify(opts.body);
        }
        const res = await fetch(path, init);
        const text = await res.text();
        let data = null;
        if (text) {
          try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch (_) { data = null; }
        }
        if (!res.ok) {
          const err = new Error((data && data.error) || text || res.statusText);
          // Some failures come with useful detail (the update clash list), so keep
          // the whole payload on the error instead of only the message.
          err.data = data;
          err.status = res.status;
          throw err;
        }
        return data;
      }
      
      function status(message, ms = 3500) {
        $('run-status').textContent = message;
        if (statusTimer) clearTimeout(statusTimer);
        if (ms) statusTimer = setTimeout(() => { $('run-status').textContent = ''; }, ms);
      }
      
      // ------------------------------------------------------------------- state --

        if (refreshInFlight) return;
        refreshInFlight = true;
        try {

          $('sub').textContent = 'cannot reach the app server: ' + err.message;
          refreshInFlight = false;

        renderVerbs();
        renderFlags();
        renderOut();
        renderConfig(forceRender);

        renderDocsNav();
        renderRunState();
      }

      function switchTab(name) {
        for (const t of document.querySelectorAll('.tab')) {

      function renderVerbs() {
        const box = $('verbs');
        box.textContent = '';
        for (const v of state.verbs) {
          const b = document.createElement('button');
          b.type = 'button';
          b.className = 'verb' + (v.name === selectedVerb ? ' is-active' : '');
          const h = document.createElement('h3');
          h.textContent = v.label;
          const p = document.createElement('p');
          p.textContent = v.hint;
          b.append(h, p);
          b.addEventListener('click', () => {
            selectedVerb = v.name;
            renderVerbs();
            renderFlags();
            renderRunState();
          });
          box.appendChild(b);
        }
      }
      
      function renderFlags() {
        const v = currentVerb();
        const box = $('flags');
        box.textContent = '';
      
        if (!v || !v.flags || v.flags.length === 0) {
          box.appendChild(el('span', 'muted', 'none for this command'));
          return;
        }
      
        for (const flag of v.flags) {
          const label = el('label', 'flag');
          label.title = FLAG_HELP[flag] || '';
      
          const input = document.createElement('input');
          input.type = 'checkbox';
          input.checked = checkedFlags.has(flag);
          input.addEventListener('change', () => {
            if (input.checked) checkedFlags.add(flag);
            else checkedFlags.delete(flag);
            renderRunState();
          });
      
          label.append(input, el('span', 'flag-name', flag));
          box.appendChild(label);
        }
      }
      
      function renderRunState() {
        const v = currentVerb();
        const ready = state && state.cloneValid && state.bashValid;
      
        // The two consoles keep separate streams and separate buffers, but they share
        // one job slot on the server: both write into the same clone, so a pull and a
        // build must never overlap.
        $('run').disabled = !ready || running || adbRunning || !v;
        $('stop').disabled = !running;
        $('run').textContent = v ? `Run ${v.label.toLowerCase()}` : 'Run';
      
        const flags = v ? [...checkedFlags].filter((f) => v.flags && v.flags.includes(f)) : [];
        const cmd = v ? `build.sh ${v.arg}${flags.length ? ' ' + flags.join(' ') : ''} -y` : '';
        $('run').title = v ? `runs: bash --noprofile --norc ./${cmd}` : '';
      
        for (const input of $('flags').querySelectorAll('input')) input.disabled = running;
        for (const b of $('verbs').querySelectorAll('.verb')) b.disabled = running;
        $('adb-run').disabled = running || adbRunning || !adbReady();
        $('adb-run').title = running ? 'a build is running — one job at a time' : '';
        $('adb-stop').disabled = !adbRunning;
      
        // One job at a time: a second preset clicked mid-run would be refused by the
        // server, and the panel under the command still running would end up with the
        // refusal in it. Blocked-for-needs is remembered by renderPresets, which is
        // what reads the codename and the adb install state.
        for (const b of $('adb-presets').querySelectorAll('button.preset')) {
          if (running || adbRunning) b.disabled = true;
          else b.disabled = b.dataset.blocked === '1';
        }
      }
      
      // -------------------------------------------------------------- last build --
      // The list of what out/ holds is only interesting right after a build, so it
      // sits folded at the bottom of the pane. renderOut keeps the summary line
      // current either way, and a finished build opens it once.
      function renderOut() {
        const box = $('out');
        const summary = $('out-summary');
        box.textContent = '';
      
        const files = state.out || [];
        if (files.length === 0) {
          summary.textContent = state.cloneValid ? 'nothing in out/ yet' : 'no clone selected';
          box.appendChild(el('span', 'muted', summary.textContent));
          return;
        }
      
        let newest = 0;
        let biggest = 0;
        for (const f of files) {
          if (f.mod > newest) newest = f.mod;
          if (f.size > biggest) biggest = f.size;
        }
        const when = ago(newest);
        summary.textContent = `${when} · ${files.length} file${files.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
        summary.title = 'built ' + new Date(newest * 1000).toLocaleString();
      
        for (const f of files) {
          const row = el('div', 'out-item');
          row.append(el('span', null, f.name), el('span', null, `${bytes(f.size)} · ${ago(f.mod)}`));
          box.appendChild(row);
        }
      }
      
      function bytes(n) {
        if (n > 1 << 20) return (n / (1 << 20)).toFixed(1) + ' MB';
        if (n > 1 << 10) return (n / (1 << 10)).toFixed(0) + ' kB';
        return n + ' B';
      }
      
      function ago(unixSeconds) {
        const s = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000 - unixSeconds));
        if (s < 60) return 'just now';
        if (s < 3600) return Math.floor(s / 60) + ' min ago';
        if (s < 86400) return Math.floor(s / 3600) + ' h ago';
        return Math.floor(s / 86400) + ' d ago';
      }

      // --------------------------------------------------------------------- log --
      function connectLog() {
        const stream = new EventSource('api/log');
      
        stream.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
          let line;
          try { line = JSON.parse(event.data); } catch (_) { return; }
          // seq restarts at 1 on every run, and the server replays its buffer to a
          // reconnecting client: either way a slow seq means "new run, start over".
          if (line.seq <= lastSeq) {
            clearLog();
            lastSeq = 0;
          }
          lastSeq = line.seq;
          // The server's own line asking for a password: not something to print, an
          // action to take. The sentence before it already explained why.
          if (line.stream === 'sudo') {
            openSudoPrompt();
            return;
          }
          appendLine(line);
        });
      
        stream.addEventListener('error', () => {
          // EventSource retries on its own; the replay would duplicate, which the
          // seq check above handles.
        });
      }
      
      function renderLogLine(pre, line) {
        const stick = pre.scrollTop + pre.clientHeight >= pre.scrollHeight - 30;
      
        if (line.stream === 'progress') {
          // pacman and adb pull repaint one line with \r. Rewrite that line instead
          // of appending a row per chunk, so a download reads like a terminal.
          let live = progressNode.get(pre);
          if (!live || live.parentNode !== pre) {
            live = document.createElement('span');
            live.className = 'progress';
            pre.appendChild(live);
            progressNode.set(pre, live);
          }
          live.textContent = line.text + '\n';
          if (stick) pre.scrollTop = pre.scrollHeight;
          return false;
        }
        // Any real line ends the bar's run: the next repaint starts a new line.
        progressNode.delete(pre);
      
        const node = document.createElement('span');
      
        if (line.stream === 'done') {
          node.className = /finished/.test(line.text) ? 'done-ok' : 'done-bad';
          node.textContent = '— ' + line.text + ' —\n';
          pre.appendChild(node);
          if (stick) pre.scrollTop = pre.scrollHeight;
          return true;
        }
        if (line.stream === 'note') {
          node.className = 'note';
          node.textContent = '· ' + line.text + '\n';
        } else if (line.stream === 'err') {
          node.className = 'err';
          node.innerHTML = ansiToHtml(line.text) + '\n';
        } else {
          node.innerHTML = ansiToHtml(line.text) + '\n';
        }
        pre.appendChild(node);
        if (stick) pre.scrollTop = pre.scrollHeight;
        return false;
      }

      .udfps-conf.high { color: var(--ok); }
      .udfps-conf.medium { color: var(--warn); }
      .udfps-conf.guess, .udfps-conf.low { color: var(--bad); }
      .udfps-notes p { margin: 8px 0 0; font-size: 12px; }
      .udfps-notes p.warn { color: var(--warn); }
      .udfps-files { padding: 4px 0 2px; }
      .udfps-file { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1px; padding: 5px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); }
      .udfps-file code { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 12px; word-break: break-all; }
      #udfps-log { margin-top: 10px; max-height: 220px; }
      
      @media (max-width: 760px) {
        .docs { flex-direction: column; }
        .docs-nav { width: auto; flex-direction: row; flex-wrap: wrap; overflow: visible; }
        .files { flex-direction: column; }
        .files-side { width: auto; }
        .files-tree { min-height: 120px; max-height: 32vh; }
        .chips { display: none; }
        #sub { max-width: 70vw; }
      }
      
      /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ motion -- */
      /* Short, one-shot, and made of opacity plus a couple of pixels: enough to show
         that something changed, never enough to watch. Nothing loops and nothing
         bounces — the tabs, dialogs and answer cards are used dozens of times a
         session, and a flourish is a tax on every one of them. */
      @keyframes pane-in {
        from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(2px); }
        to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
      }
      .pane.is-active { animation: pane-in .13s var(--ease); }
      
      @keyframes dialog-in {
        from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-3px) scale(.995); }
        to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
      }
      dialog[open] { animation: dialog-in .15s var(--ease); }
      @keyframes backdrop-in { from { opacity: 0; } }
      dialog[open]::backdrop { animation: backdrop-in .15s ease-out; }
      
      /* The answer cards are unhidden when a scan starts, so the fade is the
         acknowledgement that the click landed. The power profile is the same. */
      @keyframes card-in {
        from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(3px); }
        to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
      }
      #udfps-results:not([hidden]),
      #detect-results:not([hidden]),
      #power-preview:not([hidden]) { animation: card-in .15s var(--ease); }
      
      /* A folder dragged over the tree: the border is the target, and it should not
         snap between states while the pointer crosses it. */
      .files-tree { transition: border-color .12s var(--ease), background .12s var(--ease); }
      
      /* The one-line status next to Run appears and clears on its own; an instant
         swap draws the eye to the corner it is in. */
      #run-status { transition: opacity .15s var(--ease); }
      #run-status:empty { opacity: 0; }
      
      /* One switch for the people the animations cost something: the app has no
         animation that carries information, so none of them has to survive this. */
      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
        *, *::before, *::after {
          animation-duration: .001ms !important;
          animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
          transition-duration: .001ms !important;
        }
      }

The one loop\n   is the \"a job is running\" ring on the console, which is information, not\n   decoration. `prefers-reduced-motion` at the end of this file turns all of it\n   off in one switch. */\n@keyframes pane-in {\n  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(7px); }\n  to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }\n}\n@keyframes fade-up {\n  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(7px); }\n  to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }\n}\n@keyframes fade-down {\n  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-7px); }\n  to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }\n}\n@keyframes slide-in {\n  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(-9px); }\n  to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }\n}\n@keyframes pop-in {\n  from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(.94); }\n  to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }\n}\n@keyframes line-in {\n  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-3px); }\n  to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }\n}\n@keyframes dot-beat {\n  0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 1; }\n  50% { transform: scale(1.3); opacity: .55; }\n}\n@keyframes live-ring {\n  0%, 100% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 var(--accent-soft); }\n  50% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-soft); }\n}\n\n/* Every pane fades up as a block, then its own children follow a beat later:\n   the eye lands on the tab first, then on what the tab holds.       "newString": "/* A dialog comes in slightly small and settles with a little overshoot: the\n   card the settings, the new file and the delete question all get. */\n@keyframes dialog-in {\n  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-10px) scale(.96); }\n  to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }\n}\ndialog[open] { animation: dialog-in .24s cubic-bezier(.2, 1.25, .35, 1) backwards; }\n@keyframes backdrop-in { from { opacity: 0; backdrop-filter: blur(0); } }\ndialog[open]::backdrop { animation: backdrop-in .22s ease-out; }\ndialog[open] h2 { animation: fade-down .24s var(--ease) .04s backwards; }\ndialog[open] label,\ndialog[open] input,\ndialog[open] select,\ndialog[open] menu { animation: fade-up .24s var(--ease) .06s backwards; }\n\n/* ------------------------------------------------------------------- tabs -- */\n/* The active underline is a bar that grows out of the middle instead of a\n   border that snaps on, and hovering a tab previews it at half width. */\n.tab { position: relative; }\n.tab::after {\n  content: \"\";\n  position: absolute;\n  left: 8px;\n  right: 8px;\n  bottom: -1px;\n  height: 2px;\n  border-radius: 2px;\n  background: var(--rule-strong);\n  transform: scaleX(0);\n  transform-origin: 50% 100%;\n  opacity: 0;\n  transition: transform .22s var(--ease), opacity .22s var(--ease), background-color .22s var(--ease);\n}\n.tab:hover:not(:disabled)::after { transform: scaleX(.5); opacity: .55; }\n.tab.is-active::after { transform: scaleX(1); opacity: 1; background: var(--accent); }\n/* The base rule draws the same line as a border; the bar above is the one that\n   moves, so the static border steps aside. */\n.tab.is-active { border-bottom-color: transparent; }\n\n/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- controls -- */\n/* Buttons lift a hair under the pointer and sink when pressed. The primary one\n   also gets a light sweep, which is the only place the accent reads as moving\n   without anything having happened yet. */\n@keyframes sweep {\n  from { transform: translateX(-130%); }\n  to { transform: translateX(130%); }\n}\nbutton.primary { position: relative; overflow: hidden; }\nbutton.primary::after {\n  content: \"\";\n  position: absolute;\n  top: -40%;\n  bottom: -40%;\n  left: 0;\n  width: 45%;\n  background: linear-gradient(105deg, transparent, rgba(255, 255, 255, .34), transparent);\n  transform: translateX(-130%);\n  pointer-events: none;\n}\nbutton.primary:hover:not(:disabled)::after { animation: sweep .6s var(--ease); }\nbutton:active:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(1px) scale(.985); }\nbutton.primary:hover:not(:disabled),\n.chip:hover:not(:disabled),\n.verb:hover:not(:disabled),\n.preset:hover:not(:disabled),\n.files-tools button:hover:not(:disabled),\n.folder-actions button:hover:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(-1px); }\n.files-tools button,\n.folder-actions button,\n.files-quick button { transition: transform .14s var(--ease), background .14s var(--ease), border-color .14s var(--ease), color .14s var(--ease); }\n\n/* The verb cards are the first thing anyone clicks, so they answer the pointer\n   before the click: lift, accent edge, and a bar down the left when chosen. */\n.verb { transition: border-color .16s var(--ease), background .16s var(--ease), color .16s var(--ease), transform .16s var(--ease), box-shadow .16s var(--ease); }\n.verb:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--rule-strong); box-shadow: 0 10px 22px -20px rgba(23, 24, 15, .7); }\n.verb.is-active { box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--accent), var(--shadow); }\n.preset { transition: border-color .16s var(--ease), background .16s var(--ease), transform .16s var(--ease); }\n\n/* A chip's dot beats when it has something to say: a dirty tree or a path that\n   will not work. The healthy state stays still. */\n.chip .dot { transition: transform .2s var(--ease); }\n.chip[data-tone=\"warn\"] .dot { animation: dot-beat 1.9s ease-in-out infinite; }\n.chip[data-tone=\"bad\"] .dot { animation: dot-beat 1.3s ease-in-out infinite; }\n\n/* The config switch knob runs past its stop and settles, so flipping it feels\n   like a switch instead of a checkbox with a round mark. */\n.cfg-on::after { transition: transform .2s cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1); }\n.cfg-on:active::after { width: 16px; }\n.cfg-on:checked:active::after { transform: translateX(10px); }\n.cfg-value { transition: border-color .14s var(--ease), box-shadow .14s var(--ease), background .14s var(--ease); }\n.cfg-value:focus { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-soft); }\n.cfg-row { transition: background .14s var(--ease); border-radius: 4px; }\n.cfg-row:hover { background: var(--panel-2); }\n.cfg-row.is-off:hover { background: transparent; }\n",

         before the click: lift, accent edge, and a bar down the left when chosen. */
      .verb { transition: border-color .16s var(--ease), background .16s var(--ease), color .16s var(--ease), transform .16s var(--ease), box-shadow .16s var(--ease); }
      .verb:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--rule-strong); box-shadow: 0 10px 22px -20px rgba(23, 24, 15, .7); }
      .verb.is-active { box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--accent), var(--shadow); }
      .preset { transition: border-color .16s var(--ease), background .16s var(--ease), transform .16s var(--ease); }
      
      /* A chip's dot beats when it has something to say: a dirty tree or a path that
         will not work. The healthy state stays still. */
      .chip .dot { transition: transform .2s var(--ease); }
      .chip[data-tone="warn"] .dot { animation: dot-beat 1.9s ease-in-out infinite; }
      .chip[data-tone="bad"] .dot { animation: dot-beat 1.3s ease-in-out infinite; }
      
      /* The config switch knob runs past its stop and settles, so flipping it feels
         like a switch instead of a checkbox with a round mark. */
      .cfg-on::after { transition: transform .2s cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1); }
      .cfg-on:active::after { width: 16px; }
      .cfg-on:checked:active::after { transform: translateX(10px); }
      .cfg-value { transition: border-color .14s var(--ease), box-shadow .14s var(--ease), background .14s var(--ease); }
      .cfg-value:focus { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-soft); }
      .cfg-row { transition: background .14s var(--ease); border-radius: 4px; }
      .cfg-row:hover { background: var(--panel-2); }
      .cfg-row.is-off:hover { background: transparent; }
      
      /* The answer cards are unhidden when a scan starts, so the fade is the

      @keyframes card-in {

      #udfps-results:not([hidden]),

The window app now has a full motion layer: `gui/ui/app.css` grew from a 5-rule `motion` section into ~250 lines covering the whole UI, and `gui/ui/app.js` gained one line to drive the "job running" state.

**What moves now**

- **Boot / tabs** — header drops in, logo pops, chips cascade, then each pane fades up and its own children follow 30–150ms apart. The active tab underline is a bar that grows out of the middle; hover previews it at half width.
- **Controls** — buttons lift and sink, primary buttons get a light sweep on hover, chips lift, the update/path dots beat when they're in warn/bad tone, and the config switch knob overshoots and settles like a real switch.
- **Build console** — every new line drops in (140ms), finished lines flash their `— done —` marker, and while a build runs the whole console breathes an accent ring so a quiet minute doesn't read as hung.
- **Answers** — UDFPS/Detect tables slide in row-by-row, ticked boxes scale, picked rows get an accent bar, the results cards and the "which property answered" note pop in.
- **Docs / folds / files** — docs paragraphs cascade on every doc switch, opening "Last build" or "What was read" unfolds its content, the file editor and folder view fade in, tree rows nudge sideways on hover, and the tree pulses while you drag a folder over it.
- **Dialogs and status lines** — dialogs come in small and settle with a little overshoot, and the one-line statuses (`#run-status`, `#cfg-status`, …) slide in when they have something to say.

Everything animates only opacity/transform/box-shadow, all one-shot except the two intentional loops (chip dot while dirty, running console). `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` still kills the whole layer in one switch, and now also clears delays so staggered lists don't wait to appear.

**Checks run:** CSS brace balance and a scan for undefined/duplicate `@keyframes` (0 problems, 16 keyframes), `node --check gui/ui/app.js`, and `node --test stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js` (6/6 pass). ```
// ------------------------------------------------------------------ dialog --
// A dialog grows out of the control that opened it and travels to the middle
// of the window. Only the browser knows where it will land, so the start point
// is measured after showModal: the button's centre, relative to the dialog's,
// and a scale that fits the dialog inside that button. Without a button (a
// dialog the app opens for itself) the plain centred fade in app.css is used.
function openDialog(dlg, from) {
  // Focus moves into the dialog on showModal, so the trigger is read first.
  const trigger = from || document.activeElement;
  if (dlg.open) return; // showModal() throws on an open dialog; the fields still repaint
  dlg.classList.remove('from-control');
  dlg.showModal();
  const box = trigger && trigger.getBoundingClientRect ? trigger.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
  // A body-sized or empty rect means the dialog was not opened from a control.
  if (!box || !box.width || box.width > window.innerWidth * .8) return;
  const d = dlg.getBoundingClientRect();
  const dx = (box.left + box.width / 2) - (d.left + d.width / 2);
  const dy = (box.top + box.height / 2) - (d.top + d.height / 2);
  const s = Math.min(.8, Math.max(.35, (box.width + box.height) / (d.width + d.height)));
  dlg.style.setProperty('--from-x', Math.round(dx) + 'px');
  dlg.style.setProperty('--from-y', Math.round(dy) + 'px');
  dlg.style.setProperty('--from-s', s.toFixed(3));
  dlg.classList.add('from-control');
}

function openSettings() {
  $('set-clone').value = state ? state.clone : '';
  $('set-bash').value = state ? state.bash : '';
  $('set-error').hidden = true;
  openDialog($('settings'));
}

```

Dialogs now fly out of the button you clicked.

**How it works**

- `openDialog(dlg, from)` in `gui/ui/app.js` replaces the direct `showModal()` calls for the four click-driven dialogs: **Check for updates**, **Path** (settings), **New file/folder**, and the delete/clear confirmation. It reads the trigger (the passing `from`, else the focused element — read *before* `showModal()`, since focus moves into the dialog) and skips the effect when there's no real button behind the open.
- After the dialog is in the top layer it measures both rects and stores three CSS variables: `--from-x` / `--from-y` (the vector from the dialog's centre to the button's centre) and `--from-s` (a start scale of 35–80% based on how big the button is relative to the dialog).
- `@keyframes dialog-fly` in `app.css` starts the dialog at that offset and scale, faded out, and lands it at centre at full size over 380ms with an expo-out curve, while the backdrop still fades in over 220ms. The existing head/label/menu stagger plays during the flight.
- Anything opened without a control (the settings dialog on first run, the sudo password prompt that arrives from the build stream) keeps the plain centred pop-in — the body-sized rect check falls through rather than flying in from a corner. `showModal()` is also guarded against an already-open dialog now.

**Checks:** `node --check gui/ui/app.js`, CSS brace balance, and `node --test stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js` (6/6 pass). Not visually confirmed — the window isn't running here, so the fly-in timing and the `--from-s` range are the things to judge on screen; the chip is near the top-right, so the default update dialog will travel a long diagonal, which is the best case to test.

      // ------------------------------------------------------------------ delete --
      // Deleting is the one action here that cannot be undone, so it always goes
      // through the dialog. The destructive button is on the left, Cancel is on the
      // right and is the highlighted one (and the one focused when the dialog opens).
      function askConfirm(title, text, yes = 'Delete') {
        return new Promise((resolve) => {
          confirmAnswer = resolve;
          $('confirm-title').textContent = title;
          $('confirm-text').textContent = text;
          $('confirm-yes').textContent = yes;
          openDialog($('confirm'));
          $('confirm-no').focus();
        });
      }
      
      function resolveConfirm(answer) {
        const resolve = confirmAnswer;
        confirmAnswer = null;
        if ($('confirm').open) $('confirm').close();
        if (resolve) resolve(answer);
      }
      
      // ------------------------------------------------------------------- sudo --
      // toolchain.sh says it could install the tools if something could ask for a
      // password; the server turns that into this dialog. The password is posted with
      // the retry and handed to sudo -A for that run only.
      function openSudoPrompt() {
        if (!pendingRun || sudoPromptOpen || sudoDeclined) return;
        sudoPromptOpen = true;
        $('sudo-error').hidden = true;
        if (sudoPassword) {
          $('sudo-error').textContent = 'sudo could not install with the last password — try again.';
          $('sudo-error').hidden = false;
        }
        $('sudo-password').value = '';
        $('sudo').showModal();
        $('sudo-password').focus();
      }
      
      async function submitSudo(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
        const password = $('sudo-password').value;
        if (!password) {
          $('sudo-error').textContent = 'enter the password sudo would ask for';
          $('sudo-error').hidden = false;
          return;
        }
        sudoPassword = password;
        $('sudo').close();
        if (pendingRun) await startRun(pendingRun);
      }
      
      function cancelSudo() {
        sudoDeclined = true;
        $('sudo').close();
        status('install skipped — the build tools are still missing', 6000);

      // ------------------------------------------------------------------ dialog --
      // A dialog grows out of the control that opened it and travels to the middle
      // of the window. Only the browser knows where it will land, so the start point
      // is measured after showModal: the button's centre, relative to the dialog's,
      // and a scale that fits the dialog inside that button. Without a button (a
      // dialog the app opens for itself) the plain centred fade in app.css is used.
      function openDialog(dlg, from) {
        // Focus moves into the dialog on showModal, so the trigger is read first.
        const trigger = from || document.activeElement;
        if (dlg.open) return; // showModal() throws on an open dialog; the fields still repaint
        dlg.classList.remove('from-control');
        dlg.showModal();
        const box = trigger && trigger.getBoundingClientRect ? trigger.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
        // A body-sized or empty rect means the dialog was not opened from a control.
        if (!box || !box.width || box.width > window.innerWidth * .8) return;
        const d = dlg.getBoundingClientRect();
        const dx = (box.left + box.width / 2) - (d.left + d.width / 2);
        const dy = (box.top + box.height / 2) - (d.top + d.height / 2);
        const s = Math.min(.8, Math.max(.35, (box.width + box.height) / (d.width + d.height)));
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-x', Math.round(dx) + 'px');
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-y', Math.round(dy) + 'px');
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-s', s.toFixed(3));
        dlg.classList.add('from-control');
      }

      /* The header and the tab strip arrive before the pane does. */
      .top { animation: fade-down .26s var(--ease) backwards; }
      .brand .mark { animation: pop-in .3s var(--ease) .05s backwards; }
      .chips .chip { animation: fade-down .26s var(--ease) backwards; }
      .chips .chip:nth-child(1) { animation-delay: .05s; }
      .chips .chip:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: .1s; }
      .chips .chip:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: .15s; }
      .tabs { animation: fade-up .26s var(--ease) .04s backwards; }
      .mark { transition: transform .2s var(--ease), box-shadow .2s var(--ease); }
      .mark:hover { transform: rotate(-6deg) scale(1.06); box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--accent-soft); }
      
      /* A dialog comes in slightly small and settles with a little overshoot: the
         card the settings, the new file and the delete question all get. */
      @keyframes dialog-in {
        from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-10px) scale(.96); }
        to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
      }
      dialog[open] { animation: dialog-in .24s cubic-bezier(.2, 1.25, .35, 1) backwards; }
      /* Opened from a control: the dialog starts as a small card sitting on the
         button that was clicked and travels to the middle of the window. The start
         offset and scale are measured by openDialog() in app.js; the fallbacks keep
         this a centred fade when a dialog has no button behind it. */
      @keyframes dialog-fly {
        from {
          opacity: 0;
          transform: translate(var(--from-x, 0px), var(--from-y, 0px)) scale(var(--from-s, .7));
        }
        to { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
      }
      dialog[open].from-control { animation: dialog-fly .38s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) backwards; }
      @keyframes backdrop-in { from { opacity: 0; backdrop-filter: blur(0); } }
      dialog[open]::backdrop { animation: backdrop-in .22s ease-out; }
      dialog[open] h2 { animation: fade-down .24s var(--ease) .04s backwards; }
      dialog[open] label,
      dialog[open] input,
      dialog[open] select,
      dialog[open] menu { animation: fade-up .24s var(--ease) .06s backwards; }
      
      /* ------------------------------------------------------------------- tabs -- */
      /* The active underline is a bar that grows out of the middle instead of a
         border that snaps on, and hovering a tab previews it at half width. */
      .tab { position: relative; }
      .tab::after {
        content: "";
        position: absolute;
        left: 8px;
        right: 8px;
        bottom: -1px;
        height: 2px;
        border-radius: 2px;

  content: |
      // ------------------------------------------------------------------ dialog --
      // A dialog grows out of the control that opened it and travels to the middle
      // of the window. Only the browser knows where it will land, so the start point
      // is measured after showModal: the button's centre, relative to the dialog's,
      // and a scale that fits the dialog inside that button. Without a button (a
      // dialog the app opens for itself) the plain centred fade in app.css is used.
      function openDialog(dlg, from) {
        // Focus moves into the dialog on showModal, so the trigger is read first.
        const trigger = from || document.activeElement;
        // Reopened while its exit was still playing: drop the exit and start over.
        if (dlg.classList.contains('is-closing')) {
          dlg.classList.remove('is-closing', 'from-control');
          dlg.close();
        }
        if (dlg.open) return; // showModal() throws on an open dialog; the fields still repaint
        dlg.classList.remove('from-control');
        dlg.showModal();
        const box = trigger && trigger.getBoundingClientRect ? trigger.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
        // A body-sized or empty rect means the dialog was not opened from a control.
        if (!box || !box.width || box.width > window.innerWidth * .8) return;
        const d = dlg.getBoundingClientRect();
        const dx = (box.left + box.width / 2) - (d.left + d.width / 2);
        const dy = (box.top + box.height / 2) - (d.top + d.height / 2);
        const s = Math.min(.8, Math.max(.35, (box.width + box.height) / (d.width + d.height)));
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-x', Math.round(dx) + 'px');
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-y', Math.round(dy) + 'px');
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-s', s.toFixed(3));
        dlg.classList.add('from-control');
      }
      
      // Leaving: the same measured start point played backwards, so a dialog that
      // flew out of a button goes back into it. The dialog is still open while it
      // animates; closeDialog() calls the real close() once the card has left, which
      // is what the 'close' listeners that reset state wait for.
      const DIALOG_OUT_MS = 260;
      
      function closeDialog(dlg, value) {
        if (!dlg || !dlg.open || dlg.classList.contains('is-closing')) return;
      
        const finish = () => {
          dlg.removeEventListener('animationend', onEnd);
          dlg.classList.remove('is-closing', 'from-control');
          if (dlg.open) dlg.close(value);
        };
        const onEnd = (event) => {
          if (event.target === dlg) finish();
        };
      
        // With motion turned down there is nothing to wait for, and a window that is
        // not painting animations would otherwise leave the dialog stuck open.
        if (window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
          finish();
          return;
        }
        // Closed while it was still flying in: an exit would restart from the middle
        // and jump, so this one just goes.
        const arriving = dlg.getAnimations && dlg.getAnimations().some(
          (a) => a.playState === 'running' &&
            (a.animationName === 'dialog-fly' || a.animationName === 'dialog-in')
        );
        if (arriving) {
          finish();
          return;
        }
        dlg.classList.add('is-closing');
        dlg.addEventListener('animationend', onEnd);
        setTimeout(finish, DIALOG_OUT_MS + 160); // longer than the CSS animation, as a backstop
      }
      
      function openSettings() {
        $('set-clone').value = state ? state.clone : '';
        $('set-bash').value = state ? state.bash : '';
        $('set-error').hidden = true;
        openDialog($('settings'));
      }

Both changes are in, and all dialog exits now play through one helper.

**Smoother flight in** (`gui/ui/app.css`)

- The travel is slower and decelerates properly: `.46s` on `cubic-bezier(.19, 1, .22, 1)` instead of `.38s`, so the card spends most of the move easing into the middle rather than arriving at speed and stopping.
- Opacity now reaches full at 60% instead of tracking the transform the whole way, so the last of the movement is a settle rather than a fade-and-slide together — that is the part that read as "jumpy".
- The centred fallback (`dialog-in`, used for dialogs with no button behind them) lost its overshoot: `.3s` with `cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1)` and a gentler `.97` start, so it arrives instead of bouncing.
- The backdrop fades in on the same curve and 40ms longer, so the dim and the card move as one thing.

**Animated close** (`gui/ui/app.js` + `app.css`)

- `closeDialog(dlg)` fades the card and plays the measured flight *backwards* into the button it came from (`dialog-out-fly`, 260ms, accelerating away with `forwards` fill), with the backdrop fading on its own shorter animation. `close()` is only called after the exit ends, so the existing `close` listeners still reset state at the right time.
- Every exit path uses it: Save/Later/Cancel on all four dialogs, the delete answer, sudo Cancel and Install, the "Later" button, and Esc — Esc is handled by one `cancel` listener per dialog that animates and leaves the app's own Esc meanings (confirm resolves "no", sudo counts as declined) intact.
- The two buttons that previously relied on `method="dialog"` to close natively (Settings **Cancel**, Update **Later**) are now `type="button"` with ids, so they cannot skip the animation.
- Guards: reduced motion or a hidden window closes immediately; a dialog closed while still flying in just goes (an exit would restart from the centre and jump); reopening during the exit drops the exit and opens fresh; a 420ms timer backstops a missed `animationend`.

**Checks run:** `node --check gui/ui/app.js`, CSS brace balance plus a scan for undefined/duplicate `@keyframes` (20 keyframes, 0 problems — the two new ones included), and `node --test stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js` (6/6 pass, which also confirms the two new ids are wired).

**Limitation:** the native window can't be launched here, so this is verified as valid, wired CSS/JS rather than watched. The thing to eyeball is closing the update dialog right as it lands — that's the longest flight — and Esc on the settings dialog.

      function renderConfig(force = false) {
        const raw = $('cfg');
        raw.hidden = !cfgRaw;

        $('cfg-mode').textContent = cfgRaw ? 'back to the form' : 'edit the raw file';
        $('cfg-hint').hidden = cfgRaw;
      
        if (cfgRaw) {
          if (!cfgRawDirty && !fieldsFocused()) raw.value = state.configText || '';
          raw.disabled = !state.cloneValid;
          return;
        }
      
        // Never repaint over a keystroke, and never repaint away unsaved edits: the
        // 20-second poll would otherwise undo what is being typed.
        //
        // A section shows its heading and its rows only. The paragraph the file keeps
        // under that heading is the same text the row's ⓘ opens, so printing it here
        // as well made the form read like the raw file it is meant to replace.
        if (!force && (cfgEdits.size > 0 || fieldsFocused())) return;
      
        const box = $('cfg-fields');
        box.textContent = '';
      
        // Search/filter input for config entries
        const searchInput = el('input', 'filter-input');
        searchInput.type = 'text';
        searchInput.placeholder = 'Search config entries…';
        searchInput.addEventListener('input', () => {
          const term = searchInput.value.trim().toLowerCase();
          const rows = box.querySelectorAll('.cfg-row');
          for (const row of rows) {
            const text = (row.textContent || '').toLowerCase();
            row.style.display = text.includes(term) ? '' : 'none';
          }
        });
        box.insertBefore(searchInput, box.firstChild);
      
        const doc = state.config;
        if (!state.cloneValid || !doc || !doc.sections || doc.sections.length === 0) {

            ? 'config.env is empty or missing — run Build once, or Clean --all to recreate it.'
            : 'Pick the clone first.'));
          return;
        }
      
        let matchPlaced = false;
        for (const sec of doc.sections) {
          const wrap = el('div', 'cfg-sec');
          if (sec.title) wrap.appendChild(el('div', 'cfg-sec-title', sec.title));
          const entries = sec.entries || [];
          for (const entry of entries) wrap.appendChild(cfgRow(entry));
          if (!sec.title && entries.length === 0) continue;
          // The match-property card belongs with the activation keys, because a wrong
          // one is the failure that looks like success: the overlay is enabled and
          // nothing changes.
          if (!matchPlaced && isOverlaySection(sec)) {
            wrap.appendChild(matchCard());
            matchPlaced = true;

          box.appendChild(wrap);
        }
        if (!matchPlaced) box.appendChild(matchCard());
        updateCfgStatus();
      }

      ]);
      
      function cfgRow(entry) {
        const row = el('div', 'cfg-row');
        row.dataset.line = String(entry.line);
        // A value of true/false is one bit, so it gets one control: the switch is the
        // value (on = true, off = false). The row is still dimmed while the line is
        // commented out; touching the switch uncomments it.
        const isBool = !CFG_STRING_KEYS.has(entry.key) &&
          (entry.value === 'true' || entry.value === 'false');
        row.classList.toggle('is-off', !entry.enabled);
      
        const on = document.createElement('input');
        on.type = 'checkbox';
        on.className = 'cfg-on';
        on.checked = isBool ? entry.value === 'true' : entry.enabled;
        on.title = isBool
          ? (on.checked ? 'true — click to write false' : 'false — click to write true')
          : (entry.enabled ? 'on — click to comment this line out' : 'off — click to enable');
      
        const key = el('code', 'cfg-key', entry.key);
        key.title = entry.key;
      
        // A boolean needs no text field: `true` and `false` are the switch.
        const field = isBool ? null : document.createElement('input');
        if (field) {
          field.className = 'cfg-value';
          field.value = entry.value;
          field.spellcheck = false;
          field.autocomplete = 'off';
          field.setAttribute('aria-label', entry.key);

        const info = el('button', 'cfg-info', 'i');

        info.disabled = comment.length === 0;
        info.title = comment.length ? 'What this setting does' : 'the file has no note for this one';
      
        const note = el('p', 'cfg-info-text', comment.join('\n'));
        note.hidden = true;
      
        const sync = () => {

      // being replaced has to be captured first — replacing matchBodyEl with itself
      // after that is a no-op and the answer never reaches the screen.
      function refreshMatchBody() {

        if (!old || !old.isConnected) return;
        old.replaceWith(matchBody());
      }
      
      function trustLabel(trust) {
        if (trust === 'high') return 'fits';
        if (trust === 'medium') return 'partial';
        return 'risky';
      }
      
      function confidenceLabel(confidence) {
        if (confidence === 'high') return 'safe pick';
        if (confidence === 'medium') return 'no perfect pick';
        return 'nothing usable';
      }
      
      function matchBody() {
        const body = el('div', 'cfg-match-body');
        matchBodyEl = body;
      
        if (matchBusy) {
          body.appendChild(el('p', 'muted small', 'asking the phone…'));
          return body;
        }
        if (matchError) body.appendChild(el('p', 'cfg-match-error', matchError));
      
        if (!matchReport) {
          const cur = { prop: cfgEntry('HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP'), value: cfgEntry('HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE') };
          if (cur.prop && cur.prop.value) {
            body.appendChild(el('p', 'muted small',
              `config.env matches on ${cur.prop.value} == "${cur.value ? cur.value.value : ''}"${cur.prop.enabled ? '' : ' — that line is commented out'}.`));
          } else {
            body.appendChild(el('p', 'muted small', 'No match property is set: the submission would be always active, which is only right for a device that has no name to match.'));
          }
          return body;
        }
      
        const rep = matchReport;
        const summary = el('div', 'cfg-match-summary');
        summary.appendChild(el('span', 'muted small', 'codename '));
        summary.appendChild(el('code', null, rep.codename || 'not found'));
        if (rep.model) summary.appendChild(el('span', 'muted small', ' · ' + rep.model));
        summary.appendChild(el('span', 'cfg-match-badge trust-' + rep.confidence, confidenceLabel(rep.confidence)));
        body.appendChild(summary);
      
        // A match condition that does not hold is invisible: the overlay enables and
        // changes nothing. So unless a property satisfies every rule, the honest
        // answer is the one that already works — the module's own property.
        if (rep.confidence !== 'high') body.appendChild(keepCurrentNote(rep));
      
        const rows = rep.candidates || [];
        for (const c of rows.slice(0, 3)) body.appendChild(matchRow(c));
        if (rows.length > 3) {
          const more = document.createElement('details');
          const rest = rows.length - 3;
          more.appendChild(el('summary', 'muted small', `${rest} more candidate${rest === 1 ? '' : 's'}`));
          for (const c of rows.slice(3)) more.appendChild(matchRow(c));
          body.appendChild(more);
        }
      
        if ((rep.rejected || []).length) {
          const ruled = document.createElement('details');
          ruled.appendChild(el('summary', 'muted small', `${rep.rejected.length} propert${rep.rejected.length === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'} ruled out`));

        box.appendChild(el('b', null, 'Keep the match you already have. '));

      function matchRow(c) {

        head.appendChild(el('code', 'cfg-match-prop', c.prop));
        head.appendChild(el('span', 'cfg-match-eq', '='));

      async function askMatchProp() {

        if (!row) return false;
        const on = row.querySelector('.cfg-on');
        const input = row.querySelector('.cfg-value');

        if (!input) return false;
        input.value = value;

        if (!state || !state.cloneValid) return;

          renderRunState();
          adbStatus('downloading platform-tools…', 0);
        } catch (err) {
          adbPrint('✗ ' + err.message);
          adbStatus(err.message, 9000);
        }
        refreshAdbDevices();
      }
      
      // Every property the server tried, in the order it tried them. Detecting is a
      // guess — on a GSI ro.product.device names the GSI, not the phone — so the
      // answer is shown with the command that produced it and the other answers are
      // one click away.
      let detectCandidates = [];
      let detectAt = 0;
      
      async function detectDevice() {
        const pick = adbDeviceChoice();
        if (pick.blocked) {
          adbStatus(pick.blocked, 9000);
          return;
        }
        try {
          adbStatus('asking the phone…', 0);
          const d = await api('api/adb/detect', { method: 'POST', body: { serial: pick.serial } });
          detectCandidates = (d.candidates || []).filter((c) => c.value);
          detectAt = 0;
          if (d.manufacturer) $('adb-manufacturer').value = d.manufacturer;
          if (detectCandidates.length) applyDetectCandidate();
          else $('detect-note').hidden = true;
          rememberAdbValues();
          renderPresets();
          adbStatus(`detected ${d.codename || 'the device'}`, 5000);
        } catch (err) {
          adbStatus(err.message, 9000);
          adbPrint('✗ ' + err.message);
        }
      }
      
      function applyDetectCandidate() {
        const note = $('detect-note');
        const pick = detectCandidates[detectAt];
        if (!pick) {
          note.hidden = true;
          return;
        }
      
        $('adb-codename').value = pick.value;
        rememberAdbValues();
        renderPresets();
      
        const source = $('detect-source');
        source.textContent = '';
        source.append(document.createTextNode('codename from '), el('code', null, pick.prop));
        if (pick.note) source.append(el('span', 'muted', ' — ' + pick.note));
      
        const others = detectCandidates.length - 1;
        if (others === 0) source.append(el('span', 'muted', ' · no other command answered'));
        const next = $('detect-next');
        next.hidden = others === 0;
        next.title = others
          ? `${others} other command${others === 1 ? '' : 's'} returned a value — click to use the next one`
          : '';
        note.hidden = false;
      }
      
      function nextDetectCandidate() {
        if (detectCandidates.length < 2) return;
        detectAt = (detectAt + 1) % detectCandidates.length;
        applyDetectCandidate();
      }
      
      async function extract(action) {
        try {
          adbClear();
          switchTab('device');
          adbRunning = true;
          renderRunState();
          adbStatus('pulling…', 0);
          await api('api/extract', { method: 'POST', body: { action } });
        } catch (err) {
          adbRunning = false;
          renderRunState();
          adbStatus(err.message, 8000);
        }
      }

          <div class="card">
            <h2>Automatic detection</h2>
            <p class="hint">
              Reads the display settings the overlay has to match and offers each
              answer with its source. Tick the ones to keep and write them to
              <code>config.env</code>. Nothing is written until you do.
            </p>
            <div class="row actions">

              rates come from the display hardware, the cutout and status bar also
              have to be read from the ROM — on a GSI the OEM's own values are gone
              with the OEM system partition.
            </p>
          </div>

            <h2>From firmware files</h2>

              <button id="detect-pick-dir" type="button" class="pick" title="Choose the ROM folder or a tree you already unpacked">Folder…</button>
              <button id="detect-scan" type="button">Scan firmware</button>
            </div>

              status bar when a GSI has replaced the system partition. Point it at a
              fastboot ROM's <code>super.img</code>, a Samsung
              <code>AP_*.tar.md5</code>, the ROM folder, or a tree you already
              unpacked: a bare image is unpacked first, by the app, with no
              <code>lpunpack</code> or <code>simg2img</code> to install.
