```
#!/system/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay — WebUI helper
# =============================================================================
#
# Two mechanisms, because Android only allows one of them per value type:
#
#   dimens  the page patches the value straight into resources.arsc of the
#           overlay APK this module already ships (`apks`/`backup`/`restore`
#           below keep the paths and the pristine copies). A dimension the
#           build did not emit - config.env leaves the optional padding keys
#           commented out - is added to that table by the page, which then
#           writes the whole APK again. A static RRO is read when the
#           framework starts, so `reload` restarts zygote.
#           `cmd overlay fabricate` cannot be used for these: it only accepts
#           int/colour/bool/string data types and rejects a dimension with
#           "dataType is out of range of [16, 31] (too low)".
#
#   bools   a fabricated overlay (`cmd overlay fabricate`) still works and is
#           cheaper than repacking an APK, so config_displayBlanksAfterDoze is
#           registered at runtime and again at boot.
#
#   sh apply.sh get                 saved values + build-time defaults
#   sh apply.sh conf                only the saved values (webui.conf)
#   sh apply.sh set KEY=VALUE ...   store values only
#   sh apply.sh apply [--boot]      register the fabricated (bool) overlays
#   sh apply.sh manifest            the resource list the page renders
#   sh apply.sh apks                overlay APK paths the page patches
#   sh apply.sh backup              keep a pristine copy of those APKs
#   sh apply.sh restore             put the pristine APKs back
#   sh apply.sh reload              restart zygote so the patched APKs load
#   sh apply.sh verify              exit 0 when every saved value is live
#   sh apply.sh restart             restart SystemUI only (no framework reload)
#   sh apply.sh status              effective (current) device values
#   sh apply.sh reset               restore the APKs and forget the values
#   sh apply.sh arm                 the page wrote an APK, start guarding it
#   sh apply.sh boot-guard          post-fs-data: undo a patch whose boot failed
#   sh apply.sh boot-confirm        post-boot: this patch booted fine
#   sh apply.sh restore-conf        customize.sh: bring saved values into a new install
#
# Saved values are mirrored to $STATE_DIR, because the module directory itself
# is replaced when the module is updated: the new zip carries the build-time
# APKs again, and the page re-applies webui.conf onto them the next time it is
# opened. customize.sh copies the file back on install.
#
# Resource arrays such as the auto-brightness curves cannot be expressed this
# way at all - those still need a rebuild.
#
# NOTE: fabricated overlay names may only contain alphanumerics, '_' and '.'
# (AOSP OverlayManagerServiceImpl.validateName with requireFilename=true).
# A hyphen in the name makes `fabricate` fail with
# "overlay name can only consist of alphanumeric characters, '_', and '.'",
# so every character outside that set is replaced with '_'.
# =============================================================================

SELF="$0"
case "$SELF" in
    */*) SELF_DIR=${SELF%/*} ;;
    *)   SELF_DIR=. ;;
esac
MODDIR=$(cd "$SELF_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)
[ -n "$MODDIR" ] || MODDIR=$SELF_DIR
CONF="$MODDIR/webui.conf"
DEFAULTS="$MODDIR/webui-defaults.conf"
# Outside the module directory on purpose: an update replaces that directory.
# WEBUI_STATE_DIR exists so the script can be exercised off-device.
STATE_DIR="${WEBUI_STATE_DIR:-/data/adb/treble-webui/${MODDIR##*/}}"
GEN_FILE="$MODDIR/webui-gen"
OK_FILE="$MODDIR/webui-gen-ok"
TRY_FILE="$MODDIR/webui-try"
OWNER="com.android.shell"
PREFIX="treble_webui"

# WEBUI_CMD only exists so the script can be exercised off-device.
CMD=${WEBUI_CMD:-/system/bin/cmd}
DENSITY=""

KEYS="RADIUS SB_HEIGHT PAD_CONTENT PAD_START PAD_END DOZE_BLANK"

say() { echo "$*"; }
===
#!/system/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay — module addons
# =============================================================================
# An addon is a tweak the *module* makes on the phone. It is not a config.env
# key, and it is chosen in the app's Addons tab (or the page's Addons card),
# not in the overlay resource files.
#
# There are two kinds, and the catalog says which is which:
#
#   setting  a Settings value the module writes. One `settings put` changes it
#            on a running phone — no APK, no reboot — and service.sh re-applies
#            it at every boot. The overlay APK alone cannot do one.
#   overlay  a resource the build bakes into an overlay APK — framework (the
#            navigation bar height, the 180° rotation flag) or SystemUI (the
#            status bar background). It only changes after a rebuild and a
#            flash, because a resource is read when its process starts.
#
# The live addons survive an overlay rebuild; the overlay ones *are* the rebuild.
#
# One catalog lives in this file and every front-end reads it:
#
#   the desktop app   runs this script in the clone (Addons tab)
#   the module page   runs it in webroot/ on the phone (Addons card)
#   service.sh        runs it at every boot so saved choices stick
#
#   sh addons.sh list                 catalog + saved + live values, as JSON
#   sh addons.sh set ID=VALUE ...     save choices; apply the live ones now
#   sh addons.sh apply [ID ...]       apply what is saved (all ids, or those)
#   sh addons.sh reset                back to the defaults, forget the choices
#   sh addons.sh status               what the device resolves now, as key=value
#   sh addons.sh restore-conf         customize.sh: bring the saved file back
#
# The saved file is addons.conf at the module root (src/module/addons.conf in
# the clone). Only the addons that differ from the default are written into it:
# a value nobody changed is not enforced on every boot, so an untouched phone
# keeps behaving like the ROM shipped it.
#
# ADDONS_CONF, ADDONS_DIR and ADDONS_SETTINGS exist so this can be exercised
# off-device (stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js) and by the desktop app, which has
# no installed module but does have the clone.
# =============================================================================

# The module directory is one level above this script (webroot/), except when
# the script is run by its bare name from the module root ('sh addons.sh'), in
# which case '..' would be the folder above the module.
SELF="$0"
case "$SELF" in
    */*) SELF_DIR=${SELF%/*}
         MODDIR=$(cd "$SELF_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd) ;;
    *)   SELF_DIR=.
         MODDIR=$(pwd) ;;
esac
MODDIR=${ADDONS_DIR:-$MODDIR}
[ -n "$MODDIR" ] || MODDIR=$SELF_DIR
# In the clone the module files are kept in src/module/, so the script in
# src/webui/ has one directory in between; an installed module keeps the same
# files at its root.
[ -d "$MODDIR/module" ] && MODDIR="$MODDIR/module"
```

```
              <button id="adb-detect" type="button">Detect from device</button>

      <dialog id="confirm">

          <h2 id="confirm-title">Delete?</h2>
          <p class="muted" id="confirm-text"></p>
          <menu>
            <button type="button" class="danger" id="confirm-yes">Delete</button>
            <button type="button" class="primary" id="confirm-no">Cancel</button>
          </menu>

      <!-- Installing packages needs root, and the child has no terminal for sudo to

      <dialog id="sudo">

          <p class="muted">

          <label for="sudo-password">sudo password</label>
          <input id="sudo-password" type="password" autocomplete="current-password" spellcheck="false">
      
          <p class="error" id="sudo-error" hidden></p>
      
          <menu>
            <button type="button" id="sudo-cancel">Cancel</button>
            <button type="submit" class="primary">Install</button>
          </menu>
        </form>
      </dialog>
      
      <dialog id="update">
        <form method="dialog" id="update-form">
          <h2>Update available</h2>

          <p class="upd-label" id="upd-files-label" hidden>Files the update changes</p>
          <pre class="device-log" id="upd-files" hidden></pre>
      
          <div id="upd-clash" hidden>
            <p class="upd-label">Your uncommitted edits in those files</p>
            <pre class="device-log" id="upd-clash-files"></pre>
            <p class="hint" id="upd-clash-note"></p>
          </div>
      
          <pre class="device-log" id="upd-output" hidden></pre>
          <p class="error" id="upd-error" hidden></p>
      
          <menu>
            <button type="button" id="upd-later">Later</button>
            <button type="button" class="primary" id="upd-go">Update now</button>
          </menu>
        </form>
      </dialog>
      
      <script src="app.js"></script>
      </body>
      </html>
```

```
- path: gui/app.go
  content: |
      type Verb struct {
        Name  string   `json:"name"`
        Label string   `json:"label"`
        Arg   string   `json:"arg"`
        Hint  string   `json:"hint"`
        Flags []string `json:"flags"`
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The commands the app is allowed to run
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Each entry is one thing `build.sh` already does; the GUI only chooses which
      // one to run. Flags are per verb on purpose: `--all` means "also remove config
      // and device files" and is meaningless on a build, so the UI disables it and
      // the server rejects it. Keeping the table here (not only in the JS) means a
      // hand-written POST cannot widen what the app will execute.
      var verbTable = []Verb{
        {
          Name:  "build",
          Label: "Build",
          Arg:   "build",
          Hint:  "Compile and sign the module, and the submission zips",
          Flags: []string{"--with-vendor-hals", "--allow-unknown-resources"},
        },
        {
          Name:  "dryrun",
          Label: "Dry run",
          Arg:   "--dry-run",
          Hint:  "Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing",
          Flags: nil,
        },
        {
          Name:  "check",
          Label: "Check",
          Arg:   "check",
          Hint:  "Validate config.env, build nothing",
          Flags: nil,
        },
        {
          Name:  "doctor",
          Label: "Doctor",
          Arg:   "doctor",
          Hint:  "Check the toolchain, install nothing",
          Flags: nil,
        },
        {
          Name:  "setup",
          Label: "Setup",
          Arg:   "setup",
          Hint:  "Install or repair the build tools",
          Flags: []string{"--force"},
        },
        {
          Name:  "clean",
          Label: "Clean",
          Arg:   "clean",
          Hint:  "Remove build output",
          Flags: []string{"--all"},
        },
      }
      
      func lookupVerb(name string) (Verb, bool) {
        for _, v := range verbTable {
          if v.Name == name {
            return v, true
          }
        }
        return Verb{}, false
      }
      
      // buildArgs turns a verb and its ticked flags into the argv for bash.
      //
      // -y is always appended: the child has no terminal, so anything that would
      // prompt has to take its default instead of blocking forever on stdin. That is
      // also why --with-vendor-hals becomes reachable at all — build.sh only honours
      // it together with --yes.
      func buildArgs(verb string, flags []string) ([]string, error) {
        v, ok := lookupVerb(verb)
        if !ok {
          return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown command %q", verb)
        }
        args := []string{"--noprofile", "--norc", "./build.sh", v.Arg}
        for _, f := range flags {
          if !contains(v.Flags, f) {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is not available with %s", f, v.Name)
```

```
    local generic=""
    for apk in "${candidates[@]}"; do
        [ -n "$(shel "ls $apk")" ] || continue
        local local_apk="$tmpdir/power.apk"
        pull_file "$apk" "$local_apk" || {
            warn "could not read $apk"
            continue
        }
        tree="$(dump_power "$local_apk")"
        [ -n "$tree" ] || continue
        if profile_looks_real "$tree"; then
            printf '# source: %s\n' "$apk"
            printf '%s\n' "$tree"
            return 0
        fi
        [ -n "$generic" ] || generic="$apk"
        note "$apk carries a generic profile (0.1 for everything, a 1 GHz-less CPU list), so it was skipped"
    done
    die "no real power profile found — ${generic:+$generic holds the AOSP placeholder; }the OEM's own is usually in an enabled overlay APK (e.g. /vendor/overlay/FrameworksResTarget_Vendor.apk) or in the ROM dump"
}

power_profile_firmware() {
    [ -d "$fwdir" ] || die "not a folder: $fwdir"
    fwdir="$(cd "$fwdir" && pwd)"
    resolve_aapt2 || die "aapt2 not found — it is needed to read the APKs"

    # Overlay APKs first (an OEM's own profile usually lives there), then the
    # framework's copy. The first one that looks like a device wins; a generic
    # AOSP profile is remembered only to explain the failure.
    local apk tree generic=""
    while IFS= read -r apk; do
        [ -n "$apk" ] || continue
        tree="$(dump_power "$apk")"
        [ -n "$tree" ] || continue
        if profile_looks_real "$tree"; then
            printf '# source: %s\n' "$apk"
            printf '%s\n' "$tree"
            return 0
        fi
        [ -n "$generic" ] || generic="$apk"
        note "$apk carries a generic profile (0.1 for everything, a 1 GHz-less CPU list), so it was skipped"
    done <<<"$(find "$fwdir" -type f -path '*/overlay/*.apk' 2>/dev/null | head -n 300; find "$fwdir" -type f -name 'framework-res.apk' 2>/dev/null | head -n 10)"

    die "no real power profile found under $fwdir${generic:+ — $generic holds the AOSP placeholder}"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Report
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
json_escape() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr -d '\000-\037' | sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g'; }
json_list() {
    local first=1 v
    printf '['
    for v in "$@"; do
        [ "$first" -eq 1 ] || printf ','
        first=0
        printf '"%s"' "$(json_escape "$v")"
    done
    printf ']'
}

emit_json() {
    local i first=1
    printf '{'
    printf '"mode":"%s",' "$mode"
    if [ "$mode" = "device" ]; then
        printf '"device":{"serial":"%s","model":"%s","codename":"%s","rom":"%s","isGsi":%s,"width":%s,"height":%s,"density":%s},' \
            "$(json_escape "${serial:-}")" "$(json_escape "${MODEL:-}")" \
            "$(json_escape "${CODENAME:-}")" "$(json_escape "${rom:-}")" \
            "$([ "${IS_GSI:-0}" -eq 1 ] && echo true || echo false)" "${W:-0}" "${H:-0}" "${DENS:-0}"
    else
        printf '"firmware":"%s",' "$(json_escape "$fwdir")"
    fi
    printf '"aapt2":"%s",' "$(json_escape "${aapt2:-}")"
    printf '"facts":['
    for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
        [ "$first" -eq 1 ] || printf ','
        first=0
        printf '{"key":"%s","label":"%s","unit":"%s","value":"%s","source":"%s","confidence":"%s","kind":"%s","detail":"%s"}' \
            "$(json_escape "${f_key[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${f_label[$i]}")" \
            "$(json_escape "${f_unit[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${f_value[$i]}")" \
            "$(json_escape "${f_src[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${f_conf[$i]}")" \
            "$(json_escape "${f_kind[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${f_detail[$i]}")"
    done
    printf '],'
    printf '"warnings":%s,' "$(json_list "${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}")"
    printf '"notes":%s,' "$(json_list "${notes[@]+"${notes[@]}"}")"
    local fpaths=() froles=()
    for i in "${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}"; do
        fpaths+=("${i%%|*}")
        froles+=("${i#*|}")
    done
    printf '"files":['
    for i in "${!fpaths[@]}"; do
        [ "$i" -eq 0 ] || printf ','
        printf '{"path":"%s","role":"%s"}' "$(json_escape "${fpaths[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${froles[$i]}")"
    done
    printf ']'
    [ "$want_write" -eq 1 ] && printf ',"written":"config.env"'
    printf '}\n'
}

emit_human() {
    local i
    printf '\n'
    if [ "$mode" = "device" ]; then
        printf 'Device   %s (%s)  %sx%s @%s dpi\n' \
            "${MODEL:-unknown}" "${CODENAME:-unknown}" "${W:-?}" "${H:-?}" "${DENS:-?}"
        printf 'ROM      %s\n' "${rom:-unknown}"
    else
        printf 'Firmware %s\n' "$fwdir"
    fi
    printf '\n'

    if [ "${#f_key[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf 'Nothing found.\n'
        for i in "${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}"; do printf '  ! %s\n' "$i"; done
        return
    fi

    # A cutout path is a hundred characters of SVG; the table is a summary, so
    # it is cut to a readable length here and printed in full further down.
    short_value() {
        local v="$1"
        if [ "${#v}" -gt 44 ]; then printf '%s…' "${v:0:43}"; else printf '%s' "$v"; fi
    }

    printf '%-26s %-46s %-20s %s\n' "SETTING" "VALUE" "SOURCE" "CONFIDENCE"
    for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
        printf '%-26s %-46s %-20s %s\n' \
            "${f_key[$i]}" "$(short_value "${f_value[$i]}${f_unit[$i]:+ ${f_unit[$i]}}")" \
            "${f_src[$i]}" "${f_conf[$i]}"
    done

    # Disagreement is the interesting case: the same setting with two values
    # means two sources, and the user has to pick which one to believe.
    local key i j distinct first second
    for key in $(printf '%s\n' "${f_key[@]}" | awk '!seen[$0]++'); do
        distinct="$(for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
            [ "${f_key[$i]}" = "$key" ] && printf '%s\n' "${f_value[$i]}"
        done | awk '!seen[$0]++' | grep -c . || true)"
        [ "${distinct:-0}" -gt 1 ] || continue
        if [ "$distinct" -eq 2 ]; then
            first=""; second=""
            for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
                [ "${f_key[$i]}" = "$key" ] || continue
                if [ -z "$first" ]; then first="$i"
                elif [ "${f_value[$i]}" != "${f_value[$first]}" ] && [ -z "$second" ]; then second="$i"; fi
            done
            printf '\n%s differs: %s says %s, %s says %s\n' \
                "$key" "${f_src[$first]}" "$(short_value "${f_value[$first]}")" \
                "${f_src[$second]}" "$(short_value "${f_value[$second]}")"
        else
            printf '\n%s: %s different answers — pick one from the table\n' "$key" "$distinct"
        fi
    done

    printf '\nvalues for config.env:\n'
    for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
        local seen=""
        local j
        for j in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
            [ "$i" -gt "$j" ] && [ "${f_key[$i]}" = "${f_key[$j]}" ] && { seen="1"; break; }
        done
        [ -n "$seen" ] && continue
        case "${f_key[$i]}" in
            DISPLAY_CUTOUT|LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE) printf '  %s="%s"\n' "${f_key[$i]}" "${f_value[$i]}" ;;
            *) printf '  %s=%s\n' "${f_key[$i]}" "${f_value[$i]}" ;;
        esac
    done

    for i in "${notes[@]+"${notes[@]}"}"; do printf '\nnote: %s\n' "$i"; done
    for i in "${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}"; do printf '\nwarning: %s\n' "$i"; done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writing config.env
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set_config_key() {
    local key="$1" value="$2" file="$ROOT/config.env" tmp
    [ -f "$file" ] || die "no config.env in $ROOT"
    tmp="$tmpdir/config.env"
    awk -v k="$key" -v v="$value" '
        BEGIN { done = 0 }
        {
            line = $0
            sub(/\r$/, "", line)
            if (!done && line ~ "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*" k "=") {
                match(line, /^[[:space:]]*/)
                printf "%s%s=%s\n", substr(line, 1, RLENGTH), k, v
                done = 1
                next
            }
            print
        }
        END { if (!done) printf "%s=%s\n", k, v }
    ' "$file" >"$tmp" || return 1
    cp "$tmp" "$file"
}

write_config() {
    local i value
    for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
        [ "${f_conf[$i]}" = "low" ] && continue
        # One write per setting: the first fact is the highest-priority source.
        local key="${f_key[$i]}"
        local earlier=""
        local j
        for j in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
            [ "$j" -lt "$i" ] && [ "${f_key[$j]}" = "$key" ] && { earlier="1"; break; }
        done
        [ -n "$earlier" ] && continue

        value="${f_value[$i]}"
        case "$key" in
            # String settings keep the quotes every line of config.env uses.
            DISPLAY_CUTOUT|LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE) set_config_key "$key" "\"$value\"" ;;
            *) set_config_key "$key" "$value" ;;
        esac
    done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
main() {
    # Hidden helper for the tests: decide whether a tree on stdin is a device
    # profile or the AOSP placeholder, without needing adb or aapt2.
    if [ "$check_profile" -eq 1 ]; then
        local tree
        tree="$(cat)"
        if profile_looks_real "$tree"; then
            printf 'real\n'
            exit 0
        fi
        printf 'generic\n'
        exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$power_mode" -eq 1 ]; then
        if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then power_profile_firmware; else power_profile_device; fi
        exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then probe_firmware; else probe_device; fi
    if [ "$want_write" -eq 1 ]; then
        if [ "${#f_key[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
            die "nothing to write — no setting was found"
        fi
        write_config
    fi
    if [ "$want_json" -eq 1 ]; then emit_json; else emit_human; fi
}

main "$@"
```

```
        # Disagreement is the interesting case: it usually means one source is a

            fi
        done
        printf '\nconfig.env:\n'
        printf '  HAS_UDFPS=true\n  UDFPS_X=%s\n  UDFPS_Y=%s\n  UDFPS_RADIUS=%s\n' \
            "${c_x[$idx]}" "${c_y[$idx]}" "${c_r[$idx]}"
    fi

        printf '\nRead from:\n'

# Only the four lines are touched, and a commented-out one is switched back on:
# copying the block out of the file by hand is exactly where "UDFPS_X is set but
# HAS_UDFPS=false" comes from.
set_config_key() {
    local key="$1" value="$2" file="$ROOT/config.env" tmp
    [ -f "$file" ] || die "no config.env in $ROOT"
    tmp="$tmpdir/config.env"
    awk -v k="$key" -v v="$value" '
        BEGIN { done = 0 }
        {
            line = $0
            sub(/\r$/, "", line)
            if (!done && line ~ "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*" k "=") {
                match(line, /^[[:space:]]*/)
                printf "%s%s=%s\n", substr(line, 1, RLENGTH), k, v
                done = 1
                next
            }
            print
        }
        END { if (!done) printf "%s=%s\n", k, v }
    ' "$file" >"$tmp" || return 1
    cp "$tmp" "$file"
}

write_config() {
    local idx="$1"
    set_config_key HAS_UDFPS true
    set_config_key UDFPS_X "${c_x[$idx]}"
    set_config_key UDFPS_Y "${c_y[$idx]}"
    set_config_key UDFPS_RADIUS "${c_r[$idx]}"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
main() {
    files=()
    if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then probe_firmware; else probe_device; fi
    local idx
    idx="$(chosen_index)"
    if [ "$want_write" -eq 1 ]; then
        if [ -z "$idx" ]; then
            die "nothing to write — no usable geometry found"
        fi
        # An estimate is not good enough to write behind the user's back: it is
        # the one answer that is not evidence.
        if [ "${c_kind[$idx]}" = "estimate" ]; then
            die "only an estimate was found — set the values by hand from --help"
        fi
        write_config "$idx"
    fi
    if [ "$want_json" -eq 1 ]; then emit_json "$idx"; else emit_human "$idx"; fi
}

main "$@"
```

```
// The script validates both; these only keep a request from being turned into
// shell syntax. The page can only send what it rendered, but a request is not
// the page.
var (
  addonID     = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9_]+$`)
  addonChoice = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9]+$`)
)

// addonsEnv points the helper at the clone instead of an installed module.
// Paths are POSIX: Git Bash on Windows reads a backslash as an escape.
func (a *App) addonsEnv() []string {
  root := filepath.ToSlash(a.Root())
  return []string{
    "ADDONS_DIR=" + root,
    "ADDONS_CONF=" + root + "/src/module/addons.conf",
  }
}

func (a *App) runAddons(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
  root := a.Root()
  if !isClone(root) {
    return nil, errors.New("no clone selected")
  }
  bash := a.Bash()
  if !fileExists(bash) {
    return nil, errors.New("bash was not found — pick it with the Path chip")
  }
  // Short on purpose: six `settings` calls on a phone, and no work at all in
  // the clone.
  ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
  defer cancel()
  cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bash, append([]string{addonsScript}, args...)...)
  // Hide the console Windows would otherwise flash for this child. The tab
  // runs the helper on open and on every save, so an un-hidden window is a
  // black rectangle blinking at the user each time.
  setProcAttr(cmd)
  cmd.Dir = root
  // A stale ADDONS_* in the app's own environment would otherwise win over
  // the paths below (Windows keeps the first duplicate in the block).
  env := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+2)
  for _, kv := range os.Environ() {
    if strings.HasPrefix(kv, "ADDONS_") {
      continue
    }
    env = append(env, kv)
  }
  cmd.Env = append(env, a.addonsEnv()...)
  var stderr strings.Builder
  cmd.Stderr = &stderr
  out, err := cmd.Output()
  if err != nil {
    msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
    if msg == "" {
      msg = err.Error()
    }
    return nil, errors.New(msg)
  }
  return out, nil
}

// addonsDoc is the helper's own JSON, passed through: the page renders exactly
// what the module will enforce.
func (a *App) addonsDoc() (map[string]any, error) {
  out, err := a.runAddons("list")
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  var doc map[string]any
  if err := json.Unmarshal(out, &doc); err != nil {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("the addons helper did not return JSON: %v", err)
  }
  return doc, nil
}

func (a *App) handleAddons(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  doc, err := a.addonsDoc()
  if err != nil {
    writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
    return
  }
  writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, doc)
}

// handleAddonsSave stores the choices, which is also what applies them: the
// script's `set` writes the file and makes the values true on the phone when
// there is one. A phone is not required — the file is what the build packs.
func (a *App) handleAddonsSave(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  var body struct {
    Values map[string]string `json:"values"`
    Reset  bool              `json:"reset"`
  }
  if !decode(w, r, &body) {
    return
  }

  if body.Reset {
    if _, err := a.runAddons("reset"); err != nil {
      writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
      return
    }
  } else {
    pairs := make([]string, 0, len(body.Values))
    for id, value := range body.Values {
      if !addonID.MatchString(id) {
        writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "not an addon id: "+id)
        return
      }
      if !addonChoice.MatchString(value) {
        writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "not an addon value: "+value)
        return
      }
      pairs = append(pairs, id+"="+value)
    }
    sort.Strings(pairs)
    if len(pairs) > 0 {
      if _, err := a.runAddons(append([]string{"set"}, pairs...)...); err != nil {
        writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
        return
      }
    }
  }

  doc, err := a.addonsDoc()
  if err != nil {
    writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
    return
  }
  writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, doc)
}
```

```
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay — Device Configuration
# =============================================================================
# Edit this file to match YOUR device, then run: ./build.sh/cmd
#   Preview what these values produce (no tools, no build): ./build.sh/cmd --dry-run
#   Check them only:                                        ./build.sh/cmd check
#
#   Lines starting with # are OFF. Remove the # to turn one on.
#
#   Manufacturer  adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer
#   Model         adb shell getprop ro.product.model
#   Codename      adb shell getprop ro.product.device
#                 (on a GSI this often shows the ROM's name — see below)
#
# Reference values: config.env.example (Samsung Galaxy A90 5G)
# =============================================================================

# ── Device identity ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Drives the module/overlay names. Codename also names the match property below.
DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="Xiaomi"
DEVICE_MODEL="Redmi Note 17"
DEVICE_CODENAME="Zephyr"
# Battery/power profile: src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml (docs/device-extraction.md)

# ── Module metadata ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# What Magisk/KernelSU/APatch show on the Modules page, and the version of both
# APKs. Bump OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE on every release — it must be a whole number.
OVERLAY_VERSION="2.0"
OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE=2
# Author of the module. Left empty, module.prop falls back to DEVICE_MANUFACTURER.
MODULE_AUTHOR="uzbforce"

# ── Overlay activation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The overlay applies only while DEVICE_PROP_NAME == DEVICE_PROP_VALUE.
# Keep persist.sys.overlay.<codename> = true: it is readable from every domain
# and build.sh sets it at boot before zygote. DEVICE_PROP_NAME="" drops the
# check entirely (module only ever lands on this one device).
#   Why not ro.product.device? On a GSI that is the ROM's name (mivendor,
#   phh_treble, …) and zygote cannot read the prop holding the real codename.
#   Details + per-device prop table: docs/configuration.md#choosing-the-match-property
# Is it really applied? (an [x] in `cmd overlay list` does not prove it)
#   adb shell cmd overlay lookup <package> android:dimen/status_bar_height_default
#
#  If you want to use a different property, set it here and also in
#  docs/configuration.md#choosing-the-match-property
DEVICE_PROP_NAME="persist.sys.overlay.zephyr"
DEVICE_PROP_VALUE="true"

# ── Overlay Priority ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
OVERLAY_PRIORITY=628
OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI=9999

# ── Display ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Screen corner radius. Also the reference for the padding below.
ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS=135
# Status bar height in px, portrait and landscape. The effective height is
# max(this value, display-cutout inset).
STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT=113
STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE=70

# ── Status bar content padding ────────────────────────────────────────────
#   >>> OFF BY DEFAULT — uncomment the three STATUS_BAR_* lines to turn it on.
#
# Moves the clock and the status icons away from the left/right edges, so they
# do not sit under the rounded corners. Left commented, the bar keeps the
# ROM/GSI layout.
#
#   STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START / _END   SystemUI status_bar_padding_*  <- GSI obeys this
#   STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING        framework rounded_corner_content_padding
#
# Set all three to the SAME number. Rule of thumb: ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS / 3
# (15-20 should fit a 120-150px corner). The two paths never stack.
#   Measured on this device: framework value alone did nothing on the GSI,
#   the SystemUI pair moved the clock 1:1.
# More: docs/configuration.md#status-bar-content-padding-start--end
#STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING=15
#STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START=15
#STATUS_BAR_PADDING_END=15

# Rarely needed fine-tuning of the same block (all optional):
#STATUS_BAR_PADDING_TOP=0
#STATUS_BAR_ICONS_PADDING_START=3dp
#STATUS_BAR_ICONS_PADDING_END=4dp
#STATUS_BAR_DOT_MIN_PADDING=20dp
# Turns the camera/mic privacy dot off (also frees its 20dp end-side reserve).
#HAS_PRIVACY_DOT=false
# Notch / Display Cutout (SVG Path)
# Leave commented out if your device has no notch.
# Reference (Samsung Infinity-U):
DISPLAY_CUTOUT="M 0,0 H -29 V 118 H 29 V 0 H 0 Z"
```

```

- path: gui/configfile.go
  content: |
      package main
      
      import (
        "fmt"
        "regexp"
        "strings"
      )
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // config.env as a form
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // config.env is sourced by bash, so it has to stay a text file: comments are
      // documentation, `#` in front of a key is how a feature is switched off, and
      // the order of the lines is the order of the sections people read. The app used
      // to show it in a textarea, which is honest but means the user has to know bash
      // quoting rules to change a number.
      //
      // So the file is parsed here and edited line-wise: the form knows the key, the
      // value and whether the line is commented out, and a save rewrites only the
      // lines that changed. Everything else in the file — headings, prose, blank
      // lines, the `#` on features that are off — is preserved byte for byte. That is
      // also why the raw view is still there: if parsing ever gets something wrong,
      // the user can see what the file actually says.
      type ConfigEntry struct {
        Line    int      `json:"line"`
        Key     string   `json:"key"`
        Value   string   `json:"value"`
        Enabled bool     `json:"enabled"`
        Comment []string `json:"comment"`
      }
      
      type ConfigSection struct {
        Title   string        `json:"title"`
        Note    []string      `json:"note"`
        Entries []ConfigEntry `json:"entries"`
      }
      
      type ConfigDoc struct {
        Sections []ConfigSection `json:"sections"`
        Total    int             `json:"total"`
        Enabled  int             `json:"enabled"`
      }
      
      // Lookup returns an enabled value, treating a leftover template placeholder
      // ("<device_codename>") as "not set" — it is not a name, and the adb presets
      // would otherwise happily grep the device for the literal angle brackets.
      func (d ConfigDoc) Lookup(key string) string {
        for _, s := range d.Sections {
          for _, e := range s.Entries {
            if e.Key != key || !e.Enabled {
              continue
            }
            v := strings.TrimSpace(e.Value)
            if v == "" || strings.HasPrefix(v, "<") {
              return ""
            }
            return v
          }
        }
        return ""
      }
      
      func (d ConfigDoc) LookupAll(key string) []string {
        var out []string
        for _, s := range d.Sections {
          for _, e := range s.Entries {
            if e.Key == key && e.Enabled {
              v := strings.TrimSpace(e.Value)
              if v != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(v, "<") {
                out = append(out, v)
              }
            }
          }
        }
        return out
      }
      
      var (
        // "# ── Device identity ─────────────" — a section heading.
        configHeading = regexp.MustCompile(`^\s*#\s*─+\s*(.*?)\s*─*\s*$`)
        // KEY=value, optionally commented out. Keys in this file are upper case;
        // requiring that keeps prose lines ("# More: docs/…=…") out of the form.
        configKey = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\s*)(#\s*)?([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\s*=(.*)$`)
        // A value that bash will read back unchanged without quotes.
        plainValue = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9_.,:/+@%=-]*$`)
      )
      
      // parseConfig turns the file into sections and entries. It never fails on
      // content: an unparsable line is simply not shown in the form and is left
      // untouched on save.
      func parseConfig(text string) (ConfigDoc, error) {
        // Non-nil slices so the JSON the page receives is always [] and never null:
        // a section that is only a heading would otherwise break the renderer.
        doc := ConfigDoc{Sections: []ConfigSection{}}
        lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
        var cur *ConfigSection
        var pending []string // the comment run directly above the next key
      
        newSection := func() *ConfigSection {
          doc.Sections = append(doc.Sections, ConfigSection{Entries: []ConfigEntry{}, Note: []string{}})
          return &doc.Sections[len(doc.Sections)-1]
        }
      
        for i, raw := range lines {
          line := strings.TrimRight(raw, "\r")
      
          if m := configHeading.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
            s := newSection()
            s.Title = strings.TrimSpace(m[1])
            cur = s
            pending = nil
            continue
          }
          if cur == nil {
            cur = newSection()
          }
      
          if m := configKey.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
            value, _ := splitValue(m[4])
            entry := ConfigEntry{
              Line:    i,
              Key:     m[3],
              Value:   value,
              Enabled: m[2] == "",
              Comment: pending,
            }
            cur.Entries = append(cur.Entries, entry)
            doc.Total++
            if entry.Enabled {
              doc.Enabled++
            }
            pending = nil
            continue
          }
      
          if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
            // A blank line ends a comment block: a key is described by the text
            // right above it, not by every paragraph since the last key.
            pending = nil
            continue
          }
      
          if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "#") {
            text := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "#"))
            pending = append(pending, text)
            if len(cur.Entries) == 0 {
              cur.Note = append(cur.Note, text)
            }
            continue
          }
      
          // Anything else (a stray command, an array) stays in the file and out
          // of the form.
          pending = nil
        }
      
        // A section's blurb is stored twice on purpose: once as the section's
        // introduction (always visible) and once as the first key's comment, so
        // clicking ⓘ on that row answers the question where the user asked it.
        //
        // A key with no note of its own inherits the section's, so ⓘ is never a
        // dead button: in this file the explanation for a group of lines is
        // written once, above the first of them.
        for si := range doc.Sections {
          s := &doc.Sections[si]
          if len(s.Note) == 0 {
            continue
          }
          for ei := range s.Entries {
            if len(s.Entries[ei].Comment) == 0 {
              s.Entries[ei].Comment = s.Note
            }
          }
        }
        return doc, nil
      }
      
      // splitValue mirrors the two ways this file writes a value: bare, or inside
      // quotes. The quote character is remembered so a save writes the same style.
      func splitValue(raw string) (string, byte) {
        s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
        if len(s) >= 2 {
          if q := s[0]; q == '"' || q == '\'' {
            if s[len(s)-1] == q && !escapedAt(s, len(s)-1) {
              return unescape(s[1:len(s)-1], q), q
            }
          }
        }
        return s, 0
      }
      
      func escapedAt(s string, i int) bool {
        n := 0
        for j := i - 1; j >= 0 && s[j] == '\\'; j-- {
          n++
        }
        return n%2 == 1
      }
      
      // unescape only undoes what formatValue adds. A lone backslash (\d) is text,
      // exactly as bash reads it inside double quotes.
      func unescape(s string, quote byte) string {
        if quote != '"' {
          return s
        }
        var b strings.Builder
        for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
          if s[i] == '\\' && i+1 < len(s) && (s[i+1] == '\\' || s[i+1] == '"') {
            b.WriteByte(s[i+1])
            i++
            continue
          }
          b.WriteByte(s[i])
        }
        return b.String()
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Saving
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // ConfigEdit is one row the user changed. Key is sent back so a save cannot
      // land on a different line than the one the form was showing: if the file was
      // edited outside the app in the meantime, the key no longer matches and the
      // save is refused instead of quietly rewriting the wrong setting.
      type ConfigEdit struct {
        Line    int    `json:"line"`
        Key     string `json:"key"`
        Value   string `json:"value"`
        Enabled bool   `json:"enabled"`
      }
      
      func applyConfigEdits(text string, edits []ConfigEdit) (string, error) {
        if len(edits) == 0 {
          return text, nil
        }
        if len(edits) > 512 {
          return "", fmt.Errorf("too many changes in one save")
        }
      
        lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
        seen := make(map[int]struct{}, len(edits))
      
        for _, e := range edits {
          if e.Line < 0 || e.Line >= len(lines) {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: line %d is not in the file any more — reload", e.Key, e.Line+1)
          }
          if _, dup := seen[e.Line]; dup {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: two changes for line %d", e.Key, e.Line+1)
          }
          seen[e.Line] = struct{}{}
      
          if strings.ContainsAny(e.Value, "\r\n\x00") {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: a value cannot contain a line break", e.Key)
          }
      
          cr := ""
          line := lines[e.Line]
          if strings.HasSuffix(line, "\r") {
            cr = "\r"
            line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\r")
          }
      
          m := configKey.FindStringSubmatch(line)
          if m == nil {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: line %d is no longer a setting — reload", e.Key, e.Line+1)
          }
          if m[3] != e.Key {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("the file changed on disk: line %d is %s now — reload", e.Line+1, m[3])
          }
      
          current, quote := splitValue(m[4])
          if current == e.Value && (m[2] == "") == e.Enabled {
            // Nothing actually changed. Not rewriting the line is what makes a
            // no-op save byte-for-byte: the file has lines whose quoting is
            // already odd (#HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY=<number>), and a form save must
            // not restyle a row the user did not touch.
            continue
          }
      
          // Keep the marker the file used if the row is unchanged, drop it when
          // the switch went on, and add a plain '#' when it went off.
          hash := m[2]
          switch {
          case e.Enabled:
            hash = ""
          case hash == "":
            hash = "#"
          }
          lines[e.Line] = m[1] + hash + e.Key + "=" + formatValue(e.Value, quote, m[4]) + cr
        }
      
        return strings.Join(lines, "\n"), nil
      }
      
      // formatValue keeps the file's own style: a value that was quoted stays
      // quoted, a bare number stays bare, and a value that bash would re-split (a
      // path with spaces, a cutout path) gets the quotes it needs.
      func formatValue(value string, quote byte, original string) string {
        if quote != '"' && quote != '\'' && plainValue.MatchString(value) {
          return value
        }
        if quote == '\'' && !strings.ContainsRune(value, '\'') {
          return "'" + value + "'"
        }
        return `"` + escapeDouble(value) + `"`
      }
      
      func escapeDouble(s string) string {
        var b strings.Builder
        for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
          switch s[i] {
          case '\\', '"':
            b.WriteByte('\\')
          }
          b.WriteByte(s[i])
        }
        return b.String()
      }
      
```

> _Reasoning_
> I can port this parser to awk/bash faithfully enough (sections `# ──`, keys regex, quote style preservation, enabled flag). Since the CLI edits and writes immediately, I don't need the stale-line protocol; but preserving the quote style and only rewriting touched lines matters.

```

- path: src/webui/addons.sh
  content: |
      
      CONF=${ADDONS_CONF:-$MODDIR/addons.conf}
      # Outside the module directory on purpose: an update replaces that directory.
      # It is the same folder apply.sh mirrors webui.conf into.
      STATE_DIR=${ADDONS_STATE_DIR:-/data/adb/treble-webui/${MODDIR##*/}}
      SETTINGS=${ADDONS_SETTINGS:-settings}
      
      say() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Catalog
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # id|choices|default|label|summary|kind
      #
      # The value names are what the page and the app show, so they are plain words:
      # "left"/"right", not "0"/"1". The mapping to the Settings value is in
      # apply_one() below, and live_value() maps it back. Keep the summaries free of
      # '|' and keep them one sentence: they are rendered as-is.
      #
      # kind is "setting" or "overlay" (see the top of this file). Only "setting" ids
      # reach apply_one()/live_value(); the build reads the overlay ids out of the
      # saved file and emits them as overlay resources (see resources.sh).
      #
      # A two-choice addon whose choices are exactly on,off is drawn as a switch;
      # anything else is a picker.
      catalog() {
          cat << 'CATALOG_EOF'
      volume_panel|right,left|right|Volume panel side|The volume slider slides in from this edge instead of the other one.|setting
      captive_portal|on,off|on|Captive portal check|Android's "sign in to this network" probe. Off stops the false no-internet warnings a GSI shows on some networks.|setting
      stay_awake|on,off|off|Screen never sleeps|Leave the display on indefinitely, on battery too. Only the power button turns it off again.|setting
      status_clock|on,off|on|Status bar clock|Hide the time in the status bar so the notification icons get its room. The lock-screen clock is left alone.|setting
      any_rotation|on,off|off|Upside-down rotation|Allow the 180° rotation Android normally refuses, in every app and launcher that can turn.|overlay
      nav_bar_padding|on,off|on|Navigation bar padding|Reserve no space for the gesture bar: content reaches the bottom edge while the pill stays visible and swipeable.|overlay
      status_bar_background|on,off|on|Status bar background|Remove the shade behind the status bar, so the bar sits directly on the wallpaper or the app.|overlay
      hide_notch|on,off|off|Hide the notch|Black out the strip the notch sits in and keep every app below it, so nothing can draw under the camera.|overlay
      CATALOG_EOF
      }
      
      # Every id, one per line.
      ids() {
          catalog | while IFS='|' read -r id choices def label summary kind; do
              case "$id" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
              printf '%s\n' "$id"
          done
      }
      
      catalog_field() { # <id> <field number> -> that field, empty when unknown
          catalog | awk -F'|' -v id="$1" -v f="$2" '$1 == id { print $f; exit }'
      }
      
      choices_of() { catalog_field "$1" 2; }
      default_of() { catalog_field "$1" 3; }
      label_of()   { catalog_field "$1" 4; }
      summary_of() { catalog_field "$1" 5; }
      kind_of()    { catalog_field "$1" 6; }
      
      valid_value() { # <id> <value>
          case " $(choices_of "$1" | tr ',' ' ') " in
              *" $2 "*) return 0 ;;
          esac
          return 1
      }
      
      bad_value() { say "x $1: '$2' is not one of: $(choices_of "$1" | tr ',' '/')"; }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The saved file
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Same shape as config.env — ID=VALUE lines, '#' comments — so it can be read
      # and edited by hand. apply.sh keeps webui.conf in the module the same way.
      conf_value() { # <key> -> saved value, empty when not saved
          [ -f "$CONF" ] || return 0
          awk -v k="$1" 'index($0, k "=") == 1 { v = substr($0, length(k) + 2) } END { printf "%s", v }' "$CONF" 2>/dev/null
      }
      
      has_saved() {
          [ -f "$CONF" ] || return 1
          grep -q '^[A-Za-z]' "$CONF" 2>/dev/null
      }
      
      put_conf() { # <key> <value>
          key=$1
          val=$2
          tmp="$CONF.tmp"
          if [ -f "$CONF" ]; then
              awk -v k="$key" -v v="$val" '
                  index($0, k "=") == 1 { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done = 1 } next }
                  { print }
                  END { if (!done) print k "=" v }
              ' "$CONF" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
          else
              {
                  printf '%s\n' \
                      '# =============================================================================' \
                      '# Module addons — Treble Overlay' \
                      '# =============================================================================' \
                      '# Written by the desktop app (Addons tab) or by this module on the phone.' \
                      '# Only what is listed here is enforced, and it is enforced on every boot.' \
                      '# Remove an ID=VALUE line (or use Reset) to hand that setting back.' \
                      '# The list of addons and their values: docs/addons.md' \
                      '# ============================================================================='
                  printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$val"
              } > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
          fi
          if [ ! -f "$tmp" ] || ! mv "$tmp" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null; then
              rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
              say "x cannot write $CONF (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"
              say "  The WebUI host ran this script without write access to the module."
              return 1
          fi
          chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
          return 0
      }
      
      del_conf() { # <key>
          [ -f "$CONF" ] || return 0
          tmp="$CONF.tmp"
          awk -v k="$1" 'index($0, k "=") != 1' "$CONF" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null \
              && mv "$tmp" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null
          chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
          return 0
      }
      
      # The saved file lives in two places: the module (what this script reads) and
      # $STATE_DIR (what survives an update, because the update replaces the module).
      mirror_conf() {
          mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || return 0
          if [ -f "$CONF" ]; then
              cp "$CONF" "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
          else
              rm -f "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
          chmod 600 "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
      }
      
      # customize.sh calls this after the new zip is unpacked. The packaged file is
      # the app's latest word, so its choices win: restoring the old file over it made
      # a freshly built "hide the notch" come up unset, because the phone still had
      # the previous install's copy. Only the addons the new file does not name are
      # carried over - those are the ones chosen on the phone, which the app never
      # saw. A build that names nothing at all is a plain rebuild, so the saved file
      # is restored whole, the way it always was.
      restore_conf() {
          [ -f "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" ] || return 0
          if ! has_saved; then
              if cp "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null; then
                  chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
                  say "+ saved addons restored"
              fi
              return 0
          fi
      
          restored=0
          while IFS= read -r line; do
              key=${line%%=*}
              [ -n "$key" ] || continue
              # A line from an older catalog is not brought back (reset prunes it).
              [ -n "$(default_of "$key")" ] || continue
              [ -z "$(conf_value "$key")" ] || continue
              put_conf "$key" "${line#*=}" || return 1
              restored=$((restored + 1))
          done <<EOF
      $(grep '^[A-Za-z]' "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null)
      EOF
          [ "$restored" -gt 0 ] && say "+ $restored saved addon(s) restored"
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Settings
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      have_settings() { command -v "$SETTINGS" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
      
      setting_get() { # <namespace> <key> -> value, empty for null/absent
          have_settings || return 0
          out=$("$SETTINGS" get "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | tail -n 1)
          case "$out" in
              ""|null) printf '' ;;
              *) printf '%s' "$out" ;;
          esac
      }
      
      put() { # <addon> <namespace> <key> <value>
          if ! have_settings; then
              say "x $1: the settings command is not available on this device"
              return 1
          fi
          err=$("$SETTINGS" put "$2" "$3" "$4" 2>&1)
          if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
              say "x $1: $(printf '%s' "$err" | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ *$//')"
              return 1
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # What the device resolves right now, in the catalog's words. Empty when the
      # phone says nothing (or there is no phone — the desktop app has none).
      live_value() {
          case "$1" in
              volume_panel)
                  case "$(setting_get secure volume_panel_on_left)" in
                      1) printf left ;;
                      0) printf right ;;
                  esac ;;
              captive_portal)
                  case "$(setting_get global captive_portal_mode)" in
                      1) printf on ;;
                      0) printf off ;;
                  esac ;;
              stay_awake)
                  # The addon lives in one key: a screen timeout no UI can pick.
                  case "$(setting_get system screen_off_timeout)" in
                      2147483647) printf on ;;
                      *)          printf off ;;
                  esac ;;
              status_clock)
                  # icon_blacklist is one list for the whole bar ("clock", "rotate",
                  # ...), so the clock is hidden by being present in it, not by a
                  # value of its own.
                  case " $(setting_get secure icon_blacklist | tr ',' ' ') " in
                      *" clock "*) printf off ;;
                      *)           printf on ;;
                  esac ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # icon_blacklist carries every status bar icon SystemUI should leave out, and
      # the clock is one entry in it. Writing it for the clock therefore has to keep
      # whatever else the user (or another module) put there: a plain `put` would
      # replace the whole list. An empty result writes an empty value, which is what
      # a phone that never had the key answers anyway.
      icon_blacklist_set() { # <hide|show> the clock
          ib_list=$(setting_get secure icon_blacklist | tr ',' '\n' | awk 'NF && $0 != "clock"')
          if [ "$1" = hide ]; then
              ib_list=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ib_list" clock | awk 'NF')
          fi
          ib_value=$(printf '%s\n' "$ib_list" | awk 'NF { printf "%s%s", (n++ ? "," : ""), $0 }')
          put status_clock secure icon_blacklist "$ib_value"
      }
      
      apply_one() { # <id> <value>
          id=$1
          v=$2
          # An overlay addon is a build-time decision; the running APK cannot change
          # it, so there is nothing to put. The caller has already saved the choice.
          if [ "$(kind_of "$id")" = overlay ]; then
              return 0
          fi
          case "$id" in
              volume_panel)
                  case "$v" in
                      left)  put "$id" secure volume_panel_on_left 1 ;;
                      right) put "$id" secure volume_panel_on_left 0 ;;
                      *)     bad_value "$id" "$v"; return 1 ;;
                  esac ;;
              captive_portal)
                  case "$v" in
                      on)  put "$id" global captive_portal_mode 1 ;;
                      off) put "$id" global captive_portal_mode 0 ;;
                      *)   bad_value "$id" "$v"; return 1 ;;
                  esac ;;
              stay_awake)
                  # 2147483647 ms is the largest an int Setting can hold — about 24
                  # days, which is "until the power button" for any practical use.
                  case "$v" in
                      on)  put "$id" system screen_off_timeout 2147483647 ;;
                      off) put "$id" system screen_off_timeout 60000 ;;
                      *)   bad_value "$id" "$v"; return 1 ;;
                  esac ;;
              status_clock)
                  case "$v" in
                      on)  icon_blacklist_set show ;;
                      off) icon_blacklist_set hide ;;
                      *)   bad_value "$id" "$v"; return 1 ;;
                  esac ;;
              *)
                  say "x $id: no such addon"
                  return 1 ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Commands
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      cmd_list() { # JSON: the catalog, what is saved, what the phone resolves
          if has_saved; then saved_any=yes; else saved_any=no; fi
          if have_settings; then device=yes; else device=no; fi
          printf '{"conf":"%s","device":"%s","addons":[' "$saved_any" "$device"
          first=1
          catalog | while IFS='|' read -r id choices def label summary kind; do
              case "$id" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
              [ "$first" = 1 ] || printf ','
              first=0
              saved=$(conf_value "$id")
              if [ -n "$saved" ]; then
                  value=$saved
                  is_saved=true
              else
                  value=$def
                  is_saved=false
              fi
              printf '{"id":"%s","kind":"%s","label":"%s","summary":"%s","choices":[%s],"default":"%s","value":"%s","saved":%s,"live":"%s"}' \
                  "$id" "$kind" \
                  "$(printf '%s' "$label" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')" \
                  "$(printf '%s' "$summary" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')" \
                  "$(printf '%s' "$choices" | awk -F, '{ for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) printf "%s\"%s\"", (i > 1 ? "," : ""), $i }')" \
                  "$def" "$value" "$is_saved" "$(live_value "$id")"
          done
          printf ']}\n'
      }
```

```
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// src/webui/addons.sh — the module's addon helper
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The addons are Settings values the module writes on the phone, so the failure
// that matters is a *silent* one: a choice saved but never applied, or a value
// applied on every boot that nobody asked for. The fake `settings` below is the
// phone, so both cases can be checked here instead of by flashing.
//
// Run: node --test stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import {
  chmodSync, copyFileSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
const script = join(root, 'src', 'webui', 'addons.sh');
const template = join(root, 'src', 'module', 'addons.conf');

// Git Bash reads a backslash as an escape, so every path handed to the script
// (which is POSIX sh on every platform) is written with forward slashes.
const posix = (p) => p.replace(/\\/g, '/');

// The shipped file is also where the desktop app writes the user's picks, so a
// developer's clone often has active lines in it. These tests are about the
// script, so each one starts from the same comment-only file a fresh clone
// ships.
const pristineConf = () => readFileSync(template, 'utf8')
  .split(/\r?\n/).filter((line) => !/^[A-Za-z]/.test(line)).join('\n');

// The module as it is installed: webroot/addons.sh next to addons.conf.
function moduleTree() {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'addons-sh-'));
  mkdirSync(join(dir, 'mod', 'webroot'), { recursive: true });
  copyFileSync(script, join(dir, 'mod', 'webroot', 'addons.sh'));
  writeFileSync(join(dir, 'mod', 'addons.conf'), pristineConf());
  fakeSettings(dir);
  return dir;
}

// One flat file is the whole "device": `settings put` overwrites a key, `get`
// answers null for a key that was never written — exactly what Android does.
function fakeSettings(dir) {
  const bin = join(dir, 'bin');
  mkdirSync(bin, { recursive: true });
  const path = join(bin, 'settings');
  writeFileSync(path, `#!/bin/sh
k="$2/$3"
case "$1" in
  get)
    v=$(awk -F= -v k="$k" '$1==k {print $2}' "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE" 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$v" ] && echo "$v" || echo null ;;
  put)
    touch "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE"
    grep -v "^$k=" "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE" > "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE.new" 2>/dev/null
    mv "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE.new" "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE" 2>/dev/null
    echo "$k=$4" >> "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE" ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac
`);
  chmodSync(path, 0o755);
  return path;
}

function run(dir, args, opts = {}) {
  const settings = join(dir, 'bin', 'settings');

      cwd: dir,

        ADDONS_SETTINGS: posix(settings),
        ADDONS_STATE_DIR: posix(join(dir, 'state')),
        FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE: posix(join(dir, 'store.txt')),
        ...opts.env,
```

```
- path: gui/git.go
  content: |
      package main
      
      import (
        "context"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "time"
      )
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Why the app looks at git at all
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The window is a launcher for build.sh, so "is there a newer version of the
      // thing I am running" is a real question: an update can add a resource, fix a
      // build rule or change config.env. The header used to say "working tree has
      // uncommitted changes", which answers a question nobody asked — editing
      // config.env is the point of the app. What it says now is whether a newer
      // release exists, and what pulling one would do to the user's own edits.
      //
      // The danger the old label was hiding: `git pull` in a clone with local edits
      // either refuses ("would be overwritten by merge") or, worse, conflicts inside
      // config.env — which is sourced by bash, so conflict markers are not a
      // cosmetic problem. So the update is split in two:
      //
      //  check  — fetch, count commits behind, and list which of those files the
      //           user has also edited (the "clash");
      //  pull   — refuse when there is a clash, unless the caller asked to back the
      //           clashing files up first, in which case they are copied to
      //           stuff/backups/pre-update-<time>/ before being reset to HEAD.
      //
      // Nothing here runs on a timer the user cannot see: the window checks once at
      // startup and then every ten minutes, all of it asynchronous.
      type UpdateInfo struct {
        Checked   bool     `json:"checked"`
        Available bool     `json:"available"`
        Behind    int      `json:"behind"`
        Ahead     int      `json:"ahead"`
        Branch    string   `json:"branch"`
        Upstream  string   `json:"upstream"`
        Files     []string `json:"files"`
        Dirty     []string `json:"dirty"`
        Clash     []string `json:"clash"`
        // ConfigChanges is why config.env is special: it is a file the user is
        // expected to edit, so an update that rewrites it needs to say which
        // settings move, not just that the file changed.
        ConfigChanges []string `json:"configChanges"`
        CheckedAt     int64    `json:"checkedAt"`
        Error         string   `json:"error"`
      }
      
      // gitEnv keeps git from ever waiting for input: the app has no terminal, so a
      // credential prompt would hang the check until the timeout with no hint why.
      func gitEnv() []string {
        return append(os.Environ(),
          "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0",
          "GIT_ASKPASS=",
          "SSH_ASKPASS=",
          "GCM_INTERACTIVE=never",
        )
      }
      
      func gitRun(root string, timeout time.Duration, args ...string) (string, error) {
        if root == "" || !dirExists(filepath.Join(root, ".git")) {
          return "", errors.New("not a git checkout")
        }
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeout)
        defer cancel()
      
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", append([]string{"-C", root}, args...)...)
        cmd.Env = gitEnv()
        cmd.Stdin = nil
        setProcAttr(cmd)
        out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
        // Only the line endings go: `git status --porcelain` puts meaning in a
        // leading space (" M file" is modified, "M  file" is staged), so trimming
        // the whole output would shift the first line and slice a character off the
        // first path.
        text := strings.TrimRight(string(out), "\r\n")
        if err != nil {
          if text == "" {
            text = err.Error()
          }
          return text, errors.New(text)
        }
        return text, nil
      }
      
      // gitInfo is best effort: a tarball unpack has no .git and that is fine.
      func gitInfo(root string) (branch, commit string, dirty bool) {
        if root == "" || !dirExists(filepath.Join(root, ".git")) {
          return "", "", false
        }
        branch, _ = gitRun(root, 3*time.Second, "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
        commit, _ = gitRun(root, 3*time.Second, "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD")
        paths, _ := dirtyPaths(root)
        dirty = len(paths) > 0
        return branch, commit, dirty
      }
      
      // dirtyPaths is every path the working tree has changed, added or deleted —
      // staged or not. The shape is "MM path" from --porcelain, one per line.
      func dirtyPaths(root string) ([]string, error) {
        out, err := gitRun(root, 5*time.Second, "status", "--porcelain")
        if err != nil {
          return nil, err
        }
        var paths []string
        for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
          if len(line) < 4 {
            continue
          }
          // Renames read "R  old -> new"; the new name is what a pull touches.
          path := strings.TrimSpace(line[3:])
          if i := strings.Index(path, " -> "); i >= 0 {
            path = path[i+4:]
          }
          path = strings.Trim(path, `"`)
          if path != "" {
            paths = append(paths, filepath.ToSlash(path))
          }
        }
        return paths, nil
      }
      
      // checkUpdate answers "is there something newer upstream, and would pulling it
      // step on what I edited". It fetches, so it can be slow or fail offline; every
      // caller must be able to live with Error being set.
      func checkUpdate(root string) UpdateInfo {
        info := UpdateInfo{CheckedAt: time.Now().Unix()}
        if root == "" || !dirExists(filepath.Join(root, ".git")) {
          info.Error = "not a git checkout"
          return info
        }
      
        upstream, err := gitRun(root, 5*time.Second, "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "--symbolic-full-name", "@{u}")
        if err != nil || upstream == "" || upstream == "@{u}" {
          info.Error = "this branch has no upstream to compare against"
          return info
        }
        info.Upstream = upstream
        info.Branch, _ = gitRun(root, 5*time.Second, "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
      
        if out, err := gitRun(root, 30*time.Second, "fetch", "--quiet", "--prune"); err != nil {
          info.Error = "could not reach the remote: " + firstLine(out)
          return info
        }
      
        counts, err := gitRun(root, 10*time.Second, "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", "HEAD..."+upstream)
        if err != nil {
          info.Error = firstLine(counts)
          return info
        }
        fields := strings.Fields(counts)
        if len(fields) == 2 {
          // left = commits only HEAD has (ahead), right = only the upstream has.
          info.Ahead, _ = strconv.Atoi(fields[0])
          info.Behind, _ = strconv.Atoi(fields[1])
        }
      
        dirty, _ := dirtyPaths(root)
        info.Dirty = dirty
      
        if info.Behind > 0 {
          info.Available = true
          changed, err := gitRun(root, 15*time.Second, "diff", "--name-only", "HEAD.."+upstream)
          if err == nil {
            for _, line := range strings.Split(changed, "\n") {
              line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
              if line != "" {
                info.Files = append(info.Files, filepath.ToSlash(line))
              }
            }
          }
          info.Clash = intersect(info.Dirty, info.Files)
          for _, f := range info.Files {
            if f == "config.env" {
              info.ConfigChanges = configKeyDiff(root, upstream)
              break
            }
          }
        }
      
        info.Checked = true
        return info
      }
      
      // configKeyDiff lists the settings a config.env update rewrites, as the diff's
      // own -/+ lines. Those are the values the user has to look at again after the
      // pull, so they are worth showing before it happens.
      func configKeyDiff(root, upstream string) []string {
        out, err := gitRun(root, 15*time.Second, "diff", "--unified=0", "HEAD.."+upstream, "--", "config.env")
        if err != nil {
          return nil
        }
        var changes []string
        for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
          if len(line) == 0 {
            continue
          }
          sign := line[0]
          if sign != '-' && sign != '+' {
            continue
          }
          body := strings.TrimPrefix(line, string(sign))
          if strings.HasPrefix(body, "--") || strings.HasPrefix(body, "++") {
            continue
          }
          if configKey.FindStringSubmatch(body) == nil {
            continue
          }
          changes = append(changes, string(sign)+" "+strings.TrimSpace(body))
          if len(changes) >= 24 {
            changes = append(changes, "…")
            break
          }
        }
        return changes
      }
      
      func intersect(a, b []string) []string {
        set := make(map[string]struct{}, len(b))
        for _, s := range b {
          set[s] = struct{}{}
        }
        var both []string
        for _, s := range a {
          if _, ok := set[s]; ok {
            both = append(both, s)
          }
        }
        return both
      }
      
      func firstLine(s string) string {
        if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
          s = s[:i]
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(s)
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Pulling
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // pullResult is what the dialog shows after the attempt, including the reason
      // when there is nothing to show but an error.
      type pullResult struct {
        Output   string   `json:"output"`
        BackedUp []string `json:"backedUp"`
        Changed  []string `json:"changed"`
        Restart  bool     `json:"restart"`
      }
      
      // errClash is returned when pulling would overwrite local edits and the caller
      // did not agree to back them up first. The caller turns it into the dialog that
      // lists the files; it is not a crash.
      var errClash = errors.New("local changes would be overwritten")
      
      // pullUpdate fast-forwards the clone to its upstream.
      //
      // backupClash is the user's answer to the dialog: copy my versions of the
      // files that would be overwritten into stuff/backups/, then let git replace them. Any
      // edit that does not collide survives untouched — a plain `git pull --ff-only`
      // keeps those, which is why this is not implemented as a stash.
      func (a *App) pullUpdate(backupClash bool) (pullResult, error) {
        var res pullResult
        root := a.Root()
        if root == "" {
          return res, errors.New("no clone selected")
        }
      
        info := checkUpdate(root)
        if info.Error != "" {
          return res, errors.New(info.Error)
        }
        if !info.Available {
          return res, errors.New("already up to date")
        }
        if len(info.Clash) > 0 && !backupClash {
          return res, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", errClash, strings.Join(info.Clash, ", "))
        }
      
        for _, rel := range info.Clash {
          saved, err := backupPath(root, rel)
          if err != nil {
            return res, err
          }
          res.BackedUp = append(res.BackedUp, saved)
          // Tracked: go back to the committed version so the pull can land.
          // Untracked: a pull would simply refuse, so move it aside (it is in
          // stuff/backups/ now) — otherwise the update can never be applied.
          if _, err := gitRun(root, 10*time.Second, "ls-files", "--error-unmatch", rel); err == nil {
            if out, err := gitRun(root, 10*time.Second, "checkout", "HEAD", "--", rel); err != nil {
              return res, fmt.Errorf("could not reset %s: %s", rel, firstLine(out))
            }
          } else if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(rel))); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
            return res, fmt.Errorf("could not move %s aside: %w", rel, err)
          }
        }
      
        out, err := gitRun(root, 120*time.Second, "pull", "--ff-only")
        res.Output = out
        // A pull that printed conflict text is a failure even if git's exit code
        // says otherwise; --ff-only makes that unlikely, but not impossible when a
        // patch was applied by the remote.
        if err != nil {
          return res, errors.New(firstLine(out))
        }
      
        res.Changed = info.Files
        for _, f := range res.Changed {
          if strings.HasPrefix(f, "gui/") || f == "go.mod" || f == "go.sum" {
            // The running binary is the old one; build.sh itself is read fresh
            // from disk on the next run, so only the window has to restart.
            res.Restart = true
          }
        }
      
        a.invalidateUpdate()
        return res, nil
      }
      
      // backupPath copies one file from the clone into stuff/backups/pre-update-<time>/,
      // keeping its relative path so two files with the same name cannot collide.
      func backupPath(root, rel string) (string, error) {
        src := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(rel))
        stamp := time.Now().Format("2006-01-02-150405")
        dst := filepath.Join(root, "stuff", "backups", "pre-update-"+stamp, filepath.FromSlash(rel))
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
          return "", err
        }
        if err := copyFile(src, dst); err != nil {
          return "", fmt.Errorf("could not back up %s: %w", rel, err)
        }
        return filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join("stuff", "backups", "pre-update-"+stamp, filepath.FromSlash(rel))), nil
      }
      
      func copyFile(src, dst string) error {
        in, err := os.Open(src)
        if err != nil {
          return err
        }
        defer in.Close()
      
        out, err := os.Create(dst)
        if err != nil {
          return err
        }
        if _, err := io.Copy(out, in); err != nil {
          out.Close()
          return err
        }
        return out.Close()
      }
```
