````
===
# gui/ — the desktop launcher

A Go program that finds a clone, finds bash, and runs `build.sh` for you.

The module lives at the repository root (`../go.mod`) so a checkout is one Go
project, but every source file is here and `go build ./gui` works from the
root. The CLI still needs no Go toolchain: `build.sh` never touches this
folder.

**User documentation lives in [../docs/gui.md](../docs/gui.md).** This file is
for working on the app itself.

## Shape

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `main.go` | flags, wiring, shutdown; no logic |
| `app.go` | settings, clone and bash discovery, the verb table, state for the UI |
| `run.go` | one console: the child process (or in-process job), its log ring buffer and subscribers, plus `Gate`, the one-job-at-a-time token the two consoles share |
| `git.go` | update check (`git fetch` + behind/ahead + which local edits collide) and the safe pull |
| `configfile.go` | the config.env parser and the line-wise writer behind the form |
| `files.go` | the src/ workspace: safe relative paths, listing, read/write, upload, delete, and "disable" as a move into `src/.disabled/` — plus the sepolicy and VINTF checks |
| `adb.go` | adb discovery, the platform-tools download/unzip, the command tokenizer and the presets |
| `server.go` | loopback HTTP handlers, the two log streams (`/api/log`, `/api/adb/log`), embed of `ui/`, token prefix |
| `proc_windows.go` | Git Bash discovery, `taskkill /T`, Explorer, WebView2 host |
| `proc_unix.go` | `/bin/bash`, process-group kill, `xdg-open` |
| `window_cgo.go` | the native window (`//go:build cgo && (windows || linux)`) |
| `window_no_cgo.go` | same program, browser instead (`//go:build !cgo …`) |
| `icon.go`, `icon.ico` | the app mark, embedded for the window icon |
| `icon_windows.go` | `setWindowIcon`: `WM_SETICON` on the window WebView2 created |
| `icon_other.go` | the same call, doing nothing (the GTK window keeps its own) |
| `browser.go` | opens the UI in the default browser and waits for Ctrl+C |
| `pick.go` | the file-chooser endpoint (`/api/pick`) and the path arithmetic behind it |
| `pick_windows.go` | the Windows dialog, PowerShell's `OpenFileDialog` / `FolderBrowserDialog` |
| `pick_unix.go` | the Linux dialog: `zenity`, then `kdialog` |
| `ui/` | one page, one stylesheet, one script; no bundler, no `node_modules` |
| `*_test.go` | argv, clone discovery, config round trip, adb parsing, update/pull against a temp git repo |
| `build.sh`, `build.cmd` | build the app |
| `../treble-rro-creator.sh`, `../treble-rro-creator.cmd` | build-if-needed and launch; what users actually run |
| `../go.mod`, `../go.sum` | the module, at the root so the whole clone is one Go project |

The UI is embedded with `go:embed`, so a released binary is a single file. Docs
are **not** embedded: they are read from the clone at run time, because the app
is installed into a clone anyway and a second copy would drift.

## Build and run

```bash
./treble-rro-creator.sh                    # build if stale, then launch — the normal path
./treble-rro-creator.sh --rebuild          # force a build first
./treble-rro-creator.sh --detach           # accepted for scripts; the hand-off is the default
./gui/build.sh              # build only (console build, for debugging)
./gui/build.sh --release    # stripped; no console window on Windows
gui\build.cmd --release     # same from cmd/PowerShell
```

| Platform | Needs |
|---|---|
| Windows | Go 1.23+ and MinGW-w64 gcc (both downloaded into `stuff/tools/` when missing), Git for Windows at run time |
| Linux | Go 1.23+ (downloaded into `stuff/tools/_go/` when missing, or skipped when the distro's is too old), plus gcc, pkg-config and the GTK3/WebKitGTK headers — installed automatically with apt, pacman or dnf when missing (4.1 is shimmed to the 4.0 name webview_go asks for) |

`CGO_ENABLED=0 ./gui/build.sh` builds without a C compiler and without
WebKitGTK; the app then serves the same UI to the default browser instead of a
window. That is the only difference — same handlers, same behaviour.

### Why there is no cross-compilation

`CGO_ENABLED=1` cannot cross-compile without a full target toolchain: the
Windows build needs MinGW, the Linux build needs a Linux gcc plus WebKitGTK.
Each release target is therefore built on its own runner, which is also the only
way to know the binary links. A `CGO_ENABLED=0` build *can* cross-compile:

```bash
CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 go build -o dist/gui-linux-arm64 .
```
````

```
===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Everything that can be checked without Android tools
# =============================================================================
# CI runs this on every push (see .github/workflows/check.yml), and it is worth
# running before a release:
#
#   bash stuff/tests/run.sh
#
# 1. shell syntax of every shipped script (bash -n / sh -n, no execution)
# 2. the WebUI resource-table writer against stuff/tests/fixtures/*.apk
# 3. the WebUI manifest and the overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off
#    vendor_hardware_overlay), built from
#    resource XML that stuff/tests/gen-res.sh generates into a temp directory (so
#    a fresh clone needs no build first)
# 4. every relative link and #anchor in the docs
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."

status=0
step() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$*"; }

step "shell syntax"
for f in build.sh treble-rro-creator.sh gui/build.sh stuff/scripts/*.sh stuff/tests/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if bash -n "$f"; then :; else echo "bash -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
done
# apply.sh, addons.sh and the module scripts run under Android's mksh
# (/system/bin/sh).
for f in src/webui/apply.sh src/webui/addons.sh src/module/*.sh stuff/templates/*.sh stuff/templates/recoveries/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if command -v sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if sh -n "$f"; then :; else echo "sh -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
    fi
done
[ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all scripts parse"

# The bug this guards: `clean --all` copied config.env from a frozen file, so a
# full clean handed back a version from an older commit. The copies below are
# now only the no-.git fallback, so they must equal the committed blob — not the
# working file, because local edits to config.env are normal.
step "template fallbacks match the release"
if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    copy_status=0
    check_copy() {
        local rel="$1" copy="$2"
        if [ ! -f "$copy" ]; then
            echo "missing fallback: $copy"
            copy_status=1
        elif ! git show "HEAD:$rel" | diff -q - "$copy" >/dev/null; then
            echo "$copy differs from HEAD:$rel — run: git show HEAD:$rel > $copy"
            copy_status=1
        fi
    }
    check_copy config.env stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    check_copy src/module/sepolicy.rule stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
    if [ "$copy_status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "fallbacks match"; else status=1; fi
else
    echo "not a git checkout — skipping"
fi

# restore_from_release() is what clean.sh and build.sh call. Run it against a
# throwaway repository with a deliberately stale fallback, and once without
# .git, because "start over" silently returning old values is the failure mode.
step "restore picks the release, not the stale copy"
restore_here="$(pwd)"
restore_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-restore)"
if (
    cd "$restore_tmp" || exit 1
    git init -q . && git config user.email t@example.com && git config user.name t || exit 1
    # No .gitattributes here, and Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true,
    # which would check the file back out with CRLF and fail the greps below.
    git config core.autocrlf false
    mkdir -p src/module stuff/templates/recoveries
    printf 'KEY="released"\n' > config.env
    printf 'released rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
    printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule

```

```
===
package main

// ============================================================================
// Which property should the submitted overlay match on?
// ============================================================================
// A static RRO for the overlay repo matches with android:requiredSystemProperty
// Name/Value, compared with plain string equality. Getting it wrong is silent:
// the overlay installs, `cmd overlay list` shows it enabled, and nothing changes.
//
// Two things decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable from the
// phone without root:
//
//   * zygote has to be able to read the property. A zygote overlay is matched
//     while zygote preloads the framework, so a property in a SELinux area
//     zygote is denied reads as empty and the condition never holds. `getprop -Z`
//     prints the area (build_prop and build_vendor_prop are the safe ones,
//     build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps).
//   * the value has to name this device and survive what is installed. The
//     vendor, odm and bootimage partitions keep the OEM value under a GSI;
//     /system, /product and /system_ext are replaced, so ro.product.device on a
//     GSI holds the GSI's own name (phh_treble, mivendor, …).
//
// Neither rule alone is enough — on a GSI the surviving property is often the
// one zygote cannot read, and the readable one has been renamed — so this ranks
// every candidate, says what each one is gambling on, and refuses to call a
// winner when no property actually carries the codename. The values below are
// what the reference phones report: Samsung SM-A908N (everything is r3q) and
// Xiaomi 26012RN62A (ro.product.device is zephyr, but its vendor property is the
// shared mivendor and build.product is missi).

import (
  "regexp"
  "sort"
  "strings"
)

// What a codename looks like: lower case, no separators bash would eat, short
// enough to be a name rather than a build string.
var codenameShape = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,23}$`)

// MatchCandidate is one property the submission could be matched on.
type MatchCandidate struct {
  Prop  string `json:"prop"`
  Value string `json:"value"`
  Score int    `json:"score"`
  Zone  string `json:"zone"`
  Label string `json:"label"`
  Trust string `json:"trust"` // high, medium, low
  // Perfect means this is a pick nothing has to be argued about: the value
  // is the codename, zygote can read the property, and a GSI leaves it alone.
  // Only a perfect pick is offered as the answer; anything less and the card
  // tells the user to keep the match they already have.
  Perfect bool   `json:"perfect"`
  Why     string `json:"why"`
  Risk    string `json:"risk,omitempty"`
}

// MatchRejection is a property with a device-ish name that was ruled out, and
// why. The reasons are the answers to the question users ask most often, so
// they are part of the answer rather than something to work out again.
type MatchRejection struct {
  Prop   string `json:"prop"`
  Value  string `json:"value"`
  Reason string `json:"reason"`
}

// MatchReport is what the Config tab shows: the codename it settled on, the
// ranked candidates, the properties it refused, and how sure it is.
type MatchReport struct {
  Serial     string           `json:"serial"`
  Model      string           `json:"model"`
  Codename   string           `json:"codename"`
  Confidence string           `json:"confidence"` // high, medium, low
  ModuleProp string           `json:"moduleProp"`
  Candidates []MatchCandidate `json:"candidates"`
  Rejected   []MatchRejection `json:"rejected"`
}

// matchProp is one entry of the fixed candidate list. zone says which partition
// the value comes from (that is what decides GSI survival) and kind says what
// the property holds.
type matchProp struct {
  name string
  zone string
  kind string
}

var matchPropCandidates = []matchProp{
  {"ro.product.vendor.device", "vendor", "device"},
  {"ro.product.odm.device", "odm", "device"},
  {"ro.product.bootimage.device", "bootimage", "device"},
  {"ro.product.device", "system", "device"},
  {"ro.product.product.device", "product", "device"},
  {"ro.product.system.device", "system", "device"},
  {"ro.product.system_ext.device", "system_ext", "device"},
  {"ro.build.product", "build", "device"},
  {"ro.product.vendor.name", "vendor", "name"},
  {"ro.product.odm.name", "odm", "name"},
  {"ro.product.bootimage.name", "bootimage", "name"},
  {"ro.product.name", "product", "name"},
  {"ro.product.vendor.model", "vendor", "model"},
  {"ro.product.model", "product", "model"},
}

// zoneScore: vendor/odm/bootimage keep the OEM value when a GSI replaces
// /system; a `ro.product.*` value is whatever is installed now.
var zoneScore = map[string]int{
  "vendor": 40, "odm": 35, "bootimage": 35,
  "product": 25, "system": 22, "system_ext": 18, "build": 10,
}

var kindScore = map[string]int{"device": 25, "name": 12, "model": 15}

// labelScore: what the SELinux area means for zygote reading it. The negative
// numbers are the documented traps, not guesses — build_bootimage_prop and
// build_odm_prop are refused to zygote on most GSI builds.
var labelScore = map[string]int{
  "build_prop":           30,
  "build_vendor_prop":    30,
  "vendor_default_prop":  25,
  "default_prop":         15,
  "build_system_prop":    -20,
  "build_odm_prop":       -35,
  "build_bootimage_prop": -35,
  "bootloader_prop":      -20,
}

// Values that name a build rather than a device. They are the reason a "looks
// like a codename" filter is not enough: mivendor is a Xiaomi vendor tree shared
// by a whole family, generic is the GSI itself, qcom is a SoC vendor.
var genericMatchValues = map[string]string{
  "generic":        "the AOSP/GSI build name, shared by every generic image",
  "generic_x86":    "the AOSP/GSI build name, shared by every generic image",
  "generic_arm64":  "the AOSP/GSI build name, shared by every generic image",
  "generic_x86_64": "the AOSP/GSI build name, shared by every generic image",
  "aosp":           "an AOSP build name, not a device",
  "aosp_arm64":     "an AOSP build name, not a device",
  "mainline":       "the mainline/module build name, not a device",
  "treble":         "the Treble build name, not a device",
  "phh_treble":     "the GSI's own name — present on every device running that GSI",
  "mivendor":       "Xiaomi's vendor build name — shared by many Xiaomi devices, not a codename",
  "emulator":       "an emulator, not a phone",
  "unknown":        "no value",
  "qcom":           "a SoC vendor, shared by every Qualcomm device",
  "mediatek":       "a SoC vendor, shared by every MediaTek device",
  "mtk":            "a SoC vendor, shared by every MediaTek device",
  "exynos":         "a SoC vendor, shared by every Exynos device",
  "android":        "not a device name",
}

// rankMatchProps turns a phone's `getprop` and `getprop -Z` output into ranked
// candidates. Both maps are keyed by property name; a missing value or label is
// simply an empty string, because adb output loses lines on some ROMs.
func rankMatchProps(values, labels map[string]string) MatchReport {
  report := MatchReport{
    Candidates: []MatchCandidate{},
    Rejected:   []MatchRejection{},
  }

  brand := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(values["ro.product.brand"]))

```

```
- path: gui/matchprop.go
  content: |
        brand := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(values["ro.product.brand"]))
        manufacturer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(values["ro.product.manufacturer"]))
        report.Model = strings.TrimSpace(values["ro.product.model"])
      
        // Phase 1: what is this phone called? Partition order is the rule, not a sum:
        // vendor, odm and bootimage are the OEM's own naming and are what a GSI leaves
        // alone, while /system, /product and /system_ext hold the ROM's name (on a
        // GSI that is the GSI itself: generic, phh_treble, mivendor). A value the OEM
        // partitions agree on is the codename; the later props are only consulted
        // when those are empty or generic.
        codenameOrder := []string{
          "ro.product.vendor.device",
          "ro.product.odm.device",
          "ro.product.bootimage.device",
          "ro.product.device",
          "ro.product.system.device",
          "ro.product.product.device",
          "ro.product.system_ext.device",
          "ro.build.product",
        }
        codename := ""
        codenameProp := ""
        for _, name := range codenameOrder {
          value := strings.TrimSpace(values[name])
          if value == "" || genericMatchValues[strings.ToLower(value)] != "" {
            continue
          }
          if !codenameShape.MatchString(value) {
            continue
          }
          if value == brand || value == manufacturer {
            continue
          }
          codename, codenameProp = value, name
          break
        }
        report.Codename = codename
      
        // Phase 2: rank every property against that answer.
        for _, p := range matchPropCandidates {
          value := strings.TrimSpace(values[p.name])
          if value == "" {
            continue
          }
          label := shortPropertyLabel(labels[p.name])
          if reason := genericMatchValues[strings.ToLower(value)]; reason != "" {
            report.Rejected = append(report.Rejected, MatchRejection{
              Prop: p.name, Value: value, Reason: reason,
            })
            continue
          }
          if brand != "" && strings.EqualFold(value, brand) {
            report.Rejected = append(report.Rejected, MatchRejection{
              Prop: p.name, Value: value,
              Reason: "the brand, not the device — it would match every phone of this make",
            })
            continue
          }
      
          c := MatchCandidate{
            Prop:  p.name,
            Value: value,
            Zone:  p.zone,
            Label: label,
          }
          c.Score = zoneScore[p.zone] + kindScore[p.kind] + labelScore[label]
      
          var why, risk []string
          switch p.zone {
          case "vendor", "odm", "bootimage":
            why = append(why, "lives on /"+p.zone+", which a GSI leaves alone")
          default:
            why = append(why, "read from the installed /"+p.zone+" partition")
            risk = append(risk, "a GSI replaces /"+p.zone+", so the value changes and the match stops")
          }
          switch label {
          case "build_prop", "build_vendor_prop", "vendor_default_prop", "default_prop":
            why = append(why, "zygote can read "+label)
          case "":
            risk = append(risk, "this ROM did not report its SELinux area, so readability is unchecked")
          default:
            risk = append(risk, label+" is often denied to zygote — the overlay can show as enabled and do nothing")
          }
          if codename != "" && value == codename {
            c.Score += 30
            why = append(why, "holds the codename")
            if p.name == codenameProp {
              c.Score += 10
            }
          } else if codename != "" && strings.Contains(value, codename) {
            c.Score += 10
            why = append(why, "contains the codename")
          } else {
            // The missi case: a property that names this build, not this phone.
            // Matching on it would claim a different device, so every such row
            // ranks below the ones that carry the codename.
            c.Score -= 20
            if p.kind == "device" {
              risk = append(risk, "holds a different name ("+value+") than this phone's codename ("+codename+")")
            } else {
              risk = append(risk, "does not hold the codename, so it names this variant rather than the device")
            }
          }
          if codenameShape.MatchString(value) {
            c.Score += 10
          } else {
            c.Score -= 5
            if strings.ContainsRune(value, ' ') {
              risk = append(risk, "contains a space — exact matching works, but it is easy to break while editing")
            }
          }
          if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), "global") {
            c.Score -= 10
            risk = append(risk, "has a region suffix, so another region's build would not match")
          }
          if p.zone == "system" && strings.HasSuffix(p.name, ".device") && value == codename && label == "build_prop" {
            // This is the normal, good answer on a stock ROM: say so instead of
            // making the user read the /system risk as a deal-breaker.
            risk = []string{"if a GSI is installed later this property becomes the GSI's name"}
          }
      
          c.Why = strings.Join(why, " · ")
          c.Risk = strings.Join(risk, " · ")
          c.Perfect = codename != "" && value == codename && p.kind == "device" &&
            readableByZygote(label) && survivesGSI(p.zone)
          switch {
          case c.Perfect:
            c.Trust = "high"
          case value == codename:
            c.Trust = "medium"
          default:
            c.Trust = "low"
          }
          report.Candidates = append(report.Candidates, c)
        }
      
        sort.SliceStable(report.Candidates, func(i, j int) bool {
          a, b := report.Candidates[i], report.Candidates[j]
          if a.Score != b.Score {
            return a.Score > b.Score
          }
          // Same score: the one that actually carries the codename is the more
          // useful row, and after that the order only has to be stable.
          if (a.Value == codename) != (b.Value == codename) {
            return a.Value == codename
          }
          return a.Prop < b.Prop
        })
      
        // Confidence is about the answer, not the ranking. "high" is reserved for a
        // property that satisfies every rule at once (readable by zygote, carries the
        // codename, survives a GSI); anything less and the honest advice is to keep
        // the match that already works, because a submitted condition that does not
        // hold is invisible.
        report.Confidence = "low"
        if len(report.Candidates) > 0 {
          top := report.Candidates[0]
          switch {
          case top.Perfect:
            report.Confidence = "high"
          case top.Value == codename && codename != "":
            report.Confidence = "medium"
          }
        }
        if codename != "" {
          report.ModuleProp = "persist.sys.overlay." + strings.ToLower(codename)
        }
        return report
      }
      
      // survivesGSI: a property in these areas keeps the OEM value after a GSI flash.
      func survivesGSI(zone string) bool {
        switch zone {
        case "vendor", "odm", "bootimage":
          return true
        }
        return false
      }
      
      func readableByZygote(label string) bool {
        switch label {
        case "build_prop", "build_vendor_prop", "vendor_default_prop", "default_prop":
          return true
        }
        return false
      }
      
      // shortPropertyLabel turns "u:object_r:build_vendor_prop:s0" into
      // "build_vendor_prop", which is the part that means something here.
      func shortPropertyLabel(label string) string {
        parts := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(label), ":")
        if len(parts) >= 3 {
          return parts[2]
        }
        return ""
      }
      
      // parseGetprop reads `getprop` output: one `[key]: [value]` per line. Lines that
      // do not fit are skipped — some ROMs print warnings into the same stream.
      func parseGetprop(out string) map[string]string {
        props := map[string]string{}
        for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
          line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r")
          key, rest, ok := strings.Cut(line, "]: [")
          if !ok || !strings.HasPrefix(key, "[") || !strings.HasSuffix(rest, "]") {
            continue
          }
          props[strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(key, "["))] = strings.TrimSuffix(rest, "]")
        }
        return props
      }
      
      // parseGetpropLabels reads `getprop -Z`: `[key]: [u:object_r:xyz_prop:s0]`.
      func parseGetpropLabels(out string) map[string]string {
        return parseGetprop(out)
      }
```

````
# Termux (Android)

You can build the overlay on the phone itself. The toolchain is the same; only
the install step differs.

> Use Termux from **[F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/en/packages/com.termux/)**.
> The Google Play version is outdated and its packages are incompatible.

---

## 1. Prepare Termux

```bash
termux-setup-storage

apt update
apt upgrade -y

apt install -y git aapt aapt2 apksigner android-tools openjdk-17 \
               unzip zip curl tsu
```

If `pkg install` fails with signature or mirror errors, run
`termux-change-repo`, pick a mirror close to you, then repeat `apt update`.

> **`zipalign` comes from the `aapt` package, not from `aapt2`.** Installing
> `aapt2`, `apksigner` and `android-tools` leaves `zipalign` missing; adding
> `aapt` provides it. If it is still absent, `build.sh` continues and copies
> the APK instead of aligning it (valid, just not mmap-aligned) and tells you
> to run `pkg install aapt`.

---

## 2. Clone into the home directory

```bash
cd ~
git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
cd treble-rro-creator
```

> ⚠ **Do not clone into `/sdcard`.** Android's shared storage does not support
> executable permissions or the symlinks `aapt2`/`zipalign` need. Use `~`
> (`/data/data/com.termux/files/home`).

---

## 3. Build

```bash
./build.sh
```

The first run checks the toolchain. If something is missing it installs it
(aapt2/zipalign/apksigner via `pkg`, `framework-res.apk` by download), then
builds. To choose things yourself:

```bash
./build.sh setup     # [3] Android / Termux, then [1] Android 13 resources
./build.sh doctor    # verify
./build.sh check     # validate config.env only
```

If `build.sh` cannot install packages unattended, it prints the exact command
to run. `./build.sh setup` walks through the options interactively.

---

## 4. Edit the config

Use a text editor in Termux:

```bash
nano config.env
```

`Ctrl+O` then `Enter` saves, `Ctrl+X` exits. Or edit the same file with
MT Manager at:

```
````

>    - `m_cfg_get KEY` → value of last active line `KEY=` (strip quotes). (For detect currently uses active only.)
>    - `m_cfg_set KEY VALUE [on|off]` → in-place line edit, preserving quote style and comments; enable/disable comment.
>    - `m_cfg_note KEY` → comment block above the key (max ~8 lines).
>    - `m_cfg_sections` → parse `# ── Title ───` lines...
>    - `m_cfg_entries` → prints line|key|value|enabled.
> 
>    Implementation with awk for robust parsing:
>    ```
>    m_cfg_entries() {
>      awk '
>        match($0, /^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)=/) ...
>      '
>    }
>    ```
>    Simpler: use bash regex on each line:
>    ```
>    while IFS= read -r line; do
>      n=$((n+1))
>      active=1; body=$line
>      if [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]]; then active=0; body=${line#*#}; fi
>      if [[ $body =~ ^[[:space:]]*([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]]; then
>         key=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}; raw=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
>         ...
>      fi
>    done < "$file"
>    ```
>    But bash reading file in a while loop of a subshell (piped) loses state; use process substitution.
> 
>    Quoting: value may be `"..."` or `'...'` or bare. `m_cfg_unquote raw` strips surrounding quotes. Keep `quote` char to re-emit.
> 
>    Comments: config.env uses `#` comments above. Note display: collect preceding comment lines; for a compact UI show only when asked ("i").

```
- path: stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // src/webui/addons.sh — the module's addon helper
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The addons are Settings values the module writes on the phone, so the failure
      // that matters is a *silent* one: a choice saved but never applied, or a value
      // applied on every boot that nobody asked for. The fake `settings` below is the
      // phone, so both cases can be checked here instead of by flashing.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import {
        chmodSync, copyFileSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync,
      } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const script = join(root, 'src', 'webui', 'addons.sh');
      const template = join(root, 'src', 'module', 'addons.conf');
      
      // Git Bash reads a backslash as an escape, so every path handed to the script
      // (which is POSIX sh on every platform) is written with forward slashes.
      const posix = (p) => p.replace(/\\/g, '/');
      
      // The shipped file is also where the desktop app writes the user's picks, so a
      // developer's clone often has active lines in it. These tests are about the
      // script, so each one starts from the same comment-only file a fresh clone
      // ships.
      const pristineConf = () => readFileSync(template, 'utf8')
        .split(/\r?\n/).filter((line) => !/^[A-Za-z]/.test(line)).join('\n');
      
      // The module as it is installed: webroot/addons.sh next to addons.conf.
      function moduleTree() {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'addons-sh-'));
        mkdirSync(join(dir, 'mod', 'webroot'), { recursive: true });
        copyFileSync(script, join(dir, 'mod', 'webroot', 'addons.sh'));
        writeFileSync(join(dir, 'mod', 'addons.conf'), pristineConf());
        fakeSettings(dir);
        return dir;
      }
      
      // One flat file is the whole "device": `settings put` overwrites a key, `get`
      // answers null for a key that was never written — exactly what Android does.
      function fakeSettings(dir) {
        const bin = join(dir, 'bin');
        mkdirSync(bin, { recursive: true });
        const path = join(bin, 'settings');
        writeFileSync(path, `#!/bin/sh
      k="$2/$3"
      case "$1" in
        get)
          v=$(awk -F= -v k="$k" '$1==k {print $2}' "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE" 2>/dev/null)
          [ -n "$v" ] && echo "$v" || echo null ;;
        put)
          touch "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE"
          grep -v "^$k=" "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE" > "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE.new" 2>/dev/null
          mv "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE.new" "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE" 2>/dev/null
          echo "$k=$4" >> "$FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE" ;;
        *) exit 1 ;;
      esac
      `);
        chmodSync(path, 0o755);
        return path;
      }
      
      function run(dir, args, opts = {}) {
        const settings = join(dir, 'bin', 'settings');
        try {
          const out = execFileSync('sh', [posix(join(dir, 'mod', 'webroot', 'addons.sh')), ...args], {
            cwd: dir,
            encoding: 'utf8',
            env: {
              ...process.env,
              ADDONS_SETTINGS: posix(settings),
              ADDONS_STATE_DIR: posix(join(dir, 'state')),
              FAKE_SETTINGS_STORE: posix(join(dir, 'store.txt')),
              ...opts.env,
            },
          });
          return { code: 0, out };
        } catch (e) {
          return { code: e.status, out: `${e.stdout || ''}${e.stderr || ''}` };
        }
      }
      
      const conf = (dir) => readFileSync(join(dir, 'mod', 'addons.conf'), 'utf8');
      const values = (dir) =>
        conf(dir).split(/\r?\n/).filter((l) => /^[A-Za-z]/.test(l)).sort();
      const store = (dir) => {
        try {
          return readFileSync(join(dir, 'store.txt'), 'utf8');
        } catch {
          return '';
        }
      };
      
      test('list is JSON the page can parse, and a comment-only file enforces nothing', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        const { code, out } = run(dir, ['list']);
        assert.equal(code, 0);
        const doc = JSON.parse(out);
        assert.equal(doc.conf, 'no', 'the shipped template must not count as saved values');
        assert.equal(doc.device, 'yes', 'the fake settings command stands in for the phone');
        assert.ok(doc.addons.length >= 5);
        for (const a of doc.addons) {
          assert.match(a.id, /^[a-z0-9_]+$/);
          assert.ok(a.choices.includes(a.value), `${a.id}: ${a.value} is not one of its choices`);
          assert.ok(a.choices.includes(a.default), `${a.id}: default is not a choice`);
          assert.equal(a.saved, false);
          assert.equal(a.summary.includes('|'), false, 'a pipe would break the catalog line');
          assert.ok(['setting', 'overlay'].includes(a.kind), `${a.id}: kind is ${a.kind}`);
        }
        const ids = doc.addons.map((a) => a.id);
        assert.deepEqual(ids, [...new Set(ids)], 'ids must be unique');
        const overlay = doc.addons.filter((a) => a.kind === 'overlay').map((a) => a.id);
        assert.deepEqual(overlay,
          ['any_rotation', 'nav_bar_padding', 'status_bar_background', 'hide_notch'],
          'these four are resources the build emits, not settings');
      });
      
      test('only deviations are written, and setting one back to its default drops it', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['set', 'volume_panel=left', 'status_clock=off']).code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), ['status_clock=off', 'volume_panel=left']);
        // volume_panel: left is 1, right is 0.
        assert.match(store(dir), /secure\/volume_panel_on_left=1/);
        assert.match(store(dir), /secure\/icon_blacklist=clock/);
      
        // back to the default: the value is restored now, but no longer pinned
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['set', 'volume_panel=right']).code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), ['status_clock=off']);
        assert.match(store(dir), /secure\/volume_panel_on_left=0/);
        assert.equal(JSON.parse(run(dir, ['list']).out).conf, 'yes');
      });
      
      test('hiding the clock edits icon_blacklist instead of replacing it', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        // The list already hides another icon: that entry is not this addon's to drop.
        writeFileSync(join(dir, 'store.txt'), 'secure/icon_blacklist=rotate\n');
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['set', 'status_clock=off']).code, 0);
        assert.match(store(dir), /secure\/icon_blacklist=rotate,clock/);
      
        // Back to the default: the clock returns, the other entry stays.
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['set', 'status_clock=on']).code, 0);
        assert.match(store(dir), /secure\/icon_blacklist=rotate$/m);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), []);
      
        // Reset is allowed to put the clock back too, again without touching rotate.
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['set', 'status_clock=off']).code, 0);
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['reset']).code, 0);
        assert.match(store(dir), /secure\/icon_blacklist=rotate$/m);
      });
      
      test('a bad id or value is refused and changes nothing', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        const bad = run(dir, ['set', 'volume_panel=sideways']);
        assert.equal(bad.code, 1);
        assert.match(bad.out, /volume_panel: 'sideways' is not one of/);
        const unknown = run(dir, ['set', 'not_an_addon=on']);
        assert.equal(unknown.code, 1);
        assert.match(unknown.out, /no such addon/);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), []);
        assert.equal(store(dir), '');
      });
      
      test('apply is what the boot runs: saved values only, and exit 0', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        run(dir, ['set', 'stay_awake=on', 'status_clock=off']);
        writeFileSync(join(dir, 'store.txt'), '');  // a fresh boot: nothing applied yet
      
        const boot = run(dir, ['apply']);
        assert.equal(boot.code, 0);
        assert.match(boot.out, /\+ stay_awake=on/);
        assert.match(boot.out, /\+ status_clock=off/);
        // The largest int a Setting can hold: about 24 days, i.e. until power-off.
        assert.match(store(dir), /system\/screen_off_timeout=2147483647/);
        assert.match(store(dir), /secure\/icon_blacklist=clock/);
      });
      
      test('a value the device rejects is reported as saved but not live', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        run(dir, ['set', 'volume_panel=left']);
        // A settings command that accepts the write but keeps the old value: this is
        // what a restricted namespace looks like from here.
        writeFileSync(join(dir, 'bin', 'settings'), '#!/bin/sh\n[ "$1" = get ] && { echo null; exit 0; }\nexit 0\n');
        chmodSync(join(dir, 'bin', 'settings'), 0o755);
        const applied = run(dir, ['apply']);
        assert.equal(applied.code, 1);
        assert.match(applied.out, /volume_panel: the device still reports 'unset'/);
      });
      
      test('reset hands every live addon back and keeps the comments', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        run(dir, ['set', 'volume_panel=left', 'stay_awake=on']);
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['reset']).code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), []);
        assert.match(conf(dir), /^# Module addons/m);
        assert.match(store(dir), /secure\/volume_panel_on_left=0/);
        assert.match(store(dir), /system\/screen_off_timeout=60000/);
        assert.equal(JSON.parse(run(dir, ['list']).out).conf, 'no');
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['reset']).code, 0, 'reset with nothing saved is not an error');
      });
      
      test('reset and save work on a desktop, where there is no settings command', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        const noPhone = { env: { ADDONS_SETTINGS: '/nonexistent/settings' } };
        const saved = run(dir, ['set', 'volume_panel=left', 'any_rotation=on'], noPhone);
        assert.equal(saved.code, 0, 'saving must not fail just because no phone is attached');
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), ['any_rotation=on', 'volume_panel=left']);
        // There is no APK to leave alone on a desktop: Clear all is the build choice.
        const cleared = run(dir, ['reset'], noPhone);
        assert.equal(cleared.code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), []);
      });
      
      test('an overlay addon is saved for the build, never written to Settings', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['set', 'any_rotation=on', 'nav_bar_padding=off',
          'status_bar_background=off', 'hide_notch=on']).code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), ['any_rotation=on', 'hide_notch=on',
          'nav_bar_padding=off', 'status_bar_background=off']);
        assert.equal(store(dir), '', 'only a rebuilt APK can apply these');
        const doc = JSON.parse(run(dir, ['list']).out);
        for (const a of doc.addons.filter((x) => x.kind === 'overlay')) {
          assert.equal(a.saved, true);
          assert.equal(a.live, '', 'a resource has no live value to read back');
        }
        // `apply` at boot must skip them instead of reporting a put that never ran.
        const boot = run(dir, ['apply']);
        assert.equal(boot.code, 0);
        assert.equal(boot.out.trim(), '');
      });
      
      test('reset on the phone keeps the overlay addons it is running', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        run(dir, ['set', 'volume_panel=left', 'nav_bar_padding=off']);
        const reset = run(dir, ['reset']);
        assert.equal(reset.code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), ['nav_bar_padding=off'],
          'the flashed APK still has it; only a rebuild can undo that');
        assert.match(reset.out, /overlay addons stay as they are/);
      });
      
      test('a line from an older catalog is ignored at boot and pruned by reset', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        const file = join(dir, 'mod', 'addons.conf');
        writeFileSync(file, `${readFileSync(file, 'utf8')}\nanimations=fast\n`);
        const boot = run(dir, ['apply']);
        assert.equal(boot.code, 0, 'an addon that no longer exists must not fail the boot');
        assert.equal(store(dir), '');
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['reset']).code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), []);
      });
      
      test('restore-conf keeps the rebuild\'s own choices and carries the rest over', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        // The previous install had both of these; only one of them was changed on
        // the phone after it was flashed.
        run(dir, ['set', 'volume_panel=left', 'captive_portal=off']);
        // The new zip names its own choice for one addon and says nothing about the
        // other, which nobody touched in the app.
        writeFileSync(join(dir, 'mod', 'addons.conf'),
          `${pristineConf()}volume_panel=right\n`);
        assert.equal(run(dir, ['restore-conf']).code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), ['captive_portal=off', 'volume_panel=right'],
          'the new build wins for what it names; the saved file fills the gaps');
      });
      
      test('restore-conf brings the saved file back after a reinstall', () => {
        const dir = moduleTree();
        run(dir, ['set', 'captive_portal=off']);
        // The update replaced the module directory with the shipped file (which
        // names nothing here, so the whole saved file comes back).
        writeFileSync(join(dir, 'mod', 'addons.conf'), pristineConf());
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), []);
        const restored = run(dir, ['restore-conf']);
        assert.equal(restored.code, 0);
        assert.deepEqual(values(dir), ['captive_portal=off']);
      });
      
      // The overlay addons are resources, so the build is where they happen. This runs
      // the same generators build.sh runs, against a throwaway module directory.
      function generateResources(confText) {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'addons-res-'));
        const mod = join(dir, 'mod');
        const out = join(dir, 'res');
        mkdirSync(mod, { recursive: true });
        for (const sub of ['framework/values', 'framework/values-land', 'systemui/values']) {
          mkdirSync(join(out, sub), { recursive: true });
        }
        writeFileSync(join(mod, 'addons.conf'), confText);
        // MODULE_DIR is set after common.sh: that is what normalises the paths.
        const gen = `
      set -eo pipefail
      ROOT="$1"; MOD="$2"; OUT="$3"
      export ROOT
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      MODULE_DIR="$MOD"; RES_DIR="$OUT/framework"; SYSUI_RES_DIR="$OUT/systemui"
      ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS=100
      STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT=76
      STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE=24
      DISPLAY_CUTOUT="M 0,0 H -29 V 118 H 29 V 0 H 0 Z"
      HAS_UDFPS=false; HAS_AOD=true; HAS_DOZE=false; HAS_AUTO_BRIGHTNESS=false
      HAS_BURN_IN_PROTECTION=false; HAS_DOUBLE_TAP_WAKE=false; HAS_HBM=false
      HAS_5G=false; HAS_VOLTE=false
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/resources.sh"
      generate_resource_xml
      generate_systemui_resource_xml
      `;
        execFileSync('bash', ['-c', gen, 'gen', posix(root), posix(mod), posix(out)],
          { cwd: root, stdio: 'pipe' });
        const read = (rel) => {
          try {
            return readFileSync(join(out, rel), 'utf8');
          } catch {
            return '';
          }
        };
        return { read };
      }
      
      test('the overlay addons become resources, and the shade is written per density', () => {
        const on = generateResources('status_bar_background=off\nhide_notch=on\n');
        assert.match(on.read('framework/values/generated.xml'),
          /<bool name="config_maskMainBuiltInDisplayCutout">true<\/bool>/);
        assert.match(on.read('systemui/values/generated.xml'),
          /name="status_background" type="drawable">@android:color\/transparent</);
      
        // The default-config item alone loses to the ROM's density-qualified 9-patch
        // (AssetManager2::FindEntry), so every density the ROM uses gets a copy.
        for (const d of ['mdpi', 'hdpi', 'xhdpi', 'xxhdpi', 'xxxhdpi']) {
          assert.match(on.read(`systemui/values-${d}-v4/generated.xml`),
            /name="status_background" type="drawable">@android:color\/transparent</, d);
        }
      
        // Back to the defaults: the resource goes, and so do the copies — a leftover
        // one is a build that keeps removing the shade nobody asked about.
        const off = generateResources('#status_bar_background=off\n#hide_notch=on\n');
        assert.doesNotMatch(off.read('framework/values/generated.xml'),
          /config_maskMainBuiltInDisplayCutout/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(off.read('systemui/values/generated.xml'), /status_background/);
        assert.equal(off.read('systemui/values-xxhdpi-v4/generated.xml'), '',
          'a stale density copy must be removed');
      });
      
      test('the shipped template names every addon the catalog offers', () => {
        const doc = JSON.parse(run(moduleTree(), ['list']).out);
        const text = readFileSync(template, 'utf8');
        for (const a of doc.addons) {
          assert.match(text, new RegExp(`^#${a.id}=`, 'm'),
            `src/module/addons.conf should show ${a.id} as a commented example`);
        }
      });
      
- path: stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh — firmware mode has to answer from the ROM
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The failure this pins: a Xiaomi ROM puts the sensor geometry in
      // vendor/build.prop as the FOD rectangle properties, not in an overlay APK. The
      // probe used to list only the first 40 *.prop files (a real tree has hundreds,
      // starting with system_ext's per-app cust.prop) and never turned the pair into a
      // candidate at all, so a full super.img answered nothing while the same phone
      // over adb answered 540,2198,89 from the very same property.
      //
      // No phone and no aapt2 are involved: the tree is a few text files.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const probe = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'udfps-probe.sh');
      
      function tree(files) {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'udfps-fw-'));
        for (const [rel, body] of Object.entries(files)) {
          const path = join(dir, rel);
          mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
          writeFileSync(path, body);
        }
        return dir;
      }
      
      function run(dir) {
        const out = execFileSync('bash', [probe, '--firmware', dir, '--json'], {
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          env: { ...process.env, TERM: 'dumb' },
        });
        return JSON.parse(out);
      }
      
      // The zephyr (Redmi Note 17 4G) values, exactly as vendor/build.prop ships them.
      const ZEPHYR = `ro.hardware.fp.fod=true
      ro.hardware.fp.fod.location=low
      persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=451,2109
      persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=178,178
      `;
      
      test('the rectangle in vendor/build.prop is an answer, and the arithmetic is the rectangle centre', () => {
        const dir = tree({ 'vendor/build.prop': ZEPHYR });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        const c = report.candidates[0];
        assert.equal(c.source, 'firmware-fod-props');
        assert.equal(c.x, 540);
        assert.equal(c.y, 2198);
        assert.equal(c.radius, 89);
        assert.equal(c.confidence, 'high');
        assert.equal(report.chosen.x, 540, 'the answer has to be chosen, not only listed');
        assert.match(c.detail, /location\.X_Y=451,2109/);
      });
      
      // A tree carries hundreds of per-app .prop files; the vendor build.prop has to
      // be read even when it is not in the first handful find returns.
      test('a build.prop behind hundreds of other .prop files is still read', () => {
        const files = {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 220; i += 1) {
          const name = `system_ext/etc/cust/${String(i).padStart(3, '0')}/cust.prop`;
          files[name] = `ro.cust.slot=${i}\n`;
        }
        files['vendor/build.prop'] = ZEPHYR;
        const report = run(tree(files));
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        assert.equal(report.chosen.x, 540);
      });
      
      // Android 8 shipped the same pair without the vendor segment.
      test('the pre-vendor property names are read too', () => {
        const dir = tree({
          'vendor/build.prop': 'persist.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=300,1800\npersist.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=100,120\n',
        });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        assert.deepEqual(
          [report.chosen.x, report.chosen.y, report.chosen.radius],
          [350, 1860, 50]
        );
      });
      
      // A rectangle with no size is not a sensor position; inventing one would put
      // the icon where no finger can reach.
      test('an unusable pair is refused with a warning, not turned into a guess', () => {
        const dir = tree({
          'vendor/build.prop': 'persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=0,0\npersist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=0,0\n',
        });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 0);
        assert.equal(report.chosen, null);
        assert.ok(report.warnings.length > 0, 'the refusal has to be visible');
      });
      
      test('a tree with nothing to read answers nothing instead of failing', () => {
        const report = run(tree({ 'system/build.prop': 'ro.product.device=zephyr\n' }));
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 0);
        assert.equal(report.chosen, null);
        assert.equal(report.mode, 'firmware');
      });
      
      // The probe is also run through the app, which passes an absolute folder: the
      // paths it prints have to be usable, not a temp dir from this test.
      test('the probe still names the source file it answered from', () => {
        const dir = tree({ 'vendor/build.prop': ZEPHYR });
        const report = run(dir);
        const detail = report.candidates[0].detail;
        assert.ok(detail.startsWith(dir), `detail does not name the tree: ${detail}`);
      });
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh
  content: |
              while IFS= read -r cand; do
                  [ -n "$cand" ] || continue
                  kind=$(classify_binary "$cand")
                  if kind_usable "$kind"; then
                      ok "$name found: $cand [$(kind_label "$kind")]"
                      found=true
                      break
                  fi
                  warn "$name at $cand is a $(kind_label "$kind") — cannot run here, ignoring"
              done <<< "$(tool_candidates "$name")"
              $found
          }
          check_tool_report aapt2 || true
          check_tool_report zipalign || true
          check_tool_report apksigner || true
          command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "java found: $(command -v java)" || err "java not found"
          framework_res_path >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "resources found: $(framework_res_path)" || err "resources not found"
      
          if [ -z "$(toolchain_missing)" ] && [ -z "$force_res" ]; then
              echo ""
              ok "Nothing to install — everything is already available."
              echo ""
              echo "  Build with: ./build.sh"
              echo ""
              return 0
          fi
      
          # Tools are fine (only the resource dictionary is missing, or --force was
          # used): no need to reinstall the compiler/signer, just pick resources.
          local missing_tools=false
          for t in aapt2 zipalign apksigner; do
              [ "$t" = "zipalign" ] && zipalign_optional && continue
              tool_ready "$t" || missing_tools=true
          done
          command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing_tools=true
          if ! $missing_tools; then
              acquire_framework_res ask "$force_res" || true
              echo ""
              print_toolchain
              echo ""
              verify_toolchain
              return $?
          fi
      
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}How should the missing tools be installed?${NC}"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[1]${NC} Debian / Ubuntu / Mint        (apt)"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[2]${NC} Arch Linux / Manjaro         (pacman)"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[3]${NC} Android / Termux             (pkg)"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[4]${NC} Manual download into stuff/tools/  (no root)"
          if $IS_WINDOWS; then
              echo -e "    ${BOLD}[5]${NC} Windows build-tools          ${GREEN}<-- use this${NC}"
          else
              echo -e "    ${BOLD}[5]${NC} Windows build-tools          (only for Git Bash on Windows)"
          fi
          echo ""
          ask "  Selection [1/2/3/4/5]: " "$($IS_WINDOWS && echo 5 || echo 4)"
      
          case "$REPLY" in
              1)
                  if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                      warn "apt is not available on Windows. Choose [5]."
                  elif install_linux_packages; then
                      acquire_framework_res ask || true
                  fi
                  ;;
              2)
                  if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                      warn "pacman is not available on Windows. Choose [5]."
                  elif install_linux_packages; then
                      acquire_framework_res ask || true
                  fi
                  ;;
              3)
                  if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                      warn "pkg is not available on Windows. Choose [5]."
                  elif install_linux_packages; then
                      acquire_framework_res ask || true
                  fi
                  ;;
              4)
                  download_manual_tools && { acquire_framework_res ask || true; }
                  ;;
              5)
                  if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                      install_windows_tools || return 1
                      acquire_framework_res ask || true
                  else
                      warn "This option installs the Windows .exe toolchain."
                      warn "Pick the option that matches this OS instead."
                  fi
                  ;;
              *)
                  info "Nothing installed."
                  ;;
          esac
      
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Result${NC}"
          print_toolchain
          echo ""
          verify_toolchain
      }
```
