- path: gui/matchprop.go
  content: |
      package main
      
      // ============================================================================
      // Which property should the submitted overlay match on?
      // ============================================================================
      // A static RRO for the overlay repo matches with android:requiredSystemProperty
      // Name/Value, compared with plain string equality. Getting it wrong is silent:
      // the overlay installs, `cmd overlay list` shows it enabled, and nothing changes.
      //
      // Two things decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable from the
      // phone without root:
      //
      //   * zygote has to be able to read the property. A zygote overlay is matched
      //     while zygote preloads the framework, so a property in a SELinux area
      //     zygote is denied reads as empty and the condition never holds. `getprop -Z`
      //     prints the area (build_prop and build_vendor_prop are the safe ones,
      //     build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps).
      //   * the value has to name this device and survive what is installed. The
      //     vendor, odm and bootimage partitions keep the OEM value under a GSI;
      //     /system, /product and /system_ext are replaced, so ro.product.device on a
      //     GSI holds the GSI's own name (phh_treble, mivendor, …).
      //
      // Neither rule alone is enough — on a GSI the surviving property is often the
      // one zygote cannot read, and the readable one has been renamed — so this ranks
      // every candidate, says what each one is gambling on, and refuses to call a
      // winner when no property actually carries the codename. The values below are
      // what the reference phones report: Samsung SM-A908N (everything is r3q) and
      // Xiaomi 26012RN62A (ro.product.device is zephyr, but its vendor property is the
      // shared mivendor and build.product is missi).
      
      import (
        "regexp"
        "sort"
        "strings"
      )
      
      // What a codename looks like: lower case, no separators bash would eat, short
      // enough to be a name rather than a build string.
      var codenameShape = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,23}$`)
      
      // MatchCandidate is one property the submission could be matched on.
      type MatchCandidate struct {
        Prop  string `json:"prop"`
        Value string `json:"value"`
        Score int    `json:"score"`
        Zone  string `json:"zone"`
        Label string `json:"label"`
        Trust string `json:"trust"` // high, medium, low
        // Perfect means this is a pick nothing has to be argued about: the value
        // is the codename, zygote can read the property, and a GSI leaves it alone.
        // Only a perfect pick is offered as the answer; anything less and the card
        // tells the user to keep the match they already have.
        Perfect bool   `json:"perfect"`
        Why     string `json:"why"`
        Risk    string `json:"risk,omitempty"`
      }
      
      // MatchRejection is a property with a device-ish name that was ruled out, and
      // why. The reasons are the answers to the question users ask most often, so
      // they are part of the answer rather than something to work out again.
      type MatchRejection struct {
        Prop   string `json:"prop"`
        Value  string `json:"value"`
        Reason string `json:"reason"`
      }
      
      // MatchReport is what the Config tab shows: the codename it settled on, the
      // ranked candidates, the properties it refused, and how sure it is.
      type MatchReport struct {
        Serial     string           `json:"serial"`
        Model      string           `json:"model"`
        Codename   string           `json:"codename"`
        Confidence string           `json:"confidence"` // high, medium, low
        ModuleProp string           `json:"moduleProp"`
        Candidates []MatchCandidate `json:"candidates"`
        Rejected   []MatchRejection `json:"rejected"`
      }
      
      // matchProp is one entry of the fixed candidate list. zone says which partition
      // the value comes from (that is what decides GSI survival) and kind says what
      // the property holds.
      type matchProp struct {
        name string
        zone string
        kind string
      }
      
      var matchPropCandidates = []matchProp{
        {"ro.product.vendor.device", "vendor", "device"},
        {"ro.product.odm.device", "odm", "device"},
        {"ro.product.bootimage.device", "bootimage", "device"},
        {"ro.product.device", "system", "device"},
        {"ro.product.product.device", "product", "device"},
        {"ro.product.system.device", "system", "device"},
        {"ro.product.system_ext.device", "system_ext", "device"},
        {"ro.build.product", "build", "device"},
        {"ro.product.vendor.name", "vendor", "name"},
        {"ro.product.odm.name", "odm", "name"},
        {"ro.product.bootimage.name", "bootimage", "name"},
        {"ro.product.name", "product", "name"},
        {"ro.product.vendor.model", "vendor", "model"},
        {"ro.product.model", "product", "model"},
      }
      
      // zoneScore: vendor/odm/bootimage keep the OEM value when a GSI replaces
      // /system; a `ro.product.*` value is whatever is installed now.
      var zoneScore = map[string]int{
        "vendor": 40, "odm": 35, "bootimage": 35,
        "product": 25, "system": 22, "system_ext": 18, "build": 10,
      }
      
      var kindScore = map[string]int{"device": 25, "name": 12, "model": 15}
      
      // labelScore: what the SELinux area means for zygote reading it. The negative
      // numbers are the documented traps, not guesses — build_bootimage_prop and
      // build_odm_prop are refused to zygote on most GSI builds.
      var labelScore = map[string]int{
        "build_prop":           30,
        "build_vendor_prop":    30,
        "vendor_default_prop":  25,
        "default_prop":         15,
        "build_system_prop":    -20,
        "build_odm_prop":       -35,
        "build_bootimage_prop": -35,
        "bootloader_prop":      -20,
      }
      
      // Values that name a build rather than a device. They are the reason a "looks
      // like a codename" filter is not enough: mivendor is a Xiaomi vendor tree shared
      // by a whole family, generic is the GSI itself, qcom is a SoC vendor.
      var genericMatchValues = map[string]string{
        "generic":        "the AOSP/GSI build name, shared by every generic image",
        "generic_x86":    "the AOSP/GSI build name, shared by every generic image",
        "generic_arm64":  "the AOSP/GSI build name, shared by every generic image",
        "generic_x86_64": "the AOSP/GSI build name, shared by every generic image",
        "aosp":           "an AOSP build name, not a device",
        "aosp_arm64":     "an AOSP build name, not a device",
        "mainline":       "the mainline/module build name, not a device",
        "treble":         "the Treble build name, not a device",
        "phh_treble":     "the GSI's own name — present on every device running that GSI",
        "mivendor":       "Xiaomi's vendor build name — shared by many Xiaomi devices, not a codename",
        "emulator":       "an emulator, not a phone",
        "unknown":        "no value",
        "qcom":           "a SoC vendor, shared by every Qualcomm device",
        "mediatek":       "a SoC vendor, shared by every MediaTek device",
        "mtk":            "a SoC vendor, shared by every MediaTek device",
        "exynos":         "a SoC vendor, shared by every Exynos device",
        "android":        "not a device name",
      }
      
      // rankMatchProps turns a phone's `getprop` and `getprop -Z` output into ranked
      // candidates. Both maps are keyed by property name; a missing value or label is
      // simply an empty string, because adb output loses lines on some ROMs.
      func rankMatchProps(values, labels map[string]string) MatchReport {
        report := MatchReport{
          Candidates: []MatchCandidate{},
          Rejected:   []MatchRejection{},
        }
      
        brand := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(values["ro.product.brand"]))
        manufacturer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(values["ro.product.manufacturer"]))
        report.Model = strings.TrimSpace(values["ro.product.model"])
      
        // Phase 1: what is this phone called? Partition order is the rule, not a sum:
        // vendor, odm and bootimage are the OEM's own naming and are what a GSI leaves
        // alone, while /system, /product and /system_ext hold the ROM's name (on a
        // GSI that is the GSI itself: generic, phh_treble, mivendor). A value the OEM
        // partitions agree on is the codename; the later props are only consulted
        // when those are empty or generic.
        codenameOrder := []string{
          "ro.product.vendor.device",
          "ro.product.odm.device",
          "ro.product.bootimage.device",
          "ro.product.device",
          "ro.product.system.device",
          "ro.product.product.device",
          "ro.product.system_ext.device",
          "ro.build.product",
        }
        codename := ""
        codenameProp := ""
        for _, name := range codenameOrder {
          value := strings.TrimSpace(values[name])
          if value == "" || genericMatchValues[strings.ToLower(value)] != "" {
            continue
          }
          if !codenameShape.MatchString(value) {
            continue
          }
          if value == brand || value == manufacturer {
            continue
          }
          codename, codenameProp = value, name
          break
        }
        report.Codename = codename
      
        // Phase 2: rank every property against that answer.
        for _, p := range matchPropCandidates {
          value := strings.TrimSpace(values[p.name])
          if value == "" {
            continue
          }
          label := shortPropertyLabel(labels[p.name])
          if reason := genericMatchValues[strings.ToLower(value)]; reason != "" {
            report.Rejected = append(report.Rejected, MatchRejection{
              Prop: p.name, Value: value, Reason: reason,
            })
            continue
          }
          if brand != "" && strings.EqualFold(value, brand) {
            report.Rejected = append(report.Rejected, MatchRejection{
              Prop: p.name, Value: value,
              Reason: "the brand, not the device — it would match every phone of this make",
            })
            continue
          }
      
          c := MatchCandidate{
            Prop:  p.name,
            Value: value,
            Zone:  p.zone,
            Label: label,
          }
          c.Score = zoneScore[p.zone] + kindScore[p.kind] + labelScore[label]
      
          var why, risk []string
          switch p.zone {
          case "vendor", "odm", "bootimage":
            why = append(why, "lives on /"+p.zone+", which a GSI leaves alone")
          default:
            why = append(why, "read from the installed /"+p.zone+" partition")
            risk = append(risk, "a GSI replaces /"+p.zone+", so the value changes and the match stops")
          }
          switch label {
          case "build_prop", "build_vendor_prop", "vendor_default_prop", "default_prop":
            why = append(why, "zygote can read "+label)
          case "":
            risk = append(risk, "this ROM did not report its SELinux area, so readability is unchecked")
          default:
            risk = append(risk, label+" is often denied to zygote — the overlay can show as enabled and do nothing")
          }
          if codename != "" && value == codename {
            c.Score += 30
            why = append(why, "holds the codename")
            if p.name == codenameProp {
              c.Score += 10
            }
          } else if codename != "" && strings.Contains(value, codename) {
            c.Score += 10
            why = append(why, "contains the codename")
          } else {
            // The missi case: a property that names this build, not this phone.
            // Matching on it would claim a different device, so every such row
            // ranks below the ones that carry the codename.
            c.Score -= 20
            if p.kind == "device" {
              risk = append(risk, "holds a different name ("+value+") than this phone's codename ("+codename+")")
            } else {
              risk = append(risk, "does not hold the codename, so it names this variant rather than the device")
            }
          }
          if codenameShape.MatchString(value) {
            c.Score += 10
          } else {
            c.Score -= 5
            if strings.ContainsRune(value, ' ') {
              risk = append(risk, "contains a space — exact matching works, but it is easy to break while editing")
            }
          }
          if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), "global") {
            c.Score -= 10
            risk = append(risk, "has a region suffix, so another region's build would not match")
          }
          if p.zone == "system" && strings.HasSuffix(p.name, ".device") && value == codename && label == "build_prop" {
            // This is the normal, good answer on a stock ROM: say so instead of
            // making the user read the /system risk as a deal-breaker.
            risk = []string{"if a GSI is installed later this property becomes the GSI's name"}
          }
      
          c.Why = strings.Join(why, " · ")
          c.Risk = strings.Join(risk, " · ")
          c.Perfect = codename != "" && value == codename && p.kind == "device" &&
            readableByZygote(label) && survivesGSI(p.zone)
          switch {
          case c.Perfect:
            c.Trust = "high"
          case value == codename:
            c.Trust = "medium"
          default:
            c.Trust = "low"
          }
          report.Candidates = append(report.Candidates, c)
        }
      
        sort.SliceStable(report.Candidates, func(i, j int) bool {
          a, b := report.Candidates[i], report.Candidates[j]
          if a.Score != b.Score {
            return a.Score > b.Score
          }
          // Same score: the one that actually carries the codename is the more
          // useful row, and after that the order only has to be stable.
          if (a.Value == codename) != (b.Value == codename) {
            return a.Value == codename
          }
          return a.Prop < b.Prop
        })
      
        // Confidence is about the answer, not the ranking. "high" is reserved for a
        // property that satisfies every rule at once (readable by zygote, carries the
        // codename, survives a GSI); anything less and the honest advice is to keep
        // the match that already works, because a submitted condition that does not
        // hold is invisible.
        report.Confidence = "low"
        if len(report.Candidates) > 0 {
          top := report.Candidates[0]
          switch {
          case top.Perfect:
            report.Confidence = "high"
          case top.Value == codename && codename != "":
            report.Confidence = "medium"
          }
        }
        if codename != "" {
          report.ModuleProp = "persist.sys.overlay." + strings.ToLower(codename)
        }
        return report
      }
      
      // survivesGSI: a property in these areas keeps the OEM value after a GSI flash.
      func survivesGSI(zone string) bool {
        switch zone {
        case "vendor", "odm", "bootimage":
          return true
        }
        return false
      }
      
      func readableByZygote(label string) bool {
        switch label {
        case "build_prop", "build_vendor_prop", "vendor_default_prop", "default_prop":
          return true
        }
        return false
      }
      
      // shortPropertyLabel turns "u:object_r:build_vendor_prop:s0" into
      // "build_vendor_prop", which is the part that means something here.
      func shortPropertyLabel(label string) string {
        parts := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(label), ":")
        if len(parts) >= 3 {
          return parts[2]
        }
        return ""
      }
      
      // parseGetprop reads `getprop` output: one `[key]: [value]` per line. Lines that
      // do not fit are skipped — some ROMs print warnings into the same stream.
      func parseGetprop(out string) map[string]string {
        props := map[string]string{}
        for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
          line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r")
          key, rest, ok := strings.Cut(line, "]: [")
          if !ok || !strings.HasPrefix(key, "[") || !strings.HasSuffix(rest, "]") {
            continue
          }
          props[strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(key, "["))] = strings.TrimSuffix(rest, "]")
        }
        return props
      }
      
      // parseGetpropLabels reads `getprop -Z`: `[key]: [u:object_r:xyz_prop:s0]`.
      func parseGetpropLabels(out string) map[string]string {
        return parseGetprop(out)
      }
      
- path: src/webui/addons.sh
  content: |
      #!/system/bin/sh
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay — module addons
      # =============================================================================
      # An addon is a tweak the *module* makes on the phone. It is not a config.env
      # key, and it is chosen in the app's Addons tab (or the page's Addons card),
      # not in the overlay resource files.
      #
      # There are two kinds, and the catalog says which is which:
      #
      #   setting  a Settings value the module writes. One `settings put` changes it
      #            on a running phone — no APK, no reboot — and service.sh re-applies
      #            it at every boot. The overlay APK alone cannot do one.
      #   overlay  a resource the build bakes into an overlay APK — framework (the
      #            navigation bar height, the 180° rotation flag) or SystemUI (the
      #            status bar background). It only changes after a rebuild and a
      #            flash, because a resource is read when its process starts.
      #
      # The live addons survive an overlay rebuild; the overlay ones *are* the rebuild.
      #
      # One catalog lives in this file and every front-end reads it:
      #
      #   the desktop app   runs this script in the clone (Addons tab)
      #   the module page   runs it in webroot/ on the phone (Addons card)
      #   service.sh        runs it at every boot so saved choices stick
      #
      #   sh addons.sh list                 catalog + saved + live values, as JSON
      #   sh addons.sh set ID=VALUE ...     save choices; apply the live ones now
      #   sh addons.sh apply [ID ...]       apply what is saved (all ids, or those)
      #   sh addons.sh reset                back to the defaults, forget the choices
      #   sh addons.sh status               what the device resolves now, as key=value
      #   sh addons.sh restore-conf         customize.sh: bring the saved file back
      #
      # The saved file is addons.conf at the module root (src/module/addons.conf in
      # the clone). Only the addons that differ from the default are written into it:
      # a value nobody changed is not enforced on every boot, so an untouched phone
      # keeps behaving like the ROM shipped it.
      #
      # ADDONS_CONF, ADDONS_DIR and ADDONS_SETTINGS exist so this can be exercised
      # off-device (stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js) and by the desktop app, which has
      # no installed module but does have the clone.
      # =============================================================================
      
      # The module directory is one level above this script (webroot/), except when
      # the script is run by its bare name from the module root ('sh addons.sh'), in
      # which case '..' would be the folder above the module.
      SELF="$0"
      case "$SELF" in
          */*) SELF_DIR=${SELF%/*}
               MODDIR=$(cd "$SELF_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd) ;;
          *)   SELF_DIR=.
               MODDIR=$(pwd) ;;
      esac
      MODDIR=${ADDONS_DIR:-$MODDIR}
      [ -n "$MODDIR" ] || MODDIR=$SELF_DIR
      # In the clone the module files are kept in src/module/, so the script in
      # src/webui/ has one directory in between; an installed module keeps the same
      # files at its root.
      [ -d "$MODDIR/module" ] && MODDIR="$MODDIR/module"
      
      CONF=${ADDONS_CONF:-$MODDIR/addons.conf}
      # Outside the module directory on purpose: an update replaces that directory.
      # It is the same folder apply.sh mirrors webui.conf into.
      STATE_DIR=${ADDONS_STATE_DIR:-/data/adb/treble-webui/${MODDIR##*/}}
      SETTINGS=${ADDONS_SETTINGS:-settings}
      
      say() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Catalog
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # id|choices|default|label|summary|kind
      #
      # The value names are what the page and the app show, so they are plain words:
      # "left"/"right", not "0"/"1". The mapping to the Settings value is in
      # apply_one() below, and live_value() maps it back. Keep the summaries free of
      # '|' and keep them one sentence: they are rendered as-is.
      #
      # kind is "setting" or "overlay" (see the top of this file). Only "setting" ids
      # reach apply_one()/live_value(); the build reads the overlay ids out of the
      # saved file and emits them as overlay resources (see resources.sh).
      #
      # A two-choice addon whose choices are exactly on,off is drawn as a switch;
      # anything else is a picker.
      catalog() {
          cat << 'CATALOG_EOF'
      volume_panel|right,left|right|Volume panel side|The volume slider slides in from this edge instead of the other one.|setting
      captive_portal|on,off|on|Captive portal check|Android's "sign in to this network" probe. Off stops the false no-internet warnings a GSI shows on some networks.|setting
      stay_awake|on,off|off|Screen never sleeps|Leave the display on indefinitely, on battery too. Only the power button turns it off again.|setting
      status_clock|on,off|on|Status bar clock|Hide the time in the status bar so the notification icons get its room. The lock-screen clock is left alone.|setting
      any_rotation|on,off|off|Upside-down rotation|Allow the 180° rotation Android normally refuses, in every app and launcher that can turn.|overlay
      nav_bar_padding|on,off|on|Navigation bar padding|Reserve no space for the gesture bar: content reaches the bottom edge while the pill stays visible and swipeable.|overlay
      status_bar_background|on,off|on|Status bar background|Remove the shade behind the status bar, so the bar sits directly on the wallpaper or the app.|overlay
      hide_notch|on,off|off|Hide the notch|Black out the strip the notch sits in and keep every app below it, so nothing can draw under the camera.|overlay
      CATALOG_EOF
      }
      
      # Every id, one per line.
      ids() {
          catalog | while IFS='|' read -r id choices def label summary kind; do
              case "$id" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
              printf '%s\n' "$id"
          done
      }
      
      catalog_field() { # <id> <field number> -> that field, empty when unknown
          catalog | awk -F'|' -v id="$1" -v f="$2" '$1 == id { print $f; exit }'
      }
      
      choices_of() { catalog_field "$1" 2; }
      default_of() { catalog_field "$1" 3; }
      label_of()   { catalog_field "$1" 4; }
      summary_of() { catalog_field "$1" 5; }
      kind_of()    { catalog_field "$1" 6; }
      
      valid_value() { # <id> <value>
          case " $(choices_of "$1" | tr ',' ' ') " in
              *" $2 "*) return 0 ;;
          esac
          return 1
      }
      
      bad_value() { say "x $1: '$2' is not one of: $(choices_of "$1" | tr ',' '/')"; }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The saved file
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Same shape as config.env — ID=VALUE lines, '#' comments — so it can be read
      # and edited by hand. apply.sh keeps webui.conf in the module the same way.
      conf_value() { # <key> -> saved value, empty when not saved
          [ -f "$CONF" ] || return 0
          awk -v k="$1" 'index($0, k "=") == 1 { v = substr($0, length(k) + 2) } END { printf "%s", v }' "$CONF" 2>/dev/null
      }
      
      has_saved() {
          [ -f "$CONF" ] || return 1
          grep -q '^[A-Za-z]' "$CONF" 2>/dev/null
      }
      
      put_conf() { # <key> <value>
          key=$1
          val=$2
          tmp="$CONF.tmp"
          if [ -f "$CONF" ]; then
              awk -v k="$key" -v v="$val" '
                  index($0, k "=") == 1 { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done = 1 } next }
                  { print }
                  END { if (!done) print k "=" v }
              ' "$CONF" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
          else
              {
                  printf '%s\n' \
                      '# =============================================================================' \
                      '# Module addons — Treble Overlay' \
                      '# =============================================================================' \
                      '# Written by the desktop app (Addons tab) or by this module on the phone.' \
                      '# Only what is listed here is enforced, and it is enforced on every boot.' \
                      '# Remove an ID=VALUE line (or use Reset) to hand that setting back.' \
                      '# The list of addons and their values: docs/addons.md' \
                      '# ============================================================================='
                  printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$val"
              } > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
          fi
          if [ ! -f "$tmp" ] || ! mv "$tmp" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null; then
              rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
              say "x cannot write $CONF (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"
              say "  The WebUI host ran this script without write access to the module."
              return 1
          fi
          chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
          return 0
      }
      
      del_conf() { # <key>
          [ -f "$CONF" ] || return 0
          tmp="$CONF.tmp"
          awk -v k="$1" 'index($0, k "=") != 1' "$CONF" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null \
              && mv "$tmp" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null
          chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
          return 0
      }
      
      # The saved file lives in two places: the module (what this script reads) and
      # $STATE_DIR (what survives an update, because the update replaces the module).
      mirror_conf() {
          mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || return 0
          if [ -f "$CONF" ]; then
              cp "$CONF" "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
          else
              rm -f "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
          chmod 600 "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
      }
      
      # customize.sh calls this after the new zip is unpacked. The packaged file is
      # the app's latest word, so its choices win: restoring the old file over it made
      # a freshly built "hide the notch" come up unset, because the phone still had
      # the previous install's copy. Only the addons the new file does not name are
      # carried over - those are the ones chosen on the phone, which the app never
      # saw. A build that names nothing at all is a plain rebuild, so the saved file
      # is restored whole, the way it always was.
      restore_conf() {
          [ -f "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" ] || return 0
          if ! has_saved; then
              if cp "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null; then
                  chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
                  say "+ saved addons restored"
              fi
              return 0
          fi
      
          restored=0
          while IFS= read -r line; do
              key=${line%%=*}
              [ -n "$key" ] || continue
              # A line from an older catalog is not brought back (reset prunes it).
              [ -n "$(default_of "$key")" ] || continue
              [ -z "$(conf_value "$key")" ] || continue
              put_conf "$key" "${line#*=}" || return 1
              restored=$((restored + 1))
          done <<EOF
      $(grep '^[A-Za-z]' "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null)
      EOF
          [ "$restored" -gt 0 ] && say "+ $restored saved addon(s) restored"
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Settings
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      have_settings() { command -v "$SETTINGS" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
      
      setting_get() { # <namespace> <key> -> value, empty for null/absent
          have_settings || return 0
          out=$("$SETTINGS" get "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | tail -n 1)
          case "$out" in
              ""|null) printf '' ;;
              *) printf '%s' "$out" ;;
          esac
      }
      
      put() { # <addon> <namespace> <key> <value>
          if ! have_settings; then
              say "x $1: the settings command is not available on this device"
              return 1
          fi
          err=$("$SETTINGS" put "$2" "$3" "$4" 2>&1)
          if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
              say "x $1: $(printf '%s' "$err" | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ *$//')"
              return 1
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # What the device resolves right now, in the catalog's words. Empty when the
      # phone says nothing (or there is no phone — the desktop app has none).
      live_value() {
          case "$1" in
              volume_panel)
                  case "$(setting_get secure volume_panel_on_left)" in
                      1) printf left ;;
                      0) printf right ;;
                  esac ;;
              captive_portal)
                  case "$(setting_get global captive_portal_mode)" in
                      1) printf on ;;
                      0) printf off ;;
                  esac ;;
              stay_awake)
                  # The addon lives in one key: a screen timeout no UI can pick.
                  case "$(setting_get system screen_off_timeout)" in
                      2147483647) printf on ;;
                      *)          printf off ;;
                  esac ;;
              status_clock)
                  # icon_blacklist is one list for the whole bar ("clock", "rotate",
                  # ...), so the clock is hidden by being present in it, not by a
                  # value of its own.
                  case " $(setting_get secure icon_blacklist | tr ',' ' ') " in
                      *" clock "*) printf off ;;
                      *)           printf on ;;
                  esac ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # icon_blacklist carries every status bar icon SystemUI should leave out, and
      # the clock is one entry in it. Writing it for the clock therefore has to keep
      # whatever else the user (or another module) put there: a plain `put` would
      # replace the whole list. An empty result writes an empty value, which is what
      # a phone that never had the key answers anyway.
      icon_blacklist_set() { # <hide|show> the clock
          ib_list=$(setting_get secure icon_blacklist | tr ',' '\n' | awk 'NF && $0 != "clock"')
          if [ "$1" = hide ]; then
              ib_list=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ib_list" clock | awk 'NF')
          fi
          ib_value=$(printf '%s\n' "$ib_list" | awk 'NF { printf "%s%s", (n++ ? "," : ""), $0 }')
          put status_clock secure icon_blacklist "$ib_value"
      }
      
      apply_one() { # <id> <value>
          id=$1
          v=$2
          # An overlay addon is a build-time decision; the running APK cannot change
          # it, so there is nothing to put. The caller has already saved the choice.
          if [ "$(kind_of "$id")" = overlay ]; then
              return 0
          fi
          case "$id" in
              volume_panel)
                  case "$v" in
                      left)  put "$id" secure volume_panel_on_left 1 ;;
                      right) put "$id" secure volume_panel_on_left 0 ;;
                      *)     bad_value "$id" "$v"; return 1 ;;
                  esac ;;
              captive_portal)
                  case "$v" in
                      on)  put "$id" global captive_portal_mode 1 ;;
                      off) put "$id" global captive_portal_mode 0 ;;
                      *)   bad_value "$id" "$v"; return 1 ;;
                  esac ;;
              stay_awake)
                  # 2147483647 ms is the largest an int Setting can hold — about 24
                  # days, which is "until the power button" for any practical use.
                  case "$v" in
                      on)  put "$id" system screen_off_timeout 2147483647 ;;
                      off) put "$id" system screen_off_timeout 60000 ;;
                      *)   bad_value "$id" "$v"; return 1 ;;
                  esac ;;
              status_clock)
                  case "$v" in
                      on)  icon_blacklist_set show ;;
                      off) icon_blacklist_set hide ;;
                      *)   bad_value "$id" "$v"; return 1 ;;
                  esac ;;
              *)
                  say "x $id: no such addon"
                  return 1 ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Commands
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      cmd_list() { # JSON: the catalog, what is saved, what the phone resolves
          if has_saved; then saved_any=yes; else saved_any=no; fi
          if have_settings; then device=yes; else device=no; fi
          printf '{"conf":"%s","device":"%s","addons":[' "$saved_any" "$device"
          first=1
          catalog | while IFS='|' read -r id choices def label summary kind; do
              case "$id" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
              [ "$first" = 1 ] || printf ','
              first=0
              saved=$(conf_value "$id")
              if [ -n "$saved" ]; then
                  value=$saved
                  is_saved=true
              else
                  value=$def
                  is_saved=false
              fi
              printf '{"id":"%s","kind":"%s","label":"%s","summary":"%s","choices":[%s],"default":"%s","value":"%s","saved":%s,"live":"%s"}' \
                  "$id" "$kind" \
                  "$(printf '%s' "$label" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')" \
                  "$(printf '%s' "$summary" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')" \
                  "$(printf '%s' "$choices" | awk -F, '{ for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) printf "%s\"%s\"", (i > 1 ? "," : ""), $i }')" \
                  "$def" "$value" "$is_saved" "$(live_value "$id")"
          done
          printf ']}\n'
      }
      
      cmd_set() { # ID=VALUE ... — save, then make it true now
          rc=0
          for pair in "$@"; do
              id=${pair%%=*}
              if [ "$id" = "$pair" ]; then
                  say "x '$pair' is not ID=VALUE"
                  rc=1
                  continue
              fi
              v=${pair#*=}
              if [ -z "$(default_of "$id")" ]; then
                  say "x $id: no such addon"
                  rc=1
                  continue
              fi
              if ! valid_value "$id" "$v"; then
                  bad_value "$id" "$v"
                  rc=1
                  continue
              fi
              # Only deviations are kept: setting an addon back to its default hands
              # that setting back to the ROM instead of pinning it on every boot.
              if [ "$v" = "$(default_of "$id")" ]; then
                  del_conf "$id"
              else
                  put_conf "$id" "$v" || rc=1
              fi
              say "+ $id=$v"
              # An overlay addon only exists inside the APK. Saving it is the shell's
              # whole job: the page writes the entry with Apply, and build.sh emits it
              # (or stops emitting it, when the choice is the default).
              if [ "$(kind_of "$id")" = overlay ]; then
                  if [ "$v" = "$(default_of "$id")" ]; then
                      say "  overlay addon: saved as the default — nothing to enforce"
                  else
                      say "  overlay addon: saved — Apply on the phone, or the next build, writes it"
                  fi
                  continue
              fi
              # On a desktop with no phone there is nothing to apply to, and the file
              # is the whole job; the script still exits 0 so the choice is saved.
              if have_settings; then
                  # A failed put stays saved on purpose: the next boot tries again,
                  # and `list` reports the row as saved but not live.
                  apply_one "$id" "$v" || rc=1
              fi
          done
          mirror_conf
          # The choice is saved even when the device rejected a put (the next boot
          # tries again), but the exit code says so: the phone's page turns it into a
          # warning, and the desktop app has no `settings` to fail with.
          return $rc
      }
      
      cmd_apply() { # [ID ...] — apply what is saved; no output when nothing is
          rc=0
          if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then list="$*"; else list=$(ids); fi
          for id in $list; do
              v=$(conf_value "$id")
              [ -n "$v" ] || continue
              # A line left by an older catalog is not an error at boot; it is just
              # ignored. `reset` is what deletes it.
              [ -n "$(default_of "$id")" ] || continue
              # Overlay addons are already inside the APK; there is nothing to set.
              if [ "$(kind_of "$id")" = overlay ]; then
                  continue
              fi
              apply_one "$id" "$v" || { rc=1; continue; }
              # Read it back: a put that the system rejected (a restricted namespace,
              # for instance) prints nothing but leaves the old value in place.
              now=$(live_value "$id")
              if [ "$now" != "$v" ]; then
                  say "x $id: the device still reports '${now:-unset}'"
                  rc=1
              else
                  say "+ $id=$v"
              fi
          done
          return $rc
      }
      
      cmd_reset() {
          rc=0
          kept_overlay=no
          for id in $(ids); do
              v=$(conf_value "$id")
              [ -n "$v" ] || continue
              if [ "$(kind_of "$id")" = overlay ]; then
                  # The flashed APK cannot be un-built from here. On the phone the
                  # line stays because it describes what is installed; on the
                  # desktop (no phone, no `settings`) it is just a build choice and
                  # Clear all must remove it.
                  if have_settings; then
                      kept_overlay=yes
                  else
                      del_conf "$id"
                  fi
                  continue
              fi
              # Same guard as `set`: with no phone there is nothing to restore, and
              # clearing the file is the whole job.
              if have_settings; then
                  apply_one "$id" "$(default_of "$id")" || rc=1
              fi
              del_conf "$id"
          done
          # Drop lines for addons that no longer exist (an older catalog shipped the
          # battery percentage and the clock seconds, which a GSI exposes itself).
          if [ -f "$CONF" ]; then
              for id in $(grep '^[A-Za-z]' "$CONF" 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f1); do
                  [ -n "$(default_of "$id")" ] || del_conf "$id"
              done
          fi
          mirror_conf
          say "+ live addons are back to their defaults; nothing is applied on boot"
          [ "$kept_overlay" = yes ] && say "  overlay addons stay as they are — the installed APK still has them"
          return $rc
      }
      
      cmd_status() { # key=value, the way apply.sh status reports
          for id in $(ids); do
              printf '%s=%s\n' "$id" "$(live_value "$id")"
          done
      }
      
      usage() {
          say "usage: addons.sh list | set ID=VALUE ... | apply [ID ...] | reset | status"
          say "       addons.sh restore-conf"
      }
      
      cmd=${1:-list}
      [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
      
      case "$cmd" in
          list)         cmd_list ;;
          set)          cmd_set "$@" ;;
          apply)        cmd_apply "$@" ;;
          reset)        cmd_reset ;;
          status)       cmd_status ;;
          restore-conf) restore_conf ;;
          catalog)      catalog ;;
          help|-h|--help) usage ;;
          *)
              say "x unknown command: $cmd"
              usage
              exit 2 ;;
      esac
      exit $?

func (a *App) handleAddons(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  doc, err := a.addonsDoc()
  if err != nil {
    writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
    return
  }
  writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, doc)
}
---
func (a *App) handleAddonsSave(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  var body struct {
    Values map[string]string `json:"values"`
    Reset  bool              `json:"reset"`
  }
  if !decode(w, r, &body) {
    return
  }

  if body.Reset {
    if _, err := a.runAddons("reset"); err != nil {
      writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
      return
    }
  } else {
    pairs := make([]string, 0, len(body.Values))
    for id, value := range body.Values {
      if !addonID.MatchString(id) {
        writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "not an addon id: "+id)
        return
      }
      if !addonChoice.MatchString(value) {
        writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "not an addon value: "+value)
        return
      }
      pairs = append(pairs, id+"="+value)
    }
    sort.Strings(pairs)
    if len(pairs) > 0 {
      if _, err := a.runAddons(append([]string{"set"}, pairs...)...); err != nil {
        writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
        return
      }
    }
  }

  doc, err := a.addonsDoc()
  if err != nil {
    writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
    return
  }
  writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, doc)
}

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The config.env form
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // handleConfigApply saves the rows the form changed. Edits are addressed by
      // line number AND key, so a save from a stale page fails loudly instead of
      // rewriting whatever moved into that line.
      func (a *App) handleConfigApply(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Edits []ConfigEdit `json:"edits"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "no clone selected")
          return
        }
        path := filepath.Join(root, "config.env")
        text, err := os.ReadFile(path)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "config.env is missing — run Build once, or Clean --all to recreate it")
          return
        }
      
        next, err := applyConfigEdits(string(text), body.Edits)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, err.Error())
          return
        }
        if next != string(text) {
          if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(next), 0o644); err != nil {
            writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
            return
          }
        }
        doc, _ := parseConfig(next)
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"config": doc, "text": next})
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Addons
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // An addon is a tweak the module owns: either a Settings value it writes on the
      // phone (the volume panel side, the screen timeout) or, for the overlay addons,
      // a resource the build bakes into the APK. Either way the choice lives in
      // src/module/addons.conf instead of config.env, which is why the tab is
      // separate from the config form.
      //
      // The catalog and the rules are in src/webui/addons.sh — the same file the
      // module ships as webroot/addons.sh and the phone's page runs — so this tab is
      // a form over that script rather than a second list to keep in sync. The script
      // is told where the clone's src/module/addons.conf is, which is the file
      // build.sh packs into the module.
      const addonsScript = "src/webui/addons.sh"
      
      // The script validates both; these only keep a request from being turned into
      // shell syntax. The page can only send what it rendered, but a request is not
      // the page.
      var (
        addonID     = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9_]+$`)
        addonChoice = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9]+$`)
      )
      
      // addonsEnv points the helper at the clone instead of an installed module.
      // Paths are POSIX: Git Bash on Windows reads a backslash as an escape.
      func (a *App) addonsEnv() []string {
        root := filepath.ToSlash(a.Root())
        return []string{
          "ADDONS_DIR=" + root,
          "ADDONS_CONF=" + root + "/src/module/addons.conf",
        }
      }
      
      func (a *App) runAddons(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          return nil, errors.New("no clone selected")
        }
        bash := a.Bash()
        if !fileExists(bash) {
          return nil, errors.New("bash was not found — pick it with the Path chip")
        }
        // Short on purpose: six `settings` calls on a phone, and no work at all in
        // the clone.
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bash, append([]string{addonsScript}, args...)...)
        // Hide the console Windows would otherwise flash for this child. The tab
        // runs the helper on open and on every save, so an un-hidden window is a
        // black rectangle blinking at the user each time.
        setProcAttr(cmd)
        cmd.Dir = root
        // A stale ADDONS_* in the app's own environment would otherwise win over
        // the paths below (Windows keeps the first duplicate in the block).
        env := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+2)
        for _, kv := range os.Environ() {
          if strings.HasPrefix(kv, "ADDONS_") {
            continue
          }
          env = append(env, kv)
        }
        cmd.Env = append(env, a.addonsEnv()...)
        var stderr strings.Builder
        cmd.Stderr = &stderr
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
          msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
          if msg == "" {
            msg = err.Error()
          }
          return nil, errors.New(msg)
        }
        return out, nil
      }
      
      // addonsDoc is the helper's own JSON, passed through: the page renders exactly
      // what the module will enforce.
      func (a *App) addonsDoc() (map[string]any, error) {
        out, err := a.runAddons("list")
        if err != nil {
          return nil, err
        }
        var doc map[string]any
        if err := json.Unmarshal(out, &doc); err != nil {
          return nil, fmt.Errorf("the addons helper did not return JSON: %v", err)
        }
        return doc, nil
      }
      
      func (a *App) handleAddons(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        doc, err := a.addonsDoc()
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, doc)
      }
      
      // handleAddonsSave stores the choices, which is also what applies them: the
      // script's `set` writes the file and makes the values true on the phone when
      // there is one. A phone is not required — the file is what the build packs.
      func (a *App) handleAddonsSave(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Values map[string]string `json:"values"`
          Reset  bool              `json:"reset"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
      
        if body.Reset {
          if _, err := a.runAddons("reset"); err != nil {
            writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
            return
          }
        } else {
          pairs := make([]string, 0, len(body.Values))
          for id, value := range body.Values {
            if !addonID.MatchString(id) {
              writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "not an addon id: "+id)
              return
            }
            if !addonChoice.MatchString(value) {
              writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "not an addon value: "+value)
              return
            }
            pairs = append(pairs, id+"="+value)
          }
          sort.Strings(pairs)
          if len(pairs) > 0 {
            if _, err := a.runAddons(append([]string{"set"}, pairs...)...); err != nil {
              writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
              return
            }
          }
        }
      
        doc, err := a.addonsDoc()
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, doc)
      }

      func (a *App) handleAdb(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Command      string `json:"command"`
          Preset       string `json:"preset"`
          Codename     string `json:"codename"`

      // DetectCandidate is one property that answered with a value, and what that
      // property is. The Device tab offers them in this order.
      type DetectCandidate struct {
        Prop  string `json:"prop"`
        Note  string `json:"note"`
        Value string `json:"value"`
      }
      
      // DetectResult is what "Detect from device" found: the answer it would use, and
      // every other command that also had something to say.
      type DetectResult struct {
        Codename     string            `json:"codename"`
        Manufacturer string            `json:"manufacturer"`
        Model        string            `json:"model"`
        Prop         string            `json:"prop"`
        Candidates   []DetectCandidate `json:"candidates"`
      }
      
      // codenameProps is the order the codename is looked for in. The vendor
      // partition keeps the stock name on most GSIs, so it is asked first;
      // ro.product.device is near the end because on a GSI it only names the GSI
      // itself. No single property is right on every phone — which is why the answer
      // is offered with the command that produced it, and the others are one click
      // away in the UI.
      var codenameProps = []DetectCandidate{
        {Prop: "ro.product.vendor.device", Note: "vendor partition — the usual survivor on a GSI"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.odm.device", Note: "ODM partition"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.bootimage.device", Note: "boot image"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.device", Note: "system property — often the GSI's own name"},
        {Prop: "ro.build.product", Note: "legacy build.prop name"},
      }
      
      // detectCodenames asks every candidate property and keeps the answers that
      // mean something, in priority order and without duplicates. Every one is asked,
      // not just the first that answers: the ones that had a value are what "Wrong?
      // Try another command" cycles through, and that has to work without another
      // round trip to the phone.
      func detectCodenames(probe func(string) string) []DetectCandidate {
        out := []DetectCandidate{}
        seen := make(map[string]bool, len(codenameProps))
        for _, c := range codenameProps {
          value := probe(c.Prop)
          if value == "" || strings.EqualFold(value, "unknown") || seen[value] {
            continue
          }
          seen[value] = true
          out = append(out, DetectCandidate{Prop: c.Prop, Note: c.Note, Value: value})
        }
        return out
      }
      
      // handleAdbDetect asks the phone for the values the presets need, so the user
      // does not have to read one command's output and type it into another box.
      func (a *App) handleAdbDetect(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Serial string `json:"serial"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        adb := a.adbPath()
        if adb == "" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "adb is not installed yet — use \"Download platform-tools\" first")
          return
        }
        serial, err := a.deviceSerialFor(body.Serial)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        probe := func(prop string) string {
          out, err := runCapture(adb, "-s", serial, "shell", "getprop", prop)
          if err != nil {
            return ""
          }
          return strings.TrimSpace(out)
        }
      
        res := DetectResult{Candidates: []DetectCandidate{}}
        res.Manufacturer = probe("ro.product.manufacturer")
        res.Model = probe("ro.product.model")
        res.Candidates = detectCodenames(probe)
        if len(res.Candidates) > 0 {
          res.Codename = res.Candidates[0].Value
          res.Prop = res.Candidates[0].Prop
        }
      
        if res.Codename == "" && res.Manufacturer == "" && res.Model == "" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, "the phone did not answer — is it connected and authorized? (adb devices)")
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, res)
      }
      
      // handleMatchProp ranks the properties this phone could be matched on, for the
      // Overlay activation section of the Config tab. The two getprop dumps are read
      // from the same selected phone as every other device action; nothing is written
      // here — the page stages the two config.env lines and the user saves them.
      func (a *App) handleMatchProp(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Serial string `json:"serial"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        adb := a.adbPath()
        if adb == "" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "adb is not installed yet — use \"Download platform-tools\" first")
          return
        }
        serial, err := a.deviceSerialFor(body.Serial)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
      
        // Values and SELinux areas come from two commands: `getprop -Z` prints the
        // area only, and both streams are one adb round trip each.
        valuesOut, err := runCapture(adb, "-s", serial, "shell", "getprop")
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, "the phone did not answer getprop: "+err.Error())
          return
        }
        // The labels are the second-best signal, never required: `getprop -Z` is
        // missing on old Android, and without it the ranking still works (the card
        // says readability is unchecked instead of refusing to answer).
        labels := map[string]string{}
        if labelsOut, err := runCapture(adb, "-s", serial, "shell", "getprop", "-Z"); err == nil {
          labels = parseGetpropLabels(labelsOut)
        }
      
        report := rankMatchProps(parseGetprop(valuesOut), labels)
        report.Serial = serial
        if report.Codename == "" && report.Model == "" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, "the phone reported no identity properties — is it still connected?")
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, report)
      }
      
      func lookupPreset(id string) (AdbPreset, bool) {
        for _, p := range adbPresets {
          if p.ID == id {
            return p, true
          }
        }
        return AdbPreset{}, false
      }
      
      // safeToken keeps a value from being pasted into a command box unexamined: it
      // is only ever used to fill {codename}/{manufacturer} in a preset.
      func safeToken(s string) string {
        s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
        if len(s) > 64 {
          return ""
        }
        for _, r := range s {
          switch {
          case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z', r >= '0' && r <= '9', r == '.', r == '_', r == '-':
          default:
            return ""
          }
        }
        return s
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Helpers
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      func runCapture(program string, args ...string) (string, error) {
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, program, args...)
        setProcAttr(cmd)
        out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
        return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), err
      }
      
      func decode(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
        return decodeLimit(w, r, dst, 1<<20)
      }
      
      // decodeLimit is the same for a body that is legitimately bigger than a config
      // form: saving a resource XML or a manifest.
      func decodeLimit(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any, limit int64) bool {
        r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, limit)
        dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
        dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
        if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "could not read the request: "+err.Error())
          return false
        }
        return true
      }
      
      func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, code int, v any) {
        w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
        w.WriteHeader(code)
        _ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
      }
      
      func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, code int, msg string) {
        writeJSON(w, code, map[string]string{"error": msg})
      }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay)
# =============================================================================
# Writes what Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay expects, from the same resources
# this project compiles into a module. TrebleDroid/vendor_hardware_overlay is
# the upstream it continues; the tree is identical, so a PR there works too.
#
#   <brand>/<model>/AndroidManifest.xml
#   <brand>/<model>/Android.mk
#   <brand>/<model>/res/values/*, res/values-land/*, res/xml/*
#   <brand>/<model>-SystemUI/…            (when src/systemui has resources)
#   _submission/HOW-TO-SUBMIT.md          (steps, checklist, what changed)
#   _submission/overlay.mk.lines          (the PRODUCT_PACKAGES lines to add)
#
# That tree is packed into out/<overlay>-hardware-overlay.zip by build.sh; a
# maintainer merges it into the repo, the GSI builds it, and the device gets the
# values without installing a module.
#
# Differences from the module build, on purpose:
#
#   * The match condition targets a property that exists on a stock device.
#     A module is matched by persist.sys.overlay.<codename>, which this project
#     sets itself at boot — a preinstalled overlay never sees it. So the
#     submission gates on ro.product.vendor.device (exact) by default.
#
#   * Resource names on the repo's blacklist (tests/blacklist) are dropped.
#     Those are user-preference resources the repo refuses to let an overlay
#     force; keeping them fails the repo's own test script.
#
#   * android:requiredSystemPropertyValue is compared with plain string
#     equality (AOSP FrameworkParsingPackageUtils#checkRequiredSystemProperties),
#     so no "*" or "+" globs: the value must be what the device reports.
#
# Sourced by build.sh (common.sh loaded, config.env sourced, identity derived).
# Standalone, with an optional config file (default: ./config.env):
#
#   ./stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh plan [config.env]  what would be written
#   ./stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh write <dir> [config.env] write the tree
# =============================================================================

# Sourced by build.sh, or run directly for the standalone commands below.
if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" != "$0" ] && [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
    echo "This is an internal build module — run ./build.sh instead." >&2
    return 1 2>/dev/null || exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The overlay repo's rules
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tests/blacklist of Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay (identical to upstream
# TrebleDroid's): resources an overlay may not define (they are user preferences
# or would break the device). A submission that defines one fails tests/tests.sh.
HW_BLACKLIST_ARGS=(
    config_useRoundIcon
    config_swipe_up_gesture_setting_available
    config_cameraDoubleTapPowerGestureEnabled
    config_cellBroadcastAppLinks
    config_doublePressOnPowerBehavior
    config_dozeComponent
    config_enableAutoPowerModes
    config_enableMultiUserUI
    config_mainBuiltInDisplayIsRound
    config_multiuserMaximumUsers
    config_screen_magnification_multi_tap_adjustment
    config_swipe_up_gesture_default
    config_allowAllRotations
    config_volumeAdjustmentForRemoteGroupSessions
    config_unplugTurnsOnScreen
)

hw_blacklist_re() {

- path: stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh
  content: |
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Tools
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      resolve_adb() {
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          adb="$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)"
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          for adb in "$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb" "$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb.exe"; do
              [ -x "$adb" ] && return 0
          done
          adb=""
          return 1
      }
      
      resolve_aapt2() {
          [ -n "$aapt2" ] && return 0
          local candidate
          for candidate in "$ROOT/stuff/tools/aapt2" "$ROOT/stuff/tools/aapt2.exe"; do
              [ -x "$candidate" ] && { aapt2="$candidate"; return 0; }
          done
          candidate="$(command -v aapt2 2>/dev/null || true)"
          [ -n "$candidate" ] && { aapt2="$candidate"; return 0; }
          return 1
      }
      
      # apk_string_res APK RESNAME — the default-config value of a string resource.
      apk_string_res() {
          "$aapt2" dump resources "$(winpath "$1")" 2>/dev/null | awk -v res="string/$2" '
              $1 == "resource" && $3 == res { want = 1; next }
              want && $1 == "resource" { want = 0 }
              want && /^[[:space:]]*\(\) / {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/^[[:space:]]*\(\) /, "", line)
                  gsub(/^"|"$/, "", line)
                  print line
                  exit
              }'
      }
      
      # apk_dimen_res APK RESNAME WANT_CONFIG — "unit value" as aapt2 prints it, e.g.
      # "px 113.0". WANT_CONFIG is "land" for the landscape qualifier, "" otherwise.
      apk_dimen_res() {
          "$aapt2" dump resources "$(winpath "$1")" 2>/dev/null | awk -v res="dimen/$2" -v want_cfg="${3:-}" '
              $1 == "resource" && $3 == res { want = 1; next }
              want && $1 == "resource" { want = 0 }
              want && /^[[:space:]]*\(/ {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/^[[:space:]]*\(/, "", line)
                  cfg = line; sub(/\).*/, "", cfg)
                  val = line; sub(/^[^(]*\)[[:space:]]*/, "", val)
                  if (cfg != want_cfg) next
                  if (val ~ /^@/) next
                  if (val ~ /px$/) { n = val; sub(/px$/, "", n); print "px " n; exit }
                  if (val ~ /dp$/) { n = val; sub(/dp$/, "", n); print "dp " n; exit }
              }'
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Device mode
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # </dev/null matters: adb inherits stdin, and a call made inside a `while read`
      # loop would otherwise eat the rest of the loop's input after the first pass.
      shel() { "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} shell "$1" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'; }
      
      # Overlay state needs root on some ROMs (HyperOS is one): the plain call returns
      # an error, which read as "no overlays" and silently fell back to the GSI's own
      # values. Every overlay query goes through these two.
      ovl_list() {
          local out
          out="$(shel 'cmd overlay list')"
          [ -n "$out" ] || out="$(shel 'su 0 cmd overlay list')"
          printf '%s' "$out"
      }
      ovl_dump() {
          local out
          out="$(shel 'cmd overlay dump')"
          [ -n "$out" ] || out="$(shel 'su 0 cmd overlay dump')"
          printf '%s' "$out"
      }
      
      # pull that also works for a root-only file (/vendor/overlay is one): adb pull
      # runs as the shell user, `su 0 cat` does not.
      pull_file() {
          local remote="$1" local_path="$2"
          "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} pull "$remote" "$(winpath "$local_path")" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
              && [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0
          "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} exec-out "su 0 cat '$remote'" >"$local_path" 2>/dev/null \
              && [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0
          return 1
      }
      
      # cmd overlay lookup needs the shell permission; fall back to su when a build
      # only allows root. An error string is a miss, not a value.
      lookup() {
          local out
          out="$(shel "cmd overlay lookup android $1")"
          case "$out" in
              ""|Error*|error*) out="$(shel "su 0 cmd overlay lookup android $1")" ;;
          esac
          case "$out" in
              Error*|error*) out="" ;;
          esac
          printf '%s' "$out"
      }
      
      # 113.0px / 24.0dp — the module wants px. dp is converted with the panel density
      # when it is known, and left alone (with a note) when it is not.
      dimen_to_px() {
          local raw="$1" unit n
          # `cmd overlay lookup` can answer with the reference it followed:
          # "@17105807 -> 118.0px". The number after the arrow is the value.
          case "$raw" in *"-> "*) raw="${raw##*-> }" ;; esac
          # `cmd overlay lookup` spells the density unit "dip" (28.0dip), so both
          # spellings have to be caught — reading "28.0dip" as px turned a 28dp bar
          # into a 28px answer.
          case "$raw" in
              *dip) unit="dp"; n="${raw%dip}" ;;
              *px) unit="px"; n="${raw%px}" ;;
              *dp) unit="dp"; n="${raw%dp}" ;;
              *) unit="px"; n="$raw" ;;
          esac
          if [ "$unit" = "dp" ]; then
              [ -n "$DENS" ] || return 1
              awk -v n="$n" -v d="$DENS" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", n * d / 160 + 0.5 }'
          else
              awk -v n="$n" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", n + 0.5 }'
          fi
      }
      
      pick_serial() {
          # One phone: use it. Several: ask, or stop with the list and the --device
          # spelling. See stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh for the states it understands.
          adb_pick_device "$adb" "$serial" "device-probe" || exit 1
          serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
      }
      
      probe_device() {
          resolve_adb || die "adb not found — install platform-tools, or pass --adb PATH"
          pick_serial
      
          local props size dens_out
          props="$(shel getprop)"
          prop() { printf '%s\n' "$props" | sed -n "s/^\[$1\]: \[\(.*\)\]$/\1/p" | head -n1; }
      
          size="$(shel 'wm size')"
          W="$(printf '%s\n' "$size" | sed -n 's/.*Physical size: \([0-9]*\)x[0-9]*.*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
          H="$(printf '%s\n' "$size" | sed -n 's/.*Physical size: [0-9]*x\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
          [ -n "$W" ] && [ -n "$H" ] || die "could not read the display size (wm size)"
      
          # `wm size` / `wm density` print an override only when one is set. The
          # override is what the framework resolves dp with, so the conversion below
          # has to use it; the physical number is kept for the note.
          dens_out="$(shel 'wm density')"
          DENS="$(printf '%s\n' "$dens_out" | sed -n 's/.*Physical density: \([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
          local dens_ovr size_ovr
          dens_ovr="$(printf '%s\n' "$dens_out" | sed -n 's/.*Override density: \([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
          if [ -n "$dens_ovr" ]; then
              DENS_PHYS="$DENS"
              DENS="$dens_ovr"
              note "the display density is overridden: physical ${DENS_PHYS}dpi, effective ${DENS}dpi. dp values are converted with the effective one, because that is what the framework resolved them with"
          fi
          size_ovr="$(printf '%s\n' "$size" | sed -n 's/.*Override size: \([0-9]*x[0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
          [ -z "$size_ovr" ] || note "the display size is overridden to ${size_ovr} (panel is ${W}x${H}); the px values below are what this ROM reports in that mode"
      
          # Some properties answer with a placeholder rather than the phone's name.
          # Measured on a Redmi Note 17 (HyperOS 3): ro.product.vendor.model was
          # "Xiaomi for arm64" and ro.product.vendor.device was "mivendor", while the
          # ODM property had the real ones. A generic value is never used when a real
          # one exists, and the order puts the partitions most likely to keep the
          # stock name first.
          generic_name() {
              local v lc
              v="${1:-}"
              lc="$(printf '%s' "$v" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
              case "$lc" in
                  ''|unknown|aosp*|*gsi*|*treble*|*arm64*|generic*|emulator*|mivendor|qssi*|sdk_*) return 0 ;;
              esac
              return 1
          }
          pick_prop() {
              local p v
              for p in "$@"; do
                  v="$(prop "$p")"
                  [ -n "$v" ] || continue
                  generic_name "$v" && continue
                  printf '%s' "$v"
                  return 0
              done
              return 1
          }
          MODEL="$(pick_prop ro.product.odm.model ro.product.vendor.model ro.product.model || true)"
          [ -n "$MODEL" ] || MODEL="$(prop ro.product.model)"
          CODENAME="$(pick_prop ro.product.odm.device ro.product.vendor.device ro.product.bootimage.device ro.product.device || true)"
          [ -n "$CODENAME" ] || CODENAME="$(prop ro.product.device)"
          [ -n "$CODENAME" ] || CODENAME="$(prop ro.build.product)"
      
          local flavor
          flavor="$(prop ro.build.flavor)"
          IS_GSI=0
          case "$flavor" in *gsi*|*GSI*) IS_GSI=1 ;; esac
          rom="$(prop ro.build.display.id)"
          [ -n "$rom" ] || rom="${flavor:-unknown ROM}"
      
          resolve_aapt2 || warn "aapt2 not found — overlay APKs cannot be read, only the runtime values"
      
          # This module patches the phh device overlay in place, so an enabled overlay
          # APK can be this tool's own output. Knowing which files those are is the
          # difference between "the ROM says 113px" and "we said 113px last build".
          local module_apks=""
          module_apks="$(shel 'ls /data/adb/modules/*/system/product/overlay/*.apk 2>/dev/null' | sed 's#.*/##' | sort -u)"
          # The glob has to be expanded by root's shell, not by the shell user's.
          [ -n "$module_apks" ] || module_apks="$(shel "su 0 sh -c 'ls /data/adb/modules/*/system/product/overlay/*.apk 2>/dev/null'" | sed 's#.*/##' | sort -u)"
          [ -z "$module_apks" ] || note "this module's own overlays are installed; a framework resource answer can be the module reading back its own value (those rows say so)"
      
          # ---- runtime: what the panel driver and the framework report -----------
          # dumpsys display is the only place that has the refresh modes and the
          # rounded-corner geometry. Both come from the display hardware, so they are
          # still right on a GSI.
          local display window
          display="$(shel 'dumpsys display')"
          window="$(shel 'dumpsys window displays')"
      
          # The DisplayDeviceInfo block is one long line per display. A Samsung with a
          # DeX monitor, a TV over HDMI or a casting sink adds more of them, and none
          # of those describe the panel the overlay has to match. Prefer the one named
          # "Built-in Screen" and say so when there was more than one to choose from.
          local ddi ddi_all ddi_count ddi_name
          ddi_all="$(printf '%s\n' "$display" | grep 'DisplayDeviceInfo{' || true)"
          ddi_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ddi_all" | grep -c . || true)"
          ddi="$(printf '%s\n' "$ddi_all" | grep -i -m1 'DisplayDeviceInfo{"[^"]*\(built-in\|internal\)' || true)"
          [ -n "$ddi" ] || ddi="$(printf '%s\n' "$ddi_all" | head -n1)"
          if [ -z "$ddi" ]; then
              warn "dumpsys display printed no DisplayDeviceInfo — refresh rates and corners unknown"
          elif [ "${ddi_count:-0}" -gt 1 ]; then
              ddi_name="$(printf '%s' "$ddi" | sed 's/.*DisplayDeviceInfo{"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/')"
              warn "dumpsys display lists ${ddi_count} displays — the built-in panel (\"${ddi_name}\") was used; the others (a monitor, a cast sink) are not what the overlay matches"
          fi
      
          # ---- corner radius ----------------------------------------------------
          # The panel geometry is what Android is drawing, so it is reported first and
          # preselected. The dimen is what the ROM asks for; the two agreed on the
          # reference Xiaomi (144px) and disagreed on a Samsung custom ROM (panel
          # 100px, dimen 50px), which is why both stay as rows.
          local corners radius_line radius
          corners="$(printf '%s\n' "$ddi" | grep -o 'roundedCorners RoundedCorners{.*' || true)"
          [ -n "$corners" ] || corners="$(printf '%s\n' "$window" | grep -m1 -o 'mRoundedCorners=RoundedCorners{.*' || true)"
          if [ -n "$corners" ]; then
              # Every corner usually has the same radius; the largest is the one the
              # overlay's single value has to match, and a phone with different top
              # and bottom corners keeps the top one visible in the status bar.
              radius="$(printf '%s\n' "$corners" | grep -o 'radius=[0-9.]*' | sed 's/radius=//' \
                  | awk 'BEGIN { m = 0 } { v = $1 + 0; if (v > m) m = v } END { if (m > 0) printf "%d", m + 0.5 }')"
              radius_line="$(printf '%s\n' "$corners" | grep -o 'position=[A-Za-z]*' | sed 's/position=//' | tr '\n' ' ')"
              if [ -n "$radius" ] && [ "$radius" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
                  add_fact ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS "Corner radius" "px" "$radius" \
                      "display hardware" "high" "runtime" \
                      "dumpsys display: RoundedCorners radius ${radius}px (${radius_line% }); this is the panel geometry the framework is drawing" || true
              fi
          else
