      # The list is a snapshot: a phone can be listed as ready and still not open. Ask
      # adb to open it, bounded like everything else.
      adb_device_alive() {
          local adb="$1" serial="$2" dir status
          dir="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/adb-device.$$")"
          mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null
          adb_device_exec 100 "$dir/state" "$adb" -s "$serial" get-state
          status=$?
          rm -rf "$dir"
          return "$status"
      }
      
      adb_pick_device() {
          local adb="$1" want="$2" prog="$3"
          local attached ready ready_count state serial sleeping waited=0
      
          adb_device_list "$adb" || {
              printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-adb did not answer}" >&2
              return 1
          }
          attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
      
          # Wireless adb and a phone that was just plugged in show "connecting" for a
          # moment. Waiting a couple of seconds turns that into the phone the user
          # means, instead of "nothing is ready" and a retry they have to time.
          while [ -n "$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "connecting"')" ] && [ "$waited" -lt 25 ]; do
              sleep 0.2
              waited=$((waited + 1))
              adb_device_list "$adb" || break
              attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
          done
      
          ready="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "device"')"
          ready_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
      
          serial=""
          if [ -n "$want" ]; then
              # An explicit serial is used as typed, but it still has to be attached:
              # otherwise adb's own "device not found" is the only explanation the
              # user gets, with no hint about what is actually plugged in.
              state="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s { print $2; exit }')"
              case "$state" in
                  device) serial="$want" ;;
                  '')
                      printf '%s: %s is not attached.\n' "$prog" "$want" >&2
                      ;;
                  *)
                      printf '%s: %s is attached but %s.\n' "$prog" "$want" "$state" >&2
                      ;;
              esac
              if [ -z "$serial" ]; then
                  if [ -n "$attached" ]; then
                      printf 'Attached devices:\n' >&2
                      printf '%s\n' "$attached" | adb_device_table >&2
                      adb_device_advice "$attached" >&2
                  else
                      printf 'No device is attached — plug one in and allow USB debugging.\n' >&2
                      [ -z "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-}" ] || printf '  %s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" >&2
                  fi
                  return 1
              fi
          elif [ "$ready_count" -eq 0 ]; then
              [ -z "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-}" ] || printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" >&2
              if [ -n "$attached" ]; then
                  printf '%s: no device is ready to talk to:\n' "$prog" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$attached" | adb_device_table >&2
              else
                  printf '%s: no device in adb devices — plug the phone in and allow USB debugging.\n' "$prog" >&2
              fi
              adb_device_advice "$attached" >&2
              return 1
          elif [ "$ready_count" -eq 1 ]; then
              serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | awk '{print $1}' | head -n1)"
              sleeping="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 != "device" { print $1 " (" $2 ")" }' | tr '\n' ' ')"
              [ -z "$sleeping" ] || printf '%s: using %s; not ready: %s\n' "$prog" "$serial" "${sleeping% }" >&2
          else
              # Several phones. Ask when there is a terminal to ask on; never guess,
              # because picking the wrong one is how the wrong phone gets written to.
              if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s: %d devices are ready:\n' "$prog" "$ready_count" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2
                  printf '%s: choose one with --device SERIAL\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
              if ! serial="$(adb_device_choose "$ready")"; then
                  printf '%s: no device chosen.\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
          fi
      
          # The list is a snapshot; this is the check that adb can actually open it.
          adb_device_alive "$adb" "$serial"
          case $? in
              0) ;;
              124)
                  printf '%s: %s is listed as ready but adb did not answer within 10s — run adb kill-server.\n' "$prog" "$serial" >&2
                  return 1
                  ;;
              *)
                  printf '%s: %s is listed as ready but did not answer get-state — replug it.\n' "$prog" "$serial" >&2
                  return 1
                  ;;
          esac
          DEVICE_SERIAL="$serial"
          return 0
      }

- path: stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh — firmware mode has to answer from the ROM
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The failure this pins: a Xiaomi ROM puts the sensor geometry in
      // vendor/build.prop as the FOD rectangle properties, not in an overlay APK. The
      // probe used to list only the first 40 *.prop files (a real tree has hundreds,
      // starting with system_ext's per-app cust.prop) and never turned the pair into a
      // candidate at all, so a full super.img answered nothing while the same phone
      // over adb answered 540,2198,89 from the very same property.
      //
      // No phone and no aapt2 are involved: the tree is a few text files.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const probe = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'udfps-probe.sh');
      
      function tree(files) {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'udfps-fw-'));
        for (const [rel, body] of Object.entries(files)) {
          const path = join(dir, rel);
          mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
          writeFileSync(path, body);
        }
        return dir;
      }
      
      function run(dir) {
        const out = execFileSync('bash', [probe, '--firmware', dir, '--json'], {
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          env: { ...process.env, TERM: 'dumb' },
        });
        return JSON.parse(out);
      }
      
      // The zephyr (Redmi Note 17 4G) values, exactly as vendor/build.prop ships them.
      const ZEPHYR = `ro.hardware.fp.fod=true
      ro.hardware.fp.fod.location=low
      persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=451,2109
      persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=178,178
      `;
      
      test('the rectangle in vendor/build.prop is an answer, and the arithmetic is the rectangle centre', () => {
        const dir = tree({ 'vendor/build.prop': ZEPHYR });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        const c = report.candidates[0];
        assert.equal(c.source, 'firmware-fod-props');
        assert.equal(c.x, 540);
        assert.equal(c.y, 2198);
        assert.equal(c.radius, 89);
        assert.equal(c.confidence, 'high');
        assert.equal(report.chosen.x, 540, 'the answer has to be chosen, not only listed');
        assert.match(c.detail, /location\.X_Y=451,2109/);
      });
      
      // A tree carries hundreds of per-app .prop files; the vendor build.prop has to
      // be read even when it is not in the first handful find returns.
      test('a build.prop behind hundreds of other .prop files is still read', () => {
        const files = {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 220; i += 1) {
          const name = `system_ext/etc/cust/${String(i).padStart(3, '0')}/cust.prop`;
          files[name] = `ro.cust.slot=${i}\n`;
        }
        files['vendor/build.prop'] = ZEPHYR;
        const report = run(tree(files));
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        assert.equal(report.chosen.x, 540);
      });
      
      // Android 8 shipped the same pair without the vendor segment.
      test('the pre-vendor property names are read too', () => {
        const dir = tree({
          'vendor/build.prop': 'persist.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=300,1800\npersist.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=100,120\n',
        });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        assert.deepEqual(
          [report.chosen.x, report.chosen.y, report.chosen.radius],
          [350, 1860, 50]
        );
      });
      
      // A rectangle with no size is not a sensor position; inventing one would put
      // the icon where no finger can reach.
      test('an unusable pair is refused with a warning, not turned into a guess', () => {
        const dir = tree({
          'vendor/build.prop': 'persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=0,0\npersist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=0,0\n',
        });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 0);
        assert.equal(report.chosen, null);
        assert.ok(report.warnings.length > 0, 'the refusal has to be visible');
      });
      
      test('a tree with nothing to read answers nothing instead of failing', () => {
        const report = run(tree({ 'system/build.prop': 'ro.product.device=zephyr\n' }));
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 0);
        assert.equal(report.chosen, null);
        assert.equal(report.mode, 'firmware');
      });
      
      // The probe is also run through the app, which passes an absolute folder: the
      // paths it prints have to be usable, not a temp dir from this test.
      test('the probe still names the source file it answered from', () => {
        const dir = tree({ 'vendor/build.prop': ZEPHYR });
        const report = run(dir);
        const detail = report.candidates[0].detail;
        assert.ok(detail.startsWith(dir), `detail does not name the tree: ${detail}`);
      });

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# =============================================================================\n# config-edit.sh — read and write one key of config.env\n# =============================================================================\n# Sourced by the terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh) and by\n# stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh. The probes carry their own copy of the writer\n# because they are shipped standalone; anything new should source this.\n#\n# The file is the source of truth and stays hand-editable: these helpers rewrite\n# one line, keep the indentation, keep the quoting the line already used, and\n# turn a commented-out KEY= line into a live one (that is what \"enable it\"\n# means). Nothing here validates values — `./build.sh check` does that.\n# =============================================================================\n\n: \"${ROOT:?stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh must be sourced with ROOT set}\"\n\n# cfg_file -> the file the helpers act on, so a test can point somewhere else.\ncfg_file() {\n    printf '%s' \"${CFG_FILE:-${CONFIG_FILE:-$ROOT/config.env}}\"\n}\n\n# cfg_unquote VALUE -> the value without the quotes config.env puts around text.\ncfg_unquote() {\n    local v=\"$1\"\n    case \"$v\" in\n        \\\"*\\\") v=\"${v#\\\"}\"; v=\"${v%\\\"}\" ;;\n        \\'*\\') v=\"${v#\\'}\"; v=\"${v%\\'}\" ;;\n    esac\n    printf '%s' \"$v\"\n}\n\n# cfg_quote VALUE -> a value config.env can be sourced from.\n# Plain words stay bare, as they are in the file today; anything a shell would\n# split on, or anything that was already quoted, gets double quotes.\ncfg_quote() {\n    local value=\"$1\" force=\"${2:-0}\"\n    case \"$value\" in\n        \"\") printf '\"\"'; return 0 ;;\n    esac\n    if [ \"$force\" != \"1\" ]; then\n        case \"$value\" in\n            *[[:space:]]*|*'#'*|*'\"'*|*\"'\"*|*'$'*|*'`'*|*'\\'*) ;;\n            *) printf '%s' \"$value\"; return 0 ;;\n        esac\n    fi\n    value=\"${value//\\\\/\\\\\\\\}\"\n    value=\"${value//\\\"/\\\\\\\"}\"\n    printf '\"%s\"' \"$value\"\n}\n\n# cfg_get KEY -> the live value, unquoted, empty when the key is absent or off.\ncfg_get() {\n    local key=\"$1\" file line value=\"\"\n    file=\"$(cfg_file)\"\n    [ -f \"$file\" ] || return 1\n    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n \"$line\" ]; do\n        line=\"${line%$'\\r'}\"\n        case \"$line\" in\n            \"$key=\"*) value=\"${line#*=}\" ;;\n        esac\n    done <\"$file\"\n    [ -n \"$value\" ] || return 0\n    cfg_unquote \"$value\"\n}\n\n# cfg_has KEY -> 0 when KEY= (or #KEY=) exists in the file at all.\ncfg_has() {\n    local key=\"$1\" file\n    file=\"$(cfg_file)\"\n    [ -f \"$file\" ] || return 1\n    grep -qE \"^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*${key}=\" \"$file\"\n}\n\n# cfg_rows -> one row per assignment, tab separated:\n#   key <TAB> active(0|1) <TAB> line number <TAB> section <TAB> value\n# A commented-out key is listed with active=0 so it can be turned on by name\n# instead of by hunting for the '#'. Prose that happens to end in '=' is not a\n# row: only `KEY=` and `#KEY=` (no space after the '#') count.\ncfg_rows() {\n    local file\n    file=\"$(cfg_file)\"\n    [ -f \"$file\" ] || return 1\n    awk '\n        /^#[[:space:]]*─/ {\n            sec = $0\n            sub(/^#[[:space:]]*/, \"\", sec)\n            gsub(/─/, \"\", sec)\n            gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, \"\", sec)\n            next\n        }\n        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ || /^#[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ {\n            line = $0\n            sub(/\\r$/, \"\", line)\n            key = line\n            sub(/=.*/, \"\", key)\n            active = 1\n            if (key ~ /^#/) { active = 0; sub(/^#/, \"\", key) }\n            value = substr(line, index(line, \"=\") + 1)\n            printf \"%s\\t%d\\t%d\\t%s\\t%s\\n\", key, active, NR, sec, value\n        }\n    ' \"$file\"\n}\n\n# cfg_sections -> the section titles in file order, one per line.\ncfg_sections() {\n    cfg_rows | awk -F'\\t' '!seen[$4]++ && $4 != \"\" { print $4 }'\n}\n\n# cfg_set KEY VALUE -> rewrite (or add, or enable) that one line.\n# Returns 0 when the file was written — also when the value was already right,\n# because the caller only cares that the key now holds it.\ncfg_set() {\n    local key=\"$1\" value=\"$2\" file tmp line rest quoted new done=0 wrote=0\n    file=\"$(cfg_file)\"\n    if [ -f \"$file\" ]; then\n        tmp=\"$file.tmp.$$\"\n        : >\"$tmp\" || return 1\n        while IFS= read -r line || [ -n \"$line\" ]; do\n            local keep=\"${line%$'\\r'}\"\n            if [ \"$done\" -eq 0 ]; then\n                case \"$keep\" in\n                    \"$key=\"*|\"#\"*\"$key=\"*)\n                        # Only the key itself, not a prose line that mentions it.\n                        local head=\"${keep%%=*}\"\n                        local bare=\"${head#\\#}\"\n                        bare=\"${bare#\"${bare%%[![:space:]]*}\"}\"\n                        if [ \"$bare\" = \"$key\" ]; then\n                            indent=\"${head%\"$bare\"}\"\n                            rest=\"${keep#*=}\"\n                            quoted=0\n                            case \"$rest\" in \\\"*) quoted=1 ;; esac\n                            new=\"${indent}${key}=$(cfg_quote \"$value\" \"$quoted\")\"\n                            printf '%s\\n' \"$new\" >>\"$tmp\"\n                            done=1\n                            wrote=1\n                            continue\n                        fi\n                        ;;\n                esac\n            fi\n            printf '%s\\n' \"$keep\" >>\"$tmp\"\n        done <\"$file\"\n        if [ \"$done\" -eq 0 ]; then\n            printf '%s=%s\\n' \"$key\" \"$(cfg_quote \"$value\")\" >>\"$tmp\"\n            wrote=1\n        fi\n        mv \"$tmp\" \"$file\" || { rm -f \"$tmp\"; return 1; }\n    else\n        printf '%s=%s\\n' \"$key\" \"$(cfg_quote \"$value\")\" >\"$file\" || return 1\n        wrote=1\n    fi\n    return 0\n}\n\n# cfg_summary -> the four lines the menu header shows, from the live file.\ncfg_identity() {\n    local manuf model code\n    manuf=\"$(cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)\"\n    model=\"$(cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)\"\n    code=\"$(cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)\"\n    if [ -z \"$manuf\" ] && [ -z \"$model\" ] && [ -z \"$code\" ]; then\n        printf 'no device set'\n        return 0\n    fi\n    printf '%s %s (%s)' \"$manuf\" \"$model\" \"$code\" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'\n}"
}

This reads the phone and\n# ranks every property the submission could use, saying what each one is\n# gambling on.\n#\n#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh                  # connected device, then ask\n#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --write          # take the answer it trusts\n#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --json           # for scripts\n#\n#   --device SERIAL   with more than one phone attached\n#   --adb PATH        adb is looked up on PATH and in stuff/tools/platform-tools\n#   --values FILE --labels FILE   rank saved `getprop` / `getprop -Z` output\n#                                 instead of asking a phone (tests, offline)\n#\n# Two rules decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable without\n# root: zygote has to be able to read the property (`getprop -Z` prints the\n# SELinux area; build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps),\n# and the value has to survive what is installed (vendor, odm and bootimage keep\n# the OEM value under a GSI; /system, /product and /system_ext do not). When no\n# property satisfies both, this says so instead of picking one — a match that\n# never holds is invisible.\n#\n# The same ranking lives in the desktop app (gui/matchprop.go). Change one,\n# change the other.\n# =============================================================================\n\nset -uo pipefail\n\n# adb is a Windows binary under Git Bash: without this its /system/... arguments\n# are rewritten into C:/Program Files/Git/system/... before adb ever sees them.\nexport MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1\n\nROOT=\"${ROOT:-$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../..\" && pwd)}\"\n. \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh\"\n\nadb=\"${ADB:-}\"\nserial=\"\"\nwant_json=0\nwant_write=0\nassume_yes=0\nvalues_file=\"\"\nlabels_file=\"\"\n\nusage() {\n    sed -n '3,33p' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\{0,1\\}//'\n}\n\ndie() { printf 'match-prop: %s\\n' \"$1\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --device) serial=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --adb) adb=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --values) values_file=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --labels) labels_file=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --json) want_json=1; shift ;;\n        --write) want_write=1; shift ;;\n        -y|--yes) assume_yes=1; want_write=1; shift ;;\n        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;\n        *) die \"unknown option: $1 (try --help)\" ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\ntmpdir=\"$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t matchprop)\"\ncleanup() { rm -rf \"$tmpdir\"; }\ntrap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# The two getprop dumps, as `key<TAB>value` files\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# `getprop` prints `[key]: [value]`; some ROMs mix warnings into the same\n# stream, and those lines are skipped rather than parsed into nonsense.\nparse_props() {\n    awk '\n        {\n            sub(/\\r$/, \"\")\n            if ($0 !~ /^\\[.*\\]: \\[.*\\]$/) next\n            i = index($0, \"]: [\")\n            if (i <= 2) next\n            key = substr($0, 2, i - 2)\n            val = substr($0, i + 4, length($0) - i - 4)\n            printf \"%s\\t%s\\n\", key, val\n        }\n    ' \"$1\"\n}\n\n# prop_of <file> <key> -> the value, empty when absent.\nprop_of() {\n    [ -f \"$1\" ] || return 0\n    awk -F'\\t' -v k=\"$2\" '$1 == k { print $2; exit }' \"$1\"\n}\n\nresolve_adb() {\n    [ -n \"$adb\" ] && return 0\n    adb=\"$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n    [ -n \"$adb\" ] && return 0\n    local candidate\n    for candidate in \"$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb\" \"$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb.exe\"; do\n        [ -x \"$candidate\" ] && { adb=\"$candidate\"; return 0; }\n    done\n    adb=\"\"\n    return 1\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Reading the phone\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Multi-device selection is shared with the probes, so every device action asks\n# the same question and accepts the same --device value.\ncollect_from_device() {\n    . \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh\"\n    resolve_adb || die \"adb was not found — install platform-tools, or pass --adb PATH\"\n    adb_pick_device \"$adb\" \"$serial\" match-prop || exit 1\n    serial=\"$DEVICE_SERIAL\"\n\n    \"$adb\" -s \"$serial\" shell getprop </dev/null 2>/dev/null | parse_props >\"$tmpdir/values\"\n    [ -s \"$tmpdir/values\" ] || die \"the phone did not answer getprop — is it connected and authorized?\"\n    # The areas are the second-best signal, never required: `getprop -Z` is\n    # missing on old Android, and without it the ranking still works.\n    \"$adb\" -s \"$serial\" shell getprop -Z </dev/null 2>/dev/null | parse_props >\"$tmpdir/labels\"\n    : >\"$tmpdir/labels.ok\"\n}\n\ncollect_from_files() {\n    [ -f \"$values_file\" ] || die \"--values: no such file: $values_file\"\n    parse_props \"$values_file\" >\"$tmpdir/values\"\n    [ -s \"$tmpdir/values\" ] || die \"--values: nothing that looks like getprop output in $values_file\"\n    if [ -n \"$labels_file\" ]; then\n        [ -f \"$labels_file\" ] || die \"--labels: no such file: $labels_file\"\n        parse_props \"$labels_file\" >\"$tmpdir/labels\"\n        : >\"$tmpdir/labels.ok\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ==PART2=="
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# config-edit.sh — read and write one key of config.env
# =============================================================================
# Sourced by the terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh) and by
# stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh. The probes carry their own copy of the writer
# because they are shipped standalone; anything new should source this.
#
# The file is the source of truth and stays hand-editable: these helpers rewrite
# one line, keep the indentation, keep the quoting the line already used, and
# turn a commented-out KEY= line into a live one (that is what "enable it"
# means). Nothing here validates values — `./build.sh check` does that.
# =============================================================================

: "${ROOT:?stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh must be sourced with ROOT set}"

# cfg_file -> the file the helpers act on, so a test can point somewhere else.
cfg_file() {
    printf '%s' "${CFG_FILE:-${CONFIG_FILE:-$ROOT/config.env}}"
}

# cfg_unquote VALUE -> the value without the quotes config.env puts around text.
cfg_unquote() {
    local v="$1"
    case "$v" in
        \"*\") v="${v#\"}"; v="${v%\"}" ;;
        \'*\') v="${v#\'}"; v="${v%\'}" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

# cfg_quote VALUE -> a value config.env can be sourced from.
# Plain words stay bare, as they are in the file today; anything a shell would
# split on, or anything that was already quoted, gets double quotes.
cfg_quote() {
    local value="$1" force="${2:-0}"
    case "$value" in
        "") printf '""'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$force" != "1" ]; then
        case "$value" in
            *[[:space:]]*|*'#'*|*'"'*|*"'"*|*'$'*|*'`'*|*'\'*) ;;
            *) printf '%s' "$value"; return 0 ;;
        esac
    fi
    value="${value//\\/\\\\}"
    value="${value//\"/\\\"}"
    printf '"%s"' "$value"
}

# cfg_get KEY -> the live value, unquoted, empty when the key is absent or off.
cfg_get() {
    local key="$1" file line value=""
    file="$(cfg_file)"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        case "$line" in
            "$key="*) value="${line#*=}" ;;
        esac
    done <"$file"
    [ -n "$value" ] || return 0
    cfg_unquote "$value"
}

# cfg_has KEY -> 0 when KEY= (or #KEY=) exists in the file at all.
cfg_has() {
    local key="$1" file
    file="$(cfg_file)"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
    grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*${key}=" "$file"
}

# cfg_rows -> one row per assignment, tab separated:
#   key <TAB> active(0|1) <TAB> line number <TAB> section <TAB> value
# A commented-out key is listed with active=0 so it can be turned on by name
# instead of by hunting for the '#'. Prose that happens to end in '=' is not a
# row: only `KEY=` and `#KEY=` (no space after the '#') count.
cfg_rows() {
    local file
    file="$(cfg_file)"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
    awk '
        /^#[[:space:]]*─/ {
            sec = $0
            sub(/^#[[:space:]]*/, "", sec)
            gsub(/─/, "", sec)
            gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", sec)
            next
        }
        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ || /^#[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ {
            line = $0
            sub(/\r$/, "", line)
            key = line
            sub(/=.*/, "", key)
            active = 1
            if (key ~ /^#/) { active = 0; sub(/^#/, "", key) }
            value = substr(line, index(line, "=") + 1)
            printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\n", key, active, NR, sec, value
        }
    ' "$file"
}

# cfg_sections -> the section titles in file order, one per line.
cfg_sections() {
    cfg_rows | awk -F'\t' '!seen[$4]++ && $4 != "" { print $4 }'
}

# cfg_set KEY VALUE -> rewrite (or add, or enable) that one line.
# Returns 0 when the file was written — also when the value was already right,
# because the caller only cares that the key now holds it.
cfg_set() {

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # match-prop.sh — which property should the submitted overlay match on?
      # =============================================================================
      # The overlay repo compares android:requiredSystemPropertyName/Value with plain
      # string equality, and getting it wrong is silent: the overlay installs, `cmd
      # overlay list` shows it enabled, and nothing changes. This reads the phone and
      # ranks every property the submission could use, saying what each one is
      # gambling on.
      #
      #   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh                  # connected device, then ask
      #   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --write          # take the answer it trusts
      #   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --json           # for scripts
      #
      #   --device SERIAL   with more than one phone attached
      #   --adb PATH        adb is looked up on PATH and in stuff/tools/platform-tools
      #   --values FILE --labels FILE   rank saved `getprop` / `getprop -Z` output
      #                                 instead of asking a phone (tests, offline)
      #
      # Two rules decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable without
      # root: zygote has to be able to read the property (`getprop -Z` prints the
      # SELinux area; build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps),
      # and the value has to survive what is installed (vendor, odm and bootimage keep
      # the OEM value under a GSI; /system, /product and /system_ext do not). When no
      # property satisfies both, this says so instead of picking one — a match that
      # never holds is invisible.
      #
      # The same ranking lives in the desktop app (gui/matchprop.go). Change one,
      # change the other.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -uo pipefail
      
      # adb is a Windows binary under Git Bash: without this its /system/... arguments
      # are rewritten into C:/Program Files/Git/system/... before adb ever sees them.
      export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1
      
      ROOT="${ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      
      adb="${ADB:-}"
      serial=""
      want_json=0
      want_write=0
      assume_yes=0
      values_file=""
      labels_file=""
      
      usage() {
          sed -n '3,33p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
      }
      
      die() { printf 'match-prop: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
      
      while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
          case "$1" in
              --device) serial="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --adb) adb="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --values) values_file="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --labels) labels_file="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --json) want_json=1; shift ;;
              --write) want_write=1; shift ;;
              -y|--yes) assume_yes=1; want_write=1; shift ;;
              -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
              *) die "unknown option: $1 (try --help)" ;;
          esac
      done
      
      tmpdir="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t matchprop)"
      cleanup() { rm -rf "$tmpdir"; }
      trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The two getprop dumps, as `key<TAB>value` files
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # `getprop` prints `[key]: [value]`; some ROMs mix warnings into the same
      # stream, and those lines are skipped rather than parsed into nonsense.
      parse_props() {
          awk '
              {
                  sub(/\r$/, "")
                  if ($0 !~ /^\[.*\]: \[.*\]$/) next
                  i = index($0, "]: [")
                  if (i <= 2) next
                  key = substr($0, 2, i - 2)
                  val = substr($0, i + 4, length($0) - i - 4)
                  printf "%s\t%s\n", key, val
              }
          ' "$1"
      }
      
      # prop_of <file> <key> -> the value, empty when absent.
      prop_of() {
          [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
          awk -F'\t' -v k="$2" '$1 == k { print $2; exit }' "$1"
      }
      
      resolve_adb() {
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          adb="$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)"
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          local candidate
          for candidate in "$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb" "$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb.exe"; do
              [ -x "$candidate" ] && { adb="$candidate"; return 0; }
          done
          adb=""
          return 1
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Reading the phone
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Multi-device selection is shared with the probes, so every device action asks
      # the same question and accepts the same --device value.
      collect_from_device() {
          . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"
          resolve_adb || die "adb was not found — install platform-tools, or pass --adb PATH"
          adb_pick_device "$adb" "$serial" match-prop || exit 1
          serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
      
          "$adb" -s "$serial" shell getprop </dev/null 2>/dev/null | parse_props >"$tmpdir/values"
          [ -s "$tmpdir/values" ] || die "the phone did not answer getprop — is it connected and authorized?"
          # The areas are the second-best signal, never required: `getprop -Z` is
          # missing on old Android, and without it the ranking still works.
          "$adb" -s "$serial" shell getprop -Z </dev/null 2>/dev/null | parse_props >"$tmpdir/labels"
          : >"$tmpdir/labels.ok"
      }
      
      collect_from_files() {
          [ -f "$values_file" ] || die "--values: no such file: $values_file"

                      new="${indent}${key}=$(cfg_quote "$value" "$quoted")"
                      printf '%s\n' "$new" >>"$tmp"
                      done=1
                      wrote=1
                      continue
                  fi
                  printf '%s\n' "$keep" >>"$tmp"
              done <"$file"
              if [ "$done" -eq 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$(cfg_quote "$value")" >>"$tmp"
                  wrote=1
              fi
              mv "$tmp" "$file" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
          else
              printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$(cfg_quote "$value")" >"$file" || return 1
              wrote=1
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # cfg_summary -> the four lines the menu header shows, from the live file.
      cfg_identity() {
          local manuf model code
          manuf="$(cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)"
          model="$(cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)"
          code="$(cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)"
          if [ -z "$manuf" ] && [ -z "$model" ] && [ -z "$code" ]; then
              printf 'no device set'
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s %s (%s)' "$manuf" "$model" "$code" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'
      }

---verbs---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay — build implementation
# =============================================================================
# Executed by the root build.sh, which loads stuff/scripts/common.sh and
# stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh first and guarantees the toolchain is ready.
#
# Set by build.sh:  ROOT, TOOLS_DIR, BUILD_DIR, OUT_DIR, CHECK_MODE,
#                   ASSUME_YES, FORCE_VENDOR_HALS
# Edited by you:    config.env
#                   src/framework/res      framework overlay resources
#                   src/systemui/res       SystemUI overlay resources
#                   src/module/            customize.sh / service.sh / sepolicy.rule
#                   src/vendor/            optional vendor HAL files
#                   stuff/keys/            signing key + certificate
#
# Output:           out/apks/*.apk          signed overlays
#                   out/*.zip              flashable module + repo sources
# =============================================================================

if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
    echo "This is an internal build module — run ./build.sh instead." >&2
    exit 1
fi

cd "$ROOT" || exit 1

# Relative paths: native aapt2/zipalign on Windows may not open /c/... paths.
RES_DIR="${FRAMEWORK_RES#"$ROOT"/}"
SYSUI_RES_DIR="${SYSTEMUI_RES#"$ROOT"/}"
MODULE_SRC_REL="${MODULE_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
VENDOR_SRC_REL="${VENDOR_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
BUILD_REL="${BUILD_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
: "${DRY_RUN:=false}"

# Generators used by the build steps below.
source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/resources.sh"
source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/module.sh"
source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/manifest.sh"
source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/validate.sh"
source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh"

# Never die silently: an unexpected `set -e` abort says where and why.
trap 'err "Unexpected failure at line ${LINENO}: ${BASH_COMMAND}"; err "Re-run with: bash -x ./build.sh  and report the last lines"' ERR

# Ask something without ever aborting the build. When stdin is not an
# interactive terminal (IDE task, CI, launcher without a console, piped input)
# `read` fails — under `set -e` that used to kill the script mid-run.
ASK_REPLY=""
ask_reply() {
    local prompt="$1"
    ASK_REPLY=""
    $ASSUME_YES && return 0
    if ! read -r -p "$prompt" ASK_REPLY; then
        ASK_REPLY=""
        info "No terminal input available — using the default answer."
    fi
    return 0
}

# Run a build command, indent its output, and abort with a clear message if it
# fails. (A pipeline would report sed's status, not the tool's.)
run_or_die() {
    local label="$1"; shift
    local log="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/treble-build.$$.log"
    if "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; then
        [ -s "$log" ] && sed 's/^/  /' "$log"
        rm -f "$log"
        return 0
    fi
    [ -s "$log" ] && sed 's/^/  /' "$log"
    rm -f "$log"
    err "${label} failed"
    return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Target resource audit
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# An RRO that names a resource the target does not have is accepted by aapt2

- path: build.sh

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay Creator
      # =============================================================================
      # One command for everything. The first run installs whatever is missing,
      # then builds; later runs go straight to the build.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
      #   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
      #   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
      #   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
      #   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
      #   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
      #   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
      #
      #   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
      #   -h, --help                 this help
      #
      # On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
      # Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
      # drive — see docs/windows.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -e
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Project root
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      # Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
      # not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
      if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
      fi
      export ROOT
      cd "$ROOT"
      
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"
      
      # Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
      tools_on_path
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Options
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MODE="build"
      CHECK_MODE=false
      DRY_RUN=false
      ASSUME_YES=false
      FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
      CLEAN_ALL=false
      FORCE_RES=""
      ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false
      
      usage() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
          echo "    (none)             Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
          echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
          echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
          echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
          echo "    clean              Remove build output"
          echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
          echo ""
      }
      
      for arg in "$@"; do
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).
      wsl_guard
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Dispatch
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      case "$MODE" in
          doctor)
              if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
              ;;
      
          setup)
              banner "Setup — build tools"
              migrate_layout
              # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
              # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
              # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
              # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
              # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
              if $ASSUME_YES; then
                  ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
              else
                  ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
              fi
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          check)
              # Config validation only: no tools, no output.
              CHECK_MODE=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          clean)
              migrate_layout
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/clean.sh"
              ;;
      
          dryrun)
              # Needs config.env and the resource generators, no toolchain: the point
              # is to see the plan in seconds.
              DRY_RUN=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          build)
              # Move any files left in the old top-level layout into src/.
              migrate_layout
              if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Windows"
              elif $IS_TERMUX; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Termux"
              else
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Linux"
              fi
              # Installs only what is missing; prints a summary and returns non-zero
              # when the machine still cannot build.
              ensure_toolchain auto
              # The installer may just have created stuff/tools/, so refresh PATH.
              tools_on_path
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      esac

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# device-probe.sh — read the display settings an overlay has to match
# =============================================================================
# The overlay writes a handful of numbers that are properties of the panel, not
# style choices: the cutout path, the corner radius, the status bar height, the
# refresh rates. Guessing them puts content under a camera or leaves the clock
# off the edge, so this asks the phone (or an unpacked ROM) and keeps every
# answer with the source it came from.
#
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh                 # connected device
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --firmware DIR  # extracted ROM dump
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --json          # for the desktop app
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --write         # put the winners in config.env
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --power-profile # print res/xml/power_profile.xml
#
# --power-profile prints the compiled XML tree of the power profile (the
# desktop app turns it back into a file); everything else about the run goes to
# stderr.
#
# What answers, and how far to trust it:
#
#   runtime   dumpsys display / dumpsys window — what the panel driver and the
#             running framework report. Survives a GSI for anything the display
#             hardware tells Android (corners, refresh rates), but says nothing
#             about the OEM ROM once the OEM system partition is gone.
#   resource  cmd overlay lookup android:... — the value the framework is
#             serving right now. On a GSI that can be the GSI's own default, so
#             it is evidence of "what Android uses", not of "what the OEM chose".
#   firmware  aapt2 over framework-res.apk and the overlay APKs of an unpacked
#             ROM. The only source that still has the OEM's cutout path when a
#             GSI has replaced the system partition.
#
# Nothing here is root-only.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

# adb is a Windows binary under Git Bash: without this its /system/... arguments
# are rewritten into C:/Program Files/Git/system/... before adb ever sees them.
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1

winpath() {
    if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then cygpath -w "$1"; else printf '%s' "$1"; fi
}

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"

mode="device"
serial=""
want_json=0
want_write=0
power_mode=0
check_profile=0
adb="${ADB:-}"
aapt2="${AAPT2:-}"
fwdir=""

usage() {
    sed -n '3,39p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
=== udfps usage ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# udfps-probe.sh — find a device's in-display fingerprint (UDFPS) geometry
# =============================================================================
# UDFPS_X / UDFPS_Y / UDFPS_RADIUS in config.env are the sensor's centre and
# radius in px, written to android:array/config_udfps_sensor_props. Guessing
# them puts the lock-screen icon next to the sensor instead of on it, so this
# asks the phone (or a firmware dump) the same question several ways and says
# where each answer came from.
#
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh                 # connected device
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --firmware DIR  # extracted ROM dump
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --json          # for the desktop app
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --write         # put the winner in config.env
#
# Three situations, in the order the guide describes them:
#
#   1. OEM ROM on the phone. The vendor FOD properties and the preinstalled
#      device overlay are both present, so this is the strongest evidence.
#   2. GSI on the phone. The system partition is the GSI's, but /vendor and
#      /persist keep the OEM's properties, and the phh/device overlay that was
#      flashed with the GSI usually still carries the resource. Both are read
#      here; a value that came from an overlay this tool itself modified is
#      marked as such instead of being counted as independent.
#   3. Firmware files. Only useful once the images are unpacked: super.img
#      needs lpunpack before any APK or build.prop inside it can be read, so a
#      bare fastboot ROM reports what it is missing instead of guessing.
#
# Nothing here is root-only. The overlay APKs and properties it reads are
# world-readable on a normal boot.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

# adb is a Windows binary under Git Bash: without this its /system/... arguments
# are rewritten into C:/Program Files/Git/system/... before adb ever sees them.
# The local half of a pull is converted back with winpath() instead, because the
# same binary cannot open an MSYS /tmp path.
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1

winpath() {
    if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then cygpath -w "$1"; else printf '%s' "$1"; fi
}

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"

mode="device"
serial=""
want_json=0
want_write=0
adb="${ADB:-}"
aapt2="${AAPT2:-}"
fwdir=""
scan_all_apks=0

usage() {
    sed -n '3,30p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
}

die() { printf 'udfps-probe: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

#!/system/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay — module addons
# =============================================================================
# An addon is a tweak the *module* makes on the phone. It is not a config.env
# key, and it is chosen in the app's Addons tab (or the page's Addons card),
# not in the overlay resource files.
#
# There are two kinds, and the catalog says which is which:
#
#   setting  a Settings value the module writes. One `settings put` changes it
#            on a running phone — no APK, no reboot — and service.sh re-applies
#            it at every boot. The overlay APK alone cannot do one.
#   overlay  a resource the build bakes into an overlay APK — framework (the
#            navigation bar height, the 180° rotation flag) or SystemUI (the
#            status bar background). It only changes after a rebuild and a
#            flash, because a resource is read when its process starts.
#
# The live addons survive an overlay rebuild; the overlay ones *are* the rebuild.
#
# One catalog lives in this file and every front-end reads it:
#
#   the desktop app   runs this script in the clone (Addons tab)
#   the module page   runs it in webroot/ on the phone (Addons card)
#   service.sh        runs it at every boot so saved choices stick
#
#   sh addons.sh list                 catalog + saved + live values, as JSON
#   sh addons.sh set ID=VALUE ...     save choices; apply the live ones now
#   sh addons.sh apply [ID ...]       apply what is saved (all ids, or those)
#   sh addons.sh reset                back to the defaults, forget the choices
#   sh addons.sh status               what the device resolves now, as key=value
#   sh addons.sh restore-conf         customize.sh: bring the saved file back
#
# The saved file is addons.conf at the module root (src/module/addons.conf in
# the clone). Only the addons that differ from the default are written into it:
# a value nobody changed is not enforced on every boot, so an untouched phone
# keeps behaving like the ROM shipped it.
#
# ADDONS_CONF, ADDONS_DIR and ADDONS_SETTINGS exist so this can be exercised
# off-device (stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js) and by the desktop app, which has
# no installed module but does have the clone.
# =============================================================================

# The module directory is one level above this script (webroot/), except when
# the script is run by its bare name from the module root ('sh addons.sh'), in
# which case '..' would be the folder above the module.
SELF="$0"
case "$SELF" in
    */*) SELF_DIR=${SELF%/*}
         MODDIR=$(cd "$SELF_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd) ;;
    *)   SELF_DIR=.
         MODDIR=$(pwd) ;;
esac
MODDIR=${ADDONS_DIR:-$MODDIR}
[ -n "$MODDIR" ] || MODDIR=$SELF_DIR
# In the clone the module files are kept in src/module/, so the script in
# src/webui/ has one directory in between; an installed module keeps the same
# files at its root.
[ -d "$MODDIR/module" ] && MODDIR="$MODDIR/module"

CONF=${ADDONS_CONF:-$MODDIR/addons.conf}
# Outside the module directory on purpose: an update replaces that directory.
# It is the same folder apply.sh mirrors webui.conf into.
STATE_DIR=${ADDONS_STATE_DIR:-/data/adb/treble-webui/${MODDIR##*/}}
SETTINGS=${ADDONS_SETTINGS:-settings}

say() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Catalog
=== verbs ===

317:                on)  put "$id" global captive_portal_mode 1 ;;

325:                on)  put "$id" system screen_off_timeout 2147483647 ;;
326:                off) put "$id" system screen_off_timeout 60000 ;;
331:                on)  icon_blacklist_set show ;;
332:                off) icon_blacklist_set hide ;;
505:    list)         cmd_list ;;
506:    set)          cmd_set "$@" ;;
507:    apply)        cmd_apply "$@" ;;
508:    reset)        cmd_reset ;;
509:    status)       cmd_status ;;
510:    restore-conf) restore_conf ;;
511:    catalog)      catalog ;;

catalog_field() { # <id> <field number> -> that field, empty when unknown
    catalog | awk -F'|' -v id="$1" -v f="$2" '$1 == id { print $f; exit }'
}

choices_of() { catalog_field "$1" 2; }
default_of() { catalog_field "$1" 3; }
label_of()   { catalog_field "$1" 4; }
summary_of() { catalog_field "$1" 5; }
kind_of()    { catalog_field "$1" 6; }

valid_value() { # <id> <value>
    case " $(choices_of "$1" | tr ',' ' ') " in
        *" $2 "*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

bad_value() { say "x $1: '$2' is not one of: $(choices_of "$1" | tr ',' '/')"; }

cmd_list() { # JSON: the catalog, what is saved, what the phone resolves
    if has_saved; then saved_any=yes; else saved_any=no; fi
    if have_settings; then device=yes; else device=no; fi
    printf '{"conf":"%s","device":"%s","addons":[' "$saved_any" "$device"
    first=1
    catalog | while IFS='|' read -r id choices def label summary kind; do
        case "$id" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
        [ "$first" = 1 ] || printf ','
        first=0
        saved=$(conf_value "$id")
        if [ -n "$saved" ]; then
            value=$saved
            is_saved=true
        else
            value=$def
            is_saved=false
        fi
        printf '{"id":"%s","kind":"%s","label":"%s","summary":"%s","choices":[%s],"default":"%s","value":"%s","saved":%s,"live":"%s"}' \
            "$id" "$kind" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$label" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$summary" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$choices" | awk -F, '{ for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) printf "%s\"%s\"", (i > 1 ? "," : ""), $i }')" \
            "$def" "$value" "$is_saved" "$(live_value "$id")"
    done
    printf ']}\n'
}

cmd_set() { # ID=VALUE ... — save, then make it true now
    rc=0
    for pair in "$@"; do
        id=${pair%%=*}
        if [ "$id" = "$pair" ]; then
            say "x '$pair' is not ID=VALUE"
            rc=1
            continue
        fi
        v=${pair#*=}
        if [ -z "$(default_of "$id")" ]; then
            say "x $id: no such addon"
            rc=1
            continue
        fi
        if ! valid_value "$id" "$v"; then
            bad_value "$id" "$v"
            rc=1
            continue
        fi
        # Only deviations are kept: setting an addon back to its default hands
        # that setting back to the ROM instead of pinning it on every boot.
        if [ "$v" = "$(default_of "$id")" ]; then
            del_conf "$id"
        else
            put_conf "$id" "$v" || rc=1
        fi
        say "+ $id=$v"
        # An overlay addon only exists inside the APK. Saving it is the shell's
        # whole job: the page writes the entry with Apply, and build.sh emits it
        # (or stops emitting it, when the choice is the default).
        if [ "$(kind_of "$id")" = overlay ]; then
            if [ "$v" = "$(default_of "$id")" ]; then
                say "  overlay addon: saved as the default — nothing to enforce"
            else
                say "  overlay addon: saved — Apply on the phone, or the next build, writes it"
            fi
            continue
        fi
        # On a desktop with no phone there is nothing to apply to, and the file
        # is the whole job; the script still exits 0 so the choice is saved.
        if have_settings; then
            # A failed put stays saved on purpose: the next boot tries again,
            # and `list` reports the row as saved but not live.
            apply_one "$id" "$v" || rc=1
        fi
    done
    mirror_conf

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# =============================================================================\n# device-id.sh — what is this phone, as config.env spells it\n# =============================================================================\n# DEVICE_MANUFACTURER, DEVICE_MODEL and DEVICE_CODENAME end up in the overlay\n# package, the module name and the launcher icon, so a wrong one is not a build\n# error — it is an overlay for a phone that does not exist. This asks the phone\n# (or saved `getprop` output) and shows every property that answered, which\n# partition it came from, and why the winner won.\n#\n#   bash stuff/scripts/device-id.sh                 # connected device, then ask\n#   bash stuff/scripts/device-id.sh --write         # take the answer it trusts\n#   bash stuff/scripts/device-id.sh --json          # for scripts\n#\n#   --device SERIAL   with more than one phone attached\n#   --adb PATH        adb is looked up on PATH and in stuff/tools/platform-tools\n#   --values FILE     rank saved `getprop` output instead of asking a phone\n#\n# The codename rule is the same one the submission needs: a codename lives on\n# /vendor, /odm or /bootimage, holds a lower-case name that is not the brand,\n# the manufacturer, a build name or an SoC vendor, and survives a GSI. The\n# ranking here and gui/matchprop.go answer the same question; change one, change\n# the other.\n# =============================================================================\n\nset -uo pipefail\n\nexport MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1\n\nROOT=\"${ROOT:-$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../..\" && pwd)}\"\n. \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh\"\n\nadb=\"${ADB:-}\"\nserial=\"\"\nwant_json=0\nwant_write=0\nvalues_file=\"\"\n\nusage() {\n    sed -n '3,22p' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\{0,1\\}//'\n}\n\ndie() { printf 'device-id: %s\\n' \"$1\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --device) serial=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --adb) adb=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --values) values_file=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --json) want_json=1; shift ;;\n        --write|-y|--yes) want_write=1; shift ;;\n        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;\n        *) die \"unknown option: $1 (try --help)\" ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\ntmpdir=\"$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t device-id)\"\ncleanup() { rm -rf \"$tmpdir\"; }\ntrap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM\n\n# `getprop` prints `[key]: [value]`; a warning mixed into the stream is skipped\n# rather than parsed into a device called \"error\".\nparse_props() {\n    awk '\n        {\n            sub(/\\r$/, \"\")\n            if ($0 !~ /^\\[.*\\]: \\[.*\\]$/) next\n            i = index($0, \"]: [\")\n            if (i <= 2) next\n            printf \"%s\\t%s\\n\", substr($0, 2, i - 2), substr($0, i + 4, length($0) - i - 4)\n        }\n    ' \"$1\"\n}\n\nprop_of() {\n    [ -f \"$1\" ] || return 0\n    awk -F'\\t' -v k=\"$2\" '$1 == k { print $2; exit }' \"$1\"\n}\n\nresolve_adb() {\n    [ -n \"$adb\" ] && return 0\n    adb=\"$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n    [ -n \"$adb\" ] && return 0\n    local candidate\n    for candidate in \"$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb\" \"$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb.exe\"; do\n        [ -x \"$candidate\" ] && { adb=\"$candidate\"; return 0; }\n    done\n    adb=\"\"\n    return 1\n}\n\ncollect_from_device() {\n    . \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh\"\n    resolve_adb || die \"adb was not found — install platform-tools, or pass --adb PATH\"\n    adb_pick_device \"$adb\" \"$serial\" device-id || exit 1\n    serial=\"$DEVICE_SERIAL\"\n    \"$adb\" -s \"$serial\" shell getprop </dev/null 2>/dev/null | parse_props >\"$tmpdir/values\"\n    [ -s \"$tmpdir/values\" ] || die \"the phone did not answer getprop — is it connected and authorized?\"\n}\n\ncollect_from_files() {\n    [ -f \"$values_file\" ] || die \"--values: no such file: $values_file\"\n    parse_props \"$values_file\" >\"$tmpdir/values\"\n    [ -s \"$tmpdir/values\" ] || die \"--values: nothing that looks like getprop output in $values_file\"\n}\n\nvalues=\"$tmpdir/values\"\n\n# Partition order: the OEM's own naming first, the ROM's last. A GSI replaces\n# /system and /product, so a codename read from there is the GSI's, not the\n# phone's.\nCODENAME_PROPS='ro.product.vendor.device ro.product.odm.device ro.product.bootimage.device ro.product.device ro.product.product.device ro.product.system.device ro.product.system_ext.device ro.build.product'\nMANUFACTURER_PROPS='ro.product.vendor.manufacturer ro.product.odm.manufacturer ro.product.bootimage.manufacturer ro.product.manufacturer ro.product.product.manufacturer ro.product.system.manufacturer'\nMODEL_PROPS='ro.product.vendor.model ro.product.odm.model ro.product.bootimage.model ro.product.model ro.product.product.model ro.product.system.model'\n\nzone_of() {\n    case \"$1\" in\n        *.vendor.*) echo vendor ;;\n        *.odm.*) echo odm ;;\n        *.bootimage.*) echo bootimage ;;\n        *.product.*) echo product ;;\n        *.system_ext.*) echo system_ext ;;\n        *.system.*) echo system ;;\n        ro.build.product|ro.product.name|ro.product.*.name) echo build ;;\n        *) echo system ;;\n    esac\n}\n\nzone_score() {\n    case \"$1\" in\n        vendor) echo 40 ;;\n        odm|bootimage) echo 35 ;;\n        product) echo 25 ;;\n        system) echo 22 ;;\n        system_ext) echo 18 ;;\n        build) echo 10 ;;\n        *) echo 0 ;;\n    esac\n}\n\nlower() { printf '%s' \"$1\" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; }\n\n# Values that name a build, a vendor or a family rather than one phone.\ngeneric_reason() {\n    case \"$(lower \"$1\")\" in\n        ''|unknown|generic|generic_x86|generic_arm64|generic_x86_64) echo \"not a device name\" ;;\n        aosp|aosp_arm64|aosp_x86_64) echo \"an AOSP build name, not a device\" ;;\n        mainline|treble|phh_treble) echo \"the GSI's own build name, present on every phone running it\" ;;\n        mivendor) echo \"Xiaomi's vendor build name — shared by many devices\" ;;\n        qcom|mediatek|mtk|exynos|unisoc|sprd|qualcomm) echo \"a SoC vendor, shared by every phone with that chip\" ;;\n        emulator|goldfish|ranchu) echo \"an emulator, not a phone\" ;;\n        *) return 1 ;;\n    esac\n    return 0\n}\n\nis_codename_shape() { [[ \"${1:-}\" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,23}$ ]]; }"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
RED='\033[0;31m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'; BOLD='\033[1m'; NC='\033[0m'

ok()   { echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} $*"; }
info() { echo -e "  ${YELLOW}→${NC} $*"; }
warn() { echo -e "  ${YELLOW}⚠${NC} $*"; }
err()  { echo -e "  ${RED}✗${NC} $*" >&2; }
step() { echo -e "\n${BOLD}━━━ $* ━━━${NC}"; }

banner() {
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${BOLD}$*${NC}"
    echo -e "  ${BOLD}──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────${NC}"
    echo ""
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prompts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ask <question> <default>   -> answer in $REPLY
#
# `read` returns 1 at EOF (stdin redirected, CI, IDE task, no console). Under
# `set -e` that used to kill the scripts silently right after a menu had been
# printed. Falling back to a stated default keeps everything runnable
# unattended, and pressing Enter also takes the default.
ask() {
    local question="$1" default="${2:-}" answer=""
    printf '%s' "$question"
    if ! read -r answer; then
        echo ""
        info "No terminal input available — using '${default}'."
        answer="$default"
    fi
    [ -z "$answer" ] && answer="$default"
    REPLY="$answer"
}

# confirm <question> <y|n>   -> returns 0 for yes
confirm() {
    local question="$1" default="${2:-n}" answer
    ask "$question" "$default"
    answer="$REPLY"
    case "$answer" in
        [Yy]|[Yy][Ee][Ss]) return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WSL safety
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A checkout on a Windows drive that is built from inside WSL would put Linux
# binaries into the same stuff/tools/ folder the Windows build reads, and would hand
# Windows a build tree it cannot use. Refuse with instructions instead of
# producing a half-broken toolchain. (This is the "VS Code opened the folder
# with WSL" case.)
wsl_guard() {
    $IS_WSL || return 0
    case "$ROOT" in
        /mnt/[a-z]/*) ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac

    echo ""
    err "This project is on a Windows drive, but you are running inside WSL."
    echo ""
    echo "    Project:  $ROOT"
    echo "    Shell:    WSL (Linux)"
    echo ""
    echo "  The Linux toolchain would be installed into the same stuff/tools/ folder the"
    echo "  Windows build uses, so both platforms would then see the wrong binaries."
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${BOLD}Use one of these instead:${NC}"
    echo "    • Windows (cmd, PowerShell, VS Code):   build.cmd"
    echo "    • Linux / Termux:                       clone the project inside Linux"
    echo "                                            (e.g. ~/treble-rro-creator)"
    echo "                                            and run ./build.sh there"
    echo ""
    echo "  In VS Code, check the bottom-left corner: if it says \"WSL: ...\","
    echo "  close the remote window (or open a Windows terminal) and run build.cmd."
    echo ""

```
mirror_conf() {
    mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    if [ -f "$CONF" ]; then
        cp "$CONF" "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
        rm -f "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    chmod 600 "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# customize.sh calls this after the new zip is unpacked. The packaged file is
# the app's latest word, so its choices win: restoring the old file over it made
# a freshly built "hide the notch" come up unset, because the phone still had
# the previous install's copy. Only the addons the new file does not name are
# carried over - those are the ones chosen on the phone, which the app never
# saw. A build that names nothing at all is a plain rebuild, so the saved file
# is restored whole, the way it always was.
restore_conf() {
    [ -f "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" ] || return 0
    if ! has_saved; then
        if cp "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null; then
            chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
            say "+ saved addons restored"
        fi
        return 0
    fi

then\n        echo \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    MENU_ANSWER=\"$answer\"\n    return 0\n}\n\n# Wait for Enter between screens, unless stdin is not a terminal.\npause_menu() {\n    [ -t 0 ] || return 0\n    printf '\\n  %s ' \"Press Enter to go back\"\n    read -r _ || true\n    printf '\\n'\n}\n\n# Count the rows config.env has, and how many are switched off.\ncfg_counts() {\n    local rows\n    rows=\"$(cfg_rows 2>/dev/null)\" || { CFG_ON=0; do\n        echo \"\"\n        echo -e \"  ${BOLD}Build${NC}\"\n        hr\n        echo \"     1  Dry run         print the resources config.env emits, build nothing\"\n        echo \"     2  Build           build the module (installs tools if needed)\"\n        echo \"     3  Check           validate config.env without building\"\n        echo \"     4  Doctor          check the toolchain, install nothing\"\n        echo \"     5  Clean           remove build output\"\n        echo \"     6  Clean --all     start over for a different device\"\n        echo \"     0  Back\"\n        echo \"\"\n        menu_read \"  >\" || return 0\n        case \"$MENU_ANSWER\" in\n            1) run_entry --dry-run; pause_menu ;;\n            2) run_entry build; pause_menu ;;\n            3) run_entry check; pause_menu ;;\n            4) run_entry doctor; pause_menu ;;\n            5) run_entry clean; pause_menu ;;\n            6)\n                warn \"This removes config.env and the device files too.\"\n                if confirm \"  Start over for a different device? then\n        less -R \"$pick\"\n    else\n        cat \"$pick\"\n    fi\n    return 0\n}"

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble RRO Creator — desktop app
      # =============================================================================
      # One command, from anywhere:
      #
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh                  build if needed, then open the window
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh --rebuild        rebuild first (after a git pull, say)
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh --release        no console window (Windows; the default)
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh --detach         accepted for scripts; hand-off is automatic
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh --browser        no window; use the default browser
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh -clone ~/other   start on a different clone
      #
      # The first launch builds the app, downloading Go and (on Windows) a MinGW-w64
      # gcc into stuff/tools/ when the machine has none; a checkout that already has
      # gui/bin/ filled in runs without a toolchain at all, and the app finds its
      # clone by walking up from where it lives, so no path has to be typed.
      #
      # Windows: double-click treble-rro-creator.cmd; it finds Git Bash and calls this.
      # =============================================================================
      set -euo pipefail
      
      here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      exe="$here/gui/bin/treble-rro-creator-gui"
      case "$(uname -s)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) exe="$exe.exe" ;;
      esac
      
      rebuild=false
      release=false
      detach=false
      browser=false
      app_args=()
      for arg in "$@"; do
          case "$arg" in
              -h|--help)
                  # The launcher's own flags, which the app knows nothing about: the
                  # block between the second and third rule in the header above.
                  printf '%s\n\n' "Treble RRO Creator — desktop app"
                  awk '/^# =====/ { n++; next } n == 2 { sub(/^# ?/, ""); print }' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
                  exit 0
                  ;;
              --rebuild) rebuild=true ;;
              --release) release=true ;;
              # Accepted for the launchers and for people used to typing it: on
              # Windows the hand-off happens anyway.
              --detach) detach=true ;;
              --browser|-browser) browser=true ; app_args+=("$arg") ;;
              *) app_args+=("$arg") ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # On Windows the app is always the window-only build. The window is the whole
      # UI, so a binary linked against a console only drags one along behind it —
      # and dies when that console is closed. --browser is the exception: that run
      # keeps its console, because that is where the server is watched and stopped.
      case "$(uname -s)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
              if [ "$browser" = "false" ]; then
                  release=true

==== build.cmd ====
@echo off
rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
rem build.cmd - Windows entry point
rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
rem Finds Git for Windows (never WSL) and runs build.sh, which does everything:
rem
rem   build.cmd                  build (downloads the toolchain on first run)
rem   build.cmd setup            install / repair the build tools
rem   build.cmd doctor           check the toolchain
rem   build.cmd check            validate config.env
rem   build.cmd clean            remove build output
rem   build.cmd clean --all      start over for a different device
rem
rem Requirements: Git for Windows + JDK 17+ on PATH.
rem Tip: run this from cmd or PowerShell (.\\build.cmd), not from WSL.
rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
setlocal EnableExtensions
call "%~dp0stuff\windows\run-bash.cmd" build.sh %*
set "RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"

rem Keep the window open only when double-clicked from Explorer. Explorer runs
rem   cmd.exe /c ""C:\path\build.cmd" "
rem and a terminal -- cmd, PowerShell, VS Code -- starts cmd.exe with no /c. The
rem /c is the difference, and matching on it is the only test that works:
rem Windows leaves a space after the trailing quotes, so a last-three-characters
rem test never matches.
set "DOUBLE="
echo %cmdcmdline% | "%SystemRoot%\System32\findstr.exe" /i /c:" /c " >nul && set "DOUBLE=1"
if defined DOUBLE pause

exit /b %RC%
==== run.sh ====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Everything that can be checked without Android tools
# =============================================================================
# CI runs this on every push (see .github/workflows/check.yml), and it is worth
# running before a release:
#
#   bash stuff/tests/run.sh
#
# 1. shell syntax of every shipped script (bash -n / sh -n, no execution)
# 2. the WebUI resource-table writer against stuff/tests/fixtures/*.apk
# 3. the WebUI manifest and the overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off
#    vendor_hardware_overlay), built from
#    resource XML that stuff/tests/gen-res.sh generates into a temp directory (so
#    a fresh clone needs no build first)
# 4. every relative link and #anchor in the docs
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."

status=0
step() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$*"; }

step "shell syntax"
for f in build.sh treble-rro-creator.sh gui/build.sh stuff/scripts/*.sh stuff/tests/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if bash -n "$f"; then :; else echo "bash -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
done
# apply.sh, addons.sh and the module scripts run under Android's mksh
# (/system/bin/sh).
for f in src/webui/apply.sh src/webui/addons.sh src/module/*.sh stuff/templates/*.sh stuff/templates/recoveries/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if command -v sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if sh -n "$f"; then :; else echo "sh -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
    fi
done
[ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all scripts parse"

# The bug this guards: `clean --all` copied config.env from a frozen file, so a
# full clean handed back a version from an older commit. The copies below are
# now only the no-.git fallback, so they must equal the committed blob — not the
# working file, because local edits to config.env are normal.
step "template fallbacks match the release"
if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    copy_status=0
    check_copy() {
        local rel="$1" copy="$2"
        if [ ! -f "$copy" ]; then
            echo "missing fallback: $copy"
            copy_status=1
        elif ! git show "HEAD:$rel" | diff -q - "$copy" >/dev/null; then
            echo "$copy differs from HEAD:$rel — run: git show HEAD:$rel > $copy"
            copy_status=1
        fi
    }
    check_copy config.env stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    check_copy src/module/sepolicy.rule stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
    if [ "$copy_status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "fallbacks match"; else status=1; fi
else
    echo "not a git checkout — skipping"
fi

# restore_from_release() is what clean.sh and build.sh call. Run it against a
# throwaway repository with a deliberately stale fallback, and once without
# .git, because "start over" silently returning old values is the failure mode.
step "restore picks the release, not the stale copy"
restore_here="$(pwd)"
restore_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-restore)"
if (
    cd "$restore_tmp" || exit 1
    git init -q . && git config user.email t@example.com && git config user.name t || exit 1
    # No .gitattributes here, and Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true,
    # which would check the file back out with CRLF and fail the greps below.
    git config core.autocrlf false
    mkdir -p src/module stuff/templates/recoveries
    printf 'KEY="released"\n' > config.env
    printf 'released rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
    printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
    git add -A && git commit -qm one || exit 1
    # The user edits both files; the fallback copies are stale.
    printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
    printf 'my rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
    ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env" && restore_from_release src/module/sepolicy.rule "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 2
    grep -qx 'KEY="released"' config.env || { echo "git restore did not win: $(cat config.env)"; exit 3; }
    grep -qx 'released rules' src/module/sepolicy.rule || exit 4
    # No .git (a zip download): the bundled copy is the only source left.
    rm -rf .git
    printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
    ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 6
    grep -q 'STALE' config.env || { echo "fallback was not used without git"; exit 7; }
); then
    echo "restore behaves"
else
    echo "restore test failed (exit $?)"
    status=1
fi
rm -rf "$restore_tmp"

step "node tests"
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    node --test stuff/tests/arsc.test.js stuff/tests/manifest.test.js \
        stuff/tests/hw-overlay.test.js stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js \
        stuff/tests/adb-device.test.js stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js \
        stuff/tests/apply-sh.test.js stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js || status=1
else
    echo "node is not installed — skipping the resource-table tests"
    status=1
fi

# The desktop app is optional: a clone without Go is still a complete CLI
# install, so a missing toolchain skips instead of failing. CI installs Go and
# runs this step for real (see .github/workflows/check.yml).
step "desktop app (go)"
if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./... || status=1
else
    echo "go is not installed — skipping the desktop app tests"
fi

step "documentation links"
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    node stuff/tests/docs-links.js || status=1
fi

if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
    printf '\nSome checks failed.\n'
    exit 1
fi
printf '\nAll checks passed.\n'
