```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# match-prop.sh — which property should the submitted overlay match on?
# =============================================================================
# The overlay repo compares android:requiredSystemPropertyName/Value with plain
# string equality, and getting it wrong is silent: the overlay installs, `cmd
# overlay list` shows it enabled, and nothing changes. This reads the phone and
# ranks every property the submission could use, saying what each one is
# gambling on.
#
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh                  # connected device, then ask
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --write          # take the answer it trusts
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --json           # for scripts
#
#   --device SERIAL   with more than one phone attached
#   --adb PATH        adb is looked up on PATH and in stuff/tools/platform-tools
#   --values FILE --labels FILE   rank saved `getprop` / `getprop -Z` output
#                                 instead of asking a phone (tests, offline)
#
# Two rules decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable without
# root: zygote has to be able to read the property (`getprop -Z` prints the
# SELinux area; build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps),

# property satisfies both, this says so instead of picking one — a match that
# never holds is invisible.

want_write=0

labels_file=""
```

```json
}
```

```
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # `getprop` prints `[key]: [value]`; some ROMs mix warnings into the same
      # stream, and those lines are skipped rather than parsed into nonsense.
      parse_props() {
          awk '

                  sub(/\r$/, "")
                  if ($0 !~ /^\[.*\]: \[.*\]$/) next
                  i = index($0, "]: [")
                  if (i <= 2) next
                  key = substr($0, 2, i - 2)
                  val = substr($0, i + 4, length($0) - i - 4)
                  printf "%s\t%s\n", key, val
```
```json
              }

      }
```

````
- path: README.md
  content: |
      # Treble RRO Creator
      
      Build a **Magisk / KernelSU / APatch module** that adapts a GSI (Generic System Image) to
      your phone's hardware: rounded corners, display cutout, brightness curve, UDFPS,
      AOD/doze, 5G/VoLTE — and optional vendor HALs for fingerprint or vibrator.
      
      Two ways in, same tool: the **desktop app**, which puts every setting and the
      whole build in a window, or **one command** from a terminal. Both edit the same
      `config.env` and run the same build.
      
      ```bash
      treble-rro-creator.cmd    # Windows: the app (double-click it too)
      ./treble-rro-creator.sh   # Linux: the app
      ./build.sh                # or just build: Linux / Termux / Git Bash
      build.cmd                 #                 Windows
      ```
      
      The first run installs the Android build tools automatically (about 33 MB on
      disk; on Linux it uses your package manager when permitted, and otherwise
      prints the exact command to run). Every later run goes straight to the build.
      
      ---
      
      ## Requirements
      
      | Platform | What you need |
      |---|---|
      | **Windows** | [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) + JDK 17 or newer (`winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JDK`) |
      | **Linux** | `bash`, `curl`, `unzip`, `zip` and JDK 17+. `./build.sh` can install the rest with your package manager, or use `./build.sh setup` |
      | **Termux** | Termux from **F-Droid** (not Google Play). See [docs/termux.md](docs/termux.md) |
      | **Phone** | A GSI-based ROM and a root manager (KernelSU, KSU Next, APatch or Magisk) |
      
      ---
      
      ## Quick start
      
      ### Desktop app (Windows / Linux)
      
      The window is the same tool: it finds the clone it lives in, edits `config.env`,
      and runs the same `build.sh` commands — **Build**, **Dry run**, **Check**,
      **Doctor**, **Setup**, **Clean** — with the output streaming into a pane.
      Nothing is reimplemented, so the app and the CLI can be mixed freely.
      
      It also covers what used to need a terminal: `config.env` as a form (a switch
      per setting, ⓘ for the note the file already carries, the raw file one click
      away); a **Device** tab with an adb console, the commands worth running on a
      phone, and a button that installs platform-tools if you do not have them; and a
      **Files** tab that is the `src/` workspace — drop a vendor HAL tree in, disable
      a file out of the build without deleting it, and write the SELinux rules and
      VINTF manifests a custom HAL needs, checked as you type; and a **UDFPS** tab
      that finds the sensor's real geometry on the phone or in an OEM firmware — a
      `super.img`, a Samsung `AP_*.tar.md5` or an extracted tree, all unpacked by the
      app itself — with the source of every answer, instead of asking you to guess
      three numbers.
      The header tells you
      when a newer release exists, and an update that would overwrite your own edits
      asks first and backs them up.
      
      ```bash
      git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
      cd treble-rro-creator
      ./treble-rro-creator.sh   # Linux   — builds itself first (Go and missing GTK/WebKitGTK headers are installed for you)
      treble-rro-creator.cmd    # Windows — double-clickable, no console left open; Go and MinGW-w64 gcc are downloaded
      ```
      
      The first launch builds it and says what is missing if anything is. **Setup**,
      and the first build, install the Android tools with the distro's package
      manager — when sudo asks for a password, the app asks for it in a dialog and
      repeats the command, so nothing has to be typed into a terminal. Later launches
      open straight away, and a `git pull` only triggers a rebuild when the Go
      sources actually changed. Full guide, including what each button does and what
      to do when no window appears: [docs/gui.md](docs/gui.md).
      
      ### Windows (command line)
      
      1. Install **Git for Windows** and **JDK 17+**.
      2. Clone or download this project.
      3. Double-click **`build.cmd`**.
      
      From a terminal (cmd, PowerShell, VS Code) run `build.cmd` — from PowerShell use
      `.\build.cmd`. Do **not** run the `.sh` files in a WSL terminal on a Windows
      drive; see [docs/windows.md](docs/windows.md) for why and what to do instead.
      
      ### Linux
      
      ```bash
      git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
      cd treble-rro-creator
      ./build.sh
      ```
      
      ### Termux
      
      ```bash
      pkg install -y git
      cd ~ && git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
      cd treble-rro-creator
      ./build.sh
      ```
      
      Full Termux walkthrough: [docs/termux.md](docs/termux.md).
      
      ---
      
      ## Configure your device
      
      Open `config.env`. Only a few values are required:
      
      | Setting | What it is | How to find it |
      |---|---|---|
      | `DEVICE_CODENAME` | Device codename, e.g. `r3q` | `adb shell getprop ro.product.device` |
      | `DEVICE_MANUFACTURER` | Manufacturer, e.g. `samsung` | `adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer` |
      | `DEVICE_MODEL` | Model name, e.g. `SM-A908N` | `adb shell getprop ro.product.model` |
      | `DEVICE_PROP_NAME` | Property the overlay matches | `persist.sys.overlay.<codename>` (set by the module), or empty for no condition |
      | `DEVICE_PROP_VALUE` | Value the overlay matches | `true` for a `persist.sys.*` property |
      | `ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS` | Screen corner radius in px | Measure or take from your stock overlay |
      | `STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT` | Status bar height in px | Take from your stock overlay |
      
      Everything else is optional and documented in
      [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md).
      
      > **First run without `config.env`?** `build.sh` offers the example config
      > (Samsung A90 5G) or writes a placeholder and tells you what to edit.
      >
      > **`power_profile.xml` matters.** Replace
      > `src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` with your device's file —
      > see [docs/device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
      > Until you do, the empty template is detected and **left out** of the APK
      > instead of wiping the GSI's battery and CPU data.
      
      ---
      
      ## Commands
      
      `build.sh` and `build.cmd` are the only entry points. Everything else in the
      project is called by them.
      
      | Command | What it does |
      |---|---|
      | `./treble-rro-creator.sh` / `treble-rro-creator.cmd` | **Open the desktop app** — the window for everything below. Builds it on the first run, then just launches it. |
      | `./build.sh` | Build. Installs missing tools first. |
      | `./build.sh setup` | Install or repair the toolchain (menu: distro / resource version) |
      | `./build.sh doctor` | Check the toolchain, install nothing (exit 0 = ready) |
      | `./build.sh check` | Validate `config.env`, build nothing |
      | `./build.sh --dry-run` | Print the resources `config.env` emits, build nothing |
      | `./build.sh clean` | Remove `stuff/build/` and `out/` |
      | `./build.sh clean --all` | Start over for a different device (restores templates) |
      
      Options: `-y` / `--yes` (no prompts), `--with-vendor-hals` (with `--yes`),
      `--dry-run` (resource plan only), `--allow-unknown-resources` (build even when a
      resource is missing from the dictionary — see the audit note below), `--force`
      (with `setup`: re-pick the resource dictionary), `--help`.
      
      `--dry-run` is the fast feedback loop: it generates the resource XML from
      `config.env` and prints every resource it would emit (type, name, value, which
      overlay APK), without aapt2, signing or packaging. `check` reports the same
      config warnings and stops there.
      
      To check the project itself (the WebUI's resource-table writer, the manifest it
      renders from, script syntax, documentation anchors):
      
      ```bash
      bash stuff/tests/run.sh    # what CI runs, no Android tools needed
      ```
      
      On Windows, use the same words with `build.cmd`:
      `build.cmd setup`, `build.cmd doctor`, `build.cmd clean --all`.
      
      ---
      
      ## Output
      
      Everything is written to `out/`:
      
      | File | Purpose |
````

````
# Treble RRO Creator

Build a **Magisk / KernelSU / APatch module** that adapts a GSI (Generic System Image) to
your phone's hardware: rounded corners, display cutout, brightness curve, UDFPS,
AOD/doze, 5G/VoLTE — and optional vendor HALs for fingerprint or vibrator.

Two ways in, same tool: the **desktop app**, which puts every setting and the
whole build in a window, or the **terminal menu**, which offers the same things
in a numbered list. Both edit the same `config.env` and run the same build.

```bash
treble-rro-creator.cmd    # Windows: the app (double-click it too)
./treble-rro-creator.sh   # Linux: the app
./build.sh                # the terminal menu: Linux / Termux / Git Bash
build.cmd                 #                      Windows
```

The first run installs the Android build tools automatically (about 33 MB on
disk; on Linux it uses your package manager when permitted, and otherwise
prints the exact command to run). Every later run goes straight to the menu.
No terminal (a script, a CI job)? `./build.sh` without a terminal still builds,
and `./build.sh build` always builds.

---

## Requirements

| Platform | What you need |
|---|---|
| **Windows** | [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) + JDK 17 or newer (`winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JDK`) |
...

> `src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` with your device's file —
> see [docs/device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
> Until you do, the empty template is detected and **left out** of the APK
> instead of wiping the GSI's battery and CPU data.

---

## Commands

`build.sh` and `build.cmd` are the only entry points. Everything else in the
project is called by them.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `./treble-rro-creator.sh` / `treble-rro-creator.cmd` | **Open the desktop app** — the window for everything below. Builds it on the first run, then just launches it. |
| `./build.sh` | **The terminal menu** (on a terminal); a plain build without a terminal. |
| `./build.sh menu` | The menu, even when there is no terminal |
| `./build.sh build` | Build. Installs missing tools first. |
| `./build.sh setup` | Install or repair the toolchain (menu: distro / resource version) |
````

````
- path: README.md
  content: |
      The **Addons** tab is the module's own feature set: tweaks that are neither a
      `config.env` key nor a plain overlay resource. **Live** addons are Settings
      values the module writes itself — the volume panel side, a screen that never
      sleeps, hiding the status-bar clock, the captive-portal probe. **Overlay**
      addons are resources the build bakes in — upside-down rotation, a navigation bar
      with no padding but the pill kept, a status bar with no background, and a notch
      the display is masked away from so nothing can draw under the camera. Pick them
      in the app and they are packed into the module (`src/module/addons.conf`). From
      the module's WebUI both kinds can be changed: live ones immediately (and they are
      re-applied on every boot), overlay ones by **Apply**, which writes the resource
      into the installed APK — and **Use default** removes it again. Only the addons
      you chose are enforced, so an untouched install behaves exactly like the ROM.
      Details: [docs/addons.md](docs/addons.md).
      
      Both overlays are **static** RROs: Android enables them during boot, and
      `cmd overlay enable` cannot change them afterwards. Verify after reboot:
      
      ```bash
      adb shell cmd overlay list | grep <your-package>
      adb shell cmd overlay lookup <your-package> android:dimen/rounded_corner_radius
      adb shell cmd overlay lookup <your-package> android:dimen/status_bar_height_default
      ```
      
      Every build also writes `out/<name>-overrides.txt`, listing each resource as
      `APPLIES` or `IGNORED` against the target framework. If a generated name does
      not exist in the target, the build refuses to continue — a resource Android
      does not recognise is silently ignored, which is how an overlay can look
      correct and change nothing.
      
      The status bar uses `status_bar_height_default` (Android 12L+), not the old
      `status_bar_height`; both are generated, including a landscape variant. See
      [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md#status-bar-height).
      
      ---
      
      ## Project layout
      
      ```
      .
      ├── build.sh / build.cmd        ← the command line
      ├── treble-rro-creator.sh/.cmd  ← desktop app: build if stale, then launch
      ├── config.env                  ← your device settings (created on first run)
      ├── config.env.example          ← filled-in Samsung A90 5G example
      ├── src/
      │   ├── framework/res/          framework overlay resources (+ power_profile.xml)
      │   ├── systemui/res/          SystemUI overlay resources
      │   ├── module/                 optional overrides + sepolicy.rule
      │   ├── webui/                  shared WebUI page + apply.sh (packed as webroot/)
      │   └── vendor/                 optional extracted vendor HALs (git-ignored)
      ├── docs/                       guides
      ├── out/                        APKs and flashable zips (git-ignored)
      ├── gui/                        desktop app sources (+ go.mod at the root)
      └── stuff/                      everything the build uses and you do not
          ├── scripts/                internals used by build.sh (not run directly)
          ├── templates/              reference scripts + clean templates
          ├── keys/                   platform signing key (shipped)
          ├── windows/                helpers for build.cmd
          ├── tests/                  the checks CI runs
          ├── tools/                  downloaded toolchain (git-ignored)
          ├── build/                  intermediate files (git-ignored)
          └── backups/                copies made before clean/rebuild (git-ignored)
      ```
      
      The root keeps only what you act on: the two entry points, `config.env`, `src/`
      (the resources you edit), `docs/`, `gui/` and `out/` (where the APKs and zips
      appear). Everything else moved into `stuff/` — one folder instead of nine. The
      signing key, the templates, the tests and the downloaded toolchain all keep
      their own names there, so `keys/platform.pk8` became
      `stuff/keys/platform.pk8`.
      
      ---
      
      ## Coming from an older version?
      
      The scripts were merged and the folders reorganised. Old commands and files
      still work like this:
      
      | You used to run | Run now |
      |---|---|
      | `./setup.sh` / `setup.cmd` | `./build.sh setup` / `build.cmd setup` |
      | `./setup.sh --doctor` / `setup.cmd --doctor` | `./build.sh doctor` / `build.cmd doctor` |
      | `./cleanup.sh` / `cleanup.cmd` | `./build.sh clean` / `build.cmd clean` |
      | `./build.sh` / `build.cmd` | unchanged |
      
      | Old location | New location |
      |---|---|
      | `res/` | `src/framework/res/` |
      | `systemui_overlay/res/` | `src/systemui/res/` |
      | `customize.sh`, `service.sh`, `sepolicy.rule` | `src/module/` (scripts are generated by default) |
      | `system/vendor/` | `src/vendor/` |
      | `TEMPLATE RECOVERIES (Don't touch)/` | `stuff/templates/recoveries/` (fallback for `clean --all` when there is no `.git`) |
      | `YOUR BACKUPS/` | `stuff/backups/` |
      | `keys/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`, `tests/`, `windows/`, `tools/`, `build/`, `backups/` | the same names inside `stuff/` |
      
      `build.sh` moves anything it still finds in the old places into the new layout
      on the next run: the file is copied first and the old location is removed only
      afterwards, so an existing checkout keeps working after a `git pull`. If both
      locations exist, it warns and leaves the old one alone instead of overwriting
      the new one.
      
      ---
      
      ## Documentation
      
      | Guide | Contents |
      |---|---|
      | [docs/submission.md](docs/submission.md) | Getting the overlay built into the GSI (Doze-off repo PR) |
      | [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) | Every `config.env` option |
      | [docs/webui.md](docs/webui.md) | KernelSU WebUI: change values without rebuilding |
      | [docs/addons.md](docs/addons.md) | Module addons: live Settings (screen timeout, volume panel side) and overlay ones (180° rotation, navigation-bar padding) |
````

````
- path: docs/termux.md
  content: |
      # Termux (Android)
      
      You can build the overlay on the phone itself. The toolchain is the same; only
      the install step differs.
      
      > Use Termux from **[F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/en/packages/com.termux/)**.
      > The Google Play version is outdated and its packages are incompatible.
      
      ---
      
      ## 1. Prepare Termux
      
      ```bash
      termux-setup-storage
      
      apt update
      apt upgrade -y
      
      apt install -y git aapt aapt2 apksigner android-tools openjdk-17 \
                     unzip zip curl tsu
      ```
      
      If `pkg install` fails with signature or mirror errors, run
      `termux-change-repo`, pick a mirror close to you, then repeat `apt update`.
      
      > **`zipalign` comes from the `aapt` package, not from `aapt2`.** Installing
      > `aapt2`, `apksigner` and `android-tools` leaves `zipalign` missing; adding
      > `aapt` provides it. If it is still absent, `build.sh` continues and copies
      > the APK instead of aligning it (valid, just not mmap-aligned) and tells you
      > to run `pkg install aapt`.
      
      ---
      
      ## 2. Clone into the home directory
      
      ```bash
      cd ~
      git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
      cd treble-rro-creator
      ```
      
      > ⚠ **Do not clone into `/sdcard`.** Android's shared storage does not support
      > executable permissions or the symlinks `aapt2`/`zipalign` need. Use `~`
      > (`/data/data/com.termux/files/home`).
      
      ---
      
      ## 3. Build
      
      ```bash
      ./build.sh
      ```
      
      The first run checks the toolchain. If something is missing it installs it
      (aapt2/zipalign/apksigner via `pkg`, `framework-res.apk` by download), then
      builds. To choose things yourself:
      
      ```bash
      ./build.sh setup     # [3] Android / Termux, then [1] Android 13 resources
      ./build.sh doctor    # verify
      ./build.sh check     # validate config.env only
      ```
      
      If `build.sh` cannot install packages unattended, it prints the exact command
      to run. `./build.sh setup` walks through the options interactively.
      
      ---
      
      ## 4. Edit the config
      
      Use a text editor in Termux:
      
      ```bash
      nano config.env
      ```
      
      `Ctrl+O` then `Enter` saves, `Ctrl+X` exits. Or edit the same file with
      MT Manager at:
      
      ```
      /data/data/com.termux/files/home/treble-rro-creator/config.env
      ```
      
      Required values and every optional flag are listed in
      [configuration.md](configuration.md).
      
      Do not forget `src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` — replace it with your
      device's file, see
      [device-extraction.md](device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
      
      ---
      
      ## 5. Install the module
      
      ```bash
      cp out/*-ksu.zip /sdcard/
      ```
      
      Then either:
      
      - open your root manager (KernelSU / KSU Next / Magisk) → Modules → install the
        zip, or use MT Manager to pick it from `/sdcard/`, or
      - from a PC over ADB:
      
      ```bash
      adb shell su -c 'ksud module install /sdcard/treble-overlay-<device>-ksu.zip'
      ```
      
      Reboot when done.
      
      > **KernelSU / KSU Next:** install **Magic Mount** (or Hybrid Mount configured
      > for magic mount) before flashing overlay modules.
      > **Never use OverlayFS** — it mounts fine, but a mistake in a vendor build's
      > `sepolicy.rule` or VINTF manifests then bootloops the device; magic mount
      > ignores the bad file and boots.
      
      ---
      
      ## Tips
      
      - Keep the project inside Termux home. Moving it to `/sdcard` breaks execution
        permissions.
      - `./build.sh clean` frees space; `./build.sh clean --all` starts over for a
        new device. Backups go to `stuff/backups/`.
      - Building needs roughly 300 MB free for the toolchain and intermediates.
      - If Termux is killed during a download, just run `./build.sh` again — already
        downloaded pieces are reused.
      - Logs are printed in the terminal. For a detailed trace:
        `bash -x ./build.sh 2>&1 | tee build.log`.
````

```
- path: stuff/scripts/menu.sh
  content: |
      menu_items() {
          cat << 'ITEMS'
           1  Build              dry run, build, check, doctor, clean
           2  config.env         browse and edit one key at a time
           3  Addons             module tweaks: settings and overlay resources
           4  Device             read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone
           5  Detect display     cutout, corners, status bar height, refresh rates
           6  UDFPS              in-display fingerprint geometry
           7  Match property     which property the submission should match on
           8  Files              what was built, and where it is
           9  Docs               the guides in docs/
           q  Quit
      ITEMS
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The menu never re-implements a build step: it runs the entry point with the
      # verb a user would type, so `build.sh doctor` and 1 → 4 are the same command.
      run_entry() {
          ( cd "$ROOT" && bash "$ROOT/build.sh" "$@" )
      }
      
      menu_build() {
          while :; do
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}Build${NC}"
              hr
              echo "     1  Dry run         print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
              echo "     2  Build           build the module (installs tools if needed)"
              echo "     3  Check           validate config.env without building"
              echo "     4  Doctor          check the toolchain, install nothing"
              echo "     5  Clean           remove build output"
              echo "     6  Clean --all     start over for a different device"
              echo "     0  Back"
              echo ""
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) run_entry --dry-run; pause_menu ;;
                  2) run_entry build; pause_menu ;;
                  3) run_entry check; pause_menu ;;
                  4) run_entry doctor; pause_menu ;;
                  5) run_entry clean; pause_menu ;;
                  6)
                      warn "This removes config.env and the device files too."
                      if confirm "  Start over for a different device? [y/N] " n; then
                          run_entry clean --all
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Files
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_files() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Files${NC}"
          hr
          printf '  %-12s %s\n' 'Project' "$ROOT"
          printf '  %-12s %s\n' 'config.env' "$ROOT/config.env"
          printf '  %-12s %s\n' 'Build tree' "${BUILD_DIR#$ROOT/}"
          echo ""
          if [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$OUT_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
              echo "  Output"
              find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.apk' \) 2>/dev/null |
                  while IFS= read -r f; do
                      printf '    %-10s %s\n' "$(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)" "${f#$ROOT/}"
                  done
          else
              echo "  Nothing built yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
          fi
          pause_menu
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Docs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_docs() {
          local files=() i
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Docs${NC}"
          hr
          [ -d "$ROOT/docs" ] || { warn "docs/ is missing from this checkout."; pause_menu; return 0; }
          while IFS= read -r f; do
              files+=("$f")
          done < <(find "$ROOT/docs" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
          for i in "${!files[@]}"; do
              printf '  %2d  %s\n' "$((i + 1))" "$(basename "${files[$i]}")"
          done
          echo ""
          menu_read "  number to read, Enter to go back >" || return 0
          case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
              ''|q) return 0 ;;
              *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number."; return 0 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#files[@]}" ]; then
              warn "No such doc."
              return 0
          fi
          local pick="${files[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]}"
          echo ""
          if [ -t 1 ] && command -v less >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              less -R "$pick"
          else
              cat "$pick"
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The file keeps its shape: these helpers rewrite one line and leave the
      # comments, the section headers and the quoting alone. A key that is commented
      # out shows as `off` and can be switched on by number, which is the whole point
      # of listing it — hunting for the '#' in a 240-line file is where mistakes
      # happen.
      cfg_each_row() { # <section> -> `key<TAB>active<TAB>value` rows of that section
          local section="$1"
          cfg_rows 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' -v s="$section" '$4 == s { print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $5 }'
      }
      
      cfg_edit_value() {
          local key="$1" current value
          current="$(cfg_get "$key")"
          printf '\n  %s = %s\n' "$key" "${current:-<empty>}"
          menu_read "  new value (Enter keeps it, - clears it)" || return 0
          value="$MENU_ANSWER"
          [ -z "$value" ] && { info "Left it alone."; return 0; }
          [ "$value" = "-" ] && value=""
          if cfg_set "$key" "$value"; then
              ok "$key is now ${value:-<empty>}"
          else
              err "Could not write config.env — is it read-only?"
          fi
      }
      
      cfg_section() { # <section title>
          local section="$1" rows=() row i n=0
          while :; do
              rows=()
              while IFS= read -r row; do
                  [ -n "$row" ] && rows+=("$row")
              done < <(cfg_each_row "$section")
      
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${section:-Unsectioned}${NC}"
              hr
              if [ "${#rows[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  info "This section has no keys."
                  pause_menu
                  return 0
              fi
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  local key="${rows[$i]%%$'\t'*}" rest="${rows[$i]#*$'\t'}"
                  local active="${rest%%$'\t'*}" value="${rest#*$'\t'}"
                  local state='on '
                  [ "$active" = "1" ] || state='off'
                  value="$(printf '%s' "$value" | sed 's/^"\(.*\)"$/\1/')"
                  printf '  %3d  %s  %-30s %-34.34s\n' "$((i + 1))" "$state" "$key" "$value"
              done
              echo ""
              echo "    number = edit value · d number = switch off · e number = switch on"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  d*|D*)
                      i="${MENU_ANSWER#?}"
                      case "$i" in ''|*[!0-9]*) warn "d needs a number, like d3."; continue ;; esac
```

The terminal is now the same tool as the window.

## What `./build.sh` does now

With no arguments on a terminal it opens a menu instead of building immediately:

```
     1  Build              dry run, build, check, doctor, clean
     2  config.env         browse and edit one key at a time
     3  Addons             module tweaks: settings and overlay resources
     4  Device             read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone
     5  Detect display     cutout, corners, status bar height, refresh rates
     6  UDFPS              in-display fingerprint geometry
     7  Match property     which property the submission should match on
     8  Files              what was built, and where it is
     9  Docs               the guides in docs/
```

A header above it answers "where am I?" the way the app's header does: device identity read from `config.env`, how many keys are set, and what the last build produced. Every screen prints what a setting does before you change it.

## The new pieces

- **`stuff/scripts/menu.sh`** — the front end. It never re-implements a step: `1 → 2` shells out to `./build.sh build`, so a menu build *is* the build you would have typed.
- **`stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh`** — reads and rewrites one `config.env` key, preserving the file's comments and shape. Sections come from the file's own headers, keys scale to 18 sections, a commented-out key shows as `off` and can be switched on by number, and the raw-file option is still there.
- **`stuff/scripts/device-id.sh`** — the GUI's Device tab in the terminal: manufacturer, model, codename from the phone (or an unpacked firmware folder), plus the module's condition. `--write` applies only the values it found.
- **`stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh`** — the submission match-property ranking, same rules as `gui/matchprop.go` (a test asserts the two candidate lists agree): zygote must be able to read the property, and the value must survive a GSI. It refuses rather than guessing when nothing is trustworthy.
- **Addons (3)** drives the same live/overlay addon catalog via `src/webui/addons.sh`, and **Detect display (5)** / **UDFPS (6)** drive the existing probes.

## Entry points and docs

`./build.sh` (and `build.cmd`) keep every old verb; adding `menu` forces the menu even without a terminal, and `build` forces the old no-argument behaviour — so scripts keep working. Termux therefore gets addons, device detection and the probes for the first time; `docs/termux.md` now walks through the menu, and the README documents the new default.

## Verification

- `bash stuff/tests/run.sh` — **all checks passed** (95 node tests, Go tests, shell syntax, doc links).
- New `stuff/tests/match-prop.test.js`, 8 tests over saved `getprop`/`getprop -Z` dumps: ranking, the `/system`-vs-`/vendor` rule, the `build_odm_prop` trap, `--write` refusing a medium answer (leaving `config.env` byte-identical), CRLF/warning tolerance, and the Go/shell candidate-list agreement.
- Driven by hand through a PTY: header, section browser, key edit, addon list, device screen, docs viewer, help, and the no-terminal path (still builds, doesn't open the menu). The `device-id`/`match-prop` runs end at "no device in adb devices", which is the correct no-phone behaviour.

One limitation: I had no phone attached, so the adb-dependent paths (device read, display probe, UDFPS over adb) were exercised only up to the "no device attached" report; the file-based paths are covered by tests.

```
- path: stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # adb-device.sh — which connected phone a probe talks to
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by device-probe.sh and udfps-probe.sh. Both used to carry the same
      # rule ("exactly one device, or stop"), which stops being useful the moment a
      # second phone is on the desk.
      #
      #   adb_pick_device ADB SERIAL PROGRAM
      #
      # ADB is the adb binary to run, SERIAL is what --device said ("" for automatic),
      # PROGRAM names the script in the messages. On success DEVICE_SERIAL holds the
      # serial to pass to `adb -s`; on failure the reason has already been printed.
      #
      # The state matters. adb can see a phone it cannot talk to (unauthorized,
      # offline, no permissions), and each of those has its own fix — telling the user
      # to plug the phone in is wrong advice for all three.
      #
      # Detection is the fragile part, so it is hardened against what adb actually
      # does rather than what its manual says:
      #
      #   * `adb devices` is a stream, not a table. A daemon start, a version
      #     mismatch, or a "no permissions" line shares it with the devices, so only
      #     lines whose second column is a real state are read as devices.
      #   * the listing can lie. It is a snapshot, so the chosen serial is confirmed
      #     with `get-state` before anything is run against it.
      #   * a wedged server hangs instead of failing. Every adb call here is bounded,
      #     and a timeout says "adb kill-server" instead of hanging the probe.
      #   * the first call after the server restarts can come back with no header at
      #     all. That is retried; a genuinely empty list is not.
      #   * a phone that is still "connecting" (wireless adb, or just plugged in)
      #     becomes ready in a second or two, so it is waited for briefly.
      #   * a serial can be listed twice, and wireless transports look like
      #     `192.168.1.5:5555`; duplicates are dropped and the transport is labelled.
      # =============================================================================
      
      # The states adb puts in the second column of `devices`, space-padded so a
      # value can be tested with `index(states, " " $2 " ")`.
      ADB_DEVICE_STATES=" device offline unauthorized bootloader recovery sideload rescue host connecting no "
      
      # The model and product from one `adb devices -l` line, for a menu a human can
      # read. Both are optional in adb's output, so this never assumes either. A
      # TCP/mDNS serial is called out: with USB and wireless adb on, the same phone
      # can be listed twice and the two entries are otherwise identical.
      adb_device_label() {
          local line="$1" model product serial suffix=""
          model="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/.* model:\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"
          product="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/.* product:\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"
          [ -n "$model" ] || model="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/.* device:\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"
          serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $1}')"
          case "$serial" in
              *:*) suffix=" [wireless]" ;;
          esac
          if [ -n "$model" ] && [ -n "$product" ]; then
              printf '%s (%s)%s' "$model" "$product" "$suffix"
          elif [ -n "$model" ]; then
              printf '%s%s' "$model" "$suffix"
          else
              printf 'no model reported%s' "$suffix"
          fi
      }
      
      # One line per device on stdin, already in `devices -l` form.
      adb_device_table() {
          local line serial state
          while IFS= read -r line; do
              [ -n "$line" ] || continue
              serial="${line%% *}"
              state="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $2}')"
              printf '  %-18s %-13s %s\n' "$serial" "$state" "$(adb_device_label "$line")"
          done
      }
      
      # The fix for every device that is attached but not ready. Printed after the
      # table so the last thing on screen is the action, not the list.
      adb_device_advice() {
          printf '%s\n' "${1:-}" | awk '
              $2 == "unauthorized" { print "  " $1 ": unlock the phone and accept the USB debugging prompt" }
              $2 == "offline"      { print "  " $1 ": offline — unplug and replug it, or run adb kill-server" }
              $2 == "no"           { print "  " $1 ": no permissions — Linux needs a udev rule, Windows a driver" }
              $2 == "connecting"   { print "  " $1 ": still connecting — wait a moment and run it again" }
              $2 == "bootloader"   { print "  " $1 ": in the bootloader — boot Android to read the running ROM" }
              $2 == "recovery"     { print "  " $1 ": in recovery — adb works there, but dumpsys and getprop of the ROM do not" }
              $2 == "sideload"     { print "  " $1 ": sideload mode — reboot to Android first" }
              $2 == "rescue"       { print "  " $1 ": rescue mode — reboot to Android first" }
          '
      }
      
      # Turn what the user typed into a serial from READY (the `devices -l` lines of
      # ready devices): a menu number, a full serial, or a prefix that only one serial
      # starts with. Prints nothing and fails when the answer is not unambiguous.
      adb_device_resolve() {
          local ready="$1" choice="${2:-}" count n matches
          [ -n "$choice" ] || return 1
          count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
          case "$choice" in
              *[!0-9]*) ;;
              *)
                  n=$((choice + 0))
                  if [ "$n" -ge 1 ] && [ "$n" -le "$count" ]; then
                      printf '%s\n' "$ready" | sed -n "${n}p" | awk '{print $1}'
                      return 0
                  fi
                  ;;
          esac
          matches="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | awk -v c="$choice" 'index($1, c) == 1 { print $1 }')"
          if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$matches" | grep -c . || true)" -eq 1 ]; then
              printf '%s' "$matches"
              return 0
          fi
          return 1
      }
      
      # Prompt on stderr instead of stdout: stdout is often JSON that a caller parses.
      # Reads stdin, so it can be exercised with a pipe in tests.
      adb_device_choose() {
          local ready="$1" count choice resolved tries=0
          count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
          printf 'More than one device is connected:\n' >&2
          printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2
          while [ "$tries" -lt 3 ]; do
              tries=$((tries + 1))
              printf 'Which device? [1-%d] or a serial: ' "$count" >&2
              IFS= read -r choice || return 1
              if resolved="$(adb_device_resolve "$ready" "$choice")"; then
                  printf '%s' "$resolved"
                  return 0
              fi
              printf '  not one of them\n' >&2
          done

      }
      
      # Run a command with a deadline, because adb has no timeout of its own and a
      # wedged server otherwise hangs the probe with nothing on screen. LIMIT is in
      # tenths of a second. The child writes a sentinel when it finishes, so a finished
      # process is never mistaken for a running one. 124 means "did not answer".
      adb_device_exec() {

                  kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null
                  wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
                  return 124
              fi
              sleep 0.1
              waited=$((waited + 1))
          done
          wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
          status="$(cat "$out.status" 2>/dev/null || printf 0)"
          return "${status:-0}"
      }

      # Sets ADB_DEVICES to those lines and ADB_DEVICES_NOTE to whatever adb said
      # about itself, so a wedged server or a "no permissions" complaint can be shown

      # produce a list at all.

- path: stuff/tests/adb-device.test.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh — the one rule for "which phone?"
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Both probes source it, and its whole job is to not guess. That makes it worth
      // testing with more than a syntax check: the failure it prevents (writing to the
      // wrong phone) is silent until it is too late.
      //
      // The fake adb below answers `devices -l` with a canned table and `get-state`
      // with "device", so no phone is involved.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/adb-device.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import { chmodSync, mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const lib = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'adb-device.sh');
      
      const BOTH_READY = `List of devices attached
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      595648cf1cdc           device product:zephyr_global model:26012RN62A device:zephyr transport_id:37
      `;
      
      const ONE_READY = `List of devices attached
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      0123456789AB           unauthorized usb:1-1 transport_id:3
      `;
      
      const NONE_READY = `List of devices attached
      0123456789AB           unauthorized usb:1-1 transport_id:3
      emulator-5554          offline
      `;
      
      // A fake adb whose body is written by the caller, for the cases a canned table
      // cannot express: a wedged server, a state that changes between calls.
      function fakeAdbScript(body, devicesOutput = '') {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'adb-device-'));
        const adb = join(dir, 'adb');
        writeFileSync(adb, `#!/bin/sh\n${body}`);
        chmodSync(adb, 0o755);
        const table = join(dir, 'devices.txt');
        writeFileSync(table, devicesOutput);
        return { adb, table, dir };
      }
      
      function fakeAdb(devicesOutput) {
        // $1 is "devices" or "-s"; get-state only matters for a device that was
        // accepted, and a real adb would answer "device" there too.
        return fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then
        cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"
        exit 0
      fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ] && [ "$3" = "get-state" ]; then
        echo device
        exit 0
      fi
      exit 0
      `,
          devicesOutput
        );
      }
      
      // Runs adb_pick_device in a bash that sources the library, and returns both the
      // chosen serial and whatever the helper printed. stdin is a pipe unless a menu
      // answer is supplied, which is exactly the non-interactive case the app sees.
      function pickUsing(adb, table, serialArg, { stdin = '' } = {}) {
        // 2>&1: the helper explains itself on stderr, and these tests are about that
        // explanation as much as about the serial.
        const script = `{ . "${lib}" && adb_pick_device "$FAKE_ADB" ${JSON.stringify(serialArg)} test-probe && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"; } 2>&1`;
        const run = () =>
          execFileSync('bash', ['-c', script], {
            env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table, TERM: 'dumb' },
            input: stdin,
            encoding: 'utf8',
            stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          });
        try {
          return { out: run(), status: 0 };
        } catch (err) {
          return { out: `${err.stdout || ''}${err.stderr || ''}`, status: err.status ?? 1 };
        }
      }
      
      function pick(devicesOutput, serialArg, { stdin = '' } = {}) {
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdb(devicesOutput);
        return pickUsing(adb, table, serialArg, { stdin });
      }
      
      test('one ready phone is used even when another is unauthorized', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(ONE_READY, '');
        assert.equal(status, 0, out);
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
        // The unauthorized phone is called out by state, not counted as an option.
        assert.match(out, /0123456789AB.*unauthorized/);
      });
      
      test('two ready phones without a pick stop with the list, not a guess', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(BOTH_READY, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /595648cf1cdc/);
        assert.match(out, /RFCM90F5BBX/);
        assert.match(out, /--device SERIAL/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /PICKED=/);
      });
      
      test('an explicit serial is used as given', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(BOTH_READY, '595648cf1cdc');
        assert.equal(status, 0, out);
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=595648cf1cdc/);
      });
      
      test('an explicit serial that is not attached names what is', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(BOTH_READY, 'GONE');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /GONE is not attached/);
        assert.match(out, /RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      test('an explicit serial that is not ready says why', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(ONE_READY, '0123456789AB');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /attached but unauthorized/);
      });
      
      test('nothing attached says so instead of asking about states', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick('List of devices attached\n\n', '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /no device in adb devices/);
      });
      
      test('nothing ready explains each state', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(NONE_READY, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /no device is ready/);
        assert.match(out, /accept the USB debugging prompt/);
        assert.match(out, /unplug and replug/);
      });
      
      test('the menu takes a number, a serial or an unambiguous prefix', () => {
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdb(BOTH_READY);
        const run = (answer) =>
          execFileSync(
            'bash',
            [
              '-c',
              `. "${lib}" && adb_device_choose "$(cat "$FAKE_DEVICES" | awk 'NR > 1 && NF && $2 == "device"')"`,
            ],
            {
              env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table },
              input: answer,
              encoding: 'utf8',
              stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
            }
          ).trim();
        assert.equal(run('2\n'), '595648cf1cdc');
        assert.equal(run('595648cf1cdc\n'), '595648cf1cdc');
        assert.equal(run('RFCM\n'), 'RFCM90F5BBX');
      });
      
      test('a prefix two serials share is ambiguous, and it asks again', () => {
        const shared = `List of devices attached
      ABC123                 device product:one model:One device:one transport_id:1
      ABC456                 device product:two model:Two device:two transport_id:2
      `;
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdb(shared);
        const out = execFileSync(
          'bash',
          ['-c', `. "${lib}" && adb_device_choose "$(cat "$FAKE_DEVICES" | awk 'NR > 1 && NF && $2 == "device"')"`],
          {
            env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table },
            input: 'ABC\nABC456\n',
            encoding: 'utf8',
            stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          }
        ).trim();
        assert.equal(out, 'ABC456');
      });
      
      // --- hardening --------------------------------------------------------------
      // `adb devices` is not a table: the daemon's own chatter shares the stream. A
      // line that is not a device must never be offered as one.
      test('daemon chatter and version warnings are not devices', () => {
        const noisy = `List of devices attached
      adb server version (41) doesn't match this client (39); killing...
      * daemon started successfully *
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      595648cf1cdc           device product:zephyr_global model:26012RN62A device:zephyr transport_id:37
      `;
        const { out, status } = pick(noisy, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        // Two real phones, so the answer is the list — with exactly two rows.
        assert.match(out, /2 devices are ready/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /daemon started/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /server version/);
      });
      
      test('a serial listed twice is offered once', () => {
        const twice = `List of devices attached
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      `;
        const { out, status } = pick(twice, '');
        assert.equal(status, 0, out);
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /2 devices are ready/);
      });
      
      test('a wireless transport is labelled as one', () => {
        const wireless = `List of devices attached
      192.168.0.31:5555      device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      595648cf1cdc           device product:zephyr_global model:26012RN62A device:zephyr transport_id:37
      `;
        const { out, status } = pick(wireless, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /192\.168\.0\.31:5555 .*\[wireless\]/);
      });
      
      // The first call after the server restarts can come back without a header. That
      // is a retry, not an empty desk.
      test('a listing with no header is retried until the server answers', () => {
        const { adb, table, dir } = fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then
        if [ -f "$FAKE_COUNTER" ]; then cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"; else : > "$FAKE_COUNTER"; echo "adb server version (41) doesn't match this client (39); killing..." >&2; fi
        exit 0
      fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ] && [ "$3" = "get-state" ]; then echo device; exit 0; fi
      exit 0
      `,
          ONE_READY
        );
        const counter = join(dir, 'calls');
        const out = execFileSync('bash', ['-c', `{ . "${lib}" && adb_pick_device "$FAKE_ADB" "" test-probe && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"; } 2>&1`], {
          env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table, FAKE_COUNTER: counter },
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
        });
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      // A phone that is still handshaking is not "nothing is ready" — waiting is what
      // makes a just-plugged or wireless device work on the first run.
      test('a device that is still connecting is waited for', () => {
        const { adb, table, dir } = fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then
        if [ -f "$FAKE_COUNTER" ]; then cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"; else : > "$FAKE_COUNTER"; printf 'List of devices attached\nRFCM90F5BBX  connecting\n'; fi
        exit 0
      fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ] && [ "$3" = "get-state" ]; then echo device; exit 0; fi
      exit 0
      `,
          ONE_READY
        );
        const counter = join(dir, 'calls');
        const out = execFileSync('bash', ['-c', `{ . "${lib}" && adb_pick_device "$FAKE_ADB" "" test-probe && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"; } 2>&1`], {
          env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table, FAKE_COUNTER: counter },
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
        });
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      // Ready in the listing, dead on the wire: the snapshot is checked, not trusted.
      test('a phone that is listed but will not answer get-state is refused', () => {
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"; exit 0; fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ]; then echo "error: device offline" >&2; exit 1; fi
      exit 0
      `,
          ONE_READY
        );
        const { out, status } = pickUsing(adb, table, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /did not answer get-state/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /PICKED=/);
      });
      
      // A wedged adb server otherwise hangs the probe with nothing on screen, which
      // reads as the script being stuck.
      test('adb that never answers is cut off with advice, not a hang', () => {
        const { adb, dir } = fakeAdbScript(`sleep 30
      `);
        const outFile = join(dir, 'out');
        const started = Date.now();
        const out = execFileSync('bash', ['-c', `. "${lib}" && adb_device_exec 5 "$OUT" "$FAKE_ADB" devices -l; printf 'status=%s' "$?"`], {
          env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, OUT: outFile },
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
        });
        assert.match(out, /status=124/);
        assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 5000, 'the bounded runner waited past its deadline');
      
        // The same deadline in the listing, with the advice the user needs. The limit
        // is a parameter here so the test does not sit out the real 20s.
        const listOut = execFileSync(
          'bash',
          ['-c', `. "${lib}" && adb_device_list "$FAKE_ADB" 5; printf 'status=%s note=%s' "$?" "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE"`],
          { env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb }, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'] }
        );
        assert.match(listOut, /status=1/);
        assert.match(listOut, /did not answer within .*adb kill-server/);
      });
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh

      # usually wants them in `$( )`, and a subshell would throw the note away.
      adb_device_list() {
          local adb="$1" limit="${2:-200}" dir status attempt=0 header=0
          ADB_DEVICES=""
          ADB_DEVICES_NOTE=""
          if [ ! -x "$adb" ] && ! command -v "$adb" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ADB_DEVICES_NOTE="adb was not found at $adb — install platform-tools, or point ADB at it"
              return 127
          fi
          dir="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/adb-device.$$")"
          mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null
      
          # The first call after the server restarts can return no header at all (a
          # version mismatch kills the daemon mid-command). That is worth retrying; an
          # empty list under a real header is not, because the answer is the same.
          while :; do
              attempt=$((attempt + 1))
              adb_device_exec "$limit" "$dir/devices" "$adb" devices -l
              status=$?
              if [ "$status" -eq 124 ]; then
                  ADB_DEVICES_NOTE="adb did not answer within $((limit / 10))s — run adb kill-server, then try again"
                  rm -rf "$dir"
                  return 1
              fi
              if grep -q 'List of devices attached' "$dir/devices" 2>/dev/null; then header=1; break; fi
              if [ "$attempt" -ge 3 ]; then break; fi
              sleep 0.7
          done
      
          ADB_DEVICES_NOTE="$(
              sed 's/\r$//' "$dir/devices.err" 2>/dev/null |
                  sed '/^[[:space:]]*$/d' |
                  tr '\n' ' ' |
                  sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//'
          )"
          if [ "$header" -eq 0 ]; then
              [ -n "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" ] || ADB_DEVICES_NOTE="adb devices exited $status without a device list"
              rm -rf "$dir"
              return 1
          fi
      
          # Only real device lines, one per serial: the same stream carries daemon
          # chatter and version warnings, and a table with those in it is worse than
          # no table at all.
          ADB_DEVICES="$(awk -v states="$ADB_DEVICE_STATES" '
              { sub(/\r$/, "") }
              NF >= 2 && index(states, " " $2 " ") { if (!seen[$1]++) print }
          ' "$dir/devices")"
          rm -rf "$dir"
          return 0
      }
      
      # The list is a snapshot: a phone can be listed as ready and still not open. Ask
      # adb to open it, bounded like everything else.
      adb_device_alive() {
          local adb="$1" serial="$2" dir status
          dir="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/adb-device.$$")"
          mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null
          adb_device_exec 100 "$dir/state" "$adb" -s "$serial" get-state
          status=$?

              sleep 0.2
              waited=$((waited + 1))
              adb_device_list "$adb" || break
              attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
          done
      
          ready="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "device"')"
          ready_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
      
          serial=""
          if [ -n "$want" ]; then
              # An explicit serial is used as typed, but it still has to be attached:
              # otherwise adb's own "device not found" is the only explanation the
              # user gets, with no hint about what is actually plugged in.
              state="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s { print $2; exit }')"
              case "$state" in
                  device) serial="$want" ;;
                  '')
                      printf '%s: %s is not attached.\n' "$prog" "$want" >&2
                      ;;
                  *)
                      printf '%s: %s is attached but %s.\n' "$prog" "$want" "$state" >&2
                      ;;
              esac
              if [ -z "$serial" ]; then
                  if [ -n "$attached" ]; then
                      printf 'Attached devices:\n' >&2
                      printf '%s\n' "$attached" | adb_device_table >&2
                      adb_device_advice "$attached" >&2
                  else
                      printf 'No device is attached — plug one in and allow USB debugging.\n' >&2
                      [ -z "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-}" ] || printf '  %s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" >&2
                  fi
                  return 1
              fi
          elif [ "$ready_count" -eq 0 ]; then
              [ -z "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-}" ] || printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" >&2
              if [ -n "$attached" ]; then
                  printf '%s: no device is ready to talk to:\n' "$prog" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$attached" | adb_device_table >&2
              else
                  printf '%s: no device in adb devices — plug the phone in and allow USB debugging.\n' "$prog" >&2
              fi
              adb_device_advice "$attached" >&2
              return 1
          elif [ "$ready_count" -eq 1 ]; then
              serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | awk '{print $1}' | head -n1)"
              sleeping="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 != "device" { print $1 " (" $2 ")" }' | tr '\n' ' ')"
              [ -z "$sleeping" ] || printf '%s: using %s; not ready: %s\n' "$prog" "$serial" "${sleeping% }" >&2
          else
              # Several phones. Ask when there is a terminal to ask on; never guess,
              # because picking the wrong one is how the wrong phone gets written to.
              if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s: %d devices are ready:\n' "$prog" "$ready_count" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2
                  printf '%s: choose one with --device SERIAL\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
              if ! serial="$(adb_device_choose "$ready")"; then
                  printf '%s: no device chosen.\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
          fi
      
          # The list is a snapshot; this is the check that adb can actually open it.
          adb_device_alive "$adb" "$serial"
          case $? in
              0) ;;
              124)
                  printf '%s: %s is listed as ready but adb did not answer within 10s — run adb kill-server.\n' "$prog" "$serial" >&2
                  return 1
                  ;;
              *)
                  printf '%s: %s is listed as ready but did not answer get-state — replug it.\n' "$prog" "$serial" >&2
                  return 1
                  ;;
          esac
          DEVICE_SERIAL="$serial"
          return 0
```

```
  content: |
          # moment. Waiting a couple of seconds turns that into the phone the user
          # means, instead of "nothing is ready" and a retry they have to time.
          while [ -n "$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "connecting"')" ] && [ "$waited" -lt 25 ]; do
              sleep 0.2
              waited=$((waited + 1))
              adb_device_list "$adb" || break
              attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
          done
      
          ready="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "device"')"
          ready_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
      
          serial=""
          if [ -n "$want" ]; then
              # An explicit serial is used as typed, but it still has to be attached:
              # otherwise adb's own "device not found" is the only explanation the
              # user gets, with no hint about what is actually plugged in.
              state="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s { print $2; exit }')"
              case "$state" in
                  device) serial="$want" ;;
                  '')
                      printf '%s: %s is not attached.\n' "$prog" "$want" >&2
                      ;;
                  *)
                      printf '%s: %s is attached but %s.\n' "$prog" "$want" "$state" >&2
                      ;;
              esac
              if [ -z "$serial" ]; then
              if [ -n "$attached" ]; then
                  printf 'Attached devices:\n' >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$attached" | adb_device_table >&2
                  adb_device_advice "$attached" >&2
              else
                  [ -z "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-}" ] || printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" >&2
                  printf '%s: %s is not attached — plug the phone in and allow USB debugging.\n' "$prog" "$want" >&2
                  # A device that is not attached yet is exactly the case the wait is
                  # for: give it a chance to appear and be picked, rather than making
                  # the user start the whole menu again.
                  if adb_device_wait "$adb" "$prog"; then
                      attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
                      ready="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "device"')"
                      ready_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
                      state="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s { print $2; exit }')"
                      [ "$state" = "device" ] && serial="$want"
                      # The serial the user named may be the one that was already
                      # attached: if only one phone came up, that is the one meant.
                      if [ -z "$serial" ] && [ "$ready_count" -eq 1 ]; then
                          serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | awk '{print $1}' | head -n1)"
                      fi
                      if [ -z "$serial" ]; then
                          printf '%s: %s did not appear.\n' "$prog" "$want" >&2
                          return 1
                      fi
                  else
                      return 1
                  fi
              fi
              fi
          elif [ "$ready_count" -eq 0 ]; then
              [ -z "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-}" ] || printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" >&2
              if [ -n "$attached" ]; then
                  printf '%s: no device is ready to talk to:\n' "$prog" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$attached" | adb_device_table >&2
              else
                  printf '%s: no device in adb devices — plug the phone in and allow USB debugging.\n' "$prog" >&2
              fi
              adb_device_advice "$attached" >&2
              # A phone left unauthorized or offline is fixed in a second; waiting
              # turns that into the same run instead of another menu trip.
              adb_device_wait "$adb" "$prog" || return 1
              attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
              ready="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "device"')"
              ready_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
              if [ "$ready_count" -eq 1 ]; then
                  serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | awk '{print $1}' | head -n1)"
              elif [ "$ready_count" -eq 0 ]; then
                  return 1
              elif [ ! -t 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s: %d devices are ready:\n' "$prog" "$ready_count" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2
                  printf '%s: choose one with --device SERIAL\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              elif ! serial="$(adb_device_choose "$ready")"; then
                  printf '%s: no device chosen.\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
          elif [ "$ready_count" -eq 1 ]; then
              serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | awk '{print $1}' | head -n1)"
              sleeping="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 != "device" { print $1 " (" $2 ")" }' | tr '\n' ' ')"
              [ -z "$sleeping" ] || printf '%s: using %s; not ready: %s\n' "$prog" "$serial" "${sleeping% }" >&2
          else
              # Several phones. Ask when there is a terminal to ask on; never guess,

              if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s: %d devices are ready:\n' "$prog" "$ready_count" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2
                  printf '%s: choose one with --device SERIAL\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
              if ! serial="$(adb_device_choose "$ready")"; then

                  return 1
              fi
          fi

                              printf '%s: %d devices are ready — choose one with --device SERIAL\n' "$prog" "$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)" >&2

                      fi
                  elif [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)" -eq 1 ]; then
                      serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | awk '{print $1}' | head -n1)"
                  else
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/menu.sh

                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  r|R)
                      addons_call reset
                      info "Every addon is back to the ROM's own value."
                      continue
                      ;;
              esac
      
              if [[ "$ans" == *=* ]]; then
                  id="${ans%%=*}"
                  value="${ans#*=}"
                  if ! printf '%s\n' "${rows[@]}" | awk -F'|' -v id="$id" '$1 == id { found = 1 } END { exit !found }'; then
                      warn "No addon called '$id'."
                      continue
                  fi
                  addons_call set "$id=$value"
                  continue
              fi
      
              case "$ans" in
                  *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number, number=value, or r."; continue ;;
              esac
              if [ "$ans" -lt 1 ] || [ "$ans" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then
                  warn "No such addon."
                  continue
              fi
              IFS='|' read -r id choices default label row kind <<<"${rows[$((ans - 1))]}"
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${label}${NC}"
              printf '  %s\n' "$row"
              echo ""
              printf '  choices: %s · now: %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$choices" | tr ',' '/')" "$(addons_saved "$id" || printf '%s' "$default")"
              menu_read "  value (Enter keeps it)" || return 0
              value="$MENU_ANSWER"
              [ -z "$value" ] && continue
              addons_call set "$id=$value"
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Probes
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # device-probe.sh, udfps-probe.sh and device-id.sh all print a report and, with
      # --write, put the winners in config.env. That is the only difference between
      # the two answers here, so the submenu asks it instead of inventing options.
      probe_menu() { # <title> <script> <note>
          local title="$1" script="$2" note="$3" dir
          while :; do
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${title}${NC}"
              hr
              [ -n "$note" ] && echo "  $note" && echo ""
              echo "     1  Read the connected phone (report only)"
              echo "     2  Read the connected phone and write the answers to config.env"
              echo "     3  Read an unpacked firmware folder instead"
              echo "     0  Back"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) bash "$script"; pause_menu ;;
                  2) bash "$script" --write; pause_menu ;;
                  3)
                      menu_read "  folder holding the unpacked ROM" || return 0
                      dir="$MENU_ANSWER"
                      [ -n "$dir" ] || continue
                      if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
                          warn "No such folder: $dir"
                          continue
                      fi
                      if confirm "  Write what it finds to config.env? [y/N] " n; then
                          bash "$script" --firmware "$dir" --write
                      else
                          bash "$script" --firmware "$dir"
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      menu_device() {
          probe_menu "Device" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/device-id.sh" \
              "Reads DEVICE_MANUFACTURER, DEVICE_MODEL and DEVICE_CODENAME, and the module condition."
      }
      
      menu_detect() {
          probe_menu "Detect display" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh" \
              "Cutout path, corner radius, status bar height and refresh rates."
      }
      
      menu_udfps() {
          probe_menu "UDFPS" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh" \
              "The in-display fingerprint sensor's centre and radius."
      }
      
      menu_match() {
          bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh"
          pause_menu
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Main loop
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_main() {
          while :; do
              menu_header
              menu_items
              echo ""
              menu_read "  >" || { echo ""; return 0; }
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) menu_build ;;
                  2) menu_config ;;
                  3) menu_addons ;;
                  4) menu_device ;;
                  5) menu_detect ;;
                  6) menu_udfps ;;
                  7) menu_match ;;
                  8) menu_files ;;
                  9) menu_docs ;;
                  q|Q|quit|exit) return 0 ;;
                  '') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Pick a number from the list, or q to quit." ;;
              esac
              [ "$MENU_SLEEP" = "0" ] || sleep "$MENU_SLEEP"
          done
      }
      
      # Standalone: `bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh`. Sourced by build.sh, which calls
      # menu_main itself.
      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
          menu_main
      fi
```
