- path: docs/termux.md
  content: |
      # Termux (Android)
      
      You can build the overlay on the phone itself. The toolchain is the same; only
      the install step differs.
      
      > Use Termux from **[F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/en/packages/com.termux/)**.
      > The Google Play version is outdated and its packages are incompatible.
      
      ---
      
      ## 1. Prepare Termux
      
      ```bash
      termux-setup-storage
      
      apt update
      apt upgrade -y
      
      apt install -y git aapt aapt2 apksigner android-tools openjdk-17 \
                     unzip zip curl tsu
      ```
      
      If `pkg install` fails with signature or mirror errors, run
      `termux-change-repo`, pick a mirror close to you, then repeat `apt update`.
      
      > **`zipalign` comes from the `aapt` package, not from `aapt2`.** Installing
      > `aapt2`, `apksigner` and `android-tools` leaves `zipalign` missing; adding
      > `aapt` provides it. If it is still absent, `build.sh` continues and copies
      > the APK instead of aligning it (valid, just not mmap-aligned) and tells you
      > to run `pkg install aapt`.
      
      ---
      
      ## 2. Clone into the home directory
      
      ```bash
      cd ~
      git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
      cd treble-rro-creator
      ```
      
      > ⚠ **Do not clone into `/sdcard`.** Android's shared storage does not support
      > executable permissions or the symlinks `aapt2`/`zipalign` need. Use `~`
      > (`/data/data/com.termux/files/home`).
      
      ---
      
      ## 3. Build
      
      ```bash
      ./build.sh
      ```
      
      On a terminal this opens the **menu**, which is the desktop app's toolkit in a
      numbered list — the same build, the same `config.env` editor, the same phone
      probes. Termux has no window, so this is the full interface on the phone:
      
      ```
           1  Build              dry run, build, check, doctor, clean
           2  config.env         browse and edit one key at a time
           3  Addons             module tweaks: settings and overlay resources
           4  Device             read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone
           5  Auto Detect        ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G
           6  UDFPS              in-display fingerprint geometry
           7  Match property     which property the submission should match on
           8  Files              what was built, and where it is
           9  Docs               the guides in docs/
      ```
      
      `1 → 2` is the build. The first run checks the toolchain: if something is
      missing it installs it (aapt2/zipalign/apksigner via `pkg`,
      `framework-res.apk` by download), then builds.
      
      To skip the menu, use the verbs directly:
      
      ```bash
      ./build.sh build     # build, installing tools if needed
      ./build.sh setup     # [3] Android / Termux, then [1] Android 13 resources
      ./build.sh doctor    # verify
      ./build.sh check     # validate config.env only
      ```
      
      If `build.sh` cannot install packages unattended, it prints the exact command
      to run. `./build.sh setup` walks through the options interactively.
      
      ---
      
      ## 4. Edit the config
      
      `2` in the menu lists `config.env` by section with the value next to each key,
      `on`/`off` for the ones that are commented out, and writes the change in place —
      the comments and the file's shape stay as they are. That is quicker on a phone
      than hunting for a `#` in a 240-line file.
      
      Use a text editor when you want to see the notes above each key:
      
      ```bash
      nano config.env
      ```
      
      `Ctrl+O` then `Enter` saves, `Ctrl+X` exits. Or edit the same file with
      MT Manager at:
      
      ```
      /data/data/com.termux/files/home/treble-rro-creator/config.env
      ```
      
      Required values and every optional flag are listed in
      [configuration.md](configuration.md).
      
      With the phone in the same hand, `4` (Device) fills in `DEVICE_CODENAME`,
      `DEVICE_MANUFACTURER` and `DEVICE_MODEL` from `getprop`, `5` (Auto Detect) reads
      what the running ROM says about the hardware — cutout path, corner radii, status
      bar height, refresh rates, the VoLTE and 5G flags, the light sensor and the OEM
      switches — and `6` (UDFPS) finds the fingerprint sensor's real geometry. No PC,
      no typing values between screens.
      
      Do not forget `src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` — replace it with your
      device's file, see
      [device-extraction.md](device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
      
      ---
      
      ## 5. Install the module
      
      ```bash
      cp out/*-ksu.zip /sdcard/
      ```
      
      Then either:
      
      - open your root manager (KernelSU / KSU Next / Magisk) → Modules → install the
        zip, or use MT Manager to pick it from `/sdcard/`, or
      - from a PC over ADB:
      
      ```bash
      adb shell su -c 'ksud module install /sdcard/treble-overlay-<device>-ksu.zip'
      ```
      
      Reboot when done.
      
      > **KernelSU / KSU Next:** install **Magic Mount** (or Hybrid Mount configured
      > for magic mount) before flashing overlay modules.
      > **Never use OverlayFS** — it mounts fine, but a mistake in a vendor build's
      > `sepolicy.rule` or VINTF manifests then bootloops the device; magic mount
      > ignores the bad file and boots.
      
      ---
      
      ## Tips
      
      - Keep the project inside Termux home. Moving it to `/sdcard` breaks execution
        permissions.
      - `./build.sh clean` frees space; `./build.sh clean --all` starts over for a
        new device. Backups go to `stuff/backups/`.
      - Building needs roughly 300 MB free for the toolchain and intermediates.
      - If Termux is killed during a download, just run `./build.sh` again — already
        downloaded pieces are reused.
      - Logs are printed in the terminal. For a detailed trace:
        `bash -x ./build.sh 2>&1 | tee build.log`.
      
````

=== menu.sh head ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# menu.sh — the terminal front end
# =============================================================================
# The desktop app and this file drive the same tools: the device probes, the
# addon catalog, the match-property ranking and build.sh's own verbs. The goal
# is that a phone with a terminal (Termux, ssh, a server) gets the same answers
# as the window, without a GUI toolkit.
#
#   ./build.sh                 opens this (when stdin is a terminal)
#   ./build.sh menu            opens this even when stdin is not a terminal
#   bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh same thing, standalone
#
# Every action shells out to the real entry point — `build.sh build`,
# `device-probe.sh --write`, `addons.sh set` — so there is exactly one
# implementation of each step and the menu cannot drift from the app.
# =============================================================================

if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
    ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
    export ROOT
    . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
fi
. "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small things
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

- path: stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # device-probe.sh — read the display settings an overlay has to match
      # =============================================================================
      # The overlay writes a handful of numbers that are properties of the panel, not
      # style choices: the cutout path, the corner radius, the status bar height, the
      # refresh rates. Guessing them puts content under a camera or leaves the clock
      # off the edge, so this asks the phone (or an unpacked ROM) and keeps every
      # answer with the source it came from.
      #
      #   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh                 # connected device
      #   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --firmware DIR  # extracted ROM dump
      #   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --json          # for the desktop app
      #   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --write         # put the winners in config.env
      #   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --power-profile # print res/xml/power_profile.xml
      #
      # --power-profile prints the compiled XML tree of the power profile (the
      # desktop app turns it back into a file); everything else about the run goes to
      # stderr.
      #
      # What answers, and how far to trust it:
      #
      #   runtime   dumpsys display / dumpsys window — what the panel driver and the
      #             running framework report. Survives a GSI for anything the display
      #             hardware tells Android (corners, refresh rates), but says nothing
      #             about the OEM ROM once the OEM system partition is gone.
      #   resource  cmd overlay lookup android:... — the value the framework is
      #             serving right now. On a GSI that can be the GSI's own default, so
      #             it is evidence of "what Android uses", not of "what the OEM chose".
      #   firmware  aapt2 over framework-res.apk and the overlay APKs of an unpacked
      #             ROM. The only source that still has the OEM's cutout path when a
      #             GSI has replaced the system partition.

- path: stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # udfps-probe.sh — find a device's in-display fingerprint (UDFPS) geometry
      # =============================================================================
      # UDFPS_X / UDFPS_Y / UDFPS_RADIUS in config.env are the sensor's centre and
      # radius in px, written to android:array/config_udfps_sensor_props. Guessing
      # them puts the lock-screen icon next to the sensor instead of on it, so this
      # asks the phone (or a firmware dump) the same question several ways and says
      # where each answer came from.
      #
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh                 # connected device
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --firmware DIR  # extracted ROM dump
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --json          # for the desktop app
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --write         # put the winner in config.env
      #
      # Three situations, in the order the guide describes them:
      #
      #   1. OEM ROM on the phone. The vendor FOD properties and the preinstalled
      #      device overlay are both present, so this is the strongest evidence.
      #   2. GSI on the phone. The system partition is the GSI's, but /vendor and
      #      /persist keep the OEM's properties, and the phh/device overlay that was
      #      flashed with the GSI usually still carries the resource. Both are read
      #      here; a value that came from an overlay this tool itself modified is
      #      marked as such instead of being counted as independent.
      #   3. Firmware files. Only useful once the images are unpacked: super.img
      #      needs lpunpack before any APK or build.prop inside it can be read, so a
      #      bare fastboot ROM reports what it is missing instead of guessing.
      #
      # Nothing here is root-only. The overlay APKs and properties it reads are
      # world-readable on a normal boot.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# device-id.sh — what is this phone, as config.env spells it
# =============================================================================
# DEVICE_MANUFACTURER, DEVICE_MODEL and DEVICE_CODENAME end up in the overlay
# package, the module name and the launcher icon, so a wrong one is not a build
# error — it is an overlay for a phone that does not exist. This asks the phone
# (or saved `getprop` output) and shows every property that answered, which
# partition it came from, and why the winner won.
#
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-id.sh                 # connected device, then ask
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-id.sh --write         # take the answer it trusts
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-id.sh --json          # for scripts
#
#   --device SERIAL   with more than one phone attached
#   --device local    read this phone directly (Termux, needs root)
#   --adb PATH        adb is looked up on PATH and in stuff/tools/platform-tools
#   --values FILE     rank saved `getprop` output instead of asking a phone
#
# The codename rule is the same one the submission needs: a codename lives on
# /vendor, /odm or /bootimage, holds a lower-case name that is not the brand,
# the manufacturer, a build name or an SoC vendor, and survives a GSI. The
# ranking here and gui/matchprop.go answer the same question; change one, change
# the other.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1

=== match-prop 1-30 ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# match-prop.sh — which property should the submitted overlay match on?
# =============================================================================
# The overlay repo compares android:requiredSystemPropertyName/Value with plain
# string equality, and getting it wrong is silent: the overlay installs, `cmd
# overlay list` shows it enabled, and nothing changes. This reads the phone and
# ranks every property the submission could use, saying what each one is
# gambling on.
#
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh                  # connected device, then ask
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --write          # take the answer it trusts
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --json           # for scripts
#
#   --device SERIAL   with more than one phone attached
#   --adb PATH        adb is looked up on PATH and in stuff/tools/platform-tools
#   --values FILE --labels FILE   rank saved `getprop` / `getprop -Z` output
#                                 instead of asking a phone (tests, offline)
#
# Two rules decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable without
# root: zygote has to be able to read the property (`getprop -Z` prints the
# SELinux area; build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps),
# and the value has to survive what is installed (vendor, odm and bootimage keep
# the OEM value under a GSI; /system, /product and /system_ext do not). When no
# property satisfies both, this says so instead of picking one — a match that
# never holds is invisible.
#
# The same ranking lives in the desktop app (gui/matchprop.go). Change one,
# change the other.
# =============================================================================
=== id -u ===
1000

```

- path: stuff/scripts/device-id.sh
  content: |
      tmpdir="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t device-id)"
      cleanup() { rm -rf "$tmpdir"; }
      trap cleanup EXIT
      trap 'exit 130' INT
      trap 'exit 143' TERM HUP
      
      # `getprop` prints `[key]: [value]`; a warning mixed into the stream is skipped
      # rather than parsed into a device called "error".
      parse_props() {
          awk '
              {
                  sub(/\r$/, "")
                  if ($0 !~ /^\[.*\]: \[.*\]$/) next
                  i = index($0, "]: [")
                  if (i <= 2) next
                  printf "%s\t%s\n", substr($0, 2, i - 2), substr($0, i + 4, length($0) - i - 4)

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh — the one rule for "which phone?"
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Both probes source it, and its whole job is to not guess. That makes it worth
      // testing with more than a syntax check: the failure it prevents (writing to the
      // wrong phone) is silent until it is too late.
      //
      // The fake adb below answers `devices -l` with a canned table and `get-state`
      // with "device", so no phone is involved.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/adb-device.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { execFileSync, spawn } from 'node:child_process';
      import { chmodSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const lib = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'adb-device.sh');
      
      const BOTH_READY = `List of devices attached
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      595648cf1cdc           device product:zephyr_global model:26012RN62A device:zephyr transport_id:37
      `;
      
      const ONE_READY = `List of devices attached
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      0123456789AB           unauthorized usb:1-1 transport_id:3
      `;
      
      const NONE_READY = `List of devices attached
      0123456789AB           unauthorized usb:1-1 transport_id:3
      emulator-5554          offline
      `;
      
      // A fake adb whose body is written by the caller, for the cases a canned table
      // cannot express: a wedged server, a state that changes between calls.
      function fakeAdbScript(body, devicesOutput = '') {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'adb-device-'));
        const adb = join(dir, 'adb');
        writeFileSync(adb, `#!/bin/sh\n${body}`);
        chmodSync(adb, 0o755);
        const table = join(dir, 'devices.txt');
        writeFileSync(table, devicesOutput);
        return { adb, table, dir };
      }
      
      function fakeAdb(devicesOutput) {
        // $1 is "devices" or "-s"; get-state only matters for a device that was
        // accepted, and a real adb would answer "device" there too.
        return fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then
        cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"
        exit 0
      fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ] && [ "$3" = "get-state" ]; then
        echo device
        exit 0
      fi
      exit 0
      `,
          devicesOutput
        );
      }
      
      // Runs adb_pick_device in a bash that sources the library, and returns both the
      // chosen serial and whatever the helper printed. stdin is a pipe unless a menu
      // answer is supplied, which is exactly the non-interactive case the app sees.
      function pickUsing(adb, table, serialArg, { stdin = '', env = {} } = {}) {
        // 2>&1: the helper explains itself on stderr, and these tests are about that
        // explanation as much as about the serial.
        const script = `{ . "${lib}" && adb_pick_device "$FAKE_ADB" ${JSON.stringify(serialArg)} test-probe && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"; } 2>&1`;
        const run = () =>
          execFileSync('bash', ['-c', script], {
            env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table, TERM: 'dumb', ...env },
            input: stdin,
            encoding: 'utf8',
            stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          });
        try {
          return { out: run(), status: 0 };
        } catch (err) {
          return { out: `${err.stdout || ''}${err.stderr || ''}`, status: err.status ?? 1 };
        }
      }
      
      function pick(devicesOutput, serialArg, { stdin = '', env = {} } = {}) {
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdb(devicesOutput);
        return pickUsing(adb, table, serialArg, { stdin, env });
      }
      
      test('one ready phone is used even when another is unauthorized', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(ONE_READY, '');
        assert.equal(status, 0, out);
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
        // The unauthorized phone is called out by state, not counted as an option.
        assert.match(out, /0123456789AB.*unauthorized/);
      });
      
      test('two ready phones without a pick stop with the list, not a guess', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(BOTH_READY, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /595648cf1cdc/);
        assert.match(out, /RFCM90F5BBX/);
        assert.match(out, /--device SERIAL/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /PICKED=/);
      });

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# This phone, read directly (Termux)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# In Termux there is no adb server to dial: the phone is the machine the script
+# is running on. "Plug the phone in" is advice nobody can follow there, and
+# installing platform-tools only adds a binary that still has nothing to talk to.
+#
+# With root, the same commands the probes send over `adb shell` run natively —
+# getprop, cmd overlay, wm size/density, dumpsys and reads of /vendor — so local
+# mode is not a smaller detector, it is the same one with a shorter cable. Root
+# is not optional: an app UID is refused `cmd`, `dumpsys` and most /vendor files.
+#
+# DEVICE_LOCAL=1 selects it, DEVICE_ROOT_CMD says how to escalate, and the
+# probe's `serial` becomes "local" so nothing tries `adb -s local`.
+
+device_is_termux() {
+    [ -n "${TERMUX_VERSION:-}" ] && return 0
+    case "${PREFIX:-}" in */com.termux/*) return 0 ;; esac
+    case "${HOME:-}" in /data/data/com.termux/*) return 0 ;; esac
+    return 1
+}
+
+# The binary that reaches root on this phone, or "root" when we are already it.
+# su, tsu (Termux's su wrapper) and sudo all take `-c CMD`.
+device_root_cmd() {
+    if [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" = 0 ]; then printf 'root'; return 0; fi
+    local c
+    for c in su tsu sudo; do
+        command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { printf '%s' "$c"; return 0; }
+    done
+    return 1
+}
+
+# One command string as root on this phone, the same shape `adb shell` takes, so
+# the probes never learn which source they have.
+device_local_run() {
+    case "${DEVICE_ROOT_CMD:-root}" in
+        root) sh -c "$1" ;;
+        su)   su -c "$1" ;;
+        tsu)  tsu -c "$1" ;;
+        sudo) sudo sh -c "$1" ;;
+        *)    sh -c "$1" ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# Switch the probes over to this phone. PROG names the script in messages.
+# Verifies root before claiming local mode, so a denied prompt is a clear line
+# rather than a probe that silently reports nothing.
+device_local_begin() {
+    local prog="$1" cmd
+    if [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" = 0 ]; then
+        DEVICE_ROOT_CMD=root
+    else
+        cmd="$(device_root_cmd)" || {
+            printf '%s: reading this phone needs root, and no su/tsu/sudo was found.\n' "$prog" >&2
+            printf '  pkg install tsu\n  then start the tool with: tsu ./build.sh\n' >&2
+            return 1
+        }
+        DEVICE_ROOT_CMD="$cmd"
+        if [ "$(device_local_run 'id -u' </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | tail -n1)" != 0 ]; then
+            printf '%s: root was not granted — accept the su prompt (or run the tool with tsu) and try again.\n' "$prog" >&2
+            DEVICE_ROOT_CMD=""
+            return 1
+        fi
+    fi
+    DEVICE_LOCAL=1
+    DEVICE_SERIAL=local
+    # The menu announces this once before the probe starts; saying it again on
+    # every run reads like a second, failed attempt. DEVICE_LOCAL_QUIET=1 is set
+    # when the answer was already given.
+    if [ "${DEVICE_LOCAL_QUIET:-0}" != 1 ]; then
+        printf '%s: reading this phone directly%s\n' "$prog" \
+            "$([ "$DEVICE_ROOT_CMD" = root ] && printf ' (already root)' || printf ' (via %s)' "$DEVICE_ROOT_CMD")" >&2
+    fi
+    return 0
+}
+
+# Offer the local source. Only in Termux, and only when nobody already answered
+# the question (DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST=1 asked and granted, 0 declined) — the menu
+# asks once per session and passes the answer down.
+device_local_offer() {
+    local prog="$1" answer
+    device_is_termux || return 1
+    if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 2 ]; then
+        printf '%s: Termux has no adb link to a phone underneath — this machine is the phone.\n' "$prog" >&2
+        printf '%s: read it directly as root? [Y/n] ' "$prog" >&2
+        IFS= read -r answer || answer=y
+        case "$answer" in [nN]*) return 1 ;; esac
+    fi
+    device_local_begin "$prog"
+}
+
+# Whether adb can see a ready device right now, without the 120s wait: that wait
+# is for a cable being plugged in, and in Termux there is nothing to plug in.
+adb_device_ready_now() {
+    local adb="$1" want="${2:-}"
+    adb_device_list "$adb" 25 || return 1
+    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
+        printf '%s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s && $2 == "device"' | grep -q .
+    else
+        printf '%s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES" | awk '$2 == "device"' | grep -q .
+    fi
+}
+
+# One command on the chosen phone, CRs stripped and errors dropped. The single
+# place the two sources meet: both take a command string.
+device_sh() {
+    if [ "${DEVICE_LOCAL:-0}" = 1 ]; then
+        # The local shell is already root, so the probes' `su 0` retries would be
+        # a second escalation with nothing to gain — and a second su prompt. The
+        # prefix is dropped so those calls stay quiet.
+        case "$1" in
+            'su 0 '*) set -- "${1#su 0 }" ;;

+        device_local_run "$1" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'

+        "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} shell "$1" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
+    fi
+}
+
+# Copy a file off the chosen phone. adb pull runs as the shell user and falls
+# back to `su 0 cat` for root-only paths (/vendor/overlay); local mode is
+# already root, so one cat covers both.
+device_pull() {
+    local remote="$1" local_path="$2" to="$2"

+        device_local_run "cat '$remote'" >"$local_path" 2>/dev/null

+        && [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0

+}

+#
+# WANT is the --device value; "local" (also this/self/here) asks for this phone.
+# DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST=1/0 forces the answer, which is what the menu sets after
+# asking once. Sets DEVICE_LOCAL, DEVICE_ROOT_CMD, DEVICE_SERIAL and the probe's
+# `serial`; on failure the reason has already been printed.
+device_connect() {

+        local|this|self|here)

+            return 0

+    esac
+    case "$mode" in
+        1)

+            # once a session), so do not announce the switch again.
+            DEVICE_LOCAL_QUIET=1

+            serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"

+        && ! { resolve_adb 2>/dev/null && adb_device_ready_now "$adb" "$want"; }; then

+    fi
+    resolve_adb || {
+        printf '%s: adb was not found — install platform-tools, pass --adb PATH, or use --device local\n' "$prog" >&2
+        return 1
+    }
+    adb_pick_device "$adb" "$want" "$prog" || return 1
+    serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
+    return 0
+}

- path: build.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay Creator
      # =============================================================================
      # One command for everything. With a terminal attached it opens the menu, which
      # reaches every tool the desktop app has; with an argument it does exactly that
      # one thing, as before.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 the menu (on a terminal); otherwise: build
      #   ./build.sh menu            the menu, even without a terminal
      #   ./build.sh build           build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
      #   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
      #   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
      #   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
      #   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
      #   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
      #   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
      #
      #   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
      #   -h, --help                 this help
      #
      # On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
      # Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
      # drive — see docs/windows.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -e
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Project root
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      # Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
      # not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
      if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
      fi
      export ROOT
      cd "$ROOT"
      
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"
      
      # Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
      tools_on_path
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Options
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MODE="build"
      REQUESTED=$#
      CHECK_MODE=false
      DRY_RUN=false
      ASSUME_YES=false
      FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
      CLEAN_ALL=false
      FORCE_RES=""
      ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false
      
      usage() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
          echo "    (none)             The menu (on a terminal), otherwise a build"
          echo "    menu               The menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes"
          echo "    build              Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
          echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
          echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
          echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
          echo "    clean              Remove build output"
          echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
          echo ""
      }
      
      for arg in "$@"; do
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # No arguments and a terminal to talk on: the menu. Everything scripted passes
      # a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          MODE="menu"
      fi
      
      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).
      wsl_guard
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Dispatch
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      case "$MODE" in
          menu)
              # The terminal front end. It shells out to this same script for a build,
              # so a build started from the menu is the build a user would type.
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/menu.sh"
              menu_main
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          doctor)
              if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
              ;;
      
          setup)
              banner "Setup — build tools"
              migrate_layout
              # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
              # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
              # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
              # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
              # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
              if $ASSUME_YES; then
                  ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
              else
                  ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
              fi
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          check)
              # Config validation only: no tools, no output.
              CHECK_MODE=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          clean)
              migrate_layout
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/clean.sh"
              ;;
      
          dryrun)
              # Needs config.env and the resource generators, no toolchain: the point
              # is to see the plan in seconds.
              DRY_RUN=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          build)
              # Move any files left in the old top-level layout into src/.
              migrate_layout
              if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Windows"
              elif $IS_TERMUX; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Termux"
              else
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Linux"
              fi
              # Installs only what is missing; prints a summary and returns non-zero
              # when the machine still cannot build.
              ensure_toolchain auto
              # The installer may just have created stuff/tools/, so refresh PATH.
              tools_on_path
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      esac
      
- path: treble-rro-creator.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble RRO Creator — desktop app
      # =============================================================================
      # One command, from anywhere:
      #
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh                  build if needed, then open the window
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh --rebuild        rebuild first (after a git pull, say)
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh --release        no console window (Windows; the default)
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh --detach         accepted for scripts; hand-off is automatic
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh --browser        no window; use the default browser
      #   ./treble-rro-creator.sh -clone ~/other   start on a different clone
      #
      # The first launch builds the app, downloading Go and (on Windows) a MinGW-w64
      # gcc into stuff/tools/ when the machine has none; a checkout that already has
      # gui/bin/ filled in runs without a toolchain at all, and the app finds its
      # clone by walking up from where it lives, so no path has to be typed.
      #
      # Windows: double-click treble-rro-creator.cmd; it finds Git Bash and calls this.
      # =============================================================================
      set -euo pipefail
      
      here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      exe="$here/gui/bin/treble-rro-creator-gui"
      case "$(uname -s)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) exe="$exe.exe" ;;
      esac
      
      rebuild=false
      release=false
      detach=false
      browser=false
      app_args=()
      for arg in "$@"; do
          case "$arg" in
              -h|--help)
                  # The launcher's own flags, which the app knows nothing about: the
                  # block between the second and third rule in the header above.
                  printf '%s\n\n' "Treble RRO Creator — desktop app"
                  awk '/^# =====/ { n++; next } n == 2 { sub(/^# ?/, ""); print }' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
                  exit 0
                  ;;
              --rebuild) rebuild=true ;;
              --release) release=true ;;
              # Accepted for the launchers and for people used to typing it: on
              # Windows the hand-off happens anyway.
              --detach) detach=true ;;
              --browser|-browser) browser=true ; app_args+=("$arg") ;;
              *) app_args+=("$arg") ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # On Windows the app is always the window-only build. The window is the whole
      # UI, so a binary linked against a console only drags one along behind it —
      # and dies when that console is closed. --browser is the exception: that run
      # keeps its console, because that is where the server is watched and stopped.
      case "$(uname -s)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
              if [ "$browser" = "false" ]; then
                  release=true
              fi
              ;;
      esac
      build_flags=()
      if [ "$release" = "true" ]; then
          build_flags+=("--release")
      fi
      
      # Whether Windows gives a program a console window is decided by one field in
      # the executable itself: the PE subsystem, 3 for a console build (the default)
      # and 2 for one linked with -H windowsgui. Reading it means the launcher knows
      # what the binary on disk really is — including one unpacked from a release
      # archive — instead of trusting a side file that can go stale.
      pe_subsystem() {
          local off
          off=$(od -An -tu4 -j60 -N4 "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \r')
          if [ -z "$off" ]; then
              return 2
          fi
          # 0x5c into the PE header
          od -An -tu2 -j$((off + 92)) -N2 "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \r'
      }
      
      # Is the binary older than anything that goes into it? The UI is embedded, so a
      # changed app.js or app.css means the window would still show the old page.
      sources_newer() {
          [ -f "$exe" ] || return 0
          [ -n "$(find "$here/gui" -name '*.go' -newer "$exe" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ] && return 0
          [ -n "$(find "$here/gui/ui" -type f -newer "$exe" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ] && return 0
          [ -n "$(find "$here/go.mod" "$here/go.sum" -newer "$exe" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ] && return 0
          return 1
      }
      
      # Rebuild when the binary is missing or older than the Go sources and the UI.
      # --rebuild wins regardless, which is the dependable option after a pull that
      # only touched go.sum.
      stale() {
          sources_newer && return 0
          # Asked for a window-only build but the exe on disk has a console (or the
          # other way round): the mode is linked in, so that needs a rebuild.
          case "$(uname -s)" in
              MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
                  local want=3
                  if [ "$release" = "true" ]; then
                      want=2
                  fi
                  if [ "$(pe_subsystem "$exe")" != "$want" ]; then
                      return 0
                  fi
                  ;;
          esac
          return 1
      }
      
      if [ "$rebuild" = "true" ] || stale; then
          echo "building the app…"
          if ! bash "$here/gui/build.sh" ${build_flags[@]+"${build_flags[@]}"}; then
              if [ -f "$exe" ]; then
                  # The build is what would make the window new; failing it is no
                  # reason to refuse to open the one that is already there.
                  echo "the build failed — starting the app that is already built." >&2
                  if sources_newer; then
                      echo "  That binary is older than gui/, so the window shows the OLD page:" >&2
                      echo "  the UI is embedded in it, not read from disk." >&2
                      echo "  Fix what the build reported, then: ./treble-rro-creator.sh --rebuild" >&2
                  fi
              else
                  exit 1
              fi
          fi
      fi
      
      # Windows: hand the window to the background and return, however the launcher
      # was started — double-clicked, or typed into a cmd window. The window owns no
      # console of its own, so it outlives the cmd.exe that started it, and that
      # cmd.exe finishing is what closes the console instead of leaving one sitting
      # behind the app. Its output goes nowhere: with the console gone there is
      # nothing to read it on, and keeping the handles is what would hold the console
      # open. Failures land in gui.log next to the executable.
      #
      # A console build is the one thing left in the console, and only when there is
      # no go to relink with: it would take the console down with it, so it says why.
      if [ "$browser" = "false" ]; then
          case "$(uname -s)" in
              MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
                  if [ "$(pe_subsystem "$exe")" = "2" ]; then
                      "$exe" ${app_args[@]+"${app_args[@]}"} >/dev/null 2>&1 &
                      exit 0
                  fi
                  echo "note: this is a console build, so the console stays while the window is open." >&2
                  echo "      the relink needs a C compiler; run ./treble-rro-creator.sh --rebuild once it is installed." >&2
                  ;;
          esac
      fi
      
      exec "$exe" ${app_args[@]+"${app_args[@]}"}

      # Where the probes read from
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # In Termux the phone the probes want is the one the menu is running on, and the
      # reads a PC does over adb (`cmd`, `dumpsys`, /vendor) are what root unlocks
      # there. ADB on Termux has nothing to dial, so without this the answer was
      # always "no device in adb devices".
      #
      # Asked once per session and handed to every probe as DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST, so a
      # session that said yes is not asked again on each run — and one that said no is
      # not asked either.
      probe_local=""
      
      probe_source_ask() {
          [ -z "$probe_local" ] || return 0
          device_is_termux || return 0
          echo ""
          echo "  This is Termux, so the phone is this one rather than a device on a cable."
          echo "  Reading it directly needs root: the same getprop, cmd overlay, wm and"
          echo "  dumpsys reads a PC makes over adb."
          if confirm "  Read this phone as root? [Y/n] " y; then
              if device_local_begin "menu"; then
                  probe_local=1
              else
                  probe_local=0
              fi
          else
              probe_local=0
          fi
          # The menu itself never reads a phone; only the answer is passed on.
          DEVICE_LOCAL=0
          export DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST="$probe_local"
          echo ""
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Probes
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # device-probe.sh, udfps-probe.sh and device-id.sh all print a report and, with
      # --write, put the winners in config.env. That is the only difference between
      # the two answers here, so the submenu asks it instead of inventing options.
      # Ctrl-C is how the probes' device wait is left ("up to 120s; Ctrl-C stops
      # this"). A script's bash shares the foreground process group with the child it
      # is waiting on, so the interrupt reaches this menu too: without the trap the
      # whole menu died and the user lost their place. The trap lets the probe exit on
      # its own while the menu stays put; 130 is the probe's "interrupted" code, so in
      # that case there is no report to read and nothing to press a key for.
      probe_run() {
          local rc=0
          trap ':' INT
          bash "$@" || rc=$?
          trap - INT
          # Never return the probe's status: build.sh runs this with `set -e`, so a
          # 130 here would end the menu as surely as the signal did.
          if [ "$rc" -eq 130 ]; then return 0; fi
          pause_menu || true
          return 0
      }
      
      probe_menu() { # <title> <script> <note>
          local title="$1" script="$2" note="$3" dir
          while :; do
              probe_source_ask
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${title}${NC}"
              hr
              # %b so a note can wrap by itself: a one-paragraph description on a
              # phone-width terminal would otherwise run off the edge.
              [ -n "$note" ] && printf '  %b\n' "$note" && echo ""
              if [ "$probe_local" = 1 ]; then
                  echo "     1  Read this phone (report only)"
                  echo "     2  Read this phone and write the answers to config.env"
              else
                  echo "     1  Read the connected phone (report only)"
                  echo "     2  Read the connected phone and write the answers to config.env"
              fi
              echo "     3  Read an unpacked firmware folder instead"
              echo "     0  Back"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) probe_run "$script" ;;
                  2) probe_run "$script" --write ;;
                  3)
                      menu_read "  folder holding the unpacked ROM" || return 0
                      dir="$MENU_ANSWER"
                      [ -n "$dir" ] || continue
                      if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
                          warn "No such folder: $dir"
                          continue
                      fi
                      if confirm "  Write what it finds to config.env? [y/N] " n; then
                          probe_run "$script" --firmware "$dir" --write
                      else
                          probe_run "$script" --firmware "$dir"
                      fi
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac

      }
      
      menu_udfps() {
          probe_menu "UDFPS" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh" \
              "The in-display fingerprint sensor's centre and radius."
      }
      
      menu_match() {
          probe_source_ask
          probe_run "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Main loop
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_main() {
          while :; do
              menu_header
              menu_items
              echo ""
              menu_read "  >" || { echo ""; return 0; }
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) menu_build ;;
                  2) menu_config ;;
                  3) menu_addons ;;
                  4) menu_device ;;
                  5) menu_detect ;;
                  6) menu_udfps ;;
                  7) menu_match ;;
                  8) menu_files ;;
                  9) menu_docs ;;
                  q|Q|quit|exit) return 0 ;;
                  '') return 0 ;;

      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then

      # =============================================================================

      #
      # The entry point sets ROOT (the project directory) and then sources this file,

      # does not reliably convert a /c/... path for a native .exe.
      # Everything that is not the thing you build lives under stuff/, so the root
      # only holds the two entry points, config.env and the folders you open.
      STUFF_DIR="$ROOT/stuff"
      TOOLS_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/tools"

- path: stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh
  content: |
      # does rather than what its manual says:
      #
      #   * `adb devices` is a stream, not a table. A daemon start, a version
      #     mismatch, or a "no permissions" line shares it with the devices, so only
      #     lines whose second column is a real state are read as devices.
      #   * the listing can lie. It is a snapshot, so the chosen serial is confirmed
      #     with `get-state` before anything is run against it.
      #   * a wedged server hangs instead of failing. Every adb call here is bounded,
      #     and a timeout says "adb kill-server" instead of hanging the probe.
      #   * the first call after the server restarts can come back with no header at
      #     all. That is retried; a genuinely empty list is not.
      #   * a phone that is still "connecting" (wireless adb, or just plugged in)
      #     becomes ready in a second or two, so it is waited for briefly.
      #   * a serial can be listed twice, and wireless transports look like
      #     `192.168.1.5:5555`; duplicates are dropped and the transport is labelled.
      # =============================================================================
      
      # The states adb puts in the second column of `devices`, space-padded so a
      # value can be tested with `index(states, " " $2 " ")`.
      ADB_DEVICE_STATES=" device offline unauthorized bootloader recovery sideload rescue host connecting no "
      
      # Which source the probes read: 0 = a phone on the end of adb, 1 = this phone.
      DEVICE_LOCAL=0
      DEVICE_SERIAL=""
      # How a command is run as root in local mode: "root" when the script already is
      # root, otherwise the binary that escalates (su, tsu, sudo).
      DEVICE_ROOT_CMD=""
      
      # The model and product from one `adb devices -l` line, for a menu a human can
      # read. Both are optional in adb's output, so this never assumes either. A
      # TCP/mDNS serial is called out: with USB and wireless adb on, the same phone
      # can be listed twice and the two entries are otherwise identical.
      adb_device_label() {
          local line="$1" model product serial suffix=""
          model="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/.* model:\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"
          product="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/.* product:\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"
          [ -n "$model" ] || model="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | sed -n 's/.* device:\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"
          serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $1}')"
          case "$serial" in
              *:*) suffix=" [wireless]" ;;
          esac
          if [ -n "$model" ] && [ -n "$product" ]; then
              printf '%s (%s)%s' "$model" "$product" "$suffix"
          elif [ -n "$model" ]; then
              printf '%s%s' "$model" "$suffix"
          else
              printf 'no model reported%s' "$suffix"
          fi
      }
      
      # One line per device on stdin, already in `devices -l` form.
      adb_device_table() {
          local line serial state
          while IFS= read -r line; do
              [ -n "$line" ] || continue
              serial="${line%% *}"
              state="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $2}')"
              printf '  %-18s %-13s %s\n' "$serial" "$state" "$(adb_device_label "$line")"
          done
      }
      
      [read_files: showing lines 20-79 of 606. Use code_search to locate the part you need and read a window around it, or call read_files again with offset=80 to continue.]
      
              && [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0
          "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} exec-out "su 0 cat '$remote'" >"$local_path" 2>/dev/null \
              && [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0
          return 1
      }
      
      # device_connect PROG [WANT] — where the answers come from, for every probe.
      #
      # WANT is the --device value; "local" (also this/self/here) asks for this phone.
      # DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST=1/0 forces the answer, which is what the menu sets after
      # asking once. Sets DEVICE_LOCAL, DEVICE_ROOT_CMD, DEVICE_SERIAL and the probe's
      # `serial`; on failure the reason has already been printed.
      device_connect() {
          local prog="$1" want="${2:-}" mode="${DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST:-}"
          case "$want" in
              local|this|self|here)
                  device_local_begin "$prog" || return 1
                  serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
                  return 0
                  ;;
          esac
          case "$mode" in
              1)
                  # The question was answered before this probe started (the menu asks
                  # once a session), so do not announce the switch again.
                  DEVICE_LOCAL_QUIET=1
                  device_local_begin "$prog" || return 1
                  serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
                  return 0
                  ;;
          esac
          # Termux, and adb cannot see the phone right now: ask about the direct
          # source before the device wait, because in Termux that wait cannot end.
          if [ "$mode" != 0 ] && device_is_termux \
              && ! { resolve_adb 2>/dev/null && adb_device_ready_now "$adb" "$want"; }; then
              device_local_offer "$prog" && { serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"; return 0; }
          fi
          resolve_adb || {
              printf '%s: adb was not found — install platform-tools, pass --adb PATH, or use --device local\n' "$prog" >&2
              return 1
          }
          adb_pick_device "$adb" "$want" "$prog" || return 1
          serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
          return 0
      }
      
      # Prompt on stderr instead of stdout: stdout is often JSON that a caller parses.
      # Reads stdin, so it can be exercised with a pipe in tests.
      adb_device_choose() {
          local ready="$1" count choice resolved tries=0
          count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
          printf 'More than one device is connected:\n' >&2
          printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2
          while [ "$tries" -lt 3 ]; do
              tries=$((tries + 1))
              printf 'Which device? [1-%d] or a serial: ' "$count" >&2
              IFS= read -r choice || return 1
              if resolved="$(adb_device_resolve "$ready" "$choice")"; then
                  printf '%s' "$resolved"
                  return 0
              fi
              printf '  not one of them\n' >&2
          done
          return 1
      }
      
      # Run a command with a deadline, because adb has no timeout of its own and a
      # wedged server otherwise hangs the probe with nothing on screen. LIMIT is in
      # tenths of a second. The child writes a sentinel when it finishes, so a finished
      # process is never mistaken for a running one. 124 means "did not answer".

Sets DEVICE_LOCAL, DEVICE_ROOT_CMD, DEVICE_SERIAL and the probe's\n# `serial`; on failure the reason has already been printed.\n#\n# Precedence, most specific first: a serial or \"local\" typed on the command\n# line, then the session's answer, then what this machine allows (in Termux,\n# adb has nothing to talk to, so the local source is offered there instead).\ndevice_connect() {\n    local prog=\"$1\" want=\"${2:-}\" mode=\"${DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST:-}\"\n    case \"$want\" in\n        local|this|self|here)\n            device_local_begin \"$prog\" || return 1\n            serial=\"$DEVICE_SERIAL\"\n            return 0\n            ;;\n        '')\n            ;;\n        *)\n            mode=\"\"\n            ;;\n    esac\n    case \"$mode\" in\n        1)\n            # The question was answered before this probe started (the menu asks\n            # once a session), so do not announce the switch again.\n            DEVICE_LOCAL_QUIET=1\n            device_local_begin \"$prog\" || return 1\n            serial=\"$DEVICE_SERIAL\"\n            return 0\n            ;;\n    esac\n    # Termux, and adb cannot see the phone right now: ask about the direct\n    # source before the device wait, because in Termux that wait cannot end.\n    if [ -z \"$mode\" ] && device_is_termux \\\n        && ! { resolve_adb 2>/dev/null && adb_device_ready_now \"$adb\" \"$want\"; }; then\n        device_local_offer \"$prog\" && { serial=\"$DEVICE_SERIAL\"; return 0; }\n    fi\n    resolve_adb || {\n        if device_is_termux; then\n            printf '%s: adb cannot reach a phone from Termux — the phone is this machine, and reading it needs root.\\n' \"$prog\" >&2\n            printf '  start the tool as root: tsu %s/build.sh   (pkg install tsu if it is missing)\\n' \"${ROOT:-.}\" >&2\n        else\n            printf '%s: adb was not found — install platform-tools, or pass --adb PATH\\n' \"$prog\" >&2\n        fi\n        return 1\n    }\n    adb_pick_device \"$adb\" \"$want\" \"$prog\" || return 1\n    serial=\"$DEVICE_SERIAL\"\n    return 0\n}",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }

- path: stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh
  content: |
      # prop_of <file> <key> -> the value, empty when absent.
      prop_of() {
          [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
          awk -F'\t' -v k="$2" '$1 == k { print $2; exit }' "$1"
      }
      
      resolve_adb() {
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          adb="$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)"
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          local candidate
          for candidate in "$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb" "$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb.exe"; do
              [ -x "$candidate" ] && { adb="$candidate"; return 0; }
          done
          adb=""
          return 1
      }

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Device mode
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      resolve_adb() {
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          adb="$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)"
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          for adb in "$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb" "$ROOT/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb.exe"; do

          done
          adb=""
          return 1

- path: stuff/tests/adb-device.test.js
  content: |
      
      test('an explicit serial is used as given', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(BOTH_READY, '595648cf1cdc');
        assert.equal(status, 0, out);
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=595648cf1cdc/);
      });
      
      test('an explicit serial that is not attached names what is', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(BOTH_READY, 'GONE');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /GONE is not attached/);
        assert.match(out, /RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      test('an explicit serial that is not ready says why', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(ONE_READY, '0123456789AB');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /attached but unauthorized/);
      });
      
      test('nothing attached says so instead of asking about states', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick('List of devices attached\n\n', '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /no device in adb devices/);
      });
      
      test('nothing ready explains each state', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick(NONE_READY, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /no device is ready/);
        assert.match(out, /accept the USB debugging prompt/);
        assert.match(out, /unplug and replug/);
      });
      
      test('the menu takes a number, a serial or an unambiguous prefix', () => {
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdb(BOTH_READY);
        const run = (answer) =>
          execFileSync(
            'bash',
            [
              '-c',
              `. "${lib}" && adb_device_choose "$(cat "$FAKE_DEVICES" | awk 'NR > 1 && NF && $2 == "device"')"`,
            ],
            {
              env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table },
              input: answer,
              encoding: 'utf8',
              stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
            }
          ).trim();
        assert.equal(run('2\n'), '595648cf1cdc');
        assert.equal(run('595648cf1cdc\n'), '595648cf1cdc');
        assert.equal(run('RFCM\n'), 'RFCM90F5BBX');
      });
      
      test('a prefix two serials share is ambiguous, and it asks again', () => {
        const shared = `List of devices attached
      ABC123                 device product:one model:One device:one transport_id:1
      ABC456                 device product:two model:Two device:two transport_id:2
      `;
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdb(shared);
        const out = execFileSync(
          'bash',
          ['-c', `. "${lib}" && adb_device_choose "$(cat "$FAKE_DEVICES" | awk 'NR > 1 && NF && $2 == "device"')"`],
          {
            env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table },
            input: 'ABC\nABC456\n',
            encoding: 'utf8',
            stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          }
        ).trim();
        assert.equal(out, 'ABC456');
      });
      
      // --- hardening --------------------------------------------------------------
      // `adb devices` is not a table: the daemon's own chatter shares the stream. A
      // line that is not a device must never be offered as one.
      test('daemon chatter and version warnings are not devices', () => {
        const noisy = `List of devices attached
      adb server version (41) doesn't match this client (39); killing...
      * daemon started successfully *
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      595648cf1cdc           device product:zephyr_global model:26012RN62A device:zephyr transport_id:37
      `;
        const { out, status } = pick(noisy, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        // Two real phones, so the answer is the list — with exactly two rows.
        assert.match(out, /2 devices are ready/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /daemon started/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /server version/);
      });
      
      test('a serial listed twice is offered once', () => {
        const twice = `List of devices attached
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      RFCM90F5BBX            device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      `;
        const { out, status } = pick(twice, '');
        assert.equal(status, 0, out);
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /2 devices are ready/);
      });
      
      test('a wireless transport is labelled as one', () => {
        const wireless = `List of devices attached
      192.168.0.31:5555      device product:lineage_r3q model:SM_A908N device:r3q transport_id:36
      595648cf1cdc           device product:zephyr_global model:26012RN62A device:zephyr transport_id:37
      `;
        const { out, status } = pick(wireless, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /192\.168\.0\.31:5555 .*\[wireless\]/);
      });
      
      // The first call after the server restarts can come back without a header. That
      // is a retry, not an empty desk.
      test('a listing with no header is retried until the server answers', () => {
        const { adb, table, dir } = fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then
        if [ -f "$FAKE_COUNTER" ]; then cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"; else : > "$FAKE_COUNTER"; echo "adb server version (41) doesn't match this client (39); killing..." >&2; fi
        exit 0
      fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ] && [ "$3" = "get-state" ]; then echo device; exit 0; fi
      exit 0
      `,
          ONE_READY
        );
        const counter = join(dir, 'calls');
        const out = execFileSync('bash', ['-c', `{ . "${lib}" && adb_pick_device "$FAKE_ADB" "" test-probe && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"; } 2>&1`], {
          env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table, FAKE_COUNTER: counter },
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
        });
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      // A phone that is still handshaking is not "nothing is ready" — waiting is what
      // makes a just-plugged or wireless device work on the first run.
      test('a device that is still connecting is waited for', () => {
        const { adb, table, dir } = fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then
        if [ -f "$FAKE_COUNTER" ]; then cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"; else : > "$FAKE_COUNTER"; printf 'List of devices attached\nRFCM90F5BBX  connecting\n'; fi
        exit 0
      fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ] && [ "$3" = "get-state" ]; then echo device; exit 0; fi
      exit 0
      `,
          ONE_READY
        );
        const counter = join(dir, 'calls');
        const out = execFileSync('bash', ['-c', `{ . "${lib}" && adb_pick_device "$FAKE_ADB" "" test-probe && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"; } 2>&1`], {
          env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table, FAKE_COUNTER: counter },
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
        });
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      // The menu case: a serial is named (or was set in config.env) while the phone is
      // still showing its debugging prompt. Failing there means the user plugs in,
      // accepts, and then runs the menu again — so it waits instead.
      test('a named serial that is not ready yet is waited for', () => {
        const { adb, table, dir } = fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then
        if [ -f "$FAKE_COUNTER" ]; then cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"; else : > "$FAKE_COUNTER"; printf 'List of devices attached\nRFCM90F5BBX  unauthorized\n'; fi
        exit 0
      fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ] && [ "$3" = "get-state" ]; then echo device; exit 0; fi
      exit 0
      `,
          ONE_READY
        );
        const { out, status } = pickUsing(adb, table, 'RFCM90F5BBX', {
          env: { FAKE_COUNTER: join(dir, 'calls'), ADB_WAIT_SECONDS: '5' },
        });
        assert.equal(status, 0, out);
        assert.match(out, /RFCM90F5BBX is attached but unauthorized/);
        assert.match(out, /waiting for a device to become ready/);
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      // Plugging the phone in after the menu opened should be enough on its own.
      test('an empty desk is waited on until a phone appears', () => {
        const { adb, table, dir } = fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then
        if [ -f "$FAKE_COUNTER" ]; then cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"; else : > "$FAKE_COUNTER"; printf 'List of devices attached\n\n'; fi
        exit 0
      fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ] && [ "$3" = "get-state" ]; then echo device; exit 0; fi
      exit 0
      `,
          ONE_READY
        );
        const { out, status } = pickUsing(adb, table, '', {
          env: { FAKE_COUNTER: join(dir, 'calls'), ADB_WAIT_SECONDS: '5' },
        });
        assert.equal(status, 0, out);
        assert.match(out, /no device in adb devices/);
        assert.match(out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      // Nothing ever appears: the deadline is reported, not waited out forever.
      test('a wait that times out says how long it waited', () => {
        const { out, status } = pick('List of devices attached\n\n', '', {
          env: { ADB_WAIT_SECONDS: '2' },
        });
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /no device appeared within 2s/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /PICKED=/);
      });
      
      // Ready in the listing, dead on the wire: the snapshot is checked, not trusted.
      test('a phone that is listed but will not answer get-state is refused', () => {
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdbScript(
          `if [ "$1" = "devices" ]; then cat "$FAKE_DEVICES"; exit 0; fi
      if [ "$1" = "-s" ]; then echo "error: device offline" >&2; exit 1; fi
      exit 0
      `,
          ONE_READY
        );
        const { out, status } = pickUsing(adb, table, '');
        assert.notEqual(status, 0);
        assert.match(out, /did not answer get-state/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out, /PICKED=/);
      });
      
      // The wait promises "Ctrl-C stops this" on screen, so Ctrl-C has to stop it. A
      // trap that only runs the cleanup (`trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM`) replaces the
      // default action, so the interrupt cleaned up and the loop carried on polling —
      // three presses and the prompt did not come back.
      test('Ctrl-C ends the wait instead of being swallowed', async () => {
        for (const name of ['match-prop', 'device-probe', 'udfps-probe', 'device-id']) {
          const body = readFileSync(join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', `${name}.sh`), 'utf8');
          for (const line of body.match(/^trap .*$/gm) || []) {
            if (/\bINT\b/.test(line)) {
              assert.match(line, /\bexit\b/, `${name}.sh traps INT without exiting: ${line}`);
            }
          }
        }
      
        // And in practice: a 120s wait is cut short by a real SIGINT. The trap is set
        // by the probe, so the probe is what runs — match-prop is the one from the
        // bug report.
        const { adb, table, dir: tmp } = fakeAdb('List of devices attached\n\n');
        const child = spawn('bash', [join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'match-prop.sh'), '--adb', adb], {
          env: {
            ...process.env,
            FAKE_DEVICES: table,
            ADB_WAIT_SECONDS: '120',

        process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGINT');

      // reads as the script being stuck.

      `);

          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
        });
        assert.match(out, /status=124/);
        assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 5000, 'the bounded runner waited past its deadline');
      
        // The same deadline in the listing, with the advice the user needs. The limit
        // is a parameter here so the test does not sit out the real 20s.
        const listOut = execFileSync(
          'bash',
          ['-c', `. "${lib}" && adb_device_list "$FAKE_ADB" 5; printf 'status=%s note=%s' "$?" "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE"`],
          { env: { ...process.env, FAKE_ADB: adb }, encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'] }
        );
        assert.match(listOut, /status=1/);
        assert.match(listOut, /did not answer within .*adb kill-server/);
      });

      # already root, so one cat covers both.
      device_pull() {
          local remote="$1" local_path="$2" to="$2"
          if [ "${DEVICE_LOCAL:-0}" = 1 ]; then
              device_local_run "cat '$remote'" >"$local_path" 2>/dev/null
              [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0
              return 1
          fi
          # A Windows adb cannot open an MSYS /tmp path, so the local half is converted
          # when cygpath exists (Git Bash); elsewhere the path is passed as it is.
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then to="$(cygpath -w "$local_path")"; fi

          "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} exec-out "su 0 cat '$remote'" >"$local_path" 2>/dev/null \

- path: stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh — firmware mode has to answer from the ROM
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The failure this pins: a Xiaomi ROM puts the sensor geometry in
      // vendor/build.prop as the FOD rectangle properties, not in an overlay APK. The
      // probe used to list only the first 40 *.prop files (a real tree has hundreds,
      // starting with system_ext's per-app cust.prop) and never turned the pair into a
      // candidate at all, so a full super.img answered nothing while the same phone
      // over adb answered 540,2198,89 from the very same property.
      //
      // No phone and no aapt2 are involved: the tree is a few text files.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const probe = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'udfps-probe.sh');
      
      function tree(files) {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'udfps-fw-'));
        for (const [rel, body] of Object.entries(files)) {
          const path = join(dir, rel);
          mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
          writeFileSync(path, body);
        }
        return dir;
      }
      
      function run(dir) {
        const out = execFileSync('bash', [probe, '--firmware', dir, '--json'], {
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          env: { ...process.env, TERM: 'dumb' },
        });
        return JSON.parse(out);
      }
      
      // The zephyr (Redmi Note 17 4G) values, exactly as vendor/build.prop ships them.
      const ZEPHYR = `ro.hardware.fp.fod=true
      ro.hardware.fp.fod.location=low
      persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=451,2109
      persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=178,178
      `;
      
      test('the rectangle in vendor/build.prop is an answer, and the arithmetic is the rectangle centre', () => {
        const dir = tree({ 'vendor/build.prop': ZEPHYR });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        const c = report.candidates[0];
        assert.equal(c.source, 'firmware-fod-props');
        assert.equal(c.x, 540);
        assert.equal(c.y, 2198);
        assert.equal(c.radius, 89);
        assert.equal(c.confidence, 'high');
        assert.equal(report.chosen.x, 540, 'the answer has to be chosen, not only listed');
        assert.match(c.detail, /location\.X_Y=451,2109/);
      });
      
      // A tree carries hundreds of per-app .prop files; the vendor build.prop has to
      // be read even when it is not in the first handful find returns.
      test('a build.prop behind hundreds of other .prop files is still read', () => {
        const files = {};
        for (let i = 0; i < 220; i += 1) {
          const name = `system_ext/etc/cust/${String(i).padStart(3, '0')}/cust.prop`;
          files[name] = `ro.cust.slot=${i}\n`;
        }
        files['vendor/build.prop'] = ZEPHYR;
        const report = run(tree(files));
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        assert.equal(report.chosen.x, 540);
      });
      
      // Android 8 shipped the same pair without the vendor segment.
      test('the pre-vendor property names are read too', () => {
        const dir = tree({
          'vendor/build.prop': 'persist.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=300,1800\npersist.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=100,120\n',
        });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 1, JSON.stringify(report.candidates));
        assert.deepEqual(
          [report.chosen.x, report.chosen.y, report.chosen.radius],
          [350, 1860, 50]
        );
      });
      
      // A rectangle with no size is not a sensor position; inventing one would put
      // the icon where no finger can reach.
      test('an unusable pair is refused with a warning, not turned into a guess', () => {
        const dir = tree({
          'vendor/build.prop': 'persist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.location.X_Y=0,0\npersist.vendor.sys.fp.fod.size.width_height=0,0\n',
        });
        const report = run(dir);
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 0);
        assert.equal(report.chosen, null);
        assert.ok(report.warnings.length > 0, 'the refusal has to be visible');
      });
      
      test('a tree with nothing to read answers nothing instead of failing', () => {
        const report = run(tree({ 'system/build.prop': 'ro.product.device=zephyr\n' }));
        assert.equal(report.candidates.length, 0);
        assert.equal(report.chosen, null);
        assert.equal(report.mode, 'firmware');
      });
      
      // The probe is also run through the app, which passes an absolute folder: the
      // paths it prints have to be usable, not a temp dir from this test.
      test('the probe still names the source file it answered from', () => {
        const dir = tree({ 'vendor/build.prop': ZEPHYR });
        const report = run(dir);
        const detail = report.candidates[0].detail;
        assert.ok(detail.startsWith(dir), `detail does not name the tree: ${detail}`);
      });
