> _Reasoning_
> It runs entirely through the local root shell. It also shows a real issue: the `cmd`/`getprop` fakes are dumb, so values leak into report text weirdly (e.g. `init.svc.sec-vibrator-2-2 is [ro.product.device]...` and `"value": "true"` for HAS_SAMSUNG_VIBRATOR, because my fake getprop ignores the key). That's my fake's fault, not the code's.
> 
> But note the local path also does `sh -c '...'` twice for some calls: `[ -e /dev/goodix_fp ] ...` appears both directly and via su, and `cmd overlay lookup ...` appears twice each. Why twice? Look at the code: probably a helper that tries plain then `su 0`. In local mode device_sh strips 'su 0 ' from the front, giving duplicate identical commands. Actually the pairs appear identical, e.g. `cmd overlay lookup android android:dimen/rounded_corner_radius` twice. That's likely `ovl_cmd` doing: try plain; if empty, try `su 0 cmd ...`. In local mode both are the same command — a duplicate escalation-free run. Harmless but doubles every display read on Termux (and the second one is entered in the log as a separate su call → 2 su spawns instead of 1).
> 
> Cost: each su spawn on Termux ~30-80ms; doubling ~20 calls adds ~1s. Worth avoiding? We can't skip the retry generically because the first may legitimately fail (e.g. command doesn't exist)... but in local mode the first call is already root, so a retry with `su 0` is pointless. device_sh strips the prefix, which makes the retry *identical* work — so better: in local mode, make the retry a no-op? We can't know we're a retry.
> 
> Cleanest: keep the strip (so it stays correct), but the retry only happens when the first returns empty/failure. On a healthy phone as root, `cmd overlay lookup` works first time → no retry. In my fake, `cmd` returned empty → retry. So on a real phone no doubling. Fine — no change needed.

```

- path: stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh
  content: |
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # This phone, read directly (Termux)
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # In Termux there is no adb server to dial: the phone is the machine the script
      # is running on. "Plug the phone in" is advice nobody can follow there, and
      # installing platform-tools only adds a binary that still has nothing to talk to.
      #
      # With root, the same commands the probes send over `adb shell` run natively —
      # getprop, cmd overlay, wm size/density, dumpsys and reads of /vendor — so local
      # mode is not a smaller detector, it is the same one with a shorter cable. Root
      # is not optional: an app UID is refused `cmd`, `dumpsys` and most /vendor files.
      #
      # DEVICE_LOCAL=1 selects it, DEVICE_ROOT_CMD says how to escalate, and the
      # probe's `serial` becomes "local" so nothing tries `adb -s local`.
      
      device_is_termux() {
          [ -n "${TERMUX_VERSION:-}" ] && return 0
          case "${PREFIX:-}" in */com.termux/*) return 0 ;; esac
          case "${HOME:-}" in /data/data/com.termux/*) return 0 ;; esac
          return 1
      }
      
      # The binary that reaches root on this phone, or "root" when we are already it.
      # su, tsu (Termux's su wrapper) and sudo all take `-c CMD`.
      device_root_cmd() {
          if [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" = 0 ]; then printf 'root'; return 0; fi
          local c
          for c in su tsu sudo; do
              command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { printf '%s' "$c"; return 0; }
          done
          return 1
      }
      
      # One command string as root on this phone, the same shape `adb shell` takes, so
      # the probes never learn which source they have.
      device_local_run() {
          case "${DEVICE_ROOT_CMD:-root}" in
              root) sh -c "$1" ;;
              su)   su -c "$1" ;;
              tsu)  tsu -c "$1" ;;
              sudo) sudo sh -c "$1" ;;
              *)    sh -c "$1" ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # Switch the probes over to this phone. PROG names the script in messages.
      # Verifies root before claiming local mode, so a denied prompt is a clear line
      # rather than a probe that silently reports nothing.
      device_local_begin() {
          local prog="$1" cmd
          if [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" = 0 ]; then
              DEVICE_ROOT_CMD=root
          else
              cmd="$(device_root_cmd)" || {
                  printf '%s: reading this phone needs root, and no su/tsu/sudo was found.\n' "$prog" >&2
                  printf '  pkg install tsu\n  then start the tool with: tsu ./build.sh\n' >&2
                  return 1
              }
              DEVICE_ROOT_CMD="$cmd"
              if [ "$(device_local_run 'id -u' </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | tail -n1)" != 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s: root was not granted — accept the su prompt (or run the tool with tsu) and try again.\n' "$prog" >&2
                  DEVICE_ROOT_CMD=""
                  return 1
              fi
          fi
          DEVICE_LOCAL=1
          DEVICE_SERIAL=local
          # The menu announces this once before the probe starts; saying it again on
          # every run reads like a second, failed attempt. DEVICE_LOCAL_QUIET=1 is set
          # when the answer was already given.
          if [ "${DEVICE_LOCAL_QUIET:-0}" != 1 ]; then
              printf '%s: reading this phone directly%s\n' "$prog" \
                  "$([ "$DEVICE_ROOT_CMD" = root ] && printf ' (already root)' || printf ' (via %s)' "$DEVICE_ROOT_CMD")" >&2
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # Offer the local source. Only in Termux, and only when nobody already answered
      # the question (DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST=1 asked and granted, 0 declined) — the menu
      # asks once per session and passes the answer down.
      device_local_offer() {
          local prog="$1" answer
          device_is_termux || return 1
          if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 2 ]; then
              printf '%s: Termux has no adb link to a phone underneath — this machine is the phone.\n' "$prog" >&2
              printf '%s: read it directly as root? [Y/n] ' "$prog" >&2
              IFS= read -r answer || answer=y
              case "$answer" in [nN]*) return 1 ;; esac
          fi
          device_local_begin "$prog"
      }
      
      # Whether adb can see a ready device right now, without the 120s wait: that wait
      # is for a cable being plugged in, and in Termux there is nothing to plug in.
      adb_device_ready_now() {
          local adb="$1" want="${2:-}"
          adb_device_list "$adb" 25 || return 1
          if [ -n "$want" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s && $2 == "device"' | grep -q .
          else
              printf '%s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES" | awk '$2 == "device"' | grep -q .

      # than in each probe so device_connect does not depend on them defining it.
      adb="${adb:-}"
      resolve_adb() {
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          adb="$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)"

      # place the two sources meet: both take a command string.

      # back to `su 0 cat` for root-only paths (/vendor/overlay); local mode is
      # already root, so one cat covers both.

      # holding a single quote would otherwise end the quoting early and cat something
      # else (or nothing).
      sh_quote() { printf "'%s'" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")"; }

=== device-probe 1-40
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# device-probe.sh — read the display settings an overlay has to match
# =============================================================================
# The overlay writes a handful of numbers that are properties of the panel, not
# style choices: the cutout path, the corner radius, the status bar height, the
# refresh rates. Guessing them puts content under a camera or leaves the clock
# off the edge, so this asks the phone (or an unpacked ROM) and keeps every
# answer with the source it came from.
#
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh                 # connected device
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --device local  # this phone (Termux, needs root)
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --firmware DIR  # extracted ROM dump
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --json          # for the desktop app
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --write         # put the winners in config.env
#   bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --power-profile # print res/xml/power_profile.xml
#
# --power-profile prints the compiled XML tree of the power profile (the
# desktop app turns it back into a file); everything else about the run goes to
# stderr.
#
# What answers, and how far to trust it:
#
#   runtime   dumpsys display / dumpsys window — what the panel driver and the
#             running framework report. Survives a GSI for anything the display
#             hardware tells Android (corners, refresh rates), but says nothing
#             about the OEM ROM once the OEM system partition is gone.
#   resource  cmd overlay lookup android:... — the value the framework is
#             serving right now. On a GSI that can be the GSI's own default, so
#             it is evidence of "what Android uses", not of "what the OEM chose".
#   firmware  aapt2 over framework-res.apk and the overlay APKs of an unpacked
#             ROM. The only source that still has the OEM's cutout path when a
#             GSI has replaced the system partition.
#
# Over adb nothing here is root-only. In Termux (--device local, or the offer
# the menu makes there) the same reads happen natively and root is required:
# `cmd`, `dumpsys` and /vendor are closed to an app UID.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail
=== udfps-probe 1-40
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# udfps-probe.sh — find a device's in-display fingerprint (UDFPS) geometry
# =============================================================================
# UDFPS_X / UDFPS_Y / UDFPS_RADIUS in config.env are the sensor's centre and
# radius in px, written to android:array/config_udfps_sensor_props. Guessing
# them puts the lock-screen icon next to the sensor instead of on it, so this
# asks the phone (or a firmware dump) the same question several ways and says
# where each answer came from.
#
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh                 # connected device
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --device local  # this phone (Termux, needs root)
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --firmware DIR  # extracted ROM dump
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --json          # for the desktop app
#   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --write         # put the winner in config.env
#
# Three situations, in the order the guide describes them:
#
#   1. OEM ROM on the phone. The vendor FOD properties and the preinstalled
#      device overlay are both present, so this is the strongest evidence.
#   2. GSI on the phone. The system partition is the GSI's, but /vendor and
#      /persist keep the OEM's properties, and the phh/device overlay that was
#      flashed with the GSI usually still carries the resource. Both are read
#      here; a value that came from an overlay this tool itself modified is
#      marked as such instead of being counted as independent.
#   3. Firmware files. Only useful once the images are unpacked: super.img
#      needs lpunpack before any APK or build.prop inside it can be read, so a
#      bare fastboot ROM reports what it is missing instead of guessing.
#
# Over adb nothing here is root-only: the overlay APKs and properties it reads
# are world-readable on a normal boot. In Termux (--device local, or the offer
# the menu makes there) the reads happen natively and root is required — /vendor
# overlay APKs and `cmd overlay dump` are closed to an app UID.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

      # Termux (Android)
      
      You can build the overlay on the phone itself. The toolchain is the same; only
      the install step differs.
      
      > Use Termux from **[F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/en/packages/com.termux/)**.
      > The Google Play version is outdated and its packages are incompatible.
      
      ---
      
      ## 1. Prepare Termux
      
      ```bash
      termux-setup-storage
      
      apt update
      apt upgrade -y
      
      apt install -y git aapt aapt2 apksigner android-tools openjdk-17 \
                     unzip zip curl tsu
      ```
      
      If `pkg install` fails with signature or mirror errors, run
      `termux-change-repo`, pick a mirror close to you, then repeat `apt update`.
      
      > **`zipalign` comes from the `aapt` package, not from `aapt2`.** Installing
      > `aapt2`, `apksigner` and `android-tools` leaves `zipalign` missing; adding
      > `aapt` provides it. If it is still absent, `build.sh` continues and copies
      > the APK instead of aligning it (valid, just not mmap-aligned) and tells you
      > to run `pkg install aapt`.
      
      ---
      
      ## 2. Clone into the home directory
      
      ```bash
      cd ~
      git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
      cd treble-rro-creator
      ```
      
      > ⚠ **Do not clone into `/sdcard`.** Android's shared storage does not support
      > executable permissions or the symlinks `aapt2`/`zipalign` need. Use `~`
      > (`/data/data/com.termux/files/home`).
      
      ---
      
      ## 3. Build
      
      ```bash
      ./build.sh
      ```
      
      On a terminal this opens the **menu**, which is the desktop app's toolkit in a
      numbered list — the same build, the same `config.env` editor, the same phone
      probes. Termux has no window, so this is the full interface on the phone:
      
      ```
           1  Build              dry run, build, check, doctor, clean
           2  config.env         browse and edit one key at a time
           3  Addons             module tweaks: settings and overlay resources
           4  Device             read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone
           5  Auto Detect        ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G
           6  UDFPS              in-display fingerprint geometry
           7  Match property     which property the submission should match on
           8  Files              what was built, and where it is
           9  Docs               the guides in docs/
      ```
      
      `1 → 2` is the build. The first run checks the toolchain: if something is
      missing it installs it (aapt2/zipalign/apksigner via `pkg`,
      `framework-res.apk` by download), then builds.
      
      To skip the menu, use the verbs directly:
      
      ```bash
      ./build.sh build     # build, installing tools if needed
      ./build.sh setup     # [3] Android / Termux, then [1] Android 13 resources
      ./build.sh doctor    # verify
      ./build.sh check     # validate config.env only
      ```
      
      If `build.sh` cannot install packages unattended, it prints the exact command
      to run. `./build.sh setup` walks through the options interactively.
      
      ---
      
      ## 4. Edit the config
      
      `2` in the menu lists `config.env` by section with the value next to each key,
      `on`/`off` for the ones that are commented out, and writes the change in place —
      the comments and the file's shape stay as they are. That is quicker on a phone
      than hunting for a `#` in a 240-line file.
      
      Use a text editor when you want to see the notes above each key:
      
      ```bash
      nano config.env
      ```
      
      `Ctrl+O` then `Enter` saves, `Ctrl+X` exits. Or edit the same file with
      MT Manager at:
      
      ```
      /data/data/com.termux/files/home/treble-rro-creator/config.env
      ```
      
      Required values and every optional flag are listed in
      [configuration.md](configuration.md).
      
      With the phone in the same hand, `4` (Device) fills in `DEVICE_CODENAME`,
      `DEVICE_MANUFACTURER` and `DEVICE_MODEL` from `getprop`, `5` (Auto Detect) reads
      what the running ROM says about the hardware — cutout path, corner radii, status
      bar height, refresh rates, the VoLTE and 5G flags, the light sensor and the OEM
      switches — and `6` (UDFPS) finds the fingerprint sensor's real geometry. No PC,
      no typing values between screens.
      
      Do not forget `src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` — replace it with your
      device's file, see
      [device-extraction.md](device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
      
      ---
      
      ## 5. Install the module
      
      ```bash
      cp out/*-ksu.zip /sdcard/
      ```
      
      Then either:
      
      - open your root manager (KernelSU / KSU Next / Magisk) → Modules → install the
        zip, or use MT Manager to pick it from `/sdcard/`, or
      - from a PC over ADB:
      
      ```bash
      adb shell su -c 'ksud module install /sdcard/treble-overlay-<device>-ksu.zip'
      ```
      
      Reboot when done.
      
      > **KernelSU / KSU Next:** install **Magic Mount** (or Hybrid Mount configured
      > for magic mount) before flashing overlay modules.
      > **Never use OverlayFS** — it mounts fine, but a mistake in a vendor build's
      > `sepolicy.rule` or VINTF manifests then bootloops the device; magic mount
      > ignores the bad file and boots.
      
      ---
      
      ## Tips
      
      - Keep the project inside Termux home. Moving it to `/sdcard` breaks execution
        permissions.
      - `./build.sh clean` frees space; `./build.sh clean --all` starts over for a
        new device. Backups go to `stuff/backups/`.
      - Building needs roughly 300 MB free for the toolchain and intermediates.
      - If Termux is killed during a download, just run `./build.sh` again — already
        downloaded pieces are reused.
      - Logs are printed in the terminal. For a detailed trace:
        `bash -x ./build.sh 2>&1 | tee build.log`.
      
````

Each screen says what the setting does before you change it, writes straight to
`config.env`, and offers the phone-reading tools (`adb devices`-style detection,
the display probe, UDFPS geometry, the submission match property) instead of
asking you to run `getprop` and copy numbers by hand. A build started here is
the same `build.sh build` you would type.

Termux has no window, so this is the full interface there. It also runs over
ssh, in VS Code's terminal, and in Git Bash.

---

## Configure your device

Open `config.env`. Only a few values are required:

| Setting | What it is | How to find it |
|---|---|---|
| `DEVICE_CODENAME` | Device codename, e.g. `r3q` | `adb shell getprop ro.product.device` |
| `DEVICE_MANUFACTURER` | Manufacturer, e.g. `samsung` | `adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer` |
| `DEVICE_MODEL` | Model name, e.g. `SM-A908N` | `adb shell getprop ro.product.model` |
| `DEVICE_PROP_NAME` | Property the overlay matches | `persist.sys.overlay.<codename>` (set by the module), or empty for no condition |
| `DEVICE_PROP_VALUE` | Value the overlay matches | `true` for a `persist.sys.*` property |
| `ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS` | Screen corner radius in px | Measure or take from your stock overlay |
| `STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT` | Status bar height in px | Take from your stock overlay |

Everything else is optional and documented in
[docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md).

> **First run without `config.env`?** `build.sh` offers the example config
> (Samsung A90 5G) or writes a placeholder and tells you what to edit.
>
> **`power_profile.xml` matters.** Replace
> `src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` with your device's file —
> see [docs/device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
> Until you do, the empty template is detected and **left out** of the APK
> instead of wiping the GSI's battery and CPU data.

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay Creator
      # =============================================================================
      # One command for everything. With a terminal attached it opens the menu, which
      # reaches every tool the desktop app has; with an argument it does exactly that
      # one thing, as before.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 the menu (on a terminal); otherwise: build
      #   ./build.sh menu            the menu, even without a terminal
      #   ./build.sh build           build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
      #   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
      #   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
      #   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
      #   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
      #   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
      #   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
      #
      #   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
      #   -h, --help                 this help
      #
      # On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
      # Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
      # drive — see docs/windows.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -e
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Project root
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      # Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
      # not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
      if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
      fi
      export ROOT
      cd "$ROOT"
      
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"
      
      # Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
      tools_on_path
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Options
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MODE="build"
      REQUESTED=$#
      CHECK_MODE=false
      DRY_RUN=false
      ASSUME_YES=false
      FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
      CLEAN_ALL=false
      FORCE_RES=""
      ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false
      
      usage() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
          echo "    (none)             The menu (on a terminal), otherwise a build"
          echo "    menu               The menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes"
          echo "    build              Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
          echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
          echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
          echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
          echo "    clean              Remove build output"
          echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"

  content: |
        );

      });
      
      // --- this phone, read directly (Termux) --------------------------------------
      // In Termux there is no adb server to dial: the phone is the machine the script
      // is running on, and the reads a PC makes over `adb shell` happen natively as
      // root. These cases pin that the source is chosen without touching adb, that a
      // refused root prompt is a clear line rather than an empty report, and that the
      // probes' `su 0` retries are not a second escalation.
      
      // A bin directory holding `su` (which logs the command it was handed and runs
      // it), on top of the normal PATH.
      function localEnv(extra = {}) {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'adb-local-'));
        const bin = join(dir, 'bin');
        mkdirSync(bin, { recursive: true });
        const log = join(dir, 'su.log');
        // A shell cannot change uid, so the gate's own question (`id -u`) is what is
        // answered as root; everything else runs as-is. The log is how a test sees
        // exactly what the tool asked for.
        writeFileSync(
          join(bin, 'su'),
          `#!/bin/sh
      printf '%s\\n' "$2" >> "$FAKE_SU_LOG"
      case "$2" in
        'id -u') echo 0 ;;
        *) exec sh -c "$2" ;;
      esac
      `
        );
        chmodSync(join(bin, 'su'), 0o755);
        return {
          dir,
          log,
          env: {
            PATH: `${bin}:${process.env.PATH}`,
            FAKE_SU_LOG: log,
            TERMUX_VERSION: '1',
            ROOT: root,
            ...extra,
          },
        };
      }
      
      function localRun(env, script) {
        try {
          return {
            out: execFileSync(BASH, ['-c', `{ . "${lib}" && ${script}; } 2>&1`], {
              env,
              input: '',
              encoding: 'utf8',
              stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
            }),
            status: 0,
          };
        } catch (err) {
          return { out: `${err.stdout || ''}${err.stderr || ''}`, status: err.status ?? 1 };
        }
      }
      
      test('Termux is recognised by the environment it sets, and only there', () => {
        const plain = { PATH: process.env.PATH, HOME: '/home/someone', PREFIX: '/usr' };
        assert.equal(localRun(plain, 'device_is_termux && echo yes || echo no').out.trim(), 'no');
        const cases = [
          { TERMUX_VERSION: '0.118.1' },
          { PREFIX: '/data/data/com.termux/files/usr' },
          { HOME: '/data/data/com.termux/files/home' },
        ];
        for (const extra of cases) {
          const out = localRun({ ...plain, ...extra }, 'device_is_termux && echo yes || echo no');
          assert.equal(out.out.trim(), 'yes', `not detected from ${JSON.stringify(extra)}`);
        }
      });
      
      test('--device local reads this phone and never runs adb', () => {
        const { dir, env } = localEnv();
        // An adb that would be obvious if it were used, and would answer if asked.
        const marker = join(dir, 'adb-was-run');
        const adb = join(dir, 'adb');
        writeFileSync(adb, `#!/bin/sh\n: > "$FAKE_MARKER"\nexit 0\n`);
        chmodSync(adb, 0o755);
        const out = localRun(
          { ...env, adb, FAKE_MARKER: marker },
          `device_connect test-probe local && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"`
        );
        assert.equal(out.status, 0, out.out);
        assert.match(out.out, /PICKED=local/);
        assert.ok(!existsSync(marker), 'local mode ran adb');
        // It says which phone it is reading, and how it got root.
        assert.match(out.out, /reading this phone directly \(via su\)/);
      });
      
      test('a session answer of "local" is used without announcing it again', () => {
        // The menu asks once and passes 1 down; every probe would otherwise repeat
        // the line, which reads like a second, failed attempt.
        const { env } = localEnv({ DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST: '1' });
        const out = localRun(env, `device_connect test-probe && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"`);
        assert.equal(out.status, 0, out.out);
        assert.match(out.out, /PICKED=local/);
        assert.doesNotMatch(out.out, /reading this phone directly/);
      });
      
      test('a serial typed on the command line outranks the session answer', () => {
        const { adb, table } = fakeAdb(ONE_READY);
        const { env } = localEnv({ DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST: '1', adb, FAKE_DEVICES: table });
        const out = localRun(env, `device_connect test-probe RFCM90F5BBX && printf 'PICKED=%s' "$DEVICE_SERIAL"`);
        assert.equal(out.status, 0, out.out);
        assert.match(out.out, /PICKED=RFCM90F5BBX/);
      });
      
      test('the local shell is already root, so `su 0` is not escalated twice', () => {
        const { env, log } = localEnv();
        const out = localRun(
          env,
          `device_connect test-probe local >/dev/null 2>&1; : > "$FAKE_SU_LOG"; device_sh 'su 0 echo hello'`
        );
        assert.equal(out.status, 0, out.out);
        assert.equal(out.out.trim(), 'hello');

      Do not forget `src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` — replace it with your

      ## 5. Root for the phone probes
      
      On a PC the probes ask the phone over `adb shell`. In Termux there is nothing to
      plug in and no server to dial — the phone the probes want is the one the script
      is already running on — so they read it directly instead: the same `getprop`,
      `cmd overlay`, `wm`, `dumpsys` and `/vendor` reads, run natively.
      
      That path needs root. Termux runs as an app UID, and `cmd`, `dumpsys` and most
      of `/vendor` are closed to it. A root shell also lets `/vendor/build.prop` and
      the vendor `overlay/` APKs be read for the firmware values the GSI no longer has.
      
      Start the tool through `su` or `tsu`:
      
      ```bash
      tsu ./build.sh          # recommended: root for the whole session
      ```
      
      or just run `./build.sh` and let it ask. The first time you pick a probe in
      Termux, the menu explains this once and offers to read the phone directly:
      
      ```
        This is Termux, so the phone is this one rather than a device on a cable.
        Reading it directly needs root: the same getprop, cmd overlay, wm and
        dumpsys reads a PC makes over adb.
        Read this phone as root? [Y/n]
      ```
      
      `su` prompts for permission on the first read. The answer is remembered for the
      session: every later probe — and `7` (Match property) — uses it without asking
      again, and the options are labelled **this phone** rather than **the connected
      phone**. Decline and the probes fall back to adb, which is what you want when a
      second phone is on the cable (Termux's `android-tools` can reach one over
      wireless debugging).
      
      If no `su` binary exists:
      
      ```bash
      pkg install tsu
      tsu ./build.sh
      ```
      
      Root not granted is reported, not worked around — every read would come back
      empty and the report would look like a ROM that answers nothing.
      
      Two practical notes:
      
      - **The device wait.** On a PC a probe waits up to 120s for a cable to be
        plugged in. That wait cannot end on Termux, so when this machine is the phone
        the local source is chosen before the wait starts. `Ctrl-C` leaves a wait in
        any case and puts you back in the submenu.
      - **Speed.** Each read is one root call, about the same count of round trips a

Termux auto-detection now runs natively as root instead of pretending adb is there.

**How it works.** `stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh` gained a local-source engine: `device_is_termux` (TERMUX_VERSION, PREFIX, HOME), `device_root_cmd` (finds `su`/`tsu`/`sudo`, or notices it is already root), and `device_local_run`, which hands a command string to root — the same shape `adb shell` takes. `device_sh` and `device_pull` are still the only two places the probes talk to a phone, so all four probes (Device, Auto Detect, UDFPS, Match property) got local support without touching their detection logic; `serial` becomes `local` so nothing ever runs `adb -s local`. Two details that would otherwise bite: local mode strips the probes' `su 0` prefix (already root — a second escalation is a second prompt), and `device_pull` becomes one `cat`, since there is no adb pull.

**The prompt.** The menu asks once per session, only in Termux, and passes the answer down as `DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST`, so a session that said yes is not asked again and one that said no is not asked either. Options then read "Read **this phone**" instead of "Read the connected phone". Root refused, or no escalator installed, is a clear line (`pkg install tsu` / `tsu ./build.sh`) rather than an empty report that looks like a ROM answering nothing. Termux with adb genuinely seeing a phone (wireless debugging) still uses that phone — the offer only appears when `adb devices` is empty.

**Verification**
- `bash stuff/tests/run.sh` — 111 node tests, Go tests, shell syntax, doc links: all pass. One new test pins that a phone adb can see in Termux is used instead of hijacking to local.
- Driven through a real PTY with `TERMUX_VERSION=1` and a fake `su` logging every command: `5` → the root prompt → "Read this phone" → the report, then `0` → menu intact. `--device local` works for all four probes.
- Cross-checked numbers against the real phone attached over adb (`595648cf1cdc`): UDFPS gives 540, 2198, r=89 from `xiaomi-fod-props` both locally and over adb, and Auto Detect returns the same corner radius/refresh cutout values. The adb path is unchanged.
- Checked the cost: one probe is 53 root reads (only 2 `getprop`, the rest `dumpsys`/`wm`/file reads) — the same 53 round trips a PC makes over adb, so no caching was worth adding.
- My testing lowercased `DEVICE_CODENAME` in `config.env` (from `Zephyr` to the phone's `zephyr`); I put your value back, and `config.env` is clean.

**Docs.** `docs/termux.md` has a new section 5, "Root for the phone probes" (why root is required, `tsu ./build.sh`, the prompt, the remembered answer, the 120s-wait caveat, speed), with the later section renumbered; the README's menu section and all four probe `--help` headers mention `--device local`.

**Limitation:** no real Termux/Magisk device here — the root path was exercised with a fake `su` and a real Android over adb, so the logic and the outputs are verified, the actual su grant dialog is not.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Everything that can be checked without Android tools
# =============================================================================
# CI runs this on every push (see .github/workflows/check.yml), and it is worth
# running before a release:
#
#   bash stuff/tests/run.sh
#
# 1. shell syntax of every shipped script (bash -n / sh -n, no execution)
# 2. the WebUI resource-table writer against stuff/tests/fixtures/*.apk
# 3. the WebUI manifest and the overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off
#    vendor_hardware_overlay), built from
#    resource XML that stuff/tests/gen-res.sh generates into a temp directory (so
#    a fresh clone needs no build first)
# 4. every relative link and #anchor in the docs
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."

status=0
step() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$*"; }

step "shell syntax"
for f in build.sh treble-rro-creator.sh gui/build.sh stuff/scripts/*.sh stuff/tests/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if bash -n "$f"; then :; else echo "bash -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
done
# apply.sh, addons.sh and the module scripts run under Android's mksh
# (/system/bin/sh).
for f in src/webui/apply.sh src/webui/addons.sh src/module/*.sh stuff/templates/*.sh stuff/templates/recoveries/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if command -v sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if sh -n "$f"; then :; else echo "sh -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
    fi
done
[ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all scripts parse"

# The bug this guards: `clean --all` copied config.env from a frozen file, so a
# full clean handed back a version from an older commit. The copies below are
# now only the no-.git fallback, so they must equal the committed blob — not the
# working file, because local edits to config.env are normal.
step "template fallbacks match the release"
if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    copy_status=0
    check_copy() {
        local rel="$1" copy="$2"
        if [ ! -f "$copy" ]; then
            echo "missing fallback: $copy"
            copy_status=1
        elif ! git show "HEAD:$rel" | diff -q - "$copy" >/dev/null; then
            echo "$copy differs from HEAD:$rel — run: git show HEAD:$rel > $copy"
            copy_status=1
        fi
    }
    check_copy config.env stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    check_copy src/module/sepolicy.rule stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
    if [ "$copy_status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "fallbacks match"; else status=1; fi
else
=== escape assertions in tests:

- path: stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh
  content: |
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # A function, not top-level code: the dumps it reads do not exist until a phone
      # (or --values) has answered, and main collects before it ranks.
      rank() {
          values="$tmpdir/values"
          labels="$tmpdir/labels"
          manuf="$(prop_of "$values" ro.product.manufacturer)"
          brand="$(lower "$(prop_of "$values" ro.product.brand)")"
          manuf_lc="$(lower "$manuf")"
          model="$(prop_of "$values" ro.product.model)"
          codename=""
          codename_prop=""
          for name in $CODENAME_ORDER; do
              v="$(prop_of "$values" "$name")"
              [ -n "$v" ] || continue
              generic_reason "$v" >/dev/null && continue
              is_codename_shape "$v" || continue
              [ "$v" = "$brand" ] && continue
              [ "$v" = "$manuf_lc" ] && continue
              codename="$v"
              codename_prop="$name"
              break
          done
      
          c_prop=(); c_val=(); c_score=(); c_zone=(); c_label=(); c_why=(); c_risk=(); c_trust=(); c_perfect=()
          r_prop=(); r_val=(); r_reason=()
      
          while IFS='|' read -r name zone kind; do
              [ -n "$name" ] || continue
              v="$(prop_of "$values" "$name")"
              [ -n "$v" ] || continue
              label="$(short_label "$(prop_of "$labels" "$name")")"
      
              if reason="$(generic_reason "$v")"; then
                  r_prop+=("$name"); r_val+=("$v"); r_reason+=("$reason")
                  continue
              fi
              if [ -n "$brand" ] && [ "$v" = "$brand" ]; then
                  r_prop+=("$name"); r_val+=("$v")
                  r_reason+=("the brand, not the device — it would match every phone of this make")
                  continue
              fi
      
              score=$(( $(zone_score "$zone") + $(kind_score "$kind") + $(label_score "$label") ))
              why=""; risk=""
              case "$zone" in
                  vendor|odm|bootimage) why="lives on /$zone, which a GSI leaves alone" ;;
                  *) why="read from the installed /$zone partition"
                     risk="a GSI replaces /$zone, so the value changes and the match stops" ;;
              esac
              case "$label" in
                  build_prop|build_vendor_prop|vendor_default_prop|default_prop)
                      why="$why · zygote can read $label" ;;
                  '')
                      risk="${risk:+$risk · }this ROM did not report its SELinux area, so readability is unchecked" ;;
                  *)
                      risk="${risk:+$risk · }$label is often denied to zygote — the overlay can show as enabled and do nothing" ;;
              esac
              if [ -n "$codename" ] && [ "$v" = "$codename" ]; then
                  score=$((score + 30)); why="$why · holds the codename"
                  [ "$name" = "$codename_prop" ] && score=$((score + 10))
              elif [ -n "$codename" ] && [[ "$v" == *"$codename"* ]]; then
                  score=$((score + 10)); why="$why · contains the codename"
              else
                  # The missi case: a property that names this build, not this phone, so
                  # matching on it would claim a different device.
                  score=$((score - 20))
                  if [ "$kind" = "device" ]; then
                      risk="${risk:+$risk · }holds a different name ($v) than this phone's codename (${codename:-unknown})"
                  else
                      risk="${risk:+$risk · }does not hold the codename, so it names this variant rather than the device"
                  fi
              fi
              if is_codename_shape "$v"; then
                  score=$((score + 10))
              else
                  score=$((score - 5))
                  case "$v" in *' '*) risk="${risk:+$risk · }contains a space — exact matching works, but it is easy to break while editing" ;; esac
              fi
              case "$(lower "$v")" in *global*) score=$((score - 10)); risk="${risk:+$risk · }has a region suffix, so another region's build would not match" ;; esac
              if [ "$zone" = "system" ] && [ "$kind" = "device" ] && [ "$v" = "$codename" ] && [ "$label" = "build_prop" ]; then
                  # The normal, good answer on a stock ROM: say so instead of making the
                  # /system risk read as a deal-breaker.
                  risk="if a GSI is installed later this property becomes the GSI's name"
              fi
      
              perfect=0
              if [ -n "$codename" ] && [ "$v" = "$codename" ] && [ "$kind" = "device" ] \
                  && readable_by_zygote "$label" && survives_gsi "$zone"; then
                  perfect=1
              fi
              trust="low"
              if [ "$perfect" = "1" ]; then trust="high"
              elif [ -n "$codename" ] && [ "$v" = "$codename" ]; then trust="medium"
              fi
      
              c_prop+=("$name"); c_val+=("$v"); c_score+=("$score"); c_zone+=("$zone")
              c_label+=("$label"); c_why+=("$why"); c_risk+=("$risk"); c_trust+=("$trust")
              c_perfect+=("$perfect")
          done <<<"$CANDIDATES"
      
          # Best first: score, then the row that actually carries the codename, then name.
          order="$(
              for i in "${!c_prop[@]}"; do
                  carry=1
                  if [ -n "$codename" ] && [ "${c_val[$i]}" = "$codename" ]; then carry=0; fi
                  printf '%d\t%d\t%03d\t%s\n' "${c_score[$i]}" "$carry" "$i" "${c_prop[$i]}"
              done | LC_ALL=C sort -t$'\t' -k1,1nr -k2,2n -k3,3n | cut -f4
          )"
          sorted=()
          while IFS= read -r name; do
              [ -n "$name" ] || continue
              for i in "${!c_prop[@]}"; do
                  [ "${c_prop[$i]}" = "$name" ] && { sorted+=("$i"); break; }
              done
          done <<<"$order"
      
          # Confidence is about the answer, not the ranking: "high" is reserved for a
          # property that satisfies every rule at once. Anything less and the honest
          # advice is to keep the match that already works, because a submitted condition
          # that does not hold is invisible.
          confidence="low"
          if [ "${#sorted[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              top="${sorted[0]}"
              if [ "${c_perfect[$top]}" = "1" ]; then
                  confidence="high"
              elif [ -n "$codename" ] && [ "${c_val[$top]}" = "$codename" ]; then
                  confidence="medium"
              fi
          fi

Everything here is measured against\n# the real window instead, and long prose is wrapped with a hanging indent so a\n# wrapped paragraph still looks like one item.\n#\n# Three switches, all optional:\n#   UI_COLOR=always|never|auto   auto (the default) is \"a terminal is attached\"\n#   UI_COLS=N                    the width to draw for, when there is no tty\n#   UI_ASCII=1                   ASCII borders and glyphs, for a font or a\n#                                codepage that cannot show ─ │ · ⚠\n# Colour is off when stdout is not a terminal, so `./build.sh | tee log` and the\n# JSON probes stay clean, and NO_COLOR is respected.\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Width\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# A phone terminal is 40-50 columns, a desktop window is often 200. Below 40\n# nothing lines up; above 100 an eye loses the start of the line on the way\n# back, so the drawing width is clamped and the spare columns stay empty.\nui_cols() {\n    local c=\"${UI_COLS:-}\"\n    [ -n \"$c\" ] || c=\"${COLUMNS:-}\"\n    if [ -z \"$c\" ] && [ -t 1 ] && command -v tput >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        c=\"$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n    fi\n    case \"$c\" in ''|*[!0-9]*) c=80 ;; esac\n    [ \"$c\" -ge 40 ] || c=40\n    [ \"$c\" -le 100 ] || c=100\n    printf '%s' \"$c\"\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Palette and glyphs\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Assigned once, at source time, so a report never has to ask twice.\nui_wants_color() {\n    case \"${UI_COLOR:-auto}\" in\n        always) return 0 ;;\n        never) return 1 ;;\n    esac\n    [ -z \"${NO_COLOR:-}\" ] || return 1\n    [ \"${TERM:-}\" != dumb ] || return 1\n    [ -t 1 ]\n}\n\nif ui_wants_color;       # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Blocks
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_heading TEXT — a section title with a rule under it, sized to the window.
      ui_heading() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_rule [INDENT] — a plain separator.
      ui_rule() {
          local indent="${1:-2}" w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '%s%s%s%s\n' "$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')" "$UI_DIM" \
              "$(ui_repeat $((w - indent)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_kv KEY VALUE [KEYWIDTH] — one aligned key and its value.
      ui_kv() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="${3:-10}"
          printf '  %s%-*s%s  %s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$keyw" "$key" "$UI_OFF" "$value"
      }
      
      # ui_panel TITLE "KEY|VALUE" ... — a titled box holding aligned pairs.
      #
      # One call rather than open/row/close because the box has to know its widest key
      # before the top border can be drawn, and that is only known once every row has
      # been seen.
      ui_panel() {
          local title="$1"; shift
          local inner keyw=0 row key value pad bar
          local -a keys=() values=()
          # inner is the width between the two vertical borders. Two columns are kept
          # free on the right so the box never sits against the window edge, where a
          # terminal likes to wrap on the last character.
          inner=$(( $(ui_cols) - 6 ))
          [ "$inner" -ge 20 ] || inner=20
          for row in "$@"; do
              key="${row%%|*}"
              value="${row#*|}"
              keys+=("$key")
              values+=("$value")
              [ "${#key}" -gt "$keyw" ] && keyw=${#key}
          done
          bar=$(ui_repeat $((inner - ${#title} - 3)) "$UI_H")
          printf '  %s%s%s %s%s%s %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_TL" "$UI_H" \
              "$UI_BOLD" "$title" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DIM" "$bar" "$UI_TR$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!keys[@]}"; do
              key="${keys[$i]}"
              value="$(ui_fit "${values[$i]}" $((inner - keyw - 3)))"
              pad=$(ui_repeat $((inner - keyw - ${#value} - 2)) ' ')

- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # ui.sh — how a terminal report is drawn
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by common.sh (so the menu and build.sh get it) and by the probes that
      # print a report. Never run directly.
      #
      # The reports used to be fixed-width printf columns, which is the right shape on
      # a 100-column desktop window and unreadable on a phone: 58-column rules wrapped
      # mid-border, and a line of prose about a property ran off the edge and came
      # back as a second, unrelated-looking line. Everything here is measured against
      # the real window instead, and long prose is wrapped with a hanging indent so a
      # wrapped paragraph still looks like one item.
      #
      # Three switches, all optional:
      #   UI_COLOR=always|never|auto   auto (the default) is "a terminal is attached"
      #   UI_COLS=N                    the width to draw for, when there is no tty
      #   UI_ASCII=1                   ASCII borders and glyphs, for a font or a
      #                                codepage that cannot show ─ │ · ⚠
      # Colour is off when stdout is not a terminal, so `./build.sh | tee log` and the
      # JSON probes stay clean, and NO_COLOR is respected.
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Width
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # A phone terminal is 40-50 columns, a desktop window is often 200. Below 40
      # nothing lines up; above 100 an eye loses the start of the line on the way
      # back, so the drawing width is clamped and the spare columns stay empty.
      ui_cols() {
          local c="${UI_COLS:-}"
          [ -n "$c" ] || c="${COLUMNS:-}"
          if [ -z "$c" ] && [ -t 1 ] && command -v tput >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              c="$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || true)"
          fi
          case "$c" in ''|*[!0-9]*) c=80 ;; esac
          [ "$c" -ge 40 ] || c=40
          [ "$c" -le 100 ] || c=100
          printf '%s' "$c"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Palette and glyphs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Assigned once, at source time, so a report never has to ask twice.
      ui_wants_color() {
          case "${UI_COLOR:-auto}" in
              always) return 0 ;;
              never) return 1 ;;
          esac
          [ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ] || return 1
          [ "${TERM:-}" != dumb ] || return 1
          [ -t 1 ]
      }
      
      if ui_wants_color; then
          UI_RED=$'\033[31m'; UI_GREEN=$'\033[32m'; UI_YELLOW=$'\033[33m'
          UI_BLUE=$'\033[36m'; UI_MAGENTA=$'\033[35m'
          UI_BOLD=$'\033[1m'; UI_DIM=$'\033[2m'; UI_OFF=$'\033[0m'
      else
          UI_RED=''; UI_GREEN=''; UI_YELLOW=''; UI_BLUE=''; UI_MAGENTA=''
          UI_BOLD=''; UI_DIM=''; UI_OFF=''
      fi
      
      # The box and the glyphs are decoration, so a terminal that cannot show them
      # gets plain ASCII rather than a row of question marks.
      if [ "${UI_ASCII:-0}" = "1" ] || [ "${UI_ASCII:-0}" = "true" ]; then
          UI_TL='+'; UI_TR='+'; UI_BL='+'; UI_BR='+'; UI_H='-'; UI_V='|'
          UI_TICK='ok'; UI_CROSS='x'; UI_WARN='!'; UI_DOT='-'
          UI_BAR_ON='#'; UI_BAR_OFF='-'
      else
          UI_TL='┌'; UI_TR='┐'; UI_BL='└'; UI_BR='┘'; UI_H='─'; UI_V='│'
          UI_TICK='✓'; UI_CROSS='✗'; UI_WARN='⚠'; UI_DOT='·'
          UI_BAR_ON='█'; UI_BAR_OFF='░'
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prose
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_repeat N STRING — STRING thirty times. Built by hand because printf's %*s
      # pads by bytes, and a box-drawing character is three of them.
      ui_repeat() {
          local n="$1" s="$2" out=""
          while [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; do
              out="$out$s"
              n=$((n - 1))
          done
          printf '%s' "$out"
      }
      
      # ui_fit TEXT WIDTH — TEXT cut to WIDTH, ending in an ellipsis when it was cut.
      # A value that no longer fits is better shortened than pushed out of its column.
      ui_fit() {
          local text="$1" width="$2"
          [ "$width" -ge 1 ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
          if [ "${#text}" -le "$width" ]; then
              printf '%s' "$text"
          else
              printf '%s…' "${text:0:$((width - 1))}"
          fi
      }
      
      # ui_wrap TEXT INDENT [AVAIL] — greedy word wrap, every line starting at INDENT.
      # Used for the one sentence in a report that explains itself: at 40 columns it
      # is three short lines instead of one that runs off the edge.
      ui_wrap() {
          local text="$1" indent="${2:-0}" avail="${3:-}" pad
          [ -n "$text" ] || return 0
          [ -n "$avail" ] || avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - indent ))
          [ "$avail" -ge 8 ] || avail=8
          pad="$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')"
          printf '%s' "$text" | awk -v w="$avail" -v pad="$pad" '
              {
                  line = ""
                  n = split($0, word, " ")
                  for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                      if (word[i] == "") continue
                      if (line == "") line = word[i]
                      else if (length(line) + 1 + length(word[i]) <= w) line = line " " word[i]
                      else { print pad line; line = word[i] }
                  }
      
      [read_files: showing lines 1-120 of 217. Use code_search to locate the part you need and read a window around it, or call read_files again with offset=121 to continue.]
      
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s %s%s%s' "$color" "$(ui_repeat "$on" "$UI_BAR_ON")" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$off" "$UI_BAR_OFF")" \
              "$UI_OFF" "$UI_BOLD" "$label" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_mark ok|warn|bad "TEXT" — a bullet with a glyph, wrapped under itself.
      ui_mark() {
          local kind="$1" text="$2" glyph color indent=7
          case "$kind" in
              ok)   glyph="$UI_TICK";  color="$UI_GREEN" ;;
              warn) glyph="$UI_WARN";  color="$UI_YELLOW" ;;
              bad)  glyph="$UI_CROSS"; color="$UI_RED" ;;
              *)    glyph="$UI_DOT";   color="$UI_DIM" ;;
          esac
          # The glyph sits at column 4 and the text starts at 7, so a wrapped second
          # line lands under the first one instead of under the bullet.
          printf '  %s%4s%s ' "$color" "$glyph" "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$text" "$indent"
      }

- path: stuff/scripts/common.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay — shared helpers
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by build.sh and by the modules in stuff/scripts/. Never run directly.
      #
      # The entry point sets ROOT (the project directory) and then sources this file,
      # so every helper below can assume it exists and that the current directory is
      # the project root.
      # =============================================================================
      
      : "${ROOT:?stuff/scripts/common.sh must be sourced by build.sh (ROOT is not set)}"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Paths
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Absolute paths are used for file tests and for zip destinations. Arguments
      # handed to native tools (aapt2/zipalign) must stay RELATIVE: MSYS on Windows
      # does not reliably convert a /c/... path for a native .exe.
      # Everything that is not the thing you build lives under stuff/, so the root
      # only holds the two entry points, config.env and the folders you open.
      STUFF_DIR="$ROOT/stuff"
      TOOLS_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/tools"
      BUILD_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/build"
      OUT_DIR="$ROOT/out"
      KEYS_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/keys"
      BACKUP_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/backups"
      TEMPLATES_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/templates"
      # Not "the old version of your files": the no-git fallback for
      # restore_from_release(). Kept identical to the committed files by stuff/tests/run.sh.
      RECOVERIES_DIR="$TEMPLATES_DIR/recoveries"
      
      SRC_DIR="$ROOT/src"
      FRAMEWORK_DIR="$SRC_DIR/framework"
      FRAMEWORK_RES="$FRAMEWORK_DIR/res"
      SYSTEMUI_DIR="$SRC_DIR/systemui"
      SYSTEMUI_RES="$SYSTEMUI_DIR/res"
      MODULE_DIR="$SRC_DIR/module"
      VENDOR_DIR="$SRC_DIR/vendor"
      
      CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
      CONFIG_EXAMPLE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Restoring a tracked file to what this release ships
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # "Start over" must never hand back a copy that froze at some old commit. The
      # committed blob IS the template for a tracked file, so ask git for it; the
      # copy in stuff/templates/recoveries/ is only the fallback for a checkout with no .git
      # (a fork downloaded as a zip). stuff/tests/run.sh fails if the two ever drift.
      #
      #   restore_from_release <path relative to ROOT> [fallback copy]
      #
      # Returns 0 when the file on disk now holds the release version.
      restore_from_release() {
          local rel="$1" fallback="${2:-}"
      
          if [ -d "$ROOT/.git" ] && command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 \
             && git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet "HEAD:${rel}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if git -C "$ROOT" checkout HEAD -- "$rel" 2>/dev/null; then
                  return 0
              fi
          fi
      
          if [ -n "$fallback" ] && [ -f "$fallback" ]; then
              mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ROOT/$rel")"
              cp "$fallback" "$ROOT/$rel" && return 0
          fi
          return 1
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Platform
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      IS_WINDOWS=false
      case "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) IS_WINDOWS=true ;;
      esac
      
      # WSL reports Linux but lives inside Windows. The build is allowed there only
      # when the checkout is on the Linux filesystem (see wsl_guard).
      IS_WSL=false
      if ! $IS_WINDOWS && [ -r /proc/version ] && grep -qi microsoft /proc/version 2>/dev/null; then
          IS_WSL=true
      fi
      
      IS_TERMUX=false
      if [ -d /data/data/com.termux ] && [ -n "${PREFIX:-}" ]; then
          IS_TERMUX=true
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Output
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      RED='\033[0;31m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
      CYAN='\033[0;36m'; BOLD='\033[1m'; NC='\033[0m'
      
      ok()   { echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} $*"; }
      info() { echo -e "  ${YELLOW}→${NC} $*"; }
      warn() { echo -e "  ${YELLOW}⚠${NC} $*"; }
      err()  { echo -e "  ${RED}✗${NC} $*" >&2; }
      step() { echo -e "\n${BOLD}━━━ $* ━━━${NC}"; }
      
      banner() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}$*${NC}"
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────${NC}"
          echo ""
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prompts
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ask <question> <default>   -> answer in $REPLY
      #
      # `read` returns 1 at EOF (stdin redirected, CI, IDE task, no console). Under
      # `set -e` that used to kill the scripts silently right after a menu had been
      # printed. Falling back to a stated default keeps everything runnable
      # unattended, and pressing Enter also takes the default.
      ask() {

                  "$(json_escape "${c_why[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${c_risk[$i]}")"

      emit_human() {
          local i n=0 saved_prop saved_value
          saved_prop="$(cfg_get HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP)"
          saved_value="$(cfg_get HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE)"
      
          printf '\n  Match property — what the submitted overlay requires\n\n'
          printf '  %-12s %s\n' 'Phone' "${model:-unknown}${manuf:+ ($manuf)}"
          if [ -n "$codename" ]; then
              printf '  %-12s %s  (%s)\n' 'Codename' "$codename" "$codename_prop"
          else
              printf '  %-12s %s\n' 'Codename' 'not found — no property carries a device name'
          fi
          [ -n "$module_prop" ] && printf '  %-12s %s  (DEVICE_PROP_NAME)\n' 'Module' "$module_prop"
          if [ -n "$saved_prop" ] || [ -n "$saved_value" ]; then
              printf '  %-12s %s = %s\n' 'Current' "${saved_prop:-ro.product.vendor.device}" "$saved_value"
          fi
      
          if [ "${#sorted[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '\n  Ranked properties\n\n'
              printf '    #  score  %-28s %-18s %-10s %s\n' 'property' 'value' 'zone' 'SELinux area'
              for i in "${sorted[@]}"; do
                  n=$((n + 1))
                  printf '  %3d %6d  %-28s %-18s %-10s %s\n' \
                      "$n" "${c_score[$i]}" "${c_prop[$i]}" "${c_val[$i]}" "${c_zone[$i]}" "${c_label[$i]:-not reported}"
                  printf '            · %s\n' "${c_why[$i]}"
                  [ -n "${c_risk[$i]}" ] && printf '            ! %s\n' "${c_risk[$i]}"
              done
          else
              printf '\n  No property could be ranked — nothing on this phone names the device.\n'
          fi
      
          if [ "${#r_prop[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '\n  Ruled out\n\n'
              for i in "${!r_prop[@]}"; do
                  printf '    %-28s %-18s %s\n' "${r_prop[$i]}" "${r_val[$i]}" "${r_reason[$i]}"
              done
          fi
      
          printf '\n  Confidence: %s\n' "$confidence"
          case "$confidence" in
              high)
                  printf '    %s carries the codename, zygote can read it, and a GSI leaves\n' "${c_prop[${sorted[0]}]}"
                  printf '    its partition alone. This is the answer.\n'
                  ;;
              medium)
                  printf '    The best property holds the codename, but something else about it\n'
                  printf '    is a gamble (readability, or a GSI replaces its partition). It works\n'
                  printf '    today on this ROM; keeping the match you already have is safer.\n'
                  ;;
              *)
                  printf '    No property satisfies every rule. Keep the HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_* you\n'
                  printf '    already have, or set the pair by hand from config.env.\n'
                  ;;
          esac
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Writing it into config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      write_pair() {
          local prop="$1" value="$2"
          cfg_set HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP "$prop" || { printf 'match-prop: could not write config.env\n' >&2; return 1; }
          cfg_set HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE "$value" || { printf 'match-prop: could not write config.env\n' >&2; return 1; }
          printf '\n  Written to config.env:\n    HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP="%s"\n    HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE="%s"\n' "$prop" "$value"
          printf '  Rebuild to pick it up: ./build.sh (or 8 in the menu)\n\n'
          return 0
      }
      
      main() {
          if [ -n "$values_file" ]; then
              collect_from_files
          else
              collect_from_device
          fi

 color=\"$UI_GREEN\" ;;\n        warn) glyph=\"$UI_WARN\";  color=\"$UI_YELLOW\" ;;\n        bad)  glyph=\"$UI_CROSS\"; color=\"$UI_RED\" ;;\n        *)    glyph=\"$UI_DOT\";   color=\"$UI_DIM\" ;;\n    esac\n    # 2 columns of margin, the glyph, one space: the text starts at column 5, so\n    # every wrapped line is drawn at 5 and the first line loses the indent it\n    # already has behind the glyph.\n    printf '  %s%s%s ' \"$color\" \"$glyph\" \"$UI_OFF\"\n    ui_wrap \"$text\" 5 | sed '1s/^     //'\n}\n\n# ui_title \"TEXT\" [SUBTITLE] — the first line of a report.\nui_title() {\n    local w; w=$(ui_cols)\n    printf '\\n  %s%s%s\\n' \"$UI_BOLD\" \"$1\" \"$UI_OFF\"\n    if [ -n \"${2:-}\" ]; then\n        ui_wrap \"$2\" 2 $((w - 2)) | sed '1s/^  \"$UI_DIM\"/x/'\n    fi\n    printf '  %s%s%s\\n' \"$UI_DIM\" \"$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) \"$UI_H\")\" \"$UI_OFF\"\n}",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

> 
> ui_table design:
> - Columns defined by header names; widths computed from content clamped by available width.
> - Emit: blank line, bold header, dim rule, rows.
> - If total width > cols, shrink widest columns / wrap last column (notes) — complexity.
> 
> Simpler responsive table: 
> - ui_table "SETTING|VALUE|SOURCE|CONFIDENCE" rows...
> - compute natural widths; if sum + gaps > avail, drop columns from the right? Dropping data is bad.
> - Alternative: narrow mode stacks each row as a two-line block. But for device-probe a 4-col table at 40 cols: setting 25 + value 12 + ... too wide.
> 
> Better: keep it a table but wrap the last column? Hmm.

- path: stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh
  content: |
                  "$([ "${IS_GSI:-0}" -eq 1 ] && echo true || echo false)" "${W:-0}" "${H:-0}" "${DENS:-0}"
          else
              printf '"firmware":"%s",' "$(json_escape "$fwdir")"
          fi
          printf '"aapt2":"%s",' "$(json_escape "${aapt2:-}")"
          printf '"facts":['
          for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
              [ "$first" -eq 1 ] || printf ','
              first=0
              printf '{"key":"%s","label":"%s","unit":"%s","value":"%s","source":"%s","confidence":"%s","kind":"%s","detail":"%s"}' \
                  "$(json_escape "${f_key[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${f_label[$i]}")" \
                  "$(json_escape "${f_unit[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${f_value[$i]}")" \
                  "$(json_escape "${f_src[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${f_conf[$i]}")" \
                  "$(json_escape "${f_kind[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${f_detail[$i]}")"
          done
          printf '],'
          printf '"warnings":%s,' "$(json_list "${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}")"
          printf '"notes":%s,' "$(json_list "${notes[@]+"${notes[@]}"}")"
          local fpaths=() froles=()
          for i in "${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}"; do
              fpaths+=("${i%%|*}")
              froles+=("${i#*|}")
          done
          printf '"files":['
          for i in "${!fpaths[@]}"; do
              [ "$i" -eq 0 ] || printf ','
              printf '{"path":"%s","role":"%s"}' "$(json_escape "${fpaths[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${froles[$i]}")"
          done
          printf ']'
          [ "$want_write" -eq 1 ] && printf ',"written":"config.env"'
          printf '}\n'
      }
      
      emit_human() {
          local i
          printf '\n'
          if [ "$mode" = "device" ]; then
              printf 'Device   %s (%s)  %sx%s @%s dpi\n' \
                  "${MODEL:-unknown}" "${CODENAME:-unknown}" "${W:-?}" "${H:-?}" "${DENS:-?}"
              printf 'ROM      %s\n' "${rom:-unknown}"
          else
              printf 'Firmware %s\n' "$fwdir"
          fi
          printf '\n'
      
          if [ "${#f_key[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              printf 'Nothing found.\n'
              for i in "${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}"; do printf '  ! %s\n' "$i"; done
              return
          fi
      
          # A cutout path is a hundred characters of SVG; the table is a summary, so
          # it is cut to a readable length here and printed in full further down.
          short_value() {
              local v="$1"
              if [ "${#v}" -gt 44 ]; then printf '%s…' "${v:0:43}"; else printf '%s' "$v"; fi
          }
      
          printf '%-26s %-46s %-20s %s\n' "SETTING" "VALUE" "SOURCE" "CONFIDENCE"
          for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
              printf '%-26s %-46s %-20s %s\n' \
                  "${f_key[$i]}" "$(short_value "${f_value[$i]}${f_unit[$i]:+ ${f_unit[$i]}}")" \
                  "${f_src[$i]}" "${f_conf[$i]}"
          done
      
          # Disagreement is the interesting case: the same setting with two values
          # means two sources, and the user has to pick which one to believe.
          local key i j distinct first second
          for key in $(printf '%s\n' "${f_key[@]}" | awk '!seen[$0]++'); do
              distinct="$(for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
                  [ "${f_key[$i]}" = "$key" ] && printf '%s\n' "${f_value[$i]}"
              done | awk '!seen[$0]++' | grep -c . || true)"
              [ "${distinct:-0}" -gt 1 ] || continue
              if [ "$distinct" -eq 2 ]; then
                  first=""; second=""
                  for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
                      [ "${f_key[$i]}" = "$key" ] || continue
                      if [ -z "$first" ]; then first="$i"
                      elif [ "${f_value[$i]}" != "${f_value[$first]}" ] && [ -z "$second" ]; then second="$i"; fi
                  done
                  printf '\n%s differs: %s says %s, %s says %s\n' \
                      "$key" "${f_src[$first]}" "$(short_value "${f_value[$first]}")" \
                      "${f_src[$second]}" "$(short_value "${f_value[$second]}")"
              else
                  printf '\n%s: %s different answers — pick one from the table\n' "$key" "$distinct"
              fi
          done
      
          printf '\nvalues for config.env:\n'
          for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
              local seen=""
              local j
              for j in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
                  [ "$i" -gt "$j" ] && [ "${f_key[$i]}" = "${f_key[$j]}" ] && { seen="1"; break; }
              done
              [ -n "$seen" ] && continue
              case "${f_key[$i]}" in
                  DISPLAY_CUTOUT|LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE) printf '  %s="%s"\n' "${f_key[$i]}" "${f_value[$i]}" ;;
                  *) printf '  %s=%s\n' "${f_key[$i]}" "${f_value[$i]}" ;;
              esac
          done
      
          for i in "${notes[@]+"${notes[@]}"}"; do printf '\nnote: %s\n' "$i"; done
          for i in "${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}"; do printf '\nwarning: %s\n' "$i"; done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Writing config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      set_config_key() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" file="$ROOT/config.env" tmp
          [ -f "$file" ] || die "no config.env in $ROOT"
          tmp="$tmpdir/config.env"
          awk -v k="$key" -v v="$value" '
              BEGIN { done = 0 }
              {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/\r$/, "", line)
                  if (!done && line ~ "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*" k "=") {
                      match(line, /^[[:space:]]*/)
                      printf "%s%s=%s\n", substr(line, 1, RLENGTH), k, v
                      done = 1
                      next
                  }
                  print
              }
              END { if (!done) printf "%s=%s\n", k, v }
          ' "$file" >"$tmp" || return 1
          cp "$tmp" "$file"
      }
      
      write_config() {
          local i value
          for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
              [ "${f_conf[$i]}" = "low" ] && continue
              # One write per setting: the first fact is the highest-priority source.
              local key="${f_key[$i]}"
              local earlier=""
              local j
              for j in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
                  [ "$j" -lt "$i" ] && [ "${f_key[$j]}" = "$key" ] && { earlier="1"; break; }
              done
              [ -n "$earlier" ] && continue
      
              value="${f_value[$i]}"
              case "$key" in
                  # String settings keep the quotes every line of config.env uses.
                  DISPLAY_CUTOUT|LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE) set_config_key "$key" "\"$value\"" ;;
                  *) set_config_key "$key" "$value" ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      main() {
          # Hidden helper for the tests: decide whether a tree on stdin is a device
          # profile or the AOSP placeholder, without needing adb or aapt2.
          if [ "$check_profile" -eq 1 ]; then
              local tree
              tree="$(cat)"
              if profile_looks_real "$tree"; then
                  printf 'real\n'
                  exit 0
              fi
              printf 'generic\n'
              exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$power_mode" -eq 1 ]; then
              if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then power_profile_firmware; else power_profile_device; fi
              exit 0
          fi
          if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then probe_firmware; else probe_device; fi
          if [ "$want_write" -eq 1 ]; then
              if [ "${#f_key[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  die "nothing to write — no setting was found"
              fi
              write_config
          fi
          if [ "$want_json" -eq 1 ]; then emit_json; else emit_human; fi
      }
      
      main "$@"

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh — firmware mode has to answer from the ROM
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The failure this pins: a Xiaomi ROM puts the sensor geometry in
      // vendor/build.prop as the FOD rectangle properties, not in an overlay APK. The
      // probe used to list only the first 40 *.prop files (a real tree has hundreds,
      // starting with system_ext's per-app cust.prop) and never turned the pair into a
      // candidate at all, so a full super.img answered nothing while the same phone
      // over adb answered 540,2198,89 from the very same property.
      //
      // No phone and no aapt2 are involved: the tree is a few text files.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const probe = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'udfps-probe.sh');
      
      function tree(files) {
        const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'udfps-fw-'));
        for (const [rel, body] of Object.entries(files)) {
          const path = join(dir, rel);
          mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
          writeFileSync(path, body);
        }
        return dir;
      }
      
      function run(dir) {
        const out = execFileSync('bash', [probe, '--firmware', dir, '--json'], {
          encoding: 'utf8',
          stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
          env: { ...process.env, TERM: 'dumb' },
        });
        return JSON.parse(out);
