- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # ui.sh — how a terminal report is drawn
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by common.sh (so the menu and build.sh get it) and by the probes that
      # print a report. Never run directly.
      #
      # The reports used to be fixed-width printf columns, which is the right shape on
      # a 100-column desktop window and unreadable on a phone: 58-column rules wrapped
      # mid-border, and a line of prose about a property ran off the edge and came
      # back as a second, unrelated-looking line. Everything here is measured against
      # the real window instead, and long prose is wrapped with a hanging indent so a
      # wrapped paragraph still looks like one item.
      #
      # Three switches, all optional:
      #   UI_COLOR=always|never|auto   auto (the default) is "a terminal is attached"
      #   UI_COLS=N                    the width to draw for, when there is no tty
      #   UI_ASCII=1                   ASCII borders and glyphs, for a font or a
      #                                codepage that cannot show ─ │ · ⚠
      # Colour is off when stdout is not a terminal, so `./build.sh | tee log` and the
      # JSON probes stay clean, and NO_COLOR is respected.
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Width
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # A phone terminal is 40-50 columns, a desktop window is often 200. Below 40
      # nothing lines up; above 100 an eye loses the start of the line on the way
      # back, so the drawing width is clamped and the spare columns stay empty.
      ui_cols() {
          local c="${UI_COLS:-}"
          [ -n "$c" ] || c="${COLUMNS:-}"
          if [ -z "$c" ] && [ -t 1 ] && command -v tput >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              c="$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || true)"
          fi
          case "$c" in ''|*[!0-9]*) c=80 ;; esac
          [ "$c" -ge 40 ] || c=40
          [ "$c" -le 100 ] || c=100
          printf '%s' "$c"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Palette and glyphs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Assigned once, at source time, so a report never has to ask twice.
      ui_wants_color() {
          case "${UI_COLOR:-auto}" in
              always) return 0 ;;
              never) return 1 ;;
          esac
          [ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ] || return 1
          [ "${TERM:-}" != dumb ] || return 1
          [ -t 1 ]
      }
      
      if ui_wants_color; then
          UI_RED=$'\033[31m'; UI_GREEN=$'\033[32m'; UI_YELLOW=$'\033[33m'
          UI_BLUE=$'\033[36m'; UI_MAGENTA=$'\033[35m'
          UI_BOLD=$'\033[1m'; UI_DIM=$'\033[2m'; UI_OFF=$'\033[0m'
      else
          UI_RED=''; UI_GREEN=''; UI_YELLOW=''; UI_BLUE=''; UI_MAGENTA=''
          UI_BOLD=''; UI_DIM=''; UI_OFF=''
      fi
      
      # The box and the glyphs are decoration, so a terminal that cannot show them
      # gets plain ASCII rather than a row of question marks.
      if [ "${UI_ASCII:-0}" = "1" ] || [ "${UI_ASCII:-0}" = "true" ]; then
          UI_TL='+'; UI_TR='+'; UI_BL='+'; UI_BR='+'; UI_H='-'; UI_V='|'
          UI_TICK='+'; UI_CROSS='x'; UI_WARN='!'; UI_DOT='-'
          UI_BAR_ON='#'; UI_BAR_OFF='-'
      else
          UI_TL='┌'; UI_TR='┐'; UI_BL='└'; UI_BR='┘'; UI_H='─'; UI_V='│'
          UI_TICK='✓'; UI_CROSS='✗'; UI_WARN='⚠'; UI_DOT='·'
          UI_BAR_ON='█'; UI_BAR_OFF='░'
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prose
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_repeat N STRING — STRING thirty times. Built by hand because printf's %*s
      # pads by bytes, and a box-drawing character is three of them.
      ui_repeat() {
          local n="$1" s="$2" out=""
          while [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; do
              out="$out$s"
              n=$((n - 1))
          done
          printf '%s' "$out"
      }
      
      # ui_fit TEXT WIDTH — TEXT cut to WIDTH, ending in an ellipsis when it was cut.
      # A value that no longer fits is better shortened than pushed out of its column.
      ui_fit() {
          local text="$1" width="$2"
          [ "$width" -ge 1 ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
          if [ "${#text}" -le "$width" ]; then
              printf '%s' "$text"
          else
              printf '%s…' "${text:0:$((width - 1))}"
          fi
      }
      
      # ui_wrap TEXT INDENT [AVAIL] — greedy word wrap, every line starting at INDENT.
      # Used for the one sentence in a report that explains itself: at 40 columns it
      # is three short lines instead of one that runs off the edge.
      ui_wrap() {
          local text="$1" indent="${2:-0}" avail="${3:-}" pad
          [ -n "$text" ] || return 0
          [ -n "$avail" ] || avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - indent ))
          [ "$avail" -ge 8 ] || avail=8
          pad="$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')"
          printf '%s' "$text" | awk -v w="$avail" -v pad="$pad" '
              {
                  line = ""
                  n = split($0, word, " ")
                  for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                      if (word[i] == "") continue
                      if (line == "") line = word[i]
                      else if (length(line) + 1 + length(word[i]) <= w) line = line " " word[i]
                      else { print pad line; line = word[i] }
                  }
                  if (line != "") print pad line
              }
          '
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Blocks
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_heading TEXT — a section title with a rule under it, sized to the window.
      ui_heading() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_rule [INDENT] — a plain separator.
      ui_rule() {
          local indent="${1:-2}" w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '%s%s%s%s\n' "$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')" "$UI_DIM" \
              "$(ui_repeat $((w - indent)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_kv KEY VALUE [KEYWIDTH] — one aligned key and its value.
      ui_kv() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="${3:-10}"
          printf '  %s%-*s%s  %s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$keyw" "$key" "$UI_OFF" "$value"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_line CONTENT INNER — CONTENT padded to INNER and closed off with the
      # right border. CONTENT carries its own leading space, so the row never starts
      # hard against the border.
      ui_panel_line() {
          printf '  %s%s%s%-*s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF" "$2" "$1" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_row KEY VALUE KEYWIDTH INNER — one key/value row.
      # A value too long for the row is wrapped onto its own indented lines rather than
      # cut with an ellipsis: half a property name is worse than two lines.
      ui_panel_row() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="$3" inner="$4" keypad="" line
          printf -v keypad '%*s' $((keyw - ${#key})) ''
          if [ $((keyw + 3 + ${#value})) -le "$inner" ]; then
              ui_panel_line " $key$keypad  $value" "$inner"
              return 0
          fi
          ui_panel_line " $key$keypad " "$inner"
          ui_wrap "$value" $((keyw + 3)) $((inner - keyw - 4)) \
              | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  ui_panel_line "$line" "$inner"
              done
      }
      
      # ui_panel TITLE "KEY|VALUE" ... — a titled box holding aligned pairs.
      #
      # One call rather than open/row/close because the box has to know its widest key
      # before the top border can be drawn, and that is only known once every row has
      # been seen.
      ui_panel() {
          local title="$1"; shift
          local inner keyw=0 row key bar
          local -a keys=() values=()
          # inner is the width between the two vertical borders. Borders plus the two
          # columns of left margin are kept off the right edge, where a terminal likes
          # to wrap on the last character.
          inner=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
          printf '\n'
          for row in "$@"; do
              key="${row%%|*}"
              [ "${#key}" -gt "$keyw" ] && keyw=${#key}
          done
          [ "$keyw" -le 12 ] || keyw=12
          for row in "$@"; do
              keys+=("${row%%|*}")
              values+=("${row#*|}")
          done
          # A title longer than the box would draw a negative rule; shorten it instead.
          title="$(ui_fit "$title" $((inner - 6)))"
          bar=$(ui_repeat $((inner - ${#title} - 3)) "$UI_H")
          printf '  %s%s%s %s%s%s %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_TL" "$UI_H" \
              "$UI_BOLD" "$title" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DIM" "$bar" "$UI_TR$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!keys[@]}"; do
              ui_panel_row "${keys[$i]}" "${values[$i]}" "$keyw" "$inner"
          done
          printf '  %s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_BL" "$(ui_repeat "$inner" "$UI_H")" "$UI_BR$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_meter VALUE MAX [WIDTH] — a filled bar whose colour is the verdict.
      # Green is "this is the one", red is "do not".
      ui_meter() {
          local value="$1" max="$2" width="${3:-10}" on off color
          case "$max" in ''|*[!0-9]*) max=1 ;; esac
          [ "$max" -gt 0 ] || max=1
          on=$((value * width / max))
          [ "$on" -gt "$width" ] && on="$width"
          [ "$on" -lt 0 ] && on=0
          off=$((width - on))
          if [ "$value" -ge 100 ]; then color="$UI_GREEN"
          elif [ "$value" -ge 60 ]; then color="$UI_YELLOW"
          else color="$UI_RED"
          fi
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$color" "$(ui_repeat "$on" "$UI_BAR_ON")" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$off" "$UI_BAR_OFF")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_mark ok|warn|bad|note "TEXT" [INDENT] — a glyph, prose wrapped under it.
      # INDENT (default 2) is the column of the glyph; the text starts two columns
      # later and every wrapped line is drawn at that same column.
      ui_mark() {
          local kind="$1" text="$2" indent="${3:-2}" glyph color line first=1 pad
          case "$kind" in
              ok)   glyph="$UI_TICK";  color="$UI_GREEN" ;;
              warn) glyph="$UI_WARN";  color="$UI_YELLOW" ;;
              bad)  glyph="$UI_CROSS"; color="$UI_RED" ;;
              *)    glyph="$UI_DOT";   color="$UI_DIM" ;;
          esac
          printf -v pad '%*s' $((indent + 2)) ''
          ui_wrap "$text" $((indent + 2)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
              if [ "$first" = 1 ]; then
                  printf '%*s%s%s%s %s\n' "$indent" '' "$color" "$glyph" "$UI_OFF" "${line#"$pad"}"
                  first=0
              else
                  printf '%s\n' "$line"
              fi
          done
      }
      
      # ui_split TEXT SEP — TEXT split on SEP, one element per field, in UI_SPLIT.
      ui_split() {
          local item
          UI_SPLIT=()
          while IFS= read -r item; do
              UI_SPLIT+=("$item")
          done < <(printf '%s\n' "$1" | tr "$2" '\n')
      }
      
      # ui_table "COL|COL|COL" "CELL|CELL|CELL" ... — an aligned table, or, when the
      # columns would not fit the window, one block per row.
      #
      # Cutting a table in half is worse than folding it: below the width where the
      # natural columns collide, every row becomes its own two-line entry — the key in
      # bold and the rest joined with a dot — which is the same data, stacked, and
      # still comparable down the page.
      ui_table() {
          local header="$1"; shift
          local avail ncols=0 i k w total cell line first
          local -a rows=("$@") heads=() widths=()
          avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
          ui_split "$header" '|'
          heads=("${UI_SPLIT[@]}")
          ncols=${#heads[@]}
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do widths[$k]=${#heads[$k]}; done
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              for k in "${!UI_SPLIT[@]}"; do
                  [ "$k" -lt "$ncols" ] || continue
                  cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]}"
                  [ "${#cell}" -gt "${widths[$k]}" ] && widths[$k]=${#cell}
              done
          done
          total=$(( 2 * (ncols - 1) ))
          for w in "${widths[@]}"; do total=$(( total + w )); done
      
          if [ "$total" -gt "$avail" ]; then
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
                  printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}" "$UI_OFF"
                  line=""
                  for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                      cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                      [ -n "$cell" ] || continue
                      if [ -z "$line" ]; then line="$cell"; else line="$line $UI_DOT $cell"; fi
                  done
                  [ -n "$line" ] || continue
                  ui_wrap "$line" 4 | while IFS= read -r cell; do
                      printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$cell" "$UI_OFF"
                  done
              done
              return 0
          fi
      
          printf '\n  %s' "$UI_BOLD"
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do
              printf '%-*s' "${widths[$k]}" "${heads[$k]}"
              [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ] && printf '  '
          done
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$total" "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              printf '  %s' "$UI_DIM"
              printf '%-*s' "${widths[0]}" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}"
              printf '%s  ' "$UI_OFF"
              for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                  printf '%-*s' "${widths[$k]}" "${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                  [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ] && printf '  '
              done
              printf '\n'
          done
      }
      
      # ui_title "TEXT" [SUBTITLE] — the first line of a report, ruled to the width.
      ui_title() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
              ui_wrap "$2" 2 $((w - 2)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
              done
          fi
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
- path: stuff/scripts/menu.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # menu.sh — the terminal front end
      # =============================================================================
      # The desktop app and this file drive the same tools: the device probes, the
      # addon catalog, the match-property ranking and build.sh's own verbs. The goal
      # is that a phone with a terminal (Termux, ssh, a server) gets the same answers
      # as the window, without a GUI toolkit.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 opens this (when stdin is a terminal)
      #   ./build.sh menu            opens this even when stdin is not a terminal
      #   bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh same thing, standalone
      #
      # Every action shells out to the real entry point — `build.sh build`,
      # `device-probe.sh --write`, `addons.sh set` — so there is exactly one
      # implementation of each step and the menu cannot drift from the app.
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
          . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      # The device-source helpers (device_is_termux, device_local_begin) live with the
      # adb code the probes share. Sourcing it here defines functions only.
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Small things
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MENU_SLEEP="${MENU_SLEEP:-0}"
      
      hr() { printf '  %s\n' "──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"; }
      
      # Read one line. Returns 1 at EOF (piped input, a launcher with no console) so
      # callers can leave the menu instead of looping forever.
      menu_read() {
          local prompt="${1:-} " answer=""
          printf '%s' "$prompt"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              return 1
          fi
          MENU_ANSWER="$answer"
          return 0
      }
      
      # Wait for Enter between screens, unless stdin is not a terminal.
      pause_menu() {
          [ -t 0 ] || return 0
          printf '\n  %s ' "Press Enter to go back"
          read -r _ || true
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # Count the rows config.env has, and how many are switched off.
      cfg_counts() {
          local rows
          rows="$(cfg_rows 2>/dev/null)" || { CFG_ON=0; CFG_OFF=0; return 0; }
          CFG_ON="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 1' | grep -c . || true)"
          CFG_OFF="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 0' | grep -c . || true)"
      }
      
      output_summary() {
          local apks=0 zips=0 zip=""
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR/apks" ] && apks="$(find "$OUT_DIR/apks" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && zips="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          zip="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | sort | head -n1)"
          if [ "$zips" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '%s  (%s APK%s)' "${zip#$ROOT/}" "$apks" "$([ "$apks" = 1 ] || echo s)"
          else
              printf 'nothing built yet'
          fi
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Screen
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_header() {
          cfg_counts
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Treble Overlay Creator${NC}"
          hr
          printf '  %-11s %s\n' 'Device' "$(cfg_identity)"
          printf '  %-11s %s set · %s off\n' 'config.env' "$CFG_ON" "$CFG_OFF"
          printf '  %-11s %s\n' 'Output' "$(output_summary)"
          echo ""
      }
      
      menu_items() {
          cat << 'ITEMS'
           1  Build              dry run, build, check, doctor, clean
           2  config.env         browse and edit one key at a time
           3  Addons             module tweaks: settings and overlay resources
           4  Device             read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone
           5  Auto Detect        ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G
           6  UDFPS              in-display fingerprint geometry
           7  Match property     which property the submission should match on
           8  Files              what was built, and where it is
           9  Docs               the guides in docs/
           q  Quit
      ITEMS
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The menu never re-implements a build step: it runs the entry point with the
      # verb a user would type, so `build.sh doctor` and 1 → 4 are the same command.
      run_entry() {
          ( cd "$ROOT" && bash "$ROOT/build.sh" "$@" )
      }
      
      menu_build() {
          while :; do
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}Build${NC}"
              hr
              echo "     1  Dry run         print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
              echo "     2  Build           build the module (installs tools if needed)"
              echo "     3  Check           validate config.env without building"
              echo "     4  Doctor          check the toolchain, install nothing"
              echo "     5  Clean           remove build output"
              echo "     6  Clean --all     start over for a different device"
              echo "     0  Back"
              echo ""
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) run_entry --dry-run; pause_menu ;;
                  2) run_entry build; pause_menu ;;
                  3) run_entry check; pause_menu ;;
                  4) run_entry doctor; pause_menu ;;
                  5) run_entry clean; pause_menu ;;
                  6)
                      warn "This removes config.env and the device files too."
                      if confirm "  Start over for a different device? [y/N] " n; then
                          run_entry clean --all
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Files
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_files() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Files${NC}"
          hr
          printf '  %-12s %s\n' 'Project' "$ROOT"
          printf '  %-12s %s\n' 'config.env' "$ROOT/config.env"
          printf '  %-12s %s\n' 'Build tree' "${BUILD_DIR#$ROOT/}"
          echo ""
          if [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$OUT_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
              echo "  Output"
              find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.apk' \) 2>/dev/null |
                  while IFS= read -r f; do
                      printf '    %-10s %s\n' "$(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)" "${f#$ROOT/}"
                  done
          else
              echo "  Nothing built yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
          fi
          pause_menu
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Docs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_docs() {
          local files=() i
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Docs${NC}"
          hr
          [ -d "$ROOT/docs" ] || { warn "docs/ is missing from this checkout."; pause_menu; return 0; }
          while IFS= read -r f; do
              files+=("$f")
          done < <(find "$ROOT/docs" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
          for i in "${!files[@]}"; do
              printf '  %2d  %s\n' "$((i + 1))" "$(basename "${files[$i]}")"
          done
          echo ""
          menu_read "  number to read, Enter to go back >" || return 0
          case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
              ''|q) return 0 ;;
              *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number."; return 0 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#files[@]}" ]; then
              warn "No such doc."
              return 0
          fi
          local pick="${files[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]}"
          echo ""
          if [ -t 1 ] && command -v less >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              less -R "$pick"
          else
              cat "$pick"
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The file keeps its shape: these helpers rewrite one line and leave the
      # comments, the section headers and the quoting alone. A key that is commented
      # out shows as `off` and can be switched on by number, which is the whole point
      # of listing it — hunting for the '#' in a 240-line file is where mistakes
      # happen.
      cfg_each_row() { # <section> -> `key<TAB>active<TAB>value` rows of that section
          local section="$1"
          cfg_rows 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' -v s="$section" '$4 == s { print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $5 }'
      }
      
      cfg_edit_value() {
          local key="$1" current value
          current="$(cfg_get "$key")"
          printf '\n  %s = %s\n' "$key" "${current:-<empty>}"
          menu_read "  new value (Enter keeps it, - clears it)" || return 0
          value="$MENU_ANSWER"
          [ -z "$value" ] && { info "Left it alone."; return 0; }
          [ "$value" = "-" ] && value=""
          if cfg_set "$key" "$value"; then
              ok "$key is now ${value:-<empty>}"
          else
              err "Could not write config.env — is it read-only?"
          fi
      }
      
      cfg_section() { # <section title>
          local section="$1" rows=() row i n=0
          while :; do
              rows=()
              while IFS= read -r row; do
                  [ -n "$row" ] && rows+=("$row")
              done < <(cfg_each_row "$section")
      
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${section:-Unsectioned}${NC}"
              hr
              if [ "${#rows[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  info "This section has no keys."
                  pause_menu
                  return 0
              fi
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  local key="${rows[$i]%%$'\t'*}" rest="${rows[$i]#*$'\t'}"
                  local active="${rest%%$'\t'*}" value="${rest#*$'\t'}"
                  local state='on '
                  [ "$active" = "1" ] || state='off'
                  value="$(printf '%s' "$value" | sed 's/^"\(.*\)"$/\1/')"
                  printf '  %3d  %s  %-30s %-34.34s\n' "$((i + 1))" "$state" "$key" "$value"
              done
              echo ""
              echo "    number = edit value · d number = switch off · e number = switch on"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  d*|D*)
                      i="${MENU_ANSWER#?}"
                      case "$i" in ''|*[!0-9]*) warn "d needs a number, like d3."; continue ;; esac
                      if [ "$i" -lt 1 ] || [ "$i" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then warn "No such key."; continue; fi
                      key="${rows[$((i - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      if cfg_set_active "$key" 0; then ok "$key switched off"; else err "Could not write config.env"; fi
                      ;;
                  e*|E*)
                      i="${MENU_ANSWER#?}"
                      case "$i" in ''|*[!0-9]*) warn "e needs a number, like e3."; continue ;; esac
                      if [ "$i" -lt 1 ] || [ "$i" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then warn "No such key."; continue; fi
                      key="${rows[$((i - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      if cfg_set_active "$key" 1; then ok "$key switched on"; else err "Could not write config.env"; fi
                      ;;
                  *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number." ;;
                  *)
                      if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then
                          warn "No such key."
                          continue
                      fi
                      cfg_edit_value "${rows[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      menu_config() {
          local sections=() i
          while :; do
              sections=()
              while IFS= read -r s; do
                  [ -n "$s" ] && sections+=("$s")
              done < <(cfg_sections 2>/dev/null)
      
              cfg_counts
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}config.env${NC}"
              hr
              printf '  %s set · %s off · %s\n\n' "$CFG_ON" "$CFG_OFF" "$ROOT/config.env"
              if [ "${#sections[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  err "config.env is missing or empty: $ROOT/config.env"
                  pause_menu
                  return 0
              fi
              for i in "${!sections[@]}"; do
                  printf '  %2d  %s\n' "$((i + 1))" "${sections[$i]}"
              done
              echo "     0  Back"
              menu_read "  section >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number." ;;
                  *)
                      if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#sections[@]}" ]; then
                          warn "No such section."
                          continue
                      fi
                      cfg_section "${sections[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]}"
                      ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Addons
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The catalog lives in src/webui/addons.sh and is read here, not copied: the
      # module page on the phone and the desktop app read the same file. The menu
      # only chooses which `set` to run.
      addons_script() { printf '%s' "$ROOT/src/webui/addons.sh"; }
      addons_conf() { printf '%s' "$ROOT/src/module/addons.conf"; }
      
      addons_call() { # <verb> ... — in the clone, with the clone's addons.conf
          ADDONS_DIR="$ROOT" ADDONS_CONF="$(addons_conf)" sh "$(addons_script)" "$@"
      }
      
      addons_saved() { # <id> -> the value in addons.conf, empty when unset
          local file
          file="$(addons_conf)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
          awk -F= -v id="$1" '$1 == id { sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print; exit }' "$file"
      }
      
      menu_addons() {
          local script rows=() row i ans id label choices default kind value saved mark
          script="$(addons_script)"
          if [ ! -f "$script" ]; then
              err "$script is missing — this checkout is incomplete."
              pause_menu
              return 0
          fi
          while :; do
              rows=()
              while IFS= read -r row; do
                  [ -n "$row" ] && rows+=("$row")
              done < <(addons_call catalog 2>/dev/null)
      
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}Addons${NC}"
              hr
              echo "  A setting changes on the phone now; an overlay resource needs a rebuild."
              echo "    #  addon                          now          choices"
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  IFS='|' read -r id choices default label _ kind <<<"${rows[$i]}"
                  saved="$(addons_saved "$id")"
                  value="${saved:-$default}"
                  mark=' '
                  if [ -n "$saved" ]; then
                      mark='*'
                      [ "$saved" = "$default" ] && mark='-'
                  fi
                  printf '  %3d %s %-30.30s %-12.12s %s%s\n' "$((i + 1))" "$mark" "$label" "$value" \
                      "$(printf '%s' "$choices" | tr ',' '/')" "$([ "$kind" = overlay ] && echo ' (overlay)')"
              done
              echo ""
              echo "    * = chosen · - = chosen as the default · plain = the ROM's own value"
              echo "    number = choose a value · number=value = set both · r = reset · Enter = back"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              ans="$MENU_ANSWER"
              case "$ans" in
                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  r|R)
                      addons_call reset
                      info "Every addon is back to the ROM's own value."
                      continue
                      ;;
              esac
      
              if [[ "$ans" == *=* ]]; then
                  id="${ans%%=*}"
                  value="${ans#*=}"
                  if ! printf '%s\n' "${rows[@]}" | awk -F'|' -v id="$id" '$1 == id { found = 1 } END { exit !found }'; then
                      warn "No addon called '$id'."
                      continue
                  fi
                  addons_call set "$id=$value"
                  continue
              fi
      
              case "$ans" in
                  *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number, number=value, or r."; continue ;;
              esac
              if [ "$ans" -lt 1 ] || [ "$ans" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then
                  warn "No such addon."
                  continue
              fi
              IFS='|' read -r id choices default label row kind <<<"${rows[$((ans - 1))]}"
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${label}${NC}"
              printf '  %s\n' "$row"
              echo ""
              printf '  choices: %s · now: %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$choices" | tr ',' '/')" "$(addons_saved "$id" || printf '%s' "$default")"
              menu_read "  value (Enter keeps it)" || return 0
              value="$MENU_ANSWER"
              [ -z "$value" ] && continue
              addons_call set "$id=$value"
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Where the probes read from
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # In Termux the phone the probes want is the one the menu is running on, and the
      # reads a PC does over adb (`cmd`, `dumpsys`, /vendor) are what root unlocks
      # there. ADB on Termux has nothing to dial, so without this the answer was
      # always "no device in adb devices".
      #
      # Asked once per session and handed to every probe as DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST, so a
      # session that said yes is not asked again on each run — and one that said no is
      # not asked either.
      probe_local=""
      
      probe_source_ask() {
          [ -z "$probe_local" ] || return 0
          device_is_termux || return 0
          echo ""
          echo "  This is Termux, so the phone is this one rather than a device on a cable."
          echo "  Reading it directly needs root: the same getprop, cmd overlay, wm and"
          echo "  dumpsys reads a PC makes over adb."
          if confirm "  Read this phone as root? [Y/n] " y; then
              if device_local_begin "menu"; then
                  probe_local=1
              else
                  probe_local=0
              fi
          else
              probe_local=0
          fi
          # The menu itself never reads a phone; only the answer is passed on.
          DEVICE_LOCAL=0
          export DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST="$probe_local"
          echo ""
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Probes
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # device-probe.sh, udfps-probe.sh and device-id.sh all print a report and, with
      # --write, put the winners in config.env. That is the only difference between
      # the two answers here, so the submenu asks it instead of inventing options.
      # Ctrl-C is how the probes' device wait is left ("up to 120s; Ctrl-C stops
      # this"). A script's bash shares the foreground process group with the child it
      # is waiting on, so the interrupt reaches this menu too: without the trap the
      # whole menu died and the user lost their place. The trap lets the probe exit on
      # its own while the menu stays put; 130 is the probe's "interrupted" code, so in
      # that case there is no report to read and nothing to press a key for.
      probe_run() {
          local rc=0
          trap ':' INT
          bash "$@" || rc=$?
          trap - INT
          # Never return the probe's status: build.sh runs this with `set -e`, so a
          # 130 here would end the menu as surely as the signal did.
          if [ "$rc" -eq 130 ]; then return 0; fi
          pause_menu || true
          return 0
      }
      
      probe_menu() { # <title> <script> <note>
          local title="$1" script="$2" note="$3" dir
          while :; do
              probe_source_ask
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${title}${NC}"
              hr
              # %b so a note can wrap by itself: a one-paragraph description on a
              # phone-width terminal would otherwise run off the edge.
              [ -n "$note" ] && printf '  %b\n' "$note" && echo ""
              if [ "$probe_local" = 1 ]; then
                  echo "     1  Read this phone (report only)"
                  echo "     2  Read this phone and write the answers to config.env"
              else
                  echo "     1  Read the connected phone (report only)"
                  echo "     2  Read the connected phone and write the answers to config.env"
              fi
              echo "     3  Read an unpacked firmware folder instead"
              echo "     0  Back"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) probe_run "$script" ;;
                  2) probe_run "$script" --write ;;
                  3)
                      menu_read "  folder holding the unpacked ROM" || return 0
                      dir="$MENU_ANSWER"
                      [ -n "$dir" ] || continue
                      if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
                          warn "No such folder: $dir"
                          continue
                      fi
                      if confirm "  Write what it finds to config.env? [y/N] " n; then
                          probe_run "$script" --firmware "$dir" --write
                      else
                          probe_run "$script" --firmware "$dir"
                      fi
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      menu_device() {
          probe_menu "Device" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/device-id.sh" \
              "Reads DEVICE_MANUFACTURER, DEVICE_MODEL and DEVICE_CODENAME, and the module condition."
      }
      
      menu_detect() {
          probe_menu "Auto Detect" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh" \
              "What the ROM says about the hardware: cutout path, corner radius, status\n  bar height, refresh rates, VoLTE and 5G flags, the light sensor and the OEM\n  switches. Anything it cannot read is reported, not guessed."
      }
      
      menu_udfps() {
          probe_menu "UDFPS" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh" \
              "The in-display fingerprint sensor's centre and radius."
      }
      
      menu_match() {
          probe_source_ask
          probe_run "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Main loop
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_main() {
          while :; do
              menu_header
              menu_items
              echo ""
              menu_read "  >" || { echo ""; return 0; }
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) menu_build ;;
                  2) menu_config ;;
                  3) menu_addons ;;
                  4) menu_device ;;
                  5) menu_detect ;;
                  6) menu_udfps ;;
                  7) menu_match ;;
                  8) menu_files ;;
                  9) menu_docs ;;
                  q|Q|quit|exit) return 0 ;;
                  '') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Pick a number from the list, or q to quit." ;;
              esac
              [ "$MENU_SLEEP" = "0" ] || sleep "$MENU_SLEEP"
          done
      }
      
      # Standalone: `bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh`. Sourced by build.sh, which calls
      # menu_main itself.
      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
          menu_main
      fi
- path: build.cmd
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem build.cmd - Windows entry point
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem Finds Git for Windows (never WSL) and runs build.sh, which does everything:
      rem
      rem   build.cmd                  the menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes
      rem   build.cmd menu             the menu, even when there is no terminal
      rem   build.cmd build            the overlay build (installs the toolchain first)
      rem   build.cmd setup            install / repair the build tools
      rem   build.cmd doctor           check the toolchain
      rem   build.cmd check            validate config.env
      rem   build.cmd clean            remove build output
      rem   build.cmd clean --all      start over for a different device
      rem
      rem Requirements: Git for Windows + JDK 17+ on PATH.
      rem Tip: run this from cmd or PowerShell (.\\build.cmd), not from WSL.
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal EnableExtensions
      call "%~dp0stuff\windows\run-bash.cmd" build.sh %*
      set "RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
      
      rem Keep the window open only when double-clicked from Explorer. Explorer runs
      rem   cmd.exe /c ""C:\path\build.cmd" "
      rem and a terminal -- cmd, PowerShell, VS Code -- starts cmd.exe with no /c. The
      rem /c is the difference, and matching on it is the only test that works:
      rem Windows leaves a space after the trailing quotes, so a last-three-characters
      rem test never matches.
      set "DOUBLE="
      echo %cmdcmdline% | "%SystemRoot%\System32\findstr.exe" /i /c:" /c " >nul && set "DOUBLE=1"
      if defined DOUBLE pause
      
      exit /b %RC%
      
- path: treble-rro-creator.cmd
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem treble-rro-creator.cmd - launch the desktop app
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem Builds it on first run, then opens the window. The cmd companion to
      rem treble-rro-creator.sh, for people who would rather double-click.
      rem
      rem   treble-rro-creator.cmd               build if needed, then open the window
      rem   treble-rro-creator.cmd --rebuild     rebuild first
      rem   treble-rro-creator.cmd --release     no console window (the default here)
      rem   treble-rro-creator.cmd --browser     use the default browser instead
      rem   treble-rro-creator.cmd -h            this message
      rem
      rem Requirements: Git for Windows (already needed by build.cmd); Go and a
      rem MinGW-w64 gcc are downloaded on the first run. See docs/gui.md.
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal EnableExtensions
      
      if "%~1"=="-h" goto usage
      if "%~1"=="--help" goto usage
      
      rem The launcher closes its console either way (treble-rro-creator.sh always
      rem starts the window in the background), so all that is left to decide here is
      rem whether a failure should hold the window open. Explorer starts this file as
      rem   cmd.exe /c ""C:\path\treble-rro-creator.cmd" "
      rem and a terminal starts cmd.exe interactively, with no /c. The /c is the
      rem difference: nobody is watching a double-click, and a terminal is.
      rem
      rem (The command line is not matched on its trailing quotes: Windows leaves a
      rem space after them, so `" "` arrives as `" " ` and a last-three-characters
      rem test never matches.)
      set "DOUBLE="
      echo %cmdcmdline% | "%SystemRoot%\System32\findstr.exe" /i /c:" /c " >nul && set "DOUBLE=1"
      
      call "%~dp0stuff\windows\run-bash.cmd" treble-rro-creator.sh %*
      set "RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
      
      rem Only hold the console open when something failed and this was started by
      rem double-clicking; a successful launch has already closed the console.
      if "%RC%"=="0" goto done
      if defined DOUBLE pause
      
      :done
      exit /b %RC%
      
      :usage
      echo Treble RRO Creator - desktop app
      echo.
      echo   treble-rro-creator.cmd               build if needed, then open the window
      echo   treble-rro-creator.cmd --rebuild     rebuild first (after a git pull, say)
      echo   treble-rro-creator.cmd --release     no console window (the default here)
      echo   treble-rro-creator.cmd --detach      accepted for scripts; the console closes anyway
      echo   treble-rro-creator.cmd --browser     no window; use the default browser
      echo   treble-rro-creator.cmd -clone PATH   start on a different clone
      echo   treble-rro-creator.cmd -h            this message
      echo.
      echo Builds on the first run (Go and MinGW-w64 gcc are downloaded);
      echo later launches open straight away. Full guide: docs\gui.md
      exit /b 0

- path: stuff/scripts/common.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay — shared helpers
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by build.sh and by the modules in stuff/scripts/. Never run directly.
      #
      # The entry point sets ROOT (the project directory) and then sources this file,
      # so every helper below can assume it exists and that the current directory is
      # the project root.
      # =============================================================================
      
      : "${ROOT:?stuff/scripts/common.sh must be sourced by build.sh (ROOT is not set)}"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Paths
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Absolute paths are used for file tests and for zip destinations. Arguments
      # handed to native tools (aapt2/zipalign) must stay RELATIVE: MSYS on Windows
      # does not reliably convert a /c/... path for a native .exe.
      # Everything that is not the thing you build lives under stuff/, so the root
      # only holds the two entry points, config.env and the folders you open.
      STUFF_DIR="$ROOT/stuff"
      TOOLS_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/tools"
      BUILD_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/build"
      OUT_DIR="$ROOT/out"
      KEYS_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/keys"
      BACKUP_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/backups"
      TEMPLATES_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/templates"
      # Not "the old version of your files": the no-git fallback for
      # restore_from_release(). Kept identical to the committed files by stuff/tests/run.sh.
      RECOVERIES_DIR="$TEMPLATES_DIR/recoveries"
      
      SRC_DIR="$ROOT/src"
      FRAMEWORK_DIR="$SRC_DIR/framework"
      FRAMEWORK_RES="$FRAMEWORK_DIR/res"
      SYSTEMUI_DIR="$SRC_DIR/systemui"
      SYSTEMUI_RES="$SYSTEMUI_DIR/res"
      MODULE_DIR="$SRC_DIR/module"
      VENDOR_DIR="$SRC_DIR/vendor"
      
      CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
      CONFIG_EXAMPLE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Restoring a tracked file to what this release ships
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # "Start over" must never hand back a copy that froze at some old commit. The
      # committed blob IS the template for a tracked file, so ask git for it; the
      # copy in stuff/templates/recoveries/ is only the fallback for a checkout with no .git
      # (a fork downloaded as a zip). stuff/tests/run.sh fails if the two ever drift.
      #
      #   restore_from_release <path relative to ROOT> [fallback copy]
      #
      # Returns 0 when the file on disk now holds the release version.
      restore_from_release() {
          local rel="$1" fallback="${2:-}"
      
          if [ -d "$ROOT/.git" ] && command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 \
             && git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet "HEAD:${rel}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if git -C "$ROOT" checkout HEAD -- "$rel" 2>/dev/null; then
                  return 0
              fi
          fi
      
          if [ -n "$fallback" ] && [ -f "$fallback" ]; then
              mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ROOT/$rel")"
              cp "$fallback" "$ROOT/$rel" && return 0
          fi
          return 1
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Platform
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      IS_WINDOWS=false
      case "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) IS_WINDOWS=true ;;
      esac
      
      # WSL reports Linux but lives inside Windows. The build is allowed there only
      # when the checkout is on the Linux filesystem (see wsl_guard).
      IS_WSL=false
      if ! $IS_WINDOWS && [ -r /proc/version ] && grep -qi microsoft /proc/version 2>/dev/null; then
          IS_WSL=true
      fi
      
      IS_TERMUX=false
      if [ -d /data/data/com.termux ] && [ -n "${PREFIX:-}" ]; then
          IS_TERMUX=true
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Output
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The drawing helpers — the window width, the palette, boxes, tables and prose
      # that wraps — are in ui.sh. Everything below is the one-word verb for one of
      # them, so a build log, the menu and a probe report are drawn by the same rules
      # and fit the same phone.
      . "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/ui.sh"
      
      # Kept for the scripts that still colour a line by hand.
      RED='\033[0;31m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
      CYAN='\033[0;36m'; BOLD='\033[1m'; NC='\033[0m'
      
      ok()   { ui_mark ok "$*"; }
      info() { ui_mark note "$*"; }
      warn() { ui_mark warn "$*"; }
      err()  { ui_mark bad "$*" >&2; }
      step() { printf '\n'; ui_heading "$*"; }
      
      # banner TEXT — a title, ruled to the width of the window.
      banner() {
          ui_title "$*"
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prompts
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ask <question> <default>   -> answer in $REPLY
      #
      # `read` returns 1 at EOF (stdin redirected, CI, IDE task, no console). Under
      # `set -e` that used to kill the scripts silently right after a menu had been
      # printed. Falling back to a stated default keeps everything runnable
      # unattended, and pressing Enter also takes the default.
      ask() {
          local question="$1" default="${2:-}" answer=""
          printf '%s' "$question"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              info "No terminal input available — using '${default}'."
              answer="$default"
          fi
          [ -z "$answer" ] && answer="$default"
          REPLY="$answer"
      }
      
      # confirm <question> <y|n>   -> returns 0 for yes
      confirm() {
          local question="$1" default="${2:-n}" answer
          ask "$question" "$default"
          answer="$REPLY"
          case "$answer" in
              [Yy]|[Yy][Ee][Ss]) return 0 ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # WSL safety
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # A checkout on a Windows drive that is built from inside WSL would put Linux
      # binaries into the same stuff/tools/ folder the Windows build reads, and would hand
      # Windows a build tree it cannot use. Refuse with instructions instead of
      # producing a half-broken toolchain. (This is the "VS Code opened the folder
      # with WSL" case.)
      wsl_guard() {
          $IS_WSL || return 0
          case "$ROOT" in
              /mnt/[a-z]/*) ;;
              *) return 0 ;;
          esac
      
          echo ""
          err "This project is on a Windows drive, but you are running inside WSL."
          echo ""
          echo "    Project:  $ROOT"
          echo "    Shell:    WSL (Linux)"
          echo ""
          echo "  The Linux toolchain would be installed into the same stuff/tools/ folder the"
          echo "  Windows build uses, so both platforms would then see the wrong binaries."
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Use one of these instead:${NC}"
          echo "    • Windows (cmd, PowerShell, VS Code):   build.cmd"
          echo "    • Linux / Termux:                       clone the project inside Linux"
          echo "                                            (e.g. ~/treble-rro-creator)"
          echo "                                            and run ./build.sh there"
          echo ""
          echo "  In VS Code, check the bottom-left corner: if it says \"WSL: ...\","
          echo "  close the remote window (or open a Windows terminal) and run build.cmd."
          echo ""
          exit 1
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Legacy layout
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Older versions of this project kept res/, systemui_overlay/, customize.sh,
      # service.sh, sepolicy.rule and system/vendor/ at the top level. Users who
      # upgrade by pulling can still have personal (untracked) copies there. Move
      # them into src/ instead of silently ignoring them.
      migrate_layout() {
          local moved=false f
      
          # res/ -> src/framework/res
          if [ -d "$ROOT/res" ]; then
              if [ ! -d "$FRAMEWORK_RES" ]; then
                  mkdir -p "$FRAMEWORK_DIR"
                  cp -R "$ROOT/res" "$FRAMEWORK_DIR/res"
                  rm -rf "$ROOT/res"
                  info "Moved legacy ./res → src/framework/res"
                  moved=true
              else
                  warn "Legacy ./res exists but is no longer used — the build reads src/framework/res"
              fi
          fi
      
          # systemui_overlay/ -> src/systemui/res
          if [ -d "$ROOT/systemui_overlay/res" ]; then
              if [ ! -d "$SYSTEMUI_RES" ]; then
                  mkdir -p "$SYSTEMUI_DIR"
                  cp -R "$ROOT/systemui_overlay/res" "$SYSTEMUI_DIR/res"
                  rm -rf "$ROOT/systemui_overlay"
                  info "Moved legacy ./systemui_overlay → src/systemui"
                  moved=true
              else
                  warn "Legacy ./systemui_overlay exists but is no longer used — the build reads src/systemui/res"
              fi
          fi
      
          # system/vendor -> src/vendor
          if [ -d "$ROOT/system/vendor" ]; then
              mkdir -p "$VENDOR_DIR"
              cp -R "$ROOT/system/vendor/." "$VENDOR_DIR/" 2>/dev/null || true
              rm -rf "$ROOT/system"
              info "Moved legacy ./system/vendor → src/vendor"
              moved=true
          fi
      
          # Root module scripts -> src/module
          mkdir -p "$MODULE_DIR"
          for f in customize.sh service.sh sepolicy.rule; do
              [ -f "$ROOT/$f" ] || continue
              if [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/$f" ] && cmp -s "$ROOT/$f" "$MODULE_DIR/$f"; then
                  rm -f "$ROOT/$f"
              else
                  mv -f "$ROOT/$f" "$MODULE_DIR/$f"
                  info "Moved legacy ./$f → src/module/$f (now the copy that gets built)"
              fi
              moved=true
          done
      
          # YOUR BACKUPS -> stuff/backups
          if [ -d "$ROOT/YOUR BACKUPS" ] && [ ! -d "$BACKUP_DIR" ]; then
              mv "$ROOT/YOUR BACKUPS" "$BACKUP_DIR"
              info "Moved legacy ./YOUR BACKUPS → stuff/backups"
              moved=true
          fi
      
          # Everything that is not src/, docs/ or an entry point now lives in stuff/.
          # A git pull moves these itself; this covers an upgrade from a zip, which
          # would otherwise leave a second copy in the way at the root.
          mkdir -p "$STUFF_DIR"
          for f in keys templates windows tests scripts tools build backups; do
              [ -d "$ROOT/$f" ] || continue
              if [ -d "$STUFF_DIR/$f" ]; then
                  warn "Legacy ./$f exists but stuff/$f is the one in use — remove the old copy"
                  continue
              fi
              mv "$ROOT/$f" "$STUFF_DIR/$f"
              info "Moved legacy ./$f → stuff/$f"
              moved=true
          done
      
          $moved && info "Layout upgraded — internals live in stuff/, the entry points stay at the root"
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Binary inspection
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Windows cannot execute Linux binaries. If this checkout is also opened from
      # WSL/Kali (a copy on the same drive), a Linux `aapt2` can land in the same
      # stuff/tools/ folder the Windows build puts on PATH, shadow `aapt2.exe`, and fail
      # much later with "Exec format error". Classify by magic bytes so it is caught
      # up front.
      classify_binary() {
          local f="$1"
          if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then echo "missing"; return 0; fi
          if [ -d "$f" ]; then echo "directory"; return 0; fi
          local magic
          magic=$(head -c 4 "$f" 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \n')
          case "$magic" in
              4d5a*)     echo "windows-pe" ;;   # MZ  -> .exe
              7f454c46)  echo "linux-elf" ;;    # \x7fELF -> WSL/Linux build
              2321*)     echo "script" ;;       # #!
              504b0304)  echo "zip" ;;          # PK.. -> apk / jar
              "")        echo "unreadable" ;;
              *)         echo "unknown" ;;
          esac
      }
      
      kind_label() {
          case "$1" in
              windows-pe) echo "Windows executable" ;;
              linux-elf)  echo "Linux binary (ELF)" ;;
              script)     echo "shell script" ;;
              zip)        echo "archive" ;;
              missing)    echo "missing" ;;
              *)          echo "$1" ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # A native binary built for the OTHER platform. This is the real contamination
      # signal: scripts, jars and apks are fine to share between Windows and WSL.
      kind_foreign() {
          if $IS_WINDOWS; then
              [ "$1" = "linux-elf" ]
          else
              [ "$1" = "windows-pe" ]
          fi
      }
      
      # Can a binary of this kind run on the machine we are on right now?
      kind_usable() {
          if $IS_WINDOWS; then
              case "$1" in
                  windows-pe|script|zip) return 0 ;;
                  *) return 1 ;;
              esac
          fi
          case "$1" in
              linux-elf|script|zip) return 0 ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # Every path a tool could be picked up from, in the order build.sh resolves it.
      tool_candidates() {
          local name="$1" c
          for c in "$(command -v "$name" 2>/dev/null)" \
                   "${TOOLS_DIR}/${name}" \
                   "${TOOLS_DIR}/${name}.exe" \
                   "${TOOLS_DIR}/${name}.bat"; do
              [ -n "$c" ] && [ -f "$c" ] && printf '%s\n' "$c"
          done
          return 0
      }
      
      # Is this tool usable HERE (PATH, stuff/tools/, .exe/.bat on Windows)?
      tool_ready() {
          local name="$1" cand
          while IFS= read -r cand; do
              [ -n "$cand" ] || continue
              kind_usable "$(classify_binary "$cand")" && return 0
          done <<< "$(tool_candidates "$name")"
          return 1
      }
      
      # First usable copy of a tool (prints the path, returns 1 when there is none).
      tool_path() {
          local name="$1" cand
          while IFS= read -r cand; do
              [ -n "$cand" ] || continue
              if kind_usable "$(classify_binary "$cand")"; then
                  printf '%s\n' "$cand"
                  return 0
              fi
          done <<< "$(tool_candidates "$name")"
          return 1
      }
      
      # Where the aapt2 resource dictionary lives, if it is installed.
      framework_res_path() {
          local c
          for c in "$TOOLS_DIR/framework-res.apk" \
                   "/usr/share/android-framework-res/framework-res.apk"; do
              [ -f "$c" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$c"; return 0; }
          done
          # Optional local Android SDK (Arch Linux layout)
          if [ -d "/opt/android-sdk/platforms" ]; then
              c=$(find /opt/android-sdk/platforms -name "framework-res.apk" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
              [ -n "$c" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$c"; return 0; }
          fi
          return 1
      }
      
      # Everything the build needs, as a space-separated list (empty = ready).
      # zipalign is not in the Termux package repository (pkg cannot install it) and
      # an unaligned RRO still loads, so it is optional there instead of blocking the
      # build forever. Everything else still requires it.
      zipalign_optional() {
          $IS_TERMUX && ! tool_ready zipalign
      }
      
      # align_apk <unsigned> <aligned> — zipalign when available, plain copy if not.
      # An unaligned APK is valid and installs; it just cannot be mmap'ed as
      # efficiently, so this is a warning, not a failure.
      ALIGN_WARNED=false
      align_apk() {
          if tool_ready zipalign; then
              zipalign -f 4 "$1" "$2"
              return $?
          fi
          if ! $ALIGN_WARNED; then
              warn "zipalign not available — APKs stay unaligned (valid, slightly slower to map)"
              $IS_TERMUX && warn "  Termux: pkg install aapt  (that package ships zipalign)"
              ALIGN_WARNED=true
          fi
          cp -f "$1" "$2"
      }
      
      toolchain_missing() {
          local missing="" t
          for t in aapt2 zipalign apksigner; do
              [ "$t" = "zipalign" ] && zipalign_optional && continue
              tool_ready "$t" || missing="$missing $t"
          done
          command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing java"
          framework_res_path >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing framework-res.apk"
          printf '%s' "${missing# }"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Device identity
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Turns the raw DEVICE_* values from config.env into the module id, the overlay
      # package names and the match condition. Called by build.sh right after
      # config.env is sourced, and by the standalone scripts (manifest.sh,
      # hardware-overlay.sh) so they agree with the build.
      #
      # Users only need to set DEVICE_CODENAME and DEVICE_MANUFACTURER; everything
      # else is derived. A value containing "<" is a template placeholder.
      derive_overlay_identity() {
          [ -z "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER:-}" ] || [[ "$DEVICE_MANUFACTURER" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="generic"
          [ -z "${DEVICE_CODENAME:-}" ]     || [[ "$DEVICE_CODENAME" == *"<"* ]]     && DEVICE_CODENAME="generic"
      
          # Clean manufacturer for Java package names (lowercase alphanumeric only)
          SAFE_MANUFACTURER=$(printf '%s' "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]//g')
      
          # Clean codename for package name: replace non-alphanumeric with dots
          # e.g. "Infinix-X6852" → "infinix.x6852" (dots are valid Java package separators)
          PACKAGE_SEGMENT=$(printf '%s' "${DEVICE_CODENAME}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]/./g' | sed 's/\.\.*/./g' | sed 's/^\.//;s/\.$//')
      
          # Module ids are shared by Magisk, KernelSU and APatch: they must match
          # ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$ (no spaces or slashes). Use the already-cleaned
          # manufacturer/codename pieces for the generated default; an explicit
          # OVERLAY_NAME in config.env is kept as-is.
          DEFAULT_MANUFACTURER="${SAFE_MANUFACTURER:-generic}"
          DEFAULT_CODENAME="${PACKAGE_SEGMENT:-generic}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_NAME:-}" ]        || [[ "$OVERLAY_NAME" == *"<"* ]]        && OVERLAY_NAME="treble-overlay-${DEFAULT_MANUFACTURER}-${DEFAULT_CODENAME}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_PACKAGE:-}" ]     || [[ "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE" == *"<"* ]]     && OVERLAY_PACKAGE="me.phh.treble.overlay.${SAFE_MANUFACTURER}.${PACKAGE_SEGMENT}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI:-}" ] || [[ "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI" == *"<"* ]] && OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI="${OVERLAY_PACKAGE}.systemui"
          [[ "${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE:-}" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_PROP_VALUE="${DEVICE_CODENAME}"
          # Only placeholders are replaced. An EMPTY DEVICE_PROP_NAME is meaningful: it
          # builds an overlay with no match condition (always active), which is the safe
          # default for framework overlays — see the Overlay Activation section of
          # config.env for why ro.product.* conditions fail on GSI setups.
          [[ "${DEVICE_PROP_NAME:-}" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_PROP_NAME="ro.product.device"
      
          if [ -n "${DEVICE_PROP_NAME:-}" ]; then
              OVERLAY_CONDITION="        android:requiredSystemPropertyName=\"${DEVICE_PROP_NAME}\"
              android:requiredSystemPropertyValue=\"${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE}\" />"
              CONDITION_DESC="${DEVICE_PROP_NAME} == \"${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE}\""
          else
              OVERLAY_CONDITION="        />"
              CONDITION_DESC="none (always active)"
          fi
      
          [ -z "${ANDROID_VERSION:-}" ]     && ANDROID_VERSION="14"
          [ -z "${COMPILE_SDK_VERSION:-}" ] && COMPILE_SDK_VERSION="34"
          [ -z "${MIN_SDK_VERSION:-}" ]     && MIN_SDK_VERSION="34"
          [ -z "${TARGET_SDK_VERSION:-}" ]  && TARGET_SDK_VERSION="34"
      
          # Module metadata: module.prop, both manifests and the hardware overlay
          # read these. Empty or still a <placeholder> falls back to the release
          # values, so a config.env written before these keys existed still builds.
          [[ -z "${OVERLAY_VERSION:-}" || "${OVERLAY_VERSION}" == *"<"* ]] && OVERLAY_VERSION="1.0"
          [[ -z "${OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE:-}" || "${OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE}" == *"<"* ]] && OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE="1"
          # Author is free text; only an empty or placeholder one is replaced.
          [[ -z "${MODULE_AUTHOR:-}" || "${MODULE_AUTHOR}" == *"<"* ]] && MODULE_AUTHOR="${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}"
      
          [[ "${LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE:-}" == *"<"* ]] && LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE="android.sensor.light"
          [[ "${DEVICE_MODEL:-}" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_MODEL="Generic Device"
          # Status bar landscape height: only set fallback if explicitly a placeholder
          # (otherwise leave empty so the status bar section skips it)
          [[ "${STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE:-}" == *"<"* ]] && STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE=24
      
          return 0
      }
      
      # Does this power_profile.xml contain actual data, or is it the empty template?
      power_profile_is_placeholder() {
          local f="$1"
          [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
          ! grep -qE '<item[[:space:]>]' "$f"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Portable helpers
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Convert an MSYS path to a native Windows path (no-op elsewhere).
      to_win_path() {
          if $IS_WINDOWS && command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              cygpath -w "$1"
          else
              printf '%s' "$1"
          fi
      }
      
      # Create <dest> from the contents of <src>, using whichever zip tool exists:
      # Info-ZIP (Linux/Termux), 7-Zip, or PowerShell's ZipArchive API (Windows).
      create_zip() {
          local src="$1" dest="$2"
          rm -f "$dest"
          if command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ( cd "$src" && zip -r "$dest" . >/dev/null ) || return 1
          elif command -v 7z >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ( cd "$src" && 7z a -tzip "$dest" . >/dev/null ) || return 1
          elif command -v powershell >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$STUFF_DIR/windows/zipdir.ps1" ]; then
              powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass \
                  -File "$(to_win_path "$STUFF_DIR/windows/zipdir.ps1")" \
                  -Source "$(to_win_path "$(cd "$src" && pwd)")" \
                  -Dest "$(to_win_path "$dest")" >/dev/null || return 1
          else
              err "No zip tool available (install zip, 7-Zip, or re-run the build on Windows)"
              return 1
          fi
      }
      
      # Make the local toolchain visible. Windows tools are .exe files in stuff/tools/;
      # on Linux the build-tools zipalign needs the bundled libc++ from lib64/.
      tools_on_path() {
          case ":$PATH:" in
              *":$TOOLS_DIR:"*) ;;
              *) export PATH="$TOOLS_DIR:$PATH" ;;
          esac
      
          [ -d "$TOOLS_DIR" ] || return 0
          if ! $IS_WINDOWS; then
              local lib
              for lib in "$TOOLS_DIR"/android-sdk/build-tools/*/lib64; do
                  [ -d "$lib" ] && [ -f "$lib/libc++.so" ] || continue
                  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
                  break
              done
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
- path: stuff/scripts/build.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay — build implementation
      # =============================================================================
      # Executed by the root build.sh, which loads stuff/scripts/common.sh and
      # stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh first and guarantees the toolchain is ready.
      #
      # Set by build.sh:  ROOT, TOOLS_DIR, BUILD_DIR, OUT_DIR, CHECK_MODE,
      #                   ASSUME_YES, FORCE_VENDOR_HALS
      # Edited by you:    config.env
      #                   src/framework/res      framework overlay resources
      #                   src/systemui/res       SystemUI overlay resources
      #                   src/module/            customize.sh / service.sh / sepolicy.rule
      #                   src/vendor/            optional vendor HAL files
      #                   stuff/keys/            signing key + certificate
      #
      # Output:           out/apks/*.apk          signed overlays
      #                   out/*.zip              flashable module + repo sources
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          echo "This is an internal build module — run ./build.sh instead." >&2
          exit 1
      fi
      
      cd "$ROOT" || exit 1
      
      # Relative paths: native aapt2/zipalign on Windows may not open /c/... paths.
      RES_DIR="${FRAMEWORK_RES#"$ROOT"/}"
      SYSUI_RES_DIR="${SYSTEMUI_RES#"$ROOT"/}"
      MODULE_SRC_REL="${MODULE_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
      VENDOR_SRC_REL="${VENDOR_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
      BUILD_REL="${BUILD_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
      : "${DRY_RUN:=false}"
      
      # Generators used by the build steps below.
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/resources.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/module.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/manifest.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/validate.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh"
      
      # Never die silently: an unexpected `set -e` abort says where and why.
      trap 'err "Unexpected failure at line ${LINENO}: ${BASH_COMMAND}"; err "Re-run with: bash -x ./build.sh  and report the last lines"' ERR
      
      # Ask something without ever aborting the build. When stdin is not an
      # interactive terminal (IDE task, CI, launcher without a console, piped input)
      # `read` fails — under `set -e` that used to kill the script mid-run.
      ASK_REPLY=""
      ask_reply() {
          local prompt="$1"
          ASK_REPLY=""
          $ASSUME_YES && return 0
          if ! read -r -p "$prompt" ASK_REPLY; then
              ASK_REPLY=""
              info "No terminal input available — using the default answer."
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # Run a build command, indent its output, and abort with a clear message if it
      # fails. (A pipeline would report sed's status, not the tool's.)
      run_or_die() {
          local label="$1"; shift
          local log="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/treble-build.$$.log"
          if "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; then
              [ -s "$log" ] && sed 's/^/  /' "$log"
              rm -f "$log"
              return 0
          fi
          [ -s "$log" ] && sed 's/^/  /' "$log"
          rm -f "$log"
          err "${label} failed"
          return 1
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Target resource audit
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # An RRO that names a resource the target does not have is accepted by aapt2
      # (especially with --auto-add-overlay) and then silently ignored at runtime.
      # That is how a module can look fine and change nothing. Every generated entry
      # is checked against the framework dictionary here.
      framework_resource_index() {
          local cache="$BUILD_REL/framework-resources.txt"
          if [ ! -s "$cache" ] || [ "$PLATFORM_JAR" -nt "$cache" ]; then
              aapt2 dump resources "$PLATFORM_JAR" 2>/dev/null \
                  | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*resource 0x[0-9a-fA-F]* //p' \
                  | awk '{ print $1 }' \
                  | sort -u > "$cache"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$cache"
      }
      
      # Print XML with comments removed, so examples inside <!-- --> are not audited.
      strip_xml_comments() {
          awk '
              FNR == 1 { inc = 0 }
              {
                  line = $0
                  if (inc) {
                      if (line ~ /-->/) { sub(/^.*-->/, "", line); inc = 0 }
                      else next
                  }
                  while (line ~ /<!--/) {
                      if (line ~ /-->/) { sub(/<!--.*-->/, "", line) }
                      else { sub(/<!--.*$/, "", line); inc = 1; break }
                  }
                  print line
              }
          ' "$@"
      }
      
      audit_framework_resources() {
          local index report entries applied=0 ignored=0
          index=$(framework_resource_index)
          report="$OUT_DIR/${OVERLAY_NAME}-overrides.txt"
      
          if [ ! -s "$index" ]; then
              err "Could not read the resource table from ${PLATFORM_JAR}"
              return 1
          fi
      
          entries=$(strip_xml_comments "$RES_DIR"/values*/*.xml 2>/dev/null | awk '
              /<(bool|dimen|integer|string|string-array|integer-array|array|item)[[:space:]>]/ {
                  line = $0
                  tag = line
                  sub(/^[^<]*</, "", tag)
                  sub(/[^a-z-].*$/, "", tag)
                  if (match(line, /name="[^"]+"/) == 0) next
                  name = substr(line, RSTART + 6, RLENGTH - 7)
                  type = ""
                  if (tag == "item") {
                      if (match(line, /type="[^"]+"/)) type = substr(line, RSTART + 6, RLENGTH - 7)
                      if (type == "") type = "dimen"
                  } else if (tag == "string-array" || tag == "integer-array" || tag == "array") {
                      type = "array"
                  } else {
                      type = tag
                  }
                  print tag " " name " " type
              }
          ' || true)
      
          {
              echo "# Treble overlay resource audit"
              echo "# target dictionary: ${PLATFORM_JAR}"
              echo "# generated from:    ${CONFIG_FILE}"
              echo "#"
              echo "# APPLIES = the resource exists in the target and will be overridden"
              echo "# IGNORED = the resource is not in the target; Android silently drops it"
              echo ""
          } > "$report"
      
          local tag name type ignored_list=""
          while read -r tag name type; do
              [ -n "$name" ] || continue
              [ -n "$type" ] || continue
              if grep -qxF "$type/$name" "$index"; then
                  applied=$((applied + 1))
