- path: stuff/windows/run-bash.cmd
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem run-bash.cmd - run build.sh under Git Bash
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem Usage:  stuff\windows\run-bash.cmd <script.sh> [args...]
      rem
      rem Kept in one place so the Windows launchers cannot drift apart.
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal EnableExtensions
      
      set "SCRIPT=%~1"
      if "%SCRIPT%"=="" (
          echo Usage: stuff\windows\run-bash.cmd ^<script.sh^> [args...]
          exit /b 1
      )
      
      rem Project root = two levels above this file (stuff/windows/): the clone root
      set "ROOT=%~dp0..\.."
      set "BASH="
      
      rem 1) Standard Git for Windows install locations
      for %%B in (
          "%ProgramFiles%\Git\bin\bash.exe"
          "%LocalAppData%\Programs\Git\bin\bash.exe"
      ) do if not defined BASH if exist "%%~B" set "BASH=%%~B"
      
      rem 2) Any bash on PATH, but only accept a real MSYS one (never WSL's)
      if not defined BASH (
          for /f "delims=" %%B in ('%SystemRoot%\System32\where.exe bash.exe 2^>nul') do if not defined BASH call :try_bash "%%B"
      )
      
      if not defined BASH goto no_bash
      
      rem Collect arguments after the script name (cmd's %* keeps the script too)
      set "ARGS="
      :collect_args
      shift
      if "%~1"=="" goto args_done
      set ARGS=%ARGS% "%~1"
      goto collect_args
      :args_done
      
      rem Run from the project root; a relative script path avoids handing bash a
      rem C:\... path, where it would treat the backslashes as escape characters.
      pushd "%ROOT%" >nul
      "%BASH%" --noprofile --norc "./%SCRIPT%" %ARGS%
      set "RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
      popd >nul
      exit /b %RC%
      
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      :try_bash
      rem Accept the candidate only if it reports an MSYS/Cygwin environment.
      "%~1" -c "uname -s" 2>nul | "%SystemRoot%\System32\findstr.exe" /i "MINGW MSYS CYGWIN" >nul
      if errorlevel 1 exit /b 0
      set "BASH=%~1"
      exit /b 0
      
      :no_bash
      echo.
      echo   Git for Windows was not found.
      echo   Install it from https://git-scm.com/download/win and try again.
      echo.
      echo   WSL's bash.exe is not supported: this tool needs Git Bash (MSYS2),
      echo   because the Android build tools are native Windows programs.
      echo.
      pause
      exit /b 1

On a\n# phone the description does not fit beside the label, so it moves to its own\n# indented, wrapped line instead of being cut off at the edge.\nui_item() {\n    local num=\"$1\" label=\"$2\" detail=\"${3:-}\" cols head line\n    cols=$(ui_cols)\n    head=\"  $(printf '%3s' \"$num\")  ${UI_BOLD}${label}${UI_OFF}\"\n    if [ -z \"$detail\" ]; then\n        printf '%s\\n' \"$head\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    # 5 for the number column and its gaps, 2 between label and description.\n    if [ $((5 + ${#label} + 2 + ${#detail})) -le \"$cols\" ]; then\n        printf '%s  %s%s%s\\n' \"$head\" \"$UI_DIM\" \"$detail\" \"$UI_OFF\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    printf '%s\\n' \"$head\"\n    ui_wrap \"$detail\" 7 $((cols - 7)) | while IFS= read -r line; do\n        printf '%s%s%s\\n' \"$UI_DIM\" \"$line\" \"$UI_OFF\"\n    done\n}\n\n# ui_split TEXT SEP — TEXT split on SEP, one element per field, in UI_SPLIT.",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

{
  "path": "stuff/scripts/ui.sh",
  "replacements": [
    {
      "oldString": "ui_panel_row() {\n    local key=\"$1\" value=\"$2\" keyw=\"$3\" inner=\"$4\" keypad=\"\" line\n    printf -v keypad '%*s' $((keyw - ${#key})) ''\n    if [ $((keyw + 3 + ${#value})) -le \"$inner\" ]; then\n        ui_panel_line \" $key$keypad  $value\" \"$inner\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    ui_panel_line \" $key$keypad \" \"$inner\"\n    ui_wrap \"$value\" $((keyw + 3)) $((inner - keyw - 4)) \\\n        | while IFS= read -r line; do\n            ui_panel_line \"$line\" \"$inner\"\n        done\n}",
      "newString": "ui_panel_row() {\n    local key=\"$1\" value=\"$2\" keyw=\"$3\" inner=\"$4\" keypad=\"\" line avail\n    local -a parts=()\n    printf -v keypad '%*s' $((keyw - ${#key})) ''\n    avail=$((inner - keyw - 3))\n    if [ ${#value} -le \"$avail\" ]; then\n        ui_panel_line \" $key$keypad  $value\" \"$inner\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    # Too wide: wrap it, but keep the first piece on the key's own line so the\n    # two still read as one row rather than a label with a paragraph under it.\n    while IFS= read -r die; do parts+=(\"$die\"); done < <(ui_wrap \"$value\" 0 \"$avail\")\n    ui_panel_line \" $key$keypad  ${parts[0]:-}\" \"$inner\"\n    local i\n    for ((i = 1; i < ${#parts[@]}; i++)); do\n        line=\"$(ui_repeat $((keyw + 3)) ' ')${parts[$i]}\"\n        ui_panel_line \"$line\" \"$inner\"\n    done\n}",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

They are three aligned columns when the window has room\n# and two lines when it does not — the state keeps its colour either way, so\n# scanning down the page is still \"find the green ones\".\ncfg_list_row() {\n    local num=\"$1\" keyw=\"$2\" key=\"$3\" active=\"$4\" value=\"$5\"\n    local cols state statepad color avail vw\n    cols=$(ui_cols)\n    if [ \"$active\" = \"1\" ]; then state='on'; color=\"$UI_GREEN\"; else state='off'; color=\"$UI_DIM\"; fi\n    printf -v statepad '%*s' $((3 - ${#state})) ''\n    if [ -z \"$value\" ]; then value=\"${UI_DIM}(empty)${UI_OFF}\"; else value=\"${UI_BOLD}${value}${UI_OFF}\"; fi\n\n    avail=$((cols - (2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + keyw + 2)))\n    if [ \"$avail\" -ge 8 ]; then\n        vw=$((avail - 1))\n        printf '  %s%3d%s  %s%s%s%s  %s%-*s%s  %s\\n' \\\n            \"$UI_DIM\" \"$num\" \"$UI_OFF\" \"$color\" \"$state\" \"$statepad\" \"$UI_OFF\" \\\n            \"$UI_DIM\" \"$keyw\" \"$key\" \"$UI_OFF\" \"$(ui_fit \"$value\" \"$vw\")\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    printf '  %s%3d%s  %s%-3s%s  %s%s%s\\n' \\\n        \"$UI_DIM\" \"$num\" \"$UI_OFF\" \"$color\" \"$state\" \"$UI_OFF\" \"$UI_BOLD\" \"$key\" \"$UI_OFF\"\n    ui_wrap \"$value\" 10 $((cols - 10)) | while IFS= read -r l; do\n        printf '%s%s%s\\n' \"$UI_DIM\" \"$l\" \"$UI_OFF\"\n    done\n}",

```

- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # ui.sh — how a terminal report is drawn
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by common.sh (so the menu and build.sh get it) and by the probes that
      # print a report. Never run directly.
      #
      # The reports used to be fixed-width printf columns, which is the right shape on
      # a 100-column desktop window and unreadable on a phone: 58-column rules wrapped
      # mid-border, and a line of prose about a property ran off the edge and came
      # back as a second, unrelated-looking line. Everything here is measured against
      # the real window instead, and long prose is wrapped with a hanging indent so a
      # wrapped paragraph still looks like one item.
      #
      # Three switches, all optional:
      #   UI_COLOR=always|never|auto   auto (the default) is "a terminal is attached"
      #   UI_COLS=N                    the width to draw for, when there is no tty
      #   UI_ASCII=1                   ASCII borders and glyphs, for a font or a
      #                                codepage that cannot show ─ │ · ⚠
      # Colour is off when stdout is not a terminal, so `./build.sh | tee log` and the
      # JSON probes stay clean, and NO_COLOR is respected.
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Width
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # A phone terminal is 40-50 columns, a desktop window is often 200. Below 40
      # nothing lines up; above 100 an eye loses the start of the line on the way
      # back, so the drawing width is clamped and the spare columns stay empty.
      ui_cols() {
          local c="${UI_COLS:-}"
          [ -n "$c" ] || c="${COLUMNS:-}"
          if [ -z "$c" ] && [ -t 1 ] && command -v tput >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              c="$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || true)"
          fi
          case "$c" in ''|*[!0-9]*) c=80 ;; esac
          [ "$c" -ge 40 ] || c=40
          [ "$c" -le 100 ] || c=100
          printf '%s' "$c"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Palette and glyphs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Assigned once, at source time, so a report never has to ask twice.
      ui_wants_color() {
          case "${UI_COLOR:-auto}" in
              always) return 0 ;;
              never) return 1 ;;
          esac
          [ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ] || return 1
          [ "${TERM:-}" != dumb ] || return 1
          [ -t 1 ]
      }
      
      if ui_wants_color; then
          UI_RED=$'\033[31m'; UI_GREEN=$'\033[32m'; UI_YELLOW=$'\033[33m'
          UI_BLUE=$'\033[36m'; UI_MAGENTA=$'\033[35m'
          UI_BOLD=$'\033[1m'; UI_DIM=$'\033[2m'; UI_OFF=$'\033[0m'
      else
          UI_RED=''; UI_GREEN=''; UI_YELLOW=''; UI_BLUE=''; UI_MAGENTA=''
          UI_BOLD=''; UI_DIM=''; UI_OFF=''
      fi
      
      # The box and the glyphs are decoration, so a terminal that cannot show them
      # gets plain ASCII rather than a row of question marks.
      if [ "${UI_ASCII:-0}" = "1" ] || [ "${UI_ASCII:-0}" = "true" ]; then
          UI_TL='+'; UI_TR='+'; UI_BL='+'; UI_BR='+'; UI_H='-'; UI_V='|'
          UI_TICK='+'; UI_CROSS='x'; UI_WARN='!'; UI_DOT='-'
          UI_BAR_ON='#'; UI_BAR_OFF='-'
      else
          UI_TL='┌'; UI_TR='┐'; UI_BL='└'; UI_BR='┘'; UI_H='─'; UI_V='│'
          UI_TICK='✓'; UI_CROSS='✗'; UI_WARN='⚠'; UI_DOT='·'
          UI_BAR_ON='█'; UI_BAR_OFF='░'
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prose
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_repeat N STRING — STRING thirty times. Built by hand because printf's %*s
      # pads by bytes, and a box-drawing character is three of them.
      ui_repeat() {
          local n="$1" s="$2" out=""
          while [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; do
              out="$out$s"
              n=$((n - 1))
          done
          printf '%s' "$out"
      }
      
      # ui_fit TEXT WIDTH — TEXT cut to WIDTH, ending in an ellipsis when it was cut.
      # A value that no longer fits is better shortened than pushed out of its column.
      ui_fit() {
          local text="$1" width="$2"
          [ "$width" -ge 1 ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
          if [ "${#text}" -le "$width" ]; then
              printf '%s' "$text"
          else
              printf '%s…' "${text:0:$((width - 1))}"
          fi
      }
      
      # ui_wrap TEXT INDENT [AVAIL] — greedy word wrap, every line starting at INDENT.
      # Used for the one sentence in a report that explains itself: at 40 columns it
      # is three short lines instead of one that runs off the edge.
      ui_wrap() {
          local text="$1" indent="${2:-0}" avail="${3:-}" pad
          [ -n "$text" ] || return 0
          [ -n "$avail" ] || avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - indent ))
          [ "$avail" -ge 8 ] || avail=8
          pad="$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')"
          printf '%s' "$text" | awk -v w="$avail" -v pad="$pad" '
              {
                  line = ""
                  n = split($0, word, " ")
                  for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                      ww = word[i]
                      if (ww == "") continue
                      # A path is one long word and would run past the edge of a
                      # phone; break it rather than let the line wrap by itself.
                      while (length(ww) > w) {
                          if (line != "") { print pad line; line = "" }
                          print pad substr(ww, 1, w)
                          ww = substr(ww, w + 1)
                      }
                      if (ww == "") continue
                      if (line == "") line = ww
                      else if (length(line) + 1 + length(ww) <= w) line = line " " ww
                      else { print pad line; line = ww }
                  }
                  if (line != "") print pad line
              }
          '
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Blocks
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_heading TEXT — a section title with a rule under it, sized to the window.
      ui_heading() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_rule [INDENT] — a plain separator.
      ui_rule() {
          local indent="${1:-2}" w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '%s%s%s%s\n' "$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')" "$UI_DIM" \
              "$(ui_repeat $((w - indent)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_kv KEY VALUE [KEYWIDTH] — one aligned key and its value.
      ui_kv() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="${3:-10}"
          printf '  %s%-*s%s  %s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$keyw" "$key" "$UI_OFF" "$value"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_line CONTENT INNER — CONTENT padded to INNER and closed off with the
      # right border. CONTENT carries its own leading space, so the row never starts
      # hard against the border.
      ui_panel_line() {
          printf '  %s%s%s%-*s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF" "$2" "$1" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_row KEY VALUE KEYWIDTH INNER — one key/value row.
      # A value too long for the row is wrapped onto its own indented lines rather than
      # cut with an ellipsis: half a property name is worse than two lines.
      ui_panel_row() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="$3" inner="$4" keypad="" line avail
          local -a parts=()
          printf -v keypad '%*s' $((keyw - ${#key})) ''
          avail=$((inner - keyw - 3))
          if [ ${#value} -le "$avail" ]; then
              ui_panel_line " $key$keypad  $value" "$inner"
              return 0
          fi
          # Too wide: wrap it, but keep the first piece on the key's own line so the
          # two still read as one row rather than a label with a paragraph under it.
          while IFS= read -r die; do parts+=("$die"); done < <(ui_wrap "$value" 0 "$avail")
          ui_panel_line " $key$keypad  ${parts[0]:-}" "$inner"
          local i
          for ((i = 1; i < ${#parts[@]}; i++)); do
              line="$(ui_repeat $((keyw + 3)) ' ')${parts[$i]}"
              ui_panel_line "$line" "$inner"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_panel TITLE "KEY|VALUE" ... — a titled box holding aligned pairs.
      #
      # One call rather than open/row/close because the box has to know its widest key
      # before the top border can be drawn, and that is only known once every row has
      # been seen.
      ui_panel() {
          local title="$1"; shift
          local inner keyw=0 row key bar
          local -a keys=() values=()
          # inner is the width between the two vertical borders. Borders plus the two
          # columns of left margin are kept off the right edge, where a terminal likes
          # to wrap on the last character.
          inner=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
          printf '\n'
          for row in "$@"; do
              key="${row%%|*}"
              [ "${#key}" -gt "$keyw" ] && keyw=${#key}
          done
          [ "$keyw" -le 12 ] || keyw=12
          for row in "$@"; do
              keys+=("${row%%|*}")
              values+=("${row#*|}")
          done
          # A title longer than the box would draw a negative rule; shorten it instead.
          title="$(ui_fit "$title" $((inner - 6)))"
          bar=$(ui_repeat $((inner - ${#title} - 3)) "$UI_H")
          printf '  %s%s%s %s%s%s %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_TL" "$UI_H" \
              "$UI_BOLD" "$title" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DIM" "$bar" "$UI_TR$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!keys[@]}"; do
              ui_panel_row "${keys[$i]}" "${values[$i]}" "$keyw" "$inner"
          done
          printf '  %s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_BL" "$(ui_repeat "$inner" "$UI_H")" "$UI_BR$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_meter VALUE MAX [WIDTH] — a filled bar whose colour is the verdict.
      # Green is "this is the one", red is "do not".
      ui_meter() {
          local value="$1" max="$2" width="${3:-10}" on off color
          case "$max" in ''|*[!0-9]*) max=1 ;; esac
          [ "$max" -gt 0 ] || max=1
          on=$((value * width / max))
          [ "$on" -gt "$width" ] && on="$width"
          [ "$on" -lt 0 ] && on=0
          off=$((width - on))
          if [ "$value" -ge 100 ]; then color="$UI_GREEN"
          elif [ "$value" -ge 60 ]; then color="$UI_YELLOW"
          else color="$UI_RED"
          fi
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$color" "$(ui_repeat "$on" "$UI_BAR_ON")" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$off" "$UI_BAR_OFF")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_mark ok|warn|bad|note "TEXT" [INDENT] — a glyph, prose wrapped under it.
      # INDENT (default 2) is the column of the glyph; the text starts two columns
      # later and every wrapped line is drawn at that same column.
      ui_mark() {
          local kind="$1" text="$2" indent="${3:-2}" glyph color line first=1 pad
          case "$kind" in
              ok)   glyph="$UI_TICK";  color="$UI_GREEN" ;;
              warn) glyph="$UI_WARN";  color="$UI_YELLOW" ;;
              bad)  glyph="$UI_CROSS"; color="$UI_RED" ;;
              *)    glyph="$UI_DOT";   color="$UI_DIM" ;;
          esac
          printf -v pad '%*s' $((indent + 2)) ''
          ui_wrap "$text" $((indent + 2)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
              if [ "$first" = 1 ]; then
                  printf '%*s%s%s%s %s\n' "$indent" '' "$color" "$glyph" "$UI_OFF" "${line#"$pad"}"
                  first=0
              else
                  printf '%s\n' "$line"
              fi
          done
      }
      
      # ui_item NUM LABEL [DETAIL] — one row of a menu or an option list.
      #
      #   `   1  Auto Detect   cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G`
      #
      # The number is the accent colour, the label bold and the description dim, so
      # the eye follows the label column and can still find a number at a glance. On a
      # phone the description does not fit beside the label, so it moves to its own
      # indented, wrapped line instead of being cut off at the edge.
      ui_item() {
          local num="$1" label="$2" detail="${3:-}" lw="${4:-${#2}}" cols head line
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          # A label wider than the column (a long section title) widens the column
          # rather than being cut or pushing the description out of line.
          [ "$lw" -ge "${#label}" ] || lw=${#label}
          head="  $(printf '%3s' "$num")  "
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$UI_BLUE" "$head" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_BOLD" "$label"
          if [ -z "$detail" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          # 5 for the number column and its gaps, 2 between label and description.
          if [ $((5 + lw + 2 + ${#detail})) -le "$cols" ]; then
              printf '%s%*s  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_OFF" $((lw - ${#label})) '' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$detail" "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$detail" 7 $((cols - 7)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_split TEXT SEP — TEXT split on SEP, one element per field, in UI_SPLIT.
      ui_split() {
          local item
          UI_SPLIT=()
          while IFS= read -r item; do
              UI_SPLIT+=("$item")
          done < <(printf '%s\n' "$1" | tr "$2" '\n')
      }
      
      # ui_table "COL|COL|COL" "CELL|CELL|CELL" ... — an aligned table, or, when the
      # columns would not fit the window, one block per row.
      #
      # Cutting a table in half is worse than folding it: below the width where the
      # natural columns collide, every row becomes its own two-line entry — the key in
      # bold and the rest joined with a dot — which is the same data, stacked, and
      # still comparable down the page.
      ui_table() {
          local header="$1"; shift
          local avail ncols=0 i k w total cell line first
          local -a rows=("$@") heads=() widths=()
          avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
          ui_split "$header" '|'
          heads=("${UI_SPLIT[@]}")
          ncols=${#heads[@]}
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do widths[$k]=${#heads[$k]}; done
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              for k in "${!UI_SPLIT[@]}"; do
                  [ "$k" -lt "$ncols" ] || continue
                  cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]}"
                  [ "${#cell}" -gt "${widths[$k]}" ] && widths[$k]=${#cell}
              done
          done
          total=$(( 2 * (ncols - 1) ))
          for w in "${widths[@]}"; do total=$(( total + w )); done
      
          if [ "$total" -gt "$avail" ]; then
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
                  printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}" "$UI_OFF"
                  line=""
                  for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                      cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                      [ -n "$cell" ] || continue
                      if [ -z "$line" ]; then line="$cell"; else line="$line $UI_DOT $cell"; fi
                  done
                  [ -n "$line" ] || continue
                  ui_wrap "$line" 4 | while IFS= read -r cell; do
                      printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$cell" "$UI_OFF"
                  done
              done
              return 0
          fi
      
          printf '\n  %s' "$UI_BOLD"
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do
              printf '%-*s' "${widths[$k]}" "${heads[$k]}"
              [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ] && printf '  '
          done
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$total" "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              printf '  %s' "$UI_DIM"
              printf '%-*s' "${widths[0]}" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}"
              printf '%s  ' "$UI_OFF"
              for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                  printf '%-*s' "${widths[$k]}" "${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                  [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ] && printf '  '
              done
              printf '\n'
          done
      }
      
      # ui_title "TEXT" [SUBTITLE] — the first line of a report, ruled to the width.
      ui_title() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
              ui_wrap "$2" 2 $((w - 2)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
              done
          fi
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # menu.sh — the terminal front end
      # =============================================================================
      # The desktop app and this file drive the same tools: the device probes, the
      # addon catalog, the match-property ranking and build.sh's own verbs. The goal
      # is that a phone with a terminal (Termux, ssh, a server) gets the same answers
      # as the window, without a GUI toolkit.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 opens this (when stdin is a terminal)
      #   ./build.sh menu            opens this even when stdin is not a terminal
      #   bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh same thing, standalone
      #
      # Every action shells out to the real entry point — `build.sh build`,
      # `device-probe.sh --write`, `addons.sh set` — so there is exactly one
      # implementation of each step and the menu cannot drift from the app.
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
          . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      # The device-source helpers (device_is_termux, device_local_begin) live with the
      # adb code the probes share. Sourcing it here defines functions only.
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Small things
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MENU_SLEEP="${MENU_SLEEP:-0}"
      
      # A width-aware rule under a section title. Every screen used to draw a fixed
      # 58-character one, which wrapped onto a second line on a phone.
      hr() { ui_rule 2; }
      
      # Read one line. Returns 1 at EOF (piped input, a launcher with no console) so
      # callers can leave the menu instead of looping forever.
      menu_read() {
          local prompt="${1:-} " answer=""
          printf '%s' "$prompt"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              return 1
          fi
          MENU_ANSWER="$answer"
          return 0
      }
      
      # Wait for Enter between screens, unless stdin is not a terminal.
      pause_menu() {
          [ -t 0 ] || return 0
          printf '\n  %s ' "Press Enter to go back"
          read -r _ || true
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # Count the rows config.env has, and how many are switched off.
      cfg_counts() {
          local rows
          rows="$(cfg_rows 2>/dev/null)" || { CFG_ON=0; CFG_OFF=0; return 0; }
          CFG_ON="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 1' | grep -c . || true)"
          CFG_OFF="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 0' | grep -c . || true)"
      }
      
      output_summary() {
          local apks=0 zips=0 zip=""
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR/apks" ] && apks="$(find "$OUT_DIR/apks" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && zips="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          zip="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | sort | head -n1)"
          if [ "$zips" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '%s  (%s APK%s)' "${zip#$ROOT/}" "$apks" "$([ "$apks" = 1 ] || echo s)"
          else
              printf 'nothing built yet'
          fi
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Screen
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The state of the checkout in one box: which phone, how much of config.env is
      # filled in, what the last build left behind.
      menu_header() {
          cfg_counts
          ui_panel "Treble Overlay Creator" \
              "Device|$(cfg_identity)" \
              "config.env|${CFG_ON} set ${UI_DOT} ${CFG_OFF} off" \
              "Output|$(output_summary)"
      }
      
      # 11 is the width of the longest label here, so every description starts in the
      # same column instead of ragging after each label.
      MENU_LW=14
      
      menu_items() {
          ui_item 1 'Build'          'dry run, build, check, doctor, clean' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 2 'config.env'     'browse and edit one key at a time' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 3 'Addons'         'module tweaks: settings and overlay resources' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 4 'Device'         'read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 5 'Auto Detect'    'ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 6 'UDFPS'          'in-display fingerprint geometry' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 7 'Match property' 'which property the submission should match on' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 8 'Files'          'what was built, and where it is' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 9 'Docs'           'the guides in docs/' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item q 'Quit' '' "$MENU_LW"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The menu never re-implements a build step: it runs the entry point with the
      # verb a user would type, so `build.sh doctor` and 1 → 4 are the same command.
      run_entry() {
          ( cd "$ROOT" && bash "$ROOT/build.sh" "$@" )
      }
      
      menu_build() {
          while :; do
              ui_heading 'Build'
              ui_item 1 'Dry run'     'print the resources config.env emits, build nothing' 11
              ui_item 2 'Build'       'build the module (installs tools if needed)' 11
              ui_item 3 'Check'       'validate config.env without building' 11
              ui_item 4 'Doctor'      'check the toolchain, install nothing' 11
              ui_item 5 'Clean'       'remove build output' 11
              ui_item 6 'Clean --all' 'start over for a different device' 11
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 11
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) run_entry --dry-run; pause_menu ;;
                  2) run_entry build; pause_menu ;;
                  3) run_entry check; pause_menu ;;
                  4) run_entry doctor; pause_menu ;;
                  5) run_entry clean; pause_menu ;;
                  6)
                      warn "This removes config.env and the device files too."
                      if confirm "  Start over for a different device? [y/N] " n; then
                          run_entry clean --all
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Files
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_files() {
          local -a table=() f
          ui_heading 'Files'
          ui_panel 'Where things are' \
              "Project|$ROOT" \
              "config.env|$ROOT/config.env" \
              "Build tree|${BUILD_DIR#$ROOT/}"
          echo ""
          if [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$OUT_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                  table+=("$(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)|${f#$ROOT/}")
              done < <(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.apk' \) 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
              if [ "${#table[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
                  ui_table 'Size|Built file' "${table[@]}"
              else
                  info "out/ exists but holds no .zip or .apk yet."
              fi
          else
              info "Nothing built yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
          fi
          pause_menu
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Docs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_docs() {
          local files=() i
          ui_heading 'Docs'
          [ -d "$ROOT/docs" ] || { warn "docs/ is missing from this checkout."; pause_menu; return 0; }
          while IFS= read -r f; do
              files+=("$f")
          done < <(find "$ROOT/docs" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
          for i in "${!files[@]}"; do
              ui_item "$((i + 1))" "$(basename "${files[$i]}")"
          done
          echo ""
          menu_read "  number to read, Enter to go back >" || return 0
          case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
              ''|q) return 0 ;;
              *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number."; return 0 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#files[@]}" ]; then
              warn "No such doc."
              return 0
          fi
          local pick="${files[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]}"
          echo ""
          if [ -t 1 ] && command -v less >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              less -R "$pick"

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The file keeps its shape: these helpers rewrite one line and leave the
      # comments, the section headers and the quoting alone. A key that is commented
      # out shows as `off` and can be switched on by number, which is the whole point
      # of listing it — hunting for the '#' in a 240-line file is where mistakes
      # happen.
      cfg_each_row() { # <section> -> `key<TAB>active<TAB>value` rows of that section
          local section="$1"
          cfg_rows 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' -v s="$section" '$4 == s { print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $5 }'
      }
      
      cfg_section_stats() { # -> `section<TAB>set<TAB>off`, in file order
          cfg_rows 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '
              { if (!($4 in seen)) { seen[$4] = 1; order[n++] = $4 }
                if ($2 == 1) on[$4]++ ; else off[$4]++ }
              END { for (i = 0; i < n; i++) printf "%s\t%d\t%d\n", order[i], on[order[i]], off[order[i]] }
          '
      }
      
      # cfg_list_row NUM KEYW KEY ACTIVE VALUE — one line of a config.env section.
      #
      # A key has three things worth seeing at once: whether it is switched on, its
      # name, and its value. They are three aligned columns when the window has room
      # and two lines when it does not — the state keeps its colour either way, so
      # scanning down the page is still "find the green ones".
      cfg_list_row() {
          local num="$1" keyw="$2" key="$3" active="$4" value="$5"
          local cols state statepad color avail vw vcolor
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          if [ "$active" = "1" ]; then state='on'; color="$UI_GREEN"; else state='off'; color="$UI_DIM"; fi
          printf -v statepad '%*s' $((3 - ${#state})) ''
          # The colour is kept out of the text until printing, so measuring the value
          # never counts escape bytes.
          if [ -z "$value" ]; then value='(empty)'; vcolor="$UI_DIM"; else vcolor="$UI_BOLD"; fi
      
          avail=$((cols - (2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + keyw + 2)))
          if [ "$avail" -ge 8 ]; then
              vw=$((avail - 1))
              printf '  %s%3d%s  %s%-3s%s  %s%-*s%s  %s%s%s\n' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$num" "$UI_OFF" "$color" "$state" "$UI_OFF" \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$keyw" "$key" "$UI_OFF" \
                  "$vcolor" "$(ui_fit "$value" "$vw")" "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '  %s%3d%s  %s%-3s%s  %s%s%s\n' \
              "$UI_DIM" "$num" "$UI_OFF" "$color" "$state" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_BOLD" "$key" "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$value" 10 $((cols - 10)) | while IFS= read -r l; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$vcolor" "$l" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      cfg_edit_value() {
          local key="$1" current value
          current="$(cfg_get "$key")"
          printf '\n  %s = %s\n' "$key" "${current:-<empty>}"
          menu_read "  new value (Enter keeps it, - clears it)" || return 0
          value="$MENU_ANSWER"
          [ -z "$value" ] && { info "Left it alone."; return 0; }
          [ "$value" = "-" ] && value=""
          if cfg_set "$key" "$value"; then
              ok "$key is now ${value:-<empty>}"
          else
              err "Could not write config.env — is it read-only?"
          fi
      }
      
      cfg_section() { # <section title>
          local section="$1" rows=() row i n=0
          while :; do
              rows=()
              while IFS= read -r row; do
                  [ -n "$row" ] && rows+=("$row")
              done < <(cfg_each_row "$section")
      
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${section:-Unsectioned}${NC}"
              hr
              if [ "${#rows[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  info "This section has no keys."
                  pause_menu
                  return 0
              fi
              # One width for the key column, so the values line up down the page.
              local keyw=0
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  local k="${rows[$i]%%$'\t'*}"
                  [ "${#k}" -gt "$keyw" ] && keyw=${#k}
              done
              [ "$keyw" -le 30 ] || keyw=30
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  local key="${rows[$i]%%$'\t'*}" rest="${rows[$i]#*$'\t'}"
                  local active="${rest%%$'\t'*}" value="${rest#*$'\t'}"
                  value="$(printf '%s' "$value" | sed 's/^"\(.*\)"$/\1/')"
                  cfg_list_row "$((i + 1))" "$keyw" "$key" "$active" "$value"
              done
              echo ""
              ui_mark note "number = edit ${UI_DOT} d<number> = switch off ${UI_DOT} e<number> = switch on ${UI_DOT} 0 = back"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  d*|D*)
                      i="${MENU_ANSWER#?}"
                      case "$i" in ''|*[!0-9]*) warn "d needs a number, like d3."; continue ;; esac
                      if [ "$i" -lt 1 ] || [ "$i" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then warn "No such key."; continue; fi
                      key="${rows[$((i - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      if cfg_set_active "$key" 0; then ok "$key switched off"; else err "Could not write config.env"; fi
                      ;;
                  e*|E*)
                      i="${MENU_ANSWER#?}"
                      case "$i" in ''|*[!0-9]*) warn "e needs a number, like e3."; continue ;; esac
                      if [ "$i" -lt 1 ] || [ "$i" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then warn "No such key."; continue; fi
                      key="${rows[$((i - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      if cfg_set_active "$key" 1; then ok "$key switched on"; else err "Could not write config.env"; fi
                      ;;
                  *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number." ;;
                  *)
                      if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then
                          warn "No such key."
                          continue
                      fi
                      cfg_edit_value "${rows[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      menu_config() {
          local sections=() i lw name on off
          while :; do
              sections=()
              local -a counts=()
              while IFS=$'\t' read -r name on off; do
                  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
                  sections+=("$name")
                  counts+=("$(printf '%s set %s %s off' "$on" "$UI_DOT" "$off")")
              done < <(cfg_section_stats 2>/dev/null)

                  "$(json_escape "${c_why[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${c_risk[$i]}")"
              sep=","
          done
          printf '],"rejected":['
          sep=""
          for i in "${!r_prop[@]}"; do

                  "$(json_escape "${r_reason[$i]}")"
              sep=","
          done
          printf ']}\n'
      }
      
      # Emit one why/risk string as one bullet per fact.
      #
      # Both are a list joined with " · " — "read from /system · zygote can read it ·
      # holds the codename" — which wrapped as prose is the wall of text this report
      # used to be. Split, each fact is a line the eye can check off.
      emit_facts() {
          local kind="$1" indent="$2" rest="$3" fact
          while [ -n "$rest" ]; do
              case "$rest" in
                  *" · "*) fact="${rest%% · *}"; rest="${rest#* · }" ;;
                  *) fact="$rest"; rest="" ;;
              esac
              [ -n "$fact" ] && ui_mark "$kind" "$fact" "$indent"
          done
      }
      
      # emit_candidate INDEX RANK DETAIL — one ranked property.
      #
      # The score, the property and its facts, stacked: a fixed table cannot hold a
      # 24-character property name and a 26-character value on a phone, and cutting
      # either is worse than reading down.
      emit_candidate() {
          local i="$1" n="$2" detail="$3" line w
          w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%2d%s  %s %s%3d%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$n" "$UI_OFF" \
              "$(ui_meter "${c_score[$i]:-0}" 120 10)" "$UI_BOLD" "${c_score[$i]:-0}" "$UI_OFF"
          line="${c_prop[$i]} = ${c_val[$i]}"
          if [ $(( ${#line} + 4 )) -le "$w" ]; then
              printf '    %s%s%s = %s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${c_prop[$i]}" "$UI_OFF" "${c_val[$i]}"
          else
              printf '    %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${c_prop[$i]}" "$UI_OFF"
              ui_wrap "${c_val[$i]}" 6 | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '      %s\n' "$line"
              done
          fi
          printf '    %s%s %s %s %s %s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "${c_zone[$i]}" "$UI_DOT" \
              "${c_label[$i]:-not reported}" "$UI_DOT" "trust ${c_trust[$i]:-unknown}" "$UI_OFF"
          [ "$detail" = "1" ] || return 0
          emit_facts note 6 "${c_why[$i]}"
          [ -n "${c_risk[$i]}" ] && emit_facts warn 6 "${c_risk[$i]}"
          return 0
      }
      
      emit_human() {

          saved_prop="$(cfg_get HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP)"
          saved_value="$(cfg_get HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE)"
      
          local -a panel=()

          if [ -n "$codename" ]; then

          if [ -n "$saved_prop" ] || [ -n "$saved_value" ]; then

import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { chmodSync, existsSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
const script = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'match-prop.sh');

function dump(pairs) {
  return Object.entries(pairs)
    .map(([k, v]) => `[${k}]: [${v}]`)
    .join('\n') + '\n';
}

// `getprop -Z` prints the same shape, with the SELinux label as the value.
function areas(pairs) {
  return dump(
    Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(pairs).map(([k, v]) => [k, `u:object_r:${v}:s0`]))
  );
}

function dir(files) {
  const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'match-prop-'));
  for (const [name, body] of Object.entries(files)) {
    writeFileSync(join(d, name), body);
  }
  return d;
}

// `getprop -Z` is missing on old Android, so --labels is optional: a test with
// only a values dump is the no-labels case on purpose.
function run(d, extra = []) {
  const args = [script, '--values', join(d, 'values')];
  if (existsSync(join(d, 'labels'))) args.push('--labels', join(d, 'labels'));
  args.push('--json', ...extra);
  const out = spawnSync('bash', args, {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    env: { ...process.env, CFG_FILE: join(d, 'config.env'), TERM: 'dumb' },
  });
  assert.equal(out.stderr.replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, ''), '', `stderr: ${out.stderr}`);

The wrap indent is 4, not aligned under the value. Better: wrap with hanging indent 6 (prop column) so continuation lines are clearly part of the row:

> if [ $(( ${#c_prop[$i]} + 6 )) -Continue: fix the narrow-tail wrap so continuation lines hang under the value instead of looking like a new row.
> 
> Implementation: in the narrow branch, if the whole `prop = value` fits, one line. Else if prop fits on its own line (`${#prop} + 2 <= cols-4`), print prop with trailing `=`, then wrap value at indent 6. Else wrap the whole line at indent 4 (rare: property longer than terminal).

> Bug: at 80, the "Features" On row is truncated: `│ On   UDFPS · AOD · Doze · VoLTE                                         │` — one column short (the row isn't padded to inner correctly). Why? The value length: "UDFPS · AOD · Doze · VoLTE" = 24 chars. avail = inner - keyw - 3 = 76 - 4 - 3 = 69... wait keyw is max key len across the panel = "Off"=3, "On"=2 → keyw=3. avail = 76-3-3 = 70. 24 <= 70 so one-line branch: ui_panel_line " On   UDFPS..." with inner=76.
> 
> Hmm but the padding is off by one — because `ui_panel_line` uses `%-*s` on the CONTENT which is measured in bytes, and the `·` characters are 3 bytes each! `printf '%-*s'` pads by bytes, so content with two `·` (2 extra bytes each) is 24 chars but 28 bytes → 76-28 = 48 spaces, total visual width 72 + 2 borders... The row ends 2 columns early per `·`. Exactly: 2 `·` → short by 4? Output shows the closing `│` 2 early... there are 2 `·` in "On" row → short by 4? Let's count visually: hard.
> 
> Fix: ui_panel_line must pad by characters, not bytes. Compute pad = inner - #content (characters) and append spaces manually instead of %-*s.
> 
> Fix in ui_panel_line:
> 
> ```bash
> ui_panel_line() {
>     local content="$1" inner="$2" pad=""
>     [ "${#content}" -le "$inner" ] && printf -v pad '%*s' $((inner - ${#content})) ''
>     printf '  %s%s%s%s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF" "$content" "$pad" "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V$UI_OFF"
> }
> ```
> Hmm existing format: `printf '  %s%s%s%-*s%s%s%s\n' dim V off inner content dim V off`. Replace with pad approach.
> 
> Note: `${#content}` counts characters in bash when locale is UTF-8 (it does for ${#var}). Empirically, ${#} gives characters in UTF-8 locale, bytes in C locale. Given LANG may be unset in some environments (C locale in Termux? usually en_US.UTF-8 / C.UTF-8). The match-prop code already uses ${#} for widths everywhere, so consistent.

- path: stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh

          return 0

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Doctor — verify the toolchain actually works on THIS platform
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      check_runs() {
          local label="$1"; shift
          local out rc=0
          out=$("$@" 2>&1) || rc=$?
          if printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qiE 'cannot execute binary file|exec format error|not a valid win32|bad cpu type'; then
              printf '    %-22s ✗ %s\n' "$label" "$(printf '%s' "$out" | head -1 | cut -c1-70)"
              return 1
          fi
          printf '    %-22s ✓ ran\n' "$label"
          if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
              printf '    %-22s   (exit %s — normal for tools without arguments)\n' "" "$rc"
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      run_doctor() {
          local problems=0 t cand kind usable bad
      
          if $IS_WINDOWS; then
              banner "Toolchain check  (build.cmd doctor)"
          else
              banner "Toolchain check  (build.sh doctor)"
          fi
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Environment${NC}"
          printf '    %-12s %s\n' "Shell:" "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)  (MSYSTEM=${MSYSTEM:-unset})"
          if $IS_WINDOWS; then
              printf '    %-12s %s\n' "Platform:" "Windows (Git Bash / MSYS2)"
          elif $IS_TERMUX; then
              printf '    %-12s %s\n' "Platform:" "Android / Termux"
          elif $IS_WSL; then
              printf '    %-12s %s\n' "Platform:" "WSL (Linux)"
          else
              printf '    %-12s %s\n' "Platform:" "Linux"
          fi
          printf '    %-12s %s\n' "Project:" "$ROOT"
          printf '    %-12s %s\n' "Tools dir:" "$TOOLS_DIR"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Tools${NC}"
      
          for t in aapt2 zipalign apksigner; do
              usable=""; bad=""
              while IFS= read -r cand; do
                  [ -n "$cand" ] || continue
                  kind=$(classify_binary "$cand")
                  if kind_usable "$kind"; then
                      [ -z "$usable" ] && usable="$cand"
                  else
                      bad="${bad}${cand} [$(kind_label "$kind")] "
                  fi
              done <<< "$(tool_candidates "$t")"
      
              if [ -n "$usable" ]; then
                  printf '    %-12s ✓ %s  [%s]\n' "$t" "$usable" "$(kind_label "$(classify_binary "$usable")")"
                  if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
                      printf '    %-12s   ⚠ shadows it, cannot run here: %s\n' "" "$bad"
                      problems=$((problems + 1))
                  fi
              elif [ -n "$bad" ]; then
                  printf '    %-12s ✗ only unusable copies: %s\n' "$t" "$bad"
                  problems=$((problems + 1))
              elif [ "$t" = "zipalign" ] && $IS_TERMUX; then
                  printf '    %-12s – missing; install with: pkg install aapt\n' "$t"
              else
                  printf '    %-12s ✗ not found\n' "$t"
                  problems=$((problems + 1))
              fi
          done
      
          local res
          if res=$(framework_res_path); then
              printf '    %-12s ✓ %s  [%s]\n' "resources" "$res" "$(kind_label "$(classify_binary "$res")")"
          else
              printf '    %-12s ✗ not found — build.sh will download it\n' "resources"
              problems=$((problems + 1))
          fi
      
          local jpath
          jpath=$(command -v java 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ -n "$jpath" ]; then
              printf '    %-12s ✓ %s  [%s]\n' "java" "$jpath" "$(kind_label "$(classify_binary "$jpath")")"
          else
              printf '    %-12s ✗ not found — apksigner will fail\n' "java"
              problems=$((problems + 1))
          fi
      
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Do they actually run here?${NC}"
          local rbin
          for t in aapt2 zipalign apksigner; do
              rbin=$(tool_path "$t") || continue
              case "$t" in
                  aapt2)     check_runs "$t version" "$rbin" version || problems=$((problems + 1)) ;;
                  zipalign)  check_runs "$t" "$rbin" || problems=$((problems + 1)) ;;
                  apksigner) check_runs "$t --version" "$rbin" --version || problems=$((problems + 1)) ;;
              esac
          done
      
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Contamination check${NC}"
          local found_foreign=false f fkind
          for f in "$TOOLS_DIR"/*; do
              [ -f "$f" ] || continue
              fkind=$(classify_binary "$f")
              if kind_foreign "$fkind"; then
                  printf '    ⚠ %s is a %s — cannot run here\n' "${f#"$TOOLS_DIR"/}" "$(kind_label "$fkind")"
                  printf '      remove it:  rm -f "%s"\n' "$f"
                  found_foreign=true
              fi
          done
          while IFS= read -r cand; do
              case "$cand" in
                  //wsl\$/*|*wsl.localhost*)
                      printf '    ⚠ PATH contains a WSL path: %s\n' "$cand"
                      found_foreign=true ;;
              esac
          done <<< "$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n')"
          if [ "$found_foreign" = "false" ]; then
              ok "No other-platform binaries in the toolchain, no WSL paths on PATH"
          else
              problems=$((problems + 1))
          fi
      
          echo ""
          if [ "$problems" -eq 0 ]; then
              ok "Toolchain is correct for this platform — ./build.sh will work."
              echo ""
              return 0
          fi
          err "${problems} problem(s) found."
          if $IS_WINDOWS; then
              echo "    Fix:      build.cmd          (downloads the Windows build-tools)"
              echo "    Then:     build.cmd doctor"
          else
              echo "    Fix:      ./build.sh setup"
              echo "    Or:       $(package_install_hint)"
          fi
          echo ""
          return 1
      }

              "$(json_escape "$codename")" "$(json_escape "$codename_prop")" \
              "$(json_escape "$module_prop")" "$confidence"
          sep=""
          for i in "${sorted[@]}"; do
              printf '%s{"prop":"%s","value":"%s","zone":"%s","score":%d,"why":"%s"}' \
                  "$sep" "$(json_escape "${c_prop[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${c_val[$i]}")" \
                  "${c_zone[$i]}" "${c_score[$i]}" "$(json_escape "${c_why[$i]}")"
              sep=","
          done
          printf '],"rejected":['
          sep=""
          for i in "${!r_prop[@]}"; do
              printf '%s{"prop":"%s","value":"%s","reason":"%s"}' \
                  "$sep" "$(json_escape "${r_prop[$i]}")" "$(json_escape "${r_val[$i]}")" \
                  "$(json_escape "${r_reason[$i]}")"
              sep=","
          done
          printf ']}\n'
      }
      
      emit_human() {
          local i n=0
          printf '\n  Device — what the overlay will claim\n\n'
          printf '  %-13s %-24s %s\n' 'Manufacturer' "${manufacturer:-not found}" "$manufacturer_prop"
          printf '  %-13s %-24s %s\n' 'Model' "${model:-not found}" "$model_prop"
          printf '  %-13s %-24s %s\n' 'Codename' "${codename:-not found}" "$codename_prop"
          if [ -n "$module_prop" ]; then
              printf '\n  Module condition (the overlay only loads where this is true)\n'
              printf '    DEVICE_PROP_NAME="%s"\n    DEVICE_PROP_VALUE="true"\n' "$module_prop"
          fi
      
          if [ "${#sorted[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '\n  Codename candidates\n\n'
              printf '     %-29s %-12s %-10s %s\n' 'property' 'value' 'zone' 'score'
              for i in "${sorted[@]}"; do
                  n=$((n + 1))
                  printf '  %2d %-29s %-12s %-10s %s\n' "$n" "${c_prop[$i]}" "${c_val[$i]}" "${c_zone[$i]}" "${c_score[$i]}"
                  printf '     · %s\n' "${c_why[$i]}"
              done
          else
              printf '\n  No property on this phone names the device.\n'
          fi
      
          if [ "${#r_prop[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '\n  Ruled out\n\n'
              for i in "${!r_prop[@]}"; do
                  printf '    %-29s %-18s %s\n' "${r_prop[$i]}" "${r_val[$i]}" "${r_reason[$i]}"
              done
          fi
      
          printf '\n  Confidence: %s\n' "$confidence"
          case "$confidence" in
              high)
                  printf '    %s reads the codename from the partition a GSI leaves alone.\n' "$codename_prop"
                  ;;
              medium)
                  printf '    The codename came from a partition a GSI replaces, so it is right\n'
                  printf '    for the ROM on the phone now, not necessarily for the GSI.\n'
                  ;;
              *)
                  printf '    Nothing usable was found — set DEVICE_CODENAME by hand in config.env,\n'
                  printf '    or point this at a different phone.\n'
                  ;;
          esac
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Writing it
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # DEVICE_PROP_NAME is only touched when it is empty or already in the shape this
      # writes: a hand-written condition is a decision, not a leftover.
      write_device() {
          local current_prop current_value
          cfg_set DEVICE_MANUFACTURER "$manufacturer" || return 1
          cfg_set DEVICE_MODEL "$model" || return 1
          cfg_set DEVICE_CODENAME "$codename" || return 1
          current_prop="$(cfg_get DEVICE_PROP_NAME)"
          current_value="$(cfg_get DEVICE_PROP_VALUE)"
          case "$current_prop" in
              ''|persist.sys.overlay.*|\<*)
                  cfg_set DEVICE_PROP_NAME "$module_prop" || return 1
                  ;;
              *)
                  printf '  Left DEVICE_PROP_NAME alone: it is set to %s, not the default shape.\n' "$current_prop"
                  ;;
          esac
          [ -n "$current_value" ] || cfg_set DEVICE_PROP_VALUE "true"
          printf '\n  Written to config.env:\n'
          printf '    DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="%s"\n    DEVICE_MODEL="%s"\n    DEVICE_CODENAME="%s"\n' \
              "$manufacturer" "$model" "$codename"
          printf '  Build now (./build.sh, or 1 in the menu) to pick it up.\n\n'
      }
      
      main() {
          if [ -n "$values_file" ]; then
              collect_from_files
          else
              collect_from_device
          fi
          detect
      
          if [ "$want_json" = "1" ]; then
              emit_json
              return 0
          fi
          emit_human
      
          if [ -z "$codename" ]; then
              return 1
          fi
      
          if [ "$want_write" = "1" ]; then
              write_device || return 1
              return 0
          fi
      
          [ -t 0 ] || return 0
          printf '  Write these to config.env? [Y/n] '
          local reply=""
          read -r reply || reply=""
          case "$reply" in
              ''|y|Y|yes|YES) write_device || return 1 ;;
              *) printf '  Left config.env alone.\n\n' ;;
          esac
          return 0
      }
      
      main

- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      # pads by bytes, and a box-drawing character is three of them.
      ui_repeat() {
          local n="$1" s="$2" out=""
          while [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; do
              out="$out$s"
              n=$((n - 1))
          done
          printf '%s' "$out"
      }
      
      # ui_fit TEXT WIDTH — TEXT cut to WIDTH, ending in an ellipsis when it was cut.
      # A value that no longer fits is better shortened than pushed out of its column.
      ui_fit() {
          local text="$1" width="$2"
          [ "$width" -ge 1 ] || { printf ''; return 0; }
          if [ "${#text}" -le "$width" ]; then
              printf '%s' "$text"
          else
              printf '%s…' "${text:0:$((width - 1))}"
          fi
      }
      
      # ui_wrap TEXT INDENT [AVAIL] — greedy word wrap, every line starting at INDENT.
      # Used for the one sentence in a report that explains itself: at 40 columns it
      # is three short lines instead of one that runs off the edge.
      ui_wrap() {
          local text="$1" indent="${2:-0}" avail="${3:-}" pad
          [ -n "$text" ] || return 0
          [ -n "$avail" ] || avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - indent ))
          [ "$avail" -ge 8 ] || avail=8
          pad="$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')"
          printf '%s' "$text" | awk -v w="$avail" -v pad="$pad" '
              {
                  line = ""
                  n = split($0, word, " ")
                  for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                      ww = word[i]
                      if (ww == "") continue
                      # A path is one long word and would run past the edge of a
                      # phone; break it rather than let the line wrap by itself, and
                      # break after a separator when there is one, so the pieces stay
                      # readable (persist.sys.overlay. / zephyr, not zephy / r).
                      while (length(ww) > w) {
                          if (line != "") { print pad line; line = "" }
                          cut = w
                          for (j = w; j > w / 2; j--) {
                              ch = substr(ww, j, 1)
                              if (ch == "/" || ch == "." || ch == "-" || ch == "_" || ch == "=" || ch == ",") { cut = j; break }
                          }
                          print pad substr(ww, 1, cut)
                          ww = substr(ww, cut + 1)
                      }
                      if (ww == "") continue
                      if (line == "") line = ww
                      else if (length(line) + 1 + length(ww) <= w) line = line " " ww
                      else { print pad line; line = ww }
                  }
                  if (line != "") print pad line
              }
          '
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Blocks
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_heading TEXT — a section title with a rule under it, sized to the window.
      ui_heading() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_rule [INDENT] — a plain separator.
      ui_rule() {
          local indent="${1:-2}" w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '%s%s%s%s\n' "$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')" "$UI_DIM" \
              "$(ui_repeat $((w - indent)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_kv KEY VALUE [KEYWIDTH] — one aligned key and its value.
      ui_kv() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="${3:-10}"
          printf '  %s%s%s  %s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_pad "$key" "$keyw")" "$UI_OFF" "$value"
      }
      
      # ui_pad TEXT WIDTH — TEXT followed by spaces up to WIDTH characters.
      #
      # printf's %-*s pads by bytes, so one `·` (three bytes) would leave a row three
      # columns short and the right border would step in once per glyph. Everything a
      # user typed — a model name, a path, a dotted list — goes through here.
      ui_pad() {
          local text="$1" width="$2" pad=""
          [ "${#text}" -lt "$width" ] && printf -v pad '%*s' $((width - ${#text})) ''
          printf '%s%s' "$text" "$pad"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_line CONTENT INNER — CONTENT padded to INNER and closed off with the
      # right border. CONTENT carries its own leading space, so the row never starts
      # hard against the border.
      ui_panel_line() {
          local content="$1" inner="$2" pad=""
          [ "${#content}" -lt "$inner" ] && printf -v pad '%*s' $((inner - ${#content})) ''
          printf '  %s%s%s%s%s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF" "$content" "$pad" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_row KEY VALUE KEYWIDTH INNER — one key/value row.
      # A value too long for the row is wrapped onto its own indented lines rather than
      # cut with an ellipsis: half a property name is worse than two lines.
      ui_panel_row() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="$3" inner="$4" keypad="" line avail
          local -a parts=()
          printf -v keypad '%*s' $((keyw - ${#key})) ''
          avail=$((inner - keyw - 3))
          if [ ${#value} -le "$avail" ]; then
              ui_panel_line " $key$keypad  $value" "$inner"
              return 0
          fi
          # Too wide: wrap it, but keep the first piece on the key's own line so the
          # two still read as one row rather than a label with a paragraph under it.
          while IFS= read -r die; do parts+=("$die"); done < <(ui_wrap "$value" 0 "$avail")
          ui_panel_line " $key$keypad  ${parts[0]:-}" "$inner"
          local i
          for ((i = 1; i < ${#parts[@]}; i++)); do
              line="$(ui_repeat $((keyw + 3)) ' ')${parts[$i]}"
              ui_panel_line "$line" "$inner"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_panel TITLE "KEY|VALUE" ... — a titled box holding aligned pairs.
      #
      # One call rather than open/row/close because the box has to know its widest key
      # before the top border can be drawn, and that is only known once every row has
      # been seen.
      ui_panel() {
          local title="$1"; shift
          local inner keyw=0 row key bar
          local -a keys=() values=()
          # inner is the width between the two vertical borders. Borders plus the two
          # columns of left margin are kept off the right edge, where a terminal likes
          # to wrap on the last character.
          inner=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
          printf '\n'
          for row in "$@"; do
              key="${row%%|*}"
              [ "${#key}" -gt "$keyw" ] && keyw=${#key}
          done
          [ "$keyw" -le 12 ] || keyw=12
          for row in "$@"; do
              keys+=("${row%%|*}")
              values+=("${row#*|}")
          done
          # A title longer than the box would draw a negative rule; shorten it instead.
          title="$(ui_fit "$title" $((inner - 6)))"
          bar=$(ui_repeat $((inner - ${#title} - 3)) "$UI_H")
          printf '  %s%s%s %s%s%s %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_TL" "$UI_H" \
              "$UI_BOLD" "$title" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DIM" "$bar" "$UI_TR$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!keys[@]}"; do
              ui_panel_row "${keys[$i]}" "${values[$i]}" "$keyw" "$inner"
          done
          printf '  %s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_BL" "$(ui_repeat "$inner" "$UI_H")" "$UI_BR$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_meter VALUE MAX [WIDTH] — a filled bar whose colour is the verdict.
      # Green is "this is the one", red is "do not".
      ui_meter() {
          local value="$1" max="$2" width="${3:-10}" on off color
          case "$max" in ''|*[!0-9]*) max=1 ;; esac
          [ "$max" -gt 0 ] || max=1
          on=$((value * width / max))
          [ "$on" -gt "$width" ] && on="$width"
          [ "$on" -lt 0 ] && on=0
          off=$((width - on))
          if [ "$value" -ge 100 ]; then color="$UI_GREEN"
          elif [ "$value" -ge 60 ]; then color="$UI_YELLOW"
          else color="$UI_RED"
          fi
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$color" "$(ui_repeat "$on" "$UI_BAR_ON")" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$off" "$UI_BAR_OFF")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_mark ok|warn|bad|note "TEXT" [INDENT] — a glyph, prose wrapped under it.
      # INDENT (default 2) is the column of the glyph; the text starts two columns
      # later and every wrapped line is drawn at that same column.
      ui_mark() {
          local kind="$1" text="$2" indent="${3:-2}" glyph color line first=1 pad
          case "$kind" in
              ok)   glyph="$UI_TICK";  color="$UI_GREEN" ;;
              warn) glyph="$UI_WARN";  color="$UI_YELLOW" ;;
              bad)  glyph="$UI_CROSS"; color="$UI_RED" ;;
              *)    glyph="$UI_DOT";   color="$UI_DIM" ;;
          esac
          printf -v pad '%*s' $((indent + 2)) ''
          ui_wrap "$text" $((indent + 2)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
              if [ "$first" = 1 ]; then
                  printf '%*s%s%s%s %s\n' "$indent" '' "$color" "$glyph" "$UI_OFF" "${line#"$pad"}"
                  first=0
              else
                  printf '%s\n' "$line"
              fi
          done
      }
      
      # ui_item NUM LABEL [DETAIL] — one row of a menu or an option list.
      #
      #   `   1  Auto Detect   cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G`
      #
      # The number is the accent colour, the label bold and the description dim, so
      # the eye follows the label column and can still find a number at a glance. On a
      # phone the description does not fit beside the label, so it moves to its own
      # indented, wrapped line instead of being cut off at the edge.
      ui_item() {
          local num="$1" label="$2" detail="${3:-}" lw="${4:-${#2}}" cols head line
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          # A label wider than the column (a long section title) widens the column
          # rather than being cut or pushing the description out of line.
          [ "$lw" -ge "${#label}" ] || lw=${#label}
          head="  $(printf '%3s' "$num")  "
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$UI_BLUE" "$head" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_BOLD" "$label"
          if [ -z "$detail" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          # 5 for the number column and its gaps, 2 between label and description.
          if [ $((5 + lw + 2 + ${#detail})) -le "$cols" ]; then
              printf '%s%*s  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_OFF" $((lw - ${#label})) '' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$detail" "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$detail" 7 $((cols - 7)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_trust_color high|medium|low — green for an answer, red for a gamble.
      # The trust word is the one thing a reader scans a ranked list for, so it is
      # coloured rather than left in the same grey as the rest of the meta line.
      ui_trust_color() {
          case "${1:-}" in
              high) printf '%s' "$UI_GREEN" ;;
              medium) printf '%s' "$UI_YELLOW" ;;
              low|*) printf '%s' "$UI_RED" ;;
          esac
      }

      # ui_split TEXT SEP — TEXT split on SEP, one element per field, in UI_SPLIT.
      ui_split() {
          local item
          UI_SPLIT=()
          while IFS= read -r item; do
              UI_SPLIT+=("$item")
          done < <(printf '%s\n' "$1" | tr "$2" '\n')
      }
      
      # ui_table "COL|COL|COL" "CELL|CELL|CELL" ... — an aligned table, or, when the
      # columns would not fit the window, one block per row.
      #
      # Cutting a table in half is worse than folding it: below the width where the
      # natural columns collide, every row becomes its own two-line entry — the key in
      # bold and the rest joined with a dot — which is the same data, stacked, and
      # still comparable down the page.
      ui_table() {
          local header="$1"; shift
          local avail ncols=0 i k w total cell line first
          local -a rows=("$@") heads=() widths=()
          avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
          ui_split "$header" '|'
          heads=("${UI_SPLIT[@]}")
          ncols=${#heads[@]}
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do widths[$k]=${#heads[$k]}; done
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              for k in "${!UI_SPLIT[@]}"; do
                  [ "$k" -lt "$ncols" ] || continue
                  cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]}"
                  [ "${#cell}" -gt "${widths[$k]}" ] && widths[$k]=${#cell}
              done
          done
          total=$(( 2 * (ncols - 1) ))
          for w in "${widths[@]}"; do total=$(( total + w )); done
      
          if [ "$total" -gt "$avail" ]; then
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
                  printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}" "$UI_OFF"
                  line=""
                  for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                      cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                      [ -n "$cell" ] || continue
                      if [ -z "$line" ]; then line="$cell"; else line="$line $UI_DOT $cell"; fi
                  done
                  [ -n "$line" ] || continue
                  ui_wrap "$line" 4 | while IFS= read -r cell; do
                      printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$cell" "$UI_OFF"
                  done
              done
              return 0
          fi
      
          printf '\n  %s' "$UI_BOLD"
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do
              printf '%-*s' "${widths[$k]}" "${heads[$k]}"
              [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ] && printf '  '
          done
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$total" "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              printf '  %s' "$UI_DIM"
              printf '%-*s' "${widths[0]}" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}"
              printf '%s  ' "$UI_OFF"
              for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                  printf '%-*s' "${widths[$k]}" "${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                  [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ] && printf '  '
              done
              printf '\n'
          done
      }
      
      # ui_title "TEXT" [SUBTITLE] — the first line of a report, ruled to the width.
      ui_title() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
              ui_wrap "$2" 2 $((w - 2)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
              done
          fi
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# ui.sh — how a terminal report is drawn
# =============================================================================
# Sourced by common.sh (so the menu and build.sh get it) and by the probes that
# print a report. Never run directly.
#
# The reports used to be fixed-width printf columns, which is the right shape on
# a 100-column desktop window and unreadable on a phone: 58-column rules wrapped
# mid-border, and a line of prose about a property ran off the edge and came
# back as a second, unrelated-looking line. Everything here is measured against
# the real window instead, and long prose is wrapped with a hanging indent so a
# wrapped paragraph still looks like one item.
#
# Three switches, all optional:
#   UI_COLOR=always|never|auto   auto (the default) is "a terminal is attached"
#   UI_COLS=N                    the width to draw for, when there is no tty
#   UI_ASCII=1                   ASCII borders and glyphs, for a font or a
#                                codepage that cannot show ─ │ · ⚠
# Colour is off when stdout is not a terminal, so `./build.sh | tee log` and the
# JSON probes stay clean, and NO_COLOR is respected.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Width
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A phone terminal is 40-50 columns, a desktop window is often 200. Below 40
# nothing lines up; above 100 an eye loses the start of the line on the way
# back, so the drawing width is clamped and the spare columns stay empty.
ui_cols() {
    local c="${UI_COLS:-}"
    [ -n "$c" ] || c="${COLUMNS:-}"
    if [ -z "$c" ] && [ -t 1 ] && command -v tput >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        c="$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    case "$c" in ''|*[!0-9]*) c=80 ;; esac
    [ "$c" -ge 40 ] || c=40
    [ "$c" -le 100 ] || c=100
    printf '%s' "$c"
}

}

    local v="$1"
    case "$v" in

        \'*\') v="${v#\'}"; v="${v%\'}" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s' "$v"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# adb-device.sh — which connected phone a probe talks to
# =============================================================================
# Sourced by device-probe.sh and udfps-probe.sh. Both used to carry the same
# rule ("exactly one device, or stop"), which stops being useful the moment a
# second phone is on the desk.
#
#   adb_pick_device ADB SERIAL PROGRAM
#
# ADB is the adb binary to run, SERIAL is what --device said ("" for automatic),
# PROGRAM names the script in the messages. On success DEVICE_SERIAL holds the
# serial to pass to `adb -s`; on failure the reason has already been printed.
#
# The state matters. adb can see a phone it cannot talk to (unauthorized,
# offline, no permissions), and each of those has its own fix — telling the user
# to plug the phone in is wrong advice for all three.
#
# Detection is the fragile part, so it is hardened against what adb actually
# does rather than what its manual says:
#
#   * `adb devices` is a stream, not a table. A daemon start, a version
#     mismatch, or a "no permissions" line shares it with the devices, so only
#     lines whose second column is a real state are read as devices.
#   * the listing can lie. It is a snapshot, so the chosen serial is confirmed
#     with `get-state` before anything is run against it.
#   * a wedged server hangs instead of failing. Every adb call here is bounded,
#     and a timeout says "adb kill-server" instead of hanging the probe.
#   * the first call after the server restarts can come back with no header at
#     all. That is retried; a genuinely empty list is not.
#   * a phone that is still "connecting" (wireless adb, or just plugged in)
#     becomes ready in a second or two, so it is waited for briefly.
#   * a serial can be listed twice, and wireless transports look like
#     `192.168.1.5:5555`; duplicates are dropped and the transport is labelled.
# =============================================================================

# The states adb puts in the second column of `devices`, space-padded so a
# value can be tested with `index(states, " " $2 " ")`.
ADB_DEVICE_STATES=" device offline unauthorized bootloader recovery sideload rescue host connecting no "

      adb_device_advice() {

              $2 == "unauthorized" { print "  " $1 ": unlock the phone and accept the USB debugging prompt" }
              $2 == "offline"      { print "  " $1 ": offline — unplug and replug it, or run adb kill-server" }
              $2 == "no"           { print "  " $1 ": no permissions — Linux needs a udev rule, Windows a driver" }
              $2 == "connecting"   { print "  " $1 ": still connecting — wait a moment and run it again" }
              $2 == "bootloader"   { print "  " $1 ": in the bootloader — boot Android to read the running ROM" }
              $2 == "recovery"     { print "  " $1 ": in recovery — adb works there, but dumpsys and getprop of the ROM do not" }
              $2 == "sideload"     { print "  " $1 ": sideload mode — reboot to Android first" }
