```
notes=()
warnings=()

# Candidates, kept parallel so the report can be sorted after the fact.
c_kind=(); c_source=(); c_label=(); c_x=(); c_y=(); c_r=()
c_conf=(); c_score=(); c_detail=()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# aapt2
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The APK is the authority: an overlay that is enabled and maps the array is
# what the framework is actually serving. aapt2 is already downloaded for the
# build, so reuse that copy instead of asking for a second install.
resolve_aapt2() {
    [ -n "$aapt2" ] && return 0
    local candidate
    for candidate in "$ROOT/stuff/tools/aapt2" "$ROOT/stuff/tools/aapt2.exe"; do
        [ -x "$candidate" ] && { aapt2="$candidate"; return 0; }
    done
    candidate="$(command -v aapt2 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ -n "$candidate" ] && { aapt2="$candidate"; return 0; }
    return 1
}

# Prints "x y r" for array/config_udfps_sensor_props, or nothing.
apk_udfps() {
    [ -n "$aapt2" ] || return 1
    "$aapt2" dump resources "$(winpath "$1")" 2>/dev/null | awk '
        /array\/config_udfps_sensor_props/ { found = 1; next }
        found && /\[/ {
            gsub(/[^0-9, ]/, "")
            n = split($0, a, ",")
            if (n >= 3) { gsub(/ /, "", a[1]); gsub(/ /, "", a[2]); gsub(/ /, "", a[3]); print a[1], a[2], a[3] }
            exit
        }'
}

# Prints the sensor-list entry ("0:2:15") for array/config_biometric_sensors.
apk_biometric() {
    [ -n "$aapt2" ] || return 1
    "$aapt2" dump resources "$(winpath "$1")" 2>/dev/null | awk '
        /array\/config_biometric_sensors/ { found = 1; next }
        found && /\[/ { gsub(/[^0-9:;]/, ""); print; exit }'
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Candidate bookkeeping
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
is_uint() { case "${1:-}" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; *) return 0 ;; esac; }

# add_candidate kind source label x y radius confidence score detail
#
# Anything that does not survive the range checks is dropped with a warning: a
# value that puts the icon off the panel is worse than no value at all, because
# the module would then override a sensor the HAL could have located itself.
add_candidate() {
    local kind="$1" source="$2" label="$3" x="$4" y="$5" r="$6"
    local conf="$7" score="$8" detail="${9:-}"

    if ! is_uint "$x" || ! is_uint "$y" || ! is_uint "$r" \
        || [ "$x" -le 0 ] || [ "$y" -le 0 ] || [ "$r" -le 0 ]; then
        warn "ignored $label: not a usable triple ($x, $y, $r)"
        return 1
    fi
    if [ -n "${W:-}" ] && [ -n "${H:-}" ]; then
        if [ "$x" -ge "$W" ] || [ "$y" -ge "$H" ]; then
            warn "ignored $label: $x,$y is outside the ${W}x${H} panel"
            return 1
        fi
        if [ "$r" -gt "$((W / 6))" ] || [ "$r" -lt 20 ]; then
            warn "ignored $label: radius $r is not a fingerprint sensor ($W px wide)"
            return 1
        fi
    fi

    # A sensor sits on the panel's centre line on every UDFPS phone made so
    # far; an answer that is not close to it is more likely a misparse.
    local bonus=0
    if [ -n "${W:-}" ] && [ $((x - W / 2)) -le 8 ] && [ $((W / 2 - x)) -le 8 ]; then
        bonus=5
    fi

    c_kind+=("$kind"); c_source+=("$source"); c_label+=("$label")
    c_x+=("$x"); c_y+=("$y"); c_r+=("$r")
    c_conf+=("$conf"); c_score+=($((score + bonus))); c_detail+=("$detail")
    return 0
}

# True when a candidate with these coordinates is already recorded; used to stop
# "cmd overlay lookup" from adding a second copy of the overlay's own answer.
have_values() {
    local i
    for i in "${!c_x[@]}"; do
        [ "${c_x[$i]}" = "$1" ] && [ "${c_y[$i]}" = "$2" ] && [ "${c_r[$i]}" = "$3" ] && return 0
    done
    return 1
}
```

```
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Palette and glyphs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Assigned once, at source time, so a report never has to ask twice.
      ui_wants_color() {
          case "${UI_COLOR:-auto}" in
              always) return 0 ;;
              never) return 1 ;;
          esac
          [ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ] || return 1
          [ "${TERM:-}" != dumb ] || return 1
          [ -t 1 ]
      }
      
      if ui_wants_color; then
          UI_RED=$'\033[31m'; UI_GREEN=$'\033[32m'; UI_YELLOW=$'\033[33m'
          UI_BLUE=$'\033[36m'; UI_MAGENTA=$'\033[35m'
          UI_BOLD=$'\033[1m'; UI_DIM=$'\033[2m'; UI_OFF=$'\033[0m'
      else
          UI_RED=''; UI_GREEN=''; UI_YELLOW=''; UI_BLUE=''; UI_MAGENTA=''
          UI_BOLD=''; UI_DIM=''; UI_OFF=''
      fi
      
      # The box and the glyphs are decoration, so a terminal that cannot show them
      # gets plain ASCII rather than a row of question marks.
      if [ "${UI_ASCII:-0}" = "1" ] || [ "${UI_ASCII:-0}" = "true" ]; then
          UI_TL='+'; UI_TR='+'; UI_BL='+'; UI_BR='+'; UI_H='-'; UI_V='|'
          UI_TICK='+'; UI_CROSS='x'; UI_WARN='!'; UI_DOT='-'
          UI_BAR_ON='#'; UI_BAR_OFF='-'
      else
          UI_TL='┌'; UI_TR='┐'; UI_BL='└'; UI_BR='┘'; UI_H='─'; UI_V='│'
          UI_TICK='✓'; UI_CROSS='✗'; UI_WARN='⚠'; UI_DOT='·'
          UI_BAR_ON='█'; UI_BAR_OFF='░'
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prose
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_repeat N STRING — STRING thirty times. Built by hand because printf's %*s
```

> _Reasoning_
> Looks good. Two issues at 40 cols:
> 
> 1. `Panel 1080 x 2400 px at 440 dpi` overflows the border by 0 columns? "│ Panel     1080 x 2400 px at 440 dpi│" — it fits exactly at width 40 but no space before border. ui_panel_row only wraps when value > avail; here value length == avail so it just fits but touches the border. Acceptable-ish, but nicer to reserve one trailing space. Actually ui_panel_row: avail = inner - keyw - 3; the line is " " + key + pad + "  " + value = 1+keyw+2+value = inner → exactly inner. - path: stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh
```
  content: |
                  *) fact="$rest"; rest="" ;;
              esac
              [ -n "$fact" ] && ui_mark "$kind" "$fact" "$indent"
          done
      }
      
      # emit_candidate INDEX RANK DETAIL — one ranked property.
      #
      # The score, the property and its facts, stacked: a fixed table cannot hold a
      # 24-character property name and a 26-character value on a phone, and cutting
      # either is worse than reading down.
      emit_candidate() {
          local i="$1" n="$2" detail="$3" line w
          w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%2d%s  %s %s%3d%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$n" "$UI_OFF" \
              "$(ui_meter "${c_score[$i]:-0}" 120 10)" "$UI_BOLD" "${c_score[$i]:-0}" "$UI_OFF"
          line="${c_prop[$i]} = ${c_val[$i]}"
          if [ $(( ${#line} + 4 )) -le "$w" ]; then
              printf '    %s%s%s = %s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${c_prop[$i]}" "$UI_OFF" "${c_val[$i]}"
          else
              printf '    %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${c_prop[$i]}" "$UI_OFF"
              ui_wrap "${c_val[$i]}" 6 | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '      %s\n' "$line"
              done
          fi
          printf '    %s%s %s %s %s trust %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "${c_zone[$i]}" "$UI_DOT" \
              "${c_label[$i]:-not reported}" "$UI_DOT" \
              "$(ui_trust_color "${c_trust[$i]:-low}")" "${c_trust[$i]:-unknown}" "$UI_OFF"
          [ "$detail" = "1" ] || return 0
          emit_facts note 6 "${c_why[$i]}"
          [ -n "${c_risk[$i]}" ] && emit_facts warn 6 "${c_risk[$i]}"
          return 0
      }
      
      # emit_tail INDEX:RANK ... — every property after the top three, as a table.
      #
      # Twelve cards, each with a paragraph of facts, is a page nobody reads to the
      # end. The three that could win keep their facts; the rest become one row each —
      # rank, score, property, value, trust — so the list is something to scan down
      # rather than a wall of prose. On a phone the row is two lines instead of one:
      # the score line, then `property = value` wrapped under it.
      emit_tail() {
          local -a pairs=("$@") idx=() ranks=()
          local p i k cols pw=0 vw=0 need line
          for p in "${pairs[@]}"; do
              idx+=("${p%%:*}")
              ranks+=("${p#*:}")
          done
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          for i in "${idx[@]}"; do
              [ "${#c_prop[$i]}" -gt "$pw" ] && pw=${#c_prop[$i]}
              [ "${#c_val[$i]}" -gt "$vw" ] && vw=${#c_val[$i]}
          done
          # 2 margin, 3 rank, 2, 6 meter, 1, 3 score, 2, property, 2, value, 2, trust
          need=$(( 2 + 3 + 2 + 10 + 2 + pw + 2 + vw + 2 + 6 ))
      
          if [ "$need" -le "$cols" ]; then
              printf '\n  %s%3s  %-10s  %-*s  %-*s  %-6s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" '#' 'score' \
                  "$pw" 'property' "$vw" 'value' 'trust' "$UI_OFF"
              printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((need - 2)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
              for k in "${!idx[@]}"; do
                  i="${idx[$k]}"
                  printf '  %s%3s%s  %s %s%3d%s  %s%-*s%s  %-*s  %s%s%s\n' \
                      "$UI_DIM" "${ranks[$k]}" "$UI_OFF" \
                      "$(ui_meter "${c_score[$i]:-0}" 140 6)" \
                      "$UI_DIM" "${c_score[$i]:-0}" "$UI_OFF" \
                      "$UI_BOLD" "$pw" "${c_prop[$i]}" "$UI_OFF" \
                      "$vw" "${c_val[$i]}" \
                      "$(ui_trust_color "${c_trust[$i]:-low}")" "${c_trust[$i]:-unknown}" "$UI_OFF"
              done
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/device-id.sh
  content: |
                  ;;
              medium)
                  printf '    The codename came from a partition a GSI replaces, so it is right\n'
                  printf '    for the ROM on the phone now, not necessarily for the GSI.\n'
                  ;;
              *)
                  printf '    Nothing usable was found — set DEVICE_CODENAME by hand in config.env,\n'
                  printf '    or point this at a different phone.\n'
                  ;;
          esac
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Writing it
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # DEVICE_PROP_NAME is only touched when it is empty or already in the shape this
      # writes: a hand-written condition is a decision, not a leftover.
      write_device() {
          local current_prop current_value
          cfg_set DEVICE_MANUFACTURER "$manufacturer" || return 1
          cfg_set DEVICE_MODEL "$model" || return 1
          cfg_set DEVICE_CODENAME "$codename" || return 1
          current_prop="$(cfg_get DEVICE_PROP_NAME)"
          current_value="$(cfg_get DEVICE_PROP_VALUE)"
          case "$current_prop" in
              ''|persist.sys.overlay.*|\<*)
                  cfg_set DEVICE_PROP_NAME "$module_prop" || return 1
                  ;;
              *)
                  printf '  Left DEVICE_PROP_NAME alone: it is set to %s, not the default shape.\n' "$current_prop"
                  ;;
          esac
          [ -n "$current_value" ] || cfg_set DEVICE_PROP_VALUE "true"
          printf '\n  Written to config.env:\n'
          printf '    DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="%s"\n    DEVICE_MODEL="%s"\n    DEVICE_CODENAME="%s"\n' \
              "$manufacturer" "$model" "$codename"
```

```
      # Prompt on stderr instead of stdout: stdout is often JSON that a caller parses.

      adb_device_choose() {
          local ready="$1" count choice resolved tries=0
          count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
          printf 'More than one device is connected:\n' >&2
          printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2

                  printf '%s' "$resolved"
                  return 0
              fi
              printf '  not one of them\n' >&2
          done
          return 1
      }
      
      # Run a command with a deadline, because adb has no timeout of its own and a
      # wedged server otherwise hangs the probe with nothing on screen. LIMIT is in
      # tenths of a second. The child writes a sentinel when it finishes, so a finished
      # process is never mistaken for a running one. 124 means "did not answer".
```

```
  content: |
      # Text folded at INDENT, using the shared wrapper when the caller has ui.sh and
      # a plain indented line when it does not (this file is sourced by probes that
      # print JSON and never draw a box).
      adb_device_wrap() { # TEXT INDENT
          if command -v ui_wrap >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ui_wrap "$1" "$2"
          else
              printf '%*s%s\n' "${2:-0}" '' "$1"
          fi
      }
      
      # One line per device on stdin, already in `devices -l` form.
      #
      # Numbered, because the prompt right after the list accepts a number. The model
      # sits beside the serial when the window is wide enough for it and moves to its
      # own indented line on a phone, rather than being cut or pushing the row wide.
      adb_device_table() {
          local line serial state label cols n=0
          cols="${COLUMNS:-80}"
          if command -v ui_cols >/dev/null 2>&1; then cols="$(ui_cols)"; fi
          case "$cols" in ''|*[!0-9]*) cols=80 ;; esac
          while IFS= read -r line; do
              [ -n "$line" ] || continue
              n=$((n + 1))
              serial="${line%% *}"
              state="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $2}')"
              label="$(adb_device_label "$line")"
              # 2 margin, 2 number, 2, serial column, 2, state column
              if [ $(( 2 + 2 + 2 + 18 + 2 + 13 + ${#label} )) -le "$cols" ]; then
                  printf '  %2d  %-18s %-13s %s\n' "$n" "$serial" "$state" "$label"
              else
                  printf '  %2d  %-18s %s\n' "$n" "$serial" "$state"
                  adb_device_wrap "$label" 6
              fi
          done
      }
      
      # The fix for every device that is attached but not ready. Printed after the
      # table so the last thing on screen is the action, not the list.
      adb_device_advice() {
          local serial message
          printf '%s\n' "${1:-}" | awk '
              $2 == "unauthorized" { print $1 "|unlock the phone and accept the USB debugging prompt" }
              $2 == "offline"      { print $1 "|offline — unplug and replug it, or run adb kill-server" }
              $2 == "no"           { print $1 "|no permissions — Linux needs a udev rule, Windows a driver" }
              $2 == "connecting"   { print $1 "|still connecting — wait a moment and run it again" }
              $2 == "bootloader"   { print $1 "|in the bootloader — boot Android to read the running ROM" }
              $2 == "recovery"     { print $1 "|in recovery — adb works there, but dumpsys and getprop of the ROM do not" }
              $2 == "sideload"     { print $1 "|sideload mode — reboot to Android first" }
              $2 == "rescue"       { print $1 "|rescue mode — reboot to Android first" }
          ' | while IFS='|' read -r serial message; do
              [ -n "$serial" ] || continue
              printf '  %s%s%s\n' "${UI_BOLD:-}" "$serial" "${UI_OFF:-}"
              adb_device_wrap "$message" 4
          done
      }
      
      # Turn what the user typed into a serial from READY (the `devices -l` lines of
      # ready devices): a menu number, a full serial, or a prefix that only one serial
      # starts with. Prints nothing and fails when the answer is not unambiguous.
```

> _Reasoning_
> The adb table check has a bug: `$(( 2 + 2 + 2 + 18 + 2 + 13 + ${#label} ))` — if label is short, this is 39+, so at 40 cols it will use the wide form with a 18-wide serial and 13-wide state, which likely overflows. Wait: 2+2+2+18+2+13+label = 39 + label_len. At cols=40, only label of length 1 fits. Hmm — but the printf uses `%-13s` for state which is shorter typically ("device" = 6), and `%-18s` for serial with actual serial shorter. So the real width is less. The estimate is the worst case and it's too conservative-in-reverse: it demands 39+label but the actual printed width may be ~2+2+2+len(serial)+... Actually %-18s pads to 18 always, so printed width = 2+2+2+18+1+13+1+len(label) = 39+len(label). So the condition `-le cols` is correct-ish: at 40 cols and label 1 char it fits exactly at 40. Fine but very tight; a normal label (e.g., "Xiaomi · Redmi Note 17") is long, so it wraps to 2-line form. That's fine.
> 
> But the padding columns of 18 and 13 are fixed regardless of actual serial length. On a phone (40 cols), the fallback prints `  1  SERIAL(%-18s) state` = 2+2+2+18+1+6 = 31, fine unless serial is long (>18 → it just expands). OK.

```
- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # ui.sh — how a terminal report is drawn
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by common.sh (so the menu and build.sh get it) and by the probes that
      # print a report. Never run directly.
      #
      # The reports used to be fixed-width printf columns, which is the right shape on
      # a 100-column desktop window and unreadable on a phone: 58-column rules wrapped
      # mid-border, and a line of prose about a property ran off the edge and came
      # back as a second, unrelated-looking line. Everything here is measured against
      # the real window instead, and long prose is wrapped with a hanging indent so a
      # wrapped paragraph still looks like one item.
      #
      # Three switches, all optional:
      #   UI_COLOR=always|never|auto   auto (the default) is "a terminal is attached"
      #   UI_COLS=N                    the width to draw for, when there is no tty
      #   UI_ASCII=1                   ASCII borders and glyphs, for a font or a
      #                                codepage that cannot show ─ │ · ⚠
      # Colour is off when stdout is not a terminal, so `./build.sh | tee log` and the
      # JSON probes stay clean, and NO_COLOR is respected.
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Width
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # A phone terminal is 40-50 columns, a desktop window is often 200. Below 40
      # nothing lines up; above 100 an eye loses the start of the line on the way
      # back, so the drawing width is clamped and the spare columns stay empty.
      ui_cols() {
          local c="${UI_COLS:-}"
          [ -n "$c" ] || c="${COLUMNS:-}"
          if [ -z "$c" ] && [ -t 1 ] && command -v tput >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              c="$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || true)"
          fi
          case "$c" in ''|*[!0-9]*) c=80 ;; esac
          [ "$c" -ge 40 ] || c=40
          [ "$c" -le 100 ] || c=100
          printf '%s' "$c"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Palette and glyphs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Assigned once, at source time, so a report never has to ask twice.
      ui_wants_color() {
          case "${UI_COLOR:-auto}" in
              always) return 0 ;;
              never) return 1 ;;
          esac
          [ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ] || return 1
          [ "${TERM:-}" != dumb ] || return 1
          [ -t 1 ]
      }
      
      if ui_wants_color; then
          UI_RED=$'\033[31m'; UI_GREEN=$'\033[32m'; UI_YELLOW=$'\033[33m'
          UI_BLUE=$'\033[36m'; UI_MAGENTA=$'\033[35m'
          UI_BOLD=$'\033[1m'; UI_DIM=$'\033[2m'; UI_OFF=$'\033[0m'
      else
          UI_RED=''; UI_GREEN=''; UI_YELLOW=''; UI_BLUE=''; UI_MAGENTA=''
```

```
          fi

      # One line per device on stdin, already in `devices -l` form.
      #
      # Numbered, because the prompt right after the list accepts a number. The model
      # sits beside the serial when the window is wide enough for it and moves to its
      # own indented line on a phone, rather than being cut or pushing the row wide.
      adb_device_table() {
          local line serial state label cols n=0
          cols="${COLUMNS:-80}"
          if command -v ui_cols >/dev/null 2>&1; then cols="$(ui_cols)"; fi
          case "$cols" in ''|*[!0-9]*) cols=80 ;; esac
          while IFS= read -r line; do
              [ -n "$line" ] || continue
              n=$((n + 1))
              serial="${line%% *}"
              state="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $2}')"
              label="$(adb_device_label "$line")"
              # 2 margin, 2 number, 2, serial column, 2, state column
              if [ $(( 2 + 2 + 2 + 18 + 2 + 13 + ${#label} )) -le "$cols" ]; then
                  printf '  %2d  %-18s %-13s %s\n' "$n" "$serial" "$state" "$label"
              else
                  printf '  %2d  %-18s %s\n' "$n" "$serial" "$state"
                  adb_device_wrap "$label" 6
              fi
          done
```
```
      }

      # udfps_row NUM CHOSEN SOURCE CONF X Y R DETAIL — one candidate.

      # The triple is the answer, so it is bold; the source is the line under it. The

      udfps_row() { # NUM CHOSEN SOURCE CONF X Y R DETAIL
          local num="$1" chosen="$2" source="$3" conf="$4" x="$5" y="$6" r="$7" detail="$8"
          local mark color line
          if [ "$chosen" = "1" ]; then mark="$UI_TICK"; color="$UI_GREEN"

          printf '  %s%s%s %s%d%s  %s%d, %d%s %sr=%d%s  %s%s%s\n' \
              "$color" "$mark" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DIM" "$num" "$UI_OFF" \
              "$UI_BOLD" "$x" "$y" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DIM" "$r" "$UI_OFF" \
              "$(ui_trust_color "$conf")" "$conf" "$UI_OFF"
          printf '    %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$source" "$UI_OFF"
          [ -n "$detail" ] || return 0
          ui_wrap "$detail" 6 | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      emit_human() {
          local idx="$1" i
          ui_title 'UDFPS' 'in-display fingerprint geometry — where the sensor sits'
          if [ "$mode" = "device" ]; then
              ui_panel 'Device' \
                  "Model|${MODEL:-unknown}" \
                  "Codename|${CODENAME:-unknown}" \
                  "Panel|${W:-?} x ${H:-?} px at ${DENS:-?} dpi" \
                  "ROM|${rom:-unknown}"

              ui_mark warn 'No UDFPS geometry found.'
              for i in "${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}"; do ui_mark warn "$i" 4; done

          fi
      
          printf '\n  %s%d source(s) answered%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "${#c_x[@]}" "$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!c_x[@]}"; do
              local chosen=0

          if [ -n "$idx" ]; then
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh
  content: |
      # HAS_UDFPS=false" comes from.
      set_config_key() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" file="$ROOT/config.env" tmp
          [ -f "$file" ] || die "no config.env in $ROOT"
          tmp="$tmpdir/config.env"
          awk -v k="$key" -v v="$value" '
              BEGIN { done = 0 }
              {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/\r$/, "", line)
                  if (!done && line ~ "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*" k "=") {
                      match(line, /^[[:space:]]*/)
                      printf "%s%s=%s\n", substr(line, 1, RLENGTH), k, v
                      done = 1
                      next
                  }
                  print
              }
              END { if (!done) printf "%s=%s\n", k, v }
          ' "$file" >"$tmp" || return 1
          cp "$tmp" "$file"
      }
      
      write_config() {
          local idx="$1"
          set_config_key HAS_UDFPS true
          set_config_key UDFPS_X "${c_x[$idx]}"
          set_config_key UDFPS_Y "${c_y[$idx]}"
          set_config_key UDFPS_RADIUS "${c_r[$idx]}"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      main() {
          files=()
          if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then probe_firmware; else probe_device; fi
          local idx
          idx="$(chosen_index)"
          if [ "$want_write" -eq 1 ]; then
              if [ -z "$idx" ]; then
                  die "nothing to write — no usable geometry found"
              fi
              # An estimate is not good enough to write behind the user's back: it is
              # the one answer that is not evidence.
              if [ "${c_kind[$idx]}" = "estimate" ]; then
                  die "only an estimate was found — set the values by hand from --help"
              fi
              write_config "$idx"
          fi
          if [ "$want_json" -eq 1 ]; then emit_json "$idx"; else emit_human "$idx"; fi
      }
      
      main "$@"
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # udfps-probe.sh — find a device's in-display fingerprint (UDFPS) geometry
      # =============================================================================
      # UDFPS_X / UDFPS_Y / UDFPS_RADIUS in config.env are the sensor's centre and
      # radius in px, written to android:array/config_udfps_sensor_props. Guessing
      # them puts the lock-screen icon next to the sensor instead of on it, so this
      # asks the phone (or a firmware dump) the same question several ways and says
      # where each answer came from.
      #
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh                 # connected device
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --device local  # this phone (Termux, needs root)
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --firmware DIR  # extracted ROM dump
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --json          # for the desktop app
      #   bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --write         # put the winner in config.env
      #
      # Three situations, in the order the guide describes them:
      #
      #   1. OEM ROM on the phone. The vendor FOD properties and the preinstalled
      #      device overlay are both present, so this is the strongest evidence.
      #   2. GSI on the phone. The system partition is the GSI's, but /vendor and
      #      /persist keep the OEM's properties, and the phh/device overlay that was
      #      flashed with the GSI usually still carries the resource. Both are read
      #      here; a value that came from an overlay this tool itself modified is
      #      marked as such instead of being counted as independent.
      #   3. Firmware files. Only useful once the images are unpacked: super.img
      #      needs lpunpack before any APK or build.prop inside it can be read, so a
      #      bare fastboot ROM reports what it is missing instead of guessing.
      #
      # Over adb nothing here is root-only: the overlay APKs and properties it reads
      # are world-readable on a normal boot. In Termux (--device local, or the offer
      # the menu makes there) the reads happen natively and root is required — /vendor
      # overlay APKs and `cmd overlay dump` are closed to an app UID.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -uo pipefail
      
      # adb is a Windows binary under Git Bash: without this its /system/... arguments
      # are rewritten into C:/Program Files/Git/system/... before adb ever sees them.
      # The local half of a pull is converted back with winpath() instead, because the
      # same binary cannot open an MSYS /tmp path.
      export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1
      
      winpath() {
          if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then cygpath -w "$1"; else printf '%s' "$1"; fi
```

```
}

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"

mode="device"
serial=""
want_json=0
want_write=0
adb="${ADB:-}"
aapt2="${AAPT2:-}"
fwdir=""
scan_all_apks=0

usage() {
    sed -n '3,34p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
}

die() { printf 'udfps-probe: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

# Multi-device selection is shared with the Detect probe.
ADB_DEVICE_LIB="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/adb-device.sh"
[ -f "$ADB_DEVICE_LIB" ] || die "stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh is missing — the checkout is incomplete"
. "$ADB_DEVICE_LIB"
# The report is drawn with the shared UI layer: width-aware, colour off when
# piped, ASCII glyphs when UI_ASCII=1.
UI_LIB="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/ui.sh"
[ -f "$UI_LIB" ] || die "stuff/scripts/ui.sh is missing — the checkout is incomplete"
. "$UI_LIB"
note() { notes+=("$1"); }
warn() { warnings+=("$1"); }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --device)
            mode="device"
            shift
            if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ "${1#--}" = "$1" ]; then serial="$1"; shift; fi
            ;;
        --firmware)
            mode="firmware"
            [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--firmware needs a folder"
            fwdir="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --json) want_json=1; shift ;;
        --write) want_write=1; shift ;;
        --adb) adb="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --aapt2) aapt2="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --all-apks) scan_all_apks=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option: $1 (try --help)" ;;
    esac
done

tmpdir="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t udfps)"

```
```
ui_wrap() {
    local text="$1" indent="${2:-0}" avail="${3:-}" pad
    [ -n "$text" ] || return 0
    [ -n "$avail" ] || avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - indent ))
    [ "$avail" -ge 8 ] || avail=8
    pad="$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')"
    printf '%s' "$text" | awk -v w="$avail" -v pad="$pad" '
        {
            line = ""
            n = split($0, word, " ")
            for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                ww = word[i]
                if (ww == "") continue
                # A path is one long word and would run past the edge of a
                # phone; break it rather than let the line wrap by itself, and
                # break after a separator when there is one, so the pieces stay
                # readable (persist.sys.overlay. / zephyr, not zephy / r).
                while (length(ww) > w) {
                    if (line != "") { print pad line; line = "" }
                    cut = w
                    for (j = w; j > w / 2; j--) {
                        ch = substr(ww, j, 1)
                        if (ch == "/" || ch == "." || ch == "-" || ch == "_" || ch == "=" || ch == ",") { cut = j; break }
                    }
                    print pad substr(ww, 1, cut)
                    ww = substr(ww, cut + 1)
                }
                if (ww == "") continue
                if (line == "") line = ww
                else if (length(line) + 1 + length(ww) <= w) line = line " " ww
                else { print pad line; line = ww }
            }
            if (line != "") print pad line
        }
    '
}
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      #   `   1  Auto Detect   cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G`
      #
      # The number is the accent colour, the label bold and the description dim, so
      # the eye follows the label column and can still find a number at a glance. On a
      # phone the description does not fit beside the label, so it moves to its own
      # indented, wrapped line instead of being cut off at the edge.
      ui_item() {
          local num="$1" label="$2" detail="${3:-}" lw="${4:-${#2}}" cols head line
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          # A label wider than the column (a long section title) widens the column
          # rather than being cut or pushing the description out of line.
          [ "$lw" -ge "${#label}" ] || lw=${#label}
          head="  $(printf '%3s' "$num")  "
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$UI_BLUE" "$head" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_BOLD" "$label"
          if [ -z "$detail" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          # 5 for the number column and its gaps, 2 between label and description.
          if [ $((5 + lw + 2 + ${#detail})) -le "$cols" ]; then
              printf '%s%*s  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_OFF" $((lw - ${#label})) '' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$detail" "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$detail" 7 $((cols - 7)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_trust_color high|medium|low — green for an answer, red for a gamble.
      # The trust word is the one thing a reader scans a ranked list for, so it is
      # coloured rather than left in the same grey as the rest of the meta line.
      ui_trust_color() {
          case "${1:-}" in
              high) printf '%s' "$UI_GREEN" ;;
              medium) printf '%s' "$UI_YELLOW" ;;
              low|*) printf '%s' "$UI_RED" ;;
          esac
      }
```

> _Reasoning_
> Panels are exactly 44 wide, which is fine for a box (drawing to the full width is desirable and it's the last char). Some terminals wrap at exactly the width — a box at exactly cols width would trigger wrap. Real terminals wrap when the cursor advances past the last column: writing exactly N chars fills the line, cursor sits at the end without wrapping; the newline then moves down. Most terminals handle that fine (auto-wrap flag only triggers on the next char). So it's acceptable.

```
- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      # ui_item NUM LABEL [DETAIL] — one row of a menu or an option list.
      #
      #   `   1  Auto Detect   cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G`
      #
      # The number is the accent colour, the label bold and the description dim, so
      # the eye follows the label column and can still find a number at a glance. On a
      # phone the description does not fit beside the label, so it moves to its own
      # indented, wrapped line instead of being cut off at the edge.
      ui_item() {
          local num="$1" label="$2" detail="${3:-}" lw="${4:-${#2}}" cols head line
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          # A label wider than the column (a long section title) widens the column
          # rather than being cut or pushing the description out of line.
          [ "$lw" -ge "${#label}" ] || lw=${#label}
          head="  $(printf '%3s' "$num")  "
          # A label longer than the window is a section header somewhere in config.env
          # — `Overlay repo submission (Doze-off, submission only)` — and it runs off a
          # phone. It wraps under the number, and the description follows it there.
          if [ $(( 5 + ${#label} )) -ge "$cols" ]; then
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_BLUE" "$head" "$UI_OFF"
              ui_wrap "$label" 7 $((cols - 8)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
              done
              [ -n "$detail" ] || return 0
              ui_wrap "$detail" 9 $((cols - 10)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
              done
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$UI_BLUE" "$head" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_BOLD" "$label"
          if [ -z "$detail" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          # 5 for the number column and its gaps, 2 between label and description.
          if [ $((5 + lw + 2 + ${#detail})) -le "$cols" ]; then
              printf '%s%*s  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_OFF" $((lw - ${#label})) '' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$detail" "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$detail" 7 $((cols - 8)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_trust_color high|medium|low — green for an answer, red for a gamble.
      # The trust word is the one thing a reader scans a ranked list for, so it is
      # coloured rather than left in the same grey as the rest of the meta line.
      ui_trust_color() {
```

```
      menu_files() {
```

```
ui_table() {
    local header="$1"; shift
    local avail ncols=0 i k w total cell line first
    local -a rows=("$@") heads=() widths=()
    avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
    ui_split "$header" '|'
    heads=("${UI_SPLIT[@]}")
    ncols=${#heads[@]}
    for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do widths[$k]=${#heads[$k]}; done
    for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
        ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
        for k in "${!UI_SPLIT[@]}"; do
            [ "$k" -lt "$ncols" ] || continue
            cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]}"
            [ "${#cell}" -gt "${widths[$k]}" ] && widths[$k]=${#cell}
        done
    done
    total=$(( 2 * (ncols - 1) ))
    for w in "${widths[@]}"; do total=$(( total + w )); done

    if [ "$total" -gt "$avail" ]; then
        for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
            ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
            printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}" "$UI_OFF"
            line=""
            for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                [ -n "$cell" ] || continue
                if [ -z "$line" ]; then line="$cell"; else line="$line $UI_DOT $cell"; fi
            done
            [ -n "$line" ] || continue
            ui_wrap "$line" 4 | while IFS= read -r cell; do
                printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$cell" "$UI_OFF"
            done
        done
        return 0
    fi

    printf '\n  %s' "$UI_BOLD"
    for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do
        printf '%-*s' "${widths[$k]}" "${heads[$k]}"
        [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ] && printf '  '
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
    printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$total" "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
    for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
        ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
        printf '  %s' "$UI_DIM"
        printf '%-*s' "${widths[0]}" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}"
        printf '%s  ' "$UI_OFF"
        for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
            printf '%-*s' "${widths[$k]}" "${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
            [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ] && printf '  '
        done
        printf '\n'
    done
}
```

```

- path: stuff/scripts/manifest.sh
  content: |
              function esc(s) { gsub(/\\/, "\\\\", s); gsub(/"/, "\\\"", s); return s }
              BEGIN {
                  printf "{\n  \"id\": \"%s\",\n  \"generated\": \"%s\",\n  \"resources\": [", id, gen
                  first = 1
              }
              {
                  if ($6 == "") next
                  printf "%s\n    {\"res\": \"%s:%s/%s\", \"type\": \"%s\", \"name\": \"%s\", \"value\": \"%s\", \"apk\": \"%s\", \"group\": \"%s\", \"ro\": %s}", \
                      (first ? "" : ","), $3, $5, esc($6), $5, esc($6), esc($7), $3, esc($2), ($4 == "1" ? "true" : "false")
                  first = 0
              }
              END { printf "\n  ]\n}\n" }
          ' > "$out"
      
          count=$(grep -c '"res"' "$out" 2>/dev/null || true)
          printf '%s' "${count:-0}"
      }
      
      # Human-readable plan: the same rows the manifest is built from.
      #
      # A resource name and its value are what the reader is comparing, so they get the
      # line; where it came from (which APK, which type, whether it can be patched) is
      # the dim note under it. The old fixed four-column row was 60 columns before the
      # value started and ran off a phone every time.
      print_resource_plan() {
          local rank group apk ro type name value count=0 last="" line
          while IFS=$'\t' read -r rank group apk ro type name value; do
              [ -n "$name" ] || continue
              if [ "$group" != "$last" ]; then
                  ui_heading "$group"
                  last="$group"
```

```
              return 0

          for k in "${!idx[@]}"; do
              i="${idx[$k]}"
              printf '\n  %s%3s%s  %s %s%3d%s  %s%s%s\n' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "${ranks[$k]}" "$UI_OFF" \
                  "$(ui_meter "${c_score[$i]:-0}" 140 6)" \
                  "$UI_DIM" "${c_score[$i]:-0}" "$UI_OFF" \

              line="${c_prop[$i]} = ${c_val[$i]}"
              if [ $(( ${#line} + 4 )) -le "$cols" ]; then
                  printf '    %s%s%s = %s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${c_prop[$i]}" "$UI_OFF" "${c_val[$i]}"
              elif [ $(( ${#c_prop[$i]} + 8 )) -le "$cols" ]; then
                  # The name fits and only the value does not: hang the value under it,
                  # two columns further in, so the wrapped piece still belongs to the
                  # row above instead of looking like the next candidate.
                  printf '    %s%s%s =\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${c_prop[$i]}" "$UI_OFF"
                  ui_wrap "${c_val[$i]}" 6 | while IFS= read -r line; do
                      printf '%s\n' "$line"
                  done
              else
                  # ui_wrap already indents every line by four, so print it as it is.
                  ui_wrap "$line" 4 | while IFS= read -r line; do
                      printf '%s\n' "$line"
                  done
              fi
          done
      }
      
      emit_human() {
          local i n=0 saved_prop saved_value
          saved_prop="$(cfg_get HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP)"
          saved_value="$(cfg_get HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE)"
      
          local -a panel=()
          panel+=("Phone|${model:-unknown}${manuf:+ ($manuf)}")
          if [ -n "$codename" ]; then
              panel+=("Codename|$codename ($codename_prop)")
          else
              panel+=("Codename|not found — no property carries a device name")
          fi
          [ -n "$module_prop" ] && panel+=("Module|$module_prop")
          if [ -n "$saved_prop" ] || [ -n "$saved_value" ]; then
              panel+=("Current|${saved_prop:-ro.product.vendor.device} = $saved_value")
          fi
      
          ui_title "Match property" \
              "Which property the overlay requires, so the module only applies to this phone."
          ui_panel "This phone" "${panel[@]}"
      
          if [ "${#sorted[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              local -a rest_pairs=()
              ui_heading "Ranked properties"
              for i in "${sorted[@]}"; do
                  n=$((n + 1))
                  # The three that could plausibly be chosen get their facts spelled
                  # out; the rest become table rows, so twelve properties stay a list.
                  if [ "$n" -le 3 ]; then
                      emit_candidate "$i" "$n" 1
                  else
                      rest_pairs+=("$i:$n")
                  fi
              done
              [ "${#rest_pairs[@]}" -gt 0 ] && emit_tail "${rest_pairs[@]}"
          else
              ui_heading "Ranked properties"
              ui_mark bad "No property could be ranked — nothing on this phone names the device."
          fi
      
          if [ "${#r_prop[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              ui_heading "Ruled out"
              for i in "${!r_prop[@]}"; do
                  printf '\n  %s%s%s = %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "${r_prop[$i]}" "$UI_OFF" \
                      "$UI_DIM" "${r_val[$i]}" "$UI_OFF"
                  ui_mark note "${r_reason[$i]}" 4
              done
          fi
      
          local -a verdict=("Confidence|$confidence")
          if [ "${#sorted[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
              verdict+=("Best match|${c_prop[${sorted[0]}]}")
              verdict+=("Value|${c_val[${sorted[0]}]}")
          fi
          ui_panel "Verdict" "${verdict[@]}" 
          case "$confidence" in
              high)
                  ui_mark ok "${c_prop[${sorted[0]}]} carries the codename, zygote can read it, and a GSI leaves its partition alone. This is the answer."
                  ;;
              medium)
                  ui_mark warn "The best property holds the codename, but something else about it is a gamble (readability, or a GSI replaces its partition). It works today on this ROM; keeping the match you already have is safer."
                  ;;
              *)
                  ui_mark bad "No property satisfies every rule. Keep the HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_* you already have, or set the pair by hand from config.env."
                  ;;
          esac
          printf '\n'
      }
```

```
          cfg_set HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP "$prop" || { printf 'match-prop: could not write config.env\n' >&2; return 1; }
          cfg_set HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE "$value" || { printf 'match-prop: could not write config.env\n' >&2; return 1; }
          printf '\n  Written to config.env:\n    HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP="%s"\n    HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE="%s"\n' "$prop" "$value"
          printf '  Rebuild to pick it up: ./build.sh (or 8 in the menu)\n\n'
          return 0
      }
      
      main() {
          if [ -n "$values_file" ]; then
              collect_from_files
          else
              collect_from_device
          fi
          rank
      
          if [ "$want_json" = "1" ]; then
              emit_json
              # The exit code is part of the answer: a script that reads the JSON must
              # not have to count the candidates to find out there were none.
              [ "${#sorted[@]}" -gt 0 ] && return 0
              return 1
          fi
          emit_human
      
          if [ "${#sorted[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              return 1
          fi
      
          if [ "$want_write" = "1" ]; then
              # --write takes the trusted answer only. A guess written silently is
              # worse than the pair that is already there.
              if [ "$confidence" != "high" ]; then
                  printf '  Not writing: the best candidate is not trusted enough (%s).\n' "$confidence"
                  printf '  Pick one by hand with: bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh\n\n'
                  return 1
              fi
              write_pair "${c_prop[${sorted[0]}]}" "${c_val[${sorted[0]}]}"
              return 0
          fi
      
          # Interactive: a number writes that row, Enter (or anything else) keeps the
          # pair that is already in config.env.
          [ -t 0 ] || return 0
          printf '  Which one? [1-%d, Enter keeps the current match] ' "${#sorted[@]}"
          local reply=""
          read -r reply || reply=""
          case "$reply" in
              ''|*[!0-9]*) printf '  Left config.env alone.\n\n'; return 0 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$reply" -lt 1 ] || [ "$reply" -gt "${#sorted[@]}" ]; then
              printf '  Not one of them — left config.env alone.\n\n'
              return 0
          fi
          local pick="${sorted[$((reply - 1))]}"
          if [ "${c_perfect[$pick]}" != "1" ]; then
              printf '\n  Note: %s is not the property this tool would trust on its own\n' "${c_prop[$pick]}"
              printf '  (see the warning under it). It only holds while the value stays %s.\n' "${c_val[$pick]}"
          fi
          write_pair "${c_prop[$pick]}" "${c_val[$pick]}"
      }
      
      main
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # match-prop.sh — which property should the submitted overlay match on?
      # =============================================================================
      # The overlay repo compares android:requiredSystemPropertyName/Value with plain
      # string equality, and getting it wrong is silent: the overlay installs, `cmd
      # overlay list` shows it enabled, and nothing changes. This reads the phone and
      # ranks every property the submission could use, saying what each one is
      # gambling on.
      #
      #   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh                  # connected device, then ask
      #   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --write          # take the answer it trusts
      #   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --json           # for scripts
      #
      #   --device SERIAL   with more than one phone attached
      #   --device local    read this phone directly (Termux, needs root)
      #   --adb PATH        adb is looked up on PATH and in stuff/tools/platform-tools
      #   --values FILE --labels FILE   rank saved `getprop` / `getprop -Z` output
      #                                 instead of asking a phone (tests, offline)
      #
      # Two rules decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable without
      # root: zygote has to be able to read the property (`getprop -Z` prints the
      # SELinux area; build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps),
      # and the value has to survive what is installed (vendor, odm and bootimage keep
      # the OEM value under a GSI; /system, /product and /system_ext do not). When no
      # property satisfies both, this says so instead of picking one — a match that
      # never holds is invisible.
      #
      # The same ranking lives in the desktop app (gui/matchprop.go). Change one,
      # change the other.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -uo pipefail
      
      # adb is a Windows binary under Git Bash: without this its /system/... arguments
      # are rewritten into C:/Program Files/Git/system/... before adb ever sees them.
      export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1
      
      ROOT="${ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/ui.sh"
      
      adb="${ADB:-}"
      serial=""
      want_json=0
      want_write=0
      assume_yes=0
      values_file=""
      labels_file=""
      
      usage() {
          sed -n '3,31p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
      }
      
      die() { printf 'match-prop: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
      
      while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
          case "$1" in
              --device) serial="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --adb) adb="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
      
      [read_files: showing lines 1-60 of 660. Use code_search to locate the part you need and read a window around it, or call read_files again with offset=61 to continue.]
```

The CLI now has the same visual language as the web UI: panels, tables, colour-coded states, score meters and wrapped prose, all width-aware so a Termux phone at ~44 columns and a desktop terminal both get a usable layout.

**What changed**

- **New shared library `stuff/scripts/ui.sh`** (452 lines) — `ui_panel`, `ui_table`, `ui_mark`, `ui_meter`, `ui_item`, `ui_wrap`, `ui_trust_color`, plus width detection (`UI_COLS` or the real terminal size) and colour with a `NO_COLOR`/`--no-color` fallback.
- **Match property** — this was the worst offender (12 blended matches). Now the top three keep their score meter, property, value, zone and trust, with the why/warning under each; the rest collapse into one scannable `# score property value trust` table, and the "Ruled out" block explains itself. At 44 columns the table degrades gracefully: score line first, then `property = value` wrapped beneath, long fingerprints wrapped instead of running off the edge.
- **Every other screen** — Device, the adb device list and its advice, UDFPS, Auto Detect, Addons, Files, Docs, the build plan, the build summary and the menu itself all go through the same helpers, so nothing overflows or blends into one grey block anymore.
- **Bugs caught while checking** — the Auto Detect blurb was printing literal `\n` mid-sentence (fixed), and the narrow table fallback left a bare `12K` above a path (now reads `Size 12K`).

**Verification**

- `bash -n` clean on every script in `stuff/scripts/`, `build.sh` and `treble-rro-creator.sh`.
- Full suite: **111 tests, 111 pass, 0 fail**.
- Rendered the match-property report and the menu screens at 44 and 88/100 columns; output is valid UTF-8 and no lines exceed the width. Screens 4, 5, 6, 7 were smoke-tested for unbound variables/runtime errors.

One limitation: run-time checks were done against the repo's own `config.env` and synthetic probe data, not a live phone over adb, so the phone-reading code paths were exercised through their report renderers rather than a real device query.

```
- path: stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh
  content: |
              cp "${bt_dir}/lib/apksigner.jar" "${TOOLS_DIR}/apksigner.jar"
              cat > "${TOOLS_DIR}/apksigner" << 'APKSIGNER_EOF'
      #!/bin/sh
      # Generated by build.sh — runs the build-tools apksigner jar.
      here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
      case "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) here=$(cygpath -w "$here") ;;
      esac
      exec java -jar "$here/apksigner.jar" "$@"
      APKSIGNER_EOF
              chmod +x "${TOOLS_DIR}/apksigner"
              ok "Installed apksigner (java -jar stuff/tools/apksigner.jar)"
              installed=true
          else
              warn "apksigner.jar not found in the build-tools package"
          fi
      
          # Everything needed is copied into stuff/tools/; drop the ~120 MB extraction.
          rm -rf "${TOOLS_DIR}/build-tools-win"
      
          $installed
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Resource dictionary (framework-res.apk)
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # aapt2 needs the platform resource table to resolve android:* IDs. Android 13
      # is the most reliable version and links overlays for 13 through 16.
      download_platform_resources() {
          local sdk_ver="$1"
          mkdir -p "$TOOLS_DIR"
      
          local tmp_zip="${TOOLS_DIR}/platform_tmp.zip"
          local rev url success=false
      
          info "Downloading Android ${sdk_ver} resources from Google..."
          # r02 is the known-good revision for API 33; try it first, then the rest.
          for rev in r02 r01 r03 r04 r05 r06 r07 r08 ""; do
              url="https://dl.google.com/android/repository/platform-${sdk_ver}_${rev}.zip"
              url="${url%_}" # strip trailing underscore when rev is empty
              if curl --fail -L "$url" -o "$tmp_zip" 2>/dev/null; then
                  success=true
                  break
              fi
          done
      
          if [ "$success" != "true" ]; then
              err "Download failed for all revisions — Google may have moved the files."
              rm -f "$tmp_zip"
              return 1
          fi
      
          info "Extracting android.jar (resource table)..."
          if ! unzip -j -o "$tmp_zip" "*/android.jar" -d "$TOOLS_DIR/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              err "Could not extract android.jar from the platform archive"
              rm -f "$tmp_zip"
              return 1
          fi
          if [ ! -f "$TOOLS_DIR/android.jar" ]; then
              err "The archive did not contain android.jar"
              rm -f "$tmp_zip"
              return 1
          fi
      
          mv "$TOOLS_DIR/android.jar" "$TOOLS_DIR/framework-res.apk"
          rm -f "$tmp_zip"
          ok "Android ${sdk_ver} resources installed (stuff/tools/framework-res.apk, $(du -sh "$TOOLS_DIR/framework-res.apk" | cut -f1))"
      }
      
      # acquire_framework_res <auto|ask> [force]
      # `force` asks/downloads even when a resource dictionary already exists.
      acquire_framework_res() {
          local mode="${1:-ask}" force="${2:-}"
      
          if [ -z "$force" ] && framework_res_path >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              return 0
          fi
      
          if [ "$mode" = "auto" ]; then
              download_platform_resources 33
              return $?
          fi
      
          echo ""
          info "One more piece: framework-res.apk (the resource dictionary)."
          echo "  aapt2 uses it to translate android:* resource IDs. Using the wrong"
          echo "  version causes 'resource not found' errors during the build."
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Where should it come from?${NC}"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[1]${NC} Download Android 13 resources  (${GREEN}recommended${NC} — works for 13-16)"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[2]${NC} Download Android 14"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[3]${NC} Download Android 15"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[4]${NC} Download Android 16 (preview)"
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[5]${NC} Pull from the connected device  (${RED}not recommended${NC})"
          echo "        Manufacturer builds are often stripped/odexed and aapt2 will fail."
          echo -e "    ${BOLD}[n]${NC} Skip for now"
          echo ""
          ask "  Choose [1/2/3/4/5/n]: " "1"
      
          case "$REPLY" in
              1|2|3|4)
                  local sdk_ver="33"
                  [ "$REPLY" = "2" ] && sdk_ver="34"
                  [ "$REPLY" = "3" ] && sdk_ver="35"
                  [ "$REPLY" = "4" ] && sdk_ver="36"
                  download_platform_resources "$sdk_ver"
                  ;;
              5)
                  mkdir -p "$TOOLS_DIR"
                  info "Trying to pull /system/framework/framework-res.apk..."
                  if cp /system/framework/framework-res.apk "$TOOLS_DIR/framework-res.apk" 2>/dev/null; then
                      ok "framework-res.apk pulled"
                  elif command -v su >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
                       su -c "cp /system/framework/framework-res.apk \"$TOOLS_DIR/framework-res.apk\"" 2>/dev/null; then
                      ok "framework-res.apk pulled (via su)"
                  else
                      err "Could not read /system/framework/framework-res.apk (this only works on Android/Termux)."
                      info "Use one of the download options instead."
                      return 1
                  fi
                  ;;
              *)
                  info "Skipped — aapt2 will need framework-res.apk before it can link."
                  return 1
                  ;;
          esac
      }

      # error messages when an unattended install is not possible).
      package_install_hint() {
          if $IS_TERMUX; then
              # zipalign is shipped by the 'aapt' package, not by 'aapt2'.
              echo "pkg install -y aapt aapt2 apksigner android-tools openjdk-17 unzip zip curl"
          elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "sudo apt install -y aapt android-sdk-build-tools apksigner android-framework-res zip curl"
          elif command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "sudo pacman -S --needed android-tools jdk-openjdk zip curl"
          elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "sudo dnf install -y android-tools java-17-openjdk zip curl"
          else
              echo "./build.sh setup   (choose 'Manual download')"
          fi
      }
      
      # How to run a package manager as root, in $INSTALL_AS_ROOT (empty when these
      # privileges are already ours). Returns 1 when a password is needed but there
      # is no way to ask for one here: no terminal — the desktop app — and no
      # SUDO_ASKPASS helper to read it from.
      #
      # sudo -A is that helper: the app collects the password in a dialog, writes it
      # to a private file and points SUDO_ASKPASS at stuff/scripts/sudo-askpass.sh,
      # so the install below can run without a tty.
      INSTALL_AS_ROOT=()
      install_as_root() {
          INSTALL_AS_ROOT=()
          [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] && return 0
          command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
          if sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
              INSTALL_AS_ROOT=(sudo -n)
          elif [ -n "${SUDO_ASKPASS:-}" ]; then
              INSTALL_AS_ROOT=(sudo -A)
          elif [ -t 0 ] || [ -t 2 ]; then
              INSTALL_AS_ROOT=(sudo)
          else
              return 1
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # install_linux_packages
      #
      # 0  installed (or there was nothing to run)
      # 1  could not install; the caller may fall back to the no-root download
      # 2  install possible, but root needs a password and nothing here can ask for
      #    one — the caller prints @@RRO_SUDO_REQUIRED@@ so the app can offer its
      #    dialog and re-run the same command
      # 3  the package manager is busy: another one is running, or its stale lock
      #    could not be removed — waiting or removing it by hand is the only fix, so
      #    do not fall back to a download
      
      # Is something holding the pacman database right now? /proc is enough and
      # avoids depending on pgrep; comm is what the executable is called, which is
      # also why a paru/yay repo install shows up as pacman.
      package_manager_running() {
          local p comm
          for p in /proc/[0-9]*/comm; do
              [ -r "$p" ] || continue
              read -r comm < "$p" || continue
              case "$comm" in
                  pacman|pacman-key|paru|yay|pikaur|trizen|pamac*) return 0 ;;
              esac
          done
          return 1
      }
      
      # The package manager did not succeed. When the password came from the app
      # (sudo -A), the likely cause is a typo, so ask again instead of quietly falling
      # back to the no-root download. 2 = "needs a password" to the caller.
      install_failed() {
          case "${INSTALL_AS_ROOT[*]:-}" in
              *-A*)
                  warn "sudo could not install the build tools — the password may be wrong."
                  echo "@@RRO_SUDO_REQUIRED@@" >&2
                  return 2
                  ;;
          esac
          return 1
      }
      
      install_linux_packages() {
          if $IS_TERMUX; then
              info "Termux detected — running: pkg install ..."
              # 'aapt' carries zipalign (the aapt2 package does not).
              if pkg install -y aapt aapt2 apksigner android-tools openjdk-17 unzip zip curl tsu; then
                  ok "Packages installed"
                  return 0
              fi
              warn "Package installation failed (often a repository mirror problem)."
              echo "     Run: termux-change-repo   → pick a nearby mirror"
              echo "     Then: apt update && ./build.sh setup"
              return 1
          fi
      
          if ! install_as_root; then
              # One machine-readable line, because the desktop app has no terminal to
              # prompt in: it asks for the password itself and re-runs the command
              # with SUDO_ASKPASS set. The pane strips this line, so nobody sees it.
              echo "@@RRO_SUDO_REQUIRED@@" >&2
              warn "Root privileges are needed to install the build tools."
              echo "     Run: $(package_install_hint)"
              echo "     Then re-run: ./build.sh"
              return 2
          fi
      
          if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              info "Installing Debian/Ubuntu packages (apt)..."
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# menu.sh — the terminal front end
# =============================================================================
# The desktop app and this file drive the same tools: the device probes, the
# addon catalog, the match-property ranking and build.sh's own verbs. The goal
# is that a phone with a terminal (Termux, ssh, a server) gets the same answers
# as the window, without a GUI toolkit.
#
#   ./build.sh                 opens this (when stdin is a terminal)
#   ./build.sh menu            opens this even when stdin is not a terminal
#   bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh same thing, standalone
#
# Every action shells out to the real entry point — `build.sh build`,
# `device-probe.sh --write`, `addons.sh set` — so there is exactly one
# implementation of each step and the menu cannot drift from the app.
# =============================================================================

if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
    ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
    export ROOT
    . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
fi
. "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
# The device-source helpers (device_is_termux, device_local_begin) live with the
# adb code the probes share. Sourcing it here defines functions only.
. "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small things
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MENU_SLEEP="${MENU_SLEEP:-0}"

# A width-aware rule under a section title. Every screen used to draw a fixed
# 58-character one, which wrapped onto a second line on a phone.
hr() { ui_rule 2; }

# Read one line. Returns 1 at EOF (piped input, a launcher with no console) so
# callers can leave the menu instead of looping forever.
menu_read() {
    local prompt="${1:-} " answer=""
    printf '%s' "$prompt"
    if ! read -r answer; then
        echo ""
        return 1
    fi
    MENU_ANSWER="$answer"
    return 0
}

# Wait for Enter between screens, unless stdin is not a terminal.
pause_menu() {
    [ -t 0 ] || return 0
    printf '\n  %s ' "Press Enter to go back"
    read -r _ || true
    printf '\n'
}

# Count the rows config.env has, and how many are switched off.
cfg_counts() {
    local rows
    rows="$(cfg_rows 2>/dev/null)" || { CFG_ON=0; CFG_OFF=0; return 0; }
    CFG_ON="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 1' | grep -c . || true)"
    CFG_OFF="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 0' | grep -c . || true)"
}

output_summary() {
    local apks=0 zips=0 zip=""
    [ -d "$OUT_DIR/apks" ] && apks="$(find "$OUT_DIR/apks" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
    [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && zips="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
    zip="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | sort | head -n1)"
    if [ "$zips" -gt 0 ]; then
        printf '%s  (%s APK%s)' "${zip#$ROOT/}" "$apks" "$([ "$apks" = 1 ] || echo s)"
    else
        printf 'nothing built yet'
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Screen
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The state of the checkout in one box: which phone, how much of config.env is
# filled in, what the last build left behind.
menu_header() {
    cfg_counts
    ui_panel "Treble Overlay Creator" \
        "Device|$(cfg_identity)" \
        "config.env|${CFG_ON} set ${UI_DOT} ${CFG_OFF} off" \
        "Output|$(output_summary)"
}

# 11 is the width of the longest label here, so every description starts in the
# same column instead of ragging after each label.
MENU_LW=14

menu_items() {
    ui_item 1 'Build'          'dry run, build, check, doctor, clean' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item 2 'config.env'     'browse and edit one key at a time' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item 3 'Addons'         'module tweaks: settings and overlay resources' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item 4 'Device'         'read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item 5 'Auto Detect'    'ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item 6 'UDFPS'          'in-display fingerprint geometry' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item 7 'Match property' 'which property the submission should match on' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item 8 'Files'          'what was built, and where it is' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item 9 'Docs'           'the guides in docs/' "$MENU_LW"
    ui_item q 'Quit' '' "$MENU_LW"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The menu never re-implements a build step: it runs the entry point with the
# verb a user would type, so `build.sh doctor` and 1 → 4 are the same command.
run_entry() {
    ( cd "$ROOT" && bash "$ROOT/build.sh" "$@" )
}

menu_build() {
    while :; do
        ui_heading 'Build'
        ui_item 1 'Dry run'     'print the resources config.env emits, build nothing' 11
        ui_item 2 'Build'       'build the module (installs tools if needed)' 11
        ui_item 3 'Check'       'validate config.env without building' 11
        ui_item 4 'Doctor'      'check the toolchain, install nothing' 11
        ui_item 5 'Clean'       'remove build output' 11
        ui_item 6 'Clean --all' 'start over for a different device' 11
        ui_item 0 'Back' '' 11
        menu_read "  >" || return 0
        case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
            1) run_entry --dry-run; pause_menu ;;
            2) run_entry build; pause_menu ;;
            3) run_entry check; pause_menu ;;
            4) run_entry doctor; pause_menu ;;
            5) run_entry clean; pause_menu ;;
            6)
                warn "This removes config.env and the device files too."
                if confirm "  Start over for a different device? [y/N] " n; then
                    run_entry clean --all
                fi
                pause_menu
                ;;
            0|q|'') return 0 ;;
            *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
        esac
    done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Files
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```
# Whether adb can see a ready device right now, without the 120s wait: that wait
# is for a cable being plugged in, and in Termux there is nothing to plug in.
adb_device_ready_now() {
    local adb="$1" want="${2:-}"
    adb_device_list "$adb" 25 || return 1
    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s && $2 == "device"' | grep -q .
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES" | awk '$2 == "device"' | grep -q .
    fi
}

# Where adb is. A probe's `--adb PATH` (in $adb before this file is sourced)
# wins, then PATH, then the copy the toolchain installs. Defined here rather
# than in each probe so device_connect does not depend on them defining it.
adb="${adb:-}"
resolve_adb() {
    [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
    adb="$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
    for adb in "${ROOT:-.}/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb" "${ROOT:-.}/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb.exe"; do
        [ -x "$adb" ] && return 0
    done
    adb=""
    return 1
}

# One command on the chosen phone, CRs stripped and errors dropped. The single
# place the two sources meet: both take a command string.
device_sh() {
    if [ "${DEVICE_LOCAL:-0}" = 1 ]; then
        # The local shell is already root, so the probes' `su 0` retries would be
        # a second escalation with nothing to gain — and a second su prompt. The
        # prefix is dropped so those calls stay quiet.
        case "$1" in
            'su 0 '*) set -- "${1#su 0 }" ;;
        esac
        device_local_run "$1" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
    else
        "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} shell "$1" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
    fi
}

# Copy a file off the chosen phone. adb pull runs as the shell user and falls
# back to `su 0 cat` for root-only paths (/vendor/overlay); local mode is
# already root, so one cat covers both.
#
# The path is quoted for the shell on the other end, not for this one: a name
# holding a single quote would otherwise end the quoting early and cat something
# else (or nothing).
sh_quote() { printf "'%s'" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")"; }

device_pull() {
    local remote="$1" local_path="$2" to="$2"
    if [ "${DEVICE_LOCAL:-0}" = 1 ]; then
        device_local_run "cat $(sh_quote "$remote")" >"$local_path" 2>/dev/null
        [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0
        return 1
    fi
    # A Windows adb cannot open an MSYS /tmp path, so the local half is converted
    # when cygpath exists (Git Bash); elsewhere the path is passed as it is.
    if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then to="$(cygpath -w "$local_path")"; fi
    "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} pull "$remote" "$to" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        && [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0
    "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} exec-out "su 0 cat $(sh_quote "$remote")" >"$local_path" 2>/dev/null \
        && [ -s "$local_path" ] && return 0
    return 1
}

# device_connect PROG [WANT] — where the answers come from, for every probe.
#
# WANT is the --device value; "local" (also this/self/here) asks for this phone.
# DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST=1/0 forces the answer, which is what the menu sets after
# asking once. Sets DEVICE_LOCAL, DEVICE_ROOT_CMD, DEVICE_SERIAL and the probe's
# `serial`; on failure the reason has already been printed.
#
# Precedence, most specific first: a serial or "local" typed on the command
# line, then the session's answer, then what this machine allows (in Termux,
# adb has nothing to talk to, so the local source is offered there instead).
device_connect() {
    local prog="$1" want="${2:-}" mode="${DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST:-}"
    case "$want" in
        local|this|self|here)
            device_local_begin "$prog" || return 1
            serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
            return 0
            ;;
        '')
            ;;
        *)
            mode=""
            ;;
    esac
    case "$mode" in
        1)
            # The question was answered before this probe started (the menu asks
            # once a session), so do not announce the switch again.
            DEVICE_LOCAL_QUIET=1
            device_local_begin "$prog" || return 1
            serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
    # Termux, and adb cannot see the phone right now: ask about the direct
    # source before the device wait, because in Termux that wait cannot end.
    if [ -z "$mode" ] && device_is_termux \
        && ! { resolve_adb 2>/dev/null && adb_device_ready_now "$adb" "$want"; }; then
        device_local_offer "$prog" && { serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"; return 0; }
    fi
    resolve_adb || {
        if device_is_termux; then
            printf '%s: adb cannot reach a phone from Termux — the phone is this machine, and reading it needs root.\n' "$prog" >&2
            printf '  start the tool as root: tsu %s/build.sh   (pkg install tsu if it is missing)\n' "${ROOT:-.}" >&2
        else
            printf '%s: adb was not found — install platform-tools, or pass --adb PATH\n' "$prog" >&2
        fi
        return 1
    }
    adb_pick_device "$adb" "$want" "$prog" || return 1
    serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
    return 0
}

# Prompt on stderr instead of stdout: stdout is often JSON that a caller parses.
# Reads stdin, so it can be exercised with a pipe in tests.
adb_device_choose() {
    local ready="$1" count choice resolved tries=0
    count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
    printf 'More than one device is connected:\n' >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2
    while [ "$tries" -lt 3 ]; do
        tries=$((tries + 1))
        printf 'Which device? [1-%d] or a serial: ' "$count" >&2
        IFS= read -r choice || return 1
        if resolved="$(adb_device_resolve "$ready" "$choice")"; then
            printf '%s' "$resolved"
            return 0
        fi
        printf '  not one of them\n' >&2
    done
    return 1
}

# Run a command with a deadline, because adb has no timeout of its own and a
# wedged server otherwise hangs the probe with nothing on screen. LIMIT is in
# tenths of a second. The child writes a sentinel when it finishes, so a finished
# process is never mistaken for a running one. 124 means "did not answer".
adb_device_exec() {
    local limit="$1" out="$2" pid waited=0 status=0
    shift 2
    rm -f "$out.done" "$out.status"
    ( "$@" >"$out" 2>"$out.err"; printf '%s' "$?" >"$out.status"; : >"$out.done" ) &
    pid=$!
    while [ ! -f "$out.done" ]; do
        if [ "$waited" -ge "$limit" ]; then
            # The adb client only: the server is a separate process and killing
            # it is the user's decision (adb kill-server).
            kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null
            sleep 0.2

```
```
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
menu_files() {
    local -a table=() f
    ui_heading 'Files'
    ui_panel 'Where things are' \
        "Project|$ROOT" \
        "config.env|$ROOT/config.env" \
        "Build tree|${BUILD_DIR#$ROOT/}"
    echo ""
    if [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$OUT_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r f; do
            table+=("$(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)|${f#$ROOT/}")
        done < <(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.apk' \) 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
        if [ "${#table[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            ui_table 'Size|Built file' "${table[@]}"
        else
            info "out/ exists but holds no .zip or .apk yet."
        fi
    else
        info "Nothing built yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
    fi
    pause_menu
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Docs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
menu_docs() {
    local files=() i
    ui_heading 'Docs'
    [ -d "$ROOT/docs" ] || { warn "docs/ is missing from this checkout."; pause_menu; return 0; }
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        files+=("$f")
    done < <(find "$ROOT/docs" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
    for i in "${!files[@]}"; do
        ui_item "$((i + 1))" "$(basename "${files[$i]}")"
    done
    echo ""
    menu_read "  number to read, Enter to go back >" || return 0
    case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
        ''|q) return 0 ;;
        *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number."; return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#files[@]}" ]; then
        warn "No such doc."
        return 0
    fi
    local pick="${files[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]}"
    echo ""
    if [ -t 1 ] && command -v less >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        less -R "$pick"
    else
        cat "$pick"
    fi
    return 0
}
```
