      ---
      
      A GSI boots generic: square screen corners, no cutout, a brightness curve written for some other panel, and an in-display fingerprint reader it cannot locate. This project writes a static RRO with the real values and packs it into one zip you install with Magisk, KernelSU / KSU Next or APatch.
      
      Two front ends run the same build off the same `config.env`:
      
      | | Windows | Linux | Termux |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | **Desktop app** | `treble-rro-creator.cmd` | `./treble-rro-creator.sh` | not available |
      | **Terminal menu** | `build.cmd` | `./build.sh` | `./build.sh` |
      
      The app has tabs for Build, config.env, Addons, Device (adb console), Auto Detect, UDFPS, Files and Docs. The menu offers the same jobs as numbered choices, and it is the whole interface on Termux or over ssh.
      
      ## Quick start
      
      ```bash
      git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
      cd treble-rro-creator
      ./build.sh          # Linux, Termux, Git Bash  → terminal menu
      ```
      
      ```bat
      build.cmd           :: Windows               → terminal menu
      ```
      
      1. `2` config.env — fill in codename, manufacturer, model, corner radius, status bar height.
      2. `5` Auto Detect, `6` UDFPS, `7` Match property — read those numbers off the phone instead of guessing.
      3. `1` → `2` Build. The module lands in `out/`.
      
      The first run installs what is missing: aapt2, zipalign, apksigner, Java and the `framework-res.apk` resource dictionary (about 40 MB on disk). Later runs skip straight to the menu.
      
      Full walkthroughs: [docs/gui.md](docs/gui.md) · [docs/windows.md](docs/windows.md) · [docs/termux.md](docs/termux.md).
      
      ## Requirements
      
      | Platform | Needs |
      |---|---|
      | **Windows** | [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) and JDK 17+ (`winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JDK`) |
      | **Linux** | `bash`, `curl` or `wget`, `unzip`, `zip`, JDK 17+ — `./build.sh setup` installs the rest |
      | **Termux** | Termux from **F-Droid**, not Google Play; `pkg install git`, then `./build.sh` |
      | **Phone** | A GSI-based ROM and any of Magisk, KernelSU, KSU Next, APatch |
      
      Root is only needed on Termux, where the phone probes read the device the tool is running on (`tsu ./build.sh`).
      
      ## What it configures
      
      | Area | Keys |
      |---|---|
      | Screen shape | `ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS`, `DISPLAY_CUTOUT`, waterfall edges |
      | Status bar | `STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT`, landscape variant, paddings, privacy dot |
      | Brightness | dim / dark / doze / min / max, auto-brightness, `power_profile.xml` |
      | Display timing | `DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE`, `PEAK_REFRESH_RATE`, AOD, doze, burn-in protection |
      | Fingerprint | `HAS_UDFPS`, `UDFPS_X` / `_Y` / `_RADIUS`, Samsung FOD, optional vendor HAL |
      | Radios and extras | `HAS_5G`, `HAS_VOLTE`, double-tap-to-wake |
      | Module only | addons (`src/module/addons.conf`), live WebUI page, `sepolicy.rule`, VINTF fragments |
      
      Everything past the first seven keys is optional. Reference: [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md).
      
      ## config.env
      
      Required:
      
      | Key | Example | Where it comes from |
      |---|---|---|
      | `DEVICE_CODENAME` | `r3q` | `adb shell getprop ro.product.device` |
      | `DEVICE_MANUFACTURER` | `samsung` | `getprop ro.product.manufacturer` |
      | `DEVICE_MODEL` | `SM-A908N` | `getprop ro.product.model` |
      | `DEVICE_PROP_NAME` | `persist.sys.overlay.r3q` | set by the module; leave empty for an unconditional overlay |
      | `DEVICE_PROP_VALUE` | `true` | value the key above must equal |
      | `ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS` | `135` | stock overlay, or measured on the screen |
      | `STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT` | `113` | stock overlay, or `dumpsys window` |
      
      Two things worth knowing before the first build:
      
      - **`src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` must be yours.** Until you replace it, the empty template is detected and left out of the APK rather than overwriting the GSI's battery and CPU data. See [docs/device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
      - **No `config.env` yet?** The first run offers the filled-in Samsung A90 5G example (`config.env.example`) or writes a placeholder that says what to edit.
      
      ## Commands
      
      | Command | Does |
      |---|---|
      | `./build.sh` | Terminal menu; a plain build when there is no terminal |
      | `./build.sh build` | Build, installing missing tools first |
      | `./build.sh setup` | Install or repair the toolchain |
      | `./build.sh doctor` | Check the toolchain, change nothing (exit 0 = ready) |
      | `./build.sh check` | Validate `config.env`, build nothing |
      | `./build.sh --dry-run` | Print every resource the config emits, build nothing |
      | `./build.sh clean` | Remove `stuff/build/` and `out/` |
      | `./build.sh clean --all` | Start over for a different device (restores templates) |
      | `./build.sh menu` | Force the menu when there is no terminal |
      
      Flags: `-y` / `--yes`, `--with-vendor-hals`, `--allow-unknown-resources`, `--force` (with `setup`), `--help`. Same words on Windows with `build.cmd`.
      
      `--dry-run` is the fast loop: it prints type, name, value and target APK for each resource without aapt2, signing or packaging.
      
      To check the project itself (scripts, resource writer, docs anchors), run `bash stuff/tests/run.sh` — this is what CI runs, and it needs no Android tools.
      
      ## Output
      
      | File | Use |
      |---|---|
      | `out/<name>-ksu.zip` | **The module.** Install in Magisk, KernelSU, KSU Next or APatch, then reboot |
      | `out/apks/<name>.apk` | Signed framework overlay |
      | `out/apks/<name>-systemui.apk` | Signed SystemUI overlay, when generated |
      | `out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip` | Source tree to submit to the [Doze-off overlay repo](https://github.com/Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay) |
      | `out/<name>-hardware-overlay-test.zip` | Test module for that source tree |
      | `out/<name>-overrides.txt` | Every resource marked `APPLIES` or `IGNORED` against the target framework |
      
      The `-ksu` suffix is historical; the zip is a standard module and works in all four managers. To copy the build to `/sdcard/treble-rro-creator`, use `8` Files → `1` Copy.
      
      > **KernelSU / KSU Next:** mount with Magic Mount, or Hybrid Mount in magic mode. OverlayFS mounts fine but turns one bad `sepolicy.rule` or VINTF fragment into a bootloop. Reasoning in [docs/how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md#the-flashable-module).
      
      Two more things the build will not do for you: do not copy the APKs into `/system/product/overlay/` by hand (dynamic partitions drop them and the module's permissions are missing), and expect the overlays to be static — Android enables them at boot, `cmd overlay enable` changes nothing afterwards.
      
      ## After installing
      
      **WebUI.** The module carries a page in `webroot/`. Open it from the manager (KernelSU, KSU Next, APatch) and change corner radius, status bar height or paddings without rebuilding: it writes the value into `resources.arsc` of the installed APK and restarts the framework. Magisk needs a WebUI host such as WebUI X, KsuWebUI or MMRL. Notes: [docs/webui.md](docs/webui.md).
      
      **Addons.** Tweaks that are not `config.env` keys: volume panel side, keep-screen-on, hide clock, 180° rotation, notch masking. Pick them in the app under Addons; live ones are re-applied on boot, overlay ones are written into the APK. List: [docs/addons.md](docs/addons.md).
      
      **Submitting to the GSI.** `out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip` contains the folders, the `overlay.mk` lines and a filled-in `HOW-TO-SUBMIT.md`. Read [docs/submission.md](docs/submission.md) before the pull request — the wiki's `+*brand/model*` pattern never matches, and the zip writes the exact property value instead.
      
      Verify an active overlay:
      
      ```bash
      adb shell cmd overlay list | grep <your-package>
      adb shell cmd overlay lookup <your-package> android:dimen/rounded_corner_radius
      ```
      
      ## Project layout
      
      | Path | Holds |
      |---|---|
      | `build.sh`, `build.cmd` | Entry point: menu and build |
      | `treble-rro-creator.sh`, `.cmd` | Desktop app; builds itself first |
      | `config.env` | Your device values |
      | `src/framework/res/`, `src/systemui/res/` | Overlay resources you edit |
      | `src/module/` | Module overrides, `sepolicy.rule`, `addons.conf` |
      | `src/webui/` | WebUI page and `apply.sh`, packed as `webroot/` |
      | `src/vendor/` | Extracted vendor HALs, optional and git-ignored |
      | `out/` | APKs, zips, override report (git-ignored) |
      | `gui/` | Desktop app sources (GTK + WebKit, Go) |
      | `docs/` | Guides |
      | `stuff/` | Scripts, templates, signing key, tests, downloaded tools, build scratch |
      
      ## Docs
      
      | Guide | Covers |
      |---|---|
      | [configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) | Every `config.env` key |
      | [detect.md](docs/detect.md) | Reading cutout, corners, status bar, refresh rate |
      | [udfps.md](docs/udfps.md) | Fingerprint coordinates and touch-panel FOD mode |
      | [addons.md](docs/addons.md) | Module tweaks |
      | [webui.md](docs/webui.md) | Editing values after install |
      | [submission.md](docs/submission.md) | Getting the overlay into the GSI |
      | [device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md) | Vendor HALs and `power_profile.xml` |
      | [gui.md](docs/gui.md) | Desktop app |
      | [windows.md](docs/windows.md) | Windows, PowerShell, WSL |
      | [termux.md](docs/termux.md) | Building on the phone |
      | [troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Build failures, bootloops, inactive overlays |
      | [how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md) | RRO mechanics and build steps |
      
      ## Upgrading from an older layout
      
      `build.sh` moves anything it finds in the old paths (`res/`, `systemui_overlay/res/`, `YOUR BACKUPS/`, root-level `scripts/` and friends) into the current ones on the next run, copying first and deleting afterwards. Old commands map straight across: `setup.sh` → `build.sh setup`, `setup.sh --doctor` → `build.sh doctor`, `cleanup.sh` → `build.sh clean`.
      
      ---
      
      Reference device: Samsung Galaxy A90 5G (SM-A908N / `r3q`). MIT licensed — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

  content: |
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay — Device Configuration
      # =============================================================================
      # Edit this file to match YOUR device, then run: ./build.sh/cmd
      #   Preview what these values produce (no tools, no build): ./build.sh/cmd --dry-run
      #   Check them only:                                        ./build.sh/cmd check
      #
      #   Lines starting with # are OFF. Remove the # to turn one on.
      #
      #   Manufacturer  adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer
      #   Model         adb shell getprop ro.product.model
      #   Codename      adb shell getprop ro.product.device
      #                 (on a GSI this often shows the ROM's name — see below)
      #
      # Reference values: config.env.example (Samsung Galaxy A90 5G)
      # =============================================================================
      
      # ── Device identity ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Drives the module/overlay names. Codename also names the match property below.
      DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="Xiaomi"
      DEVICE_MODEL="Redmi Note 17"
      DEVICE_CODENAME="Zephyr"
      # Battery/power profile: src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml (docs/device-extraction.md)
      
      # ── Module metadata ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # What Magisk/KernelSU/APatch show on the Modules page, and the version of both
      # APKs. Bump OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE on every release — it must be a whole number.
      OVERLAY_VERSION="2.0"
      OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE=2
      # Author of the module. Left empty, module.prop falls back to DEVICE_MANUFACTURER.
      MODULE_AUTHOR="uzbforce"
      
      # ── Overlay activation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # The overlay applies only while DEVICE_PROP_NAME == DEVICE_PROP_VALUE.
      # Keep persist.sys.overlay.<codename> = true: it is readable from every domain
      # and build.sh sets it at boot before zygote. DEVICE_PROP_NAME="" drops the
      # check entirely (module only ever lands on this one device).
      #   Why not ro.product.device? On a GSI that is the ROM's name (mivendor,
      #   phh_treble, …) and zygote cannot read the prop holding the real codename.
      #   Details + per-device prop table: docs/configuration.md#choosing-the-match-property
      # Is it really applied? (an [x] in `cmd overlay list` does not prove it)
      #   adb shell cmd overlay lookup <package> android:dimen/status_bar_height_default
      #
      #  If you want to use a different property, set it here and also in
      #  docs/configuration.md#choosing-the-match-property
      DEVICE_PROP_NAME="persist.sys.overlay.zephyr"
      DEVICE_PROP_VALUE="true"
      
      # ── Overlay Priority ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      OVERLAY_PRIORITY=628
      OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI=9999
      
      # ── Display ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Screen corner radius. Also the reference for the padding below.
      ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS=135
      # Status bar height in px, portrait and landscape. The effective height is
      # max(this value, display-cutout inset).
      STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT=113
      STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE=70
      
      # ── Status bar content padding ────────────────────────────────────────────
      #   >>> OFF BY DEFAULT — uncomment the three STATUS_BAR_* lines to turn it on.
      #
      # Moves the clock and the status icons away from the left/right edges, so they
      # do not sit under the rounded corners. Left commented, the bar keeps the
      # ROM/GSI layout.
      #
      #   STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START / _END   SystemUI status_bar_padding_*  <- GSI obeys this
      #   STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING        framework rounded_corner_content_padding
      #
      # Set all three to the SAME number. Rule of thumb: ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS / 3
      # (15-20 should fit a 120-150px corner). The two paths never stack.
      #   Measured on this device: framework value alone did nothing on the GSI,
      #   the SystemUI pair moved the clock 1:1.
      # More: docs/configuration.md#status-bar-content-padding-start--end
      #STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING=15
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START=15
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_END=15
      
      # Rarely needed fine-tuning of the same block (all optional):
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_TOP=0
      #STATUS_BAR_ICONS_PADDING_START=3dp
      #STATUS_BAR_ICONS_PADDING_END=4dp
      #STATUS_BAR_DOT_MIN_PADDING=20dp
      # Turns the camera/mic privacy dot off (also frees its 20dp end-side reserve).
      #HAS_PRIVACY_DOT=false
      # Notch / Display Cutout (SVG Path)
      # Leave commented out if your device has no notch.
      # Reference (Samsung Infinity-U):
      DISPLAY_CUTOUT="M 0,0 H -29 V 118 H 29 V 0 H 0 Z"
      
      # ── Waterfall panel (optional) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
      # A waterfall screen curves down the sides, so the framework reserves a strip
      # there and every app keeps its content out of it — that is the gutter buttons
      # and lists show on the left and right. These are the four insets of that strip
      # (px, or dp). Commented out, the ROM's own values stay. Only the edges your
      # panel actually curves need a value.
      # More: docs/configuration.md#waterfall-cutout-band
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_LEFT=40
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_RIGHT=40
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_TOP=0
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_BOTTOM=0
      
      # ── Fingerprint (UDFPS) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # HAS_UDFPS also registers config_biometric_sensors (0:2:15 by default).
      # The coordinates are optional: when all three are set they are written to
      # config_udfps_sensor_props. When they are not set, the GSI/HAL reports the
      # sensor location itself and the array is left untouched.
      HAS_UDFPS=true
      UDFPS_X=540
      UDFPS_Y=2198
      UDFPS_RADIUS=89
      # Override the biometric sensor list (id:modality:strength; separate with ;)
      #CONFIG_BIOMETRIC_SENSORS="0:2:15"
      HAS_SAMSUNG_FINGERPRINT=false
      
      # ── Samsung Vendor Service Control ────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_SAMSUNG_FOD=false
      HAS_SAMSUNG_VIBRATOR=false
      
      # ── Light sensor type ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE="android.sensor.light"
      
      # ── Refresh Rate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE=120
      PEAK_REFRESH_RATE=120
      
      # ── Brightness (0-255) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      BRIGHTNESS_DIM=10
      BRIGHTNESS_DARK=1
      BRIGHTNESS_DOZE=1
      BRIGHTNESS_DEFAULT=102
      BRIGHTNESS_MIN=10
      BRIGHTNESS_MAX=255
      
      # ── Feature Flags ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_AOD=true
      HAS_DOZE=true
      DOZE_SUSPEND_UNSUPPORTED=false
      HAS_5G=false
      HAS_VOLTE=true
      HAS_BURN_IN_PROTECTION=true
      HAS_DOUBLE_TAP_WAKE=true
      
      # ── Vendor HAL flags ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_VENDOR_FINGERPRINT_HAL=false
      HAS_VENDOR_VIBRATOR_HAL=false
      
      # ── Build Tools ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      PLATFORM_JAR="/usr/share/android-framework-res/framework-res.apk"
      PLATFORM_KEY="stuff/keys/platform.pk8"
      PLATFORM_CERT="stuff/keys/platform.x509.pem"
      
      # ── Advanced Build Settings (DO NOT EDIT) ─────────────────────────────────
      # The values below are for aapt2 dictionary compatibility (linking against 
      # the Android 13 resource dictionary). 
      #
      # ⚠ DO NOT CHANGE THESE to match your GSI version. 
      # They are for build-time linking only and do NOT affect GSI compatibility.
      # Changing them will likely cause "Resource not found" errors.
      COMPILE_SDK_VERSION=35
      ANDROID_VERSION="15"
      MIN_SDK_VERSION=33
      TARGET_SDK_VERSION=34
      
      # ── Overlay repo submission (Doze-off, submission only) ───────────────────
      # These affect only out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip: the source tree you submit
      # as a pull request to github.com/Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay (base branch
      # pie), so the GSI builds ship the overlay with no module. Upstream
      # TrebleDroid/vendor_hardware_overlay takes the same tree.
      # Step-by-step: docs/submission.md
      #
      # The device must match the preinstalled overlay without a module, so this uses
      # a property that already exists on it. android:requiredSystemPropertyValue is
      # compared with plain string equality — no "*" or "+" globs (the wiki's
      # "+*brand/model*" form never matches; the overlay stays inert).
      #   adb shell getprop ro.product.vendor.device
      # ro.product.vendor.device comes from the vendor partition: it survives a GSI
      # flash and does not change between OTAs. The full ro.vendor.build.fingerprint
      # works too, but every OTA changes it. An empty HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP submits an
      # always-active overlay.
      # Default value: the DEVICE_CODENAME above.
      HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP="ro.product.device"
      HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE="zephyr"
      #
      # The repo rejects a priority that another overlay already uses. Left unset, the
      # build picks a free number from the device name; `bash tests/tests.sh` in a
      # clone of the repo prints its own suggestion before you open the pull request.
      HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY=9999
      
      # ── OPTIONAL STOCK VALUES (Extract from your stock firmware) ────────────────
      # Uncomment these and set values from your STOCK OVERLAY APKs.
      # Extract them following the TrebleDroid guide:
      #   https://github.com/TrebleDroid/treble_experimentations/wiki/How-to-create-an-overlay%3F
      #
      # ⚠ These are OPTIONAL — the build works without them, but for best results
      #    extract your device's actual values from the stock product overlay APK.
      #    Only include values that DIFFER between product and vendor overlays!
      # =============================================================================
      
      # --- Radio / Telephony ---
      #CONFIG_RADIO_ACCESS_FAMILY="GSM|WCDMA|LTE|NR"
      #SKIP_RESTORING_NETWORK_SELECTION=true
      #CONFIG_SWITCH_PHONE_ON_VOICE_REG_STATE_CHANGE=false
      
      # --- Biometric / Fingerprint ---
      #CONFIG_BIOMETRIC_SENSORS="0:2:15"  # sensorId:modality:strength (multi=semicolon)
      
      # --- Display / Power ---
      #CONFIG_FILL_MAIN_BUILTIN_DISPLAY_CUTOUT=true
      #CONFIG_POWER_DECOUPLE_INTERACTIVE_MODE_FROM_DISPLAY=true
      #CONFIG_POWER_DECOUPLE_AUTO_SUSPEND_MODE_FROM_DISPLAY=true
      #CONFIG_DISPLAY_BLANKS_AFTER_DOZE=false
      #CONFIG_DOZE_SUPPORTS_AOD_WALLPAPER=false
      
      # --- Audio ---
      #CONFIG_SUPPORT_AUDIO_SOURCE_UNPROCESSED=false
      #CONFIG_CAMERA_SOUND_FORCED=false
      #CONFIG_USE_DEV_INPUT_EVENT_FOR_AUDIO_JACK=true
      
      # --- Connectivity ---
      #CONFIG_WIFI_DISPLAY_SUPPORTS_PROTECTED_BUFFERS=true
      #CONFIG_CARRIER_VOLTE_AVAILABLE=true
      #CONFIG_CARRIER_VT_AVAILABLE=true
      #CONFIG_CARRIER_WFC_IMS_AVAILABLE=true

      # --- Input ---

      # --- Other Stock Values (Strings / Integers) ---
      #CONFIG_DOZE_UDFPS_LONG_PRESS_SENSOR_TYPE="org.lineageos.sensor.udfps"
      
      # --- Auto-brightness Arrays (space-separated values) ---
      # Extract these from your stock product overlay APK!
      # AUTO_BRIGHTNESS_BACKLIGHT_VALUES needs one MORE value than LEVELS.

      # =============================================================================

      #
      # Finding your values:
      #   Manufacturer:     adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer
      #   Model:            adb shell getprop ro.product.model
      #   Device codename:  adb shell getprop ro.product.device
      #
      # Every value is explained in docs/configuration.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      # ── Device identity ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="samsung"
      DEVICE_MODEL="SM-A908N"
      DEVICE_CODENAME="r3q"
      
      # ── Module metadata ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # What Magisk/KernelSU/APatch show on the Modules page, and the version of both
      # APKs. Bump OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE on every release — it must be a whole number.
      OVERLAY_VERSION="1.0"
      OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE=1
      # Author of the module. Left empty, module.prop falls back to DEVICE_MANUFACTURER.
      MODULE_AUTHOR="samsung"
      
      # ── Overlay activation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # The overlay applies only while DEVICE_PROP_NAME == DEVICE_PROP_VALUE.
      # Keep persist.sys.overlay.<codename> = true: it is readable from every domain
      # and build.sh sets it at boot before zygote. DEVICE_PROP_NAME="" drops the
      # check entirely.
      #   Why not ro.product.device? Framework overlays are matched by zygote, which
      #   on many GSIs cannot read ro.product.bootimage.* / ro.vendor.* (SELinux):
      #   `cmd overlay list` shows [x] but nothing is applied.
      #   Details + per-device prop table: docs/configuration.md#choosing-the-match-property
      DEVICE_PROP_NAME="persist.sys.overlay.r3q"
      DEVICE_PROP_VALUE="true"
      
      # ── Overlay Priority ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      OVERLAY_PRIORITY=628
      OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI=9999
      
      # ── Display ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Screen corner radius. Also the reference for the padding below.
      ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS=100
      # Status bar height in px, portrait and landscape. The effective height is
      # max(this value, display-cutout inset).
      STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT=76
      #STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE=24
      
      # ── Status bar content padding ────────────────────────────────────────────
      #   >>> OFF BY DEFAULT — uncomment the three STATUS_BAR_* lines to turn it on.
      #
      # Moves the clock and the status icons away from the left/right edges, so they
      # do not sit under the rounded corners. Left commented, the bar keeps the
      # ROM/GSI layout.
      #
      #   STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START / _END   SystemUI status_bar_padding_*  <- GSI obeys this
      #   STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING        framework rounded_corner_content_padding
      #
      # Set all three to the SAME number. Rule of thumb: ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS / 3
      # (34 for a 100px corner). The two paths never stack.
      # More: docs/configuration.md#status-bar-content-padding-start--end
      #STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING=34
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START=34
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_END=34
      
      # Rarely needed fine-tuning of the same block (all optional):
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_TOP=0
      #STATUS_BAR_ICONS_PADDING_START=3dp
      #STATUS_BAR_ICONS_PADDING_END=4dp
      #STATUS_BAR_DOT_MIN_PADDING=20dp
      # Turns the camera/mic privacy dot off (also frees its 20dp end-side reserve).
      #HAS_PRIVACY_DOT=false
      
      # Notch / Display Cutout (SVG Path)
      # Leave commented out if your device has no notch.
      # Reference (Samsung Infinity-U):
      #DISPLAY_CUTOUT="M-35.93,0C-29.26,0,-23.46,3.85,-22.46,9.56l.12.73a22.69,22.69,0,0,0,44.68,0l.12-.73C23.5,3.85,29.26,0,35.93,0Z @dp"
      
      # ── Waterfall panel (optional) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
      # A waterfall screen curves down the sides, so the framework reserves a strip
      # there and every app keeps its content out of it — that is the gutter buttons
      # and lists show on the left and right. These are the four insets of that strip
      # (px, or dp). Commented out, the ROM's own values stay. Only the edges your
      # panel actually curves need a value.
      # More: docs/configuration.md#waterfall-cutout-band
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_LEFT=40
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_RIGHT=40
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_TOP=0
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_BOTTOM=0
      
      # ── Fingerprint (UDFPS) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # HAS_UDFPS registers config_biometric_sensors (0:2:15 unless overridden).
      # The coordinates are optional; when set they fill config_udfps_sensor_props.
      # NOTE: 540 / 2145 / 114 are the Galaxy A90 5G's values. They are not
      # defaults — copy another device's geometry and the icon lands away from the
      # sensor. Find your own values with docs/udfps.md.
      HAS_UDFPS=true
      UDFPS_X=540
      UDFPS_Y=2145
      UDFPS_RADIUS=114
      # Colour of the icon SystemUI paints on the sensor (SystemUI's
      # config_udfpsColor). #rrggbb or #aarrggbb; the leading # is optional and the
      # AOSP default is opaque white. A grey, dim spot is normally the panel's local
      # HBM not being switched on, not this value (see docs/udfps.md).
      #UDFPS_COLOR=#ffffff
      HAS_SAMSUNG_FINGERPRINT=true
      
      # ── Samsung Vendor Service Control ────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_SAMSUNG_FOD=true
      HAS_SAMSUNG_VIBRATOR=true
      
      # ── Light sensor type ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE="com.samsung.sensor.physical_light"
      
      # ── Auto-brightness ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_AUTO_BRIGHTNESS=true
      
      # ── Refresh Rate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE=60
      PEAK_REFRESH_RATE=60
      
      # ── Brightness (0-255) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      BRIGHTNESS_DIM=15
      BRIGHTNESS_DARK=3
      BRIGHTNESS_DOZE=60
      BRIGHTNESS_DEFAULT=128
      BRIGHTNESS_MIN=0
      BRIGHTNESS_MAX=255
      
      # ── Feature Flags ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_AOD=true
      HAS_DOZE=true
      DOZE_SUSPEND_UNSUPPORTED=true   # Samsung hwcomposer can't handle DOZE_SUSPEND
      HAS_5G=true
      HAS_VOLTE=true
      HAS_BURN_IN_PROTECTION=true
      HAS_DOUBLE_TAP_WAKE=true
      
      # ── Vendor HAL flags ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_VENDOR_FINGERPRINT_HAL=true
      HAS_VENDOR_VIBRATOR_HAL=true
      
      # ── Build Tools ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      PLATFORM_JAR="/usr/share/android-framework-res/framework-res.apk"
      PLATFORM_KEY="stuff/keys/platform.pk8"
      PLATFORM_CERT="stuff/keys/platform.x509.pem"
      
      # ── Advanced Build Settings (DO NOT EDIT) ─────────────────────────────────
      # The values below are for aapt2 dictionary compatibility (linking against 
      # the Android 13 resource dictionary). 
      #
      # ⚠ DO NOT CHANGE THESE to match your GSI version. 
      # They are for build-time linking only and do NOT affect GSI compatibility.
      # Changing them will likely cause "Resource not found" errors.
      COMPILE_SDK_VERSION=35
      ANDROID_VERSION="15"
      MIN_SDK_VERSION=33
      TARGET_SDK_VERSION=34
      
      # ── Overlay repo submission (Doze-off, submission only) ───────────────────
      # These affect only out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip: the source tree you submit
      # as a pull request to github.com/Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay (base branch
      # pie), so the GSI builds ship the overlay with no module. Upstream
      # TrebleDroid/vendor_hardware_overlay takes the same tree.
      # Step-by-step: docs/submission.md
      #
      # The device must match the preinstalled overlay without a module, so this uses
      # a property that already exists on it. android:requiredSystemPropertyValue is
      # compared with plain string equality — no "*" or "+" globs (the wiki's
      # "+*brand/model*" form never matches; the overlay stays inert).
      #   adb shell getprop ro.product.vendor.device
      # ro.product.vendor.device comes from the vendor partition: it survives a GSI
      # flash and does not change between OTAs. The full ro.vendor.build.fingerprint
      # works too, but every OTA changes it. An empty HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP submits an
      # always-active overlay.
      #HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP="ro.product.vendor.device"
      #HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE="r3q"
      #
      # The repo rejects a priority that another overlay already uses. Left unset, the
      # build picks a free number from the device name; `bash tests/tests.sh` in a
      # clone of the repo prints its own suggestion before you open the pull request.
      #HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY=1000
      
      # ── OPTIONAL STOCK VALUES (Extract from your stock firmware) ────────────────
      # Uncomment these and set values from your STOCK OVERLAY APKs.
      # Extract them following the TrebleDroid guide:
      #   https://github.com/TrebleDroid/treble_experimentations/wiki/How-to-create-an-overlay%3F
      #
      # To extract: apktool d framework-res__auto_generated_rro_product.apk -o product/
      # Then take values from product/res/values/bools.xml, config.xml, etc.
      # Only include values that differ between product and vendor overlays!
      # =============================================================================
      
      # --- Radio / Telephony ---
      #CONFIG_RADIO_ACCESS_FAMILY="GSM|WCDMA|LTE|NR"
      #SKIP_RESTORING_NETWORK_SELECTION=true
      #CONFIG_SWITCH_PHONE_ON_VOICE_REG_STATE_CHANGE=false
      
      # --- Biometric / Fingerprint ---
      #CONFIG_BIOMETRIC_SENSORS="0:2:15"  # sensorId:modality:strength (multi=semicolon)
      
      # --- Display / Power ---
      #CONFIG_FILL_MAIN_BUILTIN_DISPLAY_CUTOUT=true
      #CONFIG_POWER_DECOUPLE_INTERACTIVE_MODE_FROM_DISPLAY=true
      #CONFIG_POWER_DECOUPLE_AUTO_SUSPEND_MODE_FROM_DISPLAY=true
      #CONFIG_DISPLAY_BLANKS_AFTER_DOZE=false
      #CONFIG_DOZE_SUPPORTS_AOD_WALLPAPER=false
      
      # --- Audio ---
      #CONFIG_SUPPORT_AUDIO_SOURCE_UNPROCESSED=false
      #CONFIG_CAMERA_SOUND_FORCED=false
      #CONFIG_USE_DEV_INPUT_EVENT_FOR_AUDIO_JACK=true
      
      # --- Connectivity ---

      #CONFIG_CARRIER_VT_AVAILABLE=true

      # --- Input ---

      # --- Other Stock Values (Strings / Integers) ---
      #CONFIG_DOZE_UDFPS_LONG_PRESS_SENSOR_TYPE="org.lineageos.sensor.udfps"
      
      # --- Auto-brightness Arrays (space-separated values) ---

- path: stuff/scripts/common.sh
  content: |
          # Author is free text; only an empty or placeholder one is replaced.
          [[ -z "${MODULE_AUTHOR:-}" || "${MODULE_AUTHOR}" == *"<"* ]] && MODULE_AUTHOR="${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}"
      
          [[ "${LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE:-}" == *"<"* ]] && LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE="android.sensor.light"
          [[ "${DEVICE_MODEL:-}" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_MODEL="Generic Device"
          # Status bar landscape height: only set fallback if explicitly a placeholder
          # (otherwise leave empty so the status bar section skips it)
          [[ "${STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE:-}" == *"<"* ]] && STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE=24
      
          return 0
      }
      
      # Does this power_profile.xml contain actual data, or is it the empty template?
      power_profile_is_placeholder() {
          local f="$1"
          [ -f "$f" ] || return 0
          ! grep -qE '<item[[:space:]>]' "$f"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Portable helpers
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Convert an MSYS path to a native Windows path (no-op elsewhere).
      to_win_path() {
          if $IS_WINDOWS && command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              cygpath -w "$1"
          else
              printf '%s' "$1"
          fi
      }
      
      # Create <dest> from the contents of <src>, using whichever zip tool exists:
      # Info-ZIP (Linux/Termux), 7-Zip, or PowerShell's ZipArchive API (Windows).
      create_zip() {
          local src="$1" dest="$2"
          rm -f "$dest"
          if command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ( cd "$src" && zip -r "$dest" . >/dev/null ) || return 1
          elif command -v 7z >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ( cd "$src" && 7z a -tzip "$dest" . >/dev/null ) || return 1

- path: stuff/scripts/common.sh
  content: |
          cp -f "$1" "$2"
      }
      
      toolchain_missing() {
          local missing="" t
          for t in aapt2 zipalign apksigner; do
              [ "$t" = "zipalign" ] && zipalign_optional && continue
              tool_ready "$t" || missing="$missing $t"
          done
          command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing java"
          framework_res_path >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing framework-res.apk"
          printf '%s' "${missing# }"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Device identity
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Turns the raw DEVICE_* values from config.env into the module id, the overlay
      # package names and the match condition. Called by build.sh right after
      # config.env is sourced, and by the standalone scripts (manifest.sh,
      # hardware-overlay.sh) so they agree with the build.
      #
      # Users only need to set DEVICE_CODENAME and DEVICE_MANUFACTURER; everything
      # else is derived. A value containing "<" is a template placeholder.
      derive_overlay_identity() {
          [ -z "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER:-}" ] || [[ "$DEVICE_MANUFACTURER" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="generic"
          [ -z "${DEVICE_CODENAME:-}" ]     || [[ "$DEVICE_CODENAME" == *"<"* ]]     && DEVICE_CODENAME="generic"
      
          # Clean manufacturer for Java package names (lowercase alphanumeric only)
          SAFE_MANUFACTURER=$(printf '%s' "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]//g')
      
          # Clean codename for package name: replace non-alphanumeric with dots
          # e.g. "Infinix-X6852" → "infinix.x6852" (dots are valid Java package separators)
          PACKAGE_SEGMENT=$(printf '%s' "${DEVICE_CODENAME}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]/./g' | sed 's/\.\.*/./g' | sed 's/^\.//;s/\.$//')
      
          # Module ids are shared by Magisk, KernelSU and APatch: they must match
          # ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$ (no spaces or slashes). Use the already-cleaned
          # manufacturer/codename pieces for the generated default; an explicit
          # OVERLAY_NAME in config.env is kept as-is.
          DEFAULT_MANUFACTURER="${SAFE_MANUFACTURER:-generic}"
          DEFAULT_CODENAME="${PACKAGE_SEGMENT:-generic}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_NAME:-}" ]        || [[ "$OVERLAY_NAME" == *"<"* ]]        && OVERLAY_NAME="treble-overlay-${DEFAULT_MANUFACTURER}-${DEFAULT_CODENAME}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_PACKAGE:-}" ]     || [[ "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE" == *"<"* ]]     && OVERLAY_PACKAGE="me.phh.treble.overlay.${SAFE_MANUFACTURER}.${PACKAGE_SEGMENT}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI:-}" ] || [[ "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI" == *"<"* ]] && OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI="${OVERLAY_PACKAGE}.systemui"
          [[ "${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE:-}" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_PROP_VALUE="${DEVICE_CODENAME}"
          # Only placeholders are replaced. An EMPTY DEVICE_PROP_NAME is meaningful: it
          # builds an overlay with no match condition (always active), which is the safe
          # default for framework overlays — see the Overlay Activation section of
          # config.env for why ro.product.* conditions fail on GSI setups.
          [[ "${DEVICE_PROP_NAME:-}" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_PROP_NAME="ro.product.device"
      
          if [ -n "${DEVICE_PROP_NAME:-}" ]; then
              OVERLAY_CONDITION="        android:requiredSystemPropertyName=\"${DEVICE_PROP_NAME}\"
              android:requiredSystemPropertyValue=\"${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE}\" />"
              CONDITION_DESC="${DEVICE_PROP_NAME} == \"${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE}\""
          else
              OVERLAY_CONDITION="        />"
              CONDITION_DESC="none (always active)"
          fi
      
          [ -z "${ANDROID_VERSION:-}" ]     && ANDROID_VERSION="14"
          [ -z "${COMPILE_SDK_VERSION:-}" ] && COMPILE_SDK_VERSION="34"
          [ -z "${MIN_SDK_VERSION:-}" ]     && MIN_SDK_VERSION="34"
          [ -z "${TARGET_SDK_VERSION:-}" ]  && TARGET_SDK_VERSION="34"
      
          # Module metadata: module.prop, both manifests and the hardware overlay
          # read these. Empty or still a <placeholder> falls back to the release
          # values, so a config.env written before these keys existed still builds.
          [[ -z "${OVERLAY_VERSION:-}" || "${OVERLAY_VERSION}" == *"<"* ]] && OVERLAY_VERSION="1.0"
          [[ -z "${OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE:-}" || "${OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE}" == *"<"* ]] && OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE="1"
          # Author is free text; only an empty or placeholder one is replaced.
          [[ -z "${MODULE_AUTHOR:-}" || "${MODULE_AUTHOR}" == *"<"* ]] && MODULE_AUTHOR="${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}"
      
          [[ "${LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE:-}" == *"<"* ]] && LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE="android.sensor.light"
          [[ "${DEVICE_MODEL:-}" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_MODEL="Generic Device"

VALIDATE_WARNINGS=0
VALIDATE_NOTES=0

_v_warn() {
    VALIDATE_WARNINGS=$((VALIDATE_WARNINGS + 1))
    if command -v warn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        warn "$*"
    else
        echo "  ! $*" >&2
    fi
}

_v_note() {
    VALIDATE_NOTES=$((VALIDATE_NOTES + 1))
    if command -v info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        info "$*"
    else
        echo "  - $*"
    fi
}

# is_set <value> -> true when the value is neither empty nor a placeholder.
is_set() {
    local v="${1:-}"
    [ -n "$v" ] || return 1
    case "$v" in *'<'*) return 1 ;; esac   # <codename>, <value>
    [[ "$v" =~ ^0+$ ]] && return 1        # 000, 0000
    return 0
}

_v_int() { printf '%s' "${1:-}" | tr -dc '0-9'; }

# list_count / list_ints / list_numbers come from resources.sh when build.sh
# runs; define them here for the standalone case.
command -v list_count >/dev/null 2>&1 || list_count() {
    local n=0 v
    for v in $1; do n=$((n + 1)); done
    printf '%s' "$n"
}
command -v list_ints >/dev/null 2>&1 || list_ints() {
    local v
    for v in $1; do [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1; done
    return 0
}
command -v list_numbers >/dev/null 2>&1 || list_numbers() {
    local v
    for v in $1; do [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]] || return 1; done
    return 0
}

# The bug this guards: `clean --all` copied config.env from a frozen file, so a
# full clean handed back a version from an older commit. The copies below are
# now only the no-.git fallback, so they must equal the committed blob — not the
# working file, because local edits to config.env are normal.
step "template fallbacks match the release"
if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    copy_status=0
    check_copy() {
        local rel="$1" copy="$2"
        if [ ! -f "$copy" ]; then
            echo "missing fallback: $copy"
            copy_status=1
        elif ! git show "HEAD:$rel" | diff -q - "$copy" >/dev/null; then
            echo "$copy differs from HEAD:$rel — run: git show HEAD:$rel > $copy"
            copy_status=1
        fi
    }
    check_copy config.env stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    check_copy src/module/sepolicy.rule stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
    if [ "$copy_status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "fallbacks match"; else status=1; fi
else
    echo "not a git checkout — skipping"
fi

# restore_from_release() is what clean.sh and build.sh call. Run it against a
# throwaway repository with a deliberately stale fallback, and once without
# .git, because "start over" silently returning old values is the failure mode.
step "restore picks the release, not the stale copy"
restore_here="$(pwd)"
restore_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-restore)"
if (
    cd "$restore_tmp" || exit 1
    git init -q . && git config user.email t@example.com && git config user.name t || exit 1
    # No .gitattributes here, and Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true,
    # which would check the file back out with CRLF and fail the greps below.
    git config core.autocrlf false
    mkdir -p src/module stuff/templates/recoveries
    printf 'KEY="released"\n' > config.env
    printf 'released rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
    printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
    git add -A && git commit -qm one || exit 1
    # The user edits both files; the fallback copies are stale.
    printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
    printf 'my rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
    ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env" && restore_from_release src/module/sepolicy.rule "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 2
    grep -qx 'KEY="released"' config.env || { echo "git restore did not win: $(cat config.env)"; exit 3; }
    grep -qx 'released rules' src/module/sepolicy.rule || exit 4
    # No .git (a zip download): the bundled copy is the only source left.
    rm -rf .git
    printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
    ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 6
    grep -q 'STALE' config.env || { echo "fallback was not used without git"; exit 7; }
); then
    echo "restore behaves"
else

- path: config.env
  content: |
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay — Device Configuration
      # =============================================================================
      # Edit this file to match YOUR device, then run: ./build.sh/cmd
      #   Preview what these values produce (no tools, no build): ./build.sh/cmd --dry-run
      #   Check them only:                                        ./build.sh/cmd check
      #
      #   Lines starting with # are OFF. Remove the # to turn one on.
      #
      #   Manufacturer  adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer
      #   Model         adb shell getprop ro.product.model
      #   Codename      adb shell getprop ro.product.device
      #                 (on a GSI this often shows the ROM's name — see below)
      #
      # Reference values: config.env.example (Samsung Galaxy A90 5G)
      # =============================================================================
      
      # ── Device identity ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Drives the module/overlay names. Codename also names the match property below.
      DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="Xiaomi"
      DEVICE_MODEL="Redmi Note 17"
      DEVICE_CODENAME="Zephyr"
      # Battery/power profile: src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml (docs/device-extraction.md)
      
      # ── Module metadata ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # What Magisk/KernelSU/APatch show on the Modules page, and the version of both
      # APKs. Bump OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE on every release — it must be a whole number.
      OVERLAY_VERSION="2.0"
      OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE=2
      # Author of the module. Left empty, module.prop falls back to DEVICE_MANUFACTURER.
      MODULE_AUTHOR="uzbforce"
      
      # ── Overlay activation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # The overlay applies only while DEVICE_PROP_NAME == DEVICE_PROP_VALUE.
      # Keep persist.sys.overlay.<codename> = true: it is readable from every domain
      # and build.sh sets it at boot before zygote. DEVICE_PROP_NAME="" drops the
      # check entirely (module only ever lands on this one device).
      #   Why not ro.product.device? On a GSI that is the ROM's name (mivendor,
      #   phh_treble, …) and zygote cannot read the prop holding the real codename.
      #   Details + per-device prop table: docs/configuration.md#choosing-the-match-property
      # Is it really applied? (an [x] in `cmd overlay list` does not prove it)
      #   adb shell cmd overlay lookup <package> android:dimen/status_bar_height_default
      #
      #  If you want to use a different property, set it here and also in
      #  docs/configuration.md#choosing-the-match-property
      DEVICE_PROP_NAME="persist.sys.overlay.zephyr"
      DEVICE_PROP_VALUE="true"
      
      # ── Overlay Priority ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      OVERLAY_PRIORITY=628
      OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI=9999
      
      # ── Display ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Screen corner radius. Also the reference for the padding below.
      ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS=135
      # Status bar height in px, portrait and landscape. The effective height is
      # max(this value, display-cutout inset).
      STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT=113
      STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE=70
      
      # ── Status bar content padding ────────────────────────────────────────────
      #   >>> OFF BY DEFAULT — uncomment the three STATUS_BAR_* lines to turn it on.
      #
      # Moves the clock and the status icons away from the left/right edges, so they
      # do not sit under the rounded corners. Left commented, the bar keeps the
      # ROM/GSI layout.
      #
      #   STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START / _END   SystemUI status_bar_padding_*  <- GSI obeys this
      #   STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING        framework rounded_corner_content_padding
      #
      # Set all three to the SAME number. Rule of thumb: ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS / 3
      # (15-20 should fit a 120-150px corner). The two paths never stack.
      #   Measured on this device: framework value alone did nothing on the GSI,
      #   the SystemUI pair moved the clock 1:1.
      # More: docs/configuration.md#status-bar-content-padding-start--end
      #STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING=15
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START=15
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_END=15
      
      # Rarely needed fine-tuning of the same block (all optional):
      #STATUS_BAR_PADDING_TOP=0
      #STATUS_BAR_ICONS_PADDING_START=3dp
      #STATUS_BAR_ICONS_PADDING_END=4dp
      #STATUS_BAR_DOT_MIN_PADDING=20dp
      # Turns the camera/mic privacy dot off (also frees its 20dp end-side reserve).
      #HAS_PRIVACY_DOT=false
      # Notch / Display Cutout (SVG Path)
      # Leave commented out if your device has no notch.
      # Reference (Samsung Infinity-U):
      DISPLAY_CUTOUT="M 0,0 H -29 V 118 H 29 V 0 H 0 Z"
      
      # ── Waterfall panel (optional) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
      # A waterfall screen curves down the sides, so the framework reserves a strip
      # there and every app keeps its content out of it — that is the gutter buttons
      # and lists show on the left and right. These are the four insets of that strip
      # (px, or dp). Commented out, the ROM's own values stay. Only the edges your
      # panel actually curves need a value.
      # More: docs/configuration.md#waterfall-cutout-band
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_LEFT=40
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_RIGHT=40
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_TOP=0
      #WATERFALL_EDGE_BOTTOM=0
      
      # ── Fingerprint (UDFPS) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # HAS_UDFPS also registers config_biometric_sensors (0:2:15 by default).
      # The coordinates are optional: when all three are set they are written to
      # config_udfps_sensor_props. When they are not set, the GSI/HAL reports the
      # sensor location itself and the array is left untouched.
      HAS_UDFPS=true
      UDFPS_X=540
      UDFPS_Y=2198
      UDFPS_RADIUS=89
      # Override the biometric sensor list (id:modality:strength; separate with ;)
      #CONFIG_BIOMETRIC_SENSORS="0:2:15"
      HAS_SAMSUNG_FINGERPRINT=false
      
      # ── Samsung Vendor Service Control ────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_SAMSUNG_FOD=false
      HAS_SAMSUNG_VIBRATOR=false
      
      # ── Light sensor type ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE="android.sensor.light"
      
      # ── Refresh Rate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE=120
      PEAK_REFRESH_RATE=120
      
      # ── Brightness (0-255) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      BRIGHTNESS_DIM=10
      BRIGHTNESS_DARK=1

      BRIGHTNESS_DOZE=1
      BRIGHTNESS_DEFAULT=102
      BRIGHTNESS_MIN=10
      BRIGHTNESS_MAX=255
      
      # ── Feature Flags ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_AOD=true
      HAS_DOZE=true
      DOZE_SUSPEND_UNSUPPORTED=false
      HAS_5G=false
      HAS_VOLTE=true
      HAS_BURN_IN_PROTECTION=true
      HAS_DOUBLE_TAP_WAKE=true
      
      # ── Vendor HAL flags ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      HAS_VENDOR_FINGERPRINT_HAL=false
      HAS_VENDOR_VIBRATOR_HAL=false
      
      # ── Build Tools ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      PLATFORM_JAR="/usr/share/android-framework-res/framework-res.apk"
      PLATFORM_KEY="stuff/keys/platform.pk8"
      PLATFORM_CERT="stuff/keys/platform.x509.pem"
      
      # ── Advanced Build Settings (DO NOT EDIT) ─────────────────────────────────
      # The values below are for aapt2 dictionary compatibility (linking against 
      # the Android 13 resource dictionary). 
      #
      # ⚠ DO NOT CHANGE THESE to match your GSI version. 
      # They are for build-time linking only and do NOT affect GSI compatibility.
      # Changing them will likely cause "Resource not found" errors.
      COMPILE_SDK_VERSION=35
      ANDROID_VERSION="15"
      MIN_SDK_VERSION=33
      TARGET_SDK_VERSION=34
      
      # ── Overlay repo submission (Doze-off, submission only) ───────────────────
      # These affect only out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip: the source tree you submit
      # as a pull request to github.com/Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay (base branch
      # pie), so the GSI builds ship the overlay with no module. Upstream
      # TrebleDroid/vendor_hardware_overlay takes the same tree.
      # Step-by-step: docs/submission.md
      #
      # The device must match the preinstalled overlay without a module, so this uses
      # a property that already exists on it. android:requiredSystemPropertyValue is
      # compared with plain string equality — no "*" or "+" globs (the wiki's
      # "+*brand/model*" form never matches; the overlay stays inert).
      #   adb shell getprop ro.product.vendor.device
      # ro.product.vendor.device comes from the vendor partition: it survives a GSI
      # flash and does not change between OTAs. The full ro.vendor.build.fingerprint
      # works too, but every OTA changes it. An empty HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP submits an
      # always-active overlay.
      # Default value: the DEVICE_CODENAME above.
      HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP="ro.product.device"
      HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE="zephyr"
      #
      # The repo rejects a priority that another overlay already uses. Left unset, the
      # build picks a free number from the device name; `bash tests/tests.sh` in a
      # clone of the repo prints its own suggestion before you open the pull request.
      HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY=9999

# emit_items <indent> <space-separated values>  -> writes <item> lines.
emit_items() {
    local indent="$1" values="$2" v
    for v in $values; do
        printf '%s<item>%s</item>\n' "$indent" "$v"
    done
}

# emit_brightness_key <config var> <resource name> [<float resource>]
# Appends the integer and (when AOSP has one) the matching 0.0-1.0 float dimen.
# Uses $gen from the calling generator.
emit_brightness_key() {
    local var="$1" res="$2" floatres="${3:-}" val="${!1}"
    [ -n "$val" ] || return 0
    [[ "$val" == *"<"* ]] && return 0
    if ! is_uint "$val" || [ "$val" -gt 255 ]; then
        warn "${var} must be an integer 0-255 — skipped"
        return 0
    fi
    printf '    <integer name="%s">%s</integer>\n' "$res" "$val" >> "$gen"
    if [ -n "$floatres" ]; then
        printf '    <item name="%s" format="float" type="dimen">%s</item>\n' \
            "$floatres" "$(div255 "$val")" >> "$gen"
    fi
    return 0
}

- path: stuff/scripts/validate.sh
  content: |
          local n=0 v
          for v in $1; do n=$((n + 1)); done
          printf '%s' "$n"
      }
      command -v list_ints >/dev/null 2>&1 || list_ints() {
          local v
          for v in $1; do [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1; done
          return 0
      }
      command -v list_numbers >/dev/null 2>&1 || list_numbers() {
          local v
          for v in $1; do [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]] || return 1; done
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Placeholders
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      _validate_placeholders() {
          local key value
          for key in DEVICE_MANUFACTURER DEVICE_MODEL DEVICE_CODENAME \
                     ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT UDFPS_X UDFPS_Y UDFPS_RADIUS \
                     DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE PEAK_REFRESH_RATE; do
              value="${!key:-}"
              if [ -z "$value" ]; then
                  _v_warn "${key} is empty"
              elif is_set "$value"; then
                  :
              else
                  case "$key" in
                      ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS|STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT|UDFPS_X|UDFPS_Y|UDFPS_RADIUS|DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE|PEAK_REFRESH_RATE)
                          _v_warn "${key}=\"${value}\" is still the placeholder — the build will use 0"
                          ;;
                      *)
                          _v_warn "${key}=\"${value}\" is still the placeholder"
                          ;;
                  esac
              fi
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Display geometry
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      _validate_display() {
          local radius sb_height land pad_content pad_start pad_end
          radius=$(_v_int "${ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS:-}")
          sb_height=$(_v_int "${STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT:-}")
          land=$(_v_int "${STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE:-}")
          pad_content=$(_v_int "${STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING:-}")
          pad_start=$(_v_int "${STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START:-}")
          pad_end=$(_v_int "${STATUS_BAR_PADDING_END:-}")
      
          if [ -n "$radius" ] && [ "$radius" -gt 400 ]; then
              _v_warn "ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS=${radius}px is larger than any phone corner (check the unit)"
          fi
      
          # The three padding keys only make sense together, and they must agree:
          # the framework and SystemUI paths override each other instead of adding up.
          if [ -n "$pad_content$pad_start$pad_end" ]; then
              if [ -z "$pad_content" ] || [ -z "$pad_start" ] || [ -z "$pad_end" ]; then
                  _v_warn "STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING, _PADDING_START and _PADDING_END should all be set"
              elif [ "$pad_content" != "$pad_start" ] || [ "$pad_content" != "$pad_end" ]; then
                  _v_warn "status bar padding differs (${pad_content}/${pad_start}/${pad_end}) — set all three to the same value"
              fi
              if [ -n "$radius" ] && [ "$radius" -gt 0 ] && [ "$pad_start" -gt "$radius" ]; then
                  _v_warn "STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START=${pad_start} is wider than the corner (${radius}px)"
              fi
          fi
      
          if [ -n "$sb_height" ] && [ "$sb_height" -gt 0 ]; then
              if [ "$sb_height" -lt 48 ]; then
                  _v_warn "STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT=${sb_height}px is very small (a normal bar is 60-140px)"
              elif [ "$sb_height" -gt 400 ]; then
                  _v_warn "STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT=${sb_height}px is very large (a normal bar is 60-140px)"
              fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$land" ] && [ -n "$sb_height" ] && [ "$land" -gt "$sb_height" ]; then
              _v_note "status bar landscape (${land}px) is taller than portrait (${sb_height}px)"
          fi
      
          # A path with no suffix is in px — that is the default the parser uses, and
          # it is how MIUI stores its own (e.g. "M 0,0 H -29 V 118 H 29 V 0 H 0 Z").
          # Only an unknown @unit is a mistake; @dp/@left/@right/@top/@bottom are the
          # documented ones.
          case "${DISPLAY_CUTOUT:-}" in
              "") ;;
              *'<'*) ;;
              *'@'*)
                  case "$DISPLAY_CUTOUT" in
                      *@dp|*@px|*@left|*@right|*@top|*@bottom) ;;
                      *) _v_warn "DISPLAY_CUTOUT has an unknown @unit suffix (use @dp, @left, @right, @top, @bottom, or none for px)" ;;
                  esac
                  ;;
          esac
      }

> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
> <!-- Device power profile. Replace this template with the profile from YOUR
>      stock firmware: the Auto Detect tab (menu 5 → power profile) writes it
>      here, and the build compiles it into the overlay as

> 
>      Why it matters: the framework estimates battery drain from these values.
>      A profile from another phone reports the wrong capacity and screen/modem
>      draw, so battery percentage and Doze behaviour end up wrong.
> 
>      Extract it with:
>        adb shell dumpsys power | ...            (see docs/device-extraction.md)
>        ./build.sh --power-profile               (writes this file from the phone)

  b.WriteString("     this file into the overlay as res/xml/power_profile.xml. -->\n")
  writeNode(&b, root, 0)

  body := b.String()
  // Refuse anything that would fail to compile: a well-formed document with a
  // power-profile root is the contract, and it is cheap to check here.
  var probe struct {
    XMLName xml.Name
  }
  if err := xml.Unmarshal([]byte(body), &probe); err != nil {
    return "", 0, fmt.Errorf("the converted profile is not valid XML: %w", err)
  }
  return body, items, nil
}

41:- **Power/Health** — A16 requires AIDL interfaces for power management features.
536:## Power Profile (`power_profile.xml`) — mandatory
538:The `src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` file is important for your device's health and performance on a GSI. It tells Android how much power each hardware component uses and defines the CPU cluster architecture.
543:> Add your device's entries to make battery statistics and CPU power mapping
547:While your phone might boot without it, using a generic or missing `power_profile.xml` causes:
548:- **Poor Battery Life:** The system cannot accurately calculate power-efficient task placement.
549:- **CPU Mismatch:** Modern "Big.Little" or "1+3+4" CPU cluster layouts need correct frequency/power maps to scale correctly.
551:- **Overheating:** Incorrect power maps can lead to aggressive boosting on the wrong clusters.
553:### What power_profile.xml contains
555:- **CPU clusters** — core speeds and power draw per frequency step (Essential for schedutil/schedtune)
556:- **Screen** — power drain when on, at full brightness, and in ambient/doze mode
557:- **Radio** — cellular modem power in active/idle/scanning states
558:- **Wi-Fi/Bluetooth** — power drain for each radio
561:### 🛠 How to get YOUR device's power_profile
571:2. Unzip and extract the power profile:
573:   unzip -p framework-res.apk res/xml/power_profile.xml > src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml
580:If your device has a high-quality custom ROM (like LineageOS), find the `power_profile.xml` in their device tree on GitHub. It's usually located at:
581:`device/<manufacturer>/<codename>/overlay/frameworks/base/core/res/res/xml/power_profile.xml`

Better: derive the name from the codename when it's a placeholder. i.e., set `DEVICE_PROP_NAME="persist.sys.overlay.<codename>"` and have common.sh substitute `<codename>`:

>     if [[ "${DEVICE_PROP_NAME:-}" == *"<codename>"* ]]; then
>         DEVICE_PROP_NAME="${DEVICE_PROP_NAME//<codename>/$DEVICE_CODENAME}"

- path: stuff/scripts/common.sh
  content: |
      # Turns the raw DEVICE_* values from config.env into the module id, the overlay
      # package names and the match condition. Called by build.sh right after
      # config.env is sourced, and by the standalone scripts (manifest.sh,
      # hardware-overlay.sh) so they agree with the build.
      #
      # Users only need to set DEVICE_CODENAME and DEVICE_MANUFACTURER; everything
      # else is derived. A value containing "<" is a template placeholder.
      derive_overlay_identity() {
          [ -z "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER:-}" ] || [[ "$DEVICE_MANUFACTURER" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="generic"
          [ -z "${DEVICE_CODENAME:-}" ]     || [[ "$DEVICE_CODENAME" == *"<"* ]]     && DEVICE_CODENAME="generic"
      
          # Clean manufacturer for Java package names (lowercase alphanumeric only)
          SAFE_MANUFACTURER=$(printf '%s' "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]//g')
      
          # Clean codename for package name: replace non-alphanumeric with dots
          # e.g. "Infinix-X6852" → "infinix.x6852" (dots are valid Java package separators)
          PACKAGE_SEGMENT=$(printf '%s' "${DEVICE_CODENAME}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]/./g' | sed 's/\.\.*/./g' | sed 's/^\.//;s/\.$//')
      
          # Module ids are shared by Magisk, KernelSU and APatch: they must match
          # ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$ (no spaces or slashes). Use the already-cleaned
          # manufacturer/codename pieces for the generated default; an explicit
          # OVERLAY_NAME in config.env is kept as-is.
          DEFAULT_MANUFACTURER="${SAFE_MANUFACTURER:-generic}"
          DEFAULT_CODENAME="${PACKAGE_SEGMENT:-generic}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_NAME:-}" ]        || [[ "$OVERLAY_NAME" == *"<"* ]]        && OVERLAY_NAME="treble-overlay-${DEFAULT_MANUFACTURER}-${DEFAULT_CODENAME}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_PACKAGE:-}" ]     || [[ "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE" == *"<"* ]]     && OVERLAY_PACKAGE="me.phh.treble.overlay.${SAFE_MANUFACTURER}.${PACKAGE_SEGMENT}"
          [ -z "${OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI:-}" ] || [[ "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI" == *"<"* ]] && OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI="${OVERLAY_PACKAGE}.systemui"
          [[ "${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE:-}" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_PROP_VALUE="${DEVICE_CODENAME}"
          # The template spells the property as persist.sys.overlay.<codename>, so the
          # token expands to whatever DEVICE_CODENAME resolved to.
      
      [read_files: showing lines 417-446 of 544. Use code_search to locate the part you need and read a window around it, or call read_files again with offset=447 to continue.]

message: Followups suggested!
```

Your device data is out of the repo. Here's what changed and what you should know.

**`config.env` — now a real template**

Every measured/identity value is a placeholder that the scripts already know how to treat:

| Key | Now |
|---|---|
| `DEVICE_MANUFACTURER` / `DEVICE_MODEL` / `DEVICE_CODENAME` | `<manufacturer>` / `<model>` / `<codename>` |
| `MODULE_AUTHOR` | `<author>` |
| `DEVICE_PROP_NAME` | `persist.sys.overlay.<codename>` (token expands at build time) |
| `ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS` / `STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT` | `<corner_radius>` / `<status_bar_height>` |
| `STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT_LANDSCAPE`, `DISPLAY_CUTOUT`, `UDFPS_X/Y/RADIUS` | commented out, placeholders shown |
| `DEFAULT_/PEAK_REFRESH_RATE` | `<refresh_rate>` |
| `BRIGHTNESS_DIM` / `BRIGHTNESS_DEFAULT` | `<brightness_dim>` / `<brightness_default>` |
| `HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE` | `<codename>` |

Flags that were really your device's answers are now neutral (`HAS_UDFPS`, `HAS_AOD`, `HAS_DOZE`, `HAS_VOLTE`, `HAS_BURN_IN_PROTECTION`, `HAS_DOUBLE_TAP_WAKE` all `false`; brightness range 0–255). `OVERLAY_PRIORITY`, SDK levels, signing keys and the AOSP-ish `BRIGHTNESS_DARK/DOZE=1` stayed, since they are structure rather than your phone's measurements. `stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env` is re-synced, so a fresh clone's starter config is the same file.

**`src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml`** is now the empty template. It has no `<item>` entries, so `power_profile_is_placeholder` reports true and the build leaves it out of the APK instead of shipping an empty or someone else's profile — the GSI keeps its own. The header points at Auto Detect → Power profile, `device-probe.sh --power-profile`, and `docs/device-extraction.md`.

**Three bugs the sanitizing exposed, fixed**

1. `HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE="<codename>"` would have been emitted literally into the submission manifest. `hw_match_value()` now treats a `<…>` value as unset and falls back to the codename (an explicit empty value still stays empty).
2. `DEVICE_PROP_NAME` with a `<codename>` token was used verbatim; `derive_overlay_identity()` now expands the token, so the match line reads `persist.sys.overlay.generic == "true"` rather than a prop name containing angle brackets.
3. `check` was noisy and wrong on a fresh template: it complained about UDFPS coordinates on a device with no in-display sensor (now skipped unless `HAS_UDFPS=true`), claimed placeholders meant "the build will use 0" (they are skipped, ROM value stays), and warned that `PEAK_REFRESH_RATE` was set without a default when both were placeholders. It also now says one clear line when the template identity is still in place, instead of silently building `generic-generic`.

**Checks run**

- `bash -n` on the edited scripts — clean.
- `bash build.sh check` on the sanitized config: 5 warnings, all accurate and actionable, exit 0.
- `bash build.sh --dry-run` — completes, resource list generated, no power profile emitted.
- Real `hardware-overlay.sh write` with the template: manifests get `ro.product.device="generic"`, `isStatic="true"`, and a grep for literal `<codename>` across the tree finds nothing.
- `bash stuff/tests/run.sh`: 111/111 Node tests pass, Go tests pass, docs links pass. The only red line is "template fallbacks match the release", which compares against **`HEAD`** and is expected to fail until this is committed — the two files on disk are byte-identical (`cmp` clean).

**Not changed, on purpose**

`docs/udfps.md`, `docs/detect.md`, `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/submission.md` still use `Redmi Note 17 4G (zephyr)` in worked examples with your real measured numbers (`540, 2198, 89`), and the `uzbforce` repo URLs stay. Those are documentation examples rather than device config; say the word and I'll genericize the numeric worked examples too. Nothing was committed, and `out/` plus `gui/bin/gui.json` (your local absolute path) are gitignored, so they never reach the repo.

function currentVerb() {
  if (!state) return null;
  return state.verbs.find((v) => v.name === selectedVerb) || state.verbs[0] || null;
}

function renderVerbs() {
  const box = $('verbs');
  box.textContent = '';
  for (const v of state.verbs) {
    const b = document.createElement('button');
    b.type = 'button';
    b.className = 'verb' + (v.name === selectedVerb ? ' is-active' : '');
    const h = document.createElement('h3');
    h.textContent = v.label;
    const p = document.createElement('p');
    p.textContent = v.hint;
    b.append(h, p);
    b.addEventListener('click', () => {
      selectedVerb = v.name;
      renderVerbs();
      renderFlags();
      renderRunState();
    });
    box.appendChild(b);
  }
}

function renderFlags() {
  const v = currentVerb();
  const box = $('flags');
  box.textContent = '';

  if (!v || !v.flags || v.flags.length === 0) {
    box.appendChild(el('span', 'muted', 'none for this command'));
    return;
  }

  for (const flag of v.flags) {
    const label = el('label', 'flag');
    label.title = FLAG_HELP[flag] || '';

    const input = document.createElement('input');
    input.type = 'checkbox';
    input.checked = checkedFlags.has(flag);
    input.addEventListener('change', () => {
      if (input.checked) checkedFlags.add(flag);
      else checkedFlags.delete(flag);
      renderRunState();
    });

    label.append(input, el('span', 'flag-name', flag));
    box.appendChild(label);
  }
}

```
type Verb struct {
  Name  string   `json:"name"`
  Label string   `json:"label"`
  Arg   string   `json:"arg"`
  Hint  string   `json:"hint"`
  Flags []string `json:"flags"`
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The commands the app is allowed to run
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Each entry is one thing `build.sh` already does; the GUI only chooses which
// one to run. Flags are per verb on purpose: `--all` means "also remove config
// and device files" and is meaningless on a build, so the UI disables it and
// the server rejects it. Keeping the table here (not only in the JS) means a
// hand-written POST cannot widen what the app will execute.
var verbTable = []Verb{
  {
    Name:  "build",
    Label: "Build",
    Arg:   "build",
    Hint:  "Compile and sign the module, and the submission zips",
    Flags: []string{"--with-vendor-hals", "--allow-unknown-resources"},
  },
  {
    Name:  "dryrun",
    Label: "Dry run",
    Arg:   "--dry-run",
    Hint:  "Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing",
    Flags: nil,
  },
  {
    Name:  "check",
    Label: "Check",
    Arg:   "check",
    Hint:  "Validate config.env, build nothing",
    Flags: nil,
  },
  {
    Name:  "doctor",
    Label: "Doctor",
    Arg:   "doctor",
    Hint:  "Check the toolchain, install nothing",
    Flags: nil,
  },
  {
    Name:  "setup",
    Label: "Setup",
    Arg:   "setup",
    Hint:  "Install or repair the build tools",
    Flags: []string{"--force"},
  },
  {
    Name:  "clean",
    Label: "Clean",
    Arg:   "clean",
    Hint:  "Remove build output",
    Flags: []string{"--all"},
  },
}

func lookupVerb(name string) (Verb, bool) {
  for _, v := range verbTable {
    if v.Name == name {
      return v, true
    }
  }
  return Verb{}, false
}

// buildArgs turns a verb and its ticked flags into the argv for bash.
//
// -y is always appended: the child has no terminal, so anything that would
// prompt has to take its default instead of blocking forever on stdin. That is
// also why --with-vendor-hals becomes reachable at all — build.sh only honours
// it together with --yes.
func buildArgs(verb string, flags []string) ([]string, error) {
  v, ok := lookupVerb(verb)
  if !ok {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown command %q", verb)
  }
  args := []string{"--noprofile", "--norc", "./build.sh", v.Arg}
  for _, f := range flags {
    if !contains(v.Flags, f) {
      return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is not available with %s", f, v.Name)
    }
    args = append(args, f)
  }
  return append(args, "-y"), nil
}

          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --xiaomi-fod           Include the Xiaomi FOD helper (HBM + HIDL touch mode) in the module"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
          echo ""
      }
      
      for arg in "$@"; do
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --xiaomi-fod)   XIAOMI_FOD=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # No arguments and a terminal to talk on: the menu. Everything scripted passes
      # a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          MODE="menu"
      fi
      
      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).
      wsl_guard
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Dispatch
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      case "$MODE" in
          menu)
              # The terminal front end. It shells out to this same script for a build,
              # so a build started from the menu is the build a user would type.
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/menu.sh"
              menu_main
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          doctor)
              if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
              ;;
      
          setup)
              banner "Setup — build tools"
              migrate_layout
              # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
              # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
              # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
              # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
              # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
              if $ASSUME_YES; then
                  ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
              else
                  ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
              fi
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          check)
              # Config validation only: no tools, no output.
              CHECK_MODE=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          clean)
              migrate_layout
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/clean.sh"
              ;;
      
          dryrun)
              # Needs config.env and the resource generators, no toolchain: the point
              # is to see the plan in seconds.
              DRY_RUN=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          build)
              # Move any files left in the old top-level layout into src/.
              migrate_layout
              if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Windows"
              elif $IS_TERMUX; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Termux"
              else
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Linux"
              fi
              # Installs only what is missing; prints a summary and returns non-zero
              # when the machine still cannot build.
              ensure_toolchain auto
              # The installer may just have created stuff/tools/, so refresh PATH.
              tools_on_path
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      esac

                 "${MODULE_TMP}/post-fs-data.sh"
