      type Verb struct {
        Name  string   `json:"name"`
        Label string   `json:"label"`
        Arg   string   `json:"arg"`
        Hint  string   `json:"hint"`
        Flags []string `json:"flags"`
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The commands the app is allowed to run
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Each entry is one thing `build.sh` already does; the GUI only chooses which
      // one to run. Flags are per verb on purpose: `--all` means "also remove config
      // and device files" and is meaningless on a build, so the UI disables it and
      // the server rejects it. Keeping the table here (not only in the JS) means a
      // hand-written POST cannot widen what the app will execute.
      var verbTable = []Verb{
        {
          Name:  "build",
          Label: "Build",
          Arg:   "build",
          Hint:  "Compile and sign the module, and the submission zips",
          Flags: []string{"--with-vendor-hals", "--allow-unknown-resources"},
        },
        {
          Name:  "dryrun",
          Label: "Dry run",
          Arg:   "--dry-run",
          Hint:  "Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing",
          Flags: nil,
        },
        {
          Name:  "check",
          Label: "Check",
          Arg:   "check",
          Hint:  "Validate config.env, build nothing",
          Flags: nil,

          Flags: nil,

        {
          Name:  "setup",
          Label: "Setup",
          Arg:   "setup",
          Hint:  "Install or repair the build tools",
          Flags: []string{"--force"},
        },
        {
          Name:  "clean",
          Label: "Clean",
          Arg:   "clean",
          Hint:  "Remove build output",
          Flags: []string{"--all"},
        },
      }
      
      func lookupVerb(name string) (Verb, bool) {
        for _, v := range verbTable {
          if v.Name == name {
            return v, true
          }
        }
        return Verb{}, false
      }

      'use strict';
      
      /* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
         The window is a thin client over the handlers in server.go. Everything it
         can do is one of build.sh's verbs, so there is no build logic here: it picks
         a verb, ticks flags, and renders what the child prints.
      
         Three panes talk to the phone or edit files — config.env, adb and the src/
         workspace — and all of them go through the server, which owns the parsing,
         the path rules and every write. Nothing here touches the disk directly.
         --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
      
      function el(tag, cls, text) {
        const node = document.createElement(tag);
        if (cls) node.className = cls;
        if (text !== undefined) node.textContent = text;
        return node;
      }
      
      const FLAG_HELP = {
        '--with-vendor-hals': 'include src/vendor/ in the module',
        '--allow-unknown-resources': 'build even if a resource is missing',
        '--force': 're-pick the resource dictionary',
        '--all': 'also remove config and device files',
      };
      
      let state = null;
      let selectedVerb = 'build';
      let checkedFlags = new Set();
      let running = false;      // the build console
      let adbRunning = false;  // the device console, which has its own stream
      let lastSeq = 0;
      let adbSeq = 0;
      // The node a repainting progress bar owns, per console: the build log and the
      // adb console each draw their own in place.
      const progressNode = new WeakMap();
      // Where the current adb run writes: the <pre> under the preset that started it,
      // or null for the console at the top of the pane.
      let adbTarget = null;
      // preset id -> the panel under that command, kept across the re-render every
      // finished run triggers so the answer stays where the question was clicked.
      const presetOut = new Map();
      let currentDoc = null;
      let statusTimer = null;
      let refreshInFlight = false;
      
      // A run that stopped for a sudo password keeps its verb here, so the retry is
      // exactly the same command. sudoPassword is the answer; it stays in this
      // window's memory for the session and is never written by the page.
      let pendingRun = null;
      let sudoPassword = '';
      let sudoPromptOpen = false;
      let sudoDeclined = false;
      
      // config.env: the form keeps only what the user changed, so a poll that lands
      // mid-edit cannot repaint the row they are typing in.
      let cfgEdits = new Map();
      let cfgRaw = false;

- path: docs/gui.md
  content: |
      ./gui/build.sh            # console build
      gui\build.cmd --release   # no console window behind the app
      ```
      
      **From a release** (once one is published): download the archive for your
      platform, unpack it *into the clone* (so `gui/` sits next to `build.sh`), and run
      the executable. Windows builds are unsigned, so SmartScreen shows "Windows
      protected your PC" once — **More info → Run anyway**.
      
      Nothing else has to be installed beyond what the CLI already needs (Git for
      Windows, JDK 17+). The window is drawn by the engine the system already has:
      WebView2 on Windows, WebKitGTK on Linux.
      
      ## What it does
      
      | Button | Runs | Use it when |
      |---|---|---|
      | **Build** | `build.sh build -y` | normal build; writes `out/*.zip` and `out/apks/*.apk` |
      | **Dry run** | `build.sh --dry-run -y` | see which resources `config.env` emits, build nothing |
      | **Check** | `build.sh check -y` | validate `config.env` before spending a build on it |
      | **Doctor** | `build.sh doctor -y` | something is missing; find what |
      | **Setup** | `build.sh setup -y` | install or repair the Android build tools (asks for the sudo password when it needs it) |
      | **Clean** | `build.sh clean -y` | discard `out/` (tick `--all` to also drop config and device files) |
      
      Flags appear only on the commands that accept them:
      
      - `--with-vendor-hals` — include `src/vendor/` in the module (Build)
      - `--allow-unknown-resources` — build even if a resource is missing (Build)
      - `--force` — re-pick the resource dictionary (Setup)
      - `--all` — also remove config and device files (Clean)
      
      `-y` is always appended: the app has no terminal for the script to ask
      questions in, so anything that would prompt takes its default instead of
      blocking forever. The one question the app answers itself is **sudo's
      password**: when installing the tools needs root, the run stops, the app asks
      for the password in a dialog, and the same command is repeated with it. The
      password is kept in that window's memory and handed to `sudo -A` (through
      `stuff/scripts/sudo-askpass.sh`) via a private file that is deleted when the
      run ends. **Setup** therefore installs rather than printing a command, and
      **Build** repairs a partial toolchain the same way.

          b.className = 'verb' + (v.name === selectedVerb ? ' is-active' : '');
          const h = document.createElement('h3');
          h.textContent = v.label;

      function renderFlags() {
        const v = currentVerb();
        const box = $('flags');
        box.textContent = '';
      
        if (!v || !v.flags || v.flags.length === 0) {
          box.appendChild(el('span', 'muted', 'none for this command'));
          return;
        }
      
        for (const flag of v.flags) {
          const label = el('label', 'flag');
          label.title = FLAG_HELP[flag] || '';
      
          const input = document.createElement('input');
          input.type = 'checkbox';
          input.checked = checkedFlags.has(flag);
          input.addEventListener('change', () => {
            if (input.checked) checkedFlags.add(flag);
            else checkedFlags.delete(flag);
            renderRunState();
          });
      
          label.append(input, el('span', 'flag-name', flag));
          box.appendChild(label);
        }
      }
      
      function renderRunState() {
        const v = currentVerb();
        const ready = state && state.cloneValid && state.bashValid;
      
        // The two consoles keep separate streams and separate buffers, but they share
        // one job slot on the server: both write into the same clone, so a pull and a
        // build must never overlap.
        $('run').disabled = !ready || running || adbRunning || !v;
        $('stop').disabled = !running;
        $('run').textContent = v ? `Run ${v.label.toLowerCase()}` : 'Run';
      
        const flags = v ? [...checkedFlags].filter((f) => v.flags && v.flags.includes(f)) : [];
        const cmd = v ? `build.sh ${v.arg}${flags.length ? ' ' + flags.join(' ') : ''} -y` : '';
        $('run').title = v ? `runs: bash --noprofile --norc ./${cmd}` : '';
      
        for (const input of $('flags').querySelectorAll('input')) input.disabled = running;
        for (const b of $('verbs').querySelectorAll('.verb')) b.disabled = running;
        $('adb-run').disabled = running || adbRunning || !adbReady();
        $('adb-run').title = running ? 'a build is running — one job at a time' : '';
        $('adb-stop').disabled = !adbRunning;
      
        // One job at a time: a second preset clicked mid-run would be refused by the
        // server, and the panel under the command still running would end up with the
        // refusal in it. Blocked-for-needs is remembered by renderPresets, which is
        // what reads the codename and the adb install state.
        for (const b of $('adb-presets').querySelectorAll('button.preset')) {
          if (running || adbRunning) b.disabled = true;
          else b.disabled = b.dataset.blocked === '1';
        }
      }
      
      // -------------------------------------------------------------- last build --
      // The list of what out/ holds is only interesting right after a build, so it
      // sits folded at the bottom of the pane. renderOut keeps the summary line
      // current either way, and a finished build opens it once.
      function renderOut() {
        const box = $('out');
        const summary = $('out-summary');
        box.textContent = '';
      
        const files = state.out || [];
        if (files.length === 0) {
          summary.textContent = state.cloneValid ? 'nothing in out/ yet' : 'no clone selected';
          box.appendChild(el('span', 'muted', summary.textContent));
          return;
        }
      
        let newest = 0;
        let biggest = 0;
        for (const f of files) {
          if (f.mod > newest) newest = f.mod;
          if (f.size > biggest) biggest = f.size;
        }
        const when = ago(newest);
        summary.textContent = `${when} · ${files.length} file${files.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
        summary.title = 'built ' + new Date(newest * 1000).toLocaleString();
      
        for (const f of files) {
          const row = el('div', 'out-item');
          row.append(el('span', null, f.name), el('span', null, `${bytes(f.size)} · ${ago(f.mod)}`));
          box.appendChild(row);
        }
      }
      
      function bytes(n) {
        if (n > 1 << 20) return (n / (1 << 20)).toFixed(1) + ' MB';
        if (n > 1 << 10) return (n / (1 << 10)).toFixed(0) + ' kB';
        return n + ' B';
      }
      
      function ago(unixSeconds) {
        const s = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000 - unixSeconds));
        if (s < 60) return 'just now';
        if (s < 3600) return Math.floor(s / 60) + ' min ago';
        if (s < 86400) return Math.floor(s / 3600) + ' h ago';
        return Math.floor(s / 86400) + ' d ago';
      }

````

- path: docs/udfps.md
  content: |
      fingerprint icon is controlled by the fingerprint HAL and the panel driver, not
      by the RRO. On Xiaomi devices the stock properties are
      `ro.hardware.fp.fod=true`, `ro.hardware.fp.fod.location=low` and the
      `ro.hardware.fp.fod.lowlight.*` thresholds; leave them alone.
      
      `config_udfps_sensor_props` only tells SystemUI where to draw the icon and how
      large the touch target is. It does **not** put the touch panel into fingerprint
      mode, and on Xiaomi optical sensors that is a separate step:
      
      - HyperOS: `FingerprintService` calls the vendor extension
        `vendor.xiaomi.hardware.fingerprintextension.extCmd(4, 3)`, which calls
        `vendor.xiaomi.hardware.touchfeature.setModeValue(10, 3)`.
      - `setModeValue` is `ioctl(0x5400, {10, 3})` on `/dev/xiaomi-touch`; the driver
        logs it as `Mode:FOD fod_status = 3`, and a released mode as `0`.
      - With the panel in that mode the touch controller reports presses in the
        sensor area (`/sys/devices/virtual/touch/touch_dev/fod_press_status`), and
        the vendor Goodix HAL wakes the sensor and captures an image.
      - Local HBM is a separate ioctl (`0x400c440e` on
        `/dev/mi_display/disp_feature`; 2 = on, 1 = off). On HyperOS the HAL turns it
        on around the capture; on a GSI it refuses, with
        `skip enable lhbm as fingerprint is idle` — that check expects the MIUI
        fingerprint client, which is the thing a GSI does not have.
      
      A GSI has no HyperOS fingerprint client, so the first call never happens: the
      panel stays in normal touch mode, the HAL never sees the finger, and the sensor
      looks dead even though the icon is in the right place. Even with the panel
      armed, the sensor only gets ambient light and the HBM step is skipped.
      
      The module ships `fod/xiaomi-fod`, a small arm64 helper that issues the same
      ioctls. `service.sh` starts it when `/dev/xiaomi-touch` exists and
      `ro.hardware.fp.fod=true`. The daemon copies the state machine the stock touch
      driver logs: mode 10 is armed with value 3 (FOD plus the AOD wake bit) when the
      screen turns off, stays armed while the keyguard is showing (lock screen and
      AOD) or a fingerprint client is running (settings enrollment, in-app prompts),
      and is released with 0 otherwise. It reads the panel backlight,
      `dumpsys window policy` and `dumpsys fingerprint` for that, so it needs no MIUI
      service.
      
      Because the vendor HAL will not light the panel on a GSI, the same daemon
      drives local HBM. While the panel is armed it watches `fod_press_status` every
      50 ms and turns HBM on when the finger lands, and off as soon as the finger is
      up and no prompt is left (a 150 ms hold covers the capture, and the prompt
      disappearing ends it early). That is
      the stock behaviour — the spot stays dark until the sensor is touched — and it
      keeps the bright circle out of the lock screen and the AOD.
      
      A press with the display asleep works the same way, with one extra step. The
      touch controller reports it in suspend, the daemon lights HBM (about 10 ms) and
      wakes the screen with `input keyevent 224`. The wake is not cosmetic: with the
      panel asleep the vendor HAL starts an auth, waits 1500 ms for the fingerprint
      UI to answer and aborts with
      `GF_ERROR_UI_READY_TIMEOUT`, because the GSI's SystemUI has no UDFPS view up in
      doze. Waking brings the keyguard's prompt up inside that window, so the same
      press goes on to unlock the phone. The `screen_off_udfps_enabled` Secure setting
      is not consulted: this GSI's SystemUI does not act on it, and MIUI wakes the
      display on that press anyway.
      
      The prompt itself is noticed from SystemUI's own logs: `logcat` is filtered to
      `UdfpsController` and `UdfpsControllerOverlay`, and `showUdfpsOverlay` arms the
      panel the moment the window appears (opening enrollment, an in-app biometric
      prompt), while `hideUdfpsControllerOverlay` releases it. That costs nothing
      while no line arrives. A `dumpsys fingerprint` check every 5 s is kept as a
      fallback for GSIs whose SystemUI uses different tags, and the keyguard is
      refreshed with `dumpsys window policy` every 2 s.
      
      Manual checks, useful when the icon is right but the sensor is silent. Run them
      through `su -c`; a plain adb shell process is not allowed to open the touch
      node.
      
      ```bash
      # Arm the touch panel's FOD mode (3 = FOD + AOD, 0 = release)
      su -c '/data/adb/modules/<module>/fod/xiaomi-fod touch 10 3'
      su -c 'dmesg | grep "Mode:FOD"'       # fod_status = 3 while armed, 0 after release
      
      # Local HBM: 2 = on, 1 = off. The daemon does this on press; use it to test
      # the panel and the ioctl by hand.
      su -c '/data/adb/modules/<module>/fod/xiaomi-fod hbm 2'
      su -c '/data/adb/modules/<module>/fod/xiaomi-fod hbm 1'
      
      # What the daemon did
      su -c 'cat /data/adb/modules/<module>/fod.log'
      ```
      
      ---
      
      ## The UDFPS icon colour
      
      `UDFPS_COLOR` in `config.env` sets SystemUI's `config_udfpsColor`, the colour
      the icon and the light behind it are painted with:

      rem
      rem Requirements: Git for Windows + JDK 17+ on PATH.
      rem Tip: run this from cmd or PowerShell (.\\build.cmd), not from WSL.
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal EnableExtensions
      call "%~dp0stuff\windows\run-bash.cmd" build.sh %*
      set "RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"

      rem Windows leaves a space after the trailing quotes, so a last-three-characters

      set "DOUBLE="

Done. The Xiaomi FOD helper is now opt-in everywhere, with the flag threaded through all three front ends.

**What changed**

| Place | How you turn it on |
|---|---|
| CLI | `./build.sh build --xiaomi-fod` (also honours `-y`); listed in `--help` |
| Terminal menu | Build → new row **7 · Xiaomi FOD** showing `on`/`off`, toggles in place, then Build uses it. `./build.sh menu --xiaomi-fod` starts with it already on |
| Desktop app | Build pane → new checkbox `--xiaomi-fod`, with the explanation printed under the flag list |

`gui/app.go` now allows the flag on the `build` verb, so the checkbox actually reaches `build.sh` and a hand-written POST can't send anything else. Default is **off**, which is the behaviour change: nothing ships `fod/xiaomi-fod` unless you ask.

**Why it's safe to leave off.** `stuff/scripts/build.sh` packs the binary only when `--xiaomi-fod` is set *and* `HAS_UDFPS=true` *and* the binary exists. Otherwise it prints one warning instead of silently dropping it:

- `--xiaomi-fod ignored: HAS_UDFPS is not true, so there is no in-display sensor to help`

The check in `service.sh` (`/dev/xiaomi-touch` + `ro.hardware.fp.fod=true`) is untouched, so a shipped helper still stays idle on the wrong hardware.

**Description of the file, where each audience needs it**

- App: *"Xiaomi only. Ships fod/xiaomi-fod, which puts the touch panel into FOD mode and asks the vendor fingerprint HAL for high-brightness mode, so the sensor reads the finger on Xiaomi optical UDFPS phones. Other vendors do not need it."* (`FLAG_DETAIL` in `app.js`, styled by `.flag-detail` in `app.css`)
- Menu: `7  Xiaomi FOD   off · HBM + touch-panel FOD mode for Xiaomi UDFPS`, plus a note when enabled
- `docs/udfps.md`: the "The module ships …" paragraph now says it is opt-in, names the flag and the menu row, and says why it is off by default. Also added to the flag lists in `docs/gui.md` and `README.md`.

**Checks run**

- `bash -n` on `build.sh`, `stuff/scripts/build.sh`, `stuff/scripts/menu.sh` — clean.
- Real build, flag absent: exit 0, zero `fod/xiaomi-fod` entries in the zip.
- Real build, `--xiaomi-fod` with `HAS_UDFPS=false`: exit 0, warning as above, no helper packed.
- Real build, `--xiaomi-fod` with `HAS_UDFPS=true` (config temporarily flipped, then restored — `git diff config.env` empty): `✓ fod/xiaomi-fod included`, and the ksu zip contains `fod/xiaomi-fod` at 0755.
- Menu driven with piped input: row renders `off`, toggling prints the note and re-renders as `on`.
- `node stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js` (6/6), `stuff/tests/docs-links.js`, `gofmt -l gui/app.go` (clean), and `app.js` parses.

**Limitation:** `go build ./...` can't run here — `webkit2gtk-4.0` dev headers aren't installed, so `cgo` fails before compiling `app.go`. The change there is one added string in the `build` verb's `Flags` slice; `gofmt` parsed it, but I could not execute the Go tests.

=== workflows ===
--- .github/workflows/check.yml
name: check

# The build itself needs the Android SDK (aapt2, apksigner, framework-res.apk),
# which this workflow deliberately does not install: these checks cover the
# parts that break silently — the WebUI's binary resource-table writer, the
# manifest it renders from, script syntax and documentation anchors.

on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      # The desktop app's own tests. CGO_ENABLED=0 is what stuff/tests/run.sh uses:
      # it skips the webview file, so no WebKitGTK headers are needed here —
      # and the browser fallback is the build that gets exercised.
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.23"
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum
          cache: true

      - name: Run the checks
        run: bash stuff/tests/run.sh

=== run.sh head ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Everything that can be checked without Android tools
# =============================================================================
# CI runs this on every push (see .github/workflows/check.yml), and it is worth
# running before a release:
#
#   bash stuff/tests/run.sh
#
# 1. shell syntax of every shipped script (bash -n / sh -n, no execution)
# 2. the WebUI resource-table writer against stuff/tests/fixtures/*.apk
# 3. the WebUI manifest and the overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off
#    vendor_hardware_overlay), built from
#    resource XML that stuff/tests/gen-res.sh generates into a temp directory (so
#    a fresh clone needs no build first)
# 4. every relative link and #anchor in the docs
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."

status=0
step() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$*"; }

step "shell syntax"
for f in build.sh treble-rro-creator.sh gui/build.sh stuff/scripts/*.sh stuff/tests/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if bash -n "$f"; then :; else echo "bash -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
done
# apply.sh, addons.sh and the module scripts run under Android's mksh
# (/system/bin/sh).
for f in src/webui/apply.sh src/webui/addons.sh src/module/*.sh stuff/templates/*.sh stuff/templates/recoveries/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if command -v sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if sh -n "$f"; then :; else echo "sh -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
    fi
done
[ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all scripts parse"

# The bug this guards: `clean --all` copied config.env from a frozen file, so a
# full clean handed back a version from an older commit. The copies below are
# now only the no-.git fallback, so they must equal the committed blob — not the
# working file, because local edits to config.env are normal.
step "template fallbacks match the release"
if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    copy_status=0
    check_copy() {
        local rel="$1" copy="$2"
        if [ ! -f "$copy" ]; then
            echo "missing fallback: $copy"
            copy_status=1
        elif ! git show "HEAD:$rel" | diff -q - "$copy" >/dev/null; then
            echo "$copy differs from HEAD:$rel — run: git show HEAD:$rel > $copy"
            copy_status=1
        fi
    }
    check_copy config.env stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    check_copy src/module/sepolicy.rule stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
    if [ "$copy_status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "fallbacks match"; else status=1; fi
else

> _Reasoning_
> Confirmed: `set_config_key` writes a detected value into config.env with no validation. config.env is sourced by build.sh. A value containing a newline (e.g. `ro.product.model` with newline — adb getprop values can contain weird chars?) or `$(cmd)` would not execute since it's written into a value assignment `KEY=$(cmd)` → sourced shell would execute command substitution! E.g. model `Xiaomi $(rm -rf ~)`. That's a genuine (if exotic) hardening item: values from the phone are untrusted input flowing into a sourced shell file. Also `udfps-probe.sh` same pattern. Also `cfg_set` in config-edit does cfg_quote but likely no `$`/backtick escaping.
> 
> Let me check cfg_quote.

> Also check match-prop writes value (device-sourced) via cfg_set — same.

> Also `ui_wrap` / printf "%s" fine.

Config values are user-controlled (documented), less critical but a robustness item (validate.sh could reject).

> _Reasoning_
> cfg_quote escapes `$`? It wraps in quotes when `$` present but does NOT escape `$` inside quotes — that's actually correct for config semantics? No: a quoted value `"a$(cmd)"` when sourced WILL execute command substitution. Quoting in shell does not disable `$(...)`. So config.env values containing `$` are command injection on source. cfg_quote quotes it which makes it worse (implies safety). Real hardening finding: escape `$` and backticks (e.g. `\$`) when the value contains them.
> 
> Wait, does config.env parsing use shell source? build.sh line ~40: `source "$CONFIG_FILE"`. Yes.
> 
> So: `DEVICE_MODEL="Xiaomi \$fig"`... Actually a legit model name could contain `$`? Unlikely but an OEM string with `$` is possible; also `$(...)` from a malicious phone. This is a genuine, concrete hardening item with a fix: in cfg_quote, prefix `$` and backtick with backslash; and restrict detected values (strip newlines and control chars) in set_config_key.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Why the UI is served at all
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The window is a webview pointed at a loopback URL. That is also what makes
// -browser and the Termux front-end free: same HTML, same handlers, no second
// UI to keep in sync with this one.
//
// The risk of a local server is that *any* page in the user's browser can POST
// to 127.0.0.1, and these handlers start build.sh. Two things stop that:
//
//  1. everything lives under a random /<token>/ prefix generated at launch, and
//     the page only learns it by being navigated to it — a cross-origin fetch
//     cannot read our HTML, so it cannot discover the prefix;
//  2. requests a browser marks as cross-site are refused outright.
//
// The listener is bound to 127.0.0.1, never 0.0.0.0, so nothing off-machine can
// reach it at all.
func (a *App) serve(port int) (net.Listener, string, *http.Server, error) {
  token, err := randomToken()
  if err != nil {
    return nil, "", nil, err
  }
  ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", port))
  if err != nil {
    return nil, "", nil, fmt.Errorf("could not open a loopback port: %w", err)
  }

  base := "/" + token
  assets, err := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui")
  if err != nil {
    return nil, "", nil, err
  }

  mux := http.NewServeMux()
  mux.HandleFunc(base, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    http.Redirect(w, r, base+"/", http.StatusFound)
  })
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/state", a.guard("GET", a.handleState))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/settings", a.guard("POST", a.handleSettings))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/config", a.guard("POST", a.handleConfig))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/run", a.guard("POST", a.handleRun))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/cancel", a.guard("POST", a.handleCancel))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/log", a.guard("GET", a.handleLog))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/log", a.guard("GET", a.handleAdbLog))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/open", a.guard("POST", a.handleOpen))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/docs", a.guard("GET", a.handleDocs))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/doc", a.guard("GET", a.handleDoc))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/update", a.guard("POST", a.handleUpdate))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/config/apply", a.guard("POST", a.handleConfigApply))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/addons", a.guard("GET", a.handleAddons))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/addons/save", a.guard("POST", a.handleAddonsSave))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb", a.guard("POST", a.handleAdb))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/devices", a.guard("GET", a.handleAdbDevices))

// extractPartition walks one partition and copies the kept files, returning how
// many it wrote and how large they are, plus the names of the few it could not
// decode so the caller can say so instead of quietly missing a build.prop.
func extractPartition(fs fileSystem, dest string) (kept int, bytes int64, scanned int, skipped []string, err error) {
  var paths []string
  err = fs.Walk(func(rel string, size int64, isDir bool) error {
    scanned++
    if isDir || !keepFirmwareFile(rel) || size > maxKeptFile {
      return nil
    }
    paths = append(paths, rel)
    return nil
  })
  if err != nil {
    return 0, 0, scanned, nil, err
  }

  for _, rel := range paths {
    data, err := fs.ReadPath(rel)
    if err != nil {
      // A file this reader cannot decode: skip it, keep the rest, but
      // remember it. Only the first few are named in the report.
      if len(skipped) < 5 {
        skipped = append(skipped, rel)
      }
      continue
    }
    dst := filepath.Join(dest, filepath.FromSlash(rel))
    if !strings.HasPrefix(dst, dest+string(filepath.Separator)) {
      continue // never write outside the partition folder
    }
    if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
      return kept, bytes, scanned, skipped, err
    }
    if err := os.WriteFile(dst, data, 0o644); err != nil {
      return kept, bytes, scanned, skipped, err
    }
    kept++
    bytes += int64(len(data))
  }
  if kept == 0 {
    // The folder still has to exist: the probe's `find` over it must not
    // fail just because a partition holds nothing it needs.
    if err := os.MkdirAll(dest, 0o755); err != nil {
      return 0, 0, scanned, skipped, err
    }
  }
  return kept, bytes, scanned, skipped, nil
}

#!/system/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay — WebUI helper
# =============================================================================
#
# Two mechanisms, because Android only allows one of them per value type:
#
#   dimens  the page patches the value straight into resources.arsc of the
#           overlay APK this module already ships (`apks`/`backup`/`restore`
#           below keep the paths and the pristine copies). A dimension the
#           build did not emit - config.env leaves the optional padding keys
#           commented out - is added to that table by the page, which then
#           writes the whole APK again. A static RRO is read when the
#           framework starts, so `reload` restarts zygote.
#           `cmd overlay fabricate` cannot be used for these: it only accepts
#           int/colour/bool/string data types and rejects a dimension with
#           "dataType is out of range of [16, 31] (too low)".
#
#   bools   a fabricated overlay (`cmd overlay fabricate`) still works and is
#           cheaper than repacking an APK, so config_displayBlanksAfterDoze is
#           registered at runtime and again at boot.
#
#   sh apply.sh get                 saved values + build-time defaults
#   sh apply.sh conf                only the saved values (webui.conf)
#   sh apply.sh set KEY=VALUE ...   store values only
#   sh apply.sh apply [--boot]      register the fabricated (bool) overlays
#   sh apply.sh manifest            the resource list the page renders
#   sh apply.sh apks                overlay APK paths the page patches
#   sh apply.sh backup              keep a pristine copy of those APKs
#   sh apply.sh restore             put the pristine APKs back

# Audit

Short verdict: the code is in better shape than most tools of this kind — nowhere near "rewrite me". The weak spots are concentrated in three places: **what gets written into `config.env`**, **what gets downloaded and executed**, and **the fact that the central build path is only ever tested by hand** (the Xiaomi FOD flag needed a real build run to be checked, which is exactly the gap).

---

## Do these first — hardening (real bugs, small fixes)

**1. `config.env` can still execute a command, and the probes can corrupt it.**
`build.sh:259` does `. "$ROOT/config.env"` — the file is *sourced*, not parsed. So any value that reaches it is shell code:

- `cfg_quote` in `config-edit.sh` wraps a value containing `$` or a backtick in double quotes but never escapes them, so a saved value like `$(reboot)` stays live and runs on the next build.
- `set_config_key` in `device-probe.sh:1148` writes detected values **raw**, with no quoting and no newline stripping. A device string with a newline (Easy mode writes three phone answers per run) splits the line and can make the next line look like another key.

Fix is two functions: escape `$`, `` ` ``, `"` and `\` inside the quoted branch, and reject control characters in `set_config_key` before writing. Longer term, a `config.env` reader that splits `KEY=value` instead of sourcing it removes the class of bug entirely — worth a decision, because `src/webui/apply.sh` already reads it line-by-line rather than sourcing.

**2. Downloads are trusted without a checksum.** `gui/build.sh:228-234` fetches the Go tarball and mingw and unpacks it. HTTPS protects transit, not the file. Pin one SHA-256 per version and compare before `tar xzf`; the pin can live next to the URL that's already there.

**3. The committed arm64 binary is unaudited.** `src/module/fod/xiaomi-fod` ships in every opt-in build and runs as root on the phone. Either build it in CI from `src/module/fod/main.go` and fail when the bytes differ, or add a `make fod` and stop committing the artifact. Right now nothing ties the binary to the source next to it.

**4. No `pipefail`.** `build.sh` sets `-e` only, so a failure inside a pipeline (`aapt2 … | tail`) is masked and the build reports success. `set -eo pipefail` is the cheap fix; `set -u` on the scripts hasn't been tried yet and would likely flush out a few unset-variable reads like the `$1` one you hit earlier.

**5. `src/webui/apply.sh` runs as root behind a page that patches `resources.arsc`.** The `case` statements validate types and numerics well. What I'd add: refuse any APK path that isn't under the module directory (a `..` or an absolute path from the pair loop), and keep the pristine `backup/` copy read-only so `restore` always has something real to fall back to.

---

## Fix when convenient — bugs and rough edges

| Where | Problem |
|---|---|
| `gui/build.sh:217` | `! is_termux` — the function is `is_termux`/`$IS_TERMUX` elsewhere; this is always true, so the guard never fires |
| `stuff/tests/docs-links.js:69` | `base` is assigned and never read |
| `device-probe.sh` multi-key write | "Easy" mode writes several keys; it is not atomic. A Ctrl-C between writes leaves the file half updated — build the list, then rewrite once |
| `set_config_key` / `cfg_set` | two writers, two different quoting rules for the same file. The GUI and the CLI can each produce a `config.env` the other renders differently |
| `docs/` | ~4,700 lines, no index. New users land in `configuration.md` (558 lines) and stop reading. One `docs/index.md` with a five-line map and "read this if…" is a 20-minute job that pays for itself |
| UI accessibility | 5 ARIA attributes in a 600-line `index.html`; checkboxes aren't grouped, and the build log has no `aria-live`. The new `?` badge is keyboard-reachable, the rest of the dialog isn't |
| `gui/ui/app.js` | ~4,000 lines, one file, no modules. Fine today; the next three features make it painful. Split when it hurts, not now |

---

## Missing things the tool actually needs

**1. A fake toolchain so `build.sh` can be tested.** Stub `aapt2`, `zipalign`, `apksigner`, `java` as shell scripts that emit plausible output, point `stuff/tools/` at them, and assert on the finished zip: which paths exist, what mode they have, what `module.prop` says. That is the rig that would have caught the FOD gating bug without a phone, and it makes every future flag cheap to verify. **This is the highest-value thing in the whole list.**

**2. A version number.** There is no `--version` and no version in the GUI title or the About box. Add a `VERSION` file, inject it with `-ldflags -X`, print it in the banner and the app. Without it a bug report can't say which build it came from, and an update check can't work.

**3. Profiles.** `config.env` holds one device. Anyone building for two phones (or experimenting and wanting the old values back) does it by hand. `stuff/profiles/<codename>/config.env` plus `--profile <name>` and a picker in the menu is small and removes real work.

**4. A verify step after install.** The ADB pane reads state; nothing closes the loop. "Push the module, reboot, then `cmd overlay list | grep <id>`" as one entry — with the reboot behind an explicit confirm — turns "did it work?" into a printed answer. This is the single biggest UX win after the GUI work, because the failure people actually hit is a module that installs and silently doesn't match.

**5. Root state in the header.** On Termux the tool sometimes needs root and sometimes doesn't. One line next to `Device` — `root  yes (tsu)` / `no` — saves a confusing failure later.

---

## Ideas (bigger, optional)

- **Submissions.** Emit the overlay + device facts + a filled PR body under `out/submission-<codename>/` so "match property" and "copy to sdcard" end in a ready-to-paste block.
- **Config diff on build.** Print "6 values differ from the template" with the keys; catches the placeholder left in by accident, which is the most common bad build.
- **Docs search in the app.** The docs pane lists files; it has no search. A plain `grep`-backed search over `docs/` is 30 lines and the docs are the heaviest part of the repo.
- **Screenshot of the result on device** — `adb exec-out screencap` after install, saved next to the zip, so a build has evidence attached. Say no if that's noise; it's the only item here I'd call a maybe.
- **Uzbek/Russian docs.** The audience is clearly non-English-heavy; a single translated `README` would outweigh most code work. Only if you want to maintain two copies.

---

## What I would not add

Don't add a plugin system, a second config format, a database for history, or a web dashboard for the build. The single-file `config.env`, the shell front end and the Go app are why this thing is understandable at all. Most of the value above comes from tightening what exists, not from new surface.

**Ranked, if you want an order:** fake-toolchain tests → `config.env` escaping → download checksums → `pipefail` + the `is_termux` guard → version → profiles → verify-after-install. The first four are small, and together they make everything after them safe to change.

- path: stuff/tests/run.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Everything that can be checked without Android tools
      # =============================================================================
      # CI runs this on every push (see .github/workflows/check.yml), and it is worth
      # running before a release:
      #
      #   bash stuff/tests/run.sh
      #
      # 1. shell syntax of every shipped script (bash -n / sh -n, no execution)
      # 2. the WebUI resource-table writer against stuff/tests/fixtures/*.apk
      # 3. the WebUI manifest and the overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off
      #    vendor_hardware_overlay), built from
      #    resource XML that stuff/tests/gen-res.sh generates into a temp directory (so
      #    a fresh clone needs no build first)
      # 4. every relative link and #anchor in the docs
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -euo pipefail
      cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
      
      status=0
      step() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$*"; }
      
      step "shell syntax"
      for f in build.sh treble-rro-creator.sh gui/build.sh stuff/scripts/*.sh stuff/tests/*.sh; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          if bash -n "$f"; then :; else echo "bash -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
      done
      # apply.sh, addons.sh and the module scripts run under Android's mksh
      # (/system/bin/sh).
      for f in src/webui/apply.sh src/webui/addons.sh src/module/*.sh stuff/templates/*.sh stuff/templates/recoveries/*.sh; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          if command -v sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if sh -n "$f"; then :; else echo "sh -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
          fi
      done
      [ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all scripts parse"
      
      # The bug this guards: `clean --all` copied config.env from a frozen file, so a
      # full clean handed back a version from an older commit. The copies below are
      # now only the no-.git fallback, so they must equal the committed blob — not the
      # working file, because local edits to config.env are normal.
      step "template fallbacks match the release"
      if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          copy_status=0
          check_copy() {
              local rel="$1" copy="$2"
              if [ ! -f "$copy" ]; then
                  echo "missing fallback: $copy"
                  copy_status=1
              elif ! git show "HEAD:$rel" | diff -q - "$copy" >/dev/null; then
                  echo "$copy differs from HEAD:$rel — run: git show HEAD:$rel > $copy"
                  copy_status=1
              fi
          }
          check_copy config.env stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
          check_copy src/module/sepolicy.rule stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
          if [ "$copy_status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "fallbacks match"; else status=1; fi
      else
          echo "not a git checkout — skipping"
      fi
      
      # restore_from_release() is what clean.sh and build.sh call. Run it against a
      # throwaway repository with a deliberately stale fallback, and once without
      # .git, because "start over" silently returning old values is the failure mode.
      step "restore picks the release, not the stale copy"
      restore_here="$(pwd)"
      restore_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-restore)"
      if (
          cd "$restore_tmp" || exit 1
          git init -q . && git config user.email t@example.com && git config user.name t || exit 1
          # No .gitattributes here, and Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true,
          # which would check the file back out with CRLF and fail the greps below.
          git config core.autocrlf false
          mkdir -p src/module stuff/templates/recoveries
          printf 'KEY="released"\n' > config.env
          printf 'released rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
          printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
          printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
          git add -A && git commit -qm one || exit 1
          # The user edits both files; the fallback copies are stale.
          printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
          printf 'my rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
          ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env" && restore_from_release src/module/sepolicy.rule "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 2
          grep -qx 'KEY="released"' config.env || { echo "git restore did not win: $(cat config.env)"; exit 3; }
          grep -qx 'released rules' src/module/sepolicy.rule || exit 4
          # No .git (a zip download): the bundled copy is the only source left.
          rm -rf .git
          printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
          ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 6
          grep -q 'STALE' config.env || { echo "fallback was not used without git"; exit 7; }
      ); then
          echo "restore behaves"
      else
          echo "restore test failed (exit $?)"
          status=1
      fi
      rm -rf "$restore_tmp"
      
      step "node tests"
      if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          node --test stuff/tests/arsc.test.js stuff/tests/manifest.test.js \
              stuff/tests/hw-overlay.test.js stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js \
              stuff/tests/adb-device.test.js stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js \
              stuff/tests/apply-sh.test.js stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js \
              stuff/tests/match-prop.test.js || status=1
      else
          echo "node is not installed — skipping the resource-table tests"
          status=1
      fi
      
      # The desktop app is optional: a clone without Go is still a complete CLI
      # install, so a missing toolchain skips instead of failing. CI installs Go and
      # runs this step for real (see .github/workflows/check.yml).
      step "desktop app (go)"
      if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./... || status=1
      else
          echo "go is not installed — skipping the desktop app tests"
      fi
      
      step "documentation links"
      if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          node stuff/tests/docs-links.js || status=1
      fi
      
      if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
          printf '\nSome checks failed.\n'
          exit 1
      fi
      printf '\nAll checks passed.\n'
      
- path: .github/workflows/check.yml
  content: |
      name: check
      
      # The build itself needs the Android SDK (aapt2, apksigner, framework-res.apk),
      # which this workflow deliberately does not install: these checks cover the
      # parts that break silently — the WebUI's binary resource-table writer, the
      # manifest it renders from, script syntax and documentation anchors.
      
      on:
        push:
          branches: ["**"]
        pull_request:
      
      jobs:
        check:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
              with:
                node-version: "20"
      
            # The desktop app's own tests. CGO_ENABLED=0 is what stuff/tests/run.sh uses:
            # it skips the webview file, so no WebKitGTK headers are needed here —
            # and the browser fallback is the build that gets exercised.
            - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
              with:
                go-version: "1.23"
                cache-dependency-path: go.sum
                cache: true
      
            - name: Run the checks
              run: bash stuff/tests/run.sh

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # config-edit.sh — read and write one key of config.env
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by the terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh) and by
      # stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh. The probes carry their own copy of the writer
      # because they are shipped standalone; anything new should source this.
      #
      # The file is the source of truth and stays hand-editable: these helpers rewrite
      # one line, keep the indentation, keep the quoting the line already used, and
      # turn a commented-out KEY= line into a live one (that is what "enable it"
      # means). Nothing here validates values — `./build.sh check` does that.
      # =============================================================================
      
      : "${ROOT:?stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh must be sourced with ROOT set}"
      
      # cfg_file -> the file the helpers act on, so a test can point somewhere else.
      cfg_file() {
          printf '%s' "${CFG_FILE:-${CONFIG_FILE:-$ROOT/config.env}}"
      }
      
      # cfg_unquote VALUE -> the value without the quotes config.env puts around text.
      cfg_unquote() {
          local v="$1"
          case "$v" in
              \"*\") v="${v#\"}"; v="${v%\"}" ;;
              \'*\') v="${v#\'}"; v="${v%\'}" ;;
          esac
          printf '%s' "$v"
      }
      
      # cfg_quote VALUE -> a value config.env can be sourced from.
      # Plain words stay bare, as they are in the file today; anything a shell would
      # split on, or anything that was already quoted, gets double quotes.
      cfg_quote() {
          local value="$1" force="${2:-0}"
          case "$value" in
              "") printf '""'; return 0 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$force" != "1" ]; then
              case "$value" in
                  *[[:space:]]*|*'#'*|*'"'*|*"'"*|*'$'*|*'`'*|*'\'*) ;;
                  *) printf '%s' "$value"; return 0 ;;
              esac
          fi
          value="${value//\\/\\\\}"
          value="${value//\"/\\\"}"
          printf '"%s"' "$value"
      }
      
      # cfg_get KEY -> the live value, unquoted, empty when the key is absent or off.
      cfg_get() {
          local key="$1" file line value=""
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
              line="${line%$'\r'}"
              case "$line" in
                  "$key="*) value="${line#*=}" ;;
              esac
          done <"$file"
          [ -n "$value" ] || return 0
          cfg_unquote "$value"
      }
      
      # cfg_has KEY -> 0 when KEY= (or #KEY=) exists in the file at all.
      cfg_has() {
          local key="$1" file
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*${key}=" "$file"
      }
      
      # cfg_rows -> one row per assignment, tab separated:
      #   key <TAB> active(0|1) <TAB> line number <TAB> section <TAB> value
      # A commented-out key is listed with active=0 so it can be turned on by name
      # instead of by hunting for the '#'. Prose that happens to end in '=' is not a
      # row: only `KEY=` and `#KEY=` (no space after the '#') count.
      cfg_rows() {
          local file
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          awk '
              /^#[[:space:]]*─/ {
                  sec = $0
                  sub(/^#[[:space:]]*/, "", sec)
                  gsub(/─/, "", sec)
                  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", sec)
                  next
              }
              /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ || /^#[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/\r$/, "", line)
                  key = line
                  sub(/=.*/, "", key)
                  active = 1
                  if (key ~ /^#/) { active = 0; sub(/^#/, "", key) }
                  value = substr(line, index(line, "=") + 1)
                  printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\n", key, active, NR, sec, value
              }
          ' "$file"
      }
      
      # cfg_sections -> the section titles in file order, one per line.
      cfg_sections() {

- path: gui/build.sh
  content: |
      # Go: used when present, downloaded when not
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The launcher is the first command a new clone runs, so "install Go and come
      # back" is not an answer. The official tarball is unpacked into
      # stuff/tools/_go/ — inside the clone, no root, and found again by every later
      # build. The leading underscore matters: the go tool skips such directories,
      # so this copy of Go's source tree is not pulled into `go test ./...`. A Go
      # already on PATH is used when it is new enough; distro packages are often
      # older than go.mod asks for, which is why a too-old one is passed over
      # instead of trusted.
      
      tools_dir="$here/../stuff/tools"
      local_go="$tools_dir/_go/bin/go"
      case "$(uname -s)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) local_go="$local_go.exe" ;;
      esac
      
      go_required() {
          local req
          req="$(awk '$1 == "go" { print $2; exit }' "$here/../go.mod" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          echo "${req:-1.23}"
      }
      
      # version_at_least <have> <want>, both dotted ("1.23", "1.23.4").
      version_at_least() {
          awk -v have="$1" -v want="$2" 'BEGIN {
              n = split(have, h, "."); m = split(want, w, ".")
              if (m > n) n = m
              for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                  a = (i in h) ? h[i] + 0 : 0
                  b = (i in w) ? w[i] + 0 : 0
                  if (a > b) exit 0
                  if (a < b) exit 1
              }
              exit 0
          }'
      }
      
      go_usable() {
          [ -x "$1" ] || return 1
          local v
          v="$("$1" version 2>/dev/null | awk '{ sub(/^go/, "", $3); print $3 }')"
          [ -n "$v" ] || return 1
          version_at_least "$v" "$(go_required)"
      }
      
      # fetch_url <url> [outfile]: the body on stdout, or into the file.
      fetch_url() {
          if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
                  # One repainted line: Go is ~70 MB, and a full meter for that is
                  # hundreds of lines in the launcher's output.
                  curl -fL --retry 2 --progress-bar -o "$2" "$1"
              else
                  curl -fsSL --retry 2 "$1"
              fi
          elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
                  wget -O "$2" "$1"
              else
                  wget -qO- "$1"
              fi
          else
              return 1
          fi
      }
      
      # The os-arch half of the download name, empty when there is no official
      # build for this machine.
      go_platform() {
          local os arch
          case "$(uname -s)" in
              Linux*)
                  # Termux is Android: its prefix is not an FHS root and Go's Linux
                  # tarball is not built for it, but its own package manager has Go.
                  case "${PREFIX:-}" in
                      *com.termux*) return 1 ;;
                  esac
                  os=linux
                  ;;
              Darwin*) os=darwin ;;
              MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) os=windows ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$(uname -m)" in
              x86_64|amd64)        arch=amd64 ;;
              i386|i486|i586|i686)  arch=386 ;;
              aarch64|arm64)       arch=arm64 ;;
              armv6l|armv7l)       arch=armv6l ;;
              ppc64le)             arch=ppc64le ;;

> _Reasoning_
> I spot a real bug already: `cfg_quote` case pattern has `*'\'*` written as `*'\\'*`? In the file it shows: `*[[:space:]]*|*'#'*|*'"'*|*"'"*|*'$'*|*'\`'*|*'\'*` — the raw shows `*'\\'*` which in the JSON is `*'\\\\'*`? Let me look: `*'$'*|*'`'*|*'\'*)` — the raw content shows:
> 
> ```
>             *[[:space:]]*|*'#'*|*'"'*|*"'"*|*'$'*|*'`'*|*'\'*) ;;
> ```
> 
> So backslash triggers quoting. And then escape does `value=${value//\\/\\\\}` (backslash→double) and `value=${value//\"/\\\"}` (quote→escaped). Missing: `$` and backtick escaping. So a value containing `$` is quoted but the `$` isn't escaped → executed on source. Confirmed real.
> 
> Now, careful: config.env itself is hand-editable and contains things like `DEVICE_MODEL="Redmi Note 17"`. Does escaping matter for existing values? Adding `\$` escaping only changes values that contain `$`, which are currently broken anyway.
>

# version_at_least <have> <want>, both dotted ("1.23", "1.23.4").
version_at_least() {
    awk -v have="$1" -v want="$2" 'BEGIN {
        n = split(have, h, "."); m = split(want, w, ".")
        if (m > n) n = m
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            a = (i in h) ? h[i] + 0 : 0
            b = (i in w) ? w[i] + 0 : 0
            if (a > b) exit 0
            if (a < b) exit 1
        }
        exit 0
    }'
}

go_usable() {
    [ -x "$1" ] || return 1
    local v
    v="$("$1" version 2>/dev/null | awk '{ sub(/^go/, "", $3); print $3 }')"
    [ -n "$v" ] || return 1
    version_at_least "$v" "$(go_required)"
}

# fetch_url <url> [outfile]: the body on stdout, or into the file.
fetch_url() {
    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
            # One repainted line: Go is ~70 MB, and a full meter for that is
            # hundreds of lines in the launcher's output.
            curl -fL --retry 2 --progress-bar -o "$2" "$1"
        else
            curl -fsSL --retry 2 "$1"
        fi
    elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
            wget -O "$2" "$1"
        else
            wget -qO- "$1"
        fi
    else
        return 1
    fi
}

// Command xiaomi-fod switches a Xiaomi touch panel into fingerprint-on-display
// mode, which is the one thing a GSI cannot do for the vendor fingerprint HAL.
//
// The stock flow is:
//
//  MIUI FingerprintService
//    -> vendor.xiaomi.hardware.fingerprintextension.extCmd(4, 3)
//    -> vendor.xiaomi.hardware.touchfeature.setModeValue(10, 3)

// A GSI has no MIUI fingerprint client, so the last call never happens. The

// finger, and the sensor appears dead even though the geometry is right.

// This helper issues the same ioctl directly. The daemon follows the state

=== apply.sh apk section ===
do_restart_systemui() {
    # At boot SystemUI may not have been started yet; killing an empty pid
    # would leave the stale values on screen. Wait a moment for it.
    n=0
    while [ "$n" -lt 10 ]; do
        pid=$(pidof com.android.systemui 2>/dev/null)
        [ -n "$pid" ] && break
        n=$((n + 1))
        sleep 2
    done
    if [ -n "$pid" ]; then
        # SystemUI is a persistent app: init starts it again immediately.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        kill -9 $pid 2>/dev/null && { say "SystemUI restarted (pid ${pid% *})"; return 0; }
    fi
    if command -v killall >/dev/null 2>&1 && killall com.android.systemui 2>/dev/null; then
        say "SystemUI restarted"
        return 0
    fi
    if command -v pkill >/dev/null 2>&1 && pkill -f com.android.systemui 2>/dev/null; then
        say "SystemUI restarted"
        return 0
    fi
    say "! Could not restart SystemUI - reboot or run 'killall com.android.systemui' as root"
    return 1
}

# --- the shipped overlay APKs ----------------------------------------------
# The page rewrites the value of a dimension inside resources.arsc of these
# files. Both are named after the module id; the SystemUI one has a -systemui
# suffix. Nothing here parses the APK - the page does that - this only hands
# out the paths and keeps a pristine copy to fall back to.

overlay_dir() { printf '%s' "$MODDIR/system/product/overlay"; }

fw_apk() {
    for apk in "$(overlay_dir)"/*.apk; do
        [ -f "$apk" ] || continue
        case "$apk" in
            *-systemui.apk) ;;
            *) printf '%s' "$apk"; return 0 ;;
        esac
    done
}

sui_apk() {
    for apk in "$(overlay_dir)"/*-systemui.apk; do
        [ -f "$apk" ] && { printf '%s' "$apk"; return 0; }
    done
}

do_apks() {
    fw=$(fw_apk)
    sui=$(sui_apk)
    say "fw=${fw:-}"
    say "sui=${sui:-}"
    say "write=$([ -w "$(overlay_dir)" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    say "uid=$(id -u 2>/dev/null)"
}

# Keep the APK the build produced, so the page can be undone after a patch.
# $apk.webui-orig also tells the rest of the script whether an APK was patched.
do_backup() {
    dir=$(overlay_dir)
    [ -d "$dir" ] || { say "x overlay directory not found: $dir"; return 1; }
    [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" = "0" ] || {
        say "x backup needs root (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"; return 1
    }

    rc=0
    for apk in "$dir"/*.apk; do
        [ -f "$apk" ] || continue
        name=${apk##*/}
        if [ -f "$apk.webui-orig" ]; then
            say "+ backup kept: $name"
            continue
        fi
        # cp -p keeps the timestamp, but the copy is never mounted, so only
        # its contents matter.
        if cp -p "$apk" "$apk.webui-orig" 2>/dev/null; then
            say "+ backup: $name"

main() {
    action="${1:-get}"
    [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

    case "$action" in
        get)
            do_get
            ;;
        set)
            result=0
            for pair in "$@"; do
                case "$pair" in
                    *=*) ;;
                    *) say "! not a KEY=VALUE pair: $pair"; result=2; continue ;;
                esac
                key=${pair%%=*}
                val=${pair#*=}
                val=$(printf '%s' "$val" | tr -d '\r\n')
                # Any key is accepted: the page writes full resource names
                # (dimen/status_bar_padding_top) next to the five short ones.
                put_conf "$key" "$val" || result=1
            done
            ;;
        arm)
            # Called by the page after it wrote an APK, so the boot guard also
            # covers a patch that is loaded by a normal reboot, not just by
            # 'reload'.
            boot_arm
            say "armed=$(read_num "$GEN_FILE")"
            ;;
        apply)
            boot=false
            for a in "$@"; do
                case "$a" in
                    --boot) boot=true ;;
                esac
            done

            if $boot; then
                # init/OMS/package scanning are not ready immediately at boot.
                n=0
                while [ "$n" -lt 15 ]; do
                    "$CMD" overlay list >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
                    n=$((n + 1))
                    sleep 2
                done
                # Right after boot_completed the overlay manager can still be
                # finishing its first scan, and a fabricate call then fails.
                sleep 3
            fi

            # One attempt is enough: the boolean is the only thing registered
            # here, and a failure prints its own reason.
            result=1
            attempt=0
            while :; do
                do_apply
                result=$?
                [ "$result" -eq 0 ] && break
                [ "$result" -eq 2 ] && break
                attempt=$((attempt + 1))
                # At boot the overlay manager may still be settling.
                [ "$attempt" -ge 3 ] && break
                [ "$boot" = "true" ] || break
                sleep 5
            done
            ;;
        conf)
            # Only what the page saved (no build-time defaults): this is what
            # tells the page whether there is anything to restore.
            [ -f "$CONF" ] && cat "$CONF"
            ;;
        apks)
            do_apks
            ;;
        manifest)
            if [ -f "$MODDIR/webroot/webui-manifest.json" ]; then
                cat "$MODDIR/webroot/webui-manifest.json"
            else
                say "x no manifest in this build (rebuild the module)"
                result=1
            fi

- path: stuff/scripts/menu.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # menu.sh — the terminal front end
      # =============================================================================
      # The desktop app and this file drive the same tools: the device probes, the
      # addon catalog, the match-property ranking and build.sh's own verbs. The goal
      # is that a phone with a terminal (Termux, ssh, a server) gets the same answers
      # as the window, without a GUI toolkit.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 opens this (when stdin is a terminal)
      #   ./build.sh menu            opens this even when stdin is not a terminal
      #   bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh same thing, standalone
      #
      # Every action shells out to the real entry point — `build.sh build`,
      # `device-probe.sh --write`, `addons.sh set` — so there is exactly one
      # implementation of each step and the menu cannot drift from the app.
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
          . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      # The device-source helpers (device_is_termux, device_local_begin) live with the
      # adb code the probes share. Sourcing it here defines functions only.
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Small things
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MENU_SLEEP="${MENU_SLEEP:-0}"
      
      # A width-aware rule under a section title. Every screen used to draw a fixed
      # 58-character one, which wrapped onto a second line on a phone.
      hr() { ui_rule 2; }
      
      # Read one line. Returns 1 at EOF (piped input, a launcher with no console) so
      # callers can leave the menu instead of looping forever.
      menu_read() {
          local prompt="${1:-} " answer=""
          printf '%s' "$prompt"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              return 1
          fi
          MENU_ANSWER="$answer"
          return 0
      }
      
      # Wait for Enter between screens, unless stdin is not a terminal.
      pause_menu() {
          [ -t 0 ] || return 0
          printf '\n  %s ' "Press Enter to go back"
          read -r _ || true
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # Count the rows config.env has, and how many are switched off.
      cfg_counts() {
          local rows
          rows="$(cfg_rows 2>/dev/null)" || { CFG_ON=0; CFG_OFF=0; return 0; }
          CFG_ON="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 1' | grep -c . || true)"
          CFG_OFF="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 0' | grep -c . || true)"
      }
      
      output_summary() {
          local apks=0 zips=0 zip=""
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR/apks" ] && apks="$(find "$OUT_DIR/apks" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && zips="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          zip="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | sort | head -n1)"
          if [ "$zips" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '%s  (%s APK%s)' "${zip#$ROOT/}" "$apks" "$([ "$apks" = 1 ] || echo s)"
          else
              printf 'nothing built yet'
          fi
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Screen
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The state of the checkout in one box: which phone, how much of config.env is
      # filled in, what the last build left behind.
      menu_header() {
          cfg_counts
          ui_panel "Treble Overlay Creator" \
              "Device|$(cfg_identity)" \
              "config.env|${CFG_ON} set ${UI_DOT} ${CFG_OFF} off" \
              "Output|$(output_summary)"
      }
      
      # 11 is the width of the longest label here, so every description starts in the
      # same column instead of ragging after each label.
      MENU_LW=14
      
      menu_items() {
          ui_item 1 'Build'          'dry run, build, check, doctor, clean' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 2 'config.env'     'browse and edit one key at a time' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 3 'Addons'         'module tweaks: settings and overlay resources' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 4 'Device'         'read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 5 'Auto Detect'    'ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 6 'UDFPS'          'in-display fingerprint geometry' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 7 'Match property' 'which property the submission should match on' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 8 'Files'          'what was built, and where it is' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 9 'Docs'           'the guides in docs/' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item q 'Quit' '' "$MENU_LW"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The menu never re-implements a build step: it runs the entry point with the
      # verb a user would type, so `build.sh doctor` and 1 → 4 are the same command.
      run_entry() {
          ( cd "$ROOT" && bash "$ROOT/build.sh" "$@" )
      }
      
      # Whether the Xiaomi FOD helper ships in the module. Off by default: it is only
      # useful on Xiaomi optical UDFPS phones, and on anything else it is a binary
      # that never starts. `./build.sh --xiaomi-fod menu` starts it already on.
      MENU_XIAOMI_FOD="${XIAOMI_FOD:-false}"
      
      # The --xiaomi-fod argument for a build started from here, or nothing at all.
      xiaomi_fod_arg() {
          [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ] && printf '%s' '--xiaomi-fod'
      }
      
      menu_build() {
          while :; do
              if [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ]; then
                  fod_state='on'
              else
                  fod_state='off'
              fi
              ui_heading 'Build'
              ui_item 1 'Dry run'     'print the resources config.env emits, build nothing' 11
              ui_item 2 'Build'       'build the module (installs tools if needed)' 11
              ui_item 3 'Check'       'validate config.env without building' 11
              ui_item 4 'Doctor'      'check the toolchain, install nothing' 11
              ui_item 5 'Clean'       'remove build output' 11
              ui_item 6 'Clean --all' 'start over for a different device' 11
              ui_item 7 'Xiaomi FOD' "$fod_state · HBM + touch-panel FOD mode for Xiaomi UDFPS" 11
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 11
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) run_entry --dry-run; pause_menu ;;
                  2)
                      # shellcheck disable=SC2046 # the flag is one word or none
                      run_entry build $(xiaomi_fod_arg)
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  3) run_entry check; pause_menu ;;
                  4) run_entry doctor; pause_menu ;;
                  5) run_entry clean; pause_menu ;;
                  6)
                      warn "This removes config.env and the device files too."
                      if confirm "  Start over for a different device? [y/N] " n; then
                          run_entry clean --all
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  7)
                      if [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ]; then
                          MENU_XIAOMI_FOD=false
                      else
                          MENU_XIAOMI_FOD=true
                          info "Next build ships fod/xiaomi-fod — use only if your phone is Xiaomi and has a UDFPS sensor."
                      fi
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Files
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Where a copy lands on the phone. /sdcard is the same folder whether it is this
      # phone (Termux, where ~/storage/shared points at it) or a cabled one (adb), so
      # the path in the message is one a reader can go and look in either way.
      FILES_PHONE_DIR="/sdcard/treble-rro-creator"
      
      # The build's own outputs, one path per line: the flashable zips and the APKs
      # sitting inside them.
      built_files() {
          find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.apk' \) 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort
      }
      
      # files_copy_to_phone — put the build on the phone's shared storage.
      #
      # On the phone itself (Termux) that is a plain cp, once Termux has been given
      # access to /sdcard. From a computer it is `adb push`, because the build tree is
      # on the wrong side of the cable; the destination is the same folder, so the
      # instructions afterwards do not depend on which machine ran the build.
      files_copy_to_phone() {
          local -a files=()
          local f base="" dest copied=0 failed=0 src
          while IFS= read -r f; do files+=("$f"); done < <(built_files)
          if [ "${#files[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              info "Nothing to copy yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
              return 0
          fi
      
          if device_is_termux; then
              # ~/storage/shared only exists after termux-setup-storage; /sdcard is
              # still worth trying because some builds of Termux ship it ready.
              if [ -d "$HOME/storage/shared" ]; then
                  base="$HOME/storage/shared"
              elif [ -d /sdcard ]; then
                  base="/sdcard"
              fi
              if [ -z "$base" ]; then
                  err "Termux cannot see this phone's storage."
                  echo "     Run: termux-setup-storage"
                  echo "     Then: 8 → 1 again"
                  return 1
              fi
              dest="$base/treble-rro-creator"
              if ! mkdir -p "$dest" 2>/dev/null; then
                  err "Cannot create $FILES_PHONE_DIR."
                  echo "     Run: termux-setup-storage   (it asks for the storage permission)"
                  return 1
              fi
              info "Copying ${#files[@]} file(s) to $FILES_PHONE_DIR..."
              for f in "${files[@]}"; do
                  if cp -f "$f" "$dest/" 2>/dev/null; then
                      ui_mark ok "$(basename "$f")  $(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"
                      copied=$((copied + 1))
                  else
                      ui_mark bad "$(basename "$f") — could not be written"
                      failed=$((failed + 1))
                  fi
              done
          else
              # A computer: the phone is only reachable through adb, and a build for a
              # phone that is not plugged in goes nowhere.
              if ! resolve_adb; then
                  err "adb was not found — install platform-tools and try again."
                  return 1
              fi
              adb_pick_device "$adb" "" "files" || return 1
              if ! "$adb" ${DEVICE_SERIAL:+-s "$DEVICE_SERIAL"} shell "mkdir -p $FILES_PHONE_DIR" \
                      >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  err "Could not create $FILES_PHONE_DIR on the phone."
                  echo "     Check that the phone is unlocked and the storage is not full."
                  return 1
              fi
              info "Pushing ${#files[@]} file(s) to $FILES_PHONE_DIR..."
              for f in "${files[@]}"; do
                  # A Windows adb cannot open an MSYS path, so the local half is
                  # converted when cygpath exists (Git Bash) and passed as it is
                  # everywhere else.
                  src="$f"
                  command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1 && src="$(cygpath -w "$f")"
                  if "$adb" ${DEVICE_SERIAL:+-s "$DEVICE_SERIAL"} push "$src" "$FILES_PHONE_DIR/" \
                          >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                      ui_mark ok "$(basename "$f")  $(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"
                      copied=$((copied + 1))
                  else
                      ui_mark bad "$(basename "$f") — adb push failed"
                      failed=$((failed + 1))
                  fi
              done
          fi
      
          echo ""
          if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
              warn "$copied copied, $failed failed."
              return 1
          fi
          ui_mark ok "$copied file(s) in $FILES_PHONE_DIR"
          ui_mark note "Open Files on the phone, or flash the module from there."
          return 0
      }
      
      menu_files() {
          local -a table=() f
          while :; do
              ui_heading 'Files'
              ui_panel 'Where things are' \
                  "Project|$ROOT" \
                  "config.env|$ROOT/config.env" \
                  "Build tree|${BUILD_DIR#$ROOT/}"
              echo ""
              table=()
              if [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$OUT_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
                  while IFS= read -r f; do
                      table+=("$(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)|${f#$ROOT/}")
                  done < <(built_files)
              fi
              if [ "${#table[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  info "Nothing built yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
                  pause_menu
                  return 0
              fi
              ui_table 'Size|Built file' "${table[@]}"
              echo ""
              ui_item 1 'Copy' "to $FILES_PHONE_DIR on the phone" 11
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 11
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) echo ""; files_copy_to_phone; pause_menu ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Docs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_docs() {
          local files=() i
          ui_heading 'Docs'
          [ -d "$ROOT/docs" ] || { warn "docs/ is missing from this checkout."; pause_menu; return 0; }
          while IFS= read -r f; do
              files+=("$f")
          done < <(find "$ROOT/docs" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
          for i in "${!files[@]}"; do
              ui_item "$((i + 1))" "$(basename "${files[$i]}")"
          done
          echo ""
          menu_read "  number to read, Enter to go back >" || return 0
          case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
              ''|q) return 0 ;;
              *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number."; return 0 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#files[@]}" ]; then
              warn "No such doc."
              return 0
          fi
          local pick="${files[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]}"
          echo ""
          if [ -t 1 ] && command -v less >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              less -R "$pick"
          else
              cat "$pick"
          fi
          return 0
