      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The file keeps its shape: these helpers rewrite one line and leave the
      # comments, the section headers and the quoting alone. A key that is commented
      # out shows as `off` and can be switched on by number, which is the whole point
      # of listing it — hunting for the '#' in a 240-line file is where mistakes
      # happen.
      cfg_each_row() { # <section> -> `key<TAB>active<TAB>value` rows of that section
          local section="$1"
          cfg_rows 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' -v s="$section" '$4 == s { print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $5 }'
      }
      
      cfg_section_stats() { # -> `section<TAB>set<TAB>off`, in file order
          cfg_rows 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '
              { if (!($4 in seen)) { seen[$4] = 1; order[n++] = $4 }
                if ($2 == 1) on[$4]++ ; else off[$4]++ }
              END { for (i = 0; i < n; i++) printf "%s\t%d\t%d\n", order[i], on[order[i]], off[order[i]] }
          '
      }
      
      # cfg_list_row NUM KEYW KEY ACTIVE VALUE — one line of a config.env section.
      #
      # A key has three things worth seeing at once: whether it is switched on, its
      # name, and its value. They are three aligned columns when the window has room
      # and two lines when it does not — the state keeps its colour either way, so
      # scanning down the page is still "find the green ones".
      cfg_list_row() {
          local num="$1" keyw="$2" key="$3" active="$4" value="$5"
          local cols state statepad color avail vw vcolor
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          if [ "$active" = "1" ]; then state='on'; color="$UI_GREEN"; else state='off'; color="$UI_DIM"; fi
          printf -v statepad '%*s' $((3 - ${#state})) ''
          # The colour is kept out of the text until printing, so measuring the value
          # never counts escape bytes.
          if [ -z "$value" ]; then value='(empty)'; vcolor="$UI_DIM"; else vcolor="$UI_BOLD"; fi
          # A key longer than the shared column is measured on its own: the column is
          # a convenience, not a licence to print past the window.
          [ "${#key}" -gt "$keyw" ] && keyw=${#key}
      
          avail=$((cols - (2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + keyw + 2)))
          # Three columns only when the whole value fits in the one that is left: a
          # value cut to `Redmi Not…` is worse than the two-line form, which has the
          # rest of the window to wrap into.
          if [ "$avail" -ge 8 ] && [ "${#value}" -le $((avail - 1)) ]; then
              vw=$((avail - 1))
              printf '  %s%3d%s  %s%-3s%s  %s%-*s%s  %s%s%s\n' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$num" "$UI_OFF" "$color" "$state" "$UI_OFF" \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$keyw" "$key" "$UI_OFF" \
                  "$vcolor" "$(ui_fit "$value" "$vw")" "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          # No room for three columns: the key starts on the number's line and wraps
          # under itself, and the value wraps below. A 24-character property name is
          # wider than a phone, so both are wrapped rather than run off the edge.
          local l first=1
          ui_wrap "$key" 0 $((cols - 13)) | while IFS= read -r l; do
              if [ "$first" = 1 ]; then
                  printf '  %s%3d%s  %s%-3s%s  %s%s%s\n' \
                      "$UI_DIM" "$num" "$UI_OFF" "$color" "$state" "$UI_OFF" \
                      "$UI_BOLD" "$l" "$UI_OFF"
                  first=0
              else
                  printf '            %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$l" "$UI_OFF"
              fi
          done
          ui_wrap "$value" 12 $((cols - 13)) | while IFS= read -r l; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$vcolor" "$l" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      cfg_edit_value() {
          local key="$1" current value
          current="$(cfg_get "$key")"
          printf '\n  %s = %s\n' "$key" "${current:-<empty>}"
          menu_read "  new value (Enter keeps it, - clears it)" || return 0
          value="$MENU_ANSWER"
          [ -z "$value" ] && { info "Left it alone."; return 0; }
          [ "$value" = "-" ] && value=""
          if cfg_set "$key" "$value"; then
              ok "$key is now ${value:-<empty>}"
          else
              err "Could not write config.env — is it read-only?"
          fi
      }
      
      cfg_section() { # <section title>
          local section="$1" rows=() row i n=0
          while :; do
              rows=()
              while IFS= read -r row; do
                  [ -n "$row" ] && rows+=("$row")
              done < <(cfg_each_row "$section")
      
              echo ""
              echo -e "  ${BOLD}${section:-Unsectioned}${NC}"
              hr
              if [ "${#rows[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  info "This section has no keys."
                  pause_menu
                  return 0
              fi
              # One width for the key column, so the values line up down the page.
              local keyw=0
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  local k="${rows[$i]%%$'\t'*}"
                  [ "${#k}" -gt "$keyw" ] && keyw=${#k}
              done
              [ "$keyw" -le 30 ] || keyw=30
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  local key="${rows[$i]%%$'\t'*}" rest="${rows[$i]#*$'\t'}"
                  local active="${rest%%$'\t'*}" value="${rest#*$'\t'}"
                  value="$(printf '%s' "$value" | sed 's/^"\(.*\)"$/\1/')"
                  cfg_list_row "$((i + 1))" "$keyw" "$key" "$active" "$value"
              done
              echo ""
              ui_mark note "number = edit ${UI_DOT} d<number> = switch off ${UI_DOT} e<number> = switch on ${UI_DOT} 0 = back"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  d*|D*)
                      i="${MENU_ANSWER#?}"
                      case "$i" in ''|*[!0-9]*) warn "d needs a number, like d3."; continue ;; esac
                      if [ "$i" -lt 1 ] || [ "$i" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then warn "No such key."; continue; fi
                      key="${rows[$((i - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      if cfg_set_active "$key" 0; then ok "$key switched off"; else err "Could not write config.env"; fi
                      ;;
                  e*|E*)
                      i="${MENU_ANSWER#?}"
                      case "$i" in ''|*[!0-9]*) warn "e needs a number, like e3."; continue ;; esac
                      if [ "$i" -lt 1 ] || [ "$i" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then warn "No such key."; continue; fi
                      key="${rows[$((i - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      if cfg_set_active "$key" 1; then ok "$key switched on"; else err "Could not write config.env"; fi
                      ;;
                  *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number." ;;
                  *)
                      if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#rows[@]}" ]; then
                          warn "No such key."
                          continue
                      fi
                      cfg_edit_value "${rows[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]%%$'\t'*}"
                      ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      menu_config() {
          local sections=() i lw name on off
          while :; do
              sections=()
              local -a counts=()
              while IFS=$'\t' read -r name on off; do
                  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
                  sections+=("$name")
                  counts+=("$(printf '%s set %s %s off' "$on" "$UI_DOT" "$off")")
              done < <(cfg_section_stats 2>/dev/null)
              # A config.env with no section headers still has keys.
              if [ "${#sections[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  while IFS= read -r name; do
                      [ -n "$name" ] && { sections+=("$name"); counts+=(''); }
                  done < <(cfg_sections 2>/dev/null)
              fi
      
              cfg_counts
              ui_heading 'config.env'
              local hdr_cols hdr_path
              hdr_cols=$(ui_cols)
              hdr_path="$ROOT/config.env"
              if [ $(( 2 + ${#CFG_ON} + 5 + ${#CFG_OFF} + 6 + ${#hdr_path} )) -le "$hdr_cols" ]; then
                  printf '  %s%d set%s %s %s%d off%s   %s%s%s\n\n' \
                      "$UI_GREEN" "$CFG_ON" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DOT" \
                      "$UI_DIM" "$CFG_OFF" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DIM" "$hdr_path" "$UI_OFF"
              else
                  # A full checkout path is wider than a phone: the counts keep the
                  # first line, the path wraps under them.
                  printf '  %s%d set%s %s %s%d off%s\n' \
                      "$UI_GREEN" "$CFG_ON" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DOT" \
                      "$UI_DIM" "$CFG_OFF" "$UI_OFF"
                  ui_wrap "$hdr_path" 4 $((hdr_cols - 5)) | while IFS= read -r name; do
                      printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$name" "$UI_OFF"
                  done
                  printf '\n'
              fi
              if [ "${#sections[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  err "config.env is missing or empty: $ROOT/config.env"
                  pause_menu
                  return 0
              fi
              lw=0
              for i in "${!sections[@]}"; do
                  [ "${#sections[$i]}" -gt "$lw" ] && lw=${#sections[$i]}
              done
              for i in "${!sections[@]}"; do
                  ui_item "$((i + 1))" "${sections[$i]}" "${counts[$i]}" "$lw"
              done
              ui_item 0 'Back'
              menu_read "  section >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number." ;;
                  *)
                      if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#sections[@]}" ]; then
                          warn "No such section."
                          continue
                      fi
                      cfg_section "${sections[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]}"
                      ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Addons
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The catalog lives in src/webui/addons.sh and is read here, not copied: the
      # module page on the phone and the desktop app read the same file. The menu
      # only chooses which `set` to run.
      addons_script() { printf '%s' "$ROOT/src/webui/addons.sh"; }
      addons_conf() { printf '%s' "$ROOT/src/module/addons.conf"; }
      
      addons_call() { # <verb> ... — in the clone, with the clone's addons.conf
          ADDONS_DIR="$ROOT" ADDONS_CONF="$(addons_conf)" sh "$(addons_script)" "$@"
      }
      
      addons_saved() { # <id> -> the value in addons.conf, empty when unset
          local file
          file="$(addons_conf)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
          awk -F= -v id="$1" '$1 == id { sub(/^[^=]*=/, ""); print; exit }' "$file"
      }
      
      # addons_row NUM MARK LABEL VALUE CHOICES [ (overlay) ] — one addon.
      #
      # MARK is `*` for a value you chose, `-` for one you chose that happens to be
      # the ROM's own, and a space for an untouched addon. The chosen value is the
      # bright one; the alternatives stay dim, so the page reads as a list of current
      # settings and a menu of choices at the same time.
      addons_row() {
          local num="$1" mark="$2" label="$3" value="$4" choices="$5" extra="${6:-}"
          local cols lw=30 vw=10 avail color
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          [ "$lw" -le "$cols" ] || lw=$((cols - 10))
          avail=$((cols - (2 + 3 + 1 + 2 + lw + 2 + vw + 2)))
          if [ "$mark" = '*' ]; then color="$UI_GREEN"; else color="$UI_DIM"; fi
      
          if [ "$avail" -ge 10 ]; then
              printf '  %s%3d%s %s%s%s  %s%-*s%s  %s%-*s%s  %s%s%s%s\n' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$num" "$UI_OFF" "$color" "$mark" "$UI_OFF" \
                  "$UI_BOLD" "$lw" "$label" "$UI_OFF" \
                  "$color" "$vw" "$value" "$UI_OFF" \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$choices" "$extra" "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '  %s%3d%s %s%s%s  %s%s%s%s%s\n' \
              "$UI_DIM" "$num" "$UI_OFF" "$color" "$mark" "$UI_OFF" \
              "$UI_BOLD" "$label" "$UI_OFF" "$extra" ''
          printf '       %s%s%s  %s%s%s\n' "$color" "$value" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_DIM" "$choices" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      menu_addons() {
          local script rows=() row i ans id label choices default kind value saved mark
          script="$(addons_script)"
          if [ ! -f "$script" ]; then
              err "$script is missing — this checkout is incomplete."
              pause_menu
              return 0
          fi
          while :; do
              rows=()
              while IFS= read -r row; do
                  [ -n "$row" ] && rows+=("$row")
              done < <(addons_call catalog 2>/dev/null)
      
              ui_heading 'Addons'
              ui_mark note "A setting changes on the phone now; an overlay resource needs a rebuild."
              echo ""
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  IFS='|' read -r id choices default label _ kind <<<"${rows[$i]}"
                  saved="$(addons_saved "$id")"
                  value="${saved:-$default}"
                  mark=' '
                  if [ -n "$saved" ]; then
                      mark='*'
                      [ "$saved" = "$default" ] && mark='-'
                  fi
                  addons_row "$((i + 1))" "$mark" "$label" "$value" \
                      "$(printf '%s' "$choices" | tr ',' '/')" \
                      "$([ "$kind" = overlay ] && echo " ${UI_DIM}(overlay)${UI_OFF}")"
              done
              echo ""
              ui_mark note "* chosen  ${UI_DOT}  - chosen, same as the ROM  ${UI_DOT}  plain = the ROM's own value"
              ui_mark note "number = choose a value   number=value = set both   r = reset   Enter = back"
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              ans="$MENU_ANSWER"
              case "$ans" in
                  ''|0|q) return 0 ;;
                  r|R)
                      addons_call reset

- path: stuff/scripts/menu.sh
  content: |

                      info "Every addon is back to the ROM's own value."

              esac

              echo ""
              menu_read "  value (Enter keeps it)" || return 0
              value="$MENU_ANSWER"
              [ -z "$value" ] && continue
              addons_call set "$id=$value"
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Where the probes read from
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # In Termux the phone the probes want is the one the menu is running on, and the
      # reads a PC does over adb (`cmd`, `dumpsys`, /vendor) are what root unlocks
      # there. ADB on Termux has nothing to dial, so without this the answer was
      # always "no device in adb devices".
      #
      # Asked once per session and handed to every probe as DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST, so a
      # session that said yes is not asked again on each run — and one that said no is
      # not asked either.
      probe_local=""
      
      probe_source_ask() {
          [ -z "$probe_local" ] || return 0
          device_is_termux || return 0
          echo ""
          echo "  This is Termux, so the phone is this one rather than a device on a cable."
          echo "  Reading it directly needs root: the same getprop, cmd overlay, wm and"
          echo "  dumpsys reads a PC makes over adb."
          if confirm "  Read this phone as root? [Y/n] " y; then
              if device_local_begin "menu"; then
                  probe_local=1
              else
                  probe_local=0
              fi
          else
              probe_local=0
          fi
          # The menu itself never reads a phone; only the answer is passed on.
          DEVICE_LOCAL=0
          export DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST="$probe_local"
          echo ""
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Probes
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # device-probe.sh, udfps-probe.sh and device-id.sh all print a report and, with
      # --write, put the winners in config.env. That is the only difference between
      # the two answers here, so the submenu asks it instead of inventing options.
      # Ctrl-C is how the probes' device wait is left ("up to 120s; Ctrl-C stops
      # this"). A script's bash shares the foreground process group with the child it
      # is waiting on, so the interrupt reaches this menu too: without the trap the
      # whole menu died and the user lost their place. The trap lets the probe exit on
      # its own while the menu stays put; 130 is the probe's "interrupted" code, so in
      # that case there is no report to read and nothing to press a key for.
      probe_run() {
          local rc=0
          trap ':' INT
          bash "$@" || rc=$?
          trap - INT
          # Never return the probe's status: build.sh runs this with `set -e`, so a
          # 130 here would end the menu as surely as the signal did.
          if [ "$rc" -eq 130 ]; then return 0; fi
          pause_menu || true
          return 0
      }
      
      probe_menu() { # <title> <script> <note>
          local title="$1" script="$2" note="$3" dir
          while :; do
              probe_source_ask
              ui_heading "$title"
              # ui_mark wraps the note itself: a one-paragraph description on a
              # phone-width terminal used to run off the edge.
              [ -n "$note" ] && ui_mark note "$note" && echo ""
              local who='the connected phone'
              [ "$probe_local" = 1 ] && who='this phone'
              ui_item 1 "Read $who" 'report only, nothing written' 24
              ui_item 2 "Read $who" 'and write the answers to config.env' 24
              ui_item 3 'Read a firmware folder' 'an unpacked ROM instead of a running phone' 24
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 24
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) probe_run "$script" ;;
                  2) probe_run "$script" --write ;;
                  3)
                      menu_read "  folder holding the unpacked ROM" || return 0
                      dir="$MENU_ANSWER"
                      [ -n "$dir" ] || continue
                      if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
                          warn "No such folder: $dir"
                          continue
                      fi
                      if confirm "  Write what it finds to config.env? [y/N] " n; then
                          probe_run "$script" --firmware "$dir" --write
                      else
                          probe_run "$script" --firmware "$dir"
                      fi
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      menu_device() {
          probe_menu "Device" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/device-id.sh" \
              "Reads DEVICE_MANUFACTURER, DEVICE_MODEL and DEVICE_CODENAME, and the module condition."
      }
      
      menu_detect() {
          probe_menu "Auto Detect" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh" \
              "What the ROM says about the hardware: cutout path, corner radius, status bar height, refresh rates, VoLTE and 5G flags, the light sensor and the OEM switches. Anything it cannot read is reported, not guessed."
      }
      
      menu_udfps() {
          probe_menu "UDFPS" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh" \
              "The in-display fingerprint sensor's centre and radius."
      }
      
      menu_match() {
          probe_source_ask
          probe_run "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Main loop
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_main() {
          while :; do
              menu_header
              echo ""
              menu_items
              echo ""
              menu_read "  >" || { echo ""; return 0; }
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) menu_build ;;
                  2) menu_config ;;
                  3) menu_addons ;;
                  4) menu_device ;;
                  5) menu_detect ;;
                  6) menu_udfps ;;
                  7) menu_match ;;
                  8) menu_files ;;
                  9) menu_docs ;;
                  q|Q|quit|exit) return 0 ;;
                  '') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Pick a number from the list, or q to quit." ;;
              esac
              [ "$MENU_SLEEP" = "0" ] || sleep "$MENU_SLEEP"
          done
      }
      
      # Standalone: `bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh`. Sourced by build.sh, which calls
      # menu_main itself.
      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
          menu_main
      fi

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Device identity
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Turns the raw DEVICE_* values from config.env into the module id, the overlay
      # package names and the match condition. Called by build.sh right after
      # config.env is sourced, and by the standalone scripts (manifest.sh,
      # hardware-overlay.sh) so they agree with the build.
      #
      # Users only need to set DEVICE_CODENAME and DEVICE_MANUFACTURER; everything
      # else is derived. A value containing "<" is a template placeholder.
      derive_overlay_identity() {
          # Remember which identity keys were still the template before they are
          # replaced, so check/build can warn instead of silently building "generic".
          IDENTITY_PLACEHOLDER=""
          [ -n "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER:-}" ] && [[ "$DEVICE_MANUFACTURER" != *"<"* ]] || IDENTITY_PLACEHOLDER="$IDENTITY_PLACEHOLDER DEVICE_MANUFACTURER"
          [ -n "${DEVICE_MODEL:-}" ] && [[ "$DEVICE_MODEL" != *"<"* ]]            || IDENTITY_PLACEHOLDER="$IDENTITY_PLACEHOLDER DEVICE_MODEL"
          [ -n "${DEVICE_CODENAME:-}" ] && [[ "$DEVICE_CODENAME" != *"<"* ]]      || IDENTITY_PLACEHOLDER="$IDENTITY_PLACEHOLDER DEVICE_CODENAME"
      
          [ -z "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER:-}" ] || [[ "$DEVICE_MANUFACTURER" == *"<"* ]] && DEVICE_MANUFACTURER="generic"
          [ -z "${DEVICE_CODENAME:-}" ]     || [[ "$DEVICE_CODENAME" == *"<"* ]]     && DEVICE_CODENAME="generic"
      
          # Clean manufacturer for Java package names (lowercase alphanumeric only)
          SAFE_MANUFACTURER=$(printf '%s' "${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]//g')
      
          # Clean codename for package name: replace non-alphanumeric with dots
          # e.g. "Infinix-X6852" → "infinix.x6852" (dots are valid Java package separators)
          PACKAGE_SEGMENT=$(printf '%s' "${DEVICE_CODENAME}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]/./g' | sed 's/\.\.*/./g' | sed 's/^\.//;s/\.$//')

          DEFAULT_MANUFACTURER="${SAFE_MANUFACTURER:-generic}"

          [ -z "${OVERLAY_PACKAGE:-}" ]     || [[ "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE" == *"<"* ]]     && OVERLAY_PACKAGE="me.phh.treble.overlay.${SAFE_MANUFACTURER}.${PACKAGE_SEGMENT}"

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Writing config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      set_config_key() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" file="$ROOT/config.env" tmp
          [ -f "$file" ] || die "no config.env in $ROOT"
          tmp="$tmpdir/config.env"
          awk -v k="$key" -v v="$value" '
              BEGIN { done = 0 }
              {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/\r$/, "", line)
                  if (!done && line ~ "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*" k "=") {
                      match(line, /^[[:space:]]*/)
                      printf "%s%s=%s\n", substr(line, 1, RLENGTH), k, v
                      done = 1
                      next
                  }
                  print
              }
              END { if (!done) printf "%s=%s\n", k, v }
          ' "$file" >"$tmp" || return 1
          cp "$tmp" "$file"
      }
      
      write_config() {
          local i value
          for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
              [ "${f_conf[$i]}" = "low" ] && continue
              # One write per setting: the first fact is the highest-priority source.
              local key="${f_key[$i]}"
              local earlier=""
              local j
              for j in "${!f_key[@]}"; do
                  [ "$j" -lt "$i" ] && [ "${f_key[$j]}" = "$key" ] && { earlier="1"; break; }
              done
              [ -n "$earlier" ] && continue
      
              value="${f_value[$i]}"
              case "$key" in
                  # String settings keep the quotes every line of config.env uses.
                  DISPLAY_CUTOUT|LIGHT_SENSOR_TYPE) set_config_key "$key" "\"$value\"" ;;
                  *) set_config_key "$key" "$value" ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      main() {
          # Hidden helper for the tests: decide whether a tree on stdin is a device
          # profile or the AOSP placeholder, without needing adb or aapt2.
          if [ "$check_profile" -eq 1 ]; then
              local tree
              tree="$(cat)"
              if profile_looks_real "$tree"; then
                  printf 'real\n'
                  exit 0
              fi
              printf 'generic\n'
              exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$power_mode" -eq 1 ]; then
              if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then power_profile_firmware; else power_profile_device; fi
              exit 0
          fi
          if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then probe_firmware; else probe_device; fi
          if [ "$want_write" -eq 1 ]; then
              if [ "${#f_key[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  die "nothing to write — no setting was found"
              fi
              write_config
          fi
          if [ "$want_json" -eq 1 ]; then emit_json; else emit_human; fi
      }

      # cfg_set KEY VALUE -> rewrite (or add, or enable) that one line.

      cfg_set() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" file tmp line rest quoted new done=0 wrote=0
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          if [ -f "$file" ]; then
              tmp="$file.tmp.$$"
              : >"$tmp" || return 1
              while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                  local keep="${line%$'\r'}"
                  # `KEY=` or `#KEY=` (no space after the '#'), which is how this
                  # file disables one — a sentence in a comment that happens to
                  # mention the key is left alone.
                  if [ "$done" -eq 0 ] && [[ "$keep" =~ ^([[:space:]]*)#?${key}= ]]; then
                      indent="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                      rest="${keep#*=}"
                      quoted=0
                      case "$rest" in \"*) quoted=1 ;; esac

                      done=1
                      wrote=1

              done <"$file"
              if [ "$done" -eq 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$(cfg_quote "$value")" >>"$tmp"
                  wrote=1
              fi
              mv "$tmp" "$file" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }

              printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$(cfg_quote "$value")" >"$file" || return 1

          fi

      cfg_set_active() {

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Writing config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Only the four lines are touched, and a commented-out one is switched back on:
      # copying the block out of the file by hand is exactly where "UDFPS_X is set but
      # HAS_UDFPS=false" comes from.
      set_config_key() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" file="$ROOT/config.env" tmp
          [ -f "$file" ] || die "no config.env in $ROOT"
          tmp="$tmpdir/config.env"
          awk -v k="$key" -v v="$value" '
              BEGIN { done = 0 }
              {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/\r$/, "", line)
                  if (!done && line ~ "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*" k "=") {
                      match(line, /^[[:space:]]*/)
                      printf "%s%s=%s\n", substr(line, 1, RLENGTH), k, v
                      done = 1
                      next
                  }
                  print
              }
              END { if (!done) printf "%s=%s\n", k, v }
          ' "$file" >"$tmp" || return 1
          cp "$tmp" "$file"
      }
      
      write_config() {
          local idx="$1"
          set_config_key HAS_UDFPS true
          set_config_key UDFPS_X "${c_x[$idx]}"
          set_config_key UDFPS_Y "${c_y[$idx]}"
          set_config_key UDFPS_RADIUS "${c_r[$idx]}"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      main() {
          files=()
          if [ "$mode" = "firmware" ]; then probe_firmware; else probe_device; fi

- path: stuff/tests/match-prop.test.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh — which property the overlay should match on
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The failure this pins: a match property is checked by plain string equality,
      // and getting it wrong is silent — the overlay installs, `cmd overlay list`
      // shows it enabled, and nothing on screen changes. Two ways to get it wrong, and
      // both used to look like a fine answer:
      //
      //   - a property zygote cannot read (build_odm_prop, build_bootimage_prop), so
      //     the condition never holds under a GSI;
      //   - a property on /system or /product, which the GSI itself replaces, so the
      //     value changes the moment the overlay is installed onto it.
      //
      // No phone is involved: --values/--labels read saved `getprop` and `getprop -Z`
      // output, which is the same text the script parses off the wire.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/match-prop.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import { chmodSync, existsSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const script = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'match-prop.sh');
      
      function dump(pairs) {
        return Object.entries(pairs)
          .map(([k, v]) => `[${k}]: [${v}]`)
          .join('\n') + '\n';
      }
      
      // `getprop -Z` prints the same shape, with the SELinux label as the value.
      function areas(pairs) {
        return dump(
          Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(pairs).map(([k, v]) => [k, `u:object_r:${v}:s0`]))
        );
      }
      
      function dir(files) {
        const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'match-prop-'));
        for (const [name, body] of Object.entries(files)) {
          writeFileSync(join(d, name), body);
        }
        return d;
      }

On a device with a notch, curved\ncorners or an under-display fingerprint sensor, that means the wrong cutout, the\nwrong status bar height, no working UDFPS, and — often — no VoLTE or 5G, because\nthe vendor config never reaches the GSI's `framework-res`.\n\nThis tool reads the answers off the phone and emits a **RRO overlay** that puts\nthem back: `dimen/quick_qs_offset_height`, `string/config_mainBuiltInDisplayCutout`,\n`integer/config_screenBrightnessSettingMaximumForUdfps`, `bool/config_hardwareUnavailableEs2…`\n— around 90 resources, split into a framework APK and a SystemUI APK, packed into\none Magisk / KernelSU / APatch module.\n\n| You get | Path |\n|---|---|\n| Flashable module (ksu, `fod/`, `service.sh`) | `out/treble-overlay-<mfr>-<codename>.zip` |\n| Framework RRO | `out/apks/treble-overlay-<mfr>-<codename>.apk` |\n| SystemUI RRO | `out/apks/…-systemui.apk` |\n| The module, unpacked | `out/module/` |\n| WebUI (on-device page) | `src/webui/`, installed as `/data/adb/modules/<id>/webroot/` |\n\nNothing is uploaded anywhere. The overlay is built on your machine, for your\nphone.\n\n---\n\n## Quick start\n\n<table>\n<tr><th width=\"33%\">Linux / macOS</th><th width=\"33%\">Termux (on the phone)</th><th>Windows</th></tr>\n<tr><td>\n\n```bash\ngit clone --depth 1 \\\n  https://github.com/<owner>/treble-rro-creator\ncd treble-rro-creator\n./build.sh\n```\n\n</td><td>\n\n```bash\npkg install git\ngit clone --depth 1 \\\n  https://github.com/<owner>/treble-rro-creator\ncd treble-rro-creator\n./build.sh\n```\n\n</td><td>\n\n```bat\ngit clone --depth 1 ^\n  https://github.com/<owner>/treble-rro-creator\ncd treble-rro-creator\nbuild.cmd\n```\n\n</td></tr>\n<tr><td colspan=\"3\">\n\n`./build.sh` with no arguments opens the menu on a terminal; give it a verb\n(`./build.sh build`) for scripts and CI. On Windows everything goes through\n`build.cmd`, which finds Git Bash for you — never WSL.\n\n</td></tr>\n</table>\n\nThe menu is the same nine tools everywhere:\n\n```\n  1  Build           dry run, build, check, doctor, clean\n  2  config.env      browse and edit one key at a time\n  3  Addons          module tweaks: settings and overlay resources\n  4  Device          read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone\n  5  Auto Detect     ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G\n  6  UDFPS           in-display fingerprint geometry\n  7  Match property  which property the submission should match on\n  8  Files           what was built, and where it is\n  9  Docs            the guides in docs/\n```\n\n**A first build, in four steps:**\n\n1. **4 · Device** → *Read the phone and write the answers* sets the manufacturer,\n   model and codename. Nothing builds without a real codename.\n2. **5 · Auto Detect** → *write* fills in cutout, corners, status bar height,\n   refresh rates, VoLTE/5G and the light sensor.\n3. **6 · UDFPS** only if the phone has an under-display sensor. Skip it otherwise.\n4. **1 · Build** → *Build*. It installs the toolchain first (aapt2, apksigner,\n   `framework-res.apk`), then writes `out/*.zip`.\n\nThere is a desktop app too (`./gui/build.sh`, or `treble-rro-creator.cmd` on\nWindows). It drives the same scripts, so nothing is available in one and missing\nin the other — see [docs/gui.md](docs/gui.md).\n\n---\n\n## What it needs\n\n| | Linux | Termux | Windows |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Java 17+ | `openjdk-17-jdk` | `openjdk-17` | JDK 17 on `PATH` |\n| Build tools | `aapt2`, `zipalign`, `apksigner` | same, from `pkg` | bundled in `stuff/tools/` |\n| `framework-res.apk` | downloaded (Android 13 resources) | downloaded | downloaded |\n| Unpacking a firmware zip | `unzip` | `unzip` | PowerShell, built in |\n| Optional | `adb` for a cabled phone | root (`tsu`) to read itself | `adb` |\n\n`./build.sh doctor` prints exactly what is missing and nothing else; `./build.sh\nsetup` installs or repairs it. On Termux, `pkg install -y aapt2 apksigner\nandroid-tools openjdk-17 unzip zip curl` is enough.\n\n---\n\n## The two front ends, and the one engine\n\n```\nbuild.sh ──┬── stuff/scripts/menu.sh ──┐\n           ├── build verbs ────────────┼── stuff/scripts/{build,device-probe,\n           └── gui/ (Go + WebView) ────┘   udfps-probe,match-prop,addons}.sh\n```\n\nEverything that reads a phone, writes `config.env`, or builds an APK lives in\n`stuff/scripts/`. The menu and the app only choose *which* script to run, with\nthe arguments a user would type — so `2 · Build` and `./build.sh build` cannot\ndrift apart.\n\n---\n\n## Jobs, and the file that does it\n\n| I want to… | CLI | File |\n|---|---|---|\n| Build the module | `./build.sh build` | `stuff/scripts/build.sh` |\n| See the plan without building | `./build.sh --dry-run` | same |\n| Check `config.env` | `./build.sh check` | `stuff/scripts/validate.sh` |\n| Read the phone | `bash stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh --write` | `stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh` |\n| Read the fingerprint sensor | `bash stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh --write` | `stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh` |\n| Read manufacturer/model/codename | `bash stuff/scripts/device-id.sh --write` | `stuff/scripts/device-id.sh` |\n| Pick the match property | `bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh` | `stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh` |\n| Toggle a module addon | `sh src/webui/addons.sh set <id>=<value>` | `src/webui/addons.sh` |\n| Build the overlay repo tree | `bash stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh` | `stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh` |\n| Write the submission manifest | `bash stuff/scripts/manifest.sh` | `stuff/scripts/manifest.sh` |\n| Start over | `./build.sh clean --all` | `stuff/scripts/clean.sh` |\n\n---\n\n## `config.env` is the input\n\nOne file, one line per setting, hand-editable, commented in place. The app and\nthe menu rewrite one line and leave the rest of the file — comments, sections,\nquoting — alone.\n\n```bash\nDEVICE_MANUFACTURER=Xiaomi      # drives the package name\nDEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr          # drives the module id and the match value\nDEVICE_MODEL=\"Redmi Note 17\"\nDISPLAY_CUTOUT_PATH=\"\"          # \"\" = no cutout path\nDISPLAY_ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS=48\nSTATUS_BAR_HEIGHT=28\nHAS_UDFPS=true\nUDFPS_X=540\nUDFPS_Y=2224\n```\n\n* Only `DEVICE_CODENAME` and `DEVICE_MANUFACTURER` are required. Everything else\n  derives from them (`treble-overlay-xiaomi-zephyr`,\n  `me.phh.treble.overlay.xiaomi.zephyr`, the match condition).\n* A key that starts with `#` is off but stays listed, so it can be switched on\n  by name instead of by hunting for the `#`.\n* A value containing `<` is a template placeholder. `./build.sh check` names\n  them; a build with a placeholder codename produces `…-generic`.\n* Every key and its default: [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md).\n\n---\n\n## Common problems, straight answers\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Module installs, nothing changes | `config.env` still has the sample codename, or the overlay does not match this ROM | `./build.sh check`; then **7 · Match property** |\n| `aapt2: resource not found` | `framework-res.apk` is the wrong Android version | `./build.sh setup --force`, pick the right one |\n| Cutout is off-centre | `DISPLAY_CUTOUT_PATH` came from another device | **5 · Auto Detect** → *write* |\n| UDFPS does nothing | geometry right, touch panel never armed | Xiaomi only: `--xiaomi-fod` |\n| `adb: no devices` | cable, authorisation, or a stale server | `adb kill-server && adb devices` |\n| Termux: everything says \"no device\" | it is reading *this* phone, which needs root | `tsu`, or answer yes to the root prompt |\n| Windows: `bash` not found | WSL, or Git Bash missing | install Git for Windows, run `build.cmd` |\n\n---\n\n## Docs\n\nStart at [docs/index.md](docs/index.md). The three that answer most questions:\n\n| Guide | Answers |\n|---|---|\n| [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) | every key in `config.env`, and what it changes |\n| [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md) | overlay installed but not applying; the exact commands |\n| [docs/submission.md](docs/submission.md) | how to submit the overlay upstream |\n\n<details>\n<summary>All guides</summary>\n\n| File | What is in it |\n|---|---|\n| [configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) | `config.env`, key by key |\n| [termux.md](docs/termux.md) | building on the phone, root, storage |\n| [windows.md](docs/windows.md) | Git Bash, Git for Windows, no WSL |\n| [gui.md](docs/gui.md) | the desktop app, tab by tab |\n| [resources.md](docs/resources.md) | the ~90 resources, and what each does |\n| [udfps.md](docs/udfps.md) | in-display fingerprint: geometry, the Xiaomi helper |\n| [addons.md](docs/addons.md) | module addons and the on-device page |\n| [submission.md](docs/submission.md) | the upstream overlay repo |\n| [troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md) | symptom → cause → command |\n\n</details>\n\n---\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\nbash stuff/tests/run.sh\n```\n\nShell syntax for every shipped script, the resource-table writer against real\nAPKs, the manifest and submission tree, the WebUI helpers, the docs links, and\nthe desktop app's Go tests. No Android SDK, no phone, no network.\n\n---\n\n## Licence\n\nApache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).' > /tmp/readme_check.txt; wc -l /tmp/readme_check.txt",
  "process_type": "SYNC",
  "timeout_seconds": 30
}

corners or an under-display fingerprint sensor, that means the wrong cutout, the
wrong status bar height, no working UDFPS, and — often — no VoLTE or 5G, because

- path: stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh
  content: |
          local file
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          awk '
              /^#[[:space:]]*─/ {
                  sec = $0
                  sub(/^#[[:space:]]*/, "", sec)
                  gsub(/─/, "", sec)
                  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", sec)
                  next
              }
              /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ || /^#[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/\r$/, "", line)
                  key = line
                  sub(/=.*/, "", key)
                  active = 1
                  if (key ~ /^#/) { active = 0; sub(/^#/, "", key) }
                  value = substr(line, index(line, "=") + 1)
                  printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\n", key, active, NR, sec, value
              }
          ' "$file"
      }
      
      # cfg_sections -> the section titles in file order, one per line.
      cfg_sections() {
          cfg_rows | awk -F'\t' '!seen[$4]++ && $4 != "" { print $4 }'
      }
      
      # cfg_set KEY VALUE -> rewrite (or add, or enable) that one line.
      # Returns 0 when the file was written — also when the value was already right,
      # because the caller only cares that the key now holds it.
      cfg_set() {
          local key="$1" value file tmp line rest quoted new done=0 wrote=0
          # A pasted value can carry a newline; it would end the line early and turn
          # the rest of it into a key of its own.
          value="$(cfg_safe_value "$2")"
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          if [ -f "$file" ]; then
              tmp="$file.tmp.$$"
              : >"$tmp" || return 1
              while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                  local keep="${line%$'\r'}"
                  # `KEY=` or `#KEY=` (no space after the '#'), which is how this
                  # file disables one — a sentence in a comment that happens to
                  # mention the key is left alone.
                  if [ "$done" -eq 0 ] && [[ "$keep" =~ ^([[:space:]]*)#?${key}= ]]; then
                      indent="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                      rest="${keep#*=}"
                      quoted=0
                      case "$rest" in \"*) quoted=1 ;; esac
                      new="${indent}${key}=$(cfg_quote "$value" "$quoted")"
                      printf '%s\n' "$new" >>"$tmp"
                      done=1
                      wrote=1
                      continue
                  fi
                  printf '%s\n' "$keep" >>"$tmp"
              done <"$file"
              if [ "$done" -eq 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$(cfg_quote "$value")" >>"$tmp"
                  wrote=1
              fi
              mv "$tmp" "$file" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
          else
              printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$(cfg_quote "$value")" >"$file" || return 1
              wrote=1
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # cfg_set_active KEY 0|1 -> comment out, or bring back, that one line.
      # '#' with nothing after it is the file's own way of switching a key off, and
      # cfg_rows reads it back the same way, so an inactive key stays listed.
      cfg_set_active() {
          local key="$1" want="$2" file tmp keep done=0 indent rest
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          tmp="$file.tmp.$$"
          : >"$tmp" || return 1
          while IFS= read -r keep || [ -n "$keep" ]; do
              keep="${keep%$'\r'}"
              if [ "$done" -eq 0 ] && [[ "$keep" =~ ^([[:space:]]*)#?${key}= ]]; then
                  indent="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                  rest="${keep#*=}"
                  if [ "$want" = "1" ]; then
                      printf '%s%s=%s\n' "$indent" "$key" "$rest" >>"$tmp"
                  else
                      printf '#%s%s=%s\n' "$indent" "$key" "$rest" >>"$tmp"
                  fi
                  done=1
                  continue
              fi
              printf '%s\n' "$keep" >>"$tmp"
          done <"$file"
          mv "$tmp" "$file" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
          return 0
      }
      
      # cfg_summary -> the four lines the menu header shows, from the live file.
      cfg_identity() {
          local manuf model code
          manuf="$(cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)"
          model="$(cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)"
          code="$(cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)"
          if [ -z "$manuf" ] && [ -z "$model" ] && [ -z "$code" ]; then
              printf 'no device set'
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s %s (%s)' "$manuf" "$model" "$code" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'

- path: stuff/tests/config-edit.test.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh — writing config.env
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The failure this pins: config.env is *sourced* by the build (build.sh, and
      // every standalone script via common.sh), so a saved value is shell code. A
      // model name reading `$(reboot)` used to be written into the file unchanged and
      // run on the next build; a value with a newline in it ended the line early and
      // the rest of it became a key of its own.
      //
      // No phone and no build involved: these are the functions the menu, the app and
      // match-prop.sh all write through.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/config-edit.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import { existsSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const script = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts', 'config-edit.sh');
      
      // A throwaway ROOT holding one config.env, in the shape the real file uses:
      // section headers, bare words, and two keys that are quoted.
      function workspace(body) {
        const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'config-edit-'));
        writeFileSync(
          join(d, 'config.env'),
          body ??
            [
              '# ─── Device ─────────────────────────────────────────────',
              'DEVICE_MANUFACTURER=Xiaomi',
              'DEVICE_MODEL="Redmi Note 17"',
              '#DEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr',
              'HAS_UDFPS=false',
              '',
            ].join('\n')
        );
        return d;
      }
      
      // Run a bash snippet with the helpers sourced and ROOT pointed at the fixture.
      function run(d, snippet) {
        const file = join(d, 'run.sh');
        writeFileSync(file, `. "${script}"\n${snippet}\n`);
        const out = spawnSync('bash', [file], {
          encoding: 'utf8',
          env: { ...process.env, ROOT: d, TERM: 'dumb' },
        });
        return { out, code: out.status };
      }
      
      const cfg = (d) => readFileSync(join(d, 'config.env'), 'utf8');
      
      // A JS string as a single shell word, for embedding fixtures in a snippet.
      const shq = (s) => `'${String(s).replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
      
      test('a value with $, a backtick, a quote and a backslash round-trips', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const value = 'a$(reboot)b`id`c\\ d"e';
        const r = run(
          d,
          [
            `value=${shq(value)}`,
            'v="$(cfg_quote "$value")"',
            'eval "got=$v"',
            '[ "$got" = "$value" ] || { printf "got=%s\\n" "$got" >&2; exit 1; }',
          ].join('\n')
        );
        assert.equal(r.code, 0, r.out.stderr);
      });
      
      test('cfg_quote escapes everything the shell expands inside double quotes', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(d, `cfg_quote 'x$(touch PWNED)y\`id\`z$HOME'`);
        assert.equal(r.code, 0, r.out.stderr);
        assert.equal(r.out.stdout, '"x\\$(touch PWNED)y\\`id\\`z\\$HOME"');
      });
      
      test('a written value cannot run when the file is sourced', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const marker = join(d, 'PWNED');
        const r = run(d, `cfg_set DEVICE_MODEL '$(touch ${marker})'\ncfg_set DEVICE_MANUFACTURER "\`touch ${marker}.tick\`"`);
        assert.equal(r.code, 0, r.out.stderr);
      
        // build.sh and common.sh both do exactly this.
        const source = spawnSync('bash', ['-c', `. "${join(d, 'config.env')}"`], {
          encoding: 'utf8',
          env: { ...process.env, TERM: 'dumb' },
        });
        assert.equal(source.status, 0, source.stderr);
        assert.equal(existsSync(marker), false, 'value ran as a command');
        assert.equal(existsSync(`${marker}.tick`), false, 'value ran as a command');
      
        // …and it still reads back as what the user typed.
        const back = run(d, 'cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL');
        assert.equal(back.out.stdout, `$(touch ${marker})`);
      });
      
      test('a newline in a value stays on one line', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const before = cfg(d).split('\n').length;
        const r = run(d, `cfg_set DEVICE_MODEL "$(printf 'Redmi\\nNote')"`);
        assert.equal(r.code, 0, r.out.stderr);
      
        const text = cfg(d);
        assert.equal(text.split('\n').length, before, 'the file gained a line');
        assert.match(text, /^DEVICE_MODEL="Redmi Note"$/m);
        // Nothing that looks like a key was created out of the second half.
        const keys = text.split('\n').filter((l) => /^[A-Z_]+=/i.test(l)).map((l) => l.split('=')[0]);
        assert.deepEqual(keys, ['DEVICE_MANUFACTURER', 'DEVICE_MODEL', 'HAS_UDFPS']);
      });
      
      test('control characters are stripped, not written', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(d, `cfg_set DEVICE_MODEL "$(printf 'a\\033[31mb')"`);
        assert.equal(r.code, 0, r.out.stderr);
        assert.match(cfg(d), /^DEVICE_MODEL=ab$/m);
      });
      
      test('a plain word stays bare, so the file keeps its style', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(d, 'cfg_set DEVICE_MANUFACTURER Samsung');
        assert.equal(r.code, 0, r.out.stderr);
        assert.match(cfg(d), /^DEVICE_MANUFACTURER=Samsung$/m);
      });
      
      test('a quoted line stays quoted, and a commented key is switched on', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(d, "cfg_set DEVICE_MODEL 'Redmi Note 17 Pro'\ncfg_set DEVICE_CODENAME zephyr");
        assert.equal(r.code, 0, r.out.stderr);
        const text = cfg(d);
        assert.match(text, /^DEVICE_MODEL="Redmi Note 17 Pro"$/m);

      # =============================================================================
      # config-edit.sh — read and write one key of config.env
      # =============================================================================

      #

      # one line, keep the indentation, keep the quoting the line already used, and
      # turn a commented-out KEY= line into a live one (that is what "enable it"
      # means). Nothing here validates values — `./build.sh check` does that.
      # =============================================================================
      
      : "${ROOT:?stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh must be sourced with ROOT set}"

      cfg_file() {

      }

      cfg_unquote() {

              \'*\') v="${v#\'}"; v="${v%\'}" ;;
          esac
          printf '%s' "$v"

      # file's one-key-per-line shape removed. A probe writes what the phone said, and
      # a model name with a newline in it used to split the line in two.

              value="$(printf '%s' "$value" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '[:cntrl:]')"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$value"
      }

      # Plain words stay bare, as they are in the file today; anything a shell would

      # `$(reboot)` would otherwise run as a command on the next build.

          local value="$1" force="${2:-0}"

- path: gui/configfile.go
  content: |
      package main
      
      import (
        "fmt"
        "regexp"
        "strings"
      )
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // config.env as a form
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // config.env is sourced by bash, so it has to stay a text file: comments are
      // documentation, `#` in front of a key is how a feature is switched off, and
      // the order of the lines is the order of the sections people read. The app used
      // to show it in a textarea, which is honest but means the user has to know bash
      // quoting rules to change a number.
      //
      // So the file is parsed here and edited line-wise: the form knows the key, the
      // value and whether the line is commented out, and a save rewrites only the
      // lines that changed. Everything else in the file — headings, prose, blank
      // lines, the `#` on features that are off — is preserved byte for byte. That is
      // also why the raw view is still there: if parsing ever gets something wrong,
      // the user can see what the file actually says.
      type ConfigEntry struct {
        Line    int      `json:"line"`
        Key     string   `json:"key"`
        Value   string   `json:"value"`
        Enabled bool     `json:"enabled"`
        Comment []string `json:"comment"`
      }
      
      type ConfigSection struct {
        Title   string        `json:"title"`
        Note    []string      `json:"note"`
        Entries []ConfigEntry `json:"entries"`
      }
      
      type ConfigDoc struct {
        Sections []ConfigSection `json:"sections"`
        Total    int             `json:"total"`
        Enabled  int             `json:"enabled"`
      }
      
      // Lookup returns an enabled value, treating a leftover template placeholder
      // ("<device_codename>") as "not set" — it is not a name, and the adb presets
      // would otherwise happily grep the device for the literal angle brackets.
      func (d ConfigDoc) Lookup(key string) string {
        for _, s := range d.Sections {
          for _, e := range s.Entries {
            if e.Key != key || !e.Enabled {
              continue
            }
            v := strings.TrimSpace(e.Value)
            if v == "" || strings.HasPrefix(v, "<") {
              return ""
            }
            return v
          }
        }
        return ""
      }
      
      func (d ConfigDoc) LookupAll(key string) []string {
        var out []string
        for _, s := range d.Sections {
          for _, e := range s.Entries {
            if e.Key == key && e.Enabled {
              v := strings.TrimSpace(e.Value)
              if v != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(v, "<") {
                out = append(out, v)
              }
            }
          }
        }
        return out
      }
      
      var (
        // "# ── Device identity ─────────────" — a section heading.
        configHeading = regexp.MustCompile(`^\s*#\s*─+\s*(.*?)\s*─*\s*$`)
        // KEY=value, optionally commented out. Keys in this file are upper case;
        // requiring that keeps prose lines ("# More: docs/…=…") out of the form.
        configKey = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\s*)(#\s*)?([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\s*=(.*)$`)
        // A value that bash will read back unchanged without quotes.
        plainValue = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9_.,:/+@%=-]*$`)
      )
      
      // parseConfig turns the file into sections and entries. It never fails on
      // content: an unparsable line is simply not shown in the form and is left
      // untouched on save.
      func parseConfig(text string) (ConfigDoc, error) {
        // Non-nil slices so the JSON the page receives is always [] and never null:
        // a section that is only a heading would otherwise break the renderer.
        doc := ConfigDoc{Sections: []ConfigSection{}}
        lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
        var cur *ConfigSection
        var pending []string // the comment run directly above the next key
      
        newSection := func() *ConfigSection {
          doc.Sections = append(doc.Sections, ConfigSection{Entries: []ConfigEntry{}, Note: []string{}})
          return &doc.Sections[len(doc.Sections)-1]
        }
      
        for i, raw := range lines {
          line := strings.TrimRight(raw, "\r")
      
          if m := configHeading.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
            s := newSection()
            s.Title = strings.TrimSpace(m[1])
            cur = s
            pending = nil
            continue
          }
          if cur == nil {
            cur = newSection()
          }
      
          if m := configKey.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
            value, _ := splitValue(m[4])
            entry := ConfigEntry{
              Line:    i,
              Key:     m[3],
              Value:   value,
              Enabled: m[2] == "",
              Comment: pending,
            }
            cur.Entries = append(cur.Entries, entry)
            doc.Total++
            if entry.Enabled {
              doc.Enabled++
            }
            pending = nil
            continue
          }
      
          if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
            // A blank line ends a comment block: a key is described by the text
            // right above it, not by every paragraph since the last key.
            pending = nil
            continue
          }
      
          if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "#") {
            text := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "#"))
            pending = append(pending, text)
            if len(cur.Entries) == 0 {
              cur.Note = append(cur.Note, text)
            }
            continue
          }
      
          // Anything else (a stray command, an array) stays in the file and out
          // of the form.
          pending = nil
        }
      
        // A section's blurb is stored twice on purpose: once as the section's
        // introduction (always visible) and once as the first key's comment, so
        // clicking ⓘ on that row answers the question where the user asked it.
        //
        // A key with no note of its own inherits the section's, so ⓘ is never a
        // dead button: in this file the explanation for a group of lines is
        // written once, above the first of them.
        for si := range doc.Sections {
          s := &doc.Sections[si]
          if len(s.Note) == 0 {
            continue
          }
          for ei := range s.Entries {
            if len(s.Entries[ei].Comment) == 0 {
              s.Entries[ei].Comment = s.Note
            }
          }
        }
        return doc, nil
      }
      
      // splitValue mirrors the two ways this file writes a value: bare, or inside
      // quotes. The quote character is remembered so a save writes the same style.
      func splitValue(raw string) (string, byte) {
        s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
        if len(s) >= 2 {
          if q := s[0]; q == '"' || q == '\'' {
            if s[len(s)-1] == q && !escapedAt(s, len(s)-1) {
              return unescape(s[1:len(s)-1], q), q
            }
          }
        }
        return s, 0
      }
      
      func escapedAt(s string, i int) bool {
        n := 0
        for j := i - 1; j >= 0 && s[j] == '\\'; j-- {
          n++
        }
        return n%2 == 1
      }
      
      // unescape only undoes what formatValue adds. A lone backslash (\d) is text,
      // exactly as bash reads it inside double quotes.
      func unescape(s string, quote byte) string {
        if quote != '"' {
          return s
        }
        var b strings.Builder
        for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
          if s[i] == '\\' && i+1 < len(s) && (s[i+1] == '\\' || s[i+1] == '"') {
            b.WriteByte(s[i+1])
            i++
            continue
          }
          b.WriteByte(s[i])
        }
        return b.String()
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Saving
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // ConfigEdit is one row the user changed. Key is sent back so a save cannot
      // land on a different line than the one the form was showing: if the file was
      // edited outside the app in the meantime, the key no longer matches and the
      // save is refused instead of quietly rewriting the wrong setting.
      type ConfigEdit struct {
        Line    int    `json:"line"`
        Key     string `json:"key"`
        Value   string `json:"value"`
        Enabled bool   `json:"enabled"`
      }
      
      func applyConfigEdits(text string, edits []ConfigEdit) (string, error) {
        if len(edits) == 0 {
          return text, nil
        }
        if len(edits) > 512 {
          return "", fmt.Errorf("too many changes in one save")
        }
      
        lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
        seen := make(map[int]struct{}, len(edits))
      
        for _, e := range edits {
          if e.Line < 0 || e.Line >= len(lines) {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: line %d is not in the file any more — reload", e.Key, e.Line+1)
          }
          if _, dup := seen[e.Line]; dup {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: two changes for line %d", e.Key, e.Line+1)
          }
          seen[e.Line] = struct{}{}
      
          if strings.ContainsAny(e.Value, "\r\n\x00") {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: a value cannot contain a line break", e.Key)
          }
      
          cr := ""
          line := lines[e.Line]
          if strings.HasSuffix(line, "\r") {
            cr = "\r"
            line = strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\r")
          }
      
          m := configKey.FindStringSubmatch(line)
          if m == nil {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: line %d is no longer a setting — reload", e.Key, e.Line+1)
          }
          if m[3] != e.Key {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("the file changed on disk: line %d is %s now — reload", e.Line+1, m[3])
          }
      
          current, quote := splitValue(m[4])
          if current == e.Value && (m[2] == "") == e.Enabled {
            // Nothing actually changed. Not rewriting the line is what makes a
            // no-op save byte-for-byte: the file has lines whose quoting is
            // already odd (#HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY=<number>), and a form save must
            // not restyle a row the user did not touch.
            continue
          }
      
          // Keep the marker the file used if the row is unchanged, drop it when
          // the switch went on, and add a plain '#' when it went off.
          hash := m[2]
          switch {
          case e.Enabled:
            hash = ""
          case hash == "":
            hash = "#"
          }
          lines[e.Line] = m[1] + hash + e.Key + "=" + formatValue(e.Value, quote, m[4]) + cr
        }
      
        return strings.Join(lines, "\n"), nil
      }
      
      // formatValue keeps the file's own style: a value that was quoted stays
      // quoted, a bare number stays bare, and a value that bash would re-split (a
      // path with spaces, a cutout path) gets the quotes it needs.
      func formatValue(value string, quote byte, original string) string {
        if quote != '"' && quote != '\'' && plainValue.MatchString(value) {
          return value
        }
        if quote == '\'' && !strings.ContainsRune(value, '\'') {
          return "'" + value + "'"
        }
        return `"` + escapeDouble(value) + `"`
      }
      
      func escapeDouble(s string) string {
        var b strings.Builder
        for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
          switch s[i] {
          case '\\', '"':
            b.WriteByte('\\')
          }
          b.WriteByte(s[i])
        }
        return b.String()
      }

=== addons.sh 1-130 ===
#!/system/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay — module addons
# =============================================================================
# An addon is a tweak the *module* makes on the phone. It is not a config.env
# key, and it is chosen in the app's Addons tab (or the page's Addons card),
# not in the overlay resource files.
#
# There are two kinds, and the catalog says which is which:
#
#   setting  a Settings value the module writes. One `settings put` changes it
#            on a running phone — no APK, no reboot — and service.sh re-applies
#            it at every boot. The overlay APK alone cannot do one.
#   overlay  a resource the build bakes into an overlay APK — framework (the
#            navigation bar height, the 180° rotation flag) or SystemUI (the
#            status bar background). It only changes after a rebuild and a
#            flash, because a resource is read when its process starts.
#
# The live addons survive an overlay rebuild; the overlay ones *are* the rebuild.
#
# One catalog lives in this file and every front-end reads it:
#
#   the desktop app   runs this script in the clone (Addons tab)
#   the module page   runs it in webroot/ on the phone (Addons card)
#   service.sh        runs it at every boot so saved choices stick
#
#   sh addons.sh list                 catalog + saved + live values, as JSON
#   sh addons.sh set ID=VALUE ...     save choices; apply the live ones now
#   sh addons.sh apply [ID ...]       apply what is saved (all ids, or those)
#   sh addons.sh reset                back to the defaults, forget the choices
#   sh addons.sh status               what the device resolves now, as key=value
#   sh addons.sh restore-conf         customize.sh: bring the saved file back
#
# The saved file is addons.conf at the module root (src/module/addons.conf in
# the clone). Only the addons that differ from the default are written into it:
# a value nobody changed is not enforced on every boot, so an untouched phone
# keeps behaving like the ROM shipped it.
#
# ADDONS_CONF, ADDONS_DIR and ADDONS_SETTINGS exist so this can be exercised
# off-device (stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js) and by the desktop app, which has
# no installed module but does have the clone.
# =============================================================================

# The module directory is one level above this script (webroot/), except when
# the script is run by its bare name from the module root ('sh addons.sh'), in
# which case '..' would be the folder above the module.
SELF="$0"
case "$SELF" in
    */*) SELF_DIR=${SELF%/*}
         MODDIR=$(cd "$SELF_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd) ;;
    *)   SELF_DIR=.
         MODDIR=$(pwd) ;;
esac
MODDIR=${ADDONS_DIR:-$MODDIR}
[ -n "$MODDIR" ] || MODDIR=$SELF_DIR
# In the clone the module files are kept in src/module/, so the script in
# src/webui/ has one directory in between; an installed module keeps the same
# files at its root.
[ -d "$MODDIR/module" ] && MODDIR="$MODDIR/module"

CONF=${ADDONS_CONF:-$MODDIR/addons.conf}
# Outside the module directory on purpose: an update replaces that directory.
# It is the same folder apply.sh mirrors webui.conf into.
STATE_DIR=${ADDONS_STATE_DIR:-/data/adb/treble-webui/${MODDIR##*/}}
SETTINGS=${ADDONS_SETTINGS:-settings}

say() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Catalog
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# id|choices|default|label|summary|kind
#
# The value names are what the page and the app show, so they are plain words:
# "left"/"right", not "0"/"1". The mapping to the Settings value is in
# apply_one() below, and live_value() maps it back. Keep the summaries free of
# '|' and keep them one sentence: they are rendered as-is.
#
# kind is "setting" or "overlay" (see the top of this file). Only "setting" ids
# reach apply_one()/live_value(); the build reads the overlay ids out of the
# saved file and emits them as overlay resources (see resources.sh).
#
# A two-choice addon whose choices are exactly on,off is drawn as a switch;
# anything else is a picker.
catalog() {
    cat << 'CATALOG_EOF'
volume_panel|right,left|right|Volume panel side|The volume slider slides in from this edge instead of the other one.|setting
captive_portal|on,off|on|Captive portal check|Android's "sign in to this network" probe. Off stops the false no-internet warnings a GSI shows on some networks.|setting
stay_awake|on,off|off|Screen never sleeps|Leave the display on indefinitely, on battery too. Only the power button turns it off again.|setting
status_clock|on,off|on|Status bar clock|Hide the time in the status bar so the notification icons get its room. The lock-screen clock is left alone.|setting
any_rotation|on,off|off|Upside-down rotation|Allow the 180° rotation Android normally refuses, in every app and launcher that can turn.|overlay
nav_bar_padding|on,off|on|Navigation bar padding|Reserve no space for the gesture bar: content reaches the bottom edge while the pill stays visible and swipeable.|overlay
status_bar_background|on,off|on|Status bar background|Remove the shade behind the status bar, so the bar sits directly on the wallpaper or the app.|overlay
hide_notch|on,off|off|Hide the notch|Black out the strip the notch sits in and keep every app below it, so nothing can draw under the camera.|overlay
CATALOG_EOF
}

# Every id, one per line.
ids() {
    catalog | while IFS='|' read -r id choices def label summary kind; do
        case "$id" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
        printf '%s\n' "$id"
    done
}

catalog_field() { # <id> <field number> -> that field, empty when unknown
    catalog | awk -F'|' -v id="$1" -v f="$2" '$1 == id { print $f; exit }'
}

choices_of() { catalog_field "$1" 2; }
default_of() { catalog_field "$1" 3; }
label_of()   { catalog_field "$1" 4; }
summary_of() { catalog_field "$1" 5; }
kind_of()    { catalog_field "$1" 6; }

valid_value() { # <id> <value>
    case " $(choices_of "$1" | tr ',' ' ') " in
        *" $2 "*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

bad_value() { say "x $1: '$2' is not one of: $(choices_of "$1" | tr ',' '/')"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The saved file
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Same shape as config.env — ID=VALUE lines, '#' comments — so it can be read
# and edited by hand. apply.sh keeps webui.conf in the module the same way.

del_conf() { # <key>
    [ -f "$CONF" ] || return 0
    tmp="$CONF.tmp"
    awk -v k="$1" 'index($0, k "=") != 1' "$CONF" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null \
        && mv "$tmp" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null
    chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# The saved file lives in two places: the module (what this script reads) and
# $STATE_DIR (what survives an update, because the update replaces the module).
mirror_conf() {
    mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    if [ -f "$CONF" ]; then
        cp "$CONF" "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
        rm -f "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    chmod 600 "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# customize.sh calls this after the new zip is unpacked. The packaged file is
# the app's latest word, so its choices win: restoring the old file over it made
# a freshly built "hide the notch" come up unset, because the phone still had
# the previous install's copy. Only the addons the new file does not name are
# carried over - those are the ones chosen on the phone, which the app never
# saw. A build that names nothing at all is a plain rebuild, so the saved file
# is restored whole, the way it always was.
restore_conf() {
    [ -f "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" ] || return 0
    if ! has_saved; then
        if cp "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null; then
            chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
            say "+ saved addons restored"
        fi
        return 0
    fi

    restored=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        key=${line%%=*}
        [ -n "$key" ] || continue
        # A line from an older catalog is not brought back (reset prunes it).
        [ -n "$(default_of "$key")" ] || continue
        [ -z "$(conf_value "$key")" ] || continue
        put_conf "$key" "${line#*=}" || return 1
        restored=$((restored + 1))
    done <<EOF
$(grep '^[A-Za-z]' "$STATE_DIR/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
    [ "$restored" -gt 0 ] && say "+ $restored saved addon(s) restored"
    return 0
}

//go:build android || linux

// Command xiaomi-fod switches a Xiaomi touch panel into fingerprint-on-display
// mode, which is the one thing a GSI cannot do for the vendor fingerprint HAL.
//
// The stock flow is:
//
//  MIUI FingerprintService
//    -> vendor.xiaomi.hardware.fingerprintextension.extCmd(4, 3)
//    -> vendor.xiaomi.hardware.touchfeature.setModeValue(10, 3)
//    -> /dev/xiaomi-touch ioctl(0x5400, {10, 3})
//
// A GSI has no MIUI fingerprint client, so the last call never happens. The
// vendor Goodix HAL then never sees fod_press_status change, never reports a
// finger, and the sensor appears dead even though the geometry is right.
//
// This helper issues the same ioctl directly. The daemon follows the state
// machine MIUI uses, as seen in the touch driver's dmesg: the panel is armed
// with value 3 (FOD plus the AOD wake bit) when the screen turns off, stays
// armed while the keyguard is up or a fingerprint client is running (settings
// enrollment, in-app prompts), and is released otherwise. The vendor HAL's own
// FOD engine will not light the panel on a GSI (it waits for a MIUI client that
// never runs), so the daemon also drives local HBM: on while a finger is on the
// sensor. A press that arrives with the display asleep also wakes the screen,
// because the HAL aborts the auth with ui-ready timeout when no fingerprint UI
// is up to answer it. The hbm command exposes the same
// ioctl for diagnostics.
//
// The other half of the vendor FOD stack is the display node the HAL opens;
// the module's post-fs-data.sh re-creates it. See docs/udfps.md.
//
// Build for a device (no CGO, static):
//
//  GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=off \
//      go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o xiaomi-fod main.go
package main

import (
  "bufio"
  "context"
=== stub ===
//go:build !android && !linux

// The helper talks to Android vendor nodes with Linux ioctls. This stub keeps
// `go build ./...` working on the Windows host the desktop app is built on;
// the real file is compiled for GOOS=android (and Linux, for testing the code
// on a desktop kernel).
package main

import (
  "fmt"
  "os"
)

func main() {
  fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "xiaomi-fod is built for Android: GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64")

}
