```
# Keep the APK the build produced, so the page can be undone after a patch.
# $apk.webui-orig also tells the rest of the script whether an APK was patched.
do_backup() {
    dir=$(overlay_dir)
    [ -d "$dir" ] || { say "x overlay directory not found: $dir"; return 1; }
    [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" = "0" ] || {
        say "x backup needs root (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"; return 1
    }

    rc=0
    for apk in "$dir"/*.apk; do
        [ -f "$apk" ] || continue
        name=${apk##*/}
        if [ -f "$apk.webui-orig" ]; then
            say "+ backup kept: $name"
            continue
        fi
        # cp -p keeps the timestamp, but the copy is never mounted, so only
        # its contents matter.
        if cp -p "$apk" "$apk.webui-orig" 2>/dev/null; then
            say "+ backup: $name"
        else
            say "x cannot write $apk.webui-orig"
            rc=1
        fi
    done
    return $rc
}

# Put the build-time APKs back. cat into the existing file instead of mv: that
# keeps the inode and the u:object_r:system_file:s0 label the module mount needs.
do_restore() {
    dir=$(overlay_dir)
    rc=0
    restored=0
    for apk in "$dir"/*.apk; do
        [ -f "$apk" ] || continue
        [ -f "$apk.webui-orig" ] || continue
        if cat "$apk.webui-orig" > "$apk" 2>/dev/null; then
            # The file is pristine again, so the copy is no longer needed:
            # without this the next reset would "restore" the same APK again
            # and keep reporting a patch that is gone.
            rm -f "$apk.webui-orig"
            say "+ restored: ${apk##*/}"
            restored=$((restored + 1))
        else
            say "x cannot restore ${apk##*/}"
            rc=1
        fi
    done
    rm -f "$dir"/*.webui-new 2>/dev/null
    [ "$restored" -gt 0 ] || say "! no backup found - nothing to restore"
    # The patch is gone, so there is nothing left for the boot guard to undo.
    if [ "$restored" -gt 0 ] && [ -f "$GEN_FILE" ]; then
        read_num "$GEN_FILE" > "$OK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
        rm -f "$TRY_FILE" 2>/dev/null
    fi
    return $rc
}

# A static RRO is read when the framework starts, so the overlay manager has to
=== pair validation ===
# A static RRO is read when the framework starts, so the overlay manager has to
# scan the APKs again before a patched value can show up. That happens on boot,
# or when zygote is restarted: init starts a fresh system_server, which re-reads
# /product/overlay and regenerates the cached idmaps.
do_reload() {
    if [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" != "0" ]; then
        say "x reload needs root (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"
        return 1
    fi
    # Arm the boot guard: if this patch never reaches boot_completed, the next
    # boot restores the build-time APKs before zygote reads them.
    boot_arm
    say "reload=zygote (the screen goes black for about 20 s)"
    if setprop ctl.restart zygote 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi
    for pid in $(pidof zygote64 zygote 2>/dev/null); do
        kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { say "reload=kill $pid"; return 0; }
    done
    say "x could not restart the framework - reboot to load the overlays"
    return 1
}

do_reset() {
    if [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" != "0" ]; then
        say "x reset needs root (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"
        return 1
    fi

    had_conf=false
    [ -f "$CONF" ] && had_conf=true

    # Any *.webui-orig means the page patched an APK, so there are values to
    # undo even when the boolean overlay was never registered.
    patched=$(ls "$(overlay_dir)"/*.webui-orig 2>/dev/null | grep -c .)
    [ -n "$patched" ] || patched=0

    active=$("$CMD" overlay list --user 0 2>/dev/null | grep -c "^\[x\].*$PREFIX")
    [ -n "$active" ] || active=0

    if [ "$active" -eq 0 ] && ! $had_conf && [ "$patched" -eq 0 ]; then
        say "No saved overrides - nothing to reset."
        return 0
    fi

    rc=0
    if [ "$patched" -gt 0 ]; then
        do_restore || rc=1
    fi

    if [ "$active" -gt 0 ] && "$CMD" overlay list >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        "$CMD" overlay disable --user 0 \
            "$(overlay_id bool/config_displayBlanksAfterDoze)" >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi

    rm -f "$CONF" "$CONF.failed"
    rm -f "$STATE_DIR/webui.conf"
    rm -f "$GEN_FILE" "$OK_FILE" "$TRY_FILE"
    say "Reset - saved values removed."
    # Only a restored APK needs the framework to scan again: an overlay that is
    # enabled or disabled takes effect in the running system immediately.
    if [ "$patched" -gt 0 ]; then
        say "! The framework still has the patched values: 'sh apply.sh reload'"
        say "  (or a reboot) loads the build-time ones again."
        # Machine-readable marker: the page restarts the framework for this.
        say "reload=needed"
    fi
    return $rc
}

do_diag() {
    say "uid=$(id -u 2>/dev/null)"
    say "su=$(command -v su 2>/dev/null || echo none)"
    say "write=$([ -w "$MODDIR" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    say "release=$(getprop ro.build.version.release 2>/dev/null)"
    say "sdk=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null)"
    say "module=$MODDIR"
    say "webroot=$([ -f "$MODDIR/webroot/index.html" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    say "apply=$([ -f "$MODDIR/webroot/apply.sh" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    say "defaults=$([ -f "$DEFAULTS" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    say "manifest=$([ -f "$MODDIR/webroot/webui-manifest.json" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    say "conf=$([ -f "$CONF" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    say "cmd=$("$CMD" overlay list >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo ok || echo unavailable)"
    say "boot_log=$([ -f "$MODDIR/webui-boot.log" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    say "--- overlay APKs (patched by the page) ---"
    for apk in "$(overlay_dir)"/*.apk; do
        [ -f "$apk" ] || continue
        if [ -f "$apk.webui-orig" ]; then
            say "patched: ${apk##*/} ($(wc -c < "$apk" | tr -d ' ') bytes, backup kept)"
        else
            say "build:   ${apk##*/} ($(wc -c < "$apk" | tr -d ' ') bytes)"
        fi
    done
    say "--- saved values ---"
    do_get
    say "static_overlays=$("$CMD" overlay list --user 0 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^\[x\] me\.phh\.treble\.overlay\.')"
    say "--- overlay list (mine) ---"
    "$CMD" overlay list --user 0 2>&1 | grep -E "$PREFIX|Error" || say "(none registered)"
    say "--- live values ---"
    if verify_all; then

- path: gui/build.sh
  content: |
              *)      echo "  install gcc, pkg-config, and the GTK3 and WebKitGTK development headers" ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Go: used when present, downloaded when not
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The launcher is the first command a new clone runs, so "install Go and come
      # back" is not an answer. The official tarball is unpacked into
      # stuff/tools/_go/ — inside the clone, no root, and found again by every later
      # build. The leading underscore matters: the go tool skips such directories,
      # so this copy of Go's source tree is not pulled into `go test ./...`. A Go
      # already on PATH is used when it is new enough; distro packages are often
      # older than go.mod asks for, which is why a too-old one is passed over
      # instead of trusted.
      
      tools_dir="$here/../stuff/tools"
      local_go="$tools_dir/_go/bin/go"
      case "$(uname -s)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) local_go="$local_go.exe" ;;
      esac
      
      go_required() {
          local req
          req="$(awk '$1 == "go" { print $2; exit }' "$here/../go.mod" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          echo "${req:-1.23}"
      }
      
      # version_at_least <have> <want>, both dotted ("1.23", "1.23.4").
      version_at_least() {
          awk -v have="$1" -v want="$2" 'BEGIN {
              n = split(have, h, "."); m = split(want, w, ".")
              if (m > n) n = m
              for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                  a = (i in h) ? h[i] + 0 : 0
                  b = (i in w) ? w[i] + 0 : 0
                  if (a > b) exit 0
                  if (a < b) exit 1
              }
              exit 0
          }'
      }
      
      go_usable() {
          [ -x "$1" ] || return 1
          local v
          v="$("$1" version 2>/dev/null | awk '{ sub(/^go/, "", $3); print $3 }')"
          [ -n "$v" ] || return 1
          version_at_least "$v" "$(go_required)"
      }
      
      # fetch_url <url> [outfile]: the body on stdout, or into the file.
      fetch_url() {
          if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
                  # One repainted line: Go is ~70 MB, and a full meter for that is
                  # hundreds of lines in the launcher's output.
                  curl -fL --retry 2 --progress-bar -o "$2" "$1"
              else
                  curl -fsSL --retry 2 "$1"
              fi
          elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
                  wget -O "$2" "$1"
              else
                  wget -qO- "$1"
              fi
          else
              return 1
          fi
      }
      
      # The os-arch half of the download name, empty when there is no official
      # build for this machine.
      go_platform() {
          local os arch
          case "$(uname -s)" in
              Linux*)
                  # Termux is Android: its prefix is not an FHS root and Go's Linux
                  # tarball is not built for it, but its own package manager has Go.
                  case "${PREFIX:-}" in
                      *com.termux*) return 1 ;;
                  esac
                  os=linux
                  ;;
              Darwin*) os=darwin ;;
              MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) os=windows ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$(uname -m)" in
              x86_64|amd64)        arch=amd64 ;;
              i386|i486|i586|i686)  arch=386 ;;
              aarch64|arm64)       arch=arm64 ;;
              armv6l|armv7l)       arch=armv6l ;;
              ppc64le)             arch=ppc64le ;;
              s390x)               arch=s390x ;;
              riscv64)             arch=riscv64 ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$os" = windows ] && [ "$arch" = armv6l ]; then
              return 1
          fi
          echo "$os-$arch"
      }
      
      install_go() {
          local platform ver file url tmp
      
          if ! platform="$(go_platform)"; then
              echo "Go $(go_required)+ is needed, and there is no download for this platform." >&2
              echo "  Install it from https://go.dev/dl/ and run this again." >&2
              case "${PREFIX:-}" in
                  *com.termux*) echo "  On Termux: pkg install golang" >&2 ;;
              esac
              return 1
          fi
      
          # VERSION?m=text is the smallest way to ask go.dev what "latest" is: two
          # lines, the first being go1.24.5 and the second its release time.
          ver="$(fetch_url "https://go.dev/VERSION?m=text" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d '\r')" || ver=""
          case "$ver" in
              go1.*) ;;
              *)
                  echo "Could not work out the current Go version — go.dev unreachable?" >&2
                  echo "  Install Go $(go_required)+ from https://go.dev/dl/ and run this again." >&2
                  return 1
                  ;;
          esac
      
          case "$platform" in
              windows-*) file="$ver.$platform.zip" ;;
              *)         file="$ver.$platform.tar.gz" ;;
          esac
          url="https://go.dev/dl/$file"
      
          echo "go was not found — downloading Go ${ver#go} into stuff/tools/_go…"
          tmp="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/go-download.XXXXXX")" || return 1
          if ! fetch_url "$url" "$tmp/$file"; then
              echo "  The download failed: $url" >&2
              rm -rf "$tmp"
              return 1
          fi
      
          mkdir -p "$tools_dir"
          # `go/` is the tarball's own top-level directory, and the old name of the
          # unpacked copy here — both must be gone before unpacking over them.
          rm -rf "$tools_dir/_go" "$tools_dir/go"
          case "$file" in
              *.zip)
                  if ! command -v unzip >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! unzip -q "$tmp/$file" -d "$tools_dir"; then
                      echo "  Could not unpack $file (is unzip installed?)" >&2
                      rm -rf "$tmp"
                      return 1
                  fi
                  ;;
              *)
                  if ! tar -xzf "$tmp/$file" -C "$tools_dir"; then
                      echo "  Could not unpack $file" >&2
                      rm -rf "$tmp"
                      return 1
                  fi
                  ;;
          esac
          rm -rf "$tmp"
          if [ -d "$tools_dir/go" ]; then
              mv "$tools_dir/go" "$tools_dir/_go" || return 1
          fi
      
          if ! go_usable "$local_go"; then
              echo "  Go unpacked but does not run from $local_go" >&2
              echo "  Install Go $(go_required)+ from https://go.dev/dl/ instead." >&2
              return 1
          fi
          echo "installed Go ${ver#go} in stuff/tools/_go"
      }

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Resource dictionary (framework-res.apk)
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # aapt2 needs the platform resource table to resolve android:* IDs. Android 13
      # is the most reliable version and links overlays for 13 through 16.
      download_platform_resources() {
          local sdk_ver="$1"
          mkdir -p "$TOOLS_DIR"
      
          local tmp_zip="${TOOLS_DIR}/platform_tmp.zip"
          local rev url revs success=false
      
          # Only these archive names exist in Google's repository (API 34 is published
          # as 34-ext7_r*, not 34_r*, so "Download Android 14" could never work).
          case "$sdk_ver" in
              34) revs="ext7_r02 ext7_r01 ext8_r01" ;;
              *)  revs="r02 r01" ;;
          esac
      
          info "Downloading Android ${sdk_ver} resources from Google..."
          for rev in $revs; do
              url="https://dl.google.com/android/repository/platform-${sdk_ver}_${rev}.zip"
              net_get "$url" "$tmp_zip" || continue
              # A downloader can exit 0 after writing an error page; a zip starts "PK".
              if [ "$(head -c 2 "$tmp_zip" 2>/dev/null)" != "PK" ]; then
                  NET_ERROR="the server answered with something that is not a zip"
                  rm -f "$tmp_zip"
                  continue
              fi
              success=true
              ok "Downloaded platform-${sdk_ver}_${rev}.zip"
              break
          done
      
          if [ "$success" != "true" ]; then
              err "Could not download the Android ${sdk_ver} resources."
              net_why
              info "Another route: option 5 in ./build.sh setup copies the file from the phone."
              rm -f "$tmp_zip"
              return 1
          fi
      
          info "Extracting android.jar (resource table)..."
          if ! unzip -j -o "$tmp_zip" "*/android.jar" -d "$TOOLS_DIR/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              err "Could not extract android.jar from the platform archive"
              rm -f "$tmp_zip"
              return 1
          fi
          if [ ! -f "$TOOLS_DIR/android.jar" ]; then
              err "The archive did not contain android.jar"
              rm -f "$tmp_zip"
              return 1
          fi
      
          mv "$TOOLS_DIR/android.jar" "$TOOLS_DIR/framework-res.apk"
          rm -f "$tmp_zip"
          ok "Android ${sdk_ver} resources installed (stuff/tools/framework-res.apk, $(du -sh "$TOOLS_DIR/framework-res.apk" | cut -f1))"
      }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MinGW-w64: the C compiler a Windows build links the window with
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Windows has no compiler of its own, and sending a fresh clone through MSYS2
# plus pacman is a second installation just to get gcc. WinLibs publishes the
# same MinGW-w64 build as a zip, so Git's unzip is enough and there is no
# installer to run. It lives in stuff/tools/_mingw next to Go, with the same
# leading underscore so `go test ./...` ignores it.
local_mingw="$tools_dir/_mingw"
local_gcc="$local_mingw/bin/gcc.exe"

mingw_usable() {
    [ -x "$local_gcc" ] && "$local_gcc" --version >/dev/null 2>&1

    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if ! mingw_usable; then
        echo "  MinGW unpacked but gcc does not run from $local_gcc" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    echo "installed MinGW-w64 in stuff/tools/_mingw"

      #
      #   ./build.sh            installs whatever is missing (sensible defaults)
      #   ./build.sh setup      interactive installer (pick distro / resource version)
      #   ./build.sh doctor     read-only check, exits 0 when a build would work
      # =============================================================================
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Downloads: curl, or wget when curl cannot start
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Termux ships curl as a binary linked against its rolling libcurl, and an
      # interrupted `pkg upgrade` leaves it unable to start at all:
      #   CANNOT LINK EXECUTABLE "curl": cannot locate symbol "SSL_set_quic_..."
      # `command -v curl` still succeeds, so every download then failed with a message
      # about Google having moved its files. wget comes from the same repo and still
      # runs, so each download tries curl and then wget, and keeps the last error in
      # NET_ERROR so the caller can say what actually broke.
      NET_ERROR=""
      
      net_get() {
          local url="$1" out="$2" log tool
          log="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/.treble-net-$$.log"
          NET_ERROR=""
          : > "$log" 2>/dev/null || true
      
          for tool in curl wget; do
              command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue
              rm -f "$out"
              if [ "$tool" = "curl" ]; then
                  curl --fail --location --silent --show-error --retry 2 \
                      --connect-timeout 20 --max-time 300 "$url" -o "$out" 2>"$log" \
                      && { rm -f "$log"; return 0; }
              else
                  wget --quiet --tries=2 --timeout=60 --output-document="$out" "$url" \
                      2>"$log" && { rm -f "$log"; return 0; }
              fi
              # Keep every attempt: when curl cannot start and wget then 404s, the
              # link error is the one that explains it, so it must not be overwritten.
              local said
              said="$( { tr '\n' ' ' < "$log" 2>/dev/null || true; } | cut -c1-200 )"
              [ -n "$said" ] || said="could not download it"
              NET_ERROR="${NET_ERROR}${NET_ERROR:+ | }${tool}: ${said}"
          done
      
          rm -f "$log"
          rm -f "$out"
          return 1
      }
      
      # net_cat URL — the same fallback for a small read onto stdout.
      net_cat() {
          local out
          if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
             out="$(curl --fail --location --silent --max-time 60 "$1" 2>/dev/null)"; then
              printf '%s' "$out"
              return 0
          fi
          if command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
             out="$(wget --quiet --timeout=60 -O - "$1" 2>/dev/null)"; then
              printf '%s' "$out"
              return 0
          fi
          return 1
      }
      
      # net_why — the likely fix for the last net_get failure, already indented.
      net_why() {
          local short
          short="$(printf '%s' "$NET_ERROR" | cut -c1-150)"
      
          case "$NET_ERROR" in
              *"CANNOT LINK EXECUTABLE"*|*"cannot locate symbol"*)
                  echo "  curl on this system cannot start (a package upgrade left it broken)."
                  echo "  Fix: pkg upgrade -y   (or: apt update && apt full-upgrade)"
                  echo "  If wget is not installed either: pkg install wget"
                  ;;
              *resolve*|*Resolving*|*"name resolution"*|*"Connection refused"*|*"timed out"*|*timeout*)
                  echo "  Google could not be reached from here: ${short}"
                  echo "  A stale mirror causes this on Termux — run: termux-change-repo"
                  ;;
              "")
                  echo "  Neither curl nor wget could download it — install one of them."
                  ;;
              *)
                  echo "  ${short}"
                  ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Windows: Google build-tools zip
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Git for Windows ships bash and coreutils, but no aapt2/zipalign/apksigner.
      # Google's Windows build-tools zip contains all three, so one download covers
      # the whole toolchain.
      install_windows_tools() {
          mkdir -p "$TOOLS_DIR"
      
          if ! command -v unzip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              err "unzip not found — reinstall Git for Windows (it bundles unzip)"
              return 1
          fi
          if ! command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              err "curl not found — reinstall Git for Windows (it bundles curl)"
              return 1
          fi
          if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              err "Java not found — apksigner needs a JDK (17 or newer)."
              echo "      Install one: https://adoptium.net/"
              echo "      or:          winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JDK"
              echo "      Then re-run: build.cmd"
              return 1
          fi
      
          local tmp_zip="${TOOLS_DIR}/build-tools-win.zip"
          local api="" url=""

got=\"$(hash_of \"$f\" \"$algo\")\"; then\n        warn \"This machine has no ${algo} tool — ${label} was not checked\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    if [ \"$got\" = \"$want\" ]; then\n        ok \"Checksum matches for ${label}\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    err \"Checksum mismatch for ${label} — the file on disk is not the one published\"\n    echo \"      expected ${want}\" >&2\n    echo \"      got      ${got}\" >&2\n    return 1\n}",

      "newString": "# published_sha256 URL — the \"<hash>  <name>\" text Google Maven and WinLibs\n# serve as FILE.sha256, or nothing when the link has no such sibling.\npublished_sha256() {\n    local url=\"$1\" text\n    text=\"$(net_cat \"${url}.sha256\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n    printf '%s' \"$text\" | awk '/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}/ { print $1; exit }'\n}\n\n# google_repo_checksum ARCHIVE — \"<algo> <hex>\" for an archive in Google's SDK\n# index, e.g. build-tools_r34_windows.zip, or nothing when it is not listed.\n# The index is 400 KB and is read once per run.\nGOOGLE_REPO_INDEX=\"\"\ngoogle_repo_checksum() {\n    local name=\"$1\" line\n    if [ -z \"$GOOGLE_REPO_INDEX\" ]; then\n        GOOGLE_REPO_INDEX=\"$(net_cat \\\n            \"https://dl.google.com/android/repository/repository2-3.xml\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n    fi\n    [ -n \"$GOOGLE_REPO_INDEX\" ] || return 0\n    line=\"$(printf '%s\\n' \"$GOOGLE_REPO_INDEX\" | awk -v want=\"<url>${name}</url>\" '\n        /<checksum/ { last = $0 }\n        index($0, want) { print last; exit }\n    ')\"\n    [ -n \"$line\" ] || return 0\n    printf '%s %s\\n' \\\n        \"$(printf '%s' \"$line\" | sed -n 's/.*type=\"\\(sha[0-9]*\\)\".*/\\1/p')\" \\\n        \"$(printf '%s' \"$line\" | sed -n 's/.*>\\([0-9a-fA-F]*\\)<.*/\\1/p')\"\n}",

```
google_repo_checksum() {
    local name="$1" line
    if [ -z "$GOOGLE_REPO_INDEX" ]; then
        GOOGLE_REPO_INDEX="$(net_cat \
            "https://dl.google.com/android/repository/repository2-3.xml" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    [ -n "$GOOGLE_REPO_INDEX" ] || return 0
    line="$(printf '%s\n' "$GOOGLE_REPO_INDEX" | awk -v want="<url>${name}</url>" '
        /<checksum/ { last = $0 }
        index($0, want) { print last; exit }
    ')"
    [ -n "$line" ] || return 0
    printf '%s %s\n' \
        "$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed -n 's/.*type="\(sha[0-9]*\)".*/\1/p')" \
        "$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed -n 's/.*>\([0-9a-fA-F]*\)<.*/\1/p')"
}

```

//go:build android || linux

// Command xiaomi-fod switches a Xiaomi touch panel into fingerprint-on-display
// mode, which is the one thing a GSI cannot do for the vendor fingerprint HAL.
//
// The stock flow is:
//
//  MIUI FingerprintService
//    -> vendor.xiaomi.hardware.fingerprintextension.extCmd(4, 3)
//    -> vendor.xiaomi.hardware.touchfeature.setModeValue(10, 3)
//    -> /dev/xiaomi-touch ioctl(0x5400, {10, 3})
//
// A GSI has no MIUI fingerprint client, so the last call never happens. The
// vendor Goodix HAL then never sees fod_press_status change, never reports a
// finger, and the sensor appears dead even though the geometry is right.
//
// This helper issues the same ioctl directly. The daemon follows the state
// machine MIUI uses, as seen in the touch driver's dmesg: the panel is armed
// with value 3 (FOD plus the AOD wake bit) when the screen turns off, stays
// armed while the keyguard is up or a fingerprint client is running (settings
// enrollment, in-app prompts), and is released otherwise. The vendor HAL's own
// FOD engine will not light the panel on a GSI (it waits for a MIUI client that
// never runs), so the daemon also drives local HBM: on while a finger is on the
// sensor. A press that arrives with the display asleep also wakes the screen,
// because the HAL aborts the auth with ui-ready timeout when no fingerprint UI
// is up to answer it. The hbm command exposes the same
// ioctl for diagnostics.
//
// The other half of the vendor FOD stack is the display node the HAL opens;
// the module's post-fs-data.sh re-creates it. See docs/udfps.md.
//
// Build for a device (no CGO, static):
//
//  GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=off \
//      go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o xiaomi-fod main.go
package main

import (

- path: .github/workflows/check.yml
  content: |
      name: check
      
      # The build itself needs the Android SDK (aapt2, apksigner, framework-res.apk),
      # which this workflow deliberately does not install: these checks cover the
      # parts that break silently — the WebUI's binary resource-table writer, the
      # manifest it renders from, script syntax and documentation anchors.
      
      on:
        push:
          branches: ["**"]
        pull_request:
      
      jobs:
        check:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
              with:
                node-version: "20"
      
            # The desktop app's own tests. CGO_ENABLED=0 is what stuff/tests/run.sh uses:
            # it skips the webview file, so no WebKitGTK headers are needed here —
            # and the browser fallback is the build that gets exercised.
            - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
              with:
                go-version: "1.23"
                cache-dependency-path: go.sum
                cache: true
      
            - name: Run the checks
              run: bash stuff/tests/run.sh
      
- path: stuff/tests/run.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Everything that can be checked without Android tools
      # =============================================================================
      # CI runs this on every push (see .github/workflows/check.yml), and it is worth
      # running before a release:
      #
      #   bash stuff/tests/run.sh
      #
      # 1. shell syntax of every shipped script (bash -n / sh -n, no execution)
      # 2. the WebUI resource-table writer against stuff/tests/fixtures/*.apk
      # 3. the WebUI manifest and the overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off
      #    vendor_hardware_overlay), built from
      #    resource XML that stuff/tests/gen-res.sh generates into a temp directory (so
      #    a fresh clone needs no build first)
      # 4. every relative link and #anchor in the docs
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -euo pipefail
      cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
      
      status=0
      step() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$*"; }
      
      step "shell syntax"
      for f in build.sh treble-rro-creator.sh gui/build.sh stuff/scripts/*.sh stuff/tests/*.sh; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          if bash -n "$f"; then :; else echo "bash -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
      done
      # apply.sh, addons.sh and the module scripts run under Android's mksh
      # (/system/bin/sh).
      for f in src/webui/apply.sh src/webui/addons.sh src/module/*.sh stuff/templates/*.sh stuff/templates/recoveries/*.sh; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          if command -v sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if sh -n "$f"; then :; else echo "sh -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
          fi
      done
      [ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all scripts parse"
      
      # The bug this guards: `clean --all` copied config.env from a frozen file, so a
      # full clean handed back a version from an older commit. The copies below are
      # now only the no-.git fallback, so they must equal the committed blob — not the
      # working file, because local edits to config.env are normal.
      step "template fallbacks match the release"
      if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          copy_status=0
          check_copy() {
              local rel="$1" copy="$2"
              if [ ! -f "$copy" ]; then
                  echo "missing fallback: $copy"
                  copy_status=1
              elif ! git show "HEAD:$rel" | diff -q - "$copy" >/dev/null; then
                  echo "$copy differs from HEAD:$rel — run: git show HEAD:$rel > $copy"
                  copy_status=1
              fi
          }
          check_copy config.env stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
          check_copy src/module/sepolicy.rule stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
          if [ "$copy_status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "fallbacks match"; else status=1; fi
      else
          echo "not a git checkout — skipping"
      fi
      
      # restore_from_release() is what clean.sh and build.sh call. Run it against a
      # throwaway repository with a deliberately stale fallback, and once without
      # .git, because "start over" silently returning old values is the failure mode.
      step "restore picks the release, not the stale copy"
      restore_here="$(pwd)"
      restore_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-restore)"
      if (
          cd "$restore_tmp" || exit 1
          git init -q . && git config user.email t@example.com && git config user.name t || exit 1
          # No .gitattributes here, and Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true,
          # which would check the file back out with CRLF and fail the greps below.
          git config core.autocrlf false
          mkdir -p src/module stuff/templates/recoveries
          printf 'KEY="released"\n' > config.env
          printf 'released rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
          printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
          printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
          git add -A && git commit -qm one || exit 1
          # The user edits both files; the fallback copies are stale.
          printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
          printf 'my rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
          ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env" && restore_from_release src/module/sepolicy.rule "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 2
          grep -qx 'KEY="released"' config.env || { echo "git restore did not win: $(cat config.env)"; exit 3; }
          grep -qx 'released rules' src/module/sepolicy.rule || exit 4
          # No .git (a zip download): the bundled copy is the only source left.
          rm -rf .git
          printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
          ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 6
          grep -q 'STALE' config.env || { echo "fallback was not used without git"; exit 7; }
      ); then
          echo "restore behaves"
      else
          echo "restore test failed (exit $?)"
          status=1
      fi
      rm -rf "$restore_tmp"
      
      step "node tests"
      if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          node --test stuff/tests/arsc.test.js stuff/tests/manifest.test.js \
              stuff/tests/hw-overlay.test.js stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js \
              stuff/tests/adb-device.test.js stuff/tests/udfps-probe.test.js \
              stuff/tests/apply-sh.test.js stuff/tests/addons-sh.test.js \
              stuff/tests/match-prop.test.js || status=1
      else
          echo "node is not installed — skipping the resource-table tests"
          status=1
      fi
      
      # The desktop app is optional: a clone without Go is still a complete CLI
      # install, so a missing toolchain skips instead of failing. CI installs Go and
      # runs this step for real (see .github/workflows/check.yml).
      step "desktop app (go)"
      if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./... || status=1
      else
          echo "go is not installed — skipping the desktop app tests"
      fi
      
      step "documentation links"
      if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          node stuff/tests/docs-links.js || status=1
      fi
      
      if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
          printf '\nSome checks failed.\n'
          exit 1
      fi
      printf '\nAll checks passed.\n'

{
  "path": "stuff/scripts/fod-build.sh",
  "instructions": "Add a maintainer script that rebuilds the committed arm64 FOD helper from its Go source.",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# =============================================================================\n# Rebuild src/module/fod/xiaomi-fod from its source\n# =============================================================================\n# The helper is shipped as a prebuilt arm64 binary: it is compiled for Android,\n# which neither a user's desktop nor Termux has to have a Go toolchain for. The\n# source stays next to it (src/module/fod/main.go) so the binary can be rebuilt\n# instead of being an opaque blob — this script is that rebuild.\n#\n#   ./build.sh fod-build        # or: bash stuff/scripts/fod-build.sh\n#   ./build.sh fod-build --check  # compile only, write nothing\n#\n# Go >= 1.23 on PATH is required. The output is not byte-identical across Go\n# releases, so a different hash is normal after a toolchain update; the build\n# has to succeed and the binary has to land, which is what CI checks on every\n# push (stuff/tests/run.sh compiles it for android/arm64).\n# =============================================================================\n\nset -euo pipefail\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../..\" && pwd)\" || exit 1\nSRC=\"$ROOT/src/module/fod\"\nOUT=\"$SRC/xiaomi-fod\"\n\ncheck_only=false\n[ \"${1:-}\" = \"--check\" ] && check_only=true\n\nif ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"fod-build: go is not on PATH — install Go 1.23+ to rebuild the helper\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\ndest=\"$OUT\"\nif [ \"$check_only\" = true ]; then\n    dest=\"$(mktemp -d \"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fod-build.XXXXXX\")/xiaomi-fod\"\nfi\n\necho \"fod-build: compiling src/module/fod/main.go for android/arm64\"\n(\n    cd \"$SRC\" || exit 1\n    GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=off \\\n        go build -trimpath -ldflags=\"-s -w\" -o \"$dest\" main.go\n) || { echo \"fod-build: compilation failed\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\nif [ \"$check_only\" = true ]; then\n    echo \"fod-build: compiles (nothing written)\"\n    rm -rf \"$(dirname \"$dest\")\"\n    exit 0\nfi\n\nchmod 0644 \"$dest\"\necho \"fod-build: wrote $OUT\"\nif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    printf 'fod-build: sha256 %s\\n' \"$(sha256sum \"$OUT\" | cut -d' ' -f1)\"\nfi"
}

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay Creator
      # =============================================================================
      # One command for everything. With a terminal attached it opens the menu, which
      # reaches every tool the desktop app has; with an argument it does exactly that
      # one thing, as before.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 the menu (on a terminal); otherwise: build
      #   ./build.sh menu            the menu, even without a terminal
      #   ./build.sh build           build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
      #   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
      #   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
      #   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
      #   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
      #   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
      #   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
      #
      #   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
      #   -h, --help                 this help
      #
      # On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
      # Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
      # drive — see docs/windows.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -e
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Project root
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      # Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
      # not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
      if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
      fi
      export ROOT
      cd "$ROOT"
      
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"
      
      # Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
      tools_on_path
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Options
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MODE="build"
      REQUESTED=$#
      CHECK_MODE=false
      DRY_RUN=false
      ASSUME_YES=false
      FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
      CLEAN_ALL=false
      FORCE_RES=""
      ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false
      
      usage() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
          echo "    (none)             The menu (on a terminal), otherwise a build"
          echo "    menu               The menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes"
          echo "    build              Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
          echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
          echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
          echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
          echo "    clean              Remove build output"
          echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --xiaomi-fod           Include the Xiaomi FOD helper (HBM + HIDL touch mode) in the module"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
          echo ""
      }
      
      for arg in "$@"; do
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --xiaomi-fod)   XIAOMI_FOD=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # No arguments and a terminal to talk on: the menu. Everything scripted passes
      # a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          MODE="menu"
      fi
      
      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).
      wsl_guard
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Dispatch
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      case "$MODE" in
          menu)
              # The terminal front end. It shells out to this same script for a build,
              # so a build started from the menu is the build a user would type.
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/menu.sh"
              menu_main
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          doctor)
              if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
              ;;
      
          setup)
              banner "Setup — build tools"
              migrate_layout
              # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
              # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
              # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
              # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
              # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
              if $ASSUME_YES; then
                  ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
              else
                  ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
              fi
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          check)
              # Config validation only: no tools, no output.
              CHECK_MODE=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          clean)
              migrate_layout
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/clean.sh"
              ;;
      
          dryrun)
              # Needs config.env and the resource generators, no toolchain: the point
              # is to see the plan in seconds.
              DRY_RUN=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          build)
              # Move any files left in the old top-level layout into src/.
              migrate_layout
              if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Windows"
              elif $IS_TERMUX; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Termux"
              else
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Linux"
              fi
              # Installs only what is missing; prints a summary and returns non-zero
              # when the machine still cannot build.
              ensure_toolchain auto
              # The installer may just have created stuff/tools/, so refresh PATH.
              tools_on_path
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      esac
      
```

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# =============================================================================\n# Rebuild src/module/fod/xiaomi-fod from its source\n# =============================================================================\n# The helper ships as a prebuilt arm64 binary: it is compiled for Android, and\n# neither a user's desktop nor Termux should need a Go toolchain for it. The\n# source stays next to it (src/module/fod/main.go), so the binary can be rebuilt\n# instead of being an opaque blob — this script is that rebuild.\n#\n#   ./build.sh fod-build        # or: bash stuff/scripts/fod-build.sh\n#\n# Go 1.23+ on PATH is required. The output is not byte-identical across Go\n# releases, so a changed hash after a toolchain update is normal. What has to\n# keep working is the compile, which stuff/tests/run.sh checks for android/arm64\n# on every push — that is the guard against source and binary drifting apart.\n# =============================================================================\n\nset -euo pipefail\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../..\" && pwd)\" || exit 1\nSRC=\"$ROOT/src/module/fod\"\nOUT=\"$SRC/xiaomi-fod\"\n\nif ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"fod-build: go is not on PATH — install Go 1.23+ to rebuild the helper\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\necho \"fod-build: compiling src/module/fod/main.go for android/arm64\"\n(\n    cd \"$SRC\" || exit 1\n    GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=off \\\n        go build -trimpath -ldflags=\"-s -w\" -o \"$OUT\" main.go\n) || { echo \"fod-build: compilation failed\" >&2; exit 1; }\n\nchmod 0644 \"$OUT\"\necho \"fod-build: wrote $OUT\"\nif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    printf 'fod-build: sha256 %s\\n' \"$(sha256sum \"$OUT\" | cut -d' ' -f1)\"\nfi"
}

- path: docs/udfps.md
  content: |
        `skip enable lhbm as fingerprint is idle` — that check expects the MIUI
        fingerprint client, which is the thing a GSI does not have.
      
      A GSI has no HyperOS fingerprint client, so the first call never happens: the
      panel stays in normal touch mode, the HAL never sees the finger, and the sensor
      looks dead even though the icon is in the right place. Even with the panel
      armed, the sensor only gets ambient light and the HBM step is skipped.
      
      The module can ship `fod/xiaomi-fod`, a small arm64 helper that issues the same
      ioctls. It is opt-in — `./build.sh build --xiaomi-fod`, or **Xiaomi FOD helper**
      under Build in the app and the terminal menu — because it is dead weight on a
      phone with no Xiaomi touch panel. On a Xiaomi phone it adds high-brightness mode
      around the capture and puts the panel into the HAL's FOD touch mode. `service.sh`
      starts it when `/dev/xiaomi-touch` exists and `ro.hardware.fp.fod=true`, so an
      arm64 Xiaomi UDFPS build is the only one that needs the flag. The daemon copies the state machine the stock touch
      driver logs: mode 10 is armed with value 3 (FOD plus the AOD wake bit) when the
      screen turns off, stays armed while the keyguard is showing (lock screen and
      AOD) or a fingerprint client is running (settings enrollment, in-app prompts),
      and is released with 0 otherwise. It reads the panel backlight,
      `dumpsys window policy` and `dumpsys fingerprint` for that, so it needs no MIUI
      service.
      
      Because the vendor HAL will not light the panel on a GSI, the same daemon
      drives local HBM. While the panel is armed it watches `fod_press_status` every
      50 ms and turns HBM on when the finger lands, and off as soon as the finger is
      up and no prompt is left (a 150 ms hold covers the capture, and the prompt
      disappearing ends it early). That is
      the stock behaviour — the spot stays dark until the sensor is touched — and it
      keeps the bright circle out of the lock screen and the AOD.
      
      A press with the display asleep works the same way, with one extra step. The
      touch controller reports it in suspend, the daemon lights HBM (about 10 ms) and
      wakes the screen with `input keyevent 224`. The wake is not cosmetic: with the
      panel asleep the vendor HAL starts an auth, waits 1500 ms for the fingerprint
      UI to answer and aborts with
      `GF_ERROR_UI_READY_TIMEOUT`, because the GSI's SystemUI has no UDFPS view up in
      doze. Waking brings the keyguard's prompt up inside that window, so the same
      press goes on to unlock the phone. The `screen_off_udfps_enabled` Secure setting
      is not consulted: this GSI's SystemUI does not act on it, and MIUI wakes the
      display on that press anyway.
      
      The prompt itself is noticed from SystemUI's own logs: `logcat` is filtered to
      `UdfpsController` and `UdfpsControllerOverlay`, and `showUdfpsOverlay` arms the
      panel the moment the window appears (opening enrollment, an in-app biometric
      prompt), while `hideUdfpsControllerOverlay` releases it. That costs nothing

- path: stuff/scripts/build.sh
  content: |
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          echo "This is an internal build module — run ./build.sh instead." >&2
          exit 1
      fi
      
      cd "$ROOT" || exit 1
      
      # Relative paths: native aapt2/zipalign on Windows may not open /c/... paths.
      RES_DIR="${FRAMEWORK_RES#"$ROOT"/}"
      SYSUI_RES_DIR="${SYSTEMUI_RES#"$ROOT"/}"
      MODULE_SRC_REL="${MODULE_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
      VENDOR_SRC_REL="${VENDOR_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
      BUILD_REL="${BUILD_DIR#"$ROOT"/}"
      : "${DRY_RUN:=false}"
      
      # Generators used by the build steps below.
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/resources.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/module.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/manifest.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/validate.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh"
      
      # Never die silently: an unexpected `set -e` abort says where and why.
      trap 'err "Unexpected failure at line ${LINENO}: ${BASH_COMMAND}"; err "Re-run with: bash -x ./build.sh  and report the last lines"' ERR
      
      # Ask something without ever aborting the build. When stdin is not an
      # interactive terminal (IDE task, CI, launcher without a console, piped input)
      # `read` fails — under `set -e` that used to kill the script mid-run.
      ASK_REPLY=""
      ask_reply() {
          local prompt="$1"
          ASK_REPLY=""
          $ASSUME_YES && return 0
          if ! read -r -p "$prompt" ASK_REPLY; then
              ASK_REPLY=""
              info "No terminal input available — using the default answer."
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # Run a build command, indent its output, and abort with a clear message if it
      # fails. (A pipeline would report sed's status, not the tool's.)
      run_or_die() {
          local label="$1"; shift
          local log="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/treble-build.$$.log"
          if "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; then
              [ -s "$log" ] && sed 's/^/  /' "$log"
              rm -f "$log"
              return 0
          fi
          [ -s "$log" ] && sed 's/^/  /' "$log"
          rm -f "$log"
          err "${label} failed"
          return 1
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Target resource audit
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # An RRO that names a resource the target does not have is accepted by aapt2
      # (especially with --auto-add-overlay) and then silently ignored at runtime.
      # That is how a module can look fine and change nothing. Every generated entry
      # is checked against the framework dictionary here.
      framework_resource_index() {
          local cache="$BUILD_REL/framework-resources.txt"
          if [ ! -s "$cache" ] || [ "$PLATFORM_JAR" -nt "$cache" ]; then
              aapt2 dump resources "$PLATFORM_JAR" 2>/dev/null \
                  | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*resource 0x[0-9a-fA-F]* //p' \
                  | awk '{ print $1 }' \
                  | sort -u > "$cache"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$cache"
      }
      
      # Print XML with comments removed, so examples inside <!-- --> are not audited.
      strip_xml_comments() {
          awk '
              FNR == 1 { inc = 0 }
              {
                  line = $0
                  if (inc) {
                      if (line ~ /-->/) { sub(/^.*-->/, "", line); inc = 0 }
                      else next
                  }
                  while (line ~ /<!--/) {
                      if (line ~ /-->/) { sub(/<!--.*-->/, "", line) }
                      else { sub(/<!--.*$/, "", line); inc = 1; break }
                  }
                  print line
              }
          ' "$@"
      }
      
      audit_framework_resources() {
          local index report entries applied=0 ignored=0
          index=$(framework_resource_index)
          report="$OUT_DIR/${OVERLAY_NAME}-overrides.txt"
      
          if [ ! -s "$index" ]; then
              err "Could not read the resource table from ${PLATFORM_JAR}"
              return 1
          fi
      
          entries=$(strip_xml_comments "$RES_DIR"/values*/*.xml 2>/dev/null | awk '
              /<(bool|dimen|integer|string|string-array|integer-array|array|item)[[:space:]>]/ {
                  line = $0
                  tag = line
                  sub(/^[^<]*</, "", tag)
                  sub(/[^a-z-].*$/, "", tag)
                  if (match(line, /name="[^"]+"/) == 0) next
                  name = substr(line, RSTART + 6, RLENGTH - 7)
                  type = ""
                  if (tag == "item") {
                      if (match(line, /type="[^"]+"/)) type = substr(line, RSTART + 6, RLENGTH - 7)
                      if (type == "") type = "dimen"
                  } else if (tag == "string-array" || tag == "integer-array" || tag == "array") {
                      type = "array"
                  } else {

          # Build-time values so the page can show what the module currently uses.
          # Saved WebUI values in webui.conf take precedence at runtime.
          {
              printf 'RADIUS=%s\n'      "${ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'SB_HEIGHT=%s\n'    "${STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'PAD_CONTENT=%s\n'  "${STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'PAD_START=%s\n'    "${STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'PAD_END=%s\n'      "${STATUS_BAR_PADDING_END//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'DOZE_BLANK=%s\n'   "${CONFIG_DISPLAY_BLANKS_AFTER_DOZE:-false}"
          } > "${MODULE_TMP}/webui-defaults.conf"
          # The page renders its editor from this list, so what it can edit comes
          # from the same resource XML the build compiles - not a second table.
          WEBUI_RES_COUNT=$(write_webui_manifest "${MODULE_TMP}/webroot/webui-manifest.json")
          ok "webroot/: WebUI included (KSU / KSU Next / APatch / Magisk hosts)"
          info "webroot/webui-manifest.json: ${WEBUI_RES_COUNT} resource(s) editable from the page"
      fi
      
      # Module addons: Settings values the module applies itself, which no overlay
      # resource can express (the volume panel side, the screen timeout, ...). The
      # clone keeps the choice in src/module/addons.conf — that is what the desktop
      # app's Addons tab writes — and the phone's page edits the packed copy. Only the
      # addons listed in the file are enforced, so an untouched file changes nothing.
      if [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/addons.conf" ]; then
          cp "$MODULE_DIR/addons.conf" "${MODULE_TMP}/addons.conf"
          chmod 0644 "${MODULE_TMP}/addons.conf"
          ADDON_COUNT=$(grep -c '^[A-Za-z]' "${MODULE_TMP}/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true)
          ok "addons.conf included (${ADDON_COUNT:-0} addon(s) chosen)"
      else
          info "addons.conf not found — the module ships no addons"
      fi
      
      # Use src/module/customize.sh when present, otherwise generate one.
      if [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/customize.sh" ]; then
          cp "$MODULE_DIR/customize.sh" "${MODULE_TMP}/customize.sh" && chmod +x "${MODULE_TMP}/customize.sh"
          ok "customize.sh: using src/module/customize.sh"
      elif [ "$INCLUDE_VENDOR_HALS" = "true" ]; then
          generate_customize_sh "$MODULE_TMP"
          ok "customize.sh auto-generated from vendor/ contents"
      else
          # Overlay-only: simple customize.sh
          cat > "${MODULE_TMP}/customize.sh" << 'CUSTOMIZE_SIMPLE'
      #!/sbin/sh
      # MODPATH is exported by the manager when it sources this script; fall back to
      # the script location (some managers run it as `sh customize.sh`, where $0 is
      # not a path).
      MODPATH=${MODPATH:-${0%/*}}
      [ -d "$MODPATH/system" ] || MODPATH="."
      ui_print "  Installing ${MODPATH##*/}..."
      set_perm_recursive $MODPATH/system/product/overlay 0 0 0755 0644 u:object_r:system_file:s0
      
      # The zip may lose the executable bit depending on the manager's extractor.
      if [ -f "$MODPATH/fod/xiaomi-fod" ]; then
          set_perm "$MODPATH/fod/xiaomi-fod" 0 0 0755
      fi
      
      # Values saved in the WebUI live outside the module directory (an update
      # replaces this one), so bring them back. The page re-applies them onto the new
      # APKs the next time it is opened.
      if [ -f "$MODPATH/webroot/apply.sh" ]; then
          sh "$MODPATH/webroot/apply.sh" restore-conf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      fi
      
      # Module addons: the saved choices also survive an update through that folder.
      # Applying them now means a rebuild does not need a reboot to take effect.
      if [ -f "$MODPATH/webroot/addons.sh" ]; then
          sh "$MODPATH/webroot/addons.sh" restore-conf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          sh "$MODPATH/webroot/addons.sh" apply >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      fi
      
      ui_print "  ✓ Module installed successfully!"
      CUSTOMIZE_SIMPLE
          chmod +x "${MODULE_TMP}/customize.sh"
          ok "customize.sh generated (overlay-only)"
      fi
      
      # META-INF: Magisk's installer entry point. KernelSU and APatch source
      # customize.sh directly and ignore this directory, so one zip serves all three.
      generate_magisk_meta "${MODULE_TMP}"
      
      # sepolicy.rule
      if [ "$INCLUDE_VENDOR_HALS" = "true" ] && [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/sepolicy.rule" ]; then
          if grep -q '^allow' "$MODULE_DIR/sepolicy.rule" 2>/dev/null; then
              RULE_COUNT=$(grep -c '^allow' "$MODULE_DIR/sepolicy.rule")
              cp "$MODULE_DIR/sepolicy.rule" "${MODULE_TMP}/" && ok "Included sepolicy.rule (${RULE_COUNT} allow rules)"
          else
              info "sepolicy.rule has no allow rules — template only, skipping"
          fi
      else
          if [ "$INCLUDE_VENDOR_HALS" = "true" ]; then

              -e "s/@OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI@/${OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI}/g" \
              -e "s/@MODULE_ID@/${OVERLAY_NAME}/g" \
              "$MODULE_DIR/service.sh" > "${MODULE_TMP}/service.sh"
          chmod +x "${MODULE_TMP}/service.sh"
          ok "service.sh: using src/module/service.sh (package: ${OVERLAY_PACKAGE})"
      else
          generate_service_sh "$MODULE_TMP"
          # Substitute placeholders in the generated file
          sed -i -e "s/@OVERLAY_PACKAGE@/${OVERLAY_PACKAGE}/g" \
                 -e "s/@OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI@/${OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI}/g" \
                 -e "s/@MODULE_ID@/${OVERLAY_NAME}/g" \
                 "${MODULE_TMP}/service.sh"
          ok "service.sh auto-generated (package: ${OVERLAY_PACKAGE})"
      fi
      
      # Xiaomi touch-panel FOD helper (fod/xiaomi-fod). Opt-in with --xiaomi-fod, or
      # the checkbox in the app / menu: it writes Xiaomi's touch-panel FOD mode and
      # asks the vendor HAL for high-brightness mode, so on any other vendor it is a
      # binary nobody starts and extra bytes in the zip. service.sh still checks the
      # hardware at boot, so the flag is only about what ships.
      if [ "${XIAOMI_FOD:-false}" = "true" ]; then
          if [ "${HAS_UDFPS:-false}" != "true" ]; then
              warn "--xiaomi-fod ignored: HAS_UDFPS is not true, so there is no in-display sensor to help"
          elif [ ! -f "$MODULE_DIR/fod/xiaomi-fod" ]; then
              warn "--xiaomi-fod ignored: src/module/fod/xiaomi-fod is missing from this checkout"
          else
              mkdir -p "${MODULE_TMP}/fod"
              cp "$MODULE_DIR/fod/xiaomi-fod" "${MODULE_TMP}/fod/xiaomi-fod"
              chmod 0755 "${MODULE_TMP}/fod/xiaomi-fod"
              ok "fod/xiaomi-fod included (Xiaomi touch-panel FOD mode)"
          fi
      fi
      
      # post-fs-data.sh — set a persist.* match property before zygote starts
      if [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/post-fs-data.sh" ]; then
          cp "$MODULE_DIR/post-fs-data.sh" "${MODULE_TMP}/post-fs-data.sh" \
              && chmod +x "${MODULE_TMP}/post-fs-data.sh"
          ok "post-fs-data.sh: using src/module/post-fs-data.sh"
      else
          MATCH_PROP_YES=no
          if [ -n "$DEVICE_PROP_NAME" ] && [[ "$DEVICE_PROP_NAME" == persist.* ]]; then
              MATCH_PROP_YES=yes
          fi
          generate_post_fs_data_sh "${MODULE_TMP}" "$MATCH_PROP_YES"
          sed -i -e "s|@MATCH_PROP@|${DEVICE_PROP_NAME}|g" \
                 -e "s|@MATCH_VALUE@|${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE}|g" \
                 -e "s|@MODULE_ID@|${OVERLAY_NAME}|g" \
                 "${MODULE_TMP}/post-fs-data.sh"
          if [ "$MATCH_PROP_YES" = "yes" ]; then
              ok "post-fs-data.sh sets ${DEVICE_PROP_NAME}=${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE} before zygote"
          else
              ok "post-fs-data.sh: WebUI boot guard only (no persist.* match property)"
          fi
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Copy vendor HAL files (only if INCLUDE_VENDOR_HALS is set)
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      VENDOR_HALS_COPIED=false
      
      if [ "$INCLUDE_VENDOR_HALS" = "true" ]; then
          # Vendor HAL binaries
          if [ -d "$VENDOR_SRC_REL/bin/hw" ] && [ "$(ls -A "$VENDOR_SRC_REL"/bin/hw/ 2>/dev/null | grep -c .)" -gt 0 ]; then

      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Package module
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      create_zip "$MODULE_TMP" "${ROOT}/out/${OVERLAY_NAME}-ksu.zip" \
          || { err "Failed to package module zip"; exit 1; }
      rm -rf "$MODULE_TMP"
      ok "Module packaged: out/${OVERLAY_NAME}-ksu.zip (KernelSU / KSU Next / APatch / Magisk)"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build Hardware Overlay Repo Structure (AOSP source-based)
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      step "Building Hardware Overlay Repo structure"
      
      # The submission tree (manifests, Android.mk, resources minus the repo's
      # blacklist, notes) is written by stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh, which is also
      # runnable on its own: ./stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh plan|write <dir>
      HW_OVERLAY_DIR="$BUILD_REL/hardware_overlay"
      write_hardware_overlay "$HW_OVERLAY_DIR" || { err "Failed to generate the hardware overlay tree"; exit 1; }
      FW_HW_DIR="$HW_FW_DIR"
      SYSUI_HW_DIR="${HW_SYSUI_DIR:-}"
      
      # Package it
      create_zip "$HW_OVERLAY_DIR" "${ROOT}/out/${OVERLAY_NAME}-hardware-overlay.zip" \
          || { err "Failed to package hardware overlay sources"; exit 1; }
      ok "Hardware Overlay Repo package created: out/${OVERLAY_NAME}-hardware-overlay.zip"
      
      # 3. Build Hardware Overlay TEST Flashable Zip
      # This builds an APK from the *merged* hardware overlay source and packages it
      # into a simple flashable module so you can test if the AOSP repo version works.
      step "Building Hardware Overlay TEST Flashable Zip"
      
      TEST_BUILD_DIR="$BUILD_REL/hw_test"
      rm -rf "$TEST_BUILD_DIR"
      mkdir -p "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/compiled" "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/apk" "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/module/system/product/overlay"
      
      # 3a. Compile merged Framework resources
      info "Building TEST Framework APK..."
      run_or_die "TEST: aapt2 compile (framework)" \
          aapt2 compile --dir "$FW_HW_DIR/res" -o "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/compiled/" || exit 1
      run_or_die "TEST: aapt2 link (framework)" \
          aapt2 link --manifest "$FW_HW_DIR/AndroidManifest.xml" \
          -I "${PLATFORM_JAR}" \
          --auto-add-overlay \
          --compile-sdk-version-code "${COMPILE_SDK_VERSION}" \
          --compile-sdk-version-name "${ANDROID_VERSION}" \
          -o "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/apk/unsigned.apk" \
          "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/compiled"/*.flat || exit 1
      
      run_or_die "TEST: zipalign (framework)" \
          align_apk "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/apk/unsigned.apk" "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/apk/aligned.apk" || exit 1
      run_or_die "TEST: apksigner sign (framework)" \
          "$APKSIGNER_BIN" sign --key "${PLATFORM_KEY}" --cert "${PLATFORM_CERT}" \
          --v1-signing-enabled true --v2-signing-enabled true --v4-signing-enabled false \
          --out "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/module/system/product/overlay/${OVERLAY_NAME}.apk" "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/apk/aligned.apk" || exit 1
      
      # 3b. Compile merged SystemUI resources (if exists)
      if [ "$LINKED_SYSTEMUI" = "true" ]; then
          info "Building TEST SystemUI APK..."
          mkdir -p "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/compiled_systemui" "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/apk_systemui"
          run_or_die "TEST: aapt2 compile (SystemUI)" \
              aapt2 compile --dir "$SYSUI_HW_DIR/res" -o "$TEST_BUILD_DIR/compiled_systemui/" || exit 1
          run_or_die "TEST: aapt2 link (SystemUI)" \
              aapt2 link --manifest "$SYSUI_HW_DIR/AndroidManifest.xml" \

- path: src/webui/apply.sh
  content: |
      
      do_apks() {
          fw=$(fw_apk)
          sui=$(sui_apk)
          say "fw=${fw:-}"
          say "sui=${sui:-}"
          say "write=$([ -w "$(overlay_dir)" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
          say "uid=$(id -u 2>/dev/null)"
      }
      
      # Keep the APK the build produced, so the page can be undone after a patch.
      # $apk.webui-orig also tells the rest of the script whether an APK was patched.
      do_backup() {
          dir=$(overlay_dir)
          [ -d "$dir" ] || { say "x overlay directory not found: $dir"; return 1; }
          [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" = "0" ] || {
              say "x backup needs root (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"; return 1
          }
      
          rc=0
          for apk in "$dir"/*.apk; do
              [ -f "$apk" ] || continue
              name=${apk##*/}
              if [ -f "$apk.webui-orig" ]; then
                  say "+ backup kept: $name"
                  continue
              fi
              # cp -p keeps the timestamp, but the copy is never mounted, so only
              # its contents matter.
              if cp -p "$apk" "$apk.webui-orig" 2>/dev/null; then
                  say "+ backup: $name"
              else
                  say "x cannot write $apk.webui-orig"
                  rc=1
              fi
          done
          return $rc
      }
      
      # Put the build-time APKs back. cat into the existing file instead of mv: that
      # keeps the inode and the u:object_r:system_file:s0 label the module mount needs.
      do_restore() {
          dir=$(overlay_dir)
          rc=0
          restored=0
          for apk in "$dir"/*.apk; do
              [ -f "$apk" ] || continue
              [ -f "$apk.webui-orig" ] || continue
              if cat "$apk.webui-orig" > "$apk" 2>/dev/null; then
                  # The file is pristine again, so the copy is no longer needed:
                  # without this the next reset would "restore" the same APK again
                  # and keep reporting a patch that is gone.
                  rm -f "$apk.webui-orig"
                  say "+ restored: ${apk##*/}"
                  restored=$((restored + 1))
              else
                  say "x cannot restore ${apk##*/}"
                  rc=1
              fi
          done
          rm -f "$dir"/*.webui-new 2>/dev/null
          [ "$restored" -gt 0 ] || say "! no backup found - nothing to restore"
          # The patch is gone, so there is nothing left for the boot guard to undo.
          if [ "$restored" -gt 0 ] && [ -f "$GEN_FILE" ]; then
              read_num "$GEN_FILE" > "$OK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
              rm -f "$TRY_FILE" 2>/dev/null
          fi
          return $rc
      }
      
      # A static RRO is read when the framework starts, so the overlay manager has to
      # scan the APKs again before a patched value can show up. That happens on boot,
      # or when zygote is restarted: init starts a fresh system_server, which re-reads
      # /product/overlay and regenerates the cached idmaps.
      do_reload() {
          if [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" != "0" ]; then
              say "x reload needs root (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"
              return 1
          fi
          # Arm the boot guard: if this patch never reaches boot_completed, the next
          # boot restores the build-time APKs before zygote reads them.
          boot_arm
          say "reload=zygote (the screen goes black for about 20 s)"
          if setprop ctl.restart zygote 2>/dev/null; then
              return 0
          fi
          for pid in $(pidof zygote64 zygote 2>/dev/null); do
              kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { say "reload=kill $pid"; return 0; }
          done
          say "x could not restart the framework - reboot to load the overlays"

> 
> If a user patched, rebooted (guard ok, backup kept), then installs a newer module zip: the module replaces /product/overlay/*.apk? Actually module mount: Magisk overlays the whole module dir; a new module version replaces files, but the .webui-orig file from the old module version lives in the *previous* module dir... With magic mount, module contents overlay /product/overlay; files from the old module install (including webui-orig) are in the module folder which gets replaced on update. So after an update, .webui-orig is gone (new zip has none). Unless the module update merges directories rather than replacing. Magisk uninstalls old module dir and extracts new → stale files gone. So ok.
