- path: src/webui/apply.sh
  content: |
      #
      # Saved values are mirrored to $STATE_DIR, because the module directory itself
      # is replaced when the module is updated: the new zip carries the build-time
      # APKs again, and the page re-applies webui.conf onto them the next time it is
      # opened. customize.sh copies the file back on install.
      #
      # Resource arrays such as the auto-brightness curves cannot be expressed this
      # way at all - those still need a rebuild.
      #
      # NOTE: fabricated overlay names may only contain alphanumerics, '_' and '.'
      # (AOSP OverlayManagerServiceImpl.validateName with requireFilename=true).
      # A hyphen in the name makes `fabricate` fail with
      # "overlay name can only consist of alphanumeric characters, '_', and '.'",
      # so every character outside that set is replaced with '_'.
      # =============================================================================
      
      SELF="$0"
      case "$SELF" in
          */*) SELF_DIR=${SELF%/*} ;;
          *)   SELF_DIR=. ;;
      esac
      MODDIR=$(cd "$SELF_DIR/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)
      [ -n "$MODDIR" ] || MODDIR=$SELF_DIR
      CONF="$MODDIR/webui.conf"
      DEFAULTS="$MODDIR/webui-defaults.conf"
      # Outside the module directory on purpose: an update replaces that directory.
      # WEBUI_STATE_DIR exists so the script can be exercised off-device.
      STATE_DIR="${WEBUI_STATE_DIR:-/data/adb/treble-webui/${MODDIR##*/}}"
      GEN_FILE="$MODDIR/webui-gen"
      OK_FILE="$MODDIR/webui-gen-ok"
      TRY_FILE="$MODDIR/webui-try"
      OWNER="com.android.shell"
      PREFIX="treble_webui"
      
      # WEBUI_CMD only exists so the script can be exercised off-device.
      CMD=${WEBUI_CMD:-/system/bin/cmd}
      DENSITY=""
      
      KEYS="RADIUS SB_HEIGHT PAD_CONTENT PAD_START PAD_END DOZE_BLANK"
      
      say() { echo "$*"; }
      
      # --- storage ---------------------------------------------------------------
      # Keys are either the five short names (RADIUS, SB_HEIGHT, PAD_CONTENT,
      # PAD_START, PAD_END, DOZE_BLANK) or a full resource name the page found in
      # webui-manifest.json (bool/config_showNavigationBar, dimen/status_bar_padding_top,
      # integer/config_multiuserMaximumUsers, string/config_radio_access_family).
      
      conf_value() { # <file> <key> -> last value of that key
          [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
          awk -v k="$2" 'index($0, k "=") == 1 { v = substr($0, length(k) + 2) } END { printf "%s", v }' "$1" 2>/dev/null
      }
      
      all_keys() {
          for f in "$DEFAULTS" "$STATE_DIR/webui.conf" "$CONF"; do
              [ -f "$f" ] || continue
              sed -n 's/^\([A-Za-z0-9_./][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*\)=.*/\1/p' "$f" 2>/dev/null
          done | awk '!seen[$0]++'
      }
      
      get_effective() { # <key> -> saved value, else the build-time default
          v=$(conf_value "$CONF" "$1")
          if [ -z "$v" ]; then
              v=$(conf_value "$DEFAULTS" "$1")
          fi
          if [ -z "$v" ]; then
              v=$(conf_value "$STATE_DIR/webui.conf" "$1")
          fi
          printf '%s' "$v"
      }
      
      # The saved values live in two places: the module (what the page reads) and
      # $STATE_DIR (what survives an update).
      mirror_conf() {
          mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || return 0
          cp "$CONF" "$STATE_DIR/webui.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
          chmod 600 "$STATE_DIR/webui.conf" 2>/dev/null || true
      }
      
      put_conf() { # <key> <value>
          key=$1
          val=$2
          case "$key" in
              *[!A-Za-z0-9_./-]*) say "x invalid key: $key"; return 1 ;;
          esac
          tmp="$CONF.tmp"
          if [ -f "$CONF" ]; then
              awk -v k="$key" -v v="$val" '
                  index($0, k "=") == 1 { if (!done) { print k "=" v; done = 1 } next }
                  { print }
                  END { if (!done) print k "=" v }
              ' "$CONF" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
          else
              printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$val" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
          fi
          if [ ! -f "$tmp" ] || ! mv "$tmp" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null; then
              rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
              say "x cannot write $CONF (uid $(id -u 2>/dev/null))"
              say "  The WebUI host ran this script without write access to the module."
              return 1
          fi
          chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
          mirror_conf
          return 0
      }
      
      # --- boot guard ------------------------------------------------------------
      # A patched APK is loaded before anything can react to it, so a value that
      # breaks the framework would otherwise need a reinstall to undo. apply.sh
      # counts patches instead: post-fs-data.sh gives the first boot after a patch a
      # chance, and if that boot never reaches boot_completed (service.sh confirms
      # it) the next boot puts the build-time APKs back before zygote starts.
      
      read_num() { # <file> -> integer, 0 when missing
          n=$(cat "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')
          printf '%s' "${n:-0}"
      }
      
      boot_arm() {
          n=$(read_num "$GEN_FILE")
          n=$((n + 1))
          printf '%s\n' "$n" > "$GEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
          rm -f "$TRY_FILE" 2>/dev/null
      }
      
      boot_confirm() {
          n=$(read_num "$GEN_FILE")
          printf '%s\n' "$n" > "$OK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
          rm -f "$TRY_FILE" 2>/dev/null
      }
      
      boot_guard() {
          gen=$(read_num "$GEN_FILE")
          ok=$(read_num "$OK_FILE")
          tried=$(read_num "$TRY_FILE")
          [ "$gen" -gt 0 ] || return 0
          [ "$gen" = "$ok" ] && return 0
          if [ "$tried" = "$gen" ]; then
              say "! The previous boot did not finish with this patch - restoring the build APKs"
              if ls "$(overlay_dir)"/*.webui-orig >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  do_restore
              else
                  say "  no patched APK to restore (the boot did not get far enough)"
              fi
              # Keep the rejected values, but out of the way: the page would re-apply
              # them on its next start and undo this restore.
              [ -f "$CONF" ] && mv "$CONF" "$CONF.failed" 2>/dev/null
              rm -f "$STATE_DIR/webui.conf" 2>/dev/null
              printf '%s\n' "$gen" > "$OK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
              rm -f "$TRY_FILE" 2>/dev/null
              echo "guard=restored" >> "$MODDIR/webui-boot.log" 2>/dev/null || true
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$gen" > "$TRY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
          return 0
      }
      
      restore_conf() { # customize.sh: bring the saved values into the new install
          src="$STATE_DIR/webui.conf"
          [ -f "$src" ] || return 0
          if cp "$src" "$CONF" 2>/dev/null; then
              chmod 600 "$CONF" 2>/dev/null || true
              say "+ saved WebUI values restored"
          fi
      }
      
      # --- fabrication -----------------------------------------------------------
      
      overlay_name() { # <type/name> -> name valid for FabricatedOverlay
          printf '%s_%s' "$PREFIX" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9_.' '_')"
      }
      
      # overlay_id <type/name> -> owner-qualified overlay id shown by `overlay list`
      overlay_id() {
          printf '%s:%s' "$OWNER" "$(overlay_name "$1")"
      }
      
      # wait_enabled <type/name> -> 0 when the manager reports the overlay enabled.
      # Prints the last list line seen so the caller can show what the manager thinks.
      # `cmd overlay enable` exits 0 even when the transaction is rejected (Android
      # logs the reason and leaves the overlay disabled), so its exit code proves
      # nothing; the state in `overlay list` is the only reliable signal.
      wait_enabled() {
          n=$(overlay_name "$1")
          i=0
          line=""
          while [ "$i" -lt 3 ]; do
              line=$("$CMD" overlay list --user 0 2>/dev/null | grep -F ":$n" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
              case "$line" in
                  "[x]"*) printf '%s' "$line"; return 0 ;;
              esac
              i=$((i + 1))
              sleep 1
          done
          printf '%s' "$line"
          return 1
      }
      
      fabricate() { # <target> <type/name> <type-id> <encoded-value>
          target=$1
          resource=$2
          tid=$3
          enc=$4
          name=$(overlay_name "$resource")
      
          out=$("$CMD" overlay fabricate --target "$target" --name "$name" \
              "$target:$resource" "$tid" "$enc" 2>&1)
          if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
              say "x $resource: $(printf '%s' "$out" | tr '\n' ' ')"
              return 1

> _Reasoning_
> I see a genuine gap in `restore_conf`: it copies the state file over `$CONF`, but the state dir file is only a *mirror of saved values*; nothing backs up `$CONF`… fine.
> 
> But: `restore_conf` does not handle `.webui-orig`/guard files after an update. Scenario: user patches (webui-gen=1, ok=0?) → reboot OK → ok=1. Then they install a new module version: module dir replaced → webui-gen, webui-gen-ok, webui-try files are gone (new zip has none? Actually build.sh's MODULE_TMP doesn't create webui-gen), and apply.sh restore-conf copies the saved conf back, but the new APKs are the build-time ones — good, no patch. OK.
> 
> The real gap I might be remembering: `boot_guard` requires `LS_ORIG`; if the overlay dir APKs were replaced by a module update while patched, the .webui-orig is old-build; restore would write the *old* APK. Edge case, already noted.
> 
> Hmm. Rather than invent, let me consider the audit item text I had: "Re-check the apply.sh backup/restore claim and either fix the real gap or report it as a non-bug". Given evidence: do_backup keeps only the first pristine copy (guard present), do_restore removes copy, boot guard restores on failed boot, restore-conf is install-time. That's a coherent design; and my earlier note said "apply.sh already validates keys". So this is a non-bug → report it.
> 
> But wait — there is one thing: `do_backup` writes `$apk.webui-orig` INTO the overlay dir (`/product/overlay` via module mount). Those files are inside the module dir; module mount + `*.apk.webui-orig` name — no conflict. Fine.
> 
> However: `do_restore` iterates `"$dir"/*.apk` — matches only `*.apk`, and `.webui-orig` files end with `.webui-orig`, not `.apk` — but careful: `$dir`/*.apk glob will NOT match `foo.apk.webui-orig`. Right.
> 
> So: non-bug. Mark it done with a note in the final summary. Actually — is there a *test* covering backup/restore? stuff/tests/apply-sh.test.js exists. Fine.

      ok "SystemUI AndroidManifest.xml generated"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Generate module.prop

      DESCRIPTION="${DEVICE_MODEL} overlay"
      [ -n "$ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS" ] && [[ "$ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS" != *"<"* ]] && DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION}: rounded corners (${ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS}px)"
      [ "$HAS_AOD" = "true" ] && DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION}, AOD"
      [ "$HAS_UDFPS" = "true" ] && DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION}, UDFPS"
      [ "$HAS_5G" = "true" ] && DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION}, 5G"
      [ "$HAS_VOLTE" = "true" ] && DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION}, VoLTE"
      [ "$HAS_VENDOR_FINGERPRINT_HAL" = "true" ] && DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION}, fingerprint HAL"
      [ "$HAS_VENDOR_VIBRATOR_HAL" = "true" ] && DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION}, vibrator HAL"
      
      cat > "$BUILD_REL/module.prop" << MODPROP
      id=${OVERLAY_NAME}
      name=Treble Overlay - ${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER} ${DEVICE_MODEL}
      version=${OVERLAY_VERSION}
      versionCode=${OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE}
      author=${MODULE_AUTHOR}
      description=${DESCRIPTION}
      MODPROP
      ok "module.prop generated"
      info "Generating Android.mk"
      cat > "$BUILD_REL/Android.mk" << ANDROIDMK
      LOCAL_PATH := \$(call my-dir)
      include \$(CLEAR_VARS)
      
      LOCAL_MODULE := ${OVERLAY_NAME}
      LOCAL_MODULE_TAGS := optional
      LOCAL_SRC_FILES := ${OVERLAY_NAME}.apk
      LOCAL_MODULE_CLASS := APPS
      LOCAL_CERTIFICATE := platform
      LOCAL_MODULE_OWNER := ${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}
      LOCAL_DEX_PREOPT := false
      LOCAL_MODULE_PATH := \$(TARGET_OUT_PRODUCT)/overlay

      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay — shared helpers
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by build.sh and by the modules in stuff/scripts/. Never run directly.
      #
      # The entry point sets ROOT (the project directory) and then sources this file,
      # so every helper below can assume it exists and that the current directory is
      # the project root.
      # =============================================================================

- path: build.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay Creator
      # =============================================================================
      # One command for everything. With a terminal attached it opens the menu, which
      # reaches every tool the desktop app has; with an argument it does exactly that
      # one thing, as before.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 the menu (on a terminal); otherwise: build
      #   ./build.sh menu            the menu, even without a terminal
      #   ./build.sh build           build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
      #   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
      #   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
      #   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
      #   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
      #   ./build.sh fod-build       rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper (maintainers)
      #   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
      #   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
      #
      #   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
      #   -h, --help                 this help
      #
      # On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
      # Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
      # drive — see docs/windows.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      # pipefail matters here: most build steps run a tool and parse its output in a
      # pipeline (`aapt2 dump ... | sed | awk`). Without it a failed tool still exits
      # 0 through the pipeline and the build carries on with empty input.
      set -eo pipefail
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Project root
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      # Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
      # not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
      if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
      fi
      export ROOT
      cd "$ROOT"
      
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"
      
      # Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
      tools_on_path
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Options
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MODE="build"
      REQUESTED=$#
      CHECK_MODE=false
      DRY_RUN=false
      ASSUME_YES=false
      FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
      CLEAN_ALL=false
      FORCE_RES=""
      ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false
      
      usage() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
          echo "    (none)             The menu (on a terminal), otherwise a build"
          echo "    menu               The menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes"
          echo "    build              Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
          echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
          echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
          echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
          echo "    fod-build          Rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper from its Go source"
          echo "    clean              Remove build output"
          echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --xiaomi-fod           Include the Xiaomi FOD helper (HBM + HIDL touch mode) in the module"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
          echo ""
      }
      
      for arg in "$@"; do
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              fod-build|--fod-build) MODE="fodbuild" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --xiaomi-fod)   XIAOMI_FOD=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # No arguments and a terminal to talk on: the menu. Everything scripted passes
      # a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

      type State struct {
        Clone      string      `json:"clone"`
        CloneValid bool        `json:"cloneValid"`
        Bash       string      `json:"bash"`
        BashValid  bool        `json:"bashValid"`
        ConfigText string      `json:"configText"`

        Verbs      []Verb      `json:"verbs"`
        Docs       []Doc       `json:"docs"`
        Out        []OutFile   `json:"out"`
        Run        RunState    `json:"run"`
        AdbRun     RunState    `json:"adbRun"`
        Update     UpdateInfo  `json:"update"`
        Adb        AdbInfo     `json:"adb"`
        Presets    []AdbPreset `json:"adbPresets"`
      }
      
      // adbState is the Device console's snapshot with a nil guard: a test can build
      // an App with only the build runner, and a console that does not exist has no
      // job to report.
      func (a *App) adbState() RunState {
        if a.adbRunner == nil {
          return RunState{}
        }
        return a.adbRunner.Snapshot()
      }
      
      func (a *App) State() State {
        a.mu.RLock()

      function renderHeader() {
        const upd = state.update || {};
      
        // One button for both paths: the clone and bash are set in the same dialog,
        // so two chips that open it only made the header look busier. The dot still
        // says whether the pair is usable, and the tooltip keeps both paths visible.
        const path = $('chip-path');
        path.dataset.tone = state.cloneValid && state.bashValid ? 'ok' : 'bad';
        path.title = [
          'clone: ' + (state.clone || 'none — click to set'),
          'bash: ' + (state.bash || 'none — click to set'),
          'click to change either',
        ].join('\n');
      
        const branch = $('chip-branch');
        if (state.branch) {
          branch.textContent = state.commit ? `${state.branch} @ ${state.commit}` : state.branch;
          branch.dataset.tone = state.dirty ? 'warn' : 'ok';
          branch.title = state.dirty
            ? 'you have local edits — an update will list them before touching anything'
            : 'clean working tree';
        } else {
          branch.textContent = 'not a git clone';
          branch.dataset.tone = 'warn';
        }
      
        // The button always says what it does; the dot carries the answer. Green
        // means there is something to pull, which is the one case worth a colour.
        const chip = $('chip-update');
        if (upd.available) {
          chip.dataset.tone = 'ok';
          chip.title = `${upd.behind} new commit${upd.behind === 1 ? '' : 's'} on ${upd.upstream} — click to see what it changes`;
        } else if (upd.error && !upd.checked) {
          chip.dataset.tone = 'warn';
          chip.title = 'could not check for updates: ' + upd.error;
        } else {
          chip.dataset.tone = '';
          chip.title = upd.checked ? 'up to date — click to check again' : 'click to check for updates';
        }
      
        if (state.bashValid && state.cloneValid) {
          if (upd.available) {
            $('sub').textContent = `update available: ${upd.behind} commit${upd.behind === 1 ? '' : 's'} behind ${upd.upstream}`;
          } else if (upd.checked) {
            $('sub').textContent = 'up to date';
          } else if (upd.error && state.branch) {
            $('sub').textContent = 'could not check for updates';
          } else {
            $('sub').textContent = 'ready';
          }
        }
      }
      
      function currentVerb() {
        if (!state) return null;
        return state.verbs.find((v) => v.name === selectedVerb) || state.verbs[0] || null;

      cfg_counts() {
          local rows
          rows="$(cfg_rows 2>/dev/null)" || { CFG_ON=0; CFG_OFF=0; return 0; }
          CFG_ON="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 1' | grep -c . || true)"
          CFG_OFF="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 0' | grep -c . || true)"
      }
      
      output_summary() {
          local apks=0 zips=0 zip=""
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR/apks" ] && apks="$(find "$OUT_DIR/apks" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && zips="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          zip="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | sort | head -n1)"
          if [ "$zips" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '%s  (%s APK%s)' "${zip#$ROOT/}" "$apks" "$([ "$apks" = 1 ] || echo s)"
          else
              printf 'nothing built yet'
          fi
      }

- path: build.sh
  content: |
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          MODE="menu"
      fi
      
      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).
      wsl_guard
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Dispatch
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      case "$MODE" in
          menu)
              # The terminal front end. It shells out to this same script for a build,
              # so a build started from the menu is the build a user would type.
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/menu.sh"
              menu_main
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          doctor)
              if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
              ;;
      
          setup)
              banner "Setup — build tools"
              migrate_layout
              # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
              # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
              # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
              # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
              # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
              if $ASSUME_YES; then
                  ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
              else
                  ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
              fi
              exit $?
              ;;

> _Reasoning_
> Careful: `[ -n "$v" ] && TOOL_VERSION="$v"` as the last command in a sourced file — under `set -e` in build.sh, if empty the sourced line returns 1 → build.sh exits! common.sh is sourced at line "source ... common.sh" but there are more lines after? `[ -n "$v" ] && ...` inside an `if [ -f ... ]` block; if the last command of the if-block returns 1, the `if` statement returns 1, and if that's the last command of the sourced file → sourcing returns 1 → set -e kills the script. But the source isn't the last command of build.sh, so... `set -e` triggers on any command failing, not just last. Actually `set -e` triggers on any command failing, not just last. So if VERSION missing → v empty? No: if file missing, the `if` condition fails → if statement returns 0. Good. If file exists but empty, `[ -n "$v" ]` fails → if-block returns 1 → the `if` compound returns 1 → set -e aborts! Fix by using a plain if.

      func TestGuardRejectsCrossSite(t *testing.T) {
        app := &App{runner: NewRunner()}
        req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/state", nil)
        req.Header.Set("Sec-Fetch-Site", "cross-site")
        rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
      
        app.guard("GET", app.handleState).ServeHTTP(rec, req)
      
        if rec.Code != http.StatusForbidden {
          t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 403", rec.Code)
        }
      }
      
      // TestDetectCodenames checks what the Device tab offers after "Detect from
      // device": the properties that answered, in priority order, with the GSI's own
      // name kept as an alternative rather than dropped and "unknown" ignored.
      func TestDetectCodenames(t *testing.T) {
        props := map[string]string{

- path: README.md
  content: |
      Two things worth knowing before the first build:
      
      - **`src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` must be yours.** Until you replace it, the empty template is detected and left out of the APK rather than overwriting the GSI's battery and CPU data. See [docs/device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
      - **No `config.env` yet?** The first run offers the filled-in Samsung A90 5G example (`config.env.example`) or writes a placeholder that says what to edit.
      
      ## Commands
      
      | Command | Does |
      |---|---|
      | `./build.sh` | Terminal menu; a plain build when there is no terminal |
      | `./build.sh build` | Build, installing missing tools first |
      | `./build.sh setup` | Install or repair the toolchain |
      | `./build.sh doctor` | Check the toolchain, change nothing (exit 0 = ready) |
      | `./build.sh check` | Validate `config.env`, build nothing |
      | `./build.sh --dry-run` | Print every resource the config emits, build nothing |
      | `./build.sh clean` | Remove `stuff/build/` and `out/` |
      | `./build.sh clean --all` | Start over for a different device (restores templates) |
      | `./build.sh menu` | Force the menu when there is no terminal |
      
      Flags: `-y` / `--yes`, `--with-vendor-hals`, `--xiaomi-fod`, `--allow-unknown-resources`, `--force` (with `setup`), `--help`. Same words on Windows with `build.cmd`.
      
      `--dry-run` is the fast loop: it prints type, name, value and target APK for each resource without aapt2, signing or packaging.
      
      To check the project itself (scripts, resource writer, docs anchors), run `bash stuff/tests/run.sh` — this is what CI runs, and it needs no Android tools.
      
      ## Output
      
      | File | Use |
      |---|---|
      | `out/<name>-ksu.zip` | **The module.** Install in Magisk, KernelSU, KSU Next or APatch, then reboot |

- path: stuff/scripts/validate.sh
  content: |
          fi
      
          rr=$(_v_int "${DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE:-}")
          rr_peak=$(_v_int "${PEAK_REFRESH_RATE:-}")
          if [ -n "$rr_peak" ] && [ -n "$rr" ] && [ "$rr_peak" -lt "$rr" ]; then
              _v_warn "PEAK_REFRESH_RATE=${rr_peak} is lower than DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE=${rr}"
          fi
          if [ -n "${PEAK_REFRESH_RATE:-}" ] && [ -z "$rr" ] && [[ "${PEAK_REFRESH_RATE}" != *"<"* ]]; then
              _v_warn "PEAK_REFRESH_RATE is set without DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE — neither is emitted"
          fi
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Module metadata
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # These are baked into the APK and module.prop, so a wrong one is only visible
      # on the phone. Check the one value Android refuses to take as free text.
      _validate_metadata() {
          local code="${OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE:-}"
          if [ -n "$code" ] && ! [[ "$code" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
              _v_warn "OVERLAY_VERSION_CODE=\"${code}\" is not a whole number — android:versionCode must be an integer"
          fi
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Overlay identity
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      _validate_overlay() {
          if [ -z "${DEVICE_PROP_NAME:-}" ]; then
              _v_note "DEVICE_PROP_NAME is empty — the overlay is not matched to a property (applies everywhere)"
          elif [ -z "${DEVICE_PROP_VALUE:-}" ]; then
              _v_warn "DEVICE_PROP_NAME is set but DEVICE_PROP_VALUE is empty"
          fi
      
          if [ -n "${OVERLAY_PRIORITY:-}" ] && [ -n "${OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI:-}" ] \
             && [ "$OVERLAY_PRIORITY" = "$OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI" ]; then
              _v_warn "OVERLAY_PRIORITY and OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI are identical (${OVERLAY_PRIORITY}) — the SystemUI overlay must win"
          fi
      
          if [ ! -d "${ROOT:-.}/src/vendor/bin/hw" ] || \
             [ "$(ls -A "${ROOT:-.}/src/vendor/bin/hw" 2>/dev/null | grep -c .)" -eq 0 ]; then
              if [ "${HAS_VENDOR_FINGERPRINT_HAL:-false}" = "true" ] || [ "${HAS_VENDOR_VIBRATOR_HAL:-false}" = "true" ]; then
                  _v_warn "HAS_VENDOR_*_HAL is true but src/vendor/bin/hw is empty — see docs/device-extraction.md"
              fi
          fi
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Overlay-repo submission (out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip)
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The overlay repo compares android:requiredSystemPropertyValue with plain
      # string equality and rejects duplicate priorities, so a value that looks fine
      # here can make the submitted overlay inert or fail their tests/tests.sh.
      _validate_submission() {
          local prop value prio file count
          prop="${HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP:-ro.product.vendor.device}"
          value="${HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE:-${DEVICE_CODENAME:-}}"
      
          case "$value" in
              +*|-*|\**|*\**)
                  _v_warn "HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE=\"${value}\" looks like a glob, but the overlay repo compares it with exact string equality — the submitted overlay would never activate"
                  ;;
          esac
          if [ -n "${HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP:-}" ] && [ -z "$value" ]; then
              _v_warn "HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP is set but no value — set HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE (adb shell getprop ${prop})"
          fi
          if [ -z "${HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP+x}" ] && [ -n "${HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE:-}" ]; then
              _v_note "HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE is set without HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP — the default property ro.product.vendor.device is used"
          fi
          case "$prop" in
              ro.vendor.product.*)
                  _v_warn "HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP=\"${prop}\" is deprecated in the overlay repo — ro.product.vendor.device is preferred"
                  ;;
          esac
      
          # Priority collisions: the repo's tests/tests.sh fails on a duplicate.
          prio="${HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY:-}"
          if [ -n "$prio" ]; then
              file="${ROOT:-.}/stuff/scripts/data/treble-overlay-priorities.txt"
              if [ -f "$file" ]; then
                  count=$(grep -cx "$prio" "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
                  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
                      _v_warn "HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY=${prio} is already used by another overlay in the overlay repo — tests/tests.sh will reject it"
                  fi
              fi
          fi

- path: stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh
  content: |
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Entry point
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      write_hardware_overlay() { # <outdir>
          local out="$1"
          local brand model dropped modules prop value priority
      
          [ -n "$out" ] || { err "write_hardware_overlay needs an output directory"; return 2; }
      
          brand="${DEVICE_MANUFACTURER}"
          model="${DEVICE_CODENAME}"
          prop=$(hw_match_prop)
          value=$(hw_match_value)
          priority=$(hw_priority)
      
          # The repo compares exact strings: a glob (or a "±" prefix) can never match
          # and the overlay would silently stay inert.
          case "$value" in
              +*|-*|*\**)
                  warn "HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE=\"${value}\" looks like a glob, but android:requiredSystemPropertyValue is exact-matched."
                  warn "  An overlay with a wildcard never activates. Use the literal value: adb shell getprop ${prop}"
                  ;;
          esac
          case "$prop" in
              ro.vendor.product.*)
                  warn "HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP=\"${prop}\" is deprecated in the overlay repo; ro.product.vendor.device is preferred."
                  ;;
          esac
          if [ -n "$prop" ] && [ -n "$value" ]; then
              info "Submission match: ${prop} == \"${value}\" (exact)"
          else
              info "Submission match: none (always active)"
          fi
          local uses
          uses=$(hw_priority_uses "$priority")
          if [ "${uses:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              warn "Priority ${priority} is already used by ${uses} overlay(s) in the overlay repo — tests/tests.sh rejects duplicates."
              warn "  Unset HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY to let the build pick a free one, or take the number tests/tests.sh prints."
          else
              info "Submission priority: ${priority} (free in the repo snapshot)"
          fi
      
          rm -rf "$out"
          mkdir -p "$out"
          dropped="$out/.dropped"
          modules="$out/.modules"
          : > "$dropped"
          : > "$modules"
      
          # 1. Framework overlay (targets android)
          HW_FW_DIR="$out/${brand}/${model}"
          mkdir -p "$HW_FW_DIR"
          _hw_copy_resources "$RES_DIR" "$HW_FW_DIR/res" "$dropped"
          _hw_write_android_mk "$HW_FW_DIR" "$OVERLAY_NAME"
          _hw_write_manifest "$HW_FW_DIR/AndroidManifest.xml" \
              "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE" android "$priority"
          printf '\t%s \\\n' "$OVERLAY_NAME" >> "$modules"
          ok "Submission: ${brand}/${model} (${OVERLAY_NAME}, priority ${priority})"
      
          # 2. SystemUI overlay (targets com.android.systemui), when there is one
          HW_SYSUI_DIR=""
          if [ "${LINKED_SYSTEMUI:-false}" = "true" ] || { [ -z "${LINKED_SYSTEMUI:-}" ] && hw_has_systemui_resources; }; then
              HW_SYSUI_DIR="$out/${brand}/${model}-SystemUI"
              mkdir -p "$HW_SYSUI_DIR"
              _hw_copy_resources "$SYSUI_RES_DIR" "$HW_SYSUI_DIR/res" "$dropped"
              _hw_write_android_mk "$HW_SYSUI_DIR" "${OVERLAY_NAME}-systemui"
              _hw_write_manifest "$HW_SYSUI_DIR/AndroidManifest.xml" \
                  "$OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI" com.android.systemui \
                  "${HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI:-${OVERLAY_PRIORITY_SYSTEMUI:-9999}}"
              printf '\t%s-systemui \\\n' "$OVERLAY_NAME" >> "$modules"
              ok "Submission: ${brand}/${model}-SystemUI (${OVERLAY_NAME}-systemui)"
          fi
      
          # 3. Notes + overlay.mk lines
          local folders="\`${brand}/${model}\`"
          [ -n "$HW_SYSUI_DIR" ] && folders="${folders} and \`${brand}/${model}-SystemUI\`"
          _hw_write_notes "$out" "$brand" "$model" "$dropped" "$modules" "$folders"
      
          if [ -s "$dropped" ]; then
              local names
              names=$(sort -u "$dropped" | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ *$//')
              info "Dropped ${names} (the overlay repo blacklists these; the module still sets them)"
          fi
          rm -f "$dropped" "$modules"
          return 0
      }
      
      # hw_plan_row FOLDER "APK — what it overlays" — one folder of the submission.
      # The folder is the thing being created and the APK name is the thing that ends
      # up in the submission, so the folder is bold and the rest is a dim line under
      # it: on a phone that is two short lines instead of one that runs off the edge.
      hw_plan_row() {
          local line
          printf '\n    %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$2" 6 | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      print_hardware_overlay_plan() {
          ui_heading 'Submission tree'
          ui_wrap 'Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay, branch pie — one folder per overlay.' 2
          hw_plan_row "$DEVICE_MANUFACTURER/$DEVICE_CODENAME" "$OVERLAY_NAME (android)"
          if [ "${LINKED_SYSTEMUI:-false}" = "true" ] || { [ -z "${LINKED_SYSTEMUI:-}" ] && hw_has_systemui_resources; }; then
              hw_plan_row "$DEVICE_MANUFACTURER/$DEVICE_CODENAME-SystemUI" \
                  "${OVERLAY_NAME}-systemui (com.android.systemui)"
          fi
          printf '\n'
          ui_kv match "$(hw_match_prop) == \"$(hw_match_value)\"" 9
          ui_kv priority "$(hw_priority)" 9
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Standalone use: ./stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh plan  (or "write <dir>")
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
          set -e
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
          cd "$ROOT"
          source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
          case "${1:-plan}" in
              plan|write)
                  ;;
              *)
                  echo "usage: $0 [plan|write <dir>] [config.env]" >&2
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac

- path: gui/matchprop.go
  content: |
      
      // MatchCandidate is one property the submission could be matched on.
      type MatchCandidate struct {
        Prop  string `json:"prop"`
        Value string `json:"value"`
        Score int    `json:"score"`
        Zone  string `json:"zone"`
        Label string `json:"label"`
        Trust string `json:"trust"` // high, medium, low
        // Perfect means this is a pick nothing has to be argued about: the value
        // is the codename, zygote can read the property, and a GSI leaves it alone.
        // Only a perfect pick is offered as the answer; anything less and the card
        // tells the user to keep the match they already have.
        Perfect bool   `json:"perfect"`
        Why     string `json:"why"`
        Risk    string `json:"risk,omitempty"`
      }
      
      // MatchRejection is a property with a device-ish name that was ruled out, and
      // why. The reasons are the answers to the question users ask most often, so
      // they are part of the answer rather than something to work out again.
      type MatchRejection struct {
        Prop   string `json:"prop"`
        Value  string `json:"value"`
        Reason string `json:"reason"`
      }
      
      // MatchReport is what the Config tab shows: the codename it settled on, the
      // ranked candidates, the properties it refused, and how sure it is.
      type MatchReport struct {
        Serial     string           `json:"serial"`
        Model      string           `json:"model"`
        Codename   string           `json:"codename"`
        Confidence string           `json:"confidence"` // high, medium, low
        ModuleProp string           `json:"moduleProp"`
        Candidates []MatchCandidate `json:"candidates"`
        Rejected   []MatchRejection `json:"rejected"`
      }
      
      // matchProp is one entry of the fixed candidate list. zone says which partition
      // the value comes from (that is what decides GSI survival) and kind says what
      // the property holds.
      type matchProp struct {
        name string
        zone string
        kind string
      }
      
      var matchPropCandidates = []matchProp{
        {"ro.product.vendor.device", "vendor", "device"},
        {"ro.product.odm.device", "odm", "device"},
        {"ro.product.bootimage.device", "bootimage", "device"},
        {"ro.product.device", "system", "device"},
        {"ro.product.product.device", "product", "device"},
        {"ro.product.system.device", "system", "device"},
        {"ro.product.system_ext.device", "system_ext", "device"},
        {"ro.build.product", "build", "device"},
        {"ro.product.vendor.name", "vendor", "name"},
        {"ro.product.odm.name", "odm", "name"},
        {"ro.product.bootimage.name", "bootimage", "name"},
        {"ro.product.name", "product", "name"},
        {"ro.product.vendor.model", "vendor", "model"},
        {"ro.product.model", "product", "model"},
      }
      
      // zoneScore: vendor/odm/bootimage keep the OEM value when a GSI replaces
      // /system; a `ro.product.*` value is whatever is installed now.
      var zoneScore = map[string]int{
        "vendor": 40, "odm": 35, "bootimage": 35,
        "product": 25, "system": 22, "system_ext": 18, "build": 10,
      }
      
      var kindScore = map[string]int{"device": 25, "name": 12, "model": 15}
      
      // labelScore: what the SELinux area means for zygote reading it. The negative
      // numbers are the documented traps, not guesses — build_bootimage_prop and
      // build_odm_prop are refused to zygote on most GSI builds.
      var labelScore = map[string]int{
        "build_prop":           30,
        "build_vendor_prop":    30,
        "vendor_default_prop":  25,
        "default_prop":         15,
        "build_system_prop":    -20,
        "build_odm_prop":       -35,
        "build_bootimage_prop": -35,
        "bootloader_prop":      -20,

      }
      
      // DetectResult is what "Detect from device" found: the answer it would use, and
      // every other command that also had something to say.
      type DetectResult struct {
        Codename     string            `json:"codename"`
        Manufacturer string            `json:"manufacturer"`
        Model        string            `json:"model"`
        Prop         string            `json:"prop"`
        Candidates   []DetectCandidate `json:"candidates"`
      }
      
      // codenameProps is the order the codename is looked for in. The vendor
      // partition keeps the stock name on most GSIs, so it is asked first;
      // ro.product.device is near the end because on a GSI it only names the GSI
      // itself. No single property is right on every phone — which is why the answer
      // is offered with the command that produced it, and the others are one click
      // away in the UI.
      var codenameProps = []DetectCandidate{
        {Prop: "ro.product.vendor.device", Note: "vendor partition — the usual survivor on a GSI"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.odm.device", Note: "ODM partition"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.bootimage.device", Note: "boot image"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.device", Note: "system property — often the GSI's own name"},
        {Prop: "ro.build.product", Note: "legacy build.prop name"},
      }
      
      // detectCodenames asks every candidate property and keeps the answers that
      // mean something, in priority order and without duplicates. Every one is asked,
      // not just the first that answers: the ones that had a value are what "Wrong?
      // Try another command" cycles through, and that has to work without another
      // round trip to the phone.
      func detectCodenames(probe func(string) string) []DetectCandidate {
        out := []DetectCandidate{}
        seen := make(map[string]bool, len(codenameProps))
        for _, c := range codenameProps {
          value := probe(c.Prop)
          if value == "" || strings.EqualFold(value, "unknown") || seen[value] {
            continue
          }
          seen[value] = true
          out = append(out, DetectCandidate{Prop: c.Prop, Note: c.Note, Value: value})
        }
        return out
      }
      
      // handleAdbDetect asks the phone for the values the presets need, so the user
      // does not have to read one command's output and type it into another box.
      func (a *App) handleAdbDetect(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Serial string `json:"serial"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        adb := a.adbPath()
        if adb == "" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "adb is not installed yet — use \"Download platform-tools\" first")
          return
        }
        serial, err := a.deviceSerialFor(body.Serial)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        probe := func(prop string) string {
          out, err := runCapture(adb, "-s", serial, "shell", "getprop", prop)
          if err != nil {
            return ""
          }
          return strings.TrimSpace(out)
        }
      
        res := DetectResult{Candidates: []DetectCandidate{}}
        res.Manufacturer = probe("ro.product.manufacturer")
        res.Model = probe("ro.product.model")
        res.Candidates = detectCodenames(probe)
        if len(res.Candidates) > 0 {
          res.Codename = res.Candidates[0].Value
          res.Prop = res.Candidates[0].Prop
        }
      
        if res.Codename == "" && res.Manufacturer == "" && res.Model == "" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, "the phone did not answer — is it connected and authorized? (adb devices)")
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, res)
      }

        if (trust === 'high') return 'fits';
        if (trust === 'medium') return 'partial';
        return 'risky';
      }
      
      function confidenceLabel(confidence) {
        if (confidence === 'high') return 'safe pick';
        if (confidence === 'medium') return 'no perfect pick';
        return 'nothing usable';
      }
      
      function matchBody() {
        const body = el('div', 'cfg-match-body');
        matchBodyEl = body;
      
        if (matchBusy) {
          body.appendChild(el('p', 'muted small', 'asking the phone…'));
          return body;
        }
        if (matchError) body.appendChild(el('p', 'cfg-match-error', matchError));
      
        if (!matchReport) {
          const cur = { prop: cfgEntry('HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP'), value: cfgEntry('HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE') };
          if (cur.prop && cur.prop.value) {
            body.appendChild(el('p', 'muted small',
              `config.env matches on ${cur.prop.value} == "${cur.value ? cur.value.value : ''}"${cur.prop.enabled ? '' : ' — that line is commented out'}.`));
          } else {
            body.appendChild(el('p', 'muted small', 'No match property is set: the submission would be always active, which is only right for a device that has no name to match.'));
          }
          return body;
        }
      
        const rep = matchReport;
        const summary = el('div', 'cfg-match-summary');
        summary.appendChild(el('span', 'muted small', 'codename '));
        summary.appendChild(el('code', null, rep.codename || 'not found'));
        if (rep.model) summary.appendChild(el('span', 'muted small', ' · ' + rep.model));
        summary.appendChild(el('span', 'cfg-match-badge trust-' + rep.confidence, confidenceLabel(rep.confidence)));
        body.appendChild(summary);
      
        // A match condition that does not hold is invisible: the overlay enables and
        // changes nothing. So unless a property satisfies every rule, the honest
        // answer is the one that already works — the module's own property.
        if (rep.confidence !== 'high') body.appendChild(keepCurrentNote(rep));
      
        const rows = rep.candidates || [];
        for (const c of rows.slice(0, 3)) body.appendChild(matchRow(c));
        if (rows.length > 3) {
          const more = document.createElement('details');
          const rest = rows.length - 3;
          more.appendChild(el('summary', 'muted small', `${rest} more candidate${rest === 1 ? '' : 's'}`));
          for (const c of rows.slice(3)) more.appendChild(matchRow(c));
          body.appendChild(more);
        }
      
        if ((rep.rejected || []).length) {
          const ruled = document.createElement('details');
          ruled.appendChild(el('summary', 'muted small', `${rep.rejected.length} propert${rep.rejected.length === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'} ruled out`));

          body.appendChild(ruled);
        }
      
        if (rep.moduleProp) {

        return body;
      }
      
      // "Use what already works": the property the module sets itself, which cannot

          renderDetect(res.log);

          $('detect-summary').textContent = 'nothing came back: ' + err.message;
          const log = (err.data && err.data.log) || '';

  content: |
          # Overlay APKs first (an OEM's own profile usually lives there), then the
          # framework's copy. The first one that looks like a device wins; a generic
          # AOSP profile is remembered only to explain the failure.
          local apk tree generic=""
          while IFS= read -r apk; do
              [ -n "$apk" ] || continue
              tree="$(dump_power "$apk")"
              [ -n "$tree" ] || continue
              if profile_looks_real "$tree"; then
                  printf '# source: %s\n' "$apk"
                  printf '%s\n' "$tree"
                  return 0
              fi
              [ -n "$generic" ] || generic="$apk"
              note "$apk carries a generic profile (0.1 for everything, a 1 GHz-less CPU list), so it was skipped"
          done <<<"$(find "$fwdir" -type f -path '*/overlay/*.apk' 2>/dev/null | head -n 300; find "$fwdir" -type f -name 'framework-res.apk' 2>/dev/null | head -n 10)"
      
          die "no real power profile found under $fwdir${generic:+ — $generic holds the AOSP placeholder}"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Report
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      json_escape() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr -d '\000-\037' | sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g'; }
      json_list() {
          local first=1 v
          printf '['
          for v in "$@"; do
              [ "$first" -eq 1 ] || printf ','
              first=0
              printf '"%s"' "$(json_escape "$v")"
          done
          printf ']'
      }
      
      emit_json() {
          local i first=1
          printf '{'
          printf '"mode":"%s",' "$mode"
          if [ "$mode" = "device" ]; then
              printf '"device":{"serial":"%s","model":"%s","codename":"%s","rom":"%s","isGsi":%s,"width":%s,"height":%s,"density":%s},' \
                  "$(json_escape "${serial:-}")" "$(json_escape "${MODEL:-}")" \
                  "$(json_escape "${CODENAME:-}")" "$(json_escape "${rom:-}")" \
                  "$([ "${IS_GSI:-0}" -eq 1 ] && echo true || echo false)" "${W:-0}" "${H:-0}" "${DENS:-0}"
          else
              printf '"firmware":"%s",' "$(json_escape "$fwdir")"
          fi
          printf '"aapt2":"%s",' "$(json_escape "${aapt2:-}")"
          printf '"facts":['
          for i in "${!f_key[@]}"; do

      // overlays from an unpacked ROM. This side runs it, hands its JSON to the page,
      // and writes the rows the user ticks into config.env.
      //
      // Same split as the UDFPS tab on purpose: the CLI and the window then answer the
      // same question the same way, and docs/detect.md documents one command.
      type DetectDevice struct {
        Serial   string `json:"serial"`
        Model    string `json:"model"`
        Codename string `json:"codename"`
        ROM      string `json:"rom"`
        IsGSI    bool   `json:"isGsi"`

      }

        Warnings []string      `json:"warnings"`
        Notes    []string      `json:"notes"`
        Files    []DetectFile  `json:"files"`

          short_value() {
              local v="$1"
              if [ "${#v}" -gt 29 ]; then printf '%s…' "${v:0:28}"; else printf '%s' "$v"; fi
          }
      
          local -a table=()

                      if [ -z "$first" ]; then first="$i"

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Writing config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # A value read off a device ends up in config.env, which build.sh sources. Two
      # things matter: it has to stay on one line, and the shell must not expand it

      # copy of the two rules.
      probe_safe_value() {
          local v="$1"
          v="${v//$'\r'/}"
          v="${v//$'\n'/ }"
          v="${v//$'\t'/ }"

              # a colouring wrapper would otherwise leave "[31m" inside the value.
              v="$(printf '%s' "$v" | LC_ALL=C sed $'s/\033\\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]//g' | LC_ALL=C tr -d '[:cntrl:]')"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$v"
      }

- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Blocks
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ui_heading TEXT — a section title with a rule under it, sized to the window.
      ui_heading() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_rule [INDENT] — a plain separator.
      ui_rule() {
          local indent="${1:-2}" w; w=$(ui_cols)
          # One short of the window, like ui_heading: a rule that ends in the last
          # column wraps on a terminal that is exactly that wide.
          printf '%s%s%s%s\n' "$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')" "$UI_DIM" \
              "$(ui_repeat $((w - indent - 1)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_kv KEY VALUE [KEYWIDTH] — one aligned key and its value.
      # A value wider than the window (a property name, a path) moves under its key
      # and wraps there, instead of running off the edge of a phone.
      ui_kv() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="${3:-10}" pad cols line
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          printf -v pad '%*s' $((keyw - ${#key})) ''
          if [ $(( 3 + keyw + ${#value} )) -lt "$cols" ]; then
              printf '  %s%s%s  %s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$key$pad" "$UI_OFF" "$value"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$key" "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$value" 4 | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_pad TEXT WIDTH — TEXT followed by spaces up to WIDTH characters.
      #
      # printf's %-*s pads by bytes, so one `·` (three bytes) would leave a row three
      # columns short and the right border would step in once per glyph. Everything a
      # user typed — a model name, a path, a dotted list — goes through here.
      ui_pad() {
          local text="$1" width="$2" pad=""
          [ "${#text}" -lt "$width" ] && printf -v pad '%*s' $((width - ${#text})) ''
          printf '%s%s' "$text" "$pad"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_line CONTENT INNER — CONTENT padded to INNER and closed off with the
      # right border. CONTENT carries its own leading space, so the row never starts
      # hard against the border.
      ui_panel_line() {
          local content="$1" inner="$2" pad=""
          [ "${#content}" -lt "$inner" ] && printf -v pad '%*s' $((inner - ${#content})) ''
          printf '  %s%s%s%s%s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF" "$content" "$pad" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_row KEY VALUE KEYWIDTH INNER — one key/value row.

- path: stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh
  content: |
      disabled on the repo, so the PR thread is the only place to discuss it.
      
      ---
      
      ## The match condition — read this
      
      \`\`\`xml
      android:requiredSystemPropertyName="${prop}"
      android:requiredSystemPropertyValue="${value}"
      \`\`\`
      
      \`android:requiredSystemPropertyValue\` is compared with **plain string
      equality** (\`FrameworkParsingPackageUtils#checkRequiredSystemProperties\` in
      AOSP), so \`*\` and \`+\` are not wildcards: an overlay carrying
      \`+*${brand}/${model}*\` never activates. Many older overlays in the repo still
      use that form; they are inert.
      
      Therefore the value above must be **exactly** what the device reports:
      
      \`\`\`bash
      adb shell getprop ${prop}
      \`\`\`
      
      - If that prints something else, set \`HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE\` (or
        \`HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP\`) in \`config.env\` and rebuild.
      - Prefer \`ro.product.vendor.device\`: it comes from the vendor partition, so it
        survives a GSI flash and does not change between OTA builds. The full
        \`ro.vendor.build.fingerprint\` also works, but breaks on every OTA.
      - Set \`HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP=""\` to submit an overlay that is always active.
      
      ## Priority
      
      The framework overlay uses \`android:priority="${priority}"\`, which no overlay
      in the repo used when this build was made. The repo's \`tests/tests.sh\` rejects a
      duplicate and prints a free number when it runs; if it suggests another one,
      change \`HW_OVERLAY_PRIORITY\` in \`config.env\` and rebuild.
      
      $(if [ "$dropped_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      cat << EOF2
      ## Resource names that were dropped
      
      The repo's \`tests/blacklist\` forbids these, so the submission leaves them to the
      GSI (the module you build yourself still sets them):
      
      $dropped_text
      
      EOF2
      fi)
      
      ## What is in here
      
      - \`${brand}/${model}/res/\` — framework overlay resources (\`android\`)
      - \`${brand}/${model}-SystemUI/res/\` — SystemUI overlay resources, if any
      - \`res/xml/power_profile.xml\` is only included once you replace the placeholder
        in \`src/framework/res/xml/\` with your device's profile
      
      Everything is generated: edit \`config.env\` and \`src/\` in ${ROOT##*/}, then run
      \`./build.sh\` and use the new zip.
      SUBMITEOF
      }

          box.checked = detectPick[f.key] === i;

      ## Writing the values
      
      In the tab, untick anything you do not want and press **Write the ticked values**.
      Only the settings in the table above are accepted; a typo in a key or a value
      outside the panel's range is refused instead of written. The lines keep their
      place and their comments, and a commented-out `DISPLAY_CUTOUT` is switched on
      rather than duplicated — the same edit path the `config.env` form uses.
      
      The cutout path is written quoted, because it contains spaces:
      
      ```
      DISPLAY_CUTOUT="M 0,0 L 120,0 L 120,80 L 0,80 Z @dp"
      ```
      
      MIUI's own path has neither spaces nor a unit suffix
      (`M 0,0 H -29 V 118 H 29 V 0 H 0 Z`) and is written exactly as the framework
      stores it; the path is centred by `DisplayCutout`, so the negative X is correct.
      
      ## Adding another setting
      
      The script is deliberately plain: a setting is one `add_fact` call with its key,
      label, unit, value, source, confidence and detail. A new source for an existing
      setting is another call with the same key and a different `source`; the page
      shows both and the user picks. `gui/detect.go` needs the key in `detectKeys` with
      a range check, and that is all the window needs to offer it.

      }
      
      func fileExists(p string) bool {
        if p == "" {
          return false
        }
        st, err := os.Stat(p)
        return err == nil && !st.IsDir()
      }
      
      func dirExists(p string) bool {
        if p == "" {
          return false
        }
        st, err := os.Stat(p)
        return err == nil && st.IsDir()
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Reading the clone
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      type Doc struct {
        Name  string `json:"name"`
        Title string `json:"title"`
      }
      
      // listDocs reads docs/*.md from the clone. The GUI ships no copy of the manual:
      // the app is installed into a clone, so the docs it shows are the docs that
      // match the scripts it runs.
      func listDocs(root string) []Doc {
        entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(root, "docs"))
        if err != nil {
          return nil
        }
        docs := make([]Doc, 0, len(entries))
        for _, e := range entries {
          if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
            continue
          }
          docs = append(docs, Doc{Name: e.Name(), Title: docTitle(filepath.Join(root, "docs", e.Name()))})
        }
        sort.Slice(docs, func(i, j int) bool { return docs[i].Name < docs[j].Name })
        return docs
      }
      
      func docTitle(path string) string {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
        if err != nil {
          return strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(path), ".md")
        }
        for _, line := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
          line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
          if strings.HasPrefix(line, "# ") {
            return strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "# "))
          }
        }
        return strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(path), ".md")
      }
      
      // readDoc refuses anything outside docs/*.md so a crafted name cannot walk out
      // of the clone.
      func readDoc(root, name string) (string, error) {

      package main
      
      import (
        "context"
        "crypto/rand"
        "embed"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io"

        "sort"
        "strings"
        "time"
      )
      
      //go:embed ui
      var uiFiles embed.FS
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Why the UI is served at all
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The window is a webview pointed at a loopback URL. That is also what makes
      // -browser and the Termux front-end free: same HTML, same handlers, no second
      // UI to keep in sync with this one.
      //
      // The risk of a local server is that *any* page in the user's browser can POST
      // to 127.0.0.1, and these handlers start build.sh. Two things stop that:
      //
      //  1. everything lives under a random /<token>/ prefix generated at launch, and
      //     the page only learns it by being navigated to it — a cross-origin fetch
      //     cannot read our HTML, so it cannot discover the prefix;
      //  2. requests a browser marks as cross-site are refused outright.
      //
      // The listener is bound to 127.0.0.1, never 0.0.0.0, so nothing off-machine can
      // reach it at all.
      func (a *App) serve(port int) (net.Listener, string, *http.Server, error) {
        token, err := randomToken()
        if err != nil {
          return nil, "", nil, err
        }
        ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", port))
        if err != nil {
          return nil, "", nil, fmt.Errorf("could not open a loopback port: %w", err)
        }
      
        base := "/" + token
        assets, err := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui")
        if err != nil {
          return nil, "", nil, err
        }
      
        mux := http.NewServeMux()
        mux.HandleFunc(base, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
          http.Redirect(w, r, base+"/", http.StatusFound)
        })
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/state", a.guard("GET", a.handleState))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/settings", a.guard("POST", a.handleSettings))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/config", a.guard("POST", a.handleConfig))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/run", a.guard("POST", a.handleRun))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/cancel", a.guard("POST", a.handleCancel))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/log", a.guard("GET", a.handleLog))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/log", a.guard("GET", a.handleAdbLog))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/open", a.guard("POST", a.handleOpen))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/docs", a.guard("GET", a.handleDocs))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/doc", a.guard("GET", a.handleDoc))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/update", a.guard("POST", a.handleUpdate))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/config/apply", a.guard("POST", a.handleConfigApply))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/addons", a.guard("GET", a.handleAddons))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/addons/save", a.guard("POST", a.handleAddonsSave))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb", a.guard("POST", a.handleAdb))

      func randomToken() (string, error) {
        b := make([]byte, 16)
        if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
          return "", err
        }
        return hex.EncodeToString(b), nil
      }
      
      func (a *App) guard(method string, h http.HandlerFunc) http.HandlerFunc {
        return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
          if r.Method != method {
            w.Header().Set("Allow", method)
            http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
            return
          }
          if r.Header.Get("Sec-Fetch-Site") == "cross-site" {
            http.Error(w, "forbidden", http.StatusForbidden)
            return
          }
          h(w, r)
        }
      }

         a verb, ticks flags, and renders what the child prints.
      
         Three panes talk to the phone or edit files — config.env, adb and the src/
         workspace — and all of them go through the server, which owns the parsing,
         the path rules and every write. Nothing here touches the disk directly.
         --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
      
      function el(tag, cls, text) {
        const node = document.createElement(tag);
        if (cls) node.className = cls;
        if (text !== undefined) node.textContent = text;
        return node;
      }

          init.headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };

        }

          // Some failures come with useful detail (the update clash list), so keep
          // the whole payload on the error instead of only the message.
          err.data = data;
          err.status = res.status;
          throw err;
        }
        return data;
      }

      // -------------------------------------------------------------------- docs --
      function renderDocsNav() {
        const nav = $('docs-nav');
        nav.textContent = '';
      
        // Search/filter input for docs
        const searchInput = el('input', 'filter-input');
        searchInput.type = 'text';
        searchInput.placeholder = 'Search docs…';
        const noMatch = el('p', 'filter-empty', 'No docs match your search.');
        noMatch.hidden = true;
        searchInput.addEventListener('input', () => {
          const term = searchInput.value.trim().toLowerCase();
          const buttons = nav.querySelectorAll('button');
          for (const b of buttons) {
            const text = b.textContent.toLowerCase();
            b.style.display = !term || text.includes(term) ? '' : 'none';
          }
          // The message is a sibling: rewriting nav.textContent here would remove the
          // input too, leaving no way to clear a search that matched nothing.
          noMatch.hidden = [...buttons].some((b) => b.style.display !== 'none');
        });
        nav.append(searchInput, noMatch);
      
        for (const doc of state.docs || []) {
          const b = document.createElement('button');
          b.type = 'button';
          b.textContent = doc.title;
          b.className = doc.name === currentDoc ? 'is-active' : '';
          b.addEventListener('click', () => openDoc(doc.name));
          nav.appendChild(b);
        }
      }
      
      async function openDoc(name) {
        try {
          const data = await api('api/doc?name=' + encodeURIComponent(name));
          currentDoc = name;
          renderDocsNav();
          $('docs-body').innerHTML = mdToHtml(data.text);
          $('docs-body').scrollTop = 0;
        } catch (err) {
          $('docs-body').textContent = 'could not read ' + name + ': ' + err.message;
        }
      }
      
      // ------------------------------------------------------------------ device --
      const VALUE_KEYS = { codename: 'trc.codename', manufacturer: 'trc.manufacturer' };
      
      function adbReady() {
        return !!(state && state.adb && state.adb.available);

        return $(name === 'codename' ? 'adb-codename' : 'adb-manufacturer').value.trim();

      // handleAdbDevices is what the picker reads: every attached phone and its state.
      func (a *App) handleAdbDevices(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        devices, err := a.adbDevices()
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
          "devices": devices,
          "ready":   len(readyAdbDevices(devices)),
        })
      }
      
      // handleAdbInstall downloads platform-tools once. It is the only job that runs
      // inside this process, so it holds the runner's slot like a child would.
      func (a *App) handleAdbInstall(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        if err := a.adbRunner.Begin("downloading platform-tools"); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, err.Error())
          return
        }
        go func() {
          err := a.installPlatformTools(a.adbRunner.Note)
          a.adbRunner.FinishJob(err)
        }()
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, a.adbRunner.Snapshot())
      }
      
      // DetectCandidate is one property that answered with a value, and what that
      // property is. The Device tab offers them in this order.
      type DetectCandidate struct {
        Prop  string `json:"prop"`
        Note  string `json:"note"`
        Value string `json:"value"`
      }
      
      // DetectResult is what "Detect from device" found: the answer it would use, and
      // every other command that also had something to say.
      type DetectResult struct {
        Codename     string            `json:"codename"`
        Manufacturer string            `json:"manufacturer"`
        Model        string            `json:"model"`
        Prop         string            `json:"prop"`
        Candidates   []DetectCandidate `json:"candidates"`
      }
      
      // codenameProps is the order the codename is looked for in. The vendor
      // partition keeps the stock name on most GSIs, so it is asked first;
      // ro.product.device is near the end because on a GSI it only names the GSI
      // itself. No single property is right on every phone — which is why the answer
      // is offered with the command that produced it, and the others are one click
      // away in the UI.
      var codenameProps = []DetectCandidate{
        {Prop: "ro.product.vendor.device", Note: "vendor partition — the usual survivor on a GSI"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.odm.device", Note: "ODM partition"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.bootimage.device", Note: "boot image"},
        {Prop: "ro.product.device", Note: "system property — often the GSI's own name"},
        {Prop: "ro.build.product", Note: "legacy build.prop name"},
      }
      
      // detectCodenames asks every candidate property and keeps the answers that
      // mean something, in priority order and without duplicates. Every one is asked,
      // not just the first that answers: the ones that had a value are what "Wrong?
      // Try another command" cycles through, and that has to work without another
      // round trip to the phone.
      func detectCodenames(probe func(string) string) []DetectCandidate {
        out := []DetectCandidate{}
        seen := make(map[string]bool, len(codenameProps))
        for _, c := range codenameProps {
          value := probe(c.Prop)
          if value == "" || strings.EqualFold(value, "unknown") || seen[value] {
            continue
          }
          seen[value] = true
          out = append(out, DetectCandidate{Prop: c.Prop, Note: c.Note, Value: value})
        }
        return out
      }
      
      // handleAdbDetect asks the phone for the values the presets need, so the user
      // does not have to read one command's output and type it into another box.
      func (a *App) handleAdbDetect(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Serial string `json:"serial"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        adb := a.adbPath()
        if adb == "" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "adb is not installed yet — use \"Download platform-tools\" first")
          return
        }
        serial, err := a.deviceSerialFor(body.Serial)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        probe := func(prop string) string {
          out, err := runCapture(adb, "-s", serial, "shell", "getprop", prop)
          if err != nil {
            return ""
          }
          return strings.TrimSpace(out)
        }

        res.Manufacturer = probe("ro.product.manufacturer")
        res.Model = probe("ro.product.model")
        res.Candidates = detectCodenames(probe)
        if len(res.Candidates) > 0 {
          res.Codename = res.Candidates[0].Value
          res.Prop = res.Candidates[0].Prop
        }
      
        if res.Codename == "" && res.Manufacturer == "" && res.Model == "" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadGateway, "the phone did not answer — is it connected and authorized? (adb devices)")
