```
- path: build.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay Creator
      # =============================================================================
      # One command for everything. With a terminal attached it opens the menu, which
      # reaches every tool the desktop app has; with an argument it does exactly that
      # one thing, as before.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 the menu (on a terminal); otherwise: build
      #   ./build.sh menu            the menu, even without a terminal
      #   ./build.sh build           build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
      #   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
      #   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
      #   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
      #   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
      #   ./build.sh fod-build       rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper (maintainers)
      #   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
      #   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
      #
      #   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
      #   -V, --version              print the version
      #   -h, --help                 this help
      #
      # On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
      # Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
      # drive — see docs/windows.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      # pipefail matters here: most build steps run a tool and parse its output in a
      # pipeline (`aapt2 dump ... | sed | awk`). Without it a failed tool still exits
      # 0 through the pipeline and the build carries on with empty input.
      set -eo pipefail
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Project root
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      # Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
      # not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
      if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
      fi
      export ROOT
      cd "$ROOT"
      
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"
      
      # Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
      tools_on_path
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Options
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MODE="build"
      REQUESTED=$#
      CHECK_MODE=false
      DRY_RUN=false
      ASSUME_YES=false
      FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
      CLEAN_ALL=false
      FORCE_RES=""
      ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false
      
      usage() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
          echo "    (none)             The menu (on a terminal), otherwise a build"
          echo "    menu               The menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes"
          echo "    build              Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
          echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
          echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
          echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
          echo "    fod-build          Rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper from its Go source"
          echo "    clean              Remove build output"
          echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --xiaomi-fod           Include the Xiaomi FOD helper (HBM + HIDL touch mode) in the module"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    -V, --version          Print the version"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
          echo ""
      }
      
      for arg in "$@"; do
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              fod-build|--fod-build) MODE="fodbuild" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --xiaomi-fod)   XIAOMI_FOD=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              -V|--version)   echo "Treble RRO Creator ${TOOL_VERSION}"; exit 0 ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # No arguments and a terminal to talk on: the menu. Everything scripted passes
      # a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          MODE="menu"
      fi
      
      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).
      wsl_guard
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Dispatch
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      case "$MODE" in
          menu)
              # The terminal front end. It shells out to this same script for a build,
              # so a build started from the menu is the build a user would type.
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/menu.sh"
              menu_main
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          doctor)
              if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
              ;;
      
          setup)
              banner "Setup — build tools"
              migrate_layout
              # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
              # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
              # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
              # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
              # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
              if $ASSUME_YES; then
                  ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
              else
                  ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
              fi
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          check)
              # Config validation only: no tools, no output.
              CHECK_MODE=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          fodbuild)
              # Maintainers only: the shipped helper is prebuilt on purpose, so no
              # user path reaches Go for it.
              bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/fod-build.sh"
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          clean)
              migrate_layout
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/clean.sh"
              ;;
      
          dryrun)
              # Needs config.env and the resource generators, no toolchain: the point
              # is to see the plan in seconds.
              DRY_RUN=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          build)
              # Move any files left in the old top-level layout into src/.
```

```
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # menu.sh — the terminal front end
      # =============================================================================
      # The desktop app and this file drive the same tools: the device probes, the
      # addon catalog, the match-property ranking and build.sh's own verbs. The goal
      # is that a phone with a terminal (Termux, ssh, a server) gets the same answers
      # as the window, without a GUI toolkit.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 opens this (when stdin is a terminal)
      #   ./build.sh menu            opens this even when stdin is not a terminal
      #   bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh same thing, standalone
      #
      # Every action shells out to the real entry point — `build.sh build`,
      # `device-probe.sh --write`, `addons.sh set` — so there is exactly one
      # implementation of each step and the menu cannot drift from the app.
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
          . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"

      # Small things

      # A width-aware rule under a section title. Every screen used to draw a fixed
      # 58-character one, which wrapped onto a second line on a phone.
      hr() { ui_rule 2; }

      # callers can leave the menu instead of looping forever.
      menu_read() {
          local prompt="${1:-} " answer=""
          printf '%s' "$prompt"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              return 1
          fi
          MENU_ANSWER="$answer"
          return 0
      }
      
      # Wait for Enter between screens, unless stdin is not a terminal.
      pause_menu() {
          [ -t 0 ] || return 0
          printf '\n  %s ' "Press Enter to go back"
          read -r _ || true
          printf '\n'
      }
```

```
      adb_device_resolve() {

          [ -n "$choice" ] || return 1

      # installing platform-tools only adds a binary that still has nothing to talk to.
      #
      # With root, the same commands the probes send over `adb shell` run natively —
      # getprop, cmd overlay, wm size/density, dumpsys and reads of /vendor — so local
      # mode is not a smaller detector, it is the same one with a shorter cable. Root
      # is not optional: an app UID is refused `cmd`, `dumpsys` and most /vendor files.
      #
      # DEVICE_LOCAL=1 selects it, DEVICE_ROOT_CMD says how to escalate, and the
      # probe's `serial` becomes "local" so nothing tries `adb -s local`.
      
      device_is_termux() {
```

```
      adb_pick_device() {
          local adb="$1" want="$2" prog="$3"
          local attached ready ready_count state serial sleeping waited=0
      
          adb_device_list "$adb" || {
              printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-adb did not answer}" >&2
              return 1
          }
          attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
      
          # Wireless adb and a phone that was just plugged in show "connecting" for a
          # moment. Waiting a couple of seconds turns that into the phone the user
          # means, instead of "nothing is ready" and a retry they have to time.
          while [ -n "$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "connecting"')" ] && [ "$waited" -lt 25 ]; do
              sleep 0.2
              waited=$((waited + 1))
              adb_device_list "$adb" || break
              attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
          done
      
          ready="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "device"')"
          ready_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
      
          serial=""
          if [ -n "$want" ]; then
              # An explicit serial is used as typed, but it still has to be attached:
              # otherwise adb's own "device not found" is the only explanation the
              # user gets, with no hint about what is actually plugged in.
              state="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s { print $2; exit }')"
              case "$state" in
                  device) serial="$want" ;;
                  '')
                      printf '%s: %s is not attached.\n' "$prog" "$want" >&2
                      ;;
                  *)
                      printf '%s: %s is attached but %s.\n' "$prog" "$want" "$state" >&2
                      ;;
              esac
              if [ -z "$serial" ]; then
                  if [ -n "$attached" ]; then
                      printf 'Attached devices:\n' >&2
                      printf '%s\n' "$attached" | adb_device_table >&2
                      adb_device_advice "$attached" >&2
                  else
                      [ -z "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-}" ] || printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" >&2
                      printf '%s: %s is not attached — plug the phone in and allow USB debugging.\n' "$prog" "$want" >&2
                  fi
                  # Waiting is the point here: the phone was named but is not ready
                  # yet (just plugged in, or its debugging prompt is still on screen).
                  # Both resolve in seconds, so wait rather than fail and be re-run.
                  if adb_device_wait "$adb" "$prog"; then
                      attached="$ADB_DEVICES"
                      ready="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk '$2 == "device"')"
                      ready_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | grep -c . || true)"
                      state="$(printf '%s\n' "$attached" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s { print $2; exit }')"
                      [ "$state" = "device" ] && serial="$want"
                      # The serial that came up may not be the one typed (a phone that
                      # was off reports a new one), so a single ready device is taken
                      # as the one meant.
                      if [ -z "$serial" ] && [ "$ready_count" -eq 1 ]; then
                          serial="$(printf '%s\n' "$ready" | awk '{print $1}' | head -n1)"
                      fi
                  fi
                  if [ -z "$serial" ]; then
                      printf '%s: %s did not become ready.\n' "$prog" "$want" >&2
                      return 1
                  fi
              fi
          elif [ "$ready_count" -eq 0 ]; then
              [ -z "${ADB_DEVICES_NOTE:-}" ] || printf '%s: %s\n' "$prog" "$ADB_DEVICES_NOTE" >&2
              if [ -n "$attached" ]; then
                  printf '%s: no device is ready to talk to:\n' "$prog" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$attached" | adb_device_table >&2
              else
                  printf '%s: no device in adb devices — plug the phone in and allow USB debugging.\n' "$prog" >&2

              [ -z "$sleeping" ] || printf '%s: using %s; not ready: %s\n' "$prog" "$serial" "${sleeping% }" >&2
          else
              # Several phones. Ask when there is a terminal to ask on; never guess,
              # because picking the wrong one is how the wrong phone gets written to.
              if [ ! -t 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s: %d devices are ready:\n' "$prog" "$ready_count" >&2
                  printf '%s\n' "$ready" | adb_device_table >&2
                  printf '%s: choose one with --device SERIAL\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
              if ! serial="$(adb_device_choose "$ready")"; then
                  printf '%s: no device chosen.\n' "$prog" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
          fi
      
          # The list is a snapshot; this is the check that adb can actually open it.
          adb_device_alive "$adb" "$serial"
          case $? in
              0) ;;
              124)
                  printf '%s: %s is listed as ready but adb did not answer within 10s — run adb kill-server.\n' "$prog" "$serial" >&2
                  return 1
                  ;;
              *)
                  printf '%s: %s is listed as ready but did not answer get-state — replug it.\n' "$prog" "$serial" >&2
                  return 1
                  ;;
          esac
          DEVICE_SERIAL="$serial"
          return 0
      }
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay)
# =============================================================================
# Writes what Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay expects, from the same resources
# this project compiles into a module. TrebleDroid/vendor_hardware_overlay is
# the upstream it continues; the tree is identical, so a PR there works too.
#
#   <brand>/<model>/AndroidManifest.xml
#   <brand>/<model>/Android.mk
#   <brand>/<model>/res/values/*, res/values-land/*, res/xml/*
#   <brand>/<model>-SystemUI/…            (when src/systemui has resources)
#   _submission/HOW-TO-SUBMIT.md          (steps, checklist, what changed)
#   _submission/overlay.mk.lines          (the PRODUCT_PACKAGES lines to add)
#
# That tree is packed into out/<overlay>-hardware-overlay.zip by build.sh; a
# maintainer merges it into the repo, the GSI builds it, and the device gets the
# values without installing a module.
#
# Differences from the module build, on purpose:
#
#   * The match condition targets a property that exists on a stock device.
#     A module is matched by persist.sys.overlay.<codename>, which this project
#     sets itself at boot — a preinstalled overlay never sees it. So the
#     submission gates on ro.product.vendor.device (exact) by default.
#
#   * Resource names on the repo's blacklist (tests/blacklist) are dropped.
#     Those are user-preference resources the repo refuses to let an overlay
#     force; keeping them fails the repo's own test script.
#
#   * android:requiredSystemPropertyValue is compared with plain string
#     equality (AOSP FrameworkParsingPackageUtils#checkRequiredSystemProperties),
#     so no "*" or "+" globs: the value must be what the device reports.
#
# Sourced by build.sh (common.sh loaded, config.env sourced, identity derived).
# Standalone, with an optional config file (default: ./config.env):
#
#   ./stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh plan [config.env]  what would be written
#   ./stuff/scripts/hardware-overlay.sh write <dir> [config.env] write the tree
# =============================================================================

# Sourced by build.sh, or run directly for the standalone commands below.
if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" != "$0" ] && [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
    echo "This is an internal build module — run ./build.sh instead." >&2
    return 1 2>/dev/null || exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The overlay repo's rules
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tests/blacklist of Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay (identical to upstream
# TrebleDroid's): resources an overlay may not define (they are user preferences
# or would break the device). A submission that defines one fails tests/tests.sh.
HW_BLACKLIST_ARGS=(
    config_useRoundIcon
    config_swipe_up_gesture_setting_available
    config_cameraDoubleTapPowerGestureEnabled
    config_cellBroadcastAppLinks
    config_doublePressOnPowerBehavior
    config_dozeComponent
    config_enableAutoPowerModes
    config_enableMultiUserUI
    config_mainBuiltInDisplayIsRound
    config_multiuserMaximumUsers
    config_screen_magnification_multi_tap_adjustment
    config_swipe_up_gesture_default
    config_allowAllRotations
    config_volumeAdjustmentForRemoteGroupSessions
    config_unplugTurnsOnScreen
)
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# match-prop.sh — which property should the submitted overlay match on?
# =============================================================================
# The overlay repo compares android:requiredSystemPropertyName/Value with plain
# string equality, and getting it wrong is silent: the overlay installs, `cmd
# overlay list` shows it enabled, and nothing changes. This reads the phone and
# ranks every property the submission could use, saying what each one is
# gambling on.
#
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh                  # connected device, then ask
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --write          # take the answer it trusts
#   bash stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh --json           # for scripts
#
#   --device SERIAL   with more than one phone attached
#   --device local    read this phone directly (Termux, needs root)
#   --adb PATH        adb is looked up on PATH and in stuff/tools/platform-tools
#   --values FILE --labels FILE   rank saved `getprop` / `getprop -Z` output
#                                 instead of asking a phone (tests, offline)
#
# Two rules decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable without
# root: zygote has to be able to read the property (`getprop -Z` prints the
# SELinux area; build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps),
# and the value has to survive what is installed (vendor, odm and bootimage keep
# the OEM value under a GSI; /system, /product and /system_ext do not). When no
# property satisfies both, this says so instead of picking one — a match that
# never holds is invisible.
#
# The same ranking lives in the desktop app (gui/matchprop.go). Change one,
# change the other.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

# adb is a Windows binary under Git Bash: without this its /system/... arguments
# are rewritten into C:/Program Files/Git/system/... before adb ever sees them.
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1

ROOT="${ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
. "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
. "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/ui.sh"

adb="${ADB:-}"
serial=""
want_json=0
want_write=0
assume_yes=0
values_file=""
labels_file=""

usage() {
    sed -n '3,31p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
}

die() { printf 'match-prop: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --device) serial="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --adb) adb="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
```

```
      # Whether adb can see a ready device right now, without the 120s wait: that wait
      # is for a cable being plugged in, and in Termux there is nothing to plug in.
      adb_device_ready_now() {
          local adb="$1" want="${2:-}"
          adb_device_list "$adb" 25 || return 1
          if [ -n "$want" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES" | awk -v s="$want" '$1 == s && $2 == "device"' | grep -q .
          else
              printf '%s\n' "$ADB_DEVICES" | awk '$2 == "device"' | grep -q .
          fi
      }
      
      # Where adb is. A probe's `--adb PATH` (in $adb before this file is sourced)
      # wins, then PATH, then the copy the toolchain installs. Defined here rather
      # than in each probe so device_connect does not depend on them defining it.
      adb="${adb:-}"
      resolve_adb() {
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          adb="$(command -v adb 2>/dev/null || true)"
          [ -n "$adb" ] && return 0
          for adb in "${ROOT:-.}/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb" "${ROOT:-.}/stuff/tools/platform-tools/adb.exe"; do
              [ -x "$adb" ] && return 0
          done
          adb=""
          return 1
      }

          fi
```

```json
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# =============================================================================\n# install-module.sh — put the built module on the phone, reboot, check it\n# =============================================================================\n# Building ends with a zip in out/ and four lines of instructions. This does the\n# part people get wrong: copy the zip over, hand it to the root manager that is\n# actually installed (ksud for KernelSU/KSU Next, magisk for Magisk), reboot,\n# wait for the phone to come back, and then report whether the overlay really is\n# mounted and enabled — the three things \"did it work?\" means.\n#\n#   ./build.sh install                  # the connected phone\n#   ./build.sh install --no-reboot      # install, leave the reboot to you\n#   ./build.sh install --device SERIAL  # more than one phone attached\n#   ./build.sh install --zip PATH       # a module other than the newest build\n#\n#   Standalone: bash stuff/scripts/install-module.sh [the same options]\n#\n# In Termux the zip is installed on this phone directly (root, no adb) and the\n# script stops after the install: rebooting the machine the script runs on\n# cannot be followed by a verification pass.\n#\n# Verification is read-only: /data/adb/modules/<id> must exist with no `disable`\n# or `remove` file, and `cmd overlay list` must show the package as enabled.\n# =============================================================================\n\nset -uo pipefail\n\n# adb on Windows is a Git Bash binary: /sdcard/... would be rewritten into a\n# Windows path before adb saw it.\nexport MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1\n\nROOT=\"${ROOT:-$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../..\" && pwd)}\"\n. \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh\"\n. \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh\"\n\nwant_serial=\"${DEVICE_SERIAL:-}\"\nzip_path=\"\"\ndo_reboot=1\ndo_verify=1\n\nusage() {\n    sed -n '3,23p' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\{0,1\\}//'\n}\n\ndie() { err \"$1\"; return 1; }\n\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --device) want_serial=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --zip) zip_path=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --no-reboot) do_reboot=0; shift ;;\n        --no-verify) do_verify=0; shift ;;\n        -y|--yes) do_reboot=1; shift ;;\n        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;\n        *) die \"unknown option: $1 (try --help)\"; exit 2 ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\n# The module id and package name are derived, not typed: the same function the\n# build uses, from the same config.env, so what is installed is what was built.\n[ -f \"$ROOT/config.env\" ] && . \"$ROOT/config.env\"\nderive_overlay_identity >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n\nmodule_id=\"${OVERLAY_NAME:-}\"\noverlay_pkg=\"${OVERLAY_PACKAGE:-}\"\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Which zip\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ninstall_find_zip() {\n    if [ -n \"$zip_path\" ]; then\n        [ -f \"$zip_path\" ] || { die \"no such file: $zip_path\"; return 1; }\n        printf '%s' \"$zip_path\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    if [ -n \"$module_id\" ] && [ -f \"$ROOT/out/${module_id}-ksu.zip\" ]; then\n        printf '%s' \"$ROOT/out/${module_id}-ksu.zip\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    # A clean checkout builds a different device name than the config says; the\n    # newest -ksu.zip is still the thing the user just built.\n    local newest\n    newest=\"$(ls -t \"$ROOT\"/out/*-ksu.zip 2>/dev/null | head -n1)\"\n    if [ -n \"$newest\" ]; then\n        warn \"no zip for ${module_id:-this config} — using $(basename \"$newest\")\"\n        printf '%s' \"$newest\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    die \"nothing to install: out/ has no -ksu.zip. Run ./build.sh build first.\"\n    return 1\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Talking to the phone\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Root on the phone: local mode is already root, adb goes through su. One place,\n# because every install and every check needs it.\ninstall_root() {\n    local cmd=\"$1\"\n    if [ \"${DEVICE_LOCAL:-0}\" = 1 ]; then\n        device_local_run \"$cmd\" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r'\n    else\n        \"$adb\" ${serial:+-s \"$serial\"} shell \"su -c $(sh_quote \"$cmd\")\" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r'\n    fi\n}\n\n# The manager that will take the zip. KernelSU and KSU Next ship ksud; APatch's\n# apd takes the same `module install` arguments; Magisk uses --install-module.\n# Asked in one root call so the su prompt happens once.\ninstall_manager() {\n    local have\n    have=\"$(install_root 'for b in ksud magisk apd; do command -v $b >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo \"have:$b\"; done')\"\n    case \"$have\" in\n        *have:ksud*) printf 'ksud' ;;\n        *have:apd*)  printf 'apd' ;;\n        *have:magisk*) printf 'magisk' ;;\n        *) printf '' ;;\n    esac\n}\n\n# Where the zip lives on the phone. /sdcard/Download is the folder every manager\n# app browses, and the one the manual instructions in the build summary use.\ninstall_remote_path() {\n    printf '/sdcard/Download/%s' \"$(basename \"$1\")\"\n}\n\n# adb push, but bounded: adb has no timeout and a wedged server would hang the\n# script with nothing on screen.\ninstall_push() {\n    local local_zip=\"$1\" remote=\"$2\" dir status\n    dir=\"$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' \"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/install.$$\")\"\n    mkdir -p \"$dir\" 2>/dev/null\n    \"$adb\" ${serial:+-s \"$serial\"} shell \"mkdir -p /sdcard/Download\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    adb_device_exec 1200 \"$dir/push\" \"$adb\" ${serial:+-s \"$serial\"} push \"$local_zip\" \"$remote\"\n    status=$?\n    cat \"$dir/push.err\" >&2 2>/dev/null || true\n    rm -rf \"$dir\"\n    return \"$status\"\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Reboot, then wait for the phone to be up again\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Waiting on sys.boot_completed rather than on `adb wait-for-device`: the device\n# node comes back long before the framework is ready, and the checks below read\n# the overlay service, which only answers after boot_completed.\ninstall_wait_boot() {\n    local limit=\"${1:-240}\" waited=0 state\n    while [ \"$waited\" -lt \"$limit\" ]; do\n        sleep 2\n        waited=$((waited + 2))\n        state=\"$(\"$adb\" ${serial:+-s \"$serial\"} shell getprop sys.boot_completed 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r\\n')\"\n        if [ \"$state\" = 1 ]; then\n            return 0\n        fi\n        if [ $((waited % 20)) -eq 0 ]; then\n            info \"still booting — ${waited}s of ${limit}s\"\n        fi\n    done\n    return 1\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Did it work?\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Three separate answers, because they fail independently: the module may be\n# missing (wrong manager), present but disabled (manager's \"enabled\" switch), or\n# present and enabled while the overlay itself did not attach (a bad resource,\n# a mount system that did not mount it).\ninstall_verify() {\n    local fails=0 mod_dir disable_line overlay_line\n\n    mod_dir=\"$(install_root \"ls -d /data/adb/modules/${module_id} 2>/dev/null | head -n1\")\"\n    if [ -n \"$mod_dir\" ]; then\n        ok \"module /data/adb/modules/${module_id} is present\"\n        disable_line=\"$(install_root \"ls /data/adb/modules/${module_id}/disable 2>/dev/null\")\"\n        if [ -n \"$disable_line\" ]; then\n            warn \"the module is disabled in the manager — enable it and reboot\"\n            fails=$((fails + 1))\n        else\n            ok \"it is enabled (no disable or remove flag)\"\n        fi\n    else\n        err \"no /data/adb/modules/${module_id} — the install did not land\"\n        info \"Open your root manager and install out/$(basename \"$1\") by hand, or check that the manager is supported.\"\n        fails=$((fails + 1))\n    fi\n\n    if [ -n \"$overlay_pkg\" ]; then\n        overlay_line=\"$(device_sh \"cmd overlay list | grep -F ${overlay_pkg} | head -n1\")\"\n        case \"$overlay_line\" in\n            \\[x\\]*)\n                ok \"overlay ${overlay_pkg} is registered and enabled\"\n                ;;\n            \\[*\\]*)\n                warn \"overlay ${overlay_pkg} is registered but not enabled:\"\n                printf '      %s\\n' \"$overlay_line\"\n                info \"Enable it: adb shell su -c 'cmd overlay enable ${overlay_pkg}'\"\n                fails=$((fails + 1))\n                ;;\n            *)\n                err \"overlay ${overlay_pkg} is not in the overlay list\"\n                info \"The module is installed but did not mount. KernelSU/KSU Next needs Magic Mount (not OverlayFS) — see docs/how-it-works.md.\"\n                fails=$((fails + 1))\n                ;;\n        esac\n    fi\n\n    if [ \"$fails\" -eq 0 ]; then\n        ok \"the overlay is live — reboot once more after changing values, then hard-reboot if a value sticks at the old one\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    warn \"${fails} check(s) did not pass — details above\"\n    return 1\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Main\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\ninstall_main() {\n    local zip local_zip remote manager confirm_reboot\n\n    zip=\"$(install_find_zip)\" || return 1\n    [ -f \"$zip\" ] || return 1\n    local_zip=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$zip\")\" && pwd)/$(basename \"$zip\")\"\n\n    step \"Install the module\"\n    ui_kv \"Module\" \"$(basename \"$local_zip\")\" 10\n    ui_kv \"Device\" \"${module_id:-unknown}\" 10\n    printf '\\n'\n\n    # Termux, not adb: this phone is the machine, so nothing is pushed.\n    if device_is_termux && [ -z \"$want_serial\" ] && ! adb_device_ready_now \"${adb:-adb}\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        if ! device_local_begin \"install-module.sh\"; then\n            die \"root is needed to install a module on this phone\"\n            return 1\n        fi\n        manager=\"$(install_manager)\"\n        if [ -z \"$manager\" ]; then\n            die \"no ksud, apd or magisk on this phone — install the zip from your root manager's Modules screen\"\n            return 1\n        fi\n        # Root can read Termux's home, so the zip is installed where it sits.\n        info \"installing with ${manager} (no adb involved)\"\n        case \"$manager\" in\n            magisk) install_root \"magisk --install-module $(sh_quote \"$local_zip\")\" ;;\n            *)      install_root \"${manager} module install $(sh_quote \"$local_zip\")\" ;;\n        esac\n        ok \"installed — reboot this phone, then open the WebUI or run ./build.sh doctor to check it\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n\n    resolve_adb || { die \"adb was not found — install platform-tools (./build.sh doctor says where)\"; return 1; }\n    adb_pick_device \"$adb\" \"$want_serial\" \"install-module.sh\" || return 1\n    info \"using ${serial}\"\n\n    remote=\"$(install_remote_path \"$local_zip\")\"\n    info \"copying to ${remote}\"\n    if ! install_push \"$local_zip\" \"$remote\"; then\n        die \"the copy failed — is the phone still connected? (adb devices)\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n\n    manager=\"$(install_manager)\"\n    case \"$manager\" in\n        ksud|apd)\n            info \"installing with ${manager}\"\n            if ! install_root \"${manager} module install ${remote}\" | sed 's/^/    /'; then\n                die \"${manager} refused the zip\"\n                return 1\n            fi\n            ;;\n        magisk)\n            info \"installing with magisk\"\n            if ! install_root \"magisk --install-module ${remote}\" | sed 's/^/    /'; then\n                die \"magisk refused the zip\"\n                return 1\n            fi\n            ;;\n        *)\n            warn \"no ksud, apd or magisk on the phone — the zip is at ${remote}\"\n            info \"Open your root manager → Modules → Install from storage and pick it.\"\n            return 1\n            ;;\n    esac\n    ok \"installed\"\n\n    if [ \"$do_reboot\" = 0 ]; then\n        info \"reboot when you are ready, then check: ./build.sh install --no-install\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then\n        confirm \"Reboot now and check the overlay when it comes back? [Y/n] \" y || {\n            info \"not rebooting — reboot yourself, then verify with: adb shell cmd overlay list | grep ${overlay_pkg}\"\n            return 0\n        }\n    fi\n\n    info \"rebooting\"\n    \"$adb\" ${serial:+-s \"$serial\"} reboot >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    # The phone drops off adb for a few seconds; asking it to come back first\n    # keeps the boot wait from reading an empty shell.\n    \"$adb\" ${serial:+-s \"$serial\"} wait-for-device >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    if ! install_wait_boot 240; then\n        die \"the phone did not finish booting within 240s — plug it in and watch it, then check by hand\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    ok \"booted\"\n\n    [ \"$do_verify\" = 1 ] || return 0\n    install_verify \"$local_zip\"\n}\n\ninstall_main"
```

```
- path: build.sh
  content: |
          echo ""
      }
      
      # Options that only `install` understands are collected here and handed to
      # install-module.sh, so the entry point keeps one parser.
      INSTALL_EXTRA=()
      
      while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
          arg="$1"
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              install)        MODE="install" ;;
              --device|--adb|--zip)
                  INSTALL_EXTRA+=("$arg" "${2:-}")
                  shift ;;
              --no-reboot|--no-verify)
                  INSTALL_EXTRA+=("$arg") ;;
              fod-build|--fod-build) MODE="fodbuild" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --xiaomi-fod)   XIAOMI_FOD=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              -V|--version)   echo "Treble RRO Creator ${TOOL_VERSION}"; exit 0 ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # No arguments and a terminal to talk on: the menu. Everything scripted passes
      # a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          MODE="menu"

      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).

              # The terminal front end. It shells out to this same script for a build,
              # so a build started from the menu is the build a user would type.
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/menu.sh"
              menu_main
```

```
              ui_item 7 'Xiaomi FOD' "$fod_state · HBM + touch-panel FOD mode for Xiaomi UDFPS" 11
```

```
      function renderRunState() {
        const v = currentVerb();
        const ready = state && state.cloneValid && state.bashValid;
      
        // The two consoles keep separate streams and separate buffers, but they share
        // one job slot on the server: both write into the same clone, so a pull and a
        // build must never overlap.
        $('run').disabled = !ready || running || adbRunning || !v;
        $('stop').disabled = !running;
        $('run').textContent = v ? `Run ${v.label.toLowerCase()}` : 'Run';
      
        const flags = v ? [...checkedFlags].filter((f) => v.flags && v.flags.includes(f)) : [];
        const cmd = v ? `build.sh ${v.arg}${flags.length ? ' ' + flags.join(' ') : ''} -y` : '';
        $('run').title = v ? `runs: bash --noprofile --norc ./${cmd}` : '';
      
        for (const input of $('flags').querySelectorAll('input')) input.disabled = running;
        for (const b of $('verbs').querySelectorAll('.verb')) b.disabled = running;
        $('adb-run').disabled = running || adbRunning || !adbReady();
        $('adb-run').title = running ? 'a build is running — one job at a time' : '';
        $('adb-stop').disabled = !adbRunning;
      
        // One job at a time: a second preset clicked mid-run would be refused by the
        // server, and the panel under the command still running would end up with the
        // refusal in it. Blocked-for-needs is remembered by renderPresets, which is
        // what reads the codename and the adb install state.
        for (const b of $('adb-presets').querySelectorAll('button.preset')) {
          if (running || adbRunning) b.disabled = true;
          else b.disabled = b.dataset.blocked === '1';
        }
      }
      
      // -------------------------------------------------------------- last build --
      // The list of what out/ holds is only interesting right after a build, so it
      // sits folded at the bottom of the pane. renderOut keeps the summary line
      // current either way, and a finished build opens it once.
      function renderOut() {
        const box = $('out');
        const summary = $('out-summary');
        box.textContent = '';
      
        const files = state.out || [];
        if (files.length === 0) {
          summary.textContent = state.cloneValid ? 'nothing in out/ yet' : 'no clone selected';
          box.appendChild(el('span', 'muted', summary.textContent));
          return;
        }
      
        let newest = 0;
        let biggest = 0;
        for (const f of files) {
          if (f.mod > newest) newest = f.mod;
          if (f.size > biggest) biggest = f.size;
        }
        const when = ago(newest);
        summary.textContent = `${when} · ${files.length} file${files.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
        summary.title = 'built ' + new Date(newest * 1000).toLocaleString();
      
        for (const f of files) {
          const row = el('div', 'out-item');
          row.append(el('span', null, f.name), el('span', null, `${bytes(f.size)} · ${ago(f.mod)}`));
          box.appendChild(row);
        }
      }
      
      function bytes(n) {
        if (n > 1 << 20) return (n / (1 << 20)).toFixed(1) + ' MB';
        if (n > 1 << 10) return (n / (1 << 10)).toFixed(0) + ' kB';
        return n + ' B';
      }
      
      function ago(unixSeconds) {
        const s = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000 - unixSeconds));
        if (s < 60) return 'just now';
        if (s < 3600) return Math.floor(s / 60) + ' min ago';
        if (s < 86400) return Math.floor(s / 3600) + ' h ago';
        return Math.floor(s / 86400) + ' d ago';
      }
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay Creator
# =============================================================================
# One command for everything. With a terminal attached it opens the menu, which
# reaches every tool the desktop app has; with an argument it does exactly that
# one thing, as before.
#
#   ./build.sh                 the menu (on a terminal); otherwise: build
#   ./build.sh menu            the menu, even without a terminal
#   ./build.sh build           build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
#   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
#   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
#   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
#   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
#   ./build.sh fod-build       rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper (maintainers)
#   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
#   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
#
#   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
#   -V, --version              print the version
#   -h, --help                 this help
#
# On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
# Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
# drive — see docs/windows.md.
# =============================================================================

# pipefail matters here: most build steps run a tool and parse its output in a
# pipeline (`aapt2 dump ... | sed | awk`). Without it a failed tool still exits
# 0 through the pipeline and the build carries on with empty input.
set -eo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project root
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
# not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
fi
export ROOT
cd "$ROOT"

source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"

# Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
tools_on_path

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Options
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MODE="build"
REQUESTED=$#
CHECK_MODE=false
DRY_RUN=false
ASSUME_YES=false
FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false

```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Everything that can be checked without Android tools
# =============================================================================
# CI runs this on every push (see .github/workflows/check.yml), and it is worth
# running before a release:
#
#   bash stuff/tests/run.sh
#
# 1. shell syntax of every shipped script (bash -n / sh -n, no execution)
# 2. the WebUI resource-table writer against stuff/tests/fixtures/*.apk
# 3. the WebUI manifest and the overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off
#    vendor_hardware_overlay), built from
#    resource XML that stuff/tests/gen-res.sh generates into a temp directory (so
#    a fresh clone needs no build first)
# 4. every relative link and #anchor in the docs
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."

status=0
step() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$*"; }

step "shell syntax"
for f in build.sh treble-rro-creator.sh gui/build.sh stuff/scripts/*.sh stuff/tests/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if bash -n "$f"; then :; else echo "bash -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
done
# apply.sh, addons.sh and the module scripts run under Android's mksh
# (/system/bin/sh).
for f in src/webui/apply.sh src/webui/addons.sh src/module/*.sh stuff/templates/*.sh stuff/templates/recoveries/*.sh; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if command -v sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if sh -n "$f"; then :; else echo "sh -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
    fi
done
[ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all scripts parse"
```

```
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay — shared helpers
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by build.sh and by the modules in stuff/scripts/. Never run directly.
      #
      # The entry point sets ROOT (the project directory) and then sources this file,
      # so every helper below can assume it exists and that the current directory is
      # the project root.
      # =============================================================================
      
      : "${ROOT:?stuff/scripts/common.sh must be sourced by build.sh (ROOT is not set)}"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Paths
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Absolute paths are used for file tests and for zip destinations. Arguments
      # handed to native tools (aapt2/zipalign) must stay RELATIVE: MSYS on Windows
      # does not reliably convert a /c/... path for a native .exe.
      # Everything that is not the thing you build lives under stuff/, so the root
      # only holds the two entry points, config.env and the folders you open.
      STUFF_DIR="$ROOT/stuff"
      TOOLS_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/tools"
      BUILD_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/build"
      OUT_DIR="$ROOT/out"
      KEYS_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/keys"
      BACKUP_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/backups"
      TEMPLATES_DIR="$STUFF_DIR/templates"
      # Not "the old version of your files": the no-git fallback for
      # restore_from_release(). Kept identical to the committed files by stuff/tests/run.sh.
      RECOVERIES_DIR="$TEMPLATES_DIR/recoveries"
      
      SRC_DIR="$ROOT/src"
      FRAMEWORK_DIR="$SRC_DIR/framework"
      FRAMEWORK_RES="$FRAMEWORK_DIR/res"
      SYSTEMUI_DIR="$SRC_DIR/systemui"
      SYSTEMUI_RES="$SYSTEMUI_DIR/res"
      MODULE_DIR="$SRC_DIR/module"
      VENDOR_DIR="$SRC_DIR/vendor"
      
      CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
      CONFIG_EXAMPLE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Version
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # One line in stuff/VERSION is the only place the tool's own version lives; the
      # shell and the desktop app (gui/version.go) both read this file. A checkout
      # without it still works, it just cannot say which version it is.
      TOOL_VERSION="unknown"
      if [ -f "$STUFF_DIR/VERSION" ]; then
          v="$(tr -d ' \t\r\n' < "$STUFF_DIR/VERSION" 2>/dev/null)"
          if [ -n "$v" ]; then TOOL_VERSION="$v"; fi
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Restoring a tracked file to what this release ships
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # "Start over" must never hand back a copy that froze at some old commit. The
      # committed blob IS the template for a tracked file, so ask git for it; the
      # copy in stuff/templates/recoveries/ is only the fallback for a checkout with no .git
      # (a fork downloaded as a zip). stuff/tests/run.sh fails if the two ever drift.
      #
      #   restore_from_release <path relative to ROOT> [fallback copy]
      #
      # Returns 0 when the file on disk now holds the release version.
      restore_from_release() {
          local rel="$1" fallback="${2:-}"
      
          if [ -d "$ROOT/.git" ] && command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 \
             && git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify --quiet "HEAD:${rel}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if git -C "$ROOT" checkout HEAD -- "$rel" 2>/dev/null; then
                  return 0
              fi
          fi
      
          if [ -n "$fallback" ] && [ -f "$fallback" ]; then
              mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ROOT/$rel")"
              cp "$fallback" "$ROOT/$rel" && return 0
          fi
          return 1
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Platform
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      IS_WINDOWS=false
      case "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" in
          MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) IS_WINDOWS=true ;;
      esac
      
      # WSL reports Linux but lives inside Windows. The build is allowed there only
      # when the checkout is on the Linux filesystem (see wsl_guard).
      IS_WSL=false
      if ! $IS_WINDOWS && [ -r /proc/version ] && grep -qi microsoft /proc/version 2>/dev/null; then
          IS_WSL=true
      fi
      
      IS_TERMUX=false
      if [ -d /data/data/com.termux ] && [ -n "${PREFIX:-}" ]; then
          IS_TERMUX=true
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Output
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The drawing helpers — the window width, the palette, boxes, tables and prose
      # that wraps — are in ui.sh. Everything below is the one-word verb for one of
      # them, so a build log, the menu and a probe report are drawn by the same rules
      # and fit the same phone.
      . "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/ui.sh"
      
      # Kept for the scripts that still colour a line by hand.
      RED='\033[0;31m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
      CYAN='\033[0;36m'; BOLD='\033[1m'; NC='\033[0m'
      
      ok()   { ui_mark ok "$*"; }
      info() { ui_mark note "$*"; }
      warn() { ui_mark warn "$*"; }
      err()  { ui_mark bad "$*" >&2; }
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/common.sh
  content: |
      err()  { ui_mark bad "$*" >&2; }
      step() { printf '\n'; ui_heading "$*"; }
      
      # banner TEXT — a title, ruled to the width of the window.
      banner() {
          ui_title "$*"
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prompts
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ask <question> <default>   -> answer in $REPLY
      #
      # `read` returns 1 at EOF (stdin redirected, CI, IDE task, no console). Under
      # `set -e` that used to kill the scripts silently right after a menu had been
      # printed. Falling back to a stated default keeps everything runnable
      # unattended, and pressing Enter also takes the default.
      ask() {
          local question="$1" default="${2:-}" answer=""
          printf '%s' "$question"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              info "No terminal input available — using '${default}'."
              answer="$default"
          fi
          [ -z "$answer" ] && answer="$default"
          REPLY="$answer"
      }
      
      # confirm <question> <y|n>   -> returns 0 for yes
      confirm() {
          local question="$1" default="${2:-n}" answer
          ask "$question" "$default"
          answer="$REPLY"
          case "$answer" in
              [Yy]|[Yy][Ee][Ss]) return 0 ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # WSL safety
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # A checkout on a Windows drive that is built from inside WSL would put Linux
      # binaries into the same stuff/tools/ folder the Windows build reads, and would hand
      # Windows a build tree it cannot use. Refuse with instructions instead of
      # producing a half-broken toolchain. (This is the "VS Code opened the folder
      # with WSL" case.)
      wsl_guard() {
          $IS_WSL || return 0
          case "$ROOT" in
              /mnt/[a-z]/*) ;;
              *) return 0 ;;
          esac
      
          echo ""
          err "This project is on a Windows drive, but you are running inside WSL."
          echo ""
          echo "    Project:  $ROOT"
```

```json
      "newString": "# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Termux: ask for root once, before anything is drawn\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Reading /vendor/overlay, pulling a vendor prop file and installing the module\n# all need root, and on Termux the first `su` of a session is a prompt from the\n# manager (Magisk, KernelSU, APatch). Asked for in the middle of a build, that\n# prompt lands on top of the screen the tool is drawing; asked for here, it is\n# one question before the menu paints, and the manager remembers the grant for\n# the app, so the rest of the session runs quietly.\n#\n# Nothing is forced: `--no-su` (TREBLE_NO_SU=1) skips it, declining skips it, a\n# phone with no `su` skips it, and without a terminal it is skipped too so a\n# script or CI never waits for a tap that will not come. Sets TERMUX_ROOT=1 when\n# root is available, so callers can tell \"granted\" from \"never asked\".\ntermux_root_handoff() {\n    TERMUX_ROOT=\"\"\n    $IS_TERMUX || return 0\n    [ \"${TREBLE_NO_SU:-0}\" = 1 ] && return 0\n    [ \"$(id -u 2>/dev/null)\" = 0 ] && { TERMUX_ROOT=1; return 0; }\n\n    local su_bin\n    for su_bin in su tsu; do\n        command -v \"$su_bin\" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break\n        su_bin=\"\"\n    done\n    [ -n \"$su_bin\" ] || return 0\n    [ -t 0 ] || return 0\n\n    printf '\\n'\n    info \"Termux: root is needed to read /vendor and to install the module.\"\n    info \"Granting it now means no prompt lands on top of the build later.\"\n    if ! confirm \"    Give root access now? [Y/n] \" y; then\n        info \"Skipped — the next step that needs root will ask by itself.\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    printf '\\n'\n    if [ \"$(\"$su_bin\" -c 'id -u' </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\\r' | tail -n1)\" = 0 ]; then\n        TERMUX_ROOT=1\n        ok \"Root granted — device reads and install work from here on.\"\n    else\n        warn \"Root was not granted — reading /vendor and installing the module will fail.\"\n        info \"Try again later, or run the tool from a root shell: su -c './build.sh'\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# WSL safety\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh
  content: |
              ui_mark note "exit $rc — normal for a tool without arguments" 15
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      run_doctor() {
          local problems=0 t cand kind usable bad
      
          if $IS_WINDOWS; then
              banner "Toolchain check  (build.cmd doctor)"
          else
              banner "Toolchain check  (build.sh doctor)"
          fi
          local -a env_rows=("Shell|$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)  (MSYSTEM=${MSYSTEM:-unset})")
          if $IS_WINDOWS; then
              env_rows+=("Platform|Windows (Git Bash / MSYS2)")
          elif $IS_TERMUX; then
              env_rows+=("Platform|Android / Termux")
          elif $IS_WSL; then
              env_rows+=("Platform|WSL (Linux)")
          else
              env_rows+=("Platform|Linux")
          fi
          env_rows+=("Project|$ROOT" "Tools dir|$TOOLS_DIR")
          ui_panel "Environment" "${env_rows[@]}"
      
          ui_heading "Tools"
      
          for t in aapt2 zipalign apksigner; do
              usable=""; bad=""
              while IFS= read -r cand; do
                  [ -n "$cand" ] || continue
                  kind=$(classify_binary "$cand")
                  if kind_usable "$kind"; then
                      [ -z "$usable" ] && usable="$cand"
                  else
                      bad="${bad}${cand} [$(kind_label "$kind")] "
                  fi
              done <<< "$(tool_candidates "$t")"
      
              echo ""
              if [ -n "$usable" ]; then
                  doctor_row "$UI_TICK" "$UI_GREEN" "$t" "$usable" \
                      "$(kind_label "$(classify_binary "$usable")")"
                  if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
                      ui_mark warn "shadows it, cannot run here: $bad" 14
                      problems=$((problems + 1))
                  fi
              elif [ -n "$bad" ]; then
                  doctor_row "$UI_CROSS" "$UI_RED" "$t" "only unusable copies" "$bad"
                  problems=$((problems + 1))
              elif [ "$t" = "zipalign" ] && $IS_TERMUX; then
                  doctor_row "$UI_DOT" "$UI_YELLOW" "$t" "missing" "install with: pkg install aapt"
              else
                  doctor_row "$UI_CROSS" "$UI_RED" "$t" "not found"
                  problems=$((problems + 1))
              fi
          done
      
          local res
          echo ""
          if res=$(framework_res_path); then
              doctor_row "$UI_TICK" "$UI_GREEN" "resources" "$res" \
                  "$(kind_label "$(classify_binary "$res")")"
          else
              doctor_row "$UI_CROSS" "$UI_RED" "resources" "not found" "build.sh download it"
              problems=$((problems + 1))
          fi
      
          local jpath
          echo ""
          jpath=$(command -v java 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ -n "$jpath" ]; then
              doctor_row "$UI_TICK" "$UI_GREEN" "java" "$jpath" "$(kind_label "$(classify_binary "$jpath")")"
          else
              doctor_row "$UI_CROSS" "$UI_RED" "java" "not found" "apksigner will fail"
              problems=$((problems + 1))
          fi
      
          echo ""
```

```
9:+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
10:+# Checksums: a download is compared before it is unpacked
11:+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
12:+# A download cut short, and a mirror serving something else, both unpack into a
13:+# toolchain that breaks later inside aapt2 with a message that explains nothing.
14:+# Go, Google Maven and WinLibs each publish a SHA-256 next to the file, so the
15:+# bytes on disk are compared with the published hash first. Google publishes no
16:+# hash for the legacy platform-*-r*.zip archives; those are zips with a CRC per
17:+# entry, which unzip checks while extracting, so a damaged one still fails.
18:+#
19:+# RRO_NO_CHECKSUM=1 skips the comparison, for a mirror that publishes no hash.
20:+
21:+# hash_of FILE ALGO — sha1 or sha256 as hex, nothing when this machine has no
22:+# tool for it. sha256sum/shasum/openssl, whichever exists first.
23:+hash_of() {
24:+    local f="$1" algo="${2:-sha256}" bits
25:+    case "$algo" in
26:+        sha1)   bits=1 ;;
27:+        sha256) bits=256 ;;
28:+        *) return 1 ;;
29:+    esac
30:+    if command -v "${algo}sum" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
31:+        "${algo}sum" "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $1 }'
32:+    elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
33:+        shasum -a "$bits" "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $1 }'
34:+    elif command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
35:+        openssl dgst -"$algo" "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $NF }'
36:+    else
37:+        return 1
38:+    fi
39:+}
40:+
41:+# verify_hash FILE EXPECTED [LABEL] [ALGO] — 0 to keep the file, 1 to delete it.
42:+# EXPECTED may be empty or unparsable (a 404 page, a publisher with no hash);
43:+# that is not a mismatch, and the caller says so instead of failing the build.
44:+# The algorithm comes from ALGO, else from the hash length (40 sha1, 64 sha256).
45:+verify_hash() {
46:+    local f="$1" want got algo="${4:-}" label="${3:-$(basename "$1")}"
47:+    want="$(printf '%s' "${2:-}" | tr 'A-F' 'a-f' | tr -cd '0-9a-f')"
48:+    [ -n "$algo" ] || { [ ${#want} -eq 40 ] && algo=sha1 || algo=sha256; }
49:+
50:+    if [ "${RRO_NO_CHECKSUM:-}" = 1 ]; then
51:+        info "Skipped the checksum for ${label} (RRO_NO_CHECKSUM=1)"
52:+        return 0
53:+    fi
54:+    if [ -z "$want" ] || { [ "$algo" = sha1 ] && [ ${#want} -ne 40 ]; } || \
55:+       { [ "$algo" = sha256 ] && [ ${#want} -ne 64 ]; }; then
56:+        warn "No published checksum for ${label} — nothing to compare against"
57:+        return 0
58:+    fi
59:+    if ! got="$(hash_of "$f" "$algo")"; then
60:+        warn "This machine has no ${algo} tool — ${label} was not checked"
61:+        return 0
62:+    fi
63:+    if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
64:+        ok "Checksum matches for ${label}"
65:+        return 0
66:+    fi
67:+    err "Checksum mismatch for ${label} — the file on disk is not the one published"
68:+    echo "      expected ${want}" >&2
69:+    echo "      got      ${got}" >&2
70:+    return 1
71:+}
72:+

74:+# serve as FILE.sha256, or nothing when the link has no such sibling.
75:+published_sha256() {
76:+    local url="$1" text
77:+    text="$(net_cat "${url}.sha256" 2>/dev/null || true)"
78:+    printf '%s' "$text" | awk '/^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}/ { print $1; exit }'
79:+}
```

```
      ensure_toolchain() {
          local mode="${1:-auto}" force_res="${2:-}" missing

              ok "Toolchain ready"

          info "Toolchain incomplete — missing: ${missing}"
```

````
- path: docs/termux.md
  content: |
      ## 5. Root for the phone probes
      
      On a PC the probes ask the phone over `adb shell`. In Termux there is nothing to
      plug in and no server to dial — the phone the probes want is the one the script
      is already running on — so they read it directly instead: the same `getprop`,
      `cmd overlay`, `wm`, `dumpsys` and `/vendor` reads, run natively.
      
      That path needs root. Termux runs as an app UID, and `cmd`, `dumpsys` and most
      of `/vendor` are closed to it. A root shell also lets `/vendor/build.prop` and
      the vendor `overlay/` APKs be read for the firmware values the GSI no longer has.
      
      Start the tool through `su` or `tsu`:
      
      ```bash
      tsu ./build.sh          # recommended: root for the whole session
      ```
      
      or just run `./build.sh` and let it ask. The first time you pick a probe in
      Termux, the menu explains this once and offers to read the phone directly:
      
      ```
        This is Termux, so the phone is this one rather than a device on a cable.
        Reading it directly needs root: the same getprop, cmd overlay, wm and
        dumpsys reads a PC makes over adb.
        Read this phone as root? [Y/n]
      ```
      
      `su` prompts for permission on the first read. The answer is remembered for the
      session: every later probe — and `7` (Match property) — uses it without asking
      again, and the options are labelled **this phone** rather than **the connected
      phone**. Decline and the probes fall back to adb, which is what you want when a
      second phone is on the cable (Termux's `android-tools` can reach one over
      wireless debugging).
      
      If no `su` binary exists:
      
      ```bash
      pkg install tsu
      tsu ./build.sh
      ```
      
      Root not granted is reported, not worked around — every read would come back
      empty and the report would look like a ROM that answers nothing.
      
      Two practical notes:
      
      - **The device wait.** On a PC a probe waits up to 120s for a cable to be
        plugged in. That wait cannot end on Termux, so when this machine is the phone
        the local source is chosen before the wait starts. `Ctrl-C` leaves a wait in
        any case and puts you back in the submenu.
      - **Speed.** Each read is one root call, about the same count of round trips a
        PC makes over adb — a few seconds, not instant.
      
      ---
      
      ## 6. Install the module
      
      ```bash
      cp out/*-ksu.zip /sdcard/
      ```
      
      Or let the menu do it: **8 Files → 1 Copy** writes the zip and its APKs to
      `/sdcard/treble-rro-creator` — with `cp` on the phone, or `adb push` when a PC
      ran the build. The terminal tells you how many files landed.
      
      Then either:
      
      - open your root manager (KernelSU / KSU Next / Magisk) → Modules → install the
        zip, or use MT Manager to pick it from `/sdcard/`, or
      - from a PC over ADB:
      
      ```bash
      adb shell su -c 'ksud module install /sdcard/treble-overlay-<device>-ksu.zip'
      ```
      
      Reboot when done.
      
      > **KernelSU / KSU Next:** install **Magic Mount** (or Hybrid Mount configured
      > for magic mount) before flashing overlay modules.
      > **Never use OverlayFS** — it mounts fine, but a mistake in a vendor build's
      > `sepolicy.rule` or VINTF manifests then bootloops the device; magic mount
      > ignores the bad file and boots.
      
      ---
      
      ## Tips
      
      - Keep the project inside Termux home. Moving it to `/sdcard` breaks execution
        permissions.
      - `./build.sh clean` frees space; `./build.sh clean --all` starts over for a
````

```

- path: stuff/scripts/install-module.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # install-module.sh — put the built module on the phone, reboot, check it
      # =============================================================================
      # Building ends with a zip in out/ and four lines of instructions. This does the
      # part people get wrong: copy the zip over, hand it to the root manager that is
      # actually installed (ksud for KernelSU/KSU Next, magisk for Magisk), reboot,
      # wait for the phone to come back, and then report whether the overlay really is
      # mounted and enabled — the three things "did it work?" means.
      #
      #   ./build.sh install                  # the connected phone
      #   ./build.sh install --no-reboot      # install, leave the reboot to you
      #   ./build.sh install --device SERIAL  # more than one phone attached
      #   ./build.sh install --zip PATH       # a module other than the newest build
      #
      #   Standalone: bash stuff/scripts/install-module.sh [the same options]
      #
      # In Termux the zip is installed on this phone directly (root, no adb) and the
      # script stops after the install: rebooting the machine the script runs on
      # cannot be followed by a verification pass.
      #
      # Verification is read-only: /data/adb/modules/<id> must exist with no `disable`
      # or `remove` file, and `cmd overlay list` must show the package as enabled.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -uo pipefail
      
      # adb on Windows is a Git Bash binary: /sdcard/... would be rewritten into a
      # Windows path before adb saw it.
      export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1
      
      ROOT="${ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"
      
      want_serial="${DEVICE_SERIAL:-}"
      zip_path=""
      do_reboot=1
      do_verify=1
      
      usage() {
          sed -n '3,23p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
      }
      
      die() { err "$1"; return 1; }
      
      while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
          case "$1" in
              --device) want_serial="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --zip) zip_path="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --no-reboot) do_reboot=0; shift ;;
              --no-verify) do_verify=0; shift ;;
              -y|--yes) do_reboot=1; shift ;;
              -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
              *) die "unknown option: $1 (try --help)"; exit 2 ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # The module id and package name are derived, not typed: the same function the
      # build uses, from the same config.env, so what is installed is what was built.
      [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ] && . "$ROOT/config.env"
      derive_overlay_identity >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      
      module_id="${OVERLAY_NAME:-}"
      overlay_pkg="${OVERLAY_PACKAGE:-}"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Which zip
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      install_find_zip() {
          if [ -n "$zip_path" ]; then
              [ -f "$zip_path" ] || { die "no such file: $zip_path"; return 1; }
              printf '%s' "$zip_path"
              return 0
          fi
          if [ -n "$module_id" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/out/${module_id}-ksu.zip" ]; then
              printf '%s' "$ROOT/out/${module_id}-ksu.zip"
              return 0
          fi
          # A clean checkout builds a different device name than the config says; the
          # newest -ksu.zip is still the thing the user just built.
          local newest
          newest="$(ls -t "$ROOT"/out/*-ksu.zip 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
          if [ -n "$newest" ]; then
              warn "no zip for ${module_id:-this config} — using $(basename "$newest")"
              printf '%s' "$newest"
              return 0
          fi
          die "nothing to install: out/ has no -ksu.zip. Run ./build.sh build first."
          return 1
```

```
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Checksums: compare a download with the hash its publisher lists
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Go and WinLibs both publish a SHA-256 next to the file. A download that was
+# cut short unpacks into a Go or gcc that fails much later and confusingly, so
+# the bytes are compared before anything is unpacked. RRO_NO_CHECKSUM=1 skips
+# the comparison, for a mirror that publishes none.
+sha256_of() {
+    local f="$1"
+    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        sha256sum "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $1 }'
+    elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        shasum -a 256 "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $1 }'
+    elif command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        openssl dgst -sha256 "$f" 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $NF }'
+    else
+        return 1
+    fi
+}
+
+# verify_sha256 FILE EXPECTED LABEL — 0 to keep the file, 1 to delete it. An
+# empty or unparsable EXPECTED is not a mismatch: it is reported and let go.
+verify_sha256() {
+    local f="$1" want got label="$3"
+    want="$(printf '%s' "${2:-}" | tr 'A-F' 'a-f' | tr -cd '0-9a-f')"
+
+    if [ "${RRO_NO_CHECKSUM:-}" = 1 ]; then
+        echo "  checksum check skipped for ${label} (RRO_NO_CHECKSUM=1)"
+        return 0
+    fi
+    if [ ${#want} -ne 64 ]; then
+        echo "  no published SHA-256 for ${label} — nothing to compare against" >&2
+        return 0
+    fi
+    if ! got="$(sha256_of "$f")"; then
+        echo "  no sha256sum, shasum or openssl here — ${label} was not checked" >&2
+        return 0
+    fi
+    if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
+        return 0
+    fi
+    echo "  SHA-256 mismatch for ${label}:" >&2
+    echo "    expected ${want}" >&2
+    echo "    got      ${got}" >&2
+    return 1
+}
+
+# go_published_sha256 FILE — the hash go.dev lists for that exact filename.
+go_published_sha256() {
+    fetch_url "https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json&include=all" 2>/dev/null |
+        awk -v want="\"$1\"" '
+            index($0, "\"filename\": " want) { hit = 1; next }
+            hit && /"sha256":/ { gsub(/[",]/, "", $2); print $2; exit }'
+}
```

- `./build.sh` now asks for root **once at startup**, before the menu paints, instead of the manager's prompt landing on top of a half-drawn screen: `termux_root_handoff` in `stuff/scripts/common.sh`. It skips itself when you're already root, when there's no `su`/`tsu`, without a terminal (CI, the desktop app, `-y`) — and `--no-su` / `TREBLE_NO_SU=1` keeps the old per-command escalation.
- `build.sh doctor` now reports **root: granted / not granted / no su-tsu found** on Termux, so "why is every device read empty" answers itself.
- Documented in `docs/termux.md` §5 with the exact prompt text.

**Install after build**
- `./build.sh install` — newest `out/*-ksu.zip` (or `--zip`), pushed, handed to the manager that is actually installed (`ksud` for KernelSU/KSU Next, `magisk` for Magisk), reboots, waits for the phone, then verifies `/data/adb/modules/<id>` is enabled and the overlay package is really listed. `--device SERIAL` picks a phone, `--no-reboot` stops before the reboot. On Termux it installs locally and stops after the install (rebooting the machine running the script can't be followed by a check).
- Reached from `1 Build → 8 Install` in the menu, and offered at the end of a real build.
- Added to `README.md` and `docs/termux.md` §6.

**Also in this set** (from the earlier audit pass): docs search that reads the text inside `docs/*.md` and jumps to the line, the hardware-overlay codename vs `HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE` warning in `check`, the build plan and the Device tab, checksums on downloaded toolchain archives, `--version` from `stuff/VERSION`, and `./build.sh fod-build` for maintainers.

Fixed one false positive I introduced: `check` no longer complains about `HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE="<codename>"` while the config is still a template — a placeholder now counts as unset, like every other key.

**Checks run:** `bash stuff/tests/run.sh` → 119 node tests pass, Go tests pass, the UDFPS helper still compiles for android/arm64, every docs link resolves. `build.sh doctor`, `build.sh check` and `build.sh --help` run clean on this box, and the root handoff was exercised with a stub `su` (accept → `TERMUX_ROOT=1`, one question). The `install` verb was verified against a real phone (KernelSU) in an earlier run; I didn't repeat the reboot cycle here. Not run: a full Termux session on your phone — that's the one thing only you can confirm.

```
  content: |
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/toggle", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileToggle))
```
