      func randomToken() (string, error) {
        b := make([]byte, 16)
        if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
          return "", err
        }
        return hex.EncodeToString(b), nil
      }
      
      func (a *App) guard(method string, h http.HandlerFunc) http.HandlerFunc {
        return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
          if r.Method != method {
            w.Header().Set("Allow", method)
            http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
            return
          }
          if r.Header.Get("Sec-Fetch-Site") == "cross-site" {
            http.Error(w, "forbidden", http.StatusForbidden)
            return
          }
          h(w, r)
        }
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Handlers
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      func (a *App) handleState(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, a.State())
      }
      
      // handleSettings remembers the clone and the bash binary. Nothing is run here:
      // a wrong path is stored and reported by /api/state so the field stays visible
      // and editable instead of being rejected on a typo.
      func (a *App) handleSettings(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Clone string `json:"clone"`
          Bash  string `json:"bash"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        if err := a.setPaths(body.Clone, body.Bash); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, a.State())
      }
      
      // handleConfig writes config.env exactly as typed. The file is the interface
      // build.sh reads, comments included, so it is saved verbatim rather than
      // round-tripped through a form.
      func (a *App) handleConfig(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Text string `json:"text"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "no clone selected")
          return
        }
        if len(body.Text) > 1<<20 {
          writeError(w, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, "config.env is limited to 1 MiB")
          return
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "config.env"), []byte(body.Text), 0o644); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"path": filepath.Join(root, "config.env")})
      }
      
      func (a *App) handleRun(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Verb  string   `json:"verb"`
          Flags []string `json:"flags"`
          // Sudo is the password the app collected after the installer said it
          // needed one. It lives in this request, a 0600 file for the duration of
          // the run, and the page's memory — never in a log or the clone.
          Sudo string `json:"sudo"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        args, err := buildArgs(body.Verb, body.Flags)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        // Only these two verbs install anything (see ensure_toolchain). A password
        // for check or clean would be carried for nothing.
        if body.Sudo != "" && body.Verb != "build" && body.Verb != "setup" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "that command does not install anything")
          return
        }
        extraEnv, cleanup, err := a.sudoEnv(body.Sudo)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        if err := a.runner.StartEnv(a.Root(), a.Bash(), args, "build.sh "+body.Verb, false, extraEnv, cleanup); err != nil {
          // start() already ran cleanup on its own failure paths.
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, a.runner.Snapshot())
      }
      
      // sudoEnv turns a password from the dialog into what `sudo -A` needs.
      //

- path: stuff/scripts/menu.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # menu.sh — the terminal front end
      # =============================================================================
      # The desktop app and this file drive the same tools: the device probes, the
      # addon catalog, the match-property ranking and build.sh's own verbs. The goal
      # is that a phone with a terminal (Termux, ssh, a server) gets the same answers
      # as the window, without a GUI toolkit.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 opens this (when stdin is a terminal)
      #   ./build.sh menu            opens this even when stdin is not a terminal
      #   bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh same thing, standalone
      #
      # Every action shells out to the real entry point — `build.sh build`,
      # `device-probe.sh --write`, `addons.sh set` — so there is exactly one
      # implementation of each step and the menu cannot drift from the app.
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
          . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      # The device-source helpers (device_is_termux, device_local_begin) live with the
      # adb code the probes share. Sourcing it here defines functions only.
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Small things
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MENU_SLEEP="${MENU_SLEEP:-0}"
      
      # A width-aware rule under a section title. Every screen used to draw a fixed
      # 58-character one, which wrapped onto a second line on a phone.
      hr() { ui_rule 2; }
      
      # Read one line. Returns 1 at EOF (piped input, a launcher with no console) so
      # callers can leave the menu instead of looping forever.
      menu_read() {
          local prompt="${1:-} " answer=""
          printf '%s' "$prompt"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              return 1
          fi
          MENU_ANSWER="$answer"
          return 0
      }
      
      # Wait for Enter between screens, unless stdin is not a terminal.
      pause_menu() {
          [ -t 0 ] || return 0
          printf '\n  %s ' "Press Enter to go back"
          read -r _ || true
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # Count the rows config.env has, and how many are switched off.
      cfg_counts() {
          local rows
          rows="$(cfg_rows 2>/dev/null)" || { CFG_ON=0; CFG_OFF=0; return 0; }
          CFG_ON="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 1' | grep -c . || true)"
          CFG_OFF="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 0' | grep -c . || true)"
      }
      
      output_summary() {
          local apks=0 zips=0 zip=""
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR/apks" ] && apks="$(find "$OUT_DIR/apks" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && zips="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          zip="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | sort | head -n1)"
          if [ "$zips" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '%s  (%s APK%s)' "${zip#$ROOT/}" "$apks" "$([ "$apks" = 1 ] || echo s)"
          else
              printf 'nothing built yet'
          fi
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Screen
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The state of the checkout in one box: which phone, how much of config.env is
      # filled in, what the last build left behind.
      menu_header() {
          cfg_counts
          ui_panel "Treble Overlay Creator ${TOOL_VERSION}" \
              "Device|$(cfg_identity)" \
              "config.env|${CFG_ON} set ${UI_DOT} ${CFG_OFF} off" \
              "Output|$(output_summary)"
      }
      
      # 11 is the width of the longest label here, so every description starts in the
      # same column instead of ragging after each label.
      MENU_LW=14
      
      menu_items() {
          ui_item 1 'Build'          'dry run, build, check, doctor, clean' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 2 'config.env'     'browse and edit one key at a time' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 3 'Addons'         'module tweaks: settings and overlay resources' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 4 'Device'         'read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 5 'Auto Detect'    'ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 6 'UDFPS'          'in-display fingerprint geometry' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 7 'Match property' 'which property the submission should match on' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 8 'Files'          'what was built, and where it is' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 9 'Docs'           'the guides in docs/' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item q 'Quit' '' "$MENU_LW"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The menu never re-implements a build step: it runs the entry point with the
      # verb a user would type, so `build.sh doctor` and 1 → 4 are the same command.
      run_entry() {
          ( cd "$ROOT" && bash "$ROOT/build.sh" "$@" )
      }
      
      # Whether the Xiaomi FOD helper ships in the module. Off by default: it is only
      # useful on Xiaomi optical UDFPS phones, and on anything else it is a binary
      # that never starts. `./build.sh --xiaomi-fod menu` starts it already on.
      MENU_XIAOMI_FOD="${XIAOMI_FOD:-false}"
      
      # The --xiaomi-fod argument for a build started from here, or nothing at all.
      xiaomi_fod_arg() {
          [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ] && printf '%s' '--xiaomi-fod'
      }
      
      menu_build() {
          while :; do
              if [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ]; then
                  fod_state='on'
              else
                  fod_state='off'
              fi
              ui_heading 'Build'

- path: .gitignore
  content: |
      # Build output. Everything the build or the desktop app writes lives under
      # stuff/ (internals, downloaded tools, intermediate files); only the finished
      # APKs and zips are kept at the root, in out/, because that is where you look
      # for them.
      stuff/build/
      out/
      *.apk
      *.apk.idsig
      *.zip
      
      # Test fixtures are the one place an APK is committed: the WebUI's
      # resource-table writer is tested against a real overlay APK (tests/run.sh).
      !tests/fixtures/*.apk
      
      # Auto-generated during the build
      AndroidManifest.xml
      module.prop
      Android.mk
      src/framework/res/values/generated.xml
      src/framework/res/values-land/generated.xml
      src/systemui/res/values/generated.xml
      src/systemui/res/values-*-v4/generated.xml
      
      # Backups (config.env, module scripts, extracted vendor files)
      stuff/backups/
      
      # Extracted vendor files are device-specific and must not be committed.
      # The folder itself keeps a README so a fresh clone still has it.
      src/vendor/*
      !src/vendor/README.md
      
      # Files taken out of the build with the desktop app's Disable button. They are
      # still in the clone (that is the point) but they are not source to commit.
      src/.disabled/
      
      # Downloaded build tools
      stuff/tools/
      
      # Desktop app: built binaries, the remembered paths, and the crash log written
      # next to the executable. The root entries cover a release archive unpacked
      # straight into the clone.
      gui/bin/
      gui/dist/
      gui/.pkgconfig/
      # `go build ./gui` from the root drops its binary here (Windows adds the
      # extension; on Linux it refuses to write over the gui/ directory).
      /gui.exe
      /gui.json
      /gui.log
      gui/gui.json
      gui/gui.log
      # `go build ./...` inside gui/ leaves its binary there (the Linux one has no
      # extension).
      gui/gui.exe
      gui/gui
      # Legacy top-level paths from older versions (kept ignored so an upgrade
      # never offers to commit leftovers before build.sh moves them)
      system/
      YOUR BACKUPS/
      .module_tmp/
      tmp/
      
      # IDE / OS
      .idea/
      *.iml
      .vscode/
      *.swp
      *.swo
      *~
      .DS_Store
      Thumbs.db

     here to help with (a VINTF fragment, a sepolicy starter). -->
<dialog id="file-new">
  <form method="dialog" id="file-new-form">
    <h2 id="file-new-title">New file</h2>
    <p class="muted small" id="file-new-where"></p>

    <label for="file-new-kind">Create</label>
    <select id="file-new-kind">
      <option value="file">an empty file</option>
      <option value="dir">a folder</option>
      <option value="aidl">a VINTF manifest (AIDL template)</option>
      <option value="hidl">a VINTF manifest (HIDL template)</option>
      <option value="sepolicy">SELinux rules (starter template)</option>
    </select>

    <label for="file-new-name">Name</label>
    <input id="file-new-name" spellcheck="false" placeholder="android.hardware.biometrics.fingerprint.xml">
    <p class="hint" id="file-new-hint">The HAL name is taken from the file name.</p>

    <p class="error" id="file-new-error" hidden></p>

    <menu>
      <button type="button" id="file-new-cancel">Cancel</button>
      <button type="submit" class="primary">Create</button>
    </menu>
  </form>
</dialog>

<!-- Deleting cannot be undone, so it is the one question the app insists on.
     The destructive button is on the left and Cancel is on the right, styled as
     the primary action and focused when the dialog opens: a stray Enter keeps
     the file. -->
<dialog id="confirm">
  <form method="dialog">
    <h2 id="confirm-title">Delete?</h2>
    <p class="muted" id="confirm-text"></p>
    <menu>
      <button type="button" class="danger" id="confirm-yes">Delete</button>
      <button type="button" class="primary" id="confirm-no">Cancel</button>
    </menu>
  </form>
</dialog>

<!-- Update: what is waiting upstream, and what pulling it would do to the files
     that were edited here. The second part is the whole point — a pull that
     overwrites config.env would take the device settings with it. -->
<!-- Installing packages needs root, and the child has no terminal for sudo to
     ask in. This is the one question the app answers itself: the password is

     and kept in memory for the window's lifetime. -->
<dialog id="sudo">
  <form method="dialog" id="sudo-form">
    <h2>Install the build tools</h2>
    <p class="muted">
      Installing the missing tools needs root. Enter the password sudo would
      ask for; it stays in this window and is used for the install only.
    </p>

    <label for="sudo-password">sudo password</label>
    <input id="sudo-password" type="password" autocomplete="current-password" spellcheck="false">

    <p class="error" id="sudo-error" hidden></p>

    <menu>
      <button type="button" id="sudo-cancel">Cancel</button>
      <button type="submit" class="primary">Install</button>
    </menu>
  </form>
</dialog>

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// index.html and app.js have to agree
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The window is one page and one script with no framework and no bundler: a
// rename in the HTML or a typo in the script is not caught by any compiler, and
// the failure mode is a dead button and a console error only a devtools user
// sees. Pulling the ids out of both files catches that in CI instead.
//
// Run: node --test stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';

const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
const html = readFileSync(join(root, 'gui', 'ui', 'index.html'), 'utf8');
const js = readFileSync(join(root, 'gui', 'ui', 'app.js'), 'utf8');

function idsInHtml() {
  const ids = new Set();
  for (const m of html.matchAll(/\bid="([^"]+)"/g)) ids.add(m[1]);
  return ids;
}

// $('x') and document.getElementById('x'). Anything computed is skipped: there
// are none today, and a new one should be reviewed by hand anyway.
function idsInJs() {
  const ids = new Map();
  const patterns = [/\$\('([^']+)'\)/g, /getElementById\('([^']+)'\)/g];
  for (const re of patterns) {
    for (const m of js.matchAll(re)) {
      if (m[1].includes('+') || m[1].includes('${')) continue;
      ids.set(m[1], (ids.get(m[1]) || 0) + 1);
    }
  }
  return ids;
}

// Two elements may not share an id: getElementById returns the first, so code
// that meant the second one silently reads (or overwrites) the wrong element.
// A new <select> placed next to an existing hint paragraph did exactly that and
// only showed up as a picker that would not stay filled.
test('no id appears twice in the page', () => {
  const counts = new Map();
  for (const id of idsInHtml()) {
    counts.set(id, html.split(`id="${id}"`).length - 1);
  }
  const dupes = [...counts].filter(([, n]) => n > 1).map(([id]) => id);
  assert.deepEqual(dupes, [], `ids defined more than once: ${dupes.join(', ')}`);
});

test('every id the script looks up exists in the page', () => {
  const inHtml = idsInHtml();
  const missing = [...idsInJs().keys()].filter((id) => !inHtml.has(id));
  assert.deepEqual(missing, [], `app.js reaches for ids the page does not define: ${missing.join(', ')}`);
});

test('every id in the page is wired to something', () => {
  const used = idsInJs();
  const unused = [...idsInHtml()].filter((id) => !used.has(id));
  // Some ids are only styled or read by CSS; this is a warning list, and the
  // test fails only for ids that look like controls.
  const controls = unused.filter((id) => {
    const re = new RegExp(`<[^>]*\\bid="${id}"[^>]*>`);
    const tag = html.match(re)?.[0] || '';
    return /^<(button|input|textarea|dialog)/.test(tag);
  });
  assert.deepEqual(controls, [], `controls in index.html nothing uses: ${controls.join(', ')}`);
});

test('the page loads its stylesheet and script from the same folder', () => {
  assert.match(html, /href="app\.css"/);
  assert.match(html, /src="app\.js"/);
});

// A tab is a button with data-tab and a section with the matching pane id. A
// mismatch means the tab switches to nothing — visible only by clicking it.
test('every tab has a pane', () => {
  const tabs = [...html.matchAll(/data-tab="([^"]+)"/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
  assert.ok(tabs.length >= 4, `expected the build/config/device/docs tabs, found ${tabs.join(', ')}`);
  for (const tab of tabs) {
    assert.ok(html.includes(`id="pane-${tab}"`), `tab "${tab}" has no #pane-${tab}`);
  }
  assert.ok(js.includes("'pane-' + name"), 'switchTab no longer builds pane ids the way the test assumes');
});

// The buttons the server has to serve. Keeping the list here means a handler
// that is renamed in Go fails this test instead of a 404 in the window.
test('every api path the script calls exists in server.go', () => {
  const server = readFileSync(join(root, 'gui', 'server.go'), 'utf8');
  // The page uses relative paths ('api/state'); the server registers the whole
  // path under the per-launch token prefix.
  const paths = new Set(
    [...js.matchAll(/api\('([^']+)'/g)]
      .map((m) => m[1].replace(/^api\//, '').split('?')[0])
  );
  const missing = [...paths].filter((p) => !server.includes(`"/api/${p}"`));
  assert.deepEqual(missing, [], `server.go does not register: ${missing.join(', ')}`);
});

package main

// ============================================================================
// Which property should the submitted overlay match on?
// ============================================================================
// A static RRO for the overlay repo matches with android:requiredSystemProperty
// Name/Value, compared with plain string equality. Getting it wrong is silent:
// the overlay installs, `cmd overlay list` shows it enabled, and nothing changes.
//
// Two things decide whether a candidate works, and both are readable from the
// phone without root:
//
//   * zygote has to be able to read the property. A zygote overlay is matched
//     while zygote preloads the framework, so a property in a SELinux area
//     zygote is denied reads as empty and the condition never holds. `getprop -Z`
//     prints the area (build_prop and build_vendor_prop are the safe ones,
//     build_odm_prop and build_bootimage_prop are the usual traps).
//   * the value has to name this device and survive what is installed. The
//     vendor, odm and bootimage partitions keep the OEM value under a GSI;
//     /system, /product and /system_ext are replaced, so ro.product.device on a
//     GSI holds the GSI's own name (phh_treble, mivendor, …).
//
// Neither rule alone is enough — on a GSI the surviving property is often the
// one zygote cannot read, and the readable one has been renamed — so this ranks
// every candidate, says what each one is gambling on, and refuses to call a
// winner when no property actually carries the codename. The values below are
// what the reference phones report: Samsung SM-A908N (everything is r3q) and
// Xiaomi 26012RN62A (ro.product.device is zephyr, but its vendor property is the
// shared mivendor and build.product is missi).

import (
  "regexp"
  "sort"
  "strings"
)

// What a codename looks like: lower case, no separators bash would eat, short
// enough to be a name rather than a build string.
var codenameShape = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,23}$`)

// MatchCandidate is one property the submission could be matched on.
type MatchCandidate struct {
  Prop  string `json:"prop"`
  Value string `json:"value"`
  Score int    `json:"score"`
  Zone  string `json:"zone"`
  Label string `json:"label"`
  Trust string `json:"trust"` // high, medium, low
  // Perfect means this is a pick nothing has to be argued about: the value
  // is the codename, zygote can read the property, and a GSI leaves it alone.
  // Only a perfect pick is offered as the answer; anything less and the card
  // tells the user to keep the match they already have.
  Perfect bool   `json:"perfect"`
  Why     string `json:"why"`
  Risk    string `json:"risk,omitempty"`
}

// MatchRejection is a property with a device-ish name that was ruled out, and
// why. The reasons are the answers to the question users ask most often, so
// they are part of the answer rather than something to work out again.
type MatchRejection struct {
  Prop   string `json:"prop"`
  Value  string `json:"value"`
  Reason string `json:"reason"`
}

// MatchReport is what the Config tab shows: the codename it settled on, the
// ranked candidates, the properties it refused, and how sure it is.
type MatchReport struct {
  Serial     string           `json:"serial"`
  Model      string           `json:"model"`
  Codename   string           `json:"codename"`
  Confidence string           `json:"confidence"` // high, medium, low
  ModuleProp string           `json:"moduleProp"`
  Candidates []MatchCandidate `json:"candidates"`
  Rejected   []MatchRejection `json:"rejected"`
}

// matchProp is one entry of the fixed candidate list. zone says which partition
// the value comes from (that is what decides GSI survival) and kind says what

package main

import (
  "context"

//go:embed ui
var uiFiles embed.FS

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Why the UI is served at all
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The window is a webview pointed at a loopback URL. That is also what makes
// -browser and the Termux front-end free: same HTML, same handlers, no second
// UI to keep in sync with this one.
//
// The risk of a local server is that *any* page in the user's browser can POST
// to 127.0.0.1, and these handlers start build.sh. Two things stop that:
//
//  1. everything lives under a random /<token>/ prefix generated at launch, and
//     the page only learns it by being navigated to it — a cross-origin fetch
//     cannot read our HTML, so it cannot discover the prefix;
//  2. requests a browser marks as cross-site are refused outright.
//
// The listener is bound to 127.0.0.1, never 0.0.0.0, so nothing off-machine can
// reach it at all.
func (a *App) serve(port int) (net.Listener, string, *http.Server, error) {
  token, err := randomToken()
  if err != nil {
    return nil, "", nil, err
  }
  ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", port))
  if err != nil {
    return nil, "", nil, fmt.Errorf("could not open a loopback port: %w", err)
  }

  base := "/" + token
  assets, err := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui")
  if err != nil {
    return nil, "", nil, err
  }

  mux := http.NewServeMux()
  mux.HandleFunc(base, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    http.Redirect(w, r, base+"/", http.StatusFound)
  })
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/state", a.guard("GET", a.handleState))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/settings", a.guard("POST", a.handleSettings))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/config", a.guard("POST", a.handleConfig))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/run", a.guard("POST", a.handleRun))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/cancel", a.guard("POST", a.handleCancel))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/log", a.guard("GET", a.handleLog))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/log", a.guard("GET", a.handleAdbLog))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/open", a.guard("POST", a.handleOpen))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/docs", a.guard("GET", a.handleDocs))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/doc", a.guard("GET", a.handleDoc))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/docs/search", a.guard("GET", a.handleDocsSearch))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/update", a.guard("POST", a.handleUpdate))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/config/apply", a.guard("POST", a.handleConfigApply))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/addons", a.guard("GET", a.handleAddons))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/addons/save", a.guard("POST", a.handleAddonsSave))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb", a.guard("POST", a.handleAdb))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/devices", a.guard("GET", a.handleAdbDevices))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/install", a.guard("POST", a.handleAdbInstall))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/detect", a.guard("POST", a.handleAdbDetect))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/match-prop", a.guard("POST", a.handleMatchProp))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/extract", a.guard("POST", a.handleExtract))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/udfps", a.guard("POST", a.handleUDFPS))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/detect", a.guard("POST", a.handleDetect))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/pick", a.guard("POST", a.handlePick))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/url", a.guard("POST", a.handleURL))

  // The src/ workspace: the file manager, its two editors and the checks behind
  // them (see files.go). Uploads are the only route that is not JSON.
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files", a.guard("GET", a.handleFiles))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/read", a.guard("GET", a.handleFileRead))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/write", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileWrite))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/check", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileCheck))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/upload", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileUpload))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/delete", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileDelete))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/mkdir", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileMkdir))
  mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/toggle", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileToggle))

// addonsEnv points the helper at the clone instead of an installed module.
// Paths are POSIX: Git Bash on Windows reads a backslash as an escape.
func (a *App) addonsEnv() []string {
  root := filepath.ToSlash(a.Root())
  return []string{
    "ADDONS_DIR=" + root,
    "ADDONS_CONF=" + root + "/src/module/addons.conf",
  }
}

func (a *App) runAddons(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
  root := a.Root()
  if !isClone(root) {
    return nil, errors.New("no clone selected")
  }
  bash := a.Bash()
  if !fileExists(bash) {
    return nil, errors.New("bash was not found — pick it with the Path chip")
  }
  // Short on purpose: six `settings` calls on a phone, and no work at all in
  // the clone.
  ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
  defer cancel()
  cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bash, append([]string{addonsScript}, args...)...)
  // Hide the console Windows would otherwise flash for this child. The tab
  // runs the helper on open and on every save, so an un-hidden window is a
  // black rectangle blinking at the user each time.
  setProcAttr(cmd)
  cmd.Dir = root
  // A stale ADDONS_* in the app's own environment would otherwise win over
  // the paths below (Windows keeps the first duplicate in the block).
  env := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+2)
  for _, kv := range os.Environ() {
    if strings.HasPrefix(kv, "ADDONS_") {
      continue
    }
    env = append(env, kv)
  }
  cmd.Env = append(env, a.addonsEnv()...)
  var stderr strings.Builder
  cmd.Stderr = &stderr
  out, err := cmd.Output()
  if err != nil {
    msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
    if msg == "" {
      msg = err.Error()
    }
    return nil, errors.New(msg)
  }
  return out, nil
}

// addonsDoc is the helper's own JSON, passed through: the page renders exactly
// what the module will enforce.
func (a *App) addonsDoc() (map[string]any, error) {
  out, err := a.runAddons("list")
  if err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  var doc map[string]any
  if err := json.Unmarshal(out, &doc); err != nil {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("the addons helper did not return JSON: %v", err)
  }
  return doc, nil
}

```

- path: stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # config-edit.sh — read and write one key of config.env
      # =============================================================================
      # Sourced by the terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh) and by
      # stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh. The probes carry their own copy of the writer
      # because they are shipped standalone; anything new should source this.
      #
      # The file is the source of truth and stays hand-editable: these helpers rewrite
      # one line, keep the indentation, keep the quoting the line already used, and
      # turn a commented-out KEY= line into a live one (that is what "enable it"
      # means). Nothing here validates values — `./build.sh check` does that.
      # =============================================================================
      
      : "${ROOT:?stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh must be sourced with ROOT set}"
      
      # cfg_file -> the file the helpers act on, so a test can point somewhere else.
      cfg_file() {
          printf '%s' "${CFG_FILE:-${CONFIG_FILE:-$ROOT/config.env}}"
      }
      
      # cfg_unquote VALUE -> the value without the quotes config.env puts around text,
      # and without the escapes cfg_quote adds inside them.
      cfg_unquote() {
          local v="$1" dq=0
          case "$v" in
              \"*) v="${v#\"}"; v="${v%\"}"; dq=1 ;;
              \'*) v="${v#\'}"; v="${v%\'}" ;;
          esac
          if [ "$dq" = 1 ] && [[ "$v" == *\\* ]]; then
              # bash inside double quotes only treats a backslash specially before
              # these four characters, so undo exactly those and leave C:\path alone.
              v="$(printf '%s' "$v" | sed 's/\\\([$`"\\]\)/\1/g')"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$v"
      }
      
      # cfg_safe_value VALUE -> the value with the characters that would break the
      # file's one-key-per-line shape removed. A probe writes what the phone said, and
      # a model name with a newline in it used to split the line in two.
      cfg_safe_value() {
          local value="$1"
          value="${value//$'\r'/}"
          value="${value//$'\n'/ }"
          value="${value//$'\t'/ }"
          if [[ "$value" == *[[:cntrl:]]* ]]; then
              # A colour code from a pasted table is ESC + "[31m"; dropping only the
              # ESC would leave the "[31m" in the value, so the whole sequence goes.
              value="$(printf '%s' "$value" | LC_ALL=C sed $'s/\033\\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]//g' | LC_ALL=C tr -d '[:cntrl:]')"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$value"
      }
      
      # cfg_quote VALUE -> a value config.env can be sourced from.
      # Plain words stay bare, as they are in the file today; anything a shell would
      # split on, or anything that was already quoted, gets double quotes.
      #
      # Everything the shell expands inside double quotes is escaped, `$` and the
      # backtick included: build.sh sources this file, so a saved value like
      # `$(reboot)` would otherwise run as a command on the next build.
      cfg_quote() {
          local value="$1" force="${2:-0}"
          case "$value" in
              "") printf '""'; return 0 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$force" != "1" ]; then
              case "$value" in
                  *[[:space:]]*|*'#'*|*'"'*|*"'"*|*'$'*|*'`'*|*'\'*) ;;
                  *) printf '%s' "$value"; return 0 ;;
              esac
          fi
          value="${value//\\/\\\\}"
          value="${value//\"/\\\"}"
          value="${value//\$/\\\$}"
          value="${value//\`/\\\`}"
          printf '"%s"' "$value"
      }
      
      # cfg_get KEY -> the live value, unquoted, empty when the key is absent or off.
      cfg_get() {
          local key="$1" file line value=""
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
              line="${line%$'\r'}"
              case "$line" in
                  "$key="*) value="${line#*=}" ;;
              esac
          done <"$file"
          [ -n "$value" ] || return 0
          cfg_unquote "$value"
      }
      
      # cfg_has KEY -> 0 when KEY= (or #KEY=) exists in the file at all.
      cfg_has() {
          local key="$1" file
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*#?[[:space:]]*${key}=" "$file"
      }
      
      # cfg_rows -> one row per assignment, tab separated:
      #   key <TAB> active(0|1) <TAB> line number <TAB> section <TAB> value
      # A commented-out key is listed with active=0 so it can be turned on by name
      # instead of by hunting for the '#'. Prose that happens to end in '=' is not a
      # row: only `KEY=` and `#KEY=` (no space after the '#') count.
      cfg_rows() {
          local file
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          awk '
              /^#[[:space:]]*─/ {
                  sec = $0
                  sub(/^#[[:space:]]*/, "", sec)
                  gsub(/─/, "", sec)
                  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", sec)
                  next
              }
              /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ || /^#[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/ {
                  line = $0
                  sub(/\r$/, "", line)
                  key = line
                  sub(/=.*/, "", key)
                  active = 1
                  if (key ~ /^#/) { active = 0; sub(/^#/, "", key) }
                  value = substr(line, index(line, "=") + 1)
                  printf "%s\t%d\t%d\t%s\t%s\n", key, active, NR, sec, value
              }
          ' "$file"
      }
      
      # cfg_sections -> the section titles in file order, one per line.
      cfg_sections() {
          cfg_rows | awk -F'\t' '!seen[$4]++ && $4 != "" { print $4 }'
      }
      
      # cfg_set KEY VALUE -> rewrite (or add, or enable) that one line.
      # Returns 0 when the file was written — also when the value was already right,
      # because the caller only cares that the key now holds it.
      cfg_set() {
          local key="$1" value file tmp line rest quoted new done=0 wrote=0
          # A pasted value can carry a newline; it would end the line early and turn
          # the rest of it into a key of its own.
          value="$(cfg_safe_value "$2")"
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          if [ -f "$file" ]; then
              tmp="$file.tmp.$$"
              : >"$tmp" || return 1
              while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
                  local keep="${line%$'\r'}"
                  # `KEY=` or `#KEY=` (no space after the '#'), which is how this
                  # file disables one — a sentence in a comment that happens to
                  # mention the key is left alone.
                  if [ "$done" -eq 0 ] && [[ "$keep" =~ ^([[:space:]]*)#?${key}= ]]; then
                      indent="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                      rest="${keep#*=}"
                      quoted=0
                      case "$rest" in \"*) quoted=1 ;; esac
                      new="${indent}${key}=$(cfg_quote "$value" "$quoted")"
                      printf '%s\n' "$new" >>"$tmp"
                      done=1
                      wrote=1
                      continue
                  fi
                  printf '%s\n' "$keep" >>"$tmp"
              done <"$file"
              if [ "$done" -eq 0 ]; then
                  printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$(cfg_quote "$value")" >>"$tmp"
                  wrote=1
              fi
              mv "$tmp" "$file" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
          else
              printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$(cfg_quote "$value")" >"$file" || return 1
              wrote=1
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # cfg_set_active KEY 0|1 -> comment out, or bring back, that one line.
      # '#' with nothing after it is the file's own way of switching a key off, and
      # cfg_rows reads it back the same way, so an inactive key stays listed.
      cfg_set_active() {
          local key="$1" want="$2" file tmp keep done=0 indent rest
          file="$(cfg_file)"
          [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
          tmp="$file.tmp.$$"
          : >"$tmp" || return 1
          while IFS= read -r keep || [ -n "$keep" ]; do
              keep="${keep%$'\r'}"
              if [ "$done" -eq 0 ] && [[ "$keep" =~ ^([[:space:]]*)#?${key}= ]]; then
                  indent="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                  rest="${keep#*=}"
                  if [ "$want" = "1" ]; then
                      printf '%s%s=%s\n' "$indent" "$key" "$rest" >>"$tmp"
                  else
                      printf '#%s%s=%s\n' "$indent" "$key" "$rest" >>"$tmp"
                  fi
                  done=1
                  continue
              fi
              printf '%s\n' "$keep" >>"$tmp"
          done <"$file"
          mv "$tmp" "$file" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
          return 0
      }
      
      # cfg_summary -> the four lines the menu header shows, from the live file.
      cfg_identity() {
          local manuf model code
          manuf="$(cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)"
          model="$(cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)"
          code="$(cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)"
          if [ -z "$manuf" ] && [ -z "$model" ] && [ -z "$code" ]; then
              printf 'no device set'
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s %s (%s)' "$manuf" "$model" "$code" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'
      }

// Stages one config line the way the row itself would, so the change shows up in
// the form and Save sends it. Nothing is written to disk here.
function stageCfgValue(key, value) {
  const entry = cfgEntry(key);
  if (!entry) return false;
  const row = document.querySelector(`#cfg-fields .cfg-row[data-line="${entry.line}"]`);
  if (!row) return false;
  const on = row.querySelector('.cfg-on');
  const input = row.querySelector('.cfg-value');
  // The match keys are strings; a boolean row has no text field to stage.
  if (!input) return false;
  input.value = value;
  if (on && !on.checked) {
    on.checked = true;
    on.dispatchEvent(new Event('change'));
  }
  input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input'));
  row.classList.add('is-flash');
  setTimeout(() => row.classList.remove('is-flash'), 1500);
  return true;
}

function useMatch(c) {
  const prop = stageCfgValue('HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP', c.prop);
  const value = stageCfgValue('HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_VALUE', c.value);
  if (!prop || !value) {
    status('config.env has no HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_* lines — add them in the raw editor', 9000);
    return;
  }
  const row = document.querySelector(`#cfg-fields .cfg-row[data-line="${(cfgEntry('HW_OVERLAY_MATCH_PROP') || {}).line}"]`);
  if (row) row.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' });
  status(`staged ${c.prop} = "${c.value}" — Save writes it`, 9000);
}

async function saveConfig() {
  if (!state || !state.cloneValid) return;
  try {
    if (cfgRaw) {
      if (!$('cfg').value) return;
      await api('api/config', { method: 'POST', body: { text: $('cfg').value } });
      cfgRawDirty = false;
      updateCfgStatus();
      status('config.env saved', 3000);
    } else {
      if (cfgEdits.size === 0) {
        status('nothing to save', 3000);
        return;
      }
      const edits = [...cfgEdits.values()];
      const res = await api('api/config/apply', { method: 'POST', body: { edits } });
      cfgEdits.clear();
      state.config = res.config;
      state.configText = res.text;
      renderConfig(true);
      status(`saved ${edits.length} change${edits.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`, 4000);
    }
  } catch (err) {
    status(err.message, 9000);
  }
}

function setConfigMode(raw) {
  cfgRaw = raw;
  if (!raw) {
    // Coming back from the textarea: re-read the file, because it may have been
    // edited there and a form built from the old text would show stale values.
    cfgEdits.clear();
    cfgRawDirty = false;
    updateCfgStatus();
    refreshState(true);
    return;
  }
  renderConfig(true);
  updateCfgStatus();
}

      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Treble Overlay Creator
      # =============================================================================
      # One command for everything. With a terminal attached it opens the menu, which
      # reaches every tool the desktop app has; with an argument it does exactly that
      # one thing, as before.
      #
      #   ./build.sh                 the menu (on a terminal); otherwise: build
      #   ./build.sh menu            the menu, even without a terminal
      #   ./build.sh build           build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
      #   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
      #   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
      #   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
      #   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
      #   ./build.sh fod-build       rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper (maintainers)
      #   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
      #   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
      #
      #   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
      #   -V, --version              print the version
      #   -h, --help                 this help
      #
      # On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
      # Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
      # drive — see docs/windows.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      # pipefail matters here: most build steps run a tool and parse its output in a
      # pipeline (`aapt2 dump ... | sed | awk`). Without it a failed tool still exits
      # 0 through the pipeline and the build carries on with empty input.
      set -eo pipefail
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Project root
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      # Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
      # not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
      if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
      fi
      export ROOT
      cd "$ROOT"
      
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"
      
      # Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
      tools_on_path
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Options
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MODE="build"
      REQUESTED=$#
      CHECK_MODE=false
      DRY_RUN=false
      ASSUME_YES=false
      FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
      CLEAN_ALL=false
      FORCE_RES=""
      ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false
      
      usage() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
          echo "    (none)             The menu (on a terminal), otherwise a build"
          echo "    menu               The menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes"
          echo "    build              Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
          echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
          echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
          echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
          echo "    install            Install out/<name>-ksu.zip on the phone, reboot, verify"
          echo "    fod-build          Rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper from its Go source"
          echo "    clean              Remove build output"
          echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --xiaomi-fod           Include the Xiaomi FOD helper (HBM + HIDL touch mode) in the module"
          echo "    --device SERIAL        With install: the phone to use, when more than one is attached"
          echo "    --zip PATH             With install: a module other than the newest build"
          echo "    --no-reboot            With install: hand it over, do not reboot or verify"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    --no-su                Termux: do not ask for root up front"
          echo "    -V, --version          Print the version"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
          echo ""
      }
      
      # Options that only `install` understands are collected here and handed to
      # install-module.sh, so the entry point keeps one parser.
      INSTALL_EXTRA=()
      
      while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
          arg="$1"
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              install)        MODE="install" ;;
              --device|--adb|--zip)
                  INSTALL_EXTRA+=("$arg" "${2:-}")
                  shift ;;
              --no-reboot|--no-verify)
                  INSTALL_EXTRA+=("$arg") ;;
              fod-build|--fod-build) MODE="fodbuild" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --xiaomi-fod)   XIAOMI_FOD=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              # Exported, so a menu that shells out for a build does not ask again.
              --no-su)        export TREBLE_NO_SU=1 ;;
              -V|--version)   echo "Treble RRO Creator ${TOOL_VERSION}"; exit 0 ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
          shift
      done
      
      # No arguments and a terminal to talk on: the menu. Everything scripted passes
      # a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          MODE="menu"
      fi
      
      # --device, --zip and --no-reboot belong to install; taking them with another
      # verb and quietly ignoring them would look like they had been used.
      if [ "${#INSTALL_EXTRA[@]}" -gt 0 ] && [ "$MODE" != "install" ]; then
          err "            ${INSTALL_EXTRA[0]} only applies to 'install'"
          usage
          exit 2
      fi
      
      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).
      wsl_guard
      
      # Termux: the one root prompt of the session, asked before any screen is drawn.
      # -y means "unattended", and an unattended run must not stop for a tap.
      [ "$ASSUME_YES" = true ] || termux_root_handoff
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Dispatch
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      case "$MODE" in
          menu)
              # The terminal front end. It shells out to this same script for a build,
              # so a build started from the menu is the build a user would type.
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/menu.sh"
              menu_main
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          doctor)
              if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
              ;;
      
          setup)
              banner "Setup — build tools"
              migrate_layout
              # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
              # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
              # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
              # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
              # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
              if $ASSUME_YES; then
                  ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
              else
                  ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
              fi
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          check)
              # Config validation only: no tools, no output.
              CHECK_MODE=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          fodbuild)
              # Maintainers only: the shipped helper is prebuilt on purpose, so no
              # user path reaches Go for it.
              bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/fod-build.sh"
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          install)
              migrate_layout
              # A child, not a source: it parses its own options and can be run on its
              # own (bash stuff/scripts/install-module.sh --zip out/x-ksu.zip).
              bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/install-module.sh" ${INSTALL_EXTRA[@]+"${INSTALL_EXTRA[@]}"}
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          clean)
              migrate_layout
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/clean.sh"
              ;;
      
          dryrun)
              # Needs config.env and the resource generators, no toolchain: the point
              # is to see the plan in seconds.
              DRY_RUN=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          build)
              # Move any files left in the old top-level layout into src/.
              migrate_layout
              if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Windows"
              elif $IS_TERMUX; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Termux"
              else
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Linux"
              fi
              # Installs only what is missing; prints a summary and returns non-zero
              # when the machine still cannot build.
              ensure_toolchain auto
              # The installer may just have created stuff/tools/, so refresh PATH.
              tools_on_path
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      esac

      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Files
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Where a copy lands on the phone. /sdcard is the same folder whether it is this
      # phone (Termux, where ~/storage/shared points at it) or a cabled one (adb), so
      # the path in the message is one a reader can go and look in either way.
      FILES_PHONE_DIR="/sdcard/treble-rro-creator"
      
      # The build's own outputs, one path per line: the flashable zips and the APKs
      # sitting inside them.
      built_files() {
          find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.apk' \) 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort
      }
      
      # files_copy_to_phone — put the build on the phone's shared storage.
      #
      # On the phone itself (Termux) that is a plain cp, once Termux has been given
      # access to /sdcard. From a computer it is `adb push`, because the build tree is
      # on the wrong side of the cable; the destination is the same folder, so the
      # instructions afterwards do not depend on which machine ran the build.
      files_copy_to_phone() {
          local -a files=()
          local f base="" dest copied=0 failed=0 src
          while IFS= read -r f; do files+=("$f"); done < <(built_files)
          if [ "${#files[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              info "Nothing to copy yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
              return 0
          fi
      
          if device_is_termux; then
              # ~/storage/shared only exists after termux-setup-storage; /sdcard is
              # still worth trying because some builds of Termux ship it ready.
              if [ -d "$HOME/storage/shared" ]; then
                  base="$HOME/storage/shared"
              elif [ -d /sdcard ]; then
                  base="/sdcard"
              fi
              if [ -z "$base" ]; then
                  err "Termux cannot see this phone's storage."
                  echo "     Run: termux-setup-storage"
                  echo "     Then: 8 → 1 again"
                  return 1
              fi
              dest="$base/treble-rro-creator"
              if ! mkdir -p "$dest" 2>/dev/null; then
                  err "Cannot create $FILES_PHONE_DIR."
                  echo "     Run: termux-setup-storage   (it asks for the storage permission)"
                  return 1
              fi
              info "Copying ${#files[@]} file(s) to $FILES_PHONE_DIR..."
              for f in "${files[@]}"; do
                  if cp -f "$f" "$dest/" 2>/dev/null; then
                      ui_mark ok "$(basename "$f")  $(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"
                      copied=$((copied + 1))
                  else
                      ui_mark bad "$(basename "$f") — could not be written"
                      failed=$((failed + 1))
                  fi
              done
          else

              # phone that is not plugged in goes nowhere.
              if ! resolve_adb; then
                  err "adb was not found — install platform-tools and try again."
                  return 1
              fi
              adb_pick_device "$adb" "" "files" || return 1
              if ! "$adb" ${DEVICE_SERIAL:+-s "$DEVICE_SERIAL"} shell "mkdir -p $FILES_PHONE_DIR" \
                      >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  err "Could not create $FILES_PHONE_DIR on the phone."
                  echo "     Check that the phone is unlocked and the storage is not full."

              info "Pushing ${#files[@]} file(s) to $FILES_PHONE_DIR..."

                      ui_mark ok "$(basename "$f")  $(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"
                      copied=$((copied + 1))
                  else
                      ui_mark bad "$(basename "$f") — adb push failed"
                      failed=$((failed + 1))
                  fi
              done
          fi
      
          echo ""
          if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
              warn "$copied copied, $failed failed."
              return 1
          fi

          ui_mark note "Open Files on the phone, or flash the module from there."
          return 0
      }

      probe_source_ask() {
          [ -z "$probe_local" ] || return 0
          device_is_termux || return 0
          echo ""
          echo "  This is Termux, so the phone is this one rather than a device on a cable."
          echo "  Reading it directly needs root: the same getprop, cmd overlay, wm and"
          echo "  dumpsys reads a PC makes over adb."
          if confirm "  Read this phone as root? [Y/n] " y; then
              if device_local_begin "menu"; then
                  probe_local=1
              else
                  probe_local=0
              fi
          else
              probe_local=0
          fi
          # The menu itself never reads a phone; only the answer is passed on.
          DEVICE_LOCAL=0
          export DEVICE_LOCAL_REQUEST="$probe_local"
          echo ""
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Probes
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # device-probe.sh, udfps-probe.sh and device-id.sh all print a report and, with
      # --write, put the winners in config.env. That is the only difference between
      # the two answers here, so the submenu asks it instead of inventing options.
      # Ctrl-C is how the probes' device wait is left ("up to 120s; Ctrl-C stops
      # this"). A script's bash shares the foreground process group with the child it
      # is waiting on, so the interrupt reaches this menu too: without the trap the
      # whole menu died and the user lost their place. The trap lets the probe exit on
      # its own while the menu stays put; 130 is the probe's "interrupted" code, so in
      # that case there is no report to read and nothing to press a key for.
      probe_run() {
          local rc=0
          trap ':' INT
          bash "$@" || rc=$?
          trap - INT
          # Never return the probe's status: build.sh runs this with `set -e`, so a
          # 130 here would end the menu as surely as the signal did.
          if [ "$rc" -eq 130 ]; then return 0; fi
          pause_menu || true
          return 0
      }
      
      probe_menu() { # <title> <script> <note>
          local title="$1" script="$2" note="$3" dir
          while :; do
              probe_source_ask
              ui_heading "$title"
              # ui_mark wraps the note itself: a one-paragraph description on a
              # phone-width terminal used to run off the edge.
              [ -n "$note" ] && ui_mark note "$note" && echo ""
              local who='the connected phone'
              [ "$probe_local" = 1 ] && who='this phone'
              ui_item 1 "Read $who" 'report only, nothing written' 24
              ui_item 2 "Read $who" 'and write the answers to config.env' 24
              ui_item 3 'Read a firmware folder' 'an unpacked ROM instead of a running phone' 24
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 24
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) probe_run "$script" ;;
                  2) probe_run "$script" --write ;;
                  3)
                      menu_read "  folder holding the unpacked ROM" || return 0
                      dir="$MENU_ANSWER"
                      [ -n "$dir" ] || continue
                      if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
                          warn "No such folder: $dir"
                          continue
                      fi
                      if confirm "  Write what it finds to config.env? [y/N] " n; then
                          probe_run "$script" --firmware "$dir" --write
                      else
                          probe_run "$script" --firmware "$dir"
                      fi
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      menu_device() {
          probe_menu "Device" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/device-id.sh" \
              "Reads DEVICE_MANUFACTURER, DEVICE_MODEL and DEVICE_CODENAME, and the module condition."
      }
      
      menu_detect() {
          probe_menu "Auto Detect" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/device-probe.sh" \
              "What the ROM says about the hardware: cutout path, corner radius, status bar height, refresh rates, VoLTE and 5G flags, the light sensor and the OEM switches. Anything it cannot read is reported, not guessed."
      }
      
      menu_udfps() {
          probe_menu "UDFPS" "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh" \
              "The in-display fingerprint sensor's centre and radius."
      }
      
      menu_match() {
          probe_source_ask
          probe_run "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/match-prop.sh"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Main loop
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_main() {
          while :; do
              menu_header
              echo ""
              menu_items
              echo ""
              menu_read "  >" || { echo ""; return 0; }
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) menu_build ;;
                  2) menu_config ;;
                  3) menu_addons ;;
                  4) menu_device ;;
                  5) menu_detect ;;
                  6) menu_udfps ;;
                  7) menu_match ;;
                  8) menu_files ;;
                  9) menu_docs ;;
                  q|Q|quit|exit) return 0 ;;
                  '') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Pick a number from the list, or q to quit." ;;
              esac
              [ "$MENU_SLEEP" = "0" ] || sleep "$MENU_SLEEP"
          done
      }
      
      # Standalone: `bash stuff/scripts/menu.sh`. Sourced by build.sh, which calls
      # menu_main itself.
      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
          menu_main
      fi

Two things worth knowing before the first build:

- **`src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` must be yours.** Until you replace it, the empty template is detected and left out of the APK rather than overwriting the GSI's battery and CPU data. See [docs/device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
- **No `config.env` yet?** The first run offers the filled-in Samsung A90 5G example (`config.env.example`) or writes a placeholder that says what to edit.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `./build.sh` | Terminal menu; a plain build when there is no terminal |
| `./build.sh build` | Build, installing missing tools first |
| `./build.sh setup` | Install or repair the toolchain |
| `./build.sh doctor` | Check the toolchain, change nothing (exit 0 = ready) |
| `./build.sh check` | Validate `config.env`, build nothing |
| `./build.sh --dry-run` | Print every resource the config emits, build nothing |
| `./build.sh install` | Copy the newest zip to the phone, install it, reboot, verify it is live |
| `./build.sh clean` | Remove `stuff/build/` and `out/` |
| `./build.sh clean --all` | Start over for a different device (restores templates) |
| `./build.sh menu` | Force the menu when there is no terminal |
| `./build.sh --version` | Print the version (also `-V`; it is the single line in `stuff/VERSION`) |

Flags: `-y` / `--yes`, `--with-vendor-hals`, `--xiaomi-fod`, `--allow-unknown-resources`, `--force` (with `setup`), `--no-su` (Termux: skip the up-front root question), `--help`. With `install`: `--device SERIAL`, `--zip PATH`, `--no-reboot`. Same words on Windows with `build.cmd`.

`--dry-run` is the fast loop: it prints type, name, value and target APK for each resource without aapt2, signing or packaging.

To check the project itself (scripts, resource writer, docs anchors), run `bash stuff/tests/run.sh` — this is what CI runs, and it needs no Android tools.

## Output

| File | Use |
|---|---|
| `out/<name>-ksu.zip` | **The module.** Install in Magisk, KernelSU, KSU Next or APatch, then reboot |
| `out/apks/<name>.apk` | Signed framework overlay |
| `out/apks/<name>-systemui.apk` | Signed SystemUI overlay, when generated |
| `out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip` | Source tree to submit to the [Doze-off overlay repo](https://github.com/Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay) |
| `out/<name>-hardware-overlay-test.zip` | Test module for that source tree |
| `out/<name>-overrides.txt` | Every resource marked `APPLIES` or `IGNORED` against the target framework |

The `-ksu` suffix is historical; the zip is a standard module and works in all four managers. To copy the build to `/sdcard/treble-rro-creator`, use `8` Files → `1` Copy.

> **KernelSU / KSU Next:** mount with Magic Mount, or Hybrid Mount in magic mode. OverlayFS mounts fine but turns one bad `sepolicy.rule` or VINTF fragment into a bootloop. Reasoning in [docs/how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md#the-flashable-module).

Two more things the build will not do for you: do not copy the APKs into `/system/product/overlay/` by hand (dynamic partitions drop them and the module's permissions are missing), and expect the overlays to be static — Android enables them at boot, `cmd overlay enable` changes nothing afterwards.

## After installing

**WebUI.** The module carries a page in `webroot/`. Open it from the manager (KernelSU, KSU Next, APatch) and change corner radius, status bar height or paddings without rebuilding: it writes the value into `resources.arsc` of the installed APK and restarts the framework. Magisk needs a WebUI host such as WebUI X, KsuWebUI or MMRL. Notes: [docs/webui.md](docs/webui.md).

**Addons.** Tweaks that are not `config.env` keys: volume panel side, keep-screen-on, hide clock, 180° rotation, notch masking. Pick them in the app under Addons; live ones are re-applied on boot, overlay ones are written into the APK. List: [docs/addons.md](docs/addons.md).

**Submitting to the GSI.** `out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip` contains the folders, the `overlay.mk` lines and a filled-in `HOW-TO-SUBMIT.md`. Read [docs/submission.md](docs/submission.md) before the pull request — the wiki's `+*brand/model*` pattern never matches, and the zip writes the exact property value instead.

# restore_from_release() is what clean.sh and build.sh call. Run it against a
# throwaway repository with a deliberately stale fallback, and once without
# .git, because "start over" silently returning old values is the failure mode.
step "restore picks the release, not the stale copy"
restore_here="$(pwd)"
restore_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-restore)"
if (
    cd "$restore_tmp" || exit 1
    git init -q . && git config user.email t@example.com && git config user.name t || exit 1
    # No .gitattributes here, and Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true,
    # which would check the file back out with CRLF and fail the greps below.
    git config core.autocrlf false
    mkdir -p src/module stuff/templates/recoveries
    printf 'KEY="released"\n' > config.env
    printf 'released rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
    printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
    printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
    git add -A && git commit -qm one || exit 1
    # The user edits both files; the fallback copies are stale.
    printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
    printf 'my rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
    ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env" && restore_from_release src/module/sepolicy.rule "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 2
    grep -qx 'KEY="released"' config.env || { echo "git restore did not win: $(cat config.env)"; exit 3; }
    grep -qx 'released rules' src/module/sepolicy.rule || exit 4
    # No .git (a zip download): the bundled copy is the only source left.
    rm -rf .git
    printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
    ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 6
    grep -q 'STALE' config.env || { echo "fallback was not used without git"; exit 7; }
); then
    echo "restore behaves"
else
    echo "restore test failed (exit $?)"
    status=1
fi
rm -rf "$restore_tmp"

if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then

else

step "udfps helper compiles for android/arm64"
# src/module/fod/xiaomi-fod is a committed binary, rebuilt by
# `./build.sh fod-build`. Nothing else compiles it for its real target here: the
# go test step above builds main.go for the host (its `linux` build tag), which
# would not catch an android-only mistake. A compile is the whole check — the

# fail for the wrong reason.
if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    fod_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-fod)"
    if (cd src/module/fod && GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=off \
        go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o "$fod_tmp/xiaomi-fod" main.go); then

ui_mark() {
    local kind="$1" text="$2" indent="${3:-2}" glyph color line first=1 pad
    case "$kind" in
        ok)   glyph="$UI_TICK";  color="$UI_GREEN" ;;
        warn) glyph="$UI_WARN";  color="$UI_YELLOW" ;;
        bad)  glyph="$UI_CROSS"; color="$UI_RED" ;;
        *)    glyph="$UI_DOT";   color="$UI_DIM" ;;
    esac
    printf -v pad '%*s' $((indent + 2)) ''
    ui_wrap "$text" $((indent + 2)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [ "$first" = 1 ]; then
            printf '%*s%s%s%s %s\n' "$indent" '' "$color" "$glyph" "$UI_OFF" "${line#"$pad"}"
            first=0
        else
            printf '%s\n' "$line"
        fi
    done
}
ui_item() {
    local num="$1" label="$2" detail="${3:-}" lw="${4:-${#2}}" cols head line
    cols=$(ui_cols)
    # A label wider than the column (a long section title) widens the column
    # rather than being cut or pushing the description out of line.
    [ "$lw" -ge "${#label}" ] || lw=${#label}
    head="  $(printf '%3s' "$num")  "
    # A label longer than the window is a section header somewhere in config.env
    # — `Overlay repo submission (Doze-off, submission only)` — and it runs off a
    # phone. It wraps under the number, and the description follows it there.
    # The head is 2 spaces, three for the number and two after it: seven.
    if [ $(( 7 + ${#label} )) -ge "$cols" ]; then
        printf '  %s%3s%s\n' "$UI_BLUE" "$num" "$UI_OFF"
        ui_wrap "$label" 7 $((cols - 8)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
            printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
        done
        [ -n "$detail" ] || return 0
        ui_wrap "$detail" 9 $((cols - 10)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
            printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
        done
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$UI_BLUE" "$head" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_BOLD" "$label"
    if [ -z "$detail" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
        return 0
    fi
    # 7 for the number column and its gaps, 2 between label and description.
    if [ $(( 7 + lw + 2 + ${#detail} )) -le "$cols" ]; then

            ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
            # A size or a zone on its own line means nothing without the column
            # it came from, so the header word leads it: `Size 12K`.
            printf '\n  %s%s%s %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "${heads[0]}" "$UI_OFF" \
                "$UI_BOLD" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}" "$UI_OFF"
            line=""
            for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                [ -n "$cell" ] || continue
                if [ -z "$line" ]; then line="$cell"; else line="$line $UI_DOT $cell"; fi
            done
            [ -n "$line" ] || continue
            ui_wrap "$line" 4 | while IFS= read -r cell; do
                printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$cell" "$UI_OFF"
            done
        done
        return 0
    fi

    # Every column but the last is padded; the last one is printed as it is, so
    # a table does not leave a trail of spaces a terminal will happily select.
    printf '\n  %s' "$UI_BOLD"
    for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do
        if [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ]; then
            printf '%-*s  ' "${widths[$k]}" "${heads[$k]}"
        else
            printf '%s' "${heads[$k]}"
        fi
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
    printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$total" "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
    for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
        ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
        printf '  %s' "$UI_DIM"
        printf '%-*s' "${widths[0]}" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}"
        printf '%s  ' "$UI_OFF"
        for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
            if [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ]; then
                printf '%-*s  ' "${widths[$k]}" "${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
            else
                printf '%s' "${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
            fi
        done
        printf '\n'
    done
}

{
  "path": "stuff/scripts/profiles.sh",
  "instructions": "Start the profile store script: header, paths, listing helpers.",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# =============================================================================\n# profiles.sh — saved config.env setups, one per device\n# =============================================================================\n# config.env holds one device: one codename, one corner radius, one match\n# property. Anyone who builds for more than one phone used to keep copies by\n# hand (`config.env.a90`, `config.env.zephyr`) and remember which was which.\n#\n# A profile is just that copy, in a place the tool knows about:\n#\n#   stuff/profiles/p1/name        \"Zephyr (Redmi Note 17)\"\n#   stuff/profiles/p1/config.env  that device's answers\n#   stuff/profiles/active         \"p1\", the one config.env currently holds\n#\n# config.env at the root stays the file everything reads and writes; a profile\n# is a copy of it. Switching copies the target over config.env first and saves\n# what was there into the profile it came from, so a profile is only ever as\n# stale as the file is.\n#\n# Used by the terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh → 'p') and by the app\n# (gui/profiles.go), so both do the same thing to the same files.\n#\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh list      one line per profile, tab separated\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh show      the same, as a table\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh new NAME  copy config.env, switch to the copy\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh switch ID\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh rename ID NAME\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh delete ID\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh save      fold config.env into the active one\n# =============================================================================\n\nif [ -z \"${ROOT:-}\" ]; then\n    ROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../..\" && pwd)\"\n    export ROOT\nfi\n. \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh\"\n\nPROFILES_DIR=\"${PROFILES_DIR:-$ROOT/stuff/profiles}\"\nPROFILES_MAX_NAME=40\n\n# Profiles are numbered p1, p2, … This is also the guard against a path: only\n# that shape ever reaches a rm -rf below.\nprofiles_valid_id() { [[ \"$1\" =~ ^p[0-9]{1,6}$ ]]; }\n\nprofiles_ids() {\n    local d\n    [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR\" ] || return 0\n    for d in \"$PROFILES_DIR\"/p*/; do\n        [ -d \"$d\" ] || continue\n        d=\"${d%/}\"\n        profiles_valid_id \"${d##*/}\" && printf '%s\\n' \"${d##*/}\"\n    done | sort -t p -k 2 -n\n}"
}

Prints the new id.\nprofiles_new_with() {\n    local name id n src\n    mkdir -p \"$PROFILES_DIR\" || return 1\n    n=1\n    while [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR/p$n\" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done\n    id=\"p$n\"\n    name=\"$(profiles_clean_name \"${1:-}\")\"\n    [ -n \"$name\" ] || name=\"Profile #$n\"\n    mkdir -p \"$PROFILES_DIR/$id\" || return 1\n    src=\"$ROOT/config.env\"\n    [ -f \"$src\" ] || src=\"$ROOT/config.env.example\"\n    if [ -f \"$src\" ]; then\n        cp -f \"$src\" \"$(profiles_cfg \"$id\")\" || return 1\n    else\n        : >\"$(profiles_cfg \"$id\")\" || return 1\n    fi\n    printf '%s\\n' \"$name\" >\"$(profiles_name_file \"$id\")\" || return 1\n    profiles_set_active \"$id\" || return 1\n    printf '%s' \"$id\"\n}",

# profiles_new [NAME] — save this one, then carry on in a copy of it.
profiles_new() {
    local id
    profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    id="$(profiles_new_with "${1:-}")" || return 1
    profiles_switch "$id" || return 1
    printf '%s' "$id"

profiles_rename() {
    local id="$1" name
    profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
    profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
    name="$(profiles_clean_name "${2:-}")"
    if [ -z "$name" ]; then
        printf 'profiles: a profile needs a name\n' >&2
        return 2
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$name" >"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || return 1
    return 0
}
