# profiles_save — fold config.env into the profile it belongs to.
# Nothing else writes a profile, so this is also what keeps a switch from
# throwing away edits made since the last one.
profiles_save() {
    local id
    id="$(profiles_active)"
    [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
    [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ] || return 1
    mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
    cp -f "$ROOT/config.env" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
    return 0
}

# profiles_new_with NAME -> create the next profile and make it active.
# It starts as a copy of config.env (that is the point: one device's answers,
# tweaked for the next), or of the example on a checkout with no config.env
# yet. Prints the new id.
profiles_new_with() {
    local name id n src
    mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
    n=1
    while [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/p$n" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
    id="p$n"
    name="$(profiles_clean_name "${1:-}")"
    [ -n "$name" ] || name="Profile #$n"
    mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
    src="$ROOT/config.env"
    [ -f "$src" ] || src="$ROOT/config.env.example"
    if [ -f "$src" ]; then
        cp -f "$src" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
    else
        : >"$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$name" >"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || return 1
    profiles_set_active "$id" || return 1
    printf '%s' "$id"
}

# The same thing for a person: a table with the profile in use marked.
profiles_print() {
    local -a rows=() ids=()
    local id active n=0 mark name device
    profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    active="$(profiles_active)"
    for id in $(profiles_ids); do ids+=("$id"); done
    if [ "${#ids[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf '  no profiles yet\n'
        return 0
    fi
    for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        if [ "$id" = "$active" ]; then
            rows+=("*|$(n) $(profiles_name "$id")|$(profiles_identity "$id")")
        else
            rows+=(" |$(n) $(profiles_name "$id")|$(profiles_identity "$id")")
        fi
    done
    if command -v ui_table >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ui_table 'Use|Profile|Device' "${rows[@]}"
    else
        printf '\n'
        for id in "${rows[@]}"; do
            IFS='|' read -r mark name device <<<"$id"
            printf '  %s %-32s %s\n' "$mark" "$name" "$device"
        done
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Command line
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Same verbs from a script, from the menu, or by hand:
#
#   ./build.sh profiles                 the list
#   ./build.sh profiles new "Zephyr"    copy config.env and switch to the copy
#   ./build.sh profiles switch p2       load p2 into config.env
profiles_cli() {
    local id
    case "${1:-show}" in
        show|'') profiles_print ;;
        list) profiles_list ;;
        active) profiles_active ;;
        save) profiles_save ;;
        switch|use) profiles_switch "${2:-}" ;;
        new|create)
            id="$(profiles_new "${2:-}")" || return 1
            [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
            printf 'profiles: %s — config.env now holds it\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
            ;;
        rename) profiles_rename "${2:-}" "${3:-}" ;;
        delete|remove) profiles_delete "${2:-}" ;;
        *)
            printf 'profiles: unknown command: %s\n' "$1" >&2
            printf 'try: show, list, new, switch, rename, delete, save, active\n' >&2
            return 2
            ;;
    esac
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
    profiles_cli "$@"
fi

profiles_set_active() {
    mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$1" >"$PROFILES_DIR/active"
}

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# =============================================================================\n# profiles.sh — saved config.env setups, one per device\n# =============================================================================\n# config.env holds one device: one codename, one corner radius, one match\n# property. Anyone who builds for more than one phone used to keep copies by\n# hand (`config.env.a90`, `config.env.zephyr`) and remember which was which.\n#\n# A profile is that copy, in a place the tool knows about:\n#\n#   stuff/profiles/p1/name        \"Zephyr (Redmi Note 17)\"\n#   stuff/profiles/p1/config.env  that device's answers\n#   stuff/profiles/active         \"p1\" — the profile config.env holds right now\n#\n# config.env at the root stays the file everything reads; a profile is a copy of\n# it. Switching saves what config.env holds into the profile it came from, then\n# copies the target over config.env, so a profile is only ever as stale as the\n# file is. Nothing else writes one.\n#\n# The terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh → 'p') and the app (gui/profiles.go)\n# both come through here, so they do the same thing to the same files.\n#\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh show        the list, for a person\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh list        the list, tab separated\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh new \"NAME\"  copy config.env, switch to it\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh switch p2\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh rename p2 \"Note 17\"\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh delete p3\n#   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh save        fold config.env into the active one\n# =============================================================================\n\nif [ -z \"${ROOT:-}\" ]; then\n    ROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../..\" && pwd)\"\n    export ROOT\nfi\n. \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh\"\n\nPROFILES_DIR=\"${PROFILES_DIR:-$ROOT/stuff/profiles}\"\nPROFILES_MAX_NAME=40\n\n# Profiles are numbered p1, p2, … with no exceptions, which is also the guard\n# against a path: only that shape ever reaches the rm -rf in profiles_delete.\nprofiles_valid_id() { [[ \"$1\" =~ ^p[0-9]{1,6}$ ]]; }\n\nprofiles_ids() {\n    local d\n    [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR\" ] || return 0\n    for d in \"$PROFILES_DIR\"/p*/; do\n        [ -d \"$d\" ] || continue\n        d=\"${d%/}\"\n        profiles_valid_id \"${d##*/}\" && printf '%s\\n' \"${d##*/}\"\n    done | sort -t p -k 2 -n\n}\n\nprofiles_has() { [ -n \"${1:-}\" ] && [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR/$1\" ]; }\nprofiles_cfg() { printf '%s/%s/config.env' \"$PROFILES_DIR\" \"$1\"; }\nprofiles_name_file() { printf '%s/%s/name' \"$PROFILES_DIR\" \"$1\"; }\n\n# The profile config.env belongs to, or nothing on a checkout that has none.\nprofiles_active() {\n    local id=\"\"\n    if [ -f \"$PROFILES_DIR/active\" ]; then\n        IFS= read -r id <\"$PROFILES_DIR/active\" || id=\"\"\n    fi\n    profiles_valid_id \"$id\" || return 0\n    profiles_has \"$id\" || return 0\n    printf '%s' \"$id\"\n}\n\nprofiles_set_active() {\n    mkdir -p \"$PROFILES_DIR\" || return 1\n    printf '%s\\n' \"$1\" >\"$PROFILES_DIR/active\"\n}\n\n# A name is one line and fits a menu column. Anything else (a newline from a\n# paste, a name too long for the table) is cleaned here rather than at each\n# caller.\nprofiles_clean_name() {\n    local name\n    name=\"$(printf '%s' \"${1:-}\" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\\000-\\037\\177')\"\n    name=\"${name#\"${name%%[![:space:]]*}\"}\"\n    name=\"${name%\"${name##*[![:space:]]}\"}\"\n    while [ \"${#name}\" -gt 0 ] && [ \"${name: -1}\" = ' ' ]; do name=\"${name% }\" ; done\n    if [ \"${#name}\" -gt \"$PROFILES_MAX_NAME\" ]; then\n        name=\"${name:0:$PROFILES_MAX_NAME}\"\n    fi\n    printf '%s' \"$name\"\n}\n\nprofiles_name() {\n    local id=\"$1\" name=\"\"\n    if [ -f \"$(profiles_name_file \"$id\")\" ]; then\n        IFS= read -r name <\"$(profiles_name_file \"$id\")\" || name=\"\"\n    fi\n    name=\"$(profiles_clean_name \"$name\")\"\n    [ -n \"$name\" ] || name=\"Profile #${id#p}\"\n    printf '%s' \"$name\"\n}"
}

For\n# the profile in use the live file wins: it may have been edited a minute ago,\n# and the list should not show yesterday's answer.\nprofiles_identity() {\n    local id=\"$1\" f manuf model code\n    if [ \"$id\" = \"$(profiles_active)\" ] && [ -f \"$ROOT/config.env\" ]; then\n        f=\"$ROOT/config.env\"\n    else\n        f=\"$(profiles_cfg \"$id\")\"\n    fi\n    [ -f \"$f\" ] || { printf 'no config.env'; return 0; }\n    manuf=\"$(CFG_FILE=\"$f\" cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)\"\n    model=\"$(CFG_FILE=\"$f\" cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)\"\n    code=\"$(CFG_FILE=\"$f\" cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)\"\n    if [ -z \"$manuf\" ] && [ -z \"$model\" ] && [ -z \"$code\" ]; then\n        printf 'no device set'\n        return 0\n    fi\n    printf '%s %s (%s)' \"$manuf\" \"$model\" \"$code\" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'\n}\n\n# Fold config.env into the profile it belongs to. This is also what keeps a\n# switch from throwing away edits made since the last one.\nprofiles_save() {\n    local id\n    id=\"$(profiles_active)\"\n    [ -n \"$id\" ] || return 1\n    [ -f \"$ROOT/config.env\" ] || return 1\n    mkdir -p \"$PROFILES_DIR/$id\" || return 1\n    cp -f \"$ROOT/config.env\" \"$(profiles_cfg \"$id\")\" || return 1\n    return 0\n}\n\n# Create the next profile and make it active. It starts as a copy of config.env\n# (that is the point: one device's answers, tweaked for the next), or of the\n# example on a checkout that has no config.env yet. Prints the new id.\nprofiles_new_with() {\n    local name id n src\n    mkdir -p \"$PROFILES_DIR\" || return 1\n    n=1\n    while [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR/p$n\" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done\n    id=\"p$n\"\n    name=\"$(profiles_clean_name \"${1:-}\")\"\n    [ -n \"$name\" ] || name=\"Profile #$n\"\n    mkdir -p \"$PROFILES_DIR/$id\" || return 1\n    src=\"$ROOT/config.env\"\n    [ -f \"$src\" ] || src=\"$ROOT/config.env.example\"\n    if [ -f \"$src\" ]; then\n        cp -f \"$src\" \"$(profiles_cfg \"$id\")\" || return 1\n    else\n        : >\"$(profiles_cfg \"$id\")\" || return 1\n    fi\n    printf '%s\\n' \"$name\" >\"$(profiles_name_file \"$id\")\" || return 1\n    profiles_set_active \"$id\" || return 1\n    printf '%s' \"$id\"\n}\n\n# A checkout that has never seen a profile gets Profile #1 from whatever\n# config.env holds, so the first look at the list is not an empty box.\nprofiles_ensure() {\n    local id\n    id=\"$(profiles_active)\"\n    [ -n \"$id\" ] && return 0\n    if [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR\" ]; then\n        id=\"$(profiles_ids | head -n 1)\"\n        if [ -n \"$id\" ]; then\n            # Profiles exist but the marker was lost, or pointed at a folder\n            # that was deleted out from under it: adopt the first one.\n            profiles_set_active \"$id\"\n            return $?\n        fi\n    fi\n    [ -n \"$(profiles_new_with '')\" ]\n}",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

return 2; }\n    profiles_has \"$id\" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\\n' \"$id\" >&2; return 1; }\n    if [ \"$id\" = \"$(profiles_active)\" ]; then\n        printf 'profiles: %s is the profile in use — switch to another one first\\n' \"$id\" >&2\n        return 1\n    fi\n    total=\"$(profiles_ids | grep -c . || true)\"\n    if [ \"${total:-0}\" -le 1 ]; then\n        printf 'profiles: that is the only profile — there has to be one\\n' >&2\n        return 1\n    fi\n    rm -rf \"$PROFILES_DIR/$id\"\n}",

This is\n# what gui/profiles.go parses; it is not meant for a person to read.\nprofiles_list() {\n    local id active mark\n    profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    active=\"$(profiles_active)\"\n    for id in $(profiles_ids); do\n        mark=0\n        [ \"$id\" = \"$active\" ] && mark=1\n        printf '%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n' \"$id\" \"$mark\" \\\n            \"$(profiles_name \"$id\")\" \"$(profiles_identity \"$id\")\"\n    done\n}\n\n# The same thing for a person: a table with the profile in use marked.\nprofiles_print() {\n    local -a rows=() ids=()\n    local id active n=0 mark name device\n    profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    active=\"$(profiles_active)\"\n    for id in $(profiles_ids); do ids+=(\"$id\"); done\n    if [ \"${#ids[@]}\" -eq 0 ]; then\n        printf '  no profiles yet\\n'\n        return 0\n    fi\n    for id in \"${ids[@]}\"; do\n        n=$((n + 1))\n        mark=' '\n        [ \"$id\" = \"$active\" ] && mark='*'\n        rows+=(\"$mark|$n $(profiles_name \"$id\")|$(profiles_identity \"$id\")\")\n    done\n    if command -v ui_table >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        ui_table 'Use|Profile|Device' \"${rows[@]}\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    printf '\\n'\n    for id in \"${rows[@]}\"; do\n        IFS='|' read -r mark name device <<<\"$id\"\n        printf '  %s %-32s %s\\n' \"$mark\" \"$name\" \"$device\"\n    done\n}",

- path: stuff/scripts/menu.sh
  content: |
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
          . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/profiles.sh"
      # The device-source helpers (device_is_termux, device_local_begin) live with the
      # adb code the probes share. Sourcing it here defines functions only.
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Small things
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MENU_SLEEP="${MENU_SLEEP:-0}"
      
      # A width-aware rule under a section title. Every screen used to draw a fixed
      # 58-character one, which wrapped onto a second line on a phone.
      hr() { ui_rule 2; }
      
      # Read one line. Returns 1 at EOF (piped input, a launcher with no console) so
      # callers can leave the menu instead of looping forever.
      menu_read() {
          local prompt="${1:-} " answer=""
          printf '%s' "$prompt"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              return 1
          fi
          MENU_ANSWER="$answer"
          return 0
      }
      
      # Wait for Enter between screens, unless stdin is not a terminal.
      pause_menu() {
          [ -t 0 ] || return 0
          printf '\n  %s ' "Press Enter to go back"
          read -r _ || true
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # Count the rows config.env has, and how many are switched off.
      cfg_counts() {
          local rows
          rows="$(cfg_rows 2>/dev/null)" || { CFG_ON=0; CFG_OFF=0; return 0; }
          CFG_ON="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 1' | grep -c . || true)"
          CFG_OFF="$(printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -F'\t' '$2 == 0' | grep -c . || true)"
      }
      
      output_summary() {
          local apks=0 zips=0 zip=""
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR/apks" ] && apks="$(find "$OUT_DIR/apks" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && zips="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          zip="$(find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | sort | head -n1)"
          if [ "$zips" -gt 0 ]; then
              printf '%s  (%s APK%s)' "${zip#$ROOT/}" "$apks" "$([ "$apks" = 1 ] || echo s)"
          else
              printf 'nothing built yet'
          fi
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Screen
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The state of the checkout in one box: which phone, how much of config.env is
      # filled in, what the last build left behind.
      menu_header() {
          cfg_counts
          ui_panel "Treble Overlay Creator ${TOOL_VERSION}" \
              "Device|$(cfg_identity)" \
              "config.env|${CFG_ON} set ${UI_DOT} ${CFG_OFF} off" \
              "Output|$(output_summary)"
      }
      
      # 11 is the width of the longest label here, so every description starts in the
      # same column instead of ragging after each label.
      MENU_LW=14
      
      menu_items() {
          ui_item 1 'Build'          'dry run, build, check, doctor, clean' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 2 'config.env'     'browse and edit one key at a time' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 3 'Addons'         'module tweaks: settings and overlay resources' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 4 'Device'         'read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 5 'Auto Detect'    'ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 6 'UDFPS'          'in-display fingerprint geometry' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 7 'Match property' 'which property the submission should match on' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 8 'Files'          'what was built, and where it is' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 9 'Docs'           'the guides in docs/' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item p 'Profiles'       'saved config.env setups: switch, rename, delete' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item q 'Quit' '' "$MENU_LW"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The menu never re-implements a build step: it runs the entry point with the
      # verb a user would type, so `build.sh doctor` and 1 → 4 are the same command.
      run_entry() {
          ( cd "$ROOT" && bash "$ROOT/build.sh" "$@" )
      }
      
      # Whether the Xiaomi FOD helper ships in the module. Off by default: it is only
      # useful on Xiaomi optical UDFPS phones, and on anything else it is a binary
      # that never starts. `./build.sh --xiaomi-fod menu` starts it already on.
      MENU_XIAOMI_FOD="${XIAOMI_FOD:-false}"
      
      # The --xiaomi-fod argument for a build started from here, or nothing at all.
      xiaomi_fod_arg() {
          [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ] && printf '%s' '--xiaomi-fod'
      }
      
      menu_build() {
          while :; do
              if [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ]; then
                  fod_state='on'
              else
                  fod_state='off'
              fi
              ui_heading 'Build'
              ui_item 1 'Dry run'     'print the resources config.env emits, build nothing' 11
              ui_item 2 'Build'       'build the module (installs tools if needed)' 11
              ui_item 3 'Check'       'validate config.env without building' 11
              ui_item 4 'Doctor'      'check the toolchain, install nothing' 11
              ui_item 5 'Clean'       'remove build output' 11
              ui_item 6 'Clean --all' 'start over for a different device' 11
              ui_item 7 'Xiaomi FOD' "$fod_state · HBM + touch-panel FOD mode for Xiaomi UDFPS" 11
              ui_item 8 'Install' "copy out/<name>-ksu.zip to the phone, install it, reboot, check" 11
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 11
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) run_entry --dry-run; pause_menu ;;

- path: stuff/scripts/ui.sh
  content: |
      # ui_item NUM LABEL [DETAIL] — one row of a menu or an option list.
      #
      #   `   1  Auto Detect   cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G`
      #
      # The number is the accent colour, the label bold and the description dim, so
      # the eye follows the label column and can still find a number at a glance. On a
      # phone the description does not fit beside the label, so it moves to its own
      # indented, wrapped line instead of being cut off at the edge.
      ui_item() {
          local num="$1" label="$2" detail="${3:-}" lw="${4:-${#2}}" cols head line
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          # A label wider than the column (a long section title) widens the column
          # rather than being cut or pushing the description out of line.
          [ "$lw" -ge "${#label}" ] || lw=${#label}
          head="  $(printf '%3s' "$num")  "
          # A label longer than the window is a section header somewhere in config.env
          # — `Overlay repo submission (Doze-off, submission only)` — and it runs off a
          # phone. It wraps under the number, and the description follows it there.
          # The head is 2 spaces, three for the number and two after it: seven.
          if [ $(( 7 + ${#label} )) -ge "$cols" ]; then
              printf '  %s%3s%s\n' "$UI_BLUE" "$num" "$UI_OFF"
              ui_wrap "$label" 7 $((cols - 8)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
              done
              [ -n "$detail" ] || return 0
              ui_wrap "$detail" 9 $((cols - 10)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
              done
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s%s%s%s%s' "$UI_BLUE" "$head" "$UI_OFF" "$UI_BOLD" "$label"
          if [ -z "$detail" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          # 7 for the number column and its gaps, 2 between label and description.
          if [ $(( 7 + lw + 2 + ${#detail} )) -le "$cols" ]; then
              printf '%s%*s  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_OFF" $((lw - ${#label})) '' \
                  "$UI_DIM" "$detail" "$UI_OFF"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$detail" 7 $((cols - 8)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_trust_color high|medium|low — green for an answer, red for a gamble.
      # The trust word is the one thing a reader scans a ranked list for, so it is
      # coloured rather than left in the same grey as the rest of the meta line.
      ui_trust_color() {
          case "${1:-}" in
              high) printf '%s' "$UI_GREEN" ;;
              medium) printf '%s' "$UI_YELLOW" ;;
              low|*) printf '%s' "$UI_RED" ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # ui_split TEXT SEP — TEXT split on SEP, one element per field, in UI_SPLIT.
      ui_split() {
          local item
          UI_SPLIT=()
          while IFS= read -r item; do
              UI_SPLIT+=("$item")
          done < <(printf '%s\n' "$1" | tr "$2" '\n')
      }
      
      # ui_table "COL|COL|COL" "CELL|CELL|CELL" ... — an aligned table, or, when the
      # columns would not fit the window, one block per row.
      #
      # Cutting a table in half is worse than folding it: below the width where the
      # natural columns collide, every row becomes its own two-line entry — the key in
      # bold and the rest joined with a dot — which is the same data, stacked, and
      # still comparable down the page.
      ui_table() {
          local header="$1"; shift
          local avail ncols=0 i k w total cell line first
          local -a rows=("$@") heads=() widths=()
          avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
          ui_split "$header" '|'
          heads=("${UI_SPLIT[@]}")
          ncols=${#heads[@]}
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do widths[$k]=${#heads[$k]}; done
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              for k in "${!UI_SPLIT[@]}"; do
                  [ "$k" -lt "$ncols" ] || continue
                  cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]}"
                  [ "${#cell}" -gt "${widths[$k]}" ] && widths[$k]=${#cell}
              done
          done
          total=$(( 2 * (ncols - 1) ))
          for w in "${widths[@]}"; do total=$(( total + w )); done
      
          if [ "$total" -gt "$avail" ]; then
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
                  # A size or a zone on its own line means nothing without the column
                  # it came from, so the header word leads it: `Size 12K`.
                  printf '\n  %s%s%s %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "${heads[0]}" "$UI_OFF" \
                      "$UI_BOLD" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}" "$UI_OFF"
                  line=""
                  for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                      cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                      [ -n "$cell" ] || continue
                      if [ -z "$line" ]; then line="$cell"; else line="$line $UI_DOT $cell"; fi
                  done
                  [ -n "$line" ] || continue
                  ui_wrap "$line" 4 | while IFS= read -r cell; do
                      printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$cell" "$UI_OFF"
                  done
              done
              return 0
          fi
      
          # Every column but the last is padded; the last one is printed as it is, so
          # a table does not leave a trail of spaces a terminal will happily select.
          printf '\n  %s' "$UI_BOLD"
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do
              if [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ]; then
                  printf '%-*s  ' "${widths[$k]}" "${heads[$k]}"
              else
                  printf '%s' "${heads[$k]}"
              fi
          done
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$total" "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              printf '  %s' "$UI_DIM"

  content: |
          printf '%s' "$question"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              info "No terminal input available — using '${default}'."
              answer="$default"
          fi
          [ -z "$answer" ] && answer="$default"
          REPLY="$answer"
      }
      
      # confirm <question> <y|n>   -> returns 0 for yes
      confirm() {
          local question="$1" default="${2:-n}" answer
          ask "$question" "$default"
          answer="$REPLY"
          case "$answer" in
              [Yy]|[Yy][Ee][Ss]) return 0 ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Termux: ask for root once, before anything is drawn
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Reading /vendor/overlay, pulling a vendor prop file and installing the module
      # all need root, and on Termux the first `su` of a session is a prompt from the
      # manager (Magisk, KernelSU, APatch). Asked for in the middle of a build, that
      # prompt lands on top of the screen the tool is drawing; asked for here, it is
      # one question before the menu paints, and the manager remembers the grant for
      # the app, so the rest of the session runs quietly.
      #
      # Nothing is forced: `--no-su` (TREBLE_NO_SU=1) skips it, declining skips it, a
      # phone with no `su` skips it, and without a terminal it is skipped too so a
      # script or CI never waits for a tap that will not come. Sets TERMUX_ROOT=1 when
      # root is available, so callers can tell "granted" from "never asked".
      termux_root_handoff() {
          TERMUX_ROOT=""
          $IS_TERMUX || return 0
          [ "${TREBLE_NO_SU:-0}" = 1 ] && return 0
          [ "$(id -u 2>/dev/null)" = 0 ] && { TERMUX_ROOT=1; return 0; }

- path: stuff/scripts/profiles.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # profiles.sh — saved config.env setups, one per device
      # =============================================================================
      # config.env holds one device: one codename, one corner radius, one match
      # property. Anyone who builds for more than one phone used to keep copies by
      # hand (`config.env.a90`, `config.env.zephyr`) and remember which was which.
      #
      # A profile is that copy, in a place the tool knows about:
      #
      #   stuff/profiles/p1/name        "Zephyr (Redmi Note 17)"
      #   stuff/profiles/p1/config.env  that device's answers
      #   stuff/profiles/active         "p1" — the profile config.env holds right now
      #
      # config.env at the root stays the file everything reads; a profile is a copy of
      # it. Switching saves what config.env holds into the profile it came from, then
      # copies the target over config.env, so a profile is only ever as stale as the
      # file is. Nothing else writes one.
      #
      # The terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh → 'p') and the app (gui/profiles.go)
      # both come through here, so they do the same thing to the same files.
      #
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh show        the list, for a person
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh list        the list, tab separated
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh new "NAME"  copy config.env, switch to it
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh switch p2
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh rename p2 "Note 17"
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh delete p3
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh save        fold config.env into the active one
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      
      PROFILES_DIR="${PROFILES_DIR:-$ROOT/stuff/profiles}"
      PROFILES_MAX_NAME=40
      
      # Profiles are numbered p1, p2, … with no exceptions, which is also the guard
      # against a path: only that shape ever reaches the rm -rf in profiles_delete.
      profiles_valid_id() { [[ "$1" =~ ^p[0-9]{1,6}$ ]]; }
      
      profiles_ids() {
          local d
          [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR" ] || return 0
          for d in "$PROFILES_DIR"/p*/; do
              [ -d "$d" ] || continue
              d="${d%/}"
              profiles_valid_id "${d##*/}" && printf '%s\n' "${d##*/}"
          done | sort -t p -k 2 -n
      }
      
      profiles_has() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/$1" ]; }
      profiles_cfg() { printf '%s/%s/config.env' "$PROFILES_DIR" "$1"; }
      profiles_name_file() { printf '%s/%s/name' "$PROFILES_DIR" "$1"; }
      
      # The profile config.env belongs to, or nothing on a checkout that has none.
      profiles_active() {
          local id=""
          if [ -f "$PROFILES_DIR/active" ]; then
              IFS= read -r id <"$PROFILES_DIR/active" || id=""
          fi
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || return 0
          profiles_has "$id" || return 0
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      profiles_set_active() {
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
          printf '%s\n' "$1" >"$PROFILES_DIR/active"
      }
      
      # A name is one line and fits a menu column. Anything else (a newline from a
      # paste, a name too long for the table) is cleaned here rather than at each
      # caller.
      profiles_clean_name() {
          local name
          name="$(printf '%s' "${1:-}" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\037\177')"
          name="${name#"${name%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
          name="${name%"${name##*[![:space:]]}"}"
          while [ "${#name}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${name: -1}" = ' ' ]; do name="${name% }" ; done
          if [ "${#name}" -gt "$PROFILES_MAX_NAME" ]; then
              name="${name:0:$PROFILES_MAX_NAME}"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$name"
      }
      
      profiles_name() {
          local id="$1" name=""
          if [ -f "$(profiles_name_file "$id")" ]; then
              IFS= read -r name <"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || name=""
          fi
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "$name")"
          [ -n "$name" ] || name="Profile #${id#p}"
          printf '%s' "$name"
      }
      
      # Manufacturer, model and codename as that profile's config.env has them. For
      # the profile in use the live file wins: it may have been edited a minute ago,
      # and the list should not show yesterday's answer.
      profiles_identity() {
          local id="$1" f manuf model code
          if [ "$id" = "$(profiles_active)" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
              f="$ROOT/config.env"
          else
              f="$(profiles_cfg "$id")"
          fi
          [ -f "$f" ] || { printf 'no config.env'; return 0; }
          manuf="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)"
          model="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)"
          code="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)"
          if [ -z "$manuf" ] && [ -z "$model" ] && [ -z "$code" ]; then
              printf 'no device set'
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s %s (%s)' "$manuf" "$model" "$code" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'
      }
      
      # Fold config.env into the profile it belongs to. This is also what keeps a
      # switch from throwing away edits made since the last one.
      profiles_save() {
          local id
          id="$(profiles_active)"
          [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
          [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ] || return 1
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
          cp -f "$ROOT/config.env" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
          return 0

- path: stuff/scripts/profiles.sh
  content: |
          return 0
      }
      
      # Create the next profile and make it active. It starts as a copy of config.env
      # (that is the point: one device's answers, tweaked for the next), or of the
      # example on a checkout that has no config.env yet. Prints the new id.
      profiles_new_with() {
          local name id n src
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
          n=1
          while [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/p$n" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
          id="p$n"
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "${1:-}")"
          [ -n "$name" ] || name="Profile #$n"
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
          src="$ROOT/config.env"
          [ -f "$src" ] || src="$ROOT/config.env.example"
          if [ -f "$src" ]; then
              cp -f "$src" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
          else
              : >"$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$name" >"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || return 1
          profiles_set_active "$id" || return 1
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      # A checkout that has never seen a profile gets Profile #1 from whatever
      # config.env holds, so the first look at the list is not an empty box.
      profiles_ensure() {
          local id
          id="$(profiles_active)"
          [ -n "$id" ] && return 0
          if [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR" ]; then
              id="$(profiles_ids | head -n 1)"
              if [ -n "$id" ]; then
                  # Profiles exist but the marker was lost, or pointed at a folder
                  # that was deleted out from under it: adopt the first one.
                  profiles_set_active "$id"
                  return $?
              fi
          fi
          [ -n "$(profiles_new_with '')" ]
      }
      
      # Keep what config.env holds, then load that profile into it.
      profiles_switch() {
          local id="$1"
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          profiles_save >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          cp -f "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" "$ROOT/config.env" || return 1
          profiles_set_active "$id" || return 1
          return 0
      }
      
      # Save this one, then carry on in a copy of it.
      profiles_new() {
          local id
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          id="$(profiles_new_with "${1:-}")" || return 1
          profiles_switch "$id" || return 1
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      profiles_rename() {
          local id="$1" name
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "${2:-}")"
          if [ -z "$name" ]; then
              printf 'profiles: a profile needs a name\n' >&2
              return 2
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$name" >"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || return 1
          return 0
      }
      
      # The profile in use is not deletable: config.env would be left belonging to
      # nothing, and one profile is always kept for the same reason.
      profiles_delete() {
          local id="$1" total
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          if [ "$id" = "$(profiles_active)" ]; then
              printf 'profiles: %s is the profile in use — switch to another one first\n' "$id" >&2
              return 1
          fi
          total="$(profiles_ids | grep -c . || true)"
          if [ "${total:-0}" -le 1 ]; then
              printf 'profiles: that is the only profile — there has to be one\n' >&2
              return 1
          fi
          rm -rf "$PROFILES_DIR/$id"
      }
      
      # One line per profile, tab separated: id, active(0|1), name, device. This is
      # what gui/profiles.go parses; it is not meant for a person to read.
      profiles_list() {
          local id active mark
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          active="$(profiles_active)"
          for id in $(profiles_ids); do
              mark=0
              [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark=1
              printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$id" "$mark" \
                  "$(profiles_name "$id")" "$(profiles_identity "$id")"
          done
      }
      
      # The same thing for a person: a table with the profile in use marked.
      profiles_print() {
          local -a rows=() ids=()
          local id active n=0 mark name device
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          active="$(profiles_active)"
          for id in $(profiles_ids); do ids+=("$id"); done
          if [ "${#ids[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              printf '  no profiles yet\n'
              return 0
          fi
          for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
              n=$((n + 1))
              mark=' '
              [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark='*'
              rows+=("$mark|$n $(profiles_name "$id")|$(profiles_identity "$id")")
          done
          if command -v ui_table >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ui_table 'Use|Profile|Device' "${rows[@]}"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '\n'
          for id in "${rows[@]}"; do
              IFS='|' read -r mark name device <<<"$id"
              printf '  %s %-32s %s\n' "$mark" "$name" "$device"
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Command line
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The same verbs from a terminal, from a script, or through build.sh:
      #
      #   ./build.sh profiles                the list
      #   ./build.sh profiles new "Zephyr"   copy config.env and switch to the copy
      #   ./build.sh profiles switch p2      load p2 into config.env
      profiles_cli() {
          local id
          case "${1:-show}" in
              show|'') profiles_print ;;
              list) profiles_list ;;
              active) profiles_active ;;
              save) profiles_save ;;
              switch|use) profiles_switch "${2:-}" ;;
              new|create)
                  id="$(profiles_new "${2:-}")" || return 1
                  [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
                  printf 'profiles: now using "%s" — config.env holds it\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
                  ;;
              rename) profiles_rename "${2:-}" "${3:-}" ;;
              delete|remove) profiles_delete "${2:-}" ;;
              *)
                  printf 'profiles: unknown command: %s\n' "$1" >&2
                  printf 'try: show, list, new, switch, rename, delete, save, active\n' >&2
                  return 2
                  ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # Sourced by build.sh and the menu, which call the functions themselves; run
      # directly, it is the command line above.
      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
          profiles_cli "$@"
          exit $?
      fi

  content: |
      package main
      
      import (
        "context"
        "crypto/rand"
        "embed"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "io/fs"
        "net"
        "net/http"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "regexp"
        "runtime"
        "sort"
        "strings"
        "time"
      )
      
      //go:embed ui
      var uiFiles embed.FS
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Why the UI is served at all
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The window is a webview pointed at a loopback URL. That is also what makes
      // -browser and the Termux front-end free: same HTML, same handlers, no second
      // UI to keep in sync with this one.
      //
      // The risk of a local server is that *any* page in the user's browser can POST
      // to 127.0.0.1, and these handlers start build.sh. Two things stop that:
      //
      //  1. everything lives under a random /<token>/ prefix generated at launch, and
      //     the page only learns it by being navigated to it — a cross-origin fetch
      //     cannot read our HTML, so it cannot discover the prefix;
      //  2. requests a browser marks as cross-site are refused outright.
      //
      // The listener is bound to 127.0.0.1, never 0.0.0.0, so nothing off-machine can
      // reach it at all.
      func (a *App) serve(port int) (net.Listener, string, *http.Server, error) {
        token, err := randomToken()
        if err != nil {
          return nil, "", nil, err
        }
        ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", port))
        if err != nil {
          return nil, "", nil, fmt.Errorf("could not open a loopback port: %w", err)
        }
      
        base := "/" + token
        assets, err := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui")
        if err != nil {
          return nil, "", nil, err
        }
      
        mux := http.NewServeMux()
        mux.HandleFunc(base, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
          http.Redirect(w, r, base+"/", http.StatusFound)
        })
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/state", a.guard("GET", a.handleState))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/settings", a.guard("POST", a.handleSettings))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/config", a.guard("POST", a.handleConfig))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/run", a.guard("POST", a.handleRun))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/cancel", a.guard("POST", a.handleCancel))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/log", a.guard("GET", a.handleLog))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/log", a.guard("GET", a.handleAdbLog))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/open", a.guard("POST", a.handleOpen))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/docs", a.guard("GET", a.handleDocs))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/doc", a.guard("GET", a.handleDoc))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/docs/search", a.guard("GET", a.handleDocsSearch))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/update", a.guard("POST", a.handleUpdate))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/config/apply", a.guard("POST", a.handleConfigApply))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/addons", a.guard("GET", a.handleAddons))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/addons/save", a.guard("POST", a.handleAddonsSave))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb", a.guard("POST", a.handleAdb))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/devices", a.guard("GET", a.handleAdbDevices))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/install", a.guard("POST", a.handleAdbInstall))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/detect", a.guard("POST", a.handleAdbDetect))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/adb/match-prop", a.guard("POST", a.handleMatchProp))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/extract", a.guard("POST", a.handleExtract))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/udfps", a.guard("POST", a.handleUDFPS))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/detect", a.guard("POST", a.handleDetect))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/pick", a.guard("POST", a.handlePick))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/url", a.guard("POST", a.handleURL))
      
        // The src/ workspace: the file manager, its two editors and the checks behind
        // them (see files.go). Uploads are the only route that is not JSON.
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files", a.guard("GET", a.handleFiles))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/read", a.guard("GET", a.handleFileRead))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/write", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileWrite))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/check", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileCheck))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/upload", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileUpload))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/delete", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileDelete))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/mkdir", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileMkdir))
        mux.HandleFunc(base+"/api/files/toggle", a.guard("POST", a.handleFileToggle))
        mux.Handle(base+"/", http.StripPrefix(base, http.FileServer(http.FS(assets))))
      
        srv := &http.Server{Handler: mux, ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second}
        url := "http://" + ln.Addr().String() + base + "/"
        return ln, url, srv, nil
      }
      
      func randomToken() (string, error) {
        b := make([]byte, 16)
        if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
          return "", err
        }
        return hex.EncodeToString(b), nil
      }
      
      func (a *App) guard(method string, h http.HandlerFunc) http.HandlerFunc {
        return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
          if r.Method != method {
            w.Header().Set("Allow", method)
            http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
            return
          }
          if r.Header.Get("Sec-Fetch-Site") == "cross-site" {
            http.Error(w, "forbidden", http.StatusForbidden)
            return
          }
          h(w, r)
        }
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Handlers
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      func (a *App) handleState(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, a.State())
      }
      
      // handleSettings remembers the clone and the bash binary. Nothing is run here:
      // a wrong path is stored and reported by /api/state so the field stays visible
      // and editable instead of being rejected on a typo.
      func (a *App) handleSettings(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Clone string `json:"clone"`
          Bash  string `json:"bash"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        if err := a.setPaths(body.Clone, body.Bash); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, a.State())
      }
      
      // handleConfig writes config.env exactly as typed. The file is the interface
      // build.sh reads, comments included, so it is saved verbatim rather than
      // round-tripped through a form.
      func (a *App) handleConfig(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Text string `json:"text"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "no clone selected")
          return
        }
        if len(body.Text) > 1<<20 {
          writeError(w, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, "config.env is limited to 1 MiB")
          return
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "config.env"), []byte(body.Text), 0o644); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"path": filepath.Join(root, "config.env")})
      }
      
      func (a *App) handleRun(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Verb  string   `json:"verb"`
          Flags []string `json:"flags"`
          // Sudo is the password the app collected after the installer said it
          // needed one. It lives in this request, a 0600 file for the duration of
          // the run, and the page's memory — never in a log or the clone.
          Sudo string `json:"sudo"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        args, err := buildArgs(body.Verb, body.Flags)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        // Only these two verbs install anything (see ensure_toolchain). A password
        // for check or clean would be carried for nothing.

      func (a *App) updateFresh() bool {
        a.updMu.Lock()
        defer a.updMu.Unlock()
        return !a.updWhen.IsZero() && time.Since(a.updWhen) < updateEvery
      }
      
      // watchUpdates keeps the chip honest without blocking anything: one check at
      // startup, then one per updateEvery. Failures are stored in the info and shown
      // as "could not check", never as a modal.
      func (a *App) watchUpdates() {
        if !isClone(a.Root()) {
          return
        }
        a.RefreshUpdate()
        for {
          time.Sleep(updateEvery)
          if !isClone(a.Root()) {
            continue
          }
          if a.runner.Snapshot().Running {
            // A build may be changing files; a fetch would just add noise.
            continue
          }
          a.RefreshUpdate()
        }
      }

      var (
        addonID     = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9_]+$`)
        addonChoice = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9]+$`)
      )
      
      // addonsEnv points the helper at the clone instead of an installed module.
      // Paths are POSIX: Git Bash on Windows reads a backslash as an escape.
      func (a *App) addonsEnv() []string {
        root := filepath.ToSlash(a.Root())
        return []string{
          "ADDONS_DIR=" + root,
          "ADDONS_CONF=" + root + "/src/module/addons.conf",
        }
      }
      
      func (a *App) runAddons(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          return nil, errors.New("no clone selected")
        }
        bash := a.Bash()
        if !fileExists(bash) {
          return nil, errors.New("bash was not found — pick it with the Path chip")
        }
        // Short on purpose: six `settings` calls on a phone, and no work at all in
        // the clone.
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bash, append([]string{addonsScript}, args...)...)
        // Hide the console Windows would otherwise flash for this child. The tab
        // runs the helper on open and on every save, so an un-hidden window is a
        // black rectangle blinking at the user each time.
        setProcAttr(cmd)
        cmd.Dir = root
        // A stale ADDONS_* in the app's own environment would otherwise win over
        // the paths below (Windows keeps the first duplicate in the block).
        env := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+2)
        for _, kv := range os.Environ() {
          if strings.HasPrefix(kv, "ADDONS_") {
            continue
          }
          env = append(env, kv)
        }
        cmd.Env = append(env, a.addonsEnv()...)
        var stderr strings.Builder
        cmd.Stderr = &stderr
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
          msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
          if msg == "" {
            msg = err.Error()
          }
          return nil, errors.New(msg)
        }
        return out, nil
      }

      // what the module will enforce.

A profile is a named copy of it, so building for\n// a second phone does not mean keeping config.env.a90 next to config.env.zephyr\n// and remembering which is which.\n//\n// All the work happens in stuff/scripts/profiles.sh, which the terminal menu\n// calls too: this file only turns its tab separated listing into JSON and its\n// verbs into a request. Switching a profile rewrites config.env, so the page\n// refreshes its config after an action rather than patching one field.\n\n// profilesScript is run through bash, like addons.sh: the clone is the source of\n// truth for what a profile is.\nconst profilesScript = \"stuff/scripts/profiles.sh\"\n\n// Profile is one saved setup, as the modal lists it.\ntype Profile struct {\n\tID     string `json:\"id\"`\n\tName   string `json:\"name\"`\n\tDevice string `json:\"device\"`\n\tActive bool   `json:\"active\"`\n}\n\n// profilesRun runs the helper with a short timeout: every verb is a copy or a\n// rename, and none of them touch the phone.\nfunc (a *App) profilesRun(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {\n\troot := a.Root()\n\tif !isClone(root) {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"no clone selected\")\n\t}\n\tscript := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(profilesScript))\n\tif !fileExists(script) {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"stuff/scripts/profiles.sh is missing — update the clone\")\n\t}\n\tbash := a.Bash()\n\tif !fileExists(bash) {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"bash was not found — pick it with the Path chip\")\n\t}\n\tctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)\n\tdefer cancel()\n\tcmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bash, append([]string{script}, args...)...)\n\tsetProcAttr(cmd)\n\tcmd.Dir = root\n\tvar stderr strings.Builder\n\tcmd.Stderr = &stderr\n\tout, err := cmd.Output()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tmsg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())\n\t\tif msg == \"\" {\n\t\t\tmsg = err.Error()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(msg)\n\t}\n\treturn out, nil\n}\n\n// Profiles is the list the modal shows. A checkout with no profiles gets its\n// first one made for it (the helper does that), so the list is never empty.\nfunc (a *App) Profiles() ([]Profile, error) {\n\tout, err := a.profilesRun(\"list\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tlist := []Profile{}\n\tfor _, line := range strings.Split(string(out), \"\\n\") {\n\t\tline = strings.TrimRight(line, \"\\r\")\n\t\tif strings.TrimSpace(line) == \"\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tf := strings.Split(line, \"\\t\")\n\t\tif len(f) < 4 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tp := Profile{ID: f[0], Name: f[2], Device: f[3], Active: f[1] == \"1\"}\n\t\tif p.Name == \"\" {\n\t\t\tp.Name = \"Profile \" + strings.TrimPrefix(p.ID, \"p\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tif p.Device == \"\" {\n\t\t\tp.Device = \"no device set\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tlist = append(list, p)\n\t}\n\treturn list, nil\n}\n\n// handleProfiles serves the list. It is a GET so the modal can open on the\n// current state without an action first.\nfunc (a *App) handleProfiles(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n\tlist, err := a.Profiles()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\twriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{\"profiles\": list, \"active\": activeID(list)})\n}\n\nfunc activeID(list []Profile) string {\n\tfor _, p := range list {\n\t\tif p.Active {\n\t\t\treturn p.ID\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn \"\"\n}\n\n// handleProfilesAction is one request for all four verbs. The id is checked\n// against the shape the helper accepts before it is passed on, so a path can\n// never reach the helper's rm -rf.\nfunc (a *App) handleProfilesAction(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {\n\tvar body struct {\n\t\tAction string `json:\"action\"`\n\t\tID     string `json:\"id\"`\n\t\tName   string `json:\"name\"`\n\t}\n\tif !decode(w, r, &body) {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tvar args []string\n\tswitch body.Action {\n\tcase \"new\":\n\t\targs = []string{\"new\", body.Name}\n\tcase \"switch\":\n\t\targs = []string{\"switch\", body.ID}\n\tcase \"rename\":\n\t\targs = []string{\"rename\", body.ID, body.Name}\n\tcase \"delete\":\n\t\targs = []string{\"delete\", body.ID}\n\tcase \"save\":\n\t\targs = []string{\"save\"}\n\tdefault:\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, \"unknown profile action: \"+body.Action)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif out, err := a.profilesRun(args...); err != nil {\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())\n\t\treturn\n\t} else if msg := strings.TrimSpace(string(out)); msg != \"\" {\n\t\t// `profiles save` prints nothing; the create path prints a confirmation,\n\t\t// which is worth showing in the modal's note line.\n\t\t_ = msg\n\t}\n\tlist, err := a.Profiles()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\twriteError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\t// The config tab keeps its own copy of config.env; a switch makes that copy\n\t// wrong, so the fresh text rides back with the list.\n\ttext := readConfig(a.Root())\n\tconfig, _ := parseConfig(text)\n\twriteJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{\n\t\t\"profiles\":   list,\n\t\t\"active\":     activeID(list),\n\t\t\"configText\": text,\n\t\t\"config\":     config,\n\t\t\"message\":    fmt.Sprintf(\"%s ok\", body.Action),\n\t})\n}"
}

      'use strict';
      
      /* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
         The window is a thin client over the handlers in server.go. Everything it
         can do is one of build.sh's verbs, so there is no build logic here: it picks
         a verb, ticks flags, and renders what the child prints.
      
         Three panes talk to the phone or edit files — config.env, adb and the src/
         workspace — and all of them go through the server, which owns the parsing,
         the path rules and every write. Nothing here touches the disk directly.
         --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
      
      function el(tag, cls, text) {
        const node = document.createElement(tag);
        if (cls) node.className = cls;
        if (text !== undefined) node.textContent = text;
        return node;
      }
      
      const FLAG_HELP = {
        '--with-vendor-hals': 'include src/vendor/ in the module',
        '--xiaomi-fod': 'include the Xiaomi FOD helper in the module',
        '--allow-unknown-resources': 'build even if a resource is missing',
        '--force': 're-pick the resource dictionary',
        '--all': 'also remove config and device files',
      };
      
      // A flag whose name does not say enough gets a ? beside it, and the text below
      // is what that ? opens. Only the one flag needs it: fod/xiaomi-fod is
      // vendor-specific, so ticking it on a Samsung is pointless.
      const FLAG_DETAIL = {
        '--xiaomi-fod': 'Use only if your phone is Xiaomi and has a UDFPS sensor.',
      };
      
      let state = null;
      let selectedVerb = 'build';
      let checkedFlags = new Set();
      let running = false;      // the build console
      let adbRunning = false;  // the device console, which has its own stream
      let lastSeq = 0;
      let adbSeq = 0;
      // The node a repainting progress bar owns, per console: the build log and the
      // adb console each draw their own in place.
      const progressNode = new WeakMap();
      // Where the current adb run writes: the <pre> under the preset that started it,
      // or null for the console at the top of the pane.
      let adbTarget = null;
      // preset id -> the panel under that command, kept across the re-render every
      // finished run triggers so the answer stays where the question was clicked.
      const presetOut = new Map();
      let currentDoc = null;
      let statusTimer = null;
      let refreshInFlight = false;
      
      // A run that stopped for a sudo password keeps its verb here, so the retry is
      // exactly the same command. sudoPassword is the answer; it stays in this
      // window's memory for the session and is never written by the page.
      let pendingRun = null;
      let sudoPassword = '';
      let sudoPromptOpen = false;
      let sudoDeclined = false;
      
      // config.env: the form keeps only what the user changed, so a poll that lands
      // mid-edit cannot repaint the row they are typing in.
      let cfgEdits = new Map();
      let cfgRaw = false;
      let cfgRawDirty = false;
      
      // --------------------------------------------------------------------- api --
      async function api(path, opts = {}) {
        const init = { method: opts.method || 'GET', cache: 'no-store' };
        if (opts.form !== undefined) {
          // Multipart upload: the browser owns the Content-Type boundary, so no
          // header is set here.
          init.body = opts.form;
        } else if (opts.body !== undefined) {
          init.headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
          init.body = JSON.stringify(opts.body);
        }
        const res = await fetch(path, init);
        const text = await res.text();
        let data = null;
        if (text) {
          try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch (_) { data = null; }
        }
        if (!res.ok) {
          const err = new Error((data && data.error) || text || res.statusText);
          // Some failures come with useful detail (the update clash list), so keep
          // the whole payload on the error instead of only the message.
          err.data = data;
          err.status = res.status;
          throw err;
        }
        return data;
      }
      
      function status(message, ms = 3500) {
        $('run-status').textContent = message;
        if (statusTimer) clearTimeout(statusTimer);
        if (ms) statusTimer = setTimeout(() => { $('run-status').textContent = ''; }, ms);
      }
      
      // ------------------------------------------------------------------- state --
      async function refreshState(forceRender = false) {
        if (refreshInFlight) return;
        refreshInFlight = true;
        try {
          state = await api('api/state');
        } catch (err) {
          $('sub').textContent = 'cannot reach the app server: ' + err.message;
          refreshInFlight = false;
          return;
        }
        refreshInFlight = false;
        adbRunning = !!(state.adbRun && state.adbRun.running);
      
        renderHeader();
        renderVerbs();
        renderFlags();
        renderOut();
        renderConfig(forceRender);
        renderAdb();
        renderDocsNav();
        renderRunState();
      }
      
      function renderHeader() {
        const upd = state.update || {};
      
        // One button for both paths: the clone and bash are set in the same dialog,
        // so two chips that open it only made the header look busier. The dot still
        // says whether the pair is usable, and the tooltip keeps both paths visible.
        const path = $('chip-path');
        path.dataset.tone = state.cloneValid && state.bashValid ? 'ok' : 'bad';
        path.title = [
          'clone: ' + (state.clone || 'none — click to set'),
          'bash: ' + (state.bash || 'none — click to set'),
          'click to change either',
      
      [read_files: showing lines 1-140 of 4124. Use code_search to locate the part you need and read a window around it, or call read_files again with offset=141 to continue.]
      
          ver.hidden = false;
          ver.textContent = 'v' + state.version;
          ver.title = `Treble RRO Creator ${state.version}`;
        } else {
          ver.hidden = true;
        }
      
        // The button always says what it does; the dot carries the answer. Green
        // means there is something to pull, which is the one case worth a colour.
        const chip = $('chip-update');
        if (upd.available) {
          chip.dataset.tone = 'ok';
          chip.title = `${upd.behind} new commit${upd.behind === 1 ? '' : 's'} on ${upd.upstream} — click to see what it changes`;
        } else if (upd.error && !upd.checked) {
          chip.dataset.tone = 'warn';
          chip.title = 'could not check for updates: ' + upd.error;
        } else {
          chip.dataset.tone = '';
          chip.title = upd.checked ? 'up to date — click to check again' : 'click to check for updates';
        }
      
        if (state.bashValid && state.cloneValid) {
          if (upd.available) {
            $('sub').textContent = `update available: ${upd.behind} commit${upd.behind === 1 ? '' : 's'} behind ${upd.upstream}`;
          } else if (upd.checked) {
            $('sub').textContent = 'up to date';
          } else if (upd.error && state.branch) {
            $('sub').textContent = 'could not check for updates';
          } else {
            $('sub').textContent = 'ready';
          }
        }
      }
      
      function currentVerb() {
        if (!state) return null;
        return state.verbs.find((v) => v.name === selectedVerb) || state.verbs[0] || null;
      }
      
      function renderVerbs() {
        const box = $('verbs');
        box.textContent = '';
        for (const v of state.verbs) {
          const b = document.createElement('button');
          b.type = 'button';
          b.className = 'verb' + (v.name === selectedVerb ? ' is-active' : '');
          const h = document.createElement('h3');
          h.textContent = v.label;
          const p = document.createElement('p');
          p.textContent = v.hint;
          b.append(h, p);
          b.addEventListener('click', () => {
            selectedVerb = v.name;
            renderVerbs();
            renderFlags();
            renderRunState();
          });
          box.appendChild(b);
        }
      }

      async function extract(action) {
        try {
          adbClear();
          switchTab('device');
          adbRunning = true;
          renderRunState();
          adbStatus('pulling…', 0);
          await api('api/extract', { method: 'POST', body: { action } });
        } catch (err) {
          adbRunning = false;
          renderRunState();
          adbStatus(err.message, 8000);
        }
      }
      
      // ------------------------------------------------------------------ update --
      let updInfo = null;
      
      async function openUpdate() {
        $('upd-error').hidden = true;
        $('upd-output').hidden = true;
        $('upd-files').hidden = true;
        $('upd-files-label').hidden = true;
        $('upd-clash').hidden = true;
        $('upd-go').disabled = true;
        $('upd-go').textContent = 'Update now';
        delete $('upd-go').dataset.done;
        $('upd-head').textContent = 'checking for updates…';
        if ($('update').showModal) openDialog($('update'));
      
        try {
          updInfo = await api('api/update', { method: 'POST', body: { action: 'check' } });
        } catch (err) {
          updInfo = null;
          $('upd-head').textContent = 'could not check for updates: ' + err.message;
          $('upd-go').hidden = true;
          return;
        }
        $('upd-go').hidden = false;
        renderUpdate();
      }
      
      function renderUpdate() {
        const u = updInfo;
        const go = $('upd-go');
        if (!u) return;
      
        $('upd-output').hidden = true;
        $('upd-error').hidden = true;
      
        if (u.error) {
          $('upd-head').textContent = 'could not check for updates: ' + u.error;
          $('upd-files').hidden = true;
          $('upd-files-label').hidden = true;
          $('upd-clash').hidden = true;
          go.disabled = true;
          return;
        }
      
        if (!u.available) {
          $('upd-head').textContent = `already up to date${u.upstream ? ` (${u.upstream})` : ''}`;
          $('upd-files').hidden = true;
          $('upd-files-label').hidden = true;
          $('upd-clash').hidden = true;
          go.disabled = true;
          return;
        }
      
        const count = `${u.behind} new commit${u.behind === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
        $('upd-head').textContent = `${count} on ${u.upstream} (you are on ${u.branch || 'this branch'}${u.ahead ? `, ${u.ahead} commit(s) of your own` : ''})`;
      
        const files = u.files || [];
        if (files.length) {
          $('upd-files-label').hidden = false;
          $('upd-files').hidden = false;
          $('upd-files').textContent = files.join('\n');
        }
      
        const clash = u.clash || [];
        if (clash.length) {
          $('upd-clash').hidden = false;
          $('upd-clash-files').textContent = clash.join('\n');
          $('upd-clash-note').textContent =
            'These files are also edited here, so git cannot fast-forward over them. ' +
            'They will be copied to stuff/backups/pre-update-<time>/ first, then replaced by ' +
            'the new version — retype any values from that copy afterwards.';
        } else {
          $('upd-clash').hidden = true;
        }
      
        if (u.configChanges && u.configChanges.length) {
          $('upd-files-label').hidden = false;
          $('upd-files').hidden = false;
          $('upd-files').textContent = files.join('\n') +
            '\n\nconfig.env settings it changes:\n' + u.configChanges.join('\n');
        }
      
        go.textContent = clash.length ? 'Back up my edits and update' : 'Update now';
        go.disabled = false;
      }
      
      async function runUpdate() {

      // A dialog grows out of the control that opened it and travels to the middle
      // of the window. Only the browser knows where it will land, so the start point
      // is measured after showModal: the button's centre, relative to the dialog's,
      // and a scale that fits the dialog inside that button. Without a button (a
      // dialog the app opens for itself) the plain centred fade in app.css is used.
      function openDialog(dlg, from) {
        // Focus moves into the dialog on showModal, so the trigger is read first.
        const trigger = from || document.activeElement;
        // Reopened while its exit was still playing: drop the exit and start over.
        if (dlg.classList.contains('is-closing')) {
          dlg.classList.remove('is-closing', 'from-control');
          dlg.close();
        }
        if (dlg.open) return; // showModal() throws on an open dialog; the fields still repaint
        dlg.classList.remove('from-control');
        dlg.showModal();
        const box = trigger && trigger.getBoundingClientRect ? trigger.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
        // A body-sized or empty rect means the dialog was not opened from a control.
        if (!box || !box.width || box.width > window.innerWidth * .8) return;
        const d = dlg.getBoundingClientRect();
        const dx = (box.left + box.width / 2) - (d.left + d.width / 2);
        const dy = (box.top + box.height / 2) - (d.top + d.height / 2);
        const s = Math.min(.8, Math.max(.35, (box.width + box.height) / (d.width + d.height)));
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-x', Math.round(dx) + 'px');
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-y', Math.round(dy) + 'px');
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-s', s.toFixed(3));
        dlg.classList.add('from-control');
      }
      
      // Leaving: the same measured start point played backwards, so a dialog that
      // flew out of a button goes back into it. The dialog is still open while it
      // animates; closeDialog() calls the real close() once the card has left, which
      // is what the 'close' listeners that reset state wait for.
      const DIALOG_OUT_MS = 260;
      
      function closeDialog(dlg, value) {
        if (!dlg || !dlg.open || dlg.classList.contains('is-closing')) return;
      
        const finish = () => {
          dlg.removeEventListener('animationend', onEnd);
          dlg.classList.remove('is-closing', 'from-control');
          if (dlg.open) dlg.close(value);
        };
        const onEnd = (event) => {
          if (event.target === dlg) finish();
        };
      
        // With motion turned down there is nothing to wait for, and a window that is
        // not painting animations would otherwise leave the dialog stuck open.
        if (window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
          finish();
          return;
        }
        // Closed while it was still flying in: an exit would restart from the middle
        // and jump, so this one just goes.
        const arriving = dlg.getAnimations && dlg.getAnimations().some(
          (a) => a.playState === 'running' &&
            (a.animationName === 'dialog-fly' || a.animationName === 'dialog-in')
        );
        if (arriving) {
          finish();
          return;
        }
        dlg.classList.add('is-closing');
        dlg.addEventListener('animationend', onEnd);
        setTimeout(finish, DIALOG_OUT_MS + 160); // longer than the CSS animation, as a backstop
      }

func TestIsCloneAndChooseClone(t *testing.T) {
  root := t.TempDir()
  if isClone(root) {
    t.Fatal("an empty folder looked like a clone")
  }
  if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "build.sh"), []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
    t.Fatal(err)
  }
  if isClone(root) {
    t.Fatal("build.sh alone should not be enough")
  }
  if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(root, "stuff", "scripts"), 0o755); err != nil {
    t.Fatal(err)
  }
  if !isClone(root) {
    t.Fatal("build.sh + stuff/scripts/ should be a clone")
  }
  if got := chooseClone(root, ""); got != root {
    t.Fatalf("chooseClone(explicit) = %q, want %q", got, root)
  }
  if got := chooseClone("", root); got != root {
    t.Fatalf("chooseClone(saved) = %q, want %q", got, root)
  }
}

// TestWalkUpForClone covers the layouts the app has to survive: a build in
// gui/bin/, a release unpacked into the clone, and a shell started somewhere
// unrelated. It also pins the depth limit, so a runaway walk cannot end up
// claiming an unrelated parent project as "the clone".
func TestWalkUpForClone(t *testing.T) {
  root := t.TempDir()
  if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "build.sh"), []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
    t.Fatal(err)
  }
  if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(root, "stuff", "scripts"), 0o755); err != nil {
    t.Fatal(err)
  }

  threeDown := filepath.Join(root, "gui", "bin", "x64")
  if err := os.MkdirAll(threeDown, 0o755); err != nil {
    t.Fatal(err)
  }
  if got := walkUpForClone(threeDown); got != root {
    t.Fatalf("three levels down: got %q, want %q", got, root)
  }

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // index.html and app.js have to agree
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The window is one page and one script with no framework and no bundler: a
      // rename in the HTML or a typo in the script is not caught by any compiler, and
      // the failure mode is a dead button and a console error only a devtools user
      // sees. Pulling the ids out of both files catches that in CI instead.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/gui-ui.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const html = readFileSync(join(root, 'gui', 'ui', 'index.html'), 'utf8');
      const js = readFileSync(join(root, 'gui', 'ui', 'app.js'), 'utf8');
      
      function idsInHtml() {
        const ids = new Set();
        for (const m of html.matchAll(/\bid="([^"]+)"/g)) ids.add(m[1]);
        return ids;
      }
      
      // $('x') and document.getElementById('x'). Anything computed is skipped: there
      // are none today, and a new one should be reviewed by hand anyway.
      function idsInJs() {
        const ids = new Map();
        const patterns = [/\$\('([^']+)'\)/g, /getElementById\('([^']+)'\)/g];
        for (const re of patterns) {
          for (const m of js.matchAll(re)) {
            if (m[1].includes('+') || m[1].includes('${')) continue;
            ids.set(m[1], (ids.get(m[1]) || 0) + 1);
          }
        }
        return ids;
      }
      
      // Two elements may not share an id: getElementById returns the first, so code
      // that meant the second one silently reads (or overwrites) the wrong element.
      // A new <select> placed next to an existing hint paragraph did exactly that and
      // only showed up as a picker that would not stay filled.
      test('no id appears twice in the page', () => {
        const counts = new Map();
        for (const id of idsInHtml()) {
          counts.set(id, html.split(`id="${id}"`).length - 1);
        }
        const dupes = [...counts].filter(([, n]) => n > 1).map(([id]) => id);
        assert.deepEqual(dupes, [], `ids defined more than once: ${dupes.join(', ')}`);
      });
      
      test('every id the script looks up exists in the page', () => {
        const inHtml = idsInHtml();
        const missing = [...idsInJs().keys()].filter((id) => !inHtml.has(id));
        assert.deepEqual(missing, [], `app.js reaches for ids the page does not define: ${missing.join(', ')}`);
      });
      
      test('every id in the page is wired to something', () => {
        const used = idsInJs();
        const unused = [...idsInHtml()].filter((id) => !used.has(id));
        // Some ids are only styled or read by CSS; this is a warning list, and the
        // test fails only for ids that look like controls.
        const controls = unused.filter((id) => {
          const re = new RegExp(`<[^>]*\\bid="${id}"[^>]*>`);
          const tag = html.match(re)?.[0] || '';
          return /^<(button|input|textarea|dialog)/.test(tag);
        });
        assert.deepEqual(controls, [], `controls in index.html nothing uses: ${controls.join(', ')}`);
      });
      
      test('the page loads its stylesheet and script from the same folder', () => {
        assert.match(html, /href="app\.css"/);
        assert.match(html, /src="app\.js"/);
      });
      
      // A tab is a button with data-tab and a section with the matching pane id. A
      // mismatch means the tab switches to nothing — visible only by clicking it.
      test('every tab has a pane', () => {
        const tabs = [...html.matchAll(/data-tab="([^"]+)"/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
        assert.ok(tabs.length >= 4, `expected the build/config/device/docs tabs, found ${tabs.join(', ')}`);
        for (const tab of tabs) {
          assert.ok(html.includes(`id="pane-${tab}"`), `tab "${tab}" has no #pane-${tab}`);
        }
        assert.ok(js.includes("'pane-' + name"), 'switchTab no longer builds pane ids the way the test assumes');
      });
      
      // The buttons the server has to serve. Keeping the list here means a handler
      // that is renamed in Go fails this test instead of a 404 in the window.
      test('every api path the script calls exists in server.go', () => {
        const server = readFileSync(join(root, 'gui', 'server.go'), 'utf8');
        // The page uses relative paths ('api/state'); the server registers the whole
        // path under the per-launch token prefix.
        const paths = new Set(
          [...js.matchAll(/api\('([^']+)'/g)]
            .map((m) => m[1].replace(/^api\//, '').split('?')[0])
        );
        const missing = [...paths].filter((p) => !server.includes(`"/api/${p}"`));
        assert.deepEqual(missing, [], `server.go does not register: ${missing.join(', ')}`);
      });
