- path: README.md
  content: |
      <p align="center">
        <img src="assets/icon.png" width="120" alt="Treble RRO Creator">
      </p>
      
      <h1 align="center">Treble RRO Creator</h1>
      
      <p align="center">Builds the overlay module that teaches a GSI about your phone's screen, brightness curve and fingerprint sensor.</p>
      
      <p align="center">
        <a href="https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator"><img alt="Platform" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20Termux-B93D0E?style=flat-square"></a>
        <a href="docs/configuration.md"><img alt="Settings" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/config-one%20env%20file-B93D0E?style=flat-square"></a>
        <a href="#output"><img alt="Output" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/output-flashable%20module-B93D0E?style=flat-square"></a>
        <a href="LICENSE"><img alt="License" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-1F2328?style=flat-square"></a>
      </p>
      
      ---
      
      A GSI boots generic: square screen corners, no cutout, a brightness curve written for some other panel, and an in-display fingerprint reader it cannot locate. This project writes a static RRO with the real values and packs it into one zip you install with Magisk, KernelSU / KSU Next or APatch.
      
      Two front ends run the same build off the same `config.env`:
      
      | | Windows | Linux | Termux |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | **Desktop app** | `treble-rro-creator.cmd` | `./treble-rro-creator.sh` | not available |
      | **Terminal menu** | `build.cmd` | `./build.sh` | `./build.sh` |
      
      The app has tabs for Build, config.env, Addons, Device (adb console), Auto Detect, UDFPS, Files and Docs. The menu offers the same jobs as numbered choices, and it is the whole interface on Termux or over ssh.
      
      ## Quick start
      
      ```bash
      git clone https://github.com/uzbforce/treble-rro-creator
      cd treble-rro-creator
      ./build.sh          # Linux, Termux, Git Bash  → terminal menu
      ```
      
      ```bat
      build.cmd           :: Windows               → terminal menu
      ```
      
      1. `2` config.env — fill in codename, manufacturer, model, corner radius, status bar height.
      2. `5` Auto Detect, `6` UDFPS, `7` Match property — read those numbers off the phone instead of guessing.
      3. `1` → `2` Build. The module lands in `out/`.
      
      The first run installs what is missing: aapt2, zipalign, apksigner, Java and the `framework-res.apk` resource dictionary. Later runs skip straight to the menu.
      
      Full walkthroughs: [docs/gui.md](docs/gui.md) · [docs/windows.md](docs/windows.md) · [docs/termux.md](docs/termux.md).
      
      ## Requirements
      
      | Platform | Needs |
      |---|---|
      | **Windows** | [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) and JDK 17+ (`winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JDK`) |
      | **Linux** | `bash`, `curl` or `wget`, `unzip`, `zip`, JDK 17+ — `./build.sh setup` installs the rest |
      | **Termux** | Termux from **F-Droid**, not Google Play; `pkg install git`, then `./build.sh` |
      | **Phone** | A GSI-based ROM and any of Magisk, KernelSU, KSU Next, APatch |
      
      Root is only needed on Termux, where the phone probes read the device the tool is running on (`tsu ./build.sh`).
      
      ## What it configures
      
      | Area | Settings |
      |---|---|
      | Screen shape | `ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS`, `DISPLAY_CUTOUT`, waterfall edges |
      | Status bar | `STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT`, landscape variant, paddings, privacy dot |
      | Brightness | dim / dark / doze / min / max, auto-brightness, `power_profile.xml` |
      | Display timing | `DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE`, `PEAK_REFRESH_RATE`, AOD, doze, burn-in protection |
      | Fingerprint | `HAS_UDFPS`, `UDFPS_X` / `_Y` / `_RADIUS`, Samsung FOD, optional vendor HAL |
      | Radios and extras | `HAS_5G`, `HAS_VOLTE`, double-tap-to-wake |
      | Module only | addons (`src/module/addons.conf`), live WebUI page, `sepolicy.rule`, VINTF fragments |
      
      Every key, its default and accepted values: [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md).
      
      ## config.env
      
      Required:
      
      | Key | Example | Where it comes from |
      |---|---|---|
      | `DEVICE_CODENAME` | `r3q` | `adb shell getprop ro.product.device` |
      | `DEVICE_MANUFACTURER` | `samsung` | `getprop ro.product.manufacturer` |
      | `DEVICE_MODEL` | `SM-A908N` | `getprop ro.product.model` |
      | `DEVICE_PROP_NAME` | `persist.sys.overlay.r3q` | set by the module; leave empty for an unconditional overlay |
      | `DEVICE_PROP_VALUE` | `true` | value the key above must equal |
      | `ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS` | `135` | stock overlay, or measured on the screen |
      | `STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT` | `113` | stock overlay, or `dumpsys window` |
      
      Everything else has a default and can be left alone.
      
      Two things worth knowing before the first build:
      
      - **`src/framework/res/xml/power_profile.xml` must be yours.** Until you replace it, the empty template is detected and left out of the APK rather than overwriting the GSI's battery and CPU data. See [docs/device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md#power-profile-power_profilexml--mandatory).
      - **No `config.env` yet?** The first run offers the filled-in Samsung A90 5G example (`config.env.example`) or writes a placeholder that says what to edit.
      
      ## Commands
      
      | Command | Does |
      |---|---|
      | `./build.sh` | Terminal menu; a plain build when there is no terminal |
      | `./build.sh build` | Build, installing missing tools first |
      | `./build.sh setup` | Install or repair the toolchain |
      | `./build.sh doctor` | Check the toolchain, change nothing (exit 0 = ready) |
      | `./build.sh check` | Validate `config.env`, build nothing |
      | `./build.sh --dry-run` | Print every resource the config emits, build nothing |
      | `./build.sh install` | Copy the newest zip to the phone, install it, reboot, verify it is live |
      | `./build.sh clean` | Remove `stuff/build/` and `out/` |
      | `./build.sh clean --all` | Start over for a different device (restores templates) |
      | `./build.sh menu` | Force the menu when there is no terminal |
      | `./build.sh --version` | Print the version (also `-V`; it is the single line in `stuff/VERSION`) |
      
      Flags: `-y` / `--yes`, `--with-vendor-hals`, `--xiaomi-fod`, `--allow-unknown-resources`, `--force` (with `setup`), `--no-su` (Termux: skip the up-front root question), `--help`. With `install`: `--device SERIAL`, `--zip PATH`, `--no-reboot`. Same words on Windows with `build.cmd`.
      
      `--dry-run` is the fast loop: it prints type, name, value and target APK for each resource without aapt2, signing or packaging.
      
      To check the project itself (scripts, resource writer, docs anchors), run `bash stuff/tests/run.sh` — this is what CI runs, and it needs no Android tools.
      
      ## Output
      
      | File | Use |
      |---|---|
      | `out/<name>-ksu.zip` | **The module.** Install in Magisk, KernelSU, KSU Next or APatch, then reboot |
      | `out/apks/<name>.apk` | Signed framework overlay |
      | `out/apks/<name>-systemui.apk` | Signed SystemUI overlay, when generated |
      | `out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip` | Source tree to submit to the [Doze-off overlay repo](https://github.com/Doze-off/vendor_hardware_overlay) |
      | `out/<name>-hardware-overlay-test.zip` | Test module for that source tree |
      | `out/<name>-overrides.txt` | Every resource marked `APPLIES` or `IGNORED` against the target framework |
      
      The `-ksu` suffix is historical; the zip is a standard module and works in all four managers. To copy the build to `/sdcard/treble-rro-creator`, use `8` Files → `1` Copy.
      
      > **KernelSU / KSU Next:** mount with Magic Mount, or Hybrid Mount in magic mode. OverlayFS mounts fine but turns one bad `sepolicy.rule` or VINTF fragment into a bootloop. Reasoning in [docs/how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md#the-flashable-module).
      
      Two more things the build will not do for you: do not copy the APKs into `/system/product/overlay/` by hand (dynamic partitions drop them and the module's permissions are missing), and expect the overlays to be static — Android enables them at boot, `cmd overlay enable` changes nothing afterwards.
      
      ## After installing
      
      **WebUI.** The module carries a page in `webroot/`. Open it from the manager (KernelSU, KSU Next, APatch) and change corner radius, status bar height or paddings without rebuilding: it writes the value into `resources.arsc` of the installed APK and restarts the framework. Magisk needs a WebUI host such as WebUI X, KsuWebUI or MMRL. Notes: [docs/webui.md](docs/webui.md).
      
      **Addons.** Tweaks that are not `config.env` keys: volume panel side, keep-screen-on, hide clock, 180° rotation, notch masking. Pick them in the app under Addons; live ones are re-applied on boot, overlay ones are written into the APK. List: [docs/addons.md](docs/addons.md).
      
      **Submitting to the GSI.** `out/<name>-hardware-overlay.zip` contains the folders, the `overlay.mk` lines and a filled-in `HOW-TO-SUBMIT.md`. Read [docs/submission.md](docs/submission.md) before the pull request — the wiki's `+*brand/model*` pattern never matches, and the zip writes the exact property value instead.
      
      Verify an active overlay:
      
      ```bash
      adb shell cmd overlay list | grep <your-package>
      adb shell cmd overlay lookup <your-package> android:dimen/rounded_corner_radius
      ```
      
      ## Project layout
      
      | Path | Holds |
      |---|---|
      | `build.sh`, `build.cmd` | Entry point: menu and build |
      | `treble-rro-creator.sh`, `.cmd` | Desktop app; builds itself first |
      | `config.env` | Your device values |
      | `src/framework/res/`, `src/systemui/res/` | Overlay resources you edit |
      | `src/module/` | Module overrides, `sepolicy.rule`, `addons.conf` |
      | `src/webui/` | WebUI page and `apply.sh`, packed as `webroot/` |
      | `src/vendor/` | Extracted vendor HALs, optional and git-ignored |
      | `out/` | APKs, zips, override report (git-ignored) |
      | `gui/` | Desktop app sources (GTK + WebKit, Go) |
      | `docs/` | Guides |
      | `stuff/` | Scripts, templates, signing key, tests, downloaded tools, build scratch |
      
      ## Docs
      
      | Guide | Covers |
      |---|---|
      | [configuration.md](docs/configuration.md) | Every `config.env` key |
      | [detect.md](docs/detect.md) | Reading cutout, corners, status bar, refresh rate |
      | [udfps.md](docs/udfps.md) | Fingerprint coordinates and touch-panel FOD mode |
      | [addons.md](docs/addons.md) | Module tweaks |
      | [webui.md](docs/webui.md) | Editing values after install |
      | [submission.md](docs/submission.md) | Getting the overlay into the GSI |
      | [device-extraction.md](docs/device-extraction.md) | Vendor HALs and `power_profile.xml` |
      | [gui.md](docs/gui.md) | Desktop app |
      | [windows.md](docs/windows.md) | Windows, PowerShell, WSL |
      | [termux.md](docs/termux.md) | Building on the phone |
      | [troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Build failures, bootloops, inactive overlays |
      | [how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md) | RRO mechanics and build steps |
      
      ## Upgrading from an older layout
      
      `build.sh` moves anything it finds in the old paths (`res/`, `systemui_overlay/res/`, `YOUR BACKUPS/`, root-level `scripts/` and friends) into the current ones on the next run, copying first and deleting afterwards. Old commands map straight across: `setup.sh` → `build.sh setup`, `setup.sh --doctor` → `build.sh doctor`, `cleanup.sh` → `build.sh clean`.
      
      ---
      
      Reference device: Samsung Galaxy A90 5G (SM-A908N / `r3q`). MIT licensed — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

````
# Configuration (`config.env`)

`config.env` is the only file you normally edit. `build.sh` reads it, generates
the overlay resources, the manifests and the module scripts, then compiles and
signs everything.

```bash
cp config.env.example config.env   # optional: Samsung A90 5G reference values
```

Values are plain shell assignments: `KEY=value` or `KEY="value"`.
`true` / `false` are lowercase.

> **Commenting a value out (`#KEY=...`) means "do not generate that resource"**,
> not "set it to zero". Booleans left out keep the GSI default; numbers left out
> keep the framework default.

The desktop app shows this file as a form — one row per setting, the switch on
the left writing exactly that `#`, and the paragraph above the key behind an ⓘ
button — so none of it has to be typed as bash. It saves only the rows you
changed; every other line stays as it was. See
[gui.md](gui.md#the-other-tabs).

Not every tweak is a resource, and those are **not** in this file. The volume
panel side, the screen timeout and similar Settings values are **live** module
addons, written by the module on the phone at boot; the 180° rotation flag, the
navigation-bar padding, the status-bar background and the masked-out notch are
**overlay** addons the build bakes into the APK. All of them live in
`src/module/addons.conf` and the app's **Addons** tab — see
[addons.md](addons.md).

---

## Checking values before a build

`build.sh` runs a preflight over `config.env` before it generates anything and
prints what it finds. `./build.sh check` runs only that preflight:

- placeholders still in place (`000`, `<codename>`) that would silently produce
  a 0 px value;

````

````

- path: docs/gui.md
  content: |
      On Windows the same flags go through `treble-rro-creator.cmd`.
      
      The scans themselves read the APKs with `aapt2`. If it is not there yet, the app
      runs `./build.sh setup -y` first, which is the installer a build uses: apt on
      Debian/Ubuntu, pacman on Arch, pkg on Termux, and a download into
      `stuff/tools/` on Windows or where no package manager is available.
      
      ## Updates
      
      The **Check for updates** button in the header is about a **newer release**, not
      about your own edits. The app runs `git fetch` at startup and every ten minutes;
      the dot on the button turns green when the branch upstream has moved, and the
      tooltip says how far. Click it to see the files the update changes — and,
      because `config.env` is a file people edit, the settings it rewrites there.
      
      Before anything is pulled, those files are compared with your uncommitted edits:
      
      - **no overlap** — **Update now** runs `git pull --ff-only`. Your edits are not
      touched.
      - **overlap** — the button becomes **Back up my edits and update**. The files in
        the way are copied to `stuff/backups/pre-update-<time>/`, replaced by the pulled
        version, and then the pull runs. Nothing is thrown away without a copy, and
        the dialog lists what changed so you can retype the values you care about.
      
      A branch with no upstream, or a checkout without `.git`, only says so; it is not
      an error. If the update touches `gui/`, the dialog tells you to close the window
      and start it again (`treble-rro-creator.sh` / `treble-rro-creator.cmd` rebuild it) — the build scripts are
      already the new ones, because they are read from disk on every run.
      
      ## Where it keeps settings
      
      Two paths only — the clone, and the `bash` binary:
      
      1. `gui.json` next to the executable, when that folder is writable (a portable
         unpack keeps its paths when moved);
      2. otherwise `%APPDATA%\TrebleRROCreator\gui.json` on Windows,
         `~/.config/TrebleRROCreator/gui.json` on Linux.
      
      Both are changed in one place: the **Path** button in the header opens the
      dialog, and its dot is green only when the pair is usable (hover it to see which
      of the two is wrong). On Windows the app accepts **Git Bash only**: WSL's `bash`
      cannot run the native Windows build tools, and mixing the two is the most common
      way to get a confusing failure (see [windows.md](windows.md)).
      
      ## When it does not work
      
      | Symptom | Cause |
      |---|---|
      | the **Path** dot is red | hover it: the tooltip says which half is wrong — bash missing (Git for Windows not installed, or `bash.exe` on PATH is WSL's) or the folder not being a clone (no `build.sh` and `stuff/scripts/`) |
      | nothing opens at all | no window can be created: run `./treble-rro-creator.sh --browser`, which serves the same UI on `127.0.0.1` and opens your default browser |

      numbered list — the same build, the same `config.env` editor, the same phone
      probes. Termux has no window, so this is the full interface on the phone:
      
      ```
           1  Build              dry run, build, check, doctor, clean
           2  config.env         browse and edit one key at a time
           3  Addons             module tweaks: settings and overlay resources
           4  Device             read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone
           5  Auto Detect        ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G
           6  UDFPS              in-display fingerprint geometry
           7  Match property     which property the submission should match on
           8  Files              what was built, and where it is
           9  Docs               the guides in docs/
      ```
      
      `1 → 2` is the build. The first run checks the toolchain: if something is
      missing it installs it (aapt2/zipalign/apksigner via `pkg`,
      `framework-res.apk` by download), then builds.
      
      To skip the menu, use the verbs directly:

---
profiles_cli() {
    local id
    case "${1:-show}" in
        show|'') profiles_print ;;
        list) profiles_list ;;
        active) profiles_active ;;
        save) profiles_save ;;
        switch|use) profiles_switch "${2:-}" ;;
        new|create)
            id="$(profiles_new "${2:-}")" || return 1
            [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
            printf 'profiles: now using "%s" — config.env holds it\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
            ;;
        rename) profiles_rename "${2:-}" "${3:-}" ;;
        delete|remove) profiles_delete "${2:-}" ;;
        *)
            printf 'profiles: unknown command: %s\n' "$1" >&2
            printf 'try: show, list, new, switch, rename, delete, save, active\n' >&2
            return 2
            ;;
    esac
}

      // a second phone does not mean keeping config.env.a90 next to config.env.zephyr
      // and remembering which is which.
      //
      // All the work happens in stuff/scripts/profiles.sh, which the terminal menu
      // calls too: this file only turns its tab separated listing into JSON and its
      // verbs into a request. Switching a profile rewrites config.env, so the page
      // refreshes its config after an action rather than patching one field.

      const profilesScript = "stuff/scripts/profiles.sh"

      type Profile struct {
        ID     string `json:"id"`
        Name   string `json:"name"`
        Device string `json:"device"`
        Active bool   `json:"active"`
      }
      
      // profilesRun runs the helper with a short timeout: every verb is a copy or a
      // rename, and none of them touch the phone.
      func (a *App) profilesRun(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          return nil, errors.New("no clone selected")
        }
        script := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(profilesScript))
        if !fileExists(script) {
          return nil, errors.New("stuff/scripts/profiles.sh is missing — update the clone")
        }
        bash := a.Bash()
        if !fileExists(bash) {
          return nil, errors.New("bash was not found — pick it with the Path chip")
        }
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bash, append([]string{script}, args...)...)

```
profiles_identity() {
    local id="$1" f manuf model code
    if [ "$id" = "$(profiles_active)" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
        f="$ROOT/config.env"
    else
        f="$(profiles_cfg "$id")"
    fi
    [ -f "$f" ] || { printf 'no config.env'; return 0; }
    manuf="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)"
    model="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)"
    code="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)"
    if [ -z "$manuf" ] && [ -z "$model" ] && [ -z "$code" ]; then
        printf 'no device set'
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s %s (%s)' "$manuf" "$model" "$code" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'
}
profiles_list() {
    local id active mark
    profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    active="$(profiles_active)"
    for id in $(profiles_ids); do
        mark=0
        [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark=1
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$id" "$mark" \
            "$(profiles_name "$id")" "$(profiles_identity "$id")"
    done
}

profiles_new_with() {
    local name id n src
    mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
    n=1
    while [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/p$n" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
    id="p$n"
    name="$(profiles_clean_name "${1:-}")"
    [ -n "$name" ] || name="Profile #$n"
    mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
    src="$ROOT/config.env"
    [ -f "$src" ] || src="$ROOT/config.env.example"
    if [ -f "$src" ]; then
        cp -f "$src" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
    else
        : >"$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$name" >"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || return 1
    profiles_set_active "$id" || return 1
    printf '%s' "$id"
}

profiles_print() {
    local -a rows=() ids=()
    local id active n=0 mark name device
    profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    active="$(profiles_active)"
    for id in $(profiles_ids); do ids+=("$id"); done
    if [ "${#ids[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf '  no profiles yet\n'
        return 0
    fi
    for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        mark=' '
        [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark='*'
        rows+=("$mark|$n $(profiles_name "$id")|$(profiles_identity "$id")")
    done
    if command -v ui_table >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ui_table 'Use|Profile|Device' "${rows[@]}"
        return 0
    fi
    printf '\n'
    for id in "${rows[@]}"; do
        IFS='|' read -r mark name device <<<"$id"
        printf '  %s %-32s %s\n' "$mark" "$name" "$device"
    done
}

**Device profiles**

- `stuff/scripts/profiles.sh` — the only thing that touches the files. A profile is a name plus a saved `config.env` under `stuff/profiles/p1/…`; the active one is the file `config.env` itself, so every existing build/validate/probe path keeps working untouched.
- **CLI**: `./build.sh profiles` lists them (active marked `*`, with manufacturer/model/codename), plus `profiles new "Name"`, `switch`/`use`, `rename`, `delete`, `save`, `active`.
- **Terminal menu**: `p Profiles` — numbered list with the same verbs, so Termux gets it too.
- **Desktop app**: a **Profiles** chip next to *Check for updates* opens a dialog listing every profile, with **Use** / **Rename** (inline edit) / **Delete** (two-click arm), an **in use** badge, and a *New profile* field. Switching pulls the new `config.env` text from the server and redraws the Config tab, and it refuses to switch while you have unsaved config edits.
- First look with no profiles creates `Profile #1` from the current `config.env`; deleting the active profile is refused.
- Saved copies are git-ignored, like `config.env`.

  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # profiles.sh — saved config.env setups, one per device
      # =============================================================================
      # config.env holds one device: one codename, one corner radius, one match
      # property. Anyone who builds for more than one phone used to keep copies by
      # hand (`config.env.a90`, `config.env.zephyr`) and remember which was which.
      #
      # A profile is that copy, in a place the tool knows about:
      #
      #   stuff/profiles/p1/name        "Zephyr (Redmi Note 17)"
      #   stuff/profiles/p1/config.env  that device's answers
      #   stuff/profiles/active         "p1" — the profile config.env holds right now
      #
      # config.env at the root stays the file everything reads; a profile is a copy of
      # it. Switching saves what config.env holds into the profile it came from, then
      # copies the target over config.env, so a profile is only ever as stale as the
      # file is. Nothing else writes one.
      #
      # The terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh → 'p') and the app (gui/profiles.go)
      # both come through here, so they do the same thing to the same files.
      #
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh show        the list, for a person
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh list        the list, tab separated
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh new "NAME"  copy config.env, switch to it
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh switch p2
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh rename p2 "Note 17"
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh delete p3
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh save        fold config.env into the active one
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      
      PROFILES_DIR="${PROFILES_DIR:-$ROOT/stuff/profiles}"
      PROFILES_MAX_NAME=40
      
      # Profiles are numbered p1, p2, … with no exceptions, which is also the guard
      # against a path: only that shape ever reaches the rm -rf in profiles_delete.
      profiles_valid_id() { [[ "$1" =~ ^p[0-9]{1,6}$ ]]; }
      
      profiles_ids() {
          local d
          [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR" ] || return 0
          for d in "$PROFILES_DIR"/p*/; do
              [ -d "$d" ] || continue
              d="${d%/}"
              profiles_valid_id "${d##*/}" && printf '%s\n' "${d##*/}"
          done | sort -t p -k 2 -n
      }
      
      profiles_has() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/$1" ]; }
      profiles_cfg() { printf '%s/%s/config.env' "$PROFILES_DIR" "$1"; }
      profiles_name_file() { printf '%s/%s/name' "$PROFILES_DIR" "$1"; }
      
      # The profile config.env belongs to, or nothing on a checkout that has none.
      profiles_active() {
          local id=""
          if [ -f "$PROFILES_DIR/active" ]; then
              IFS= read -r id <"$PROFILES_DIR/active" || id=""
          fi
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || return 0
          profiles_has "$id" || return 0
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      profiles_set_active() {
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
          printf '%s\n' "$1" >"$PROFILES_DIR/active"
      }
      
      # A name is one line and fits a menu column. Anything else (a newline from a
      # paste, a name too long for the table) is cleaned here rather than at each
      # caller.
      profiles_clean_name() {
          local name
          name="$(printf '%s' "${1:-}" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\037\177')"
          name="${name#"${name%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
          name="${name%"${name##*[![:space:]]}"}"
          while [ "${#name}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${name: -1}" = ' ' ]; do name="${name% }" ; done
          if [ "${#name}" -gt "$PROFILES_MAX_NAME" ]; then
              name="${name:0:$PROFILES_MAX_NAME}"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$name"
      }
      
      profiles_name() {
          local id="$1" name=""
          if [ -f "$(profiles_name_file "$id")" ]; then
              IFS= read -r name <"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || name=""
          fi
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "$name")"
          [ -n "$name" ] || name="Profile #${id#p}"
          printf '%s' "$name"
      }
      
      # Manufacturer, model and codename as that profile's config.env has them. For
      # the profile in use the live file wins: it may have been edited a minute ago,
      # and the list should not show yesterday's answer.
      profiles_identity() {
          local id="$1" f manuf model code
          if [ "$id" = "$(profiles_active)" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
              f="$ROOT/config.env"
          else
              f="$(profiles_cfg "$id")"
          fi
          [ -f "$f" ] || { printf 'no config.env'; return 0; }
          manuf="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)"
          model="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)"
          code="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)"
          if [ -z "$manuf" ] && [ -z "$model" ] && [ -z "$code" ]; then
              printf 'no device set'
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s %s (%s)' "$manuf" "$model" "$code" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'
      }
      
      # Fold config.env into the profile it belongs to. This is also what keeps a
      # switch from throwing away edits made since the last one.
      profiles_save() {
          local id
          id="$(profiles_active)"
          [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
          [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ] || return 1
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
          cp -f "$ROOT/config.env" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
          return 0
      }
      
      # Create the next profile and make it active. It starts as a copy of config.env
      # (that is the point: one device's answers, tweaked for the next), or of the
      # example on a checkout that has no config.env yet. Prints the new id.
      profiles_new_with() {
          local name id n src
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
          n=1
          while [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/p$n" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
          id="p$n"
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "${1:-}")"
          [ -n "$name" ] || name="Profile #$n"
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
          src="$ROOT/config.env"
          [ -f "$src" ] || src="$ROOT/config.env.example"
          if [ -f "$src" ]; then
              cp -f "$src" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
          else
              : >"$(profiles_cfg "$id")" || return 1
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$name" >"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || return 1
          profiles_set_active "$id" || return 1
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      # A checkout that has never seen a profile gets Profile #1 from whatever
      # config.env holds, so the first look at the list is not an empty box.
      profiles_ensure() {
          local id
          id="$(profiles_active)"
          [ -n "$id" ] && return 0
          if [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR" ]; then
              id="$(profiles_ids | head -n 1)"
              if [ -n "$id" ]; then
                  # Profiles exist but the marker was lost, or pointed at a folder
                  # that was deleted out from under it: adopt the first one.
                  profiles_set_active "$id"
                  return $?
              fi
          fi
          [ -n "$(profiles_new_with '')" ]
      }
      
      # Keep what config.env holds, then load that profile into it.
      profiles_switch() {
          local id="$1"
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          profiles_save >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          cp -f "$(profiles_cfg "$id")" "$ROOT/config.env" || return 1
          profiles_set_active "$id" || return 1
          return 0
      }
      
      # Save this one, then carry on in a copy of it.
      profiles_new() {
          local id
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          id="$(profiles_new_with "${1:-}")" || return 1
          profiles_switch "$id" || return 1
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      profiles_rename() {
          local id="$1" name
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "${2:-}")"
          if [ -z "$name" ]; then
              printf 'profiles: a profile needs a name\n' >&2
              return 2
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$name" >"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || return 1
          return 0
      }
      
      # The profile in use is not deletable: config.env would be left belonging to
      # nothing, and one profile is always kept for the same reason.
      profiles_delete() {
          local id="$1" total
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          if [ "$id" = "$(profiles_active)" ]; then
              printf 'profiles: %s is the profile in use — switch to another one first\n' "$id" >&2
              return 1
          fi
          total="$(profiles_ids | grep -c . || true)"
          if [ "${total:-0}" -le 1 ]; then
              printf 'profiles: that is the only profile — there has to be one\n' >&2
              return 1
          fi
          rm -rf "$PROFILES_DIR/$id"
      }
      
      # One line per profile, tab separated: id, active(0|1), name, device. This is
      # what gui/profiles.go parses; it is not meant for a person to read.
      profiles_list() {
          local id active mark
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          active="$(profiles_active)"
          for id in $(profiles_ids); do
              mark=0
              [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark=1
              printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$id" "$mark" \
                  "$(profiles_name "$id")" "$(profiles_identity "$id")"
          done
      }
      
      # The same thing for a person: a table with the profile in use marked.
      profiles_print() {
          local -a rows=() ids=()
          local id active n=0 mark name device
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          active="$(profiles_active)"
          for id in $(profiles_ids); do ids+=("$id"); done
          if [ "${#ids[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              printf '  no profiles yet\n'
              return 0
          fi
          for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
              n=$((n + 1))
              mark=' '
              [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark='*'
              rows+=("$mark|$(profiles_name "$id")|$(profiles_identity "$id")")
          done
          if command -v ui_table >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ui_table 'Use|Profile|Device' "${rows[@]}"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '\n'
          for id in "${rows[@]}"; do
              IFS='|' read -r mark name device <<<"$id"
              printf '  %s %-32s %s\n' "$mark" "$name" "$device"
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Command line
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The same verbs from a terminal, from a script, or through build.sh:
      #
      #   ./build.sh profiles                the list
      #   ./build.sh profiles new "Zephyr"   copy config.env and switch to the copy
      #   ./build.sh profiles switch p2      load p2 into config.env
      profiles_cli() {
          local id
          case "${1:-show}" in
              show|'') profiles_print ;;
              list) profiles_list ;;
              active) profiles_active ;;
              save) profiles_save ;;
              switch|use)
                  id="${2:-}"
                  profiles_switch "$id" || return 1
                  printf 'profiles: now using "%s" — config.env holds it\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
                  ;;
              new|create)
                  id="$(profiles_new "${2:-}")" || return 1
                  [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
                  printf 'profiles: now using "%s" — config.env holds it\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
                  ;;
              rename)
                  id="${2:-}"
                  profiles_rename "$id" "${3:-}" || return 1
                  printf 'profiles: now called "%s"\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
                  ;;
              delete|remove) profiles_delete "${2:-}" ;;
              *)
                  printf 'profiles: unknown command: %s\n' "$1" >&2
                  printf 'try: show, list, new, switch, rename, delete, save, active\n' >&2
                  return 2
                  ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # Sourced by build.sh and the menu, which call the functions themselves; run
      # directly, it is the command line above.
      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
          profiles_cli "$@"
          exit $?
      fi

        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          return nil, errors.New("no clone selected")
        }
        script := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(profilesScript))
        if !fileExists(script) {
          return nil, errors.New("stuff/scripts/profiles.sh is missing — update the clone")
        }
        bash := a.Bash()
        if !fileExists(bash) {
          return nil, errors.New("bash was not found — pick it with the Path chip")
        }
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bash, append([]string{script}, args...)...)
        setProcAttr(cmd)
        cmd.Dir = root
        var stderr strings.Builder
        cmd.Stderr = &stderr
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
          msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
          if msg == "" {
            msg = err.Error()
          }
          return nil, errors.New(msg)
        }
        return out, nil
      }
      
      // Profiles is the list the modal shows. A checkout with no profiles gets its
      // first one made for it (the helper does that), so the list is never empty.
      func (a *App) Profiles() ([]Profile, error) {
        out, err := a.profilesRun("list")
        if err != nil {
          return nil, err
        }
        list := []Profile{}
        for _, line := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
          line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r")
          if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
            continue
          }
          f := strings.Split(line, "\t")
          if len(f) < 4 {
            continue
          }
          p := Profile{ID: f[0], Name: f[2], Device: f[3], Active: f[1] == "1"}
          if p.Name == "" {
            p.Name = "Profile " + strings.TrimPrefix(p.ID, "p")
          }
          if p.Device == "" {
            p.Device = "no device set"
          }
          list = append(list, p)
        }
        return list, nil
      }
      
      // handleProfiles serves the list. It is a GET so the modal can open on the
      // current state without an action first.
      func (a *App) handleProfiles(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        list, err := a.Profiles()
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"profiles": list, "active": activeID(list)})
      }
      
      func activeID(list []Profile) string {
        for _, p := range list {
          if p.Active {
            return p.ID
          }
        }
        return ""
      }
      
      // handleProfilesAction is one request for all four verbs. The id is checked
      // against the shape the helper accepts before it is passed on, so a path can
      // never reach the helper's rm -rf.
      func (a *App) handleProfilesAction(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Action string `json:"action"`
          ID     string `json:"id"`
          Name   string `json:"name"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        var args []string
        switch body.Action {
        case "new":
          args = []string{"new", body.Name}
        case "switch":
          args = []string{"switch", body.ID}
        case "rename":
          args = []string{"rename", body.ID, body.Name}
        case "delete":
          args = []string{"delete", body.ID}
        case "save":
          args = []string{"save"}
        default:
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "unknown profile action: "+body.Action)
          return
        }
        // The helper's own message is not passed on: the page reloads the list and
        // says what happened in the row it changed.
        if _, err := a.profilesRun(args...); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        list, err := a.Profiles()
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        // The config tab keeps its own copy of config.env; a switch makes that copy
        // wrong, so the fresh text rides back with the list.
        text := readConfig(a.Root())
        config, _ := parseConfig(text)
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
          "profiles":   list,
          "active":     activeID(list),
          "configText": text,
          "config":     config,
        })
      }

      package main
      
      import (
        "encoding/json"
        "net/http"
        "net/http/httptest"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "strings"
        "testing"
      )
      
      // profileApp is a throwaway clone with the real helper in it. Profiles are a
      // shell feature — the app only parses what stuff/scripts/profiles.sh prints —
      // so copying the script is the honest fixture: a stub would pin nothing.
      func profileApp(t *testing.T) *App {
        t.Helper()
        bash, err := exec.LookPath("bash")
        if err != nil {
          t.Skip("bash is not available")
        }
        src := filepath.Join("..", "stuff", "scripts")
        for _, name := range []string{"profiles.sh", "config-edit.sh"} {
          if !fileExists(filepath.Join(src, name)) {
            t.Skipf("%s not found next to the package", name)
          }
        }
      
        root := t.TempDir()
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(root, "stuff", "scripts"), 0o755); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "build.sh"), []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        for _, name := range []string{"profiles.sh", "config-edit.sh"} {
          data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(src, name))
          if err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
          }
          if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "stuff", "scripts", name), data, 0o644); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
          }
        }
        cfg := "# ── Device ──\nDEVICE_MANUFACTURER=Xiaomi\nDEVICE_MODEL=Test\nDEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr\n"
        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "config.env"), []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        return &App{root: root, bash: bash}
      }
      
      func profileCall(t *testing.T, app *App, method, body string) map[string]any {
        t.Helper()
        var rec *httptest.ResponseRecorder
        if method == http.MethodGet {
          rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
          app.handleProfiles(rec, httptest.NewRequest(method, "/api/profiles", nil))
        } else {
          rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
          req := httptest.NewRequest(method, "/api/profiles/act", strings.NewReader(body))
          req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
          app.handleProfilesAction(rec, req)
        }
        if rec.Code != http.StatusOK {
          t.Fatalf("%s: status %d, body %s", method, rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
        }
        var out map[string]any
        if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &out); err != nil {
          t.Fatalf("%s: %v (%s)", method, err, rec.Body.String())
        }
        return out
      }
      
      // profilesOf turns the JSON list back into the struct, which is also what the
      // page does with it.
      func profilesOf(t *testing.T, out map[string]any) []Profile {
        t.Helper()
        raw, err := json.Marshal(out["profiles"])
        if err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        var list []Profile
        if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &list); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        return list
      }
      
      // TestProfilesLifecycle walks the four verbs through the handlers. The parts
      // worth pinning are the ones the page depends on: the first profile is made for
      // a checkout that has none, the active flag moves with a switch, and the config
      // text comes back with the list so the config tab cannot go stale.
      func TestProfilesLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
        app := profileApp(t)
      
        out := profileCall(t, app, http.MethodGet, "")
        list := profilesOf(t, out)
        if len(list) != 1 {
          t.Fatalf("first look: %d profiles, want 1 (%v)", len(list), list)
        }
        if list[0].ID != "p1" || !list[0].Active || list[0].Name != "Profile #1" {
          t.Fatalf("first look: %+v, want p1/Profile #1/active", list[0])
        }
        if list[0].Device != "Xiaomi Test (zephyr)" {
          t.Fatalf("device line = %q", list[0].Device)
        }
      
        // A new profile is a copy of config.env, and becomes the one in use.
        out = profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"new","name":"Second phone"}`)
        list = profilesOf(t, out)
        if len(list) != 2 {
          t.Fatalf("after new: %d profiles, want 2", len(list))
        }
        active := out["active"]
        if active != "p2" {
          t.Fatalf("after new: active = %v, want p2", active)
        }
        if txt, _ := out["configText"].(string); !strings.Contains(txt, "DEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr") {
          t.Fatalf("configText did not ride back with the list: %q", txt)
        }
      
        // Rename, then switch back: the marker and both names have to hold.
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"rename","id":"p1","name":"Zephyr"}`)
        out = profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"switch","id":"p1"}`)
        list = profilesOf(t, out)
        if out["active"] != "p1" {
          t.Fatalf("after switch: active = %v, want p1", out["active"])
        }
        names := map[string]string{}
        for _, p := range list {
          names[p.ID] = p.Name
        }
        if names["p1"] != "Zephyr" || names["p2"] != "Second phone" {
          t.Fatalf("names after rename/switch = %v", names)
        }
      
        // Delete the one not in use; deleting the one in use must be refused rather
        // than leaving config.env belonging to nothing.
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"delete","id":"p2"}`)
        rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
        req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/profiles/act",
          strings.NewReader(`{"action":"delete","id":"p1"}`))
        app.handleProfilesAction(rec, req)
        if rec.Code == http.StatusOK {
          t.Fatal("deleting the profile in use was allowed")
        }
      
        list = profilesOf(t, profileCall(t, app, http.MethodGet, ""))
        if len(list) != 1 || list[0].ID != "p1" || !list[0].Active {
          t.Fatalf("after delete: %+v", list)
        }
      }
      
      // TestProfilesRejectsUnknownAction keeps the handler from passing a verb it does
      // not know to the helper, whose own fallback is an error message and exit 2.
      func TestProfilesRejectsUnknownAction(t *testing.T) {
        app := profileApp(t)
        rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
        req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/profiles/act",
          strings.NewReader(`{"action":"rm -rf /","id":"p1"}`))
        app.handleProfilesAction(rec, req)
        if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest {
          t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 400", rec.Code)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(rec.Body.String(), "unknown profile action") {
          t.Fatalf("body = %s", rec.Body.String())
        }
      }

      "newString": "# Every path below is built from an id, so the shape is checked here as well as\n# at the verb that was handed one: a caller that forgets (or a marker file\n# edited by hand) then gets an empty answer, never ../../etc.\nprofiles_has() { profiles_valid_id \"${1:-}\" && [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR/$1\" ]; }\nprofiles_cfg() {\n    profiles_valid_id \"${1:-}\" || return 1\n    printf '%s/%s/config.env' \"$PROFILES_DIR\" \"$1\"\n}\nprofiles_name_file() {\n    profiles_valid_id \"${1:-}\" || return 1\n    printf '%s/%s/name' \"$PROFILES_DIR\" \"$1\"\n}\n\n# Write a file whole or not at all: written beside it, then renamed over it. A\n# switch interrupted halfway through must not leave a truncated config.env, and\n# an interrupted marker write must not leave the list pointing at nothing.\nprofiles_put() {\n    local dest=\"$1\" tmp=\"$1.tmp.$$\"\n    if cat >\"$tmp\" 2>/dev/null && mv -f \"$tmp\" \"$dest\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        return 0\n    fi\n    rm -f \"$tmp\" 2>/dev/null\n    return 1\n}",
      "allowMultiple": false
    },
    {
      "oldString": "profiles_set_active() {\n    mkdir -p \"$PROFILES_DIR\" || return 1\n    printf '%s\\n' \"$1\" >\"$PROFILES_DIR/active\"\n}",

      "allowMultiple": false
    },
    {

{

      "oldString": "# A checkout that has never seen a profile gets Profile #1 from whatever\n# config.env holds, so the first look at the list is not an empty box.\nprofiles_ensure() {\n    local id\n    id=\"$(profiles_active)\"\n    [ -n \"$id\" ] && return 0\n    if [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR\" ]; then\n        id=\"$(profiles_ids | head -n 1)\"\n        if [ -n \"$id\" ]; then\n            # Profiles exist but the marker was lost, or pointed at a folder\n            # that was deleted out from under it: adopt the first one.\n            profiles_set_active \"$id\"\n            return $?\n        fi\n    fi\n    [ -n \"$(profiles_new_with '')\" ]\n}",
      "newString": "# A checkout that has never seen a profile gets Profile #1 from whatever\n# config.env holds, so the first look at the list is not an empty box.\n#\n# When folders exist but the marker does not, the profile config.env came from\n# is the one holding the same bytes — that is provable, and it is the only case\n# adopted automatically. Guessing the first folder instead is not harmless: the\n# next switch saves config.env into the profile it is active for, so a wrong\n# guess overwrites the other device's saved answers.\nprofiles_ensure() {\n    local id\n    id=\"$(profiles_active)\"\n    [ -n \"$id\" ] && return 0\n    if [ -d \"$PROFILES_DIR\" ]; then\n        if [ -f \"$ROOT/config.env\" ]; then\n            for id in $(profiles_ids); do\n                if cmp -s \"$ROOT/config.env\" \"$(profiles_cfg \"$id\")\"; then\n                    profiles_set_active \"$id\"\n                    return $?\n                fi\n            done\n        fi\n        if [ -n \"$(profiles_ids | head -n 1)\" ]; then\n            printf 'profiles: no profile is active — the marker was lost.\\n' >&2\n            printf 'profiles: `profiles switch <id>` to say which one config.env belongs to.\\n' >&2\n            return 1\n        fi\n    fi\n    [ -n \"$(profiles_new_with '')\" ]\n}",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

func (g *Gate) release() {

// Runner owns one console: the child process it is running, that run's log
// ring buffer, and the subscribers to it.
//
// One job at a time is deliberate: build.sh writes to out/ and src/staging, and
// a second run started mid-build would corrupt both. The mutex plus `running`
// makes "Start while running" an error rather than a race.
type Runner struct {
  mu       sync.Mutex
  running  bool
  label    string
  exit     int
  seq      int
  lines    []LogLine
  subs     map[chan LogLine]struct{}
  cmd      *exec.Cmd
  maxLines int
  started  time.Time
  gate     *Gate
  // Set when the child asked for a sudo password; finish turns it into the
  // line that opens the app's dialog. cleanup removes the password file.
  sudoNeeded bool
  cleanup    func()
}

// NewRunner makes a console. A Runner given no Gate gets one of its own, which
// is all a test needs; the app passes the same Gate to both consoles.
func NewRunner(gates ...*Gate) *Runner {
  gate := NewGate()
  if len(gates) > 0 && gates[0] != nil {
    gate = gates[0]
  }
  return &Runner{maxLines: 20000, subs: make(map[chan LogLine]struct{}), gate: gate}
}

// Start launches a program in the clone and begins streaming its output.
//
// mergeStderr is for tools that report progress on stderr — adb pull does — so
// a successful pull is not painted in the pane's error colour. The exit code,
// not the stream, decides whether the run succeeded.
func (r *Runner) Start(root, program string, args []string, label string, mergeStderr bool) error {
  return r.start(root, program, args, label, mergeStderr, nil, nil)
}

// StartEnv is Start with extra environment entries and a cleanup that runs when
// the job ends. The sudo handshake uses both: the page's password goes into a
// private file, the file's path into the environment for sudo -A, and the file
// must be gone the moment the child is.
func (r *Runner) StartEnv(root, program string, args []string, label string, mergeStderr bool, extraEnv []string, cleanup func()) error {
  return r.start(root, program, args, label, mergeStderr, extraEnv, cleanup)
}

func (r *Runner) Snapshot() RunState {
  r.mu.Lock()
  defer r.mu.Unlock()
  return RunState{
    Running: r.running,
    Label:   r.label,
    Exit:    r.exit,
    Sudo:    r.sudoNeeded,
    // Non-nil so an empty buffer encodes as [] rather than null.
    Lines: append([]LogLine{}, r.lines...),
  }
}

// Subscribe returns a channel of new lines and a function that stops it.
//
// The channel is never closed: emit holds the same mutex and a close would race
// with a send. Subscribers stop on their own context instead.
func (r *Runner) Subscribe() (<-chan LogLine, func()) {

  r.mu.Lock()

Every case here is one of those, plus the out/ note that keeps a\n// previous device's module from being installed by mistake.\n//\n// Run: node --test stuff/tests/profiles-sh.test.js\nimport { test } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { tmpdir } from 'node:os';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';\nimport { dirname, join } from 'node:path';\n\nconst root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');\nconst scripts = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts');\n\n// A throwaway ROOT with the real helper, its config reader, and one config.env.\n// profiles.sh sources config-edit.sh from ROOT, so both have to be there.\nfunction workspace() {\n  const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'profiles-'));\n  mkdirSync(join(d, 'stuff', 'scripts'), { recursive: true });\n  for (const name of ['profiles.sh', 'config-edit.sh']) {\n    copyFileSync(join(scripts, name), join(d, 'stuff', 'scripts', name));\n  }\n  writeFileSync(\n    join(d, 'config.env'),\n    ['DEVICE_MANUFACTURER=Xiaomi', 'DEVICE_MODEL=\"Redmi Note 17\"', 'DEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr', ''].join('\\n')\n  );\n  return d;\n}\n\nfunction run(d, snippet) {\n  const file = join(d, 'run.sh');\n  writeFileSync(file, `. \"${join(scripts, 'profiles.sh')}\"\\n${snippet}\\n`);\n  const out = spawnSync('bash', [file], {\n    encoding: 'utf8',\n    env: { ...process.env, ROOT: d, TERM: 'dumb' },\n  });\n  return { stdout: out.stdout, stderr: out.stderr, status: out.status };\n}\n\nconst cfgOf = (d, id) => readFileSync(join(d, 'stuff', 'profiles', id, 'config.env'), 'utf8');\n\ntest('two profiles cannot share a name, whatever the case or spacing', () => {\n  const d = workspace();\n  const r = run(d, 'profiles_new_with \"Pixel 8\" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_new_with \"  pixel   8 \"');\n  assert.equal(r.status, 1);\n  assert.match(r.stderr, /already taken by p1/);\n});\n\ntest('a rename onto another profile name is refused, but its own is not', () => {\n  const d = workspace();\n  const r = run(\n    d,\n    [\n      'profiles_new_with \"Pixel\" >/dev/null || exit 9',\n      'profiles_new_with \"Note\" >/dev/null || exit 9',\n      'profiles_rename p1 \"NOTE\" && exit 8', // duplicate: must fail\n      'profiles_rename p2 \"Note\" || exit 7', // its own name: must pass\n      'profiles_name p2',\n    ].join('\\n')\n  );\n  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);\n  assert.equal(r.stdout.trim(), 'Note');\n});\n\ntest('the default name skips a number that is already in use', () => {\n  const d = workspace();\n  const r = run(d, 'profiles_new_with \"Profile #2\" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_new_with \"\" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_name p2');\n  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);\n  assert.equal(r.stdout.trim(), 'Profile #3');\n});\n\ntest('a profile whose config.env is gone is not switched to', () => {\n  const d = workspace();\n  const r = run(\n    d,\n    [\n      'profiles_new_with \"Second\" >/dev/null || exit 9',\n      'rm -f stuff/profiles/p2/config.env',\n      'profiles_switch p2',\n    ].join('\\n')\n  );\n  assert.equal(r.status, 1);\n  assert.match(r.stderr, /has no config\\.env/);\n  assert.match(readFileSync(join(d, 'config.env'), 'utf8'), /DEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr/);\n});\n\n// The marker is the only thing saying which profile config.env belongs to. When\n// it is gone, a matching saved copy is proof enough; anything else is a guess,\n// and a wrong guess overwrites the other device's saved answers on the next\n// switch.\ntest('a lost marker is adopted when config.env matches a profile, and not otherwise', () => {\n  const d = workspace();\n  const adopted = run(d, 'profiles_new_with \"Pixel\" >/dev/null || exit 9; rm -f stuff/profiles/active; profiles_active');\n  assert.equal(adopted.stdout.trim(), 'p1');\n\n  const d2 = workspace();\n  const guessed = run(\n    d2,\n    [\n      'profiles_new_with \"Pixel\" >/dev/null || exit 9',\n      'profiles_new_with \"Note\" >/dev/null || exit 9',\n      'rm -f stuff/profiles/active',\n      'printf \"DEVICE_CODENAME=edited\\\\n\" >> config.env',\n      'echo \"active=[$(profiles_active)]\"',\n      'profiles_switch p1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 9',\n      'grep -c edited stuff/profiles/p2/config.env || true',\n    ].join('\\n')\n  );\n  assert.match(guessed.stdout, /active=\\[\\]/);\n  assert.match(guessed.stderr, /no profile is active/);\n  // The edit must not be saved into a profile nobody proved it belonged to.\n  assert.equal(guessed.stdout.trim().split('\\n').pop(), '0');\n});\n\ntest('a name with a pipe does not break the table', () => {\n  const d = workspace();\n  const r = run(d, 'profiles_new_with \"Pixel\" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_rename p1 \"a|b\" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_print');\n  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);\n  assert.match(r.stdout, /a\\/b/);\n  assert.ok(!r.stdout.includes('a|b'), r.stdout);\n});\n\ntest('switching says out/ still holds the previous build', () => {\n  const d = workspace();\n  const r = run(\n    d,\n    [\n      'profiles_new_with \"Pixel\" >/dev/null || exit 9',\n      'mkdir -p out && : > out/treble-overlay-x-ksu.zip',\n      'profiles_switch p1',\n    ].join('\\n')\n  );\n  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);\n  assert.match(r.stderr, /out\\/ still holds the previous build \\(1 zip\\)/);\n});\n\ntest('an id is not a path: nothing outside stuff/profiles is touched', () => {\n  const d = workspace();\n  const r = run(\n    d,\n    [\n      'mkdir -p victim',\n      'profiles_switch \"../victim\" || echo \"switch=$?\"',\n      'profiles_delete \"p1/../../victim\" || echo \"delete=$?\"',\n      'profiles_has \"..\" || echo \"has=$?\"',\n      '[ -d victim ] || exit 3',\n    ].join('\\n')\n  );\n  assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);\n  assert.match(r.stdout, /switch=2/);\n  assert.match(r.stdout, /delete=2/);\n  assert.match(r.stdout, /has=1/);\n  assert.ok(existsSync(join(d, 'victim')), 'a refused id removed a folder');\n});"
}

- path: gui/profiles.go
  content: |
      package main
      
      import (
        "context"
        "errors"
        "net/http"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "strings"
        "time"
      )
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Profiles
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // config.env holds one device. A profile is a named copy of it, so building for
      // a second phone does not mean keeping config.env.a90 next to config.env.zephyr
      // and remembering which is which.
      //
      // All the work happens in stuff/scripts/profiles.sh, which the terminal menu
      // calls too: this file only turns its tab separated listing into JSON and its
      // verbs into a request. Switching a profile rewrites config.env, so the page
      // refreshes its config after an action rather than patching one field.
      
      // profilesScript is run through bash, like addons.sh: the clone is the source of
      // truth for what a profile is.
      const profilesScript = "stuff/scripts/profiles.sh"
      
      // Profile is one saved setup, as the modal lists it.
      type Profile struct {
        ID     string `json:"id"`
        Name   string `json:"name"`
        Device string `json:"device"`
        Active bool   `json:"active"`
      }
      
      // profilesRun runs the helper with a short timeout: every verb is a copy or a
      // rename, and none of them touch the phone.
      func (a *App) profilesRun(args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          return nil, errors.New("no clone selected")
        }
        script := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(profilesScript))
        if !fileExists(script) {
          return nil, errors.New("stuff/scripts/profiles.sh is missing — update the clone")
        }
        bash := a.Bash()
        if !fileExists(bash) {
          return nil, errors.New("bash was not found — pick it with the Path chip")
        }
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bash, append([]string{script}, args...)...)
        setProcAttr(cmd)
        cmd.Dir = root
        var stderr strings.Builder
        cmd.Stderr = &stderr
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
          msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
          if msg == "" {
            msg = err.Error()
          }
          return nil, errors.New(msg)
        }
        return out, nil
      }
      
      // Profiles is the list the modal shows. A checkout with no profiles gets its
      // first one made for it (the helper does that), so the list is never empty.
      func (a *App) Profiles() ([]Profile, error) {
        out, err := a.profilesRun("list")
        if err != nil {
          return nil, err
        }
        list := []Profile{}
        for _, line := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
          line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r")
          if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
            continue
          }
          f := strings.Split(line, "\t")
          if len(f) < 4 {
            continue
          }
          p := Profile{ID: f[0], Name: f[2], Device: f[3], Active: f[1] == "1"}
          if p.Name == "" {
            p.Name = "Profile " + strings.TrimPrefix(p.ID, "p")
          }
          if p.Device == "" {
            p.Device = "no device set"
          }
          list = append(list, p)
        }
        return list, nil
      }
      
      // handleProfiles serves the list. It is a GET so the modal can open on the
      // current state without an action first.
      func (a *App) handleProfiles(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        list, err := a.Profiles()
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"profiles": list, "active": activeID(list)})
      }
      
      func activeID(list []Profile) string {
        for _, p := range list {
          if p.Active {
            return p.ID
          }
        }
        return ""
      }
      
      // handleProfilesAction is one request for all four verbs. The id is checked
      // against the shape the helper accepts before it is passed on, so a path can
      // never reach the helper's rm -rf.
      func (a *App) handleProfilesAction(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Action string `json:"action"`
          ID     string `json:"id"`
          Name   string `json:"name"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        // A build reads config.env as it goes, and switching replaces that file under
        // it, so the module would be named for one device and filled from another.
        // Waiting costs nothing; the dialog says so and the button stays where it is.
        if a.runner != nil && a.runner.Snapshot().Running {
          switch body.Action {
          case "new", "switch", "delete":
            writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "a build is running \u2014 change profiles after it finishes")
            return
          }
        }
      
        var args []string
        switch body.Action {
        case "new":
          args = []string{"new", body.Name}
        case "switch":
          args = []string{"switch", body.ID}
        case "rename":
          args = []string{"rename", body.ID, body.Name}
        case "delete":
          args = []string{"delete", body.ID}
        case "save":
          args = []string{"save"}
        default:
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "unknown profile action: "+body.Action)
          return
        }
        // The helper's own message is not passed on: the page reloads the list and
        // says what happened in the row it changed.
        if _, err := a.profilesRun(args...); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        list, err := a.Profiles()
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        // The config tab keeps its own copy of config.env; a switch makes that copy
        // wrong, so the fresh text rides back with the list.
        text := readConfig(a.Root())
        config, _ := parseConfig(text)
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
          "profiles":   list,
          "active":     activeID(list),
          "configText": text,
          "config":     config,
        })
      }
- path: gui/ui/app.js
  content: |
        const ren = el('button', '', 'Rename');
        ren.type = 'button';
        ren.addEventListener('click', () => profStartRename(row, p));
        row.appendChild(ren);
      
        if (!p.active && profList.length > 1) {
          // Two clicks: the first asks, the second does it. A deleted profile takes
          // its config.env with it, and nothing on this side can bring it back.
          const del = el('button', '', 'Delete');
          del.type = 'button';
          let armed = false;
          del.addEventListener('click', () => {
            if (!armed) {
              armed = true;
              del.textContent = 'Delete?';
              del.classList.add('danger');
              setTimeout(() => {
                armed = false;
                del.textContent = 'Delete';
                del.classList.remove('danger');
              }, 4000);
              return;
            }
            profAct('delete', p.id);
          });
          row.appendChild(del);
        }
        return row;
      }
      
      // Rename in place: the name is the only field, so a second dialog for it would
      // be a dialog with one input and two buttons.
      function profStartRename(row, p) {
        const name = row.querySelector('.prof-name');
        if (!name) return;
        const input = el('input', 'rename');
        input.type = 'text';
        input.maxLength = 40;
        input.value = p.name;
        input.spellcheck = false;
        name.replaceWith(input);
        input.focus();
        input.select();
        let done = false;
        const commit = async (save) => {
          if (done) return;
          done = true;
          const value = input.value.trim();
          if (!save || !value || value === p.name) {
            input.replaceWith(el('span', 'prof-name', p.name));
            return;
          }
          await profAct('rename', p.id, value);
        };
        input.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
          if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); commit(true); }
          if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); commit(false); }
        });
        input.addEventListener('blur', () => commit(true));
      }
      
      // profAct sends one verb and redraws from the answer, so the list can never
      // disagree with the files on disk.
      async function profAct(action, id, name) {
        if (profBusy) return;
        // Switching replaces config.env, so anything typed into the form and not yet
        // saved would be thrown away by it.
        if ((action === 'switch' || action === 'new') && (cfgEdits.size > 0 || (cfgRaw && cfgRawDirty))) {
          profShowError('You have unsaved config.env changes — save them first, then switch.');
          return;
        }
        profBusy = true;
        $('prof-error').hidden = true;
        try {
          const res = await api('api/profiles/act', { method: 'POST', body: { action, id, name } });
          profList = res.profiles || [];
          if (typeof res.configText === 'string') {
            state.configText = res.configText;
            state.config = res.config;
            cfgEdits.clear();
            cfgRawDirty = false;
            renderConfig(true);
            updateCfgStatus();
          }
          renderProfiles();
          const active = profList.find((p) => p.active);
          if (active) status(`using “${active.name}”`, 3000);
          if (action === 'new') $('prof-new-name').value = '';
        } catch (err) {
          profShowError(err.message);
        } finally {
          profBusy = false;
        }
      }
      
      // ------------------------------------------------------------------- udfps --
      // The probe is a script (stuff/scripts/udfps-probe.sh) that answers in JSON;
      // this side only draws the answers and writes the one the user picks. Every row
      // keeps its source visible, because "540, 2198, 89" means nothing without
      // knowing which property or overlay it came from.
      let udfpsReport = null;
      let udfpsPick = -1;
      let udfpsFirmware = null; // what the path turned out to be, when it was a ROM image
      
      // firmwareLine says what the path was: a bare image the app unpacked, or a tree
      // that was already readable. The probe's own answer is the folder it scanned.
      function firmwareLine(fw, scanned) {
        if (!fw) return 'Scanned ' + (scanned || 'the folder');
        if (!fw.unpacked) return 'Read ' + (scanned || fw.dir) + ' (already unpacked)';
        const parts = ['Unpacked ' + shortName(fw.source)];
        if (fw.partitions) {
          const ok = fw.partitions.filter((p) => p.fs !== '?').length;
