- path: stuff/scripts/profiles.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # profiles.sh — saved config.env setups, one per device
      # =============================================================================
      # config.env holds one device: one codename, one corner radius, one match
      # property. Anyone who builds for more than one phone used to keep copies by
      # hand (`config.env.a90`, `config.env.zephyr`) and remember which was which.
      #
      # A profile is that copy, in a place the tool knows about:
      #
      #   stuff/profiles/p1/name        "Zephyr (Redmi Note 17)"
      #   stuff/profiles/p1/config.env  that device's answers
      #   stuff/profiles/active         "p1" — the profile config.env holds right now
      #
      # config.env at the root stays the file everything reads; a profile is a copy of
      # it. Switching saves what config.env holds into the profile it came from, then
      # copies the target over config.env, so a profile is only ever as stale as the
      # file is. Nothing else writes one.
      #
      # The terminal menu (stuff/scripts/menu.sh → 'p') and the app (gui/profiles.go)
      # both come through here, so they do the same thing to the same files.
      #
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh show        the list, for a person
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh list        the list, tab separated
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh new "NAME"  copy config.env, switch to it
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh switch p2
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh rename p2 "Note 17"
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh delete p3
      #   bash stuff/scripts/profiles.sh save        fold config.env into the active one
      # =============================================================================
      
      if [ -z "${ROOT:-}" ]; then
          ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
          export ROOT
      fi
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/config-edit.sh"
      
      PROFILES_DIR="${PROFILES_DIR:-$ROOT/stuff/profiles}"
      PROFILES_MAX_NAME=40
      
      # Profiles are numbered p1, p2, … with no exceptions, which is also the guard
      # against a path: only that shape ever reaches the rm -rf in profiles_delete.
      profiles_valid_id() { [[ "$1" =~ ^p[0-9]{1,6}$ ]]; }
      
      profiles_ids() {
          local d
          [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR" ] || return 0
          for d in "$PROFILES_DIR"/p*/; do
              [ -d "$d" ] || continue
              d="${d%/}"
              profiles_valid_id "${d##*/}" && printf '%s\n' "${d##*/}"
          done | sort -t p -k 2 -n
      }
      
      # Every path below is built from an id, so the shape is checked here as well as
      # at the verb that was handed one: a caller that forgets (or a marker file
      # edited by hand) then gets an empty answer, never ../../etc.
      profiles_has() { profiles_valid_id "${1:-}" && [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/$1" ]; }
      profiles_cfg() {
          profiles_valid_id "${1:-}" || return 1
          printf '%s/%s/config.env' "$PROFILES_DIR" "$1"
      }
      profiles_name_file() {
          profiles_valid_id "${1:-}" || return 1
          printf '%s/%s/name' "$PROFILES_DIR" "$1"
      }
      
      # Write a file whole or not at all: written beside it, then renamed over it. A
      # switch interrupted halfway through must not leave a truncated config.env, and
      # an interrupted marker write must not leave the list pointing at nothing.
      profiles_put() {
          local dest="$1" tmp="$1.tmp.$$"
          if cat >"$tmp" 2>/dev/null && mv -f "$tmp" "$dest" 2>/dev/null; then
              return 0
          fi
          rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
          return 1
      }
      
      # The profile config.env belongs to, or nothing on a checkout that has none.
      profiles_active() {
          local id=""
          if [ -f "$PROFILES_DIR/active" ]; then
              IFS= read -r id <"$PROFILES_DIR/active" || id=""
          fi
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || return 0
          profiles_has "$id" || return 0
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      profiles_set_active() {
          profiles_valid_id "${1:-}" || return 1
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
          printf '%s\n' "$1" | profiles_put "$PROFILES_DIR/active"
      }
      
      # A name is one line and fits a menu column. Anything else (a newline from a
      # paste, a name too long for the table) is cleaned here rather than at each
      # caller.
      profiles_clean_name() {
          local name
          # Control characters would end a line or a table cell early; a pipe is the
          # separator the tables are built from, so it becomes a slash.
          name="$(printf '%s' "${1:-}" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\037\177' | tr '|' '/')"
          name="${name#"${name%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
          name="${name%"${name##*[![:space:]]}"}"
          while [ "${#name}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${name: -1}" = ' ' ]; do name="${name% }" ; done
          if [ "${#name}" -gt "$PROFILES_MAX_NAME" ]; then
              name="${name:0:$PROFILES_MAX_NAME}"
          fi
          printf '%s' "$name"
      }
      
      profiles_name() {
          local id="$1" name=""
          if [ -f "$(profiles_name_file "$id")" ]; then
              IFS= read -r name <"$(profiles_name_file "$id")" || name=""
          fi
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "$name")"
          [ -n "$name" ] || name="Profile #${id#p}"
          printf '%s' "$name"
      }
      
      # Two rows that read the same are worse than no names at all: the list is what
      # the user picks from. Comparison ignores case and runs of spaces, so "Pixel  8"
      # cannot sit next to "pixel 8".
      profiles_name_key() {
          printf '%s' "$1" | LC_ALL=C tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/  */ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//'
      }
      
      # The id of the profile already called NAME (except itself, when renaming).
      profiles_named() {
          local want id
          want="$(profiles_name_key "$1")"
          [ -n "$want" ] || return 1
          for id in $(profiles_ids); do
              [ "$id" = "${2:-}" ] && continue
              if [ "$(profiles_name_key "$(profiles_name "$id")")" = "$want" ]; then
                  printf '%s' "$id"
                  return 0
              fi
          done
          return 1
      }
      
      # out/ is not per profile: it keeps what the last build produced, named for that
      # device, and nothing about a switch cleans it. Installing the previous device's
      # module looks like a working phone until something reads the wrong overlay, so
      # say it once, on stderr, and carry on.
      profiles_out_note() {
          local count
          [ -d "$ROOT/out" ] || return 0
          count="$(find "$ROOT/out" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.zip' 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"
          [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ] || return 0
          printf 'profiles: out/ still holds the previous build (%s zip%s) — build again for this device\n' \
              "$count" "$(if [ "$count" = 1 ]; then printf ''; else printf 's'; fi)" >&2
      }
      
      # Manufacturer, model and codename as that profile's config.env has them. For
      # the profile in use the live file wins: it may have been edited a minute ago,
      # and the list should not show yesterday's answer.
      profiles_identity() {
          local id="$1" f manuf model code
          if [ "$id" = "$(profiles_active)" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
              f="$ROOT/config.env"
          else
              f="$(profiles_cfg "$id")"
          fi
          [ -f "$f" ] || { printf 'no config.env'; return 0; }
          manuf="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_MANUFACTURER)"
          model="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_MODEL)"
          code="$(CFG_FILE="$f" cfg_get DEVICE_CODENAME)"
          if [ -z "$manuf" ] && [ -z "$model" ] && [ -z "$code" ]; then
              printf 'no device set'
              return 0
          fi
          printf '%s %s (%s)' "$manuf" "$model" "$code" | sed 's/^ *//; s/  */ /g'
      }
      
      # Fold config.env into the profile it belongs to. This is also what keeps a
      # switch from throwing away edits made since the last one.
      profiles_save() {
          local id
          id="$(profiles_active)"
          [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
          [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ] || return 1
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
          cat "$ROOT/config.env" | profiles_put "$(profiles_cfg "$id")"
      }
      
      # Create the next profile and make it active. It starts as a copy of config.env
      # (that is the point: one device's answers, tweaked for the next), or of the
      # example on a checkout that has no config.env yet. Prints the new id.
      profiles_new_with() {
          local name id n src taken
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR" || return 1
          n=1
          while [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/p$n" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
          id="p$n"
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "${1:-}")"
          if [ -n "$name" ]; then
              if taken="$(profiles_named "$name")"; then
                  printf 'profiles: "%s" is already taken by p%s — name this one something else\n' \
                      "$name" "${taken#p}" >&2
                  return 1
              fi
          else
              # The default name follows the folder number, but a rename or a delete
              # can leave that number in use, so skip whatever is already there.
              while [ -n "$(profiles_named "Profile #$n")" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
              name="Profile #$n"
          fi
          mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" || return 1
          src="$ROOT/config.env"
          [ -f "$src" ] || src="$ROOT/config.env.example"
          # A half-made profile (a folder with no answers, or with no name) would show
          # up in the list as a device with nothing set and switch to an empty file, so
          # the failure of any step takes the whole folder with it.
          if ! { if [ -f "$src" ]; then cp -f "$src" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")"; else : >"$(profiles_cfg "$id")"; fi; } \
              || ! printf '%s\n' "$name" | profiles_put "$(profiles_name_file "$id")" \
              || ! profiles_set_active "$id"; then
              rm -rf "$PROFILES_DIR/$id"
              printf 'profiles: could not create %s\n' "$id" >&2
              return 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      # A checkout that has never seen a profile gets Profile #1 from whatever
      # config.env holds, so the first look at the list is not an empty box.
      #
      # When folders exist but the marker does not, the profile config.env came from
      # is the one holding the same bytes — that is provable, and it is the only case
      # adopted automatically. Guessing the first folder instead is not harmless: the
      # next switch saves config.env into the profile it is active for, so a wrong
      # guess overwrites the other device's saved answers.
      profiles_ensure() {
          local id
          id="$(profiles_active)"
          [ -n "$id" ] && return 0
          if [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR" ]; then
              if [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
                  for id in $(profiles_ids); do
                      if cmp -s "$ROOT/config.env" "$(profiles_cfg "$id")"; then
                          profiles_set_active "$id"
                          return $?
                      fi
                  done
              fi
              if [ -n "$(profiles_ids | head -n 1)" ]; then
                  printf 'profiles: no profile is active — the marker was lost.\n' >&2
                  printf 'profiles: `profiles switch <id>` to say which one config.env belongs to.\n' >&2
                  return 1
              fi
          fi
          [ -n "$(profiles_new_with '')" ]
      }
      
      # Keep what config.env holds, then load that profile into it.
      profiles_switch() {
          local id="$1" src
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          src="$(profiles_cfg "$id")"
          # A profile folder whose config.env went missing (deleted by hand, a sync
          # that skipped it) would otherwise be copied as nothing and empty out
          # config.env — the one file everything reads.
          if [ ! -f "$src" ]; then
              printf 'profiles: %s has no config.env — that folder is damaged; delete it or save over it\n' "$id" >&2
              return 1
          fi
          profiles_save >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          cat "$src" | profiles_put "$ROOT/config.env" || return 1
          profiles_set_active "$id" || return 1
          profiles_out_note
          return 0
      }
      
      # Save this one, then carry on in a copy of it.
      profiles_new() {
          local id
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null || true
          id="$(profiles_new_with "${1:-}")" || return 1
          profiles_switch "$id" || return 1
          printf '%s' "$id"
      }
      
      profiles_rename() {
          local id="$1" name taken
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          name="$(profiles_clean_name "${2:-}")"
          if [ -z "$name" ]; then
              printf 'profiles: a profile needs a name\n' >&2
              return 2
          fi
          if taken="$(profiles_named "$name" "$id")"; then
              printf 'profiles: "%s" is already taken by p%s\n' "$name" "${taken#p}" >&2
              return 1
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$name" | profiles_put "$(profiles_name_file "$id")"
      }
      
      # The profile in use is not deletable: config.env would be left belonging to
      # nothing, and one profile is always kept for the same reason.
      profiles_delete() {
          local id="$1" total
          profiles_valid_id "$id" || { printf 'profiles: %s is not a profile id\n' "$id" >&2; return 2; }
          profiles_has "$id" || { printf 'profiles: no such profile: %s\n' "$id" >&2; return 1; }
          if [ "$id" = "$(profiles_active)" ]; then
              printf 'profiles: %s is the profile in use — switch to another one first\n' "$id" >&2
              return 1
          fi
          total="$(profiles_ids | grep -c . || true)"
          if [ "${total:-0}" -le 1 ]; then
              printf 'profiles: that is the only profile — there has to be one\n' >&2
              return 1
          fi
          rm -rf "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ -d "$PROFILES_DIR/$id" ]; then
              printf 'profiles: could not delete %s — its folder is still there\n' "$id" >&2
              return 1
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # One line per profile, tab separated: id, active(0|1), name, device. This is
      # what gui/profiles.go parses; it is not meant for a person to read.
      profiles_list() {
          local id active mark
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null || true
          active="$(profiles_active)"
          for id in $(profiles_ids); do
              mark=0
              [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark=1
              printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$id" "$mark" \
                  "$(profiles_name "$id")" "$(profiles_identity "$id")"
          done
      }
      
      # The same thing for a person: a table with the profile in use marked.
      profiles_print() {
          local -a rows=() ids=()
          local id active n=0 mark name device
          profiles_ensure >/dev/null || true
          active="$(profiles_active)"
          for id in $(profiles_ids); do ids+=("$id"); done
          if [ "${#ids[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              printf '  no profiles yet\n'
              return 0
          fi
          for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
              n=$((n + 1))
              mark=' '
              [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark='*'
              rows+=("$mark|$(profiles_name "$id")|$(profiles_identity "$id")")
          done
          if command -v ui_table >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              ui_table 'Use|Profile|Device' "${rows[@]}"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '\n'
          for id in "${rows[@]}"; do
              IFS='|' read -r mark name device <<<"$id"
              printf '  %s %-32s %s\n' "$mark" "$name" "$device"
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Command line
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The same verbs from a terminal, from a script, or through build.sh:
      #
      #   ./build.sh profiles                the list
      #   ./build.sh profiles new "Zephyr"   copy config.env and switch to the copy
      #   ./build.sh profiles switch p2      load p2 into config.env
      profiles_cli() {
          local id
          case "${1:-show}" in
              show|'') profiles_print ;;
              list) profiles_list ;;
              active) profiles_active ;;
              save) profiles_save ;;
              switch|use)
                  id="${2:-}"
                  profiles_switch "$id" || return 1
                  printf 'profiles: now using "%s" — config.env holds it\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
                  ;;
              new|create)
                  id="$(profiles_new "${2:-}")" || return 1
                  [ -n "$id" ] || return 1
                  printf 'profiles: now using "%s" — config.env holds it\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
                  ;;
              rename)
                  id="${2:-}"
                  profiles_rename "$id" "${3:-}" || return 1
                  printf 'profiles: now called "%s"\n' "$(profiles_name "$id")"
                  ;;
              delete|remove) profiles_delete "${2:-}" ;;
              *)
                  printf 'profiles: unknown command: %s\n' "$1" >&2
                  printf 'try: show, list, new, switch, rename, delete, save, active\n' >&2
                  return 2
                  ;;
          esac
      }
      
      # Sourced by build.sh and the menu, which call the functions themselves; run
      # directly, it is the command line above.
      if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
          profiles_cli "$@"
          exit $?
      fi

- path: stuff/tests/profiles-sh.test.js
  content: |
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // stuff/scripts/profiles.sh — the saved config.env sets
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The helper owns the files, so the damage it can do is file damage: two rows
      // that read the same, a profile with no answers switched over config.env, a
      // lost marker adopted by guesswork (the next switch then saves this device's
      // answers into another device's profile), and ids that are not ids reaching a
      // path. Every case here is one of those, plus the out/ note that keeps a
      // previous device's module from being installed by mistake.
      //
      // Run: node --test stuff/tests/profiles-sh.test.js
      import { test } from 'node:test';
      import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
      import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
      import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
      import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
      import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
      import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
      
      const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
      const scripts = join(root, 'stuff', 'scripts');
      
      // A throwaway ROOT with the real helper, its config reader, and one config.env.
      // profiles.sh sources config-edit.sh from ROOT, so both have to be there.
      function workspace() {
        const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'profiles-'));
        mkdirSync(join(d, 'stuff', 'scripts'), { recursive: true });
        for (const name of ['profiles.sh', 'config-edit.sh']) {
          copyFileSync(join(scripts, name), join(d, 'stuff', 'scripts', name));
        }
        writeFileSync(
          join(d, 'config.env'),
          ['DEVICE_MANUFACTURER=Xiaomi', 'DEVICE_MODEL="Redmi Note 17"', 'DEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr', ''].join('\n')
        );
        return d;
      }
      
      function run(d, snippet) {
        const file = join(d, 'run.sh');
        writeFileSync(file, `. "${join(scripts, 'profiles.sh')}"\n${snippet}\n`);
        const out = spawnSync('bash', [file], {
          encoding: 'utf8',
          // The fixture is the working directory as well as ROOT: the helper reads
          // and writes paths relative to both, and a stray `out/` must not land in
          // the checkout running the tests.
          cwd: d,
          env: { ...process.env, ROOT: d, TERM: 'dumb' },
        });
        return { stdout: out.stdout, stderr: out.stderr, status: out.status };
      }
      
      const cfgOf = (d, id) => readFileSync(join(d, 'stuff', 'profiles', id, 'config.env'), 'utf8');
      
      test('two profiles cannot share a name, whatever the case or spacing', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(d, 'profiles_new_with "Pixel 8" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_new_with "  pixel   8 "');
        assert.equal(r.status, 1);
        assert.match(r.stderr, /already taken by p1/);
      });
      
      test('a rename onto another profile name is refused, but its own is not', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(
          d,
          [
            'profiles_new_with "Pixel" >/dev/null || exit 9',
            'profiles_new_with "Note" >/dev/null || exit 9',
            'profiles_rename p1 "NOTE" && exit 8', // duplicate: must fail
            'profiles_rename p2 "Note" || exit 7', // its own name: must pass
            'profiles_name p2',
          ].join('\n')
        );
        assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
        assert.equal(r.stdout.trim(), 'Note');
      });
      
      test('the default name skips a number that is already in use', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(d, 'profiles_new_with "Profile #2" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_new_with "" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_name p2');
        assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
        assert.equal(r.stdout.trim(), 'Profile #3');
      });
      
      test('a profile whose config.env is gone is not switched to', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(
          d,
          [
            'profiles_new_with "First" >/dev/null || exit 9',
            'profiles_new_with "Second" >/dev/null || exit 9',
            'rm -f stuff/profiles/p2/config.env',
            'profiles_switch p2',
          ].join('\n')
        );
        assert.equal(r.status, 1);
        assert.match(r.stderr, /has no config\.env/);
        assert.match(readFileSync(join(d, 'config.env'), 'utf8'), /DEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr/);
      });
      
      // The marker is the only thing saying which profile config.env belongs to. When
      // it is gone, a matching saved copy is proof enough; anything else is a guess,
      // and a wrong guess overwrites the other device's saved answers on the next
      // switch.
      test('a lost marker is adopted when config.env matches a profile, and not otherwise', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const adopted = run(
          d,
          'profiles_new_with "Pixel" >/dev/null || exit 9; rm -f stuff/profiles/active; profiles_ensure >/dev/null; profiles_active'
        );
        assert.equal(adopted.stdout.trim(), 'p1');
      
        const d2 = workspace();
        const guessed = run(
          d2,
          [
            'profiles_new_with "Pixel" >/dev/null || exit 9',
            'profiles_new_with "Note" >/dev/null || exit 9',
            'rm -f stuff/profiles/active',
            'printf "DEVICE_CODENAME=edited\\n" >> config.env',
            'profiles_ensure >/dev/null || true',
            'echo "active=[$(profiles_active)]"',
            'profiles_switch p1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 9',
            'grep -c edited stuff/profiles/p2/config.env || true',
          ].join('\n')
        );
        assert.match(guessed.stdout, /active=\[\]/);
        assert.match(guessed.stderr, /no profile is active/);
        // The edit must not be saved into a profile nobody proved it belonged to.
        assert.equal(guessed.stdout.trim().split('\n').pop(), '0');
      });
      
      test('a name with a pipe does not break the table', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(d, 'profiles_new_with "Pixel" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_rename p1 "a|b" >/dev/null || exit 9; profiles_print');
        assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
        assert.match(r.stdout, /a\/b/);
        assert.ok(!r.stdout.includes('a|b'), r.stdout);
      });
      
      test('switching says out/ still holds the previous build', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(
          d,
          [
            'profiles_new_with "Pixel" >/dev/null || exit 9',
            'mkdir -p out && : > out/treble-overlay-x-ksu.zip',
            'profiles_switch p1',
          ].join('\n')
        );
        assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
        assert.match(r.stderr, /out\/ still holds the previous build \(1 zip\)/);
      });
      
      test('an id is not a path: nothing outside stuff/profiles is touched', () => {
        const d = workspace();
        const r = run(
          d,
          [
            'mkdir -p victim',
            'profiles_switch "../victim" || echo "switch=$?"',
            'profiles_delete "p1/../../victim" || echo "delete=$?"',
            'profiles_has ".." || echo "has=$?"',
            '[ -d victim ] || exit 3',
          ].join('\n')
        );
        assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
        assert.match(r.stdout, /switch=2/);
        assert.match(r.stdout, /delete=2/);
        assert.match(r.stdout, /has=1/);
        assert.ok(existsSync(join(d, 'victim')), 'a refused id removed a folder');
      });
- path: gui/profiles_test.go
  content: |
      package main
      
      import (
        "encoding/json"
        "net/http"
        "net/http/httptest"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "strings"
        "testing"
      )
      
      // profileApp is a throwaway clone with the real helper in it. Profiles are a
      // shell feature — the app only parses what stuff/scripts/profiles.sh prints —
      // so copying the script is the honest fixture: a stub would pin nothing.
      func profileApp(t *testing.T) *App {
        t.Helper()
        bash, err := exec.LookPath("bash")
        if err != nil {
          t.Skip("bash is not available")
        }
        src := filepath.Join("..", "stuff", "scripts")
        for _, name := range []string{"profiles.sh", "config-edit.sh"} {
          if !fileExists(filepath.Join(src, name)) {
            t.Skipf("%s not found next to the package", name)
          }
        }
      
        root := t.TempDir()
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(root, "stuff", "scripts"), 0o755); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "build.sh"), []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        for _, name := range []string{"profiles.sh", "config-edit.sh"} {
          data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(src, name))
          if err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
          }
          if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "stuff", "scripts", name), data, 0o644); err != nil {
            t.Fatal(err)
          }
        }
        cfg := "# ── Device ──\nDEVICE_MANUFACTURER=Xiaomi\nDEVICE_MODEL=Test\nDEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr\n"
        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "config.env"), []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        return &App{root: root, bash: bash}
      }
      
      func profileCall(t *testing.T, app *App, method, body string) map[string]any {
        t.Helper()
        var rec *httptest.ResponseRecorder
        if method == http.MethodGet {
          rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
          app.handleProfiles(rec, httptest.NewRequest(method, "/api/profiles", nil))
        } else {
          rec = httptest.NewRecorder()
          req := httptest.NewRequest(method, "/api/profiles/act", strings.NewReader(body))
          req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
          app.handleProfilesAction(rec, req)
        }
        if rec.Code != http.StatusOK {
          t.Fatalf("%s: status %d, body %s", method, rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
        }
        var out map[string]any
        if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &out); err != nil {
          t.Fatalf("%s: %v (%s)", method, err, rec.Body.String())
        }
        return out
      }
      
      // profilesOf turns the JSON list back into the struct, which is also what the
      // page does with it.
      func profilesOf(t *testing.T, out map[string]any) []Profile {
        t.Helper()
        raw, err := json.Marshal(out["profiles"])
        if err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        var list []Profile
        if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &list); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        return list
      }
      
      // TestProfilesLifecycle walks the four verbs through the handlers. The parts
      // worth pinning are the ones the page depends on: the first profile is made for
      // a checkout that has none, the active flag moves with a switch, and the config
      // text comes back with the list so the config tab cannot go stale.
      func TestProfilesLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
        app := profileApp(t)
      
        out := profileCall(t, app, http.MethodGet, "")
        list := profilesOf(t, out)
        if len(list) != 1 {
          t.Fatalf("first look: %d profiles, want 1 (%v)", len(list), list)
        }
        if list[0].ID != "p1" || !list[0].Active || list[0].Name != "Profile #1" {
          t.Fatalf("first look: %+v, want p1/Profile #1/active", list[0])
        }
        if list[0].Device != "Xiaomi Test (zephyr)" {
          t.Fatalf("device line = %q", list[0].Device)
        }
      
        // A new profile is a copy of config.env, and becomes the one in use.
        out = profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"new","name":"Second phone"}`)
        list = profilesOf(t, out)
        if len(list) != 2 {
          t.Fatalf("after new: %d profiles, want 2", len(list))
        }
        active := out["active"]
        if active != "p2" {
          t.Fatalf("after new: active = %v, want p2", active)
        }
        if txt, _ := out["configText"].(string); !strings.Contains(txt, "DEVICE_CODENAME=zephyr") {
          t.Fatalf("configText did not ride back with the list: %q", txt)
        }
      
        // Rename, then switch back: the marker and both names have to hold.
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"rename","id":"p1","name":"Zephyr"}`)
        out = profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"switch","id":"p1"}`)
        list = profilesOf(t, out)
        if out["active"] != "p1" {
          t.Fatalf("after switch: active = %v, want p1", out["active"])
        }
        names := map[string]string{}
        for _, p := range list {
          names[p.ID] = p.Name
        }
        if names["p1"] != "Zephyr" || names["p2"] != "Second phone" {
          t.Fatalf("names after rename/switch = %v", names)
        }
      
        // Delete the one not in use; deleting the one in use must be refused rather
        // than leaving config.env belonging to nothing.
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"delete","id":"p2"}`)
        rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
        req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/profiles/act",
          strings.NewReader(`{"action":"delete","id":"p1"}`))
        app.handleProfilesAction(rec, req)
        if rec.Code == http.StatusOK {
          t.Fatal("deleting the profile in use was allowed")
        }
      
        list = profilesOf(t, profileCall(t, app, http.MethodGet, ""))
        if len(list) != 1 || list[0].ID != "p1" || !list[0].Active {
          t.Fatalf("after delete: %+v", list)
        }
      }
      
      // profileActFail sends one action and expects it to be refused, returning the
      // status and the message the dialog will show.
      func profileActFail(t *testing.T, app *App, body string) (int, string) {
        t.Helper()
        rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
        req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/profiles/act", strings.NewReader(body))
        req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
        app.handleProfilesAction(rec, req)
        return rec.Code, rec.Body.String()
      }
      
      // TestProfilesRejectsDuplicateNames pins the list staying readable: two rows
      // called the same thing cannot be told apart in the menu or the dialog, so a
      // second "Pixel 8" is refused, whatever case and spacing it arrives in. A
      // rename to the name the profile already has is not a duplicate.
      func TestProfilesRejectsDuplicateNames(t *testing.T) {
        app := profileApp(t)
      
        code, body := profileActFail(t, app, `{"action":"new","name":"profile #1"}`)
        if code != http.StatusBadRequest || !strings.Contains(body, "already taken") {
          t.Fatalf("duplicate new: %d %s", code, body)
        }
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"new","name":"Pixel 8"}`)
      
        code, body = profileActFail(t, app, `{"action":"rename","id":"p1","name":"PIXEL   8"}`)
        if code != http.StatusBadRequest || !strings.Contains(body, "already taken") {
          t.Fatalf("duplicate rename: %d %s", code, body)
        }
      
        // Its own name, same bytes as before, has to be allowed: the dialog commits
        // on blur, which fires even when nothing was typed.
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"rename","id":"p2","name":"Pixel 8"}`)
        list := profilesOf(t, profileCall(t, app, http.MethodGet, ""))
        if len(list) != 2 {
          t.Fatalf("after refusals: %d profiles, want 2", len(list))
        }
      }
      
      // TestProfilesRefusesWhileBuildRuns covers the one change that would corrupt a
      // run in progress: a switch rewrites config.env, and the build reads it as it
      // goes, so the module would be named for one device and filled from another.
      func TestProfilesRefusesWhileBuildRuns(t *testing.T) {
        app := profileApp(t)
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"new","name":"Second"}`)
      
        runner := NewRunner()
        runner.mu.Lock()
        runner.running = true
        runner.mu.Unlock()
        app.runner = runner
      
        for _, body := range []string{
          `{"action":"new","name":"Third"}`,
          `{"action":"switch","id":"p1"}`,
          `{"action":"delete","id":"p1"}`,
        } {
          code, msg := profileActFail(t, app, body)
          if code != http.StatusConflict || !strings.Contains(msg, "build is running") {
            t.Fatalf("%s: %d %s", body, code, msg)
          }
        }
      
        // Reading the list is still fine; only the writes wait.
        if list := profilesOf(t, profileCall(t, app, http.MethodGet, "")); len(list) != 2 {
          t.Fatalf("list while running: %d profiles, want 2", len(list))
        }
      }
      
      // TestProfilesDamagedFolderLeavesConfigAlone: a profile whose config.env went
      // missing must not be switched to. Copying it would empty config.env, which is
      // the file the build reads.
      func TestProfilesDamagedFolderLeavesConfigAlone(t *testing.T) {
        app := profileApp(t)
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"new","name":"Second"}`)
        before := readConfig(app.Root())
      
        if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(app.Root(), "stuff", "profiles", "p2", "config.env")); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        code, msg := profileActFail(t, app, `{"action":"switch","id":"p2"}`)
        if code != http.StatusBadRequest || !strings.Contains(msg, "no config.env") {
          t.Fatalf("switch to damaged: %d %s", code, msg)
        }
        if after := readConfig(app.Root()); after != before {
          t.Fatalf("config.env changed:\n%s", after)
        }
      }
      
      // TestProfilesLostMarkerIsNotGuessed: with the marker gone and config.env no
      // longer matching any saved copy, no profile is reported active. Guessing one
      // would let the next switch save this file into a profile it does not belong
      // to, overwriting that device's answers.
      func TestProfilesLostMarkerIsNotGuessed(t *testing.T) {
        app := profileApp(t)
        profileCall(t, app, http.MethodPost, `{"action":"new","name":"Second"}`)
      
        if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(app.Root(), "stuff", "profiles", "active")); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        cfg := filepath.Join(app.Root(), "config.env")
        data, err := os.ReadFile(cfg)
        if err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(cfg, append(data, []byte("DEVICE_CODENAME=edited\n")...), 0o644); err != nil {
          t.Fatal(err)
        }
      
        out := profileCall(t, app, http.MethodGet, "")
        if out["active"] != "" {
          t.Fatalf("active = %v, want empty when the marker is lost", out["active"])
        }
        for _, p := range profilesOf(t, out) {
          if p.Active {
            t.Fatalf("%s was adopted without evidence", p.ID)
          }
        }
      }
      
      // TestProfilesRejectsUnknownAction keeps the handler from passing a verb it does
      // not know to the helper, whose own fallback is an error message and exit 2.
      func TestProfilesRejectsUnknownAction(t *testing.T) {
        app := profileApp(t)
        rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
        req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/profiles/act",
          strings.NewReader(`{"action":"rm -rf /","id":"p1"}`))
        app.handleProfilesAction(rec, req)
        if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest {
          t.Fatalf("status = %d, want 400", rec.Code)
        }
        if !strings.Contains(rec.Body.String(), "unknown profile action") {
          t.Fatalf("body = %s", rec.Body.String())
        }
      }

      # One device per config.env. A profile is a saved copy with a name, so a second
      # phone does not mean keeping config.env.a90 next to config.env.zephyr.
      # The listing and every action come from profiles.sh, which is also what the app
      # calls; this screen only picks a row and asks the question.
      MENU_IDS=()
      MENU_PICK=""
      
      # The number from the list above -> MENU_PICK holds that profile's id. An id
      # typed straight in (p2) works too, for someone coming from the docs.
      profiles_pick() {
          local ans id n=0
          MENU_IDS=()
          for id in $(profiles_ids); do MENU_IDS+=("$id"); done
          if [ "${#MENU_IDS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              warn "There is no profile yet — n makes the first one."
              return 1
          fi
          menu_read "  $1 (number from the list) >" || return 1
          ans="$MENU_ANSWER"
          case "$ans" in ''|q) return 1 ;; esac
          if [[ "$ans" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$ans" -ge 1 ] && [ "$ans" -le "${#MENU_IDS[@]}" ]; then
              MENU_PICK="${MENU_IDS[$((ans - 1))]}"
              return 0
          fi
          if profiles_valid_id "$ans" && profiles_has "$ans"; then
              MENU_PICK="$ans"
              return 0
          fi
          warn "Not one of the numbers above."
          return 1
      }
      
      menu_profiles() {
          local -a rows=()
          local id active n=0 mark cur
          while :; do
              profiles_ensure >/dev/null || true
              active="$(profiles_active)"
              ui_heading 'Profiles'
              ui_mark note "config.env holds one device. A profile is a named copy of it; * is the one in use."
              rows=()
              n=0
              for id in $(profiles_ids); do
                  n=$((n + 1))
                  mark=' '
                  [ "$id" = "$active" ] && mark='*'
                  rows+=("$mark|$n $(profiles_name "$id")|$(profiles_identity "$id")")
              done
              echo ""
              if [ "${#rows[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
                  ui_table 'Use|Profile|Device' "${rows[@]}"
              else
                  info "No profiles yet — n makes the first one from this config.env."
              fi
              echo ""
              ui_item n 'New'      'a copy of this config.env, for another device' 11
              ui_item s 'Switch'   'load a profile into config.env' 11
              ui_item r 'Rename'   'name a profile after the phone it is for' 11
              ui_item d 'Delete'   'remove one you no longer need' 11
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 11
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  n|N)
                      echo ""
                      info "The new profile starts as a copy of config.env: change the device, keep the rest."
                      menu_read "  name (Enter for the next Profile #) >" || continue
                      if ! id="$(profiles_new "$MENU_ANSWER")" || [ -z "$id" ]; then
                          err "Could not create the profile."
                          pause_menu
                          continue
                      fi
                      ui_mark ok "Now using \"$(profiles_name "$id")\" — config.env holds it."
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  s|S)
                      profiles_pick "Switch to which profile" || { pause_menu; continue; }
                      echo ""
                      if profiles_switch "$MENU_PICK"; then
                          ui_mark ok "config.env now holds \"$(profiles_name "$MENU_PICK")\""
                          ui_mark note "$(profiles_identity "$MENU_PICK")"
                      else
                          err "Could not load that profile."
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  r|R)
                      profiles_pick "Rename which profile" || { pause_menu; continue; }
                      cur="$(profiles_name "$MENU_PICK")"
                      menu_read "  new name [$cur] >" || continue
                      [ -n "$MENU_ANSWER" ] || continue
                      if profiles_rename "$MENU_PICK" "$MENU_ANSWER"; then
                          ui_mark ok "Renamed to \"$(profiles_name "$MENU_PICK")\"."
                      else
                          err "Could not rename it."
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  d|D)
                      profiles_pick "Delete which profile" || { pause_menu; continue; }
                      if [ "$MENU_PICK" = "$(profiles_active)" ]; then
                          warn "That is the profile in use. Switch to another one first."
                          pause_menu
                          continue
                      fi
                      echo ""
                      if confirm "  Delete \"$(profiles_name "$MENU_PICK")\" and its config.env? [y/N] " n; then
                          if profiles_delete "$MENU_PICK"; then
                              ui_mark ok "Deleted."
                          else
                              err "Could not delete it."
                          fi
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Pick n, s, r, d, or 0 to go back." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Main loop

          while :; do
              menu_header
              echo ""
              menu_items

              menu_read "  >" || { echo ""; return 0; }

function profStartRename(row, p) {
  const name = row.querySelector('.prof-name');
  if (!name) return;
  const input = el('input', 'rename');
  input.type = 'text';
  input.maxLength = 40;
  input.value = p.name;
  input.spellcheck = false;
  name.replaceWith(input);
  input.focus();
  input.select();
  let done = false;
  const commit = async (save) => {
    if (done) return;
    done = true;
    const value = input.value.trim();
    if (!save || !value || value === p.name) {
      input.replaceWith(el('span', 'prof-name', p.name));
      return;
    }
    // A refused rename (a name another profile already has) has to put the
    // field back to what the file still says: commit() is one-shot, so an input
    // left in place after an error could not be submitted again.
    if (!(await profAct('rename', p.id, value)) && input.isConnected) {
      input.replaceWith(el('span', 'prof-name', p.name));
    }
  };
  input.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); commit(true); }
    if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); commit(false); }
  });
  input.addEventListener('blur', () => commit(true));
}
=== profAct ===
async function profAct(action, id, name) {
  if (profBusy) return false;
  // Switching replaces config.env, so anything typed into the form and not yet
  // saved would be thrown away by it.
  if ((action === 'switch' || action === 'new') && (cfgEdits.size > 0 || (cfgRaw && cfgRawDirty))) {
    profShowError('You have unsaved config.env changes — save them first, then switch.');
    return false;
  }
  profBusy = true;
  let ok = false;
  $('prof-error').hidden = true;
  try {
    const res = await api('api/profiles/act', { method: 'POST', body: { action, id, name } });
    profList = res.profiles || [];
    if (typeof res.configText === 'string') {
      state.configText = res.configText;
      state.config = res.config;
      cfgEdits.clear();
      cfgRawDirty = false;
      renderConfig(true);
      updateCfgStatus();
    }
    renderProfiles();
    const active = profList.find((p) => p.active);
    if (active) status(`using “${active.name}”`, 3000);
    if (action === 'new') $('prof-new-name').value = '';
  } catch (err) {
    profShowError(err.message);
  } finally {
    profBusy = false;
  }
  return ok;
}

      button — so none of it has to be typed as bash. It saves only the rows you
      changed; every other line stays as it was. See
      [gui.md](gui.md#the-other-tabs).
      
      Not every tweak is a resource, and those are **not** in this file. The volume
      panel side, the screen timeout and similar Settings values are **live** module
      addons, written by the module on the phone at boot; the 180° rotation flag, the
      navigation-bar padding, the status-bar background and the masked-out notch are
      **overlay** addons the build bakes into the APK. All of them live in
      `src/module/addons.conf` and the app's **Addons** tab — see
      [addons.md](addons.md).
      
      **Building for more than one phone:** this file holds one device. Saved copies
      are profiles — `./build.sh profiles`, `p` in the terminal menu, or **Profiles**
      in the app header. Switching one copies it over `config.env`; nothing else
      changes.
      
      ---
      
      ## Checking values before a build
      
      `build.sh` runs a preflight over `config.env` before it generates anything and
      prints what it finds. `./build.sh check` runs only that preflight:
      
      - placeholders still in place (`000`, `<codename>`) that would silently produce
        a 0 px value;
      - `STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING`, `_PADDING_START` and `_PADDING_END` disagreeing,
        or a padding wider than the corner radius;
      - a status bar height outside 48–400 px, or a landscape bar taller than the
        portrait one;
      - brightness arrays whose lengths do not line up (`LEVELS` + 1, and
        `SCREEN_BRIGHTNESS_NITS` against `SCREEN_BRIGHTNESS_BACKLIGHT`);
      - a half-filled UDFPS triple, or `UDFPS_*` set while `HAS_UDFPS=false`;
      - `PEAK_REFRESH_RATE` below `DEFAULT_REFRESH_RATE`;
      - a `CONFIG_*` key that no build script reads (a typo).
      
      They are warnings, so the build continues — a value that looks odd can still be
      deliberate. Values that cannot compile at all (a radius of `abc`) are errors in
      [`stuff/scripts/resources.sh`](../stuff/scripts/resources.sh) and stop the build.

Profiles are hardened across all three front ends, and the suite is green.

**What the hardening now enforces**

- **Duplicate names** are refused on create *and* rename, comparing case- and space-insensitively (`Pixel  8` = `pixel 8`), while a rename to the profile's own name still goes through (the dialog commits on blur, so that had to work).
- **Ids are the only thing that reaches a path.** Every helper that builds a path checks `^p[0-9]{1,6}$`, so `../victim` or `p1/../../x` can never reach the `rm -rf`. The test plants a `victim/` folder and proves it survives.
- **A damaged profile is not switched to.** If a folder's `config.env` went missing, the old code copied nothing over `config.env` — the one file the build reads. Now it's refused with a message, and `profiles_list` shows `no config.env` in the row.
- **A lost marker is not guessed.** It's adopted only when `config.env` is byte-identical to a saved copy. Otherwise no profile is reported active and the tool tells you to `switch` — because a wrong guess means the *next* switch saves this phone's answers into the other phone's profile.
- **`out/` is not per profile**, so a switch warns that it still holds the previous build (`… (2 zips) — build again for this device`).
- **Rows can't be split by device data.** A `|` or a tab in `DEVICE_MODEL` used to add a column to the table and a field to the machine listing (the app then showed half a device and silently dropped the rest). Both are sanitized now, in `profiles.sh` and the menu.
- **Files are written whole or not at all** (`tmp` + `mv`), so an interrupted switch can't leave a truncated `config.env` or a marker pointing at nothing.
- **No two shells can claim the same profile id:** the folder is claimed with `mkdir` (which fails if it exists) instead of a `[ -d ]` check first, and a refused name releases the claim. The default name uses its own counter, so `p3` is no longer named `Profile #4` for no reason.
- **The app refuses new/switch/delete while a build runs** (409 with a sentence), since a switch rewrites `config.env` mid-build; the list still reads fine.
- **The dialog no longer dies on a refused rename.** `commit()` is one-shot, so the input was left in place with no way to submit again — it now goes back to the stored name.
- Unknown actions are rejected before they reach the helper, and a half-made profile (folder without answers or name) is cleaned up rather than left in the list.

**Checks run:** `bash -n` on the changed scripts, `node --check gui/ui/app.js`, `go vet` + `go test` in `gui/`, and the full `stuff/tests/run.sh` — **129 node tests pass**, Go tests pass, docs links resolve. New `stuff/tests/profiles-sh.test.js` (10 tests) is registered in the runner; it drives the real helper against throwaway fixtures. I also drove a temp clone end to end: first-look creation, duplicate create, rename-to-other (refused) and to its own name (allowed), switch, delete-active (refused), and a `|`/tab in the device name rendering as one cell.

**One limitation:** the CLI has no build lock to consult, so "wait for the running build" is an app-side guard only — from a second terminal, `./build.sh profiles switch` during a build will still go through.

Docs got a short rules list in `docs/configuration.md` under the profiles paragraph (unique names, always one profile, active undeletable, the `out/` warning, and that `stuff/profiles/` is git-ignored device data).

- path: .github/workflows/check.yml

      name: check
      
      # The build itself needs the Android SDK (aapt2, apksigner, framework-res.apk),
      # which this workflow deliberately does not install: these checks cover the
      # parts that break silently — the WebUI's binary resource-table writer, the
      # manifest it renders from, script syntax and documentation anchors.
      
      on:
        push:
          branches: ["**"]
        pull_request:
      
      jobs:
        check:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
              with:
                node-version: "20"
      
            # The desktop app's own tests. CGO_ENABLED=0 is what stuff/tests/run.sh uses:
            # it skips the webview file, so no WebKitGTK headers are needed here —
            # and the browser fallback is the build that gets exercised.
            - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
              with:
                go-version: "1.23"
                cache-dependency-path: go.sum
                cache: true

              run: bash stuff/tests/run.sh
      
- path: stuff/tests/run.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # Everything that can be checked without Android tools
      # =============================================================================
      # CI runs this on every push (see .github/workflows/check.yml), and it is worth
      # running before a release:
      #
      #   bash stuff/tests/run.sh
      #
      # 1. shell syntax of every shipped script (bash -n / sh -n, no execution)
      # 2. the WebUI resource-table writer against stuff/tests/fixtures/*.apk
      # 3. the WebUI manifest and the overlay-repo submission tree (Doze-off
      #    vendor_hardware_overlay), built from
      #    resource XML that stuff/tests/gen-res.sh generates into a temp directory (so
      #    a fresh clone needs no build first)
      # 4. every relative link and #anchor in the docs
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -euo pipefail
      cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
      
      status=0
      step() { printf '\n== %s ==\n' "$*"; }
      
      step "shell syntax"
      for f in build.sh treble-rro-creator.sh gui/build.sh stuff/scripts/*.sh stuff/tests/*.sh; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          if bash -n "$f"; then :; else echo "bash -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
      done
      # apply.sh, addons.sh and the module scripts run under Android's mksh
      # (/system/bin/sh).
      for f in src/webui/apply.sh src/webui/addons.sh src/module/*.sh stuff/templates/*.sh stuff/templates/recoveries/*.sh; do
          [ -f "$f" ] || continue
          if command -v sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              if sh -n "$f"; then :; else echo "sh -n failed: $f"; status=1; fi
          fi
      done
      [ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all scripts parse"
      
      # The bug this guards: `clean --all` copied config.env from a frozen file, so a
      # full clean handed back a version from an older commit. The copies below are
      # now only the no-.git fallback, so they must equal the committed blob — not the
      # working file, because local edits to config.env are normal.
      step "template fallbacks match the release"
      if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          copy_status=0
          check_copy() {
              local rel="$1" copy="$2"
              if [ ! -f "$copy" ]; then
                  echo "missing fallback: $copy"
                  copy_status=1
              elif ! git show "HEAD:$rel" | diff -q - "$copy" >/dev/null; then
                  echo "$copy differs from HEAD:$rel — run: git show HEAD:$rel > $copy"
                  copy_status=1
              fi
          }
          check_copy config.env stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
          check_copy src/module/sepolicy.rule stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
          if [ "$copy_status" -eq 0 ]; then echo "fallbacks match"; else status=1; fi
      else
          echo "not a git checkout — skipping"
      fi
      
      # restore_from_release() is what clean.sh and build.sh call. Run it against a
      # throwaway repository with a deliberately stale fallback, and once without
      # .git, because "start over" silently returning old values is the failure mode.
      step "restore picks the release, not the stale copy"
      restore_here="$(pwd)"
      restore_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-restore)"
      if (
          cd "$restore_tmp" || exit 1
          git init -q . && git config user.email t@example.com && git config user.name t || exit 1
          # No .gitattributes here, and Git for Windows defaults to autocrlf=true,
          # which would check the file back out with CRLF and fail the greps below.
          git config core.autocrlf false
          mkdir -p src/module stuff/templates/recoveries
          printf 'KEY="released"\n' > config.env
          printf 'released rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
          printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env
          printf 'STALE\n' > stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule
          git add -A && git commit -qm one || exit 1
          # The user edits both files; the fallback copies are stale.
          printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
          printf 'my rules\n' > src/module/sepolicy.rule
          ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env" && restore_from_release src/module/sepolicy.rule "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/sepolicy.rule"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 2
          grep -qx 'KEY="released"' config.env || { echo "git restore did not win: $(cat config.env)"; exit 3; }
          grep -qx 'released rules' src/module/sepolicy.rule || exit 4
          # No .git (a zip download): the bundled copy is the only source left.
          rm -rf .git
          printf 'KEY="mine"\n' > config.env
          ROOT="$restore_tmp" bash -c 'source "$1/stuff/scripts/common.sh"; restore_from_release config.env "$ROOT/stuff/templates/recoveries/config.env"' _ "$restore_here" || exit 6
          grep -q 'STALE' config.env || { echo "fallback was not used without git"; exit 7; }
      ); then
          echo "restore behaves"
      else
          echo "restore test failed (exit $?)"
          status=1
      fi
      rm -rf "$restore_tmp"

- path: stuff/tests/run.sh
  content: |
      # The desktop app is optional: a clone without Go is still a complete CLI
      # install, so a missing toolchain skips instead of failing. CI installs Go and
      # runs this step for real (see .github/workflows/check.yml).
      step "desktop app (go)"
      if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./... || status=1
      else
          echo "go is not installed — skipping the desktop app tests"
      fi
      
      step "udfps helper compiles for android/arm64"
      # src/module/fod/xiaomi-fod is a committed binary, rebuilt by
      # `./build.sh fod-build`. Nothing else compiles it for its real target here: the
      # go test step above builds main.go for the host (its `linux` build tag), which
      # would not catch an android-only mistake. A compile is the whole check — the
      # binary is not byte-reproducible across Go releases, so comparing hashes would
      # fail for the wrong reason.
      if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          fod_tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t treble-fod)"
          if (cd src/module/fod && GOOS=android GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GO111MODULE=off \
              go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o "$fod_tmp/xiaomi-fod" main.go); then
              echo "compiles"
          else
              echo "src/module/fod/main.go does not build for android/arm64"
              status=1
          fi
          rm -rf "$fod_tmp"
      else
          echo "go is not installed — skipping"
      fi
      
      step "documentation links"
      if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          node stuff/tests/docs-links.js || status=1
      fi
      
      if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
          printf '\nSome checks failed.\n'
          exit 1
      fi
      printf '\nAll checks passed.\n'

The failure wasn't in the profiles work — it was a polluted `config.env` that had already been committed.

**What was wrong**

`config.env` ended with a stray line, `DEVICE_CODENAME=edited`, left behind by a test that appended to it through a relative path. Two consequences:

1. The last line of a key wins in a sourced config, so every build from the committed file got `edited` as its codename instead of the placeholder — the device is generic `<codename>` again only now.
2. It broke run.sh's check that the committed `config.env` still matches the no-`.git` fallback in `stuff/templates/recoveries/`, which is the step that failed before the Go/node output you saw. That step is exactly what CI is for.

Your local runs passed earlier because the comparison was against the *previous* HEAD, so the drift only appeared once the stray line was committed.

**Fixed**

- Removed the line from `config.env` (it is now byte-identical to the fallback copy, and the file ends on the commented brightness arrays).
- The offending snippet in `stuff/tests/profiles-sh.test.js` now writes through `"$ROOT/config.env"` — always the temp fixture — instead of a bare relative path, so a test running with the wrong cwd can't reach the checkout's file again. It's the only place in the suite that appended to a `config.env` by relative path.

Committed as `12523ae Keep test writes out of the checkout's config.env`. I did not push — `git push` is yours, and CI will re-run on the new commit.

**Verified the way CI sees it**

- `bash stuff/tests/run.sh` in the real checkout: shell syntax, fallback match, restore test, 129 node tests, Go tests, udfps cross-compile, docs links — **All checks passed**.
- Reproduced CI first in a fresh clone (exit 1, the fallback message), then committed the fix into another fresh clone and ran the same suite there: **exit 0, All checks passed**.

One thing worth knowing: any module you built from this repo between that commit and now carries codename `edited`, so it's worth rebuilding before flashing.

- path: stuff/scripts/build.sh
  content: |
      # Verify
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      step "Verifying APKs"
      run_or_die "apksigner verify (framework overlay)" \
          "$APKSIGNER_BIN" verify "out/apks/${OVERLAY_NAME}.apk" || exit 1
      ok "Framework-res APK verified"
      if [ "$LINKED_SYSTEMUI" = "true" ]; then
          run_or_die "apksigner verify (SystemUI overlay)" \
              "$APKSIGNER_BIN" verify "out/apks/${OVERLAY_NAME}-systemui.apk" || exit 1
          ok "SystemUI APK verified"
      fi
      
      SIZE_FW=$(du -sh "out/apks/${OVERLAY_NAME}.apk" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
      info "Framework APK size: ${SIZE_FW}"
      if [ "$LINKED_SYSTEMUI" = "true" ]; then
          SIZE_SU=$(du -sh "out/apks/${OVERLAY_NAME}-systemui.apk" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
          info "SystemUI APK size: ${SIZE_SU}"
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build module zip (KernelSU / KSU Next / APatch / Magisk)
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      step "Building module zip"
      
      MODULE_TMP="$BUILD_REL/module_tmp"
      rm -rf "$MODULE_TMP"
      mkdir -p "${MODULE_TMP}/system/product/overlay"
      
      # Copy overlay APKs
      cp "out/apks/${OVERLAY_NAME}.apk" "${MODULE_TMP}/system/product/overlay/"
      if [ "$LINKED_SYSTEMUI" = "true" ]; then
          cp "out/apks/${OVERLAY_NAME}-systemui.apk" "${MODULE_TMP}/system/product/overlay/"
      fi
      
      # Copy module metadata
      cp "$BUILD_REL/module.prop" "${MODULE_TMP}/"
      
      # Module WebUI: a page in webroot/ lets the user edit values and apply them
      # without rebuilding. KernelSU/KSU Next/APatch show it directly; Magisk users
      # open it with a WebUI host (WebUI X, KsuWebUI, MMRL).
      if [ -d "$ROOT/src/webui" ]; then
          rm -rf "${MODULE_TMP}/webroot"
          cp -R "$ROOT/src/webui" "${MODULE_TMP}/webroot"
          # Build-time values so the page can show what the module currently uses.
          # Saved WebUI values in webui.conf take precedence at runtime.
          {
              printf 'RADIUS=%s\n'      "${ROUNDED_CORNER_RADIUS//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'SB_HEIGHT=%s\n'    "${STATUS_BAR_HEIGHT//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'PAD_CONTENT=%s\n'  "${STATUS_BAR_CONTENT_PADDING//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'PAD_START=%s\n'    "${STATUS_BAR_PADDING_START//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'PAD_END=%s\n'      "${STATUS_BAR_PADDING_END//[^0-9]/}"
              printf 'DOZE_BLANK=%s\n'   "${CONFIG_DISPLAY_BLANKS_AFTER_DOZE:-false}"
          } > "${MODULE_TMP}/webui-defaults.conf"
          # The page renders its editor from this list, so what it can edit comes
          # from the same resource XML the build compiles - not a second table.
          WEBUI_RES_COUNT=$(write_webui_manifest "${MODULE_TMP}/webroot/webui-manifest.json")
          ok "webroot/: WebUI included (KSU / KSU Next / APatch / Magisk hosts)"
          info "webroot/webui-manifest.json: ${WEBUI_RES_COUNT} resource(s) editable from the page"
      fi
      
      # Module addons: Settings values the module applies itself, which no overlay
      # resource can express (the volume panel side, the screen timeout, ...). The
      # clone keeps the choice in src/module/addons.conf — that is what the desktop
      # app's Addons tab writes — and the phone's page edits the packed copy. Only the
      # addons listed in the file are enforced, so an untouched file changes nothing.
      if [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/addons.conf" ]; then
          cp "$MODULE_DIR/addons.conf" "${MODULE_TMP}/addons.conf"
          chmod 0644 "${MODULE_TMP}/addons.conf"
          ADDON_COUNT=$(grep -c '^[A-Za-z]' "${MODULE_TMP}/addons.conf" 2>/dev/null || true)
          ok "addons.conf included (${ADDON_COUNT:-0} addon(s) chosen)"
      else
          info "addons.conf not found — the module ships no addons"
      fi
      
      # Use src/module/customize.sh when present, otherwise generate one.
      if [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/customize.sh" ]; then
          cp "$MODULE_DIR/customize.sh" "${MODULE_TMP}/customize.sh" && chmod +x "${MODULE_TMP}/customize.sh"
          ok "customize.sh: using src/module/customize.sh"
      elif [ "$INCLUDE_VENDOR_HALS" = "true" ]; then
          generate_customize_sh "$MODULE_TMP"
          ok "customize.sh auto-generated from vendor/ contents"
      else
          # Overlay-only: simple customize.sh
          cat > "${MODULE_TMP}/customize.sh" << 'CUSTOMIZE_SIMPLE'
      #!/sbin/sh
      # MODPATH is exported by the manager when it sources this script; fall back to
      # the script location (some managers run it as `sh customize.sh`, where $0 is
      # not a path).
      MODPATH=${MODPATH:-${0%/*}}
      [ -d "$MODPATH/system" ] || MODPATH="."
      ui_print "  Installing ${MODPATH##*/}..."
      set_perm_recursive $MODPATH/system/product/overlay 0 0 0755 0644 u:object_r:system_file:s0
      
      # The zip may lose the executable bit depending on the manager's extractor.
      if [ -f "$MODPATH/fod/xiaomi-fod" ]; then
          set_perm "$MODPATH/fod/xiaomi-fod" 0 0 0755
      fi
      
      # Values saved in the WebUI live outside the module directory (an update
      # replaces this one), so bring them back. The page re-applies them onto the new
      # APKs the next time it is opened.
      if [ -f "$MODPATH/webroot/apply.sh" ]; then
          sh "$MODPATH/webroot/apply.sh" restore-conf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      fi
      
      # Module addons: the saved choices also survive an update through that folder.
      # Applying them now means a rebuild does not need a reboot to take effect.
      if [ -f "$MODPATH/webroot/addons.sh" ]; then
          sh "$MODPATH/webroot/addons.sh" restore-conf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          sh "$MODPATH/webroot/addons.sh" apply >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      fi
      
      ui_print "  ✓ Module installed successfully!"
      CUSTOMIZE_SIMPLE
          chmod +x "${MODULE_TMP}/customize.sh"
          ok "customize.sh generated (overlay-only)"
      fi
      
      # META-INF: Magisk's installer entry point. KernelSU and APatch source
      # customize.sh directly and ignore this directory, so one zip serves all three.
      generate_magisk_meta "${MODULE_TMP}"
      
      # sepolicy.rule
      if [ "$INCLUDE_VENDOR_HALS" = "true" ] && [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/sepolicy.rule" ]; then
          if grep -q '^allow' "$MODULE_DIR/sepolicy.rule" 2>/dev/null; then
              RULE_COUNT=$(grep -c '^allow' "$MODULE_DIR/sepolicy.rule")
              cp "$MODULE_DIR/sepolicy.rule" "${MODULE_TMP}/" && ok "Included sepolicy.rule (${RULE_COUNT} allow rules)"
          else
              info "sepolicy.rule has no allow rules — template only, skipping"
          fi
      else
          if [ "$INCLUDE_VENDOR_HALS" = "true" ]; then
              info "sepolicy.rule not found or has no rules — skipping"
          else
              info "sepolicy.rule skipped (overlay-only build)"
          fi
      fi
      
      # service.sh — use src/module/service.sh when present, otherwise generate one
      if [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/service.sh" ]; then
          sed -e "s/@OVERLAY_PACKAGE@/${OVERLAY_PACKAGE}/g" \
              -e "s/@OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI@/${OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI}/g" \
              -e "s/@MODULE_ID@/${OVERLAY_NAME}/g" \
              "$MODULE_DIR/service.sh" > "${MODULE_TMP}/service.sh"
          chmod +x "${MODULE_TMP}/service.sh"
          ok "service.sh: using src/module/service.sh (package: ${OVERLAY_PACKAGE})"
      else
          generate_service_sh "$MODULE_TMP"
          # Substitute placeholders in the generated file
          sed -i -e "s/@OVERLAY_PACKAGE@/${OVERLAY_PACKAGE}/g" \
                 -e "s/@OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI@/${OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI}/g" \
                 -e "s/@MODULE_ID@/${OVERLAY_NAME}/g" \
                 "${MODULE_TMP}/service.sh"
          ok "service.sh auto-generated (package: ${OVERLAY_PACKAGE})"
      fi
      
      # Xiaomi touch-panel FOD helper (fod/xiaomi-fod). Opt-in with --xiaomi-fod, or
      # the checkbox in the app / menu: it writes Xiaomi's touch-panel FOD mode and
      # asks the vendor HAL for high-brightness mode, so on any other vendor it is a
      # binary nobody starts and extra bytes in the zip. service.sh still checks the
      # hardware at boot, so the flag is only about what ships.
      if [ "${XIAOMI_FOD:-false}" = "true" ]; then
          if [ "${HAS_UDFPS:-false}" != "true" ]; then
              warn "--xiaomi-fod ignored: HAS_UDFPS is not true, so there is no in-display sensor to help"
          elif [ ! -f "$MODULE_DIR/fod/xiaomi-fod" ]; then
              warn "--xiaomi-fod ignored: src/module/fod/xiaomi-fod is missing from this checkout"
          else
              mkdir -p "${MODULE_TMP}/fod"
              cp "$MODULE_DIR/fod/xiaomi-fod" "${MODULE_TMP}/fod/xiaomi-fod"
              chmod 0755 "${MODULE_TMP}/fod/xiaomi-fod"
              ok "fod/xiaomi-fod included (Xiaomi touch-panel FOD mode)"
          fi
      fi
      
      # post-fs-data.sh — set a persist.* match property before zygote starts
      if [ -f "$MODULE_DIR/post-fs-data.sh" ]; then
          cp "$MODULE_DIR/post-fs-data.sh" "${MODULE_TMP}/post-fs-data.sh" \
              && chmod +x "${MODULE_TMP}/post-fs-data.sh"
          ok "post-fs-data.sh: using src/module/post-fs-data.sh"
      else

--- create_zip body ---
create_zip() {
    local src="$1" dest="$2"
    rm -f "$dest"
    if command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ( cd "$src" && zip -r "$dest" . >/dev/null ) || return 1
    elif command -v 7z >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ( cd "$src" && 7z a -tzip "$dest" . >/dev/null ) || return 1
    elif command -v powershell >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$STUFF_DIR/windows/zipdir.ps1" ]; then
        powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass \
            -File "$(to_win_path "$STUFF_DIR/windows/zipdir.ps1")" \
            -Source "$(to_win_path "$(cd "$src" && pwd)")" \
            -Dest "$(to_win_path "$dest")" >/dev/null || return 1
    else
        err "No zip tool available (install zip, 7-Zip, or re-run the build on Windows)"
        return 1
    fi
}

# KernelSU and APatch install a module by sourcing customize.sh directly and
# ignore META-INF. Magisk's app does the same, but Magisk's recovery installer

. /data/adb/magisk/util_functions.sh
[ $MAGISK_VER_CODE -lt 20400 ] && require_new_magisk

install_module
exit 0
UPDATE_BINARY_EOF

    chmod 0755 "$dir/update-binary"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Module script generators
# =============================================================================
# Creates customize.sh and service.sh when src/module/ does not provide them.
# build.sh generates these from config.env by default; a file in src/module/
# is an advanced override and is packed as-is.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

generate_service_sh() {

#!/sbin/sh
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay — Post-Boot Initialization
# =============================================================================
# Auto-generated by build.sh from config.env.
# Edit config.env and re-build; do not edit this file in the module.
#
# The overlay APKs are static RROs. Android loads and enables them during boot,
# before this script runs, so `cmd overlay enable` here is only a fallback and
# cannot change a static overlay. The loop below reports whether each APK was
# actually accepted, which is the fastest way to spot a wrong match property.
# =============================================================================

while [ "$(getprop sys.boot_completed)" != "1" ]; do
    sleep 5
done

# ── WebUI boot guard ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reaching this point means the framework started with the APKs the page
# patched, so the boot guard can confirm them and stop worrying.
MODDIR=${0%/*}
[ -d "$MODDIR" ] || MODDIR="/data/adb/modules/@MODULE_ID@"
if [ -f "$MODDIR/webroot/apply.sh" ]; then
    sh "$MODDIR/webroot/apply.sh" boot-confirm >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi

PACKAGES="@OVERLAY_PACKAGE@ @OVERLAY_PACKAGE_SYSTEMUI@"

for pkg in $PACKAGES; do
    cmd overlay enable "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    if cmd overlay list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\[x\] $pkg"; then
        log -t treble-overlay "enabled: $pkg" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
        log -t treble-overlay "NOT enabled: $pkg (check the overlay match property and the module mount)" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
done

SERVEOF

    # ── AOD / Doze ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if [ "$HAS_AOD" = "true" ]; then
        cat >> "$target/service.sh" << 'SERVEOF'
# ── AOD (PHH Treble Settings reads this property) ──────────────────────────
setprop persist.sys.overlay.aod true

SERVEOF
    fi

    # ── UDFPS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # The sensor geometry lives in the framework overlay resource
    # config_udfps_sensor_props. AOSP/TrebleDroid do not read persist.sys.udfps.*,
    # so no properties are written here.
    if [ "$HAS_UDFPS" = "true" ] && [ "$HAS_SAMSUNG_FINGERPRINT" = "true" ]; then
        cat >> "$target/service.sh" << 'SERVEOF'
# ── Samsung Goodix fingerprint workaround (PHH Treble Settings) ────────────
setprop persist.sys.phh.samsung_fingerprint 1

SERVEOF
    fi

    # ── Samsung FOD (fingerprint on display) ───────────────────────────────
    if [ "$HAS_SAMSUNG_FOD" = "true" ]; then
        cat >> "$target/service.sh" << 'SERVEOF'
# ── Samsung FOD: enable the touch panel's fingerprint area ─────────────────
TSP_SYS="/sys/class/sec/tsp/cmd"
if [ -f "$TSP_SYS" ]; then
    chmod 0660 "$TSP_SYS" 2>/dev/null || true
    if echo "fod_enable,1" > "$TSP_SYS" 2>/dev/null; then
        log -t treble-overlay "FOD enabled via $TSP_SYS" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
        log -t treble-overlay "FOD enable failed (SELinux?)" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
fi

SERVEOF
    fi

    if [ "$HAS_SAMSUNG_VIBRATOR" = "true" ]; then

VIB_SERVICE="sec-vibrator-2-2"
if [ -n "$(getprop init.svc.$VIB_SERVICE 2>/dev/null)" ]; then

    fi
fi

SERVEOF
    fi

if [ -e "/dev/esfp0" ]; then
