```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Treble Overlay Creator
# =============================================================================
# One command for everything. With a terminal attached it opens the menu, which
# reaches every tool the desktop app has; with an argument it does exactly that
# one thing, as before.
#
#   ./build.sh                 the menu (on a terminal); otherwise: build
#   ./build.sh menu            the menu, even without a terminal
#   ./build.sh build           build (auto-installs the toolchain if needed)
#   ./build.sh setup           install / repair the toolchain only
#   ./build.sh doctor          check the toolchain (read-only)
#   ./build.sh check           validate config.env without building
#   ./build.sh --dry-run       print the resources config.env emits, build nothing
#   ./build.sh fod-build       rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper (maintainers)
#   ./build.sh profiles        saved config.env setups, one per device
#   ./build.sh clean           remove build output
#   ./build.sh clean --all     start over for a different device
#
#   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
#   -V, --version              print the version
#   -h, --help                 this help
#
# On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
# Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
# drive — see docs/windows.md.
# =============================================================================

# pipefail matters here: most build steps run a tool and parse its output in a
# pipeline (`aapt2 dump ... | sed | awk`). Without it a failed tool still exits
# 0 through the pipeline and the build carries on with empty input.
set -eo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project root
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
# not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
fi
export ROOT
cd "$ROOT"

source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"

# Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
tools_on_path

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Options
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MODE="build"
REQUESTED=$#
CHECK_MODE=false
DRY_RUN=false
ASSUME_YES=false
FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
CLEAN_ALL=false
FORCE_RES=""
ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false

usage() {
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
    echo "    (none)             The menu (on a terminal), otherwise a build"
    echo "    menu               The menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes"
    echo "    build              Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
    echo "    profiles           Saved config.env setups: show, new, switch, rename, delete"
    echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
    echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
    echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
    echo "    install            Install out/<name>-ksu.zip on the phone, reboot, verify"
    echo "    fod-build          Rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper from its Go source"
    echo "    clean              Remove build output"
    echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
    echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
    echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
    echo "    --xiaomi-fod           Include the Xiaomi FOD helper (HBM + HIDL touch mode) in the module"
    echo "    --device SERIAL        With install: the phone to use, when more than one is attached"
    echo "    --zip PATH             With install: a module other than the newest build"
    echo "    --no-reboot            With install: hand it over, do not reboot or verify"
    echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
    echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
    echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
    echo "    --no-su                Termux: do not ask for root up front"
    echo "    -V, --version          Print the version"
    echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
    echo ""
}

# Options that only `install` understands are collected here and handed to
# install-module.sh, so the entry point keeps one parser.
INSTALL_EXTRA=()

# Everything after `profiles` belongs to profiles.sh (switch p2, rename p2 "…").
PROFILES_ARGS=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    arg="$1"
    case "$arg" in
        build)          MODE="build" ;;
        menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
        setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
        doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
        check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
        install)        MODE="install" ;;
        profiles)
            MODE="profiles"
            PROFILES_ARGS=("${@:2}")
            break
            ;;
        --device|--adb|--zip)
            INSTALL_EXTRA+=("$arg" "${2:-}")
            shift ;;
        --no-reboot|--no-verify)
            INSTALL_EXTRA+=("$arg") ;;
        fod-build|--fod-build) MODE="fodbuild" ;;
        clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
        dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
        -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
        --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
        --xiaomi-fod)   XIAOMI_FOD=true ;;
        --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
        --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
        --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
        # Exported, so a menu that shells out for a build does not ask again.
        --no-su)        export TREBLE_NO_SU=1 ;;
        -V|--version)   echo "Treble RRO Creator ${TOOL_VERSION}"; exit 0 ;;
        -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
        *)
```

```
# a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then

        migrate_layout

        exit $?

    doctor)
        if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi

    setup)
        banner "Setup — build tools"
        migrate_layout
        # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
        # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
        # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
        # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
        # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
        if $ASSUME_YES; then
            ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
        else
            ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
        fi
        exit $?
        ;;

    check)
        # Config validation only: no tools, no output.
        CHECK_MODE=true
        source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
        ;;

    fodbuild)
        # Maintainers only: the shipped helper is prebuilt on purpose, so no
        # user path reaches Go for it.
        bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/fod-build.sh"
        exit $?
        ;;

    install)
        migrate_layout
        # A child, not a source: it parses its own options and can be run on its
        # own (bash stuff/scripts/install-module.sh --zip out/x-ksu.zip).
        bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/install-module.sh" ${INSTALL_EXTRA[@]+"${INSTALL_EXTRA[@]}"}
        exit $?
        ;;

    profiles)
        migrate_layout
        . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/profiles.sh"
        profiles_cli ${PROFILES_ARGS[@]+"${PROFILES_ARGS[@]}"}
        exit $?
        ;;

    clean)
        migrate_layout
        source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/clean.sh"
        ;;

    dryrun)
        # Needs config.env and the resource generators, no toolchain: the point
        # is to see the plan in seconds.
        DRY_RUN=true
        source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
        ;;

    build)
        # Move any files left in the old top-level layout into src/.
        migrate_layout
        if $IS_WINDOWS; then
            banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Windows"
        elif $IS_TERMUX; then
            banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Termux"
        else
            banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Linux"
        fi
        # Installs only what is missing; prints a summary and returns non-zero
        # when the machine still cannot build.
        ensure_toolchain auto
        # The installer may just have created stuff/tools/, so refresh PATH.
        tools_on_path
        source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
        ;;
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# install-module.sh — put the built module on the phone, reboot, check it
# =============================================================================
# Building ends with a zip in out/ and four lines of instructions. This does the
# part people get wrong: copy the zip over, hand it to the root manager that is
# actually installed (ksud for KernelSU/KSU Next, magisk for Magisk), reboot,
# wait for the phone to come back, and then report whether the overlay really is
# mounted and enabled — the three things "did it work?" means.
#
#   ./build.sh install                  # the connected phone
#   ./build.sh install --no-reboot      # install, leave the reboot to you
#   ./build.sh install --device SERIAL  # more than one phone attached
#   ./build.sh install --zip PATH       # a module other than the newest build
#
#   Standalone: bash stuff/scripts/install-module.sh [the same options]
#
# In Termux the zip is installed on this phone directly (root, no adb) and the
# script stops after the install: rebooting the machine the script runs on
# cannot be followed by a verification pass.
#
# Verification is read-only: /data/adb/modules/<id> must exist with no `disable`
# or `remove` file, and `cmd overlay list` must show the package as enabled.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

# adb on Windows is a Git Bash binary: /sdcard/... would be rewritten into a
# Windows path before adb saw it.
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1

ROOT="${ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
. "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
. "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/adb-device.sh"

want_serial="${DEVICE_SERIAL:-}"
zip_path=""
do_reboot=1
do_verify=1

usage() {
    sed -n '3,23p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
}

die() { err "$1"; return 1; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --device) want_serial="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --zip) zip_path="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --no-reboot) do_reboot=0; shift ;;
        --no-verify) do_verify=0; shift ;;
        -y|--yes) do_reboot=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option: $1 (try --help)"; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

# The module id and package name are derived, not typed: the same function the
# build uses, from the same config.env, so what is installed is what was built.
[ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ] && . "$ROOT/config.env"
derive_overlay_identity >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

module_id="${OVERLAY_NAME:-}"
overlay_pkg="${OVERLAY_PACKAGE:-}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Which zip
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
install_find_zip() {
    if [ -n "$zip_path" ]; then
        [ -f "$zip_path" ] || { die "no such file: $zip_path"; return 1; }
        printf '%s' "$zip_path"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -n "$module_id" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/out/${module_id}-ksu.zip" ]; then
        printf '%s' "$ROOT/out/${module_id}-ksu.zip"
        return 0
    fi
    # A clean checkout builds a different device name than the config says; the
    # newest -ksu.zip is still the thing the user just built.
    local newest
    newest="$(ls -t "$ROOT"/out/*-ksu.zip 2>/dev/null | head -n1)"
    if [ -n "$newest" ]; then
        warn "no zip for ${module_id:-this config} — using $(basename "$newest")"
        printf '%s' "$newest"
        return 0
    fi
    die "nothing to install: out/ has no -ksu.zip. Run ./build.sh build first."
    return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Talking to the phone
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Root on the phone: local mode is already root, adb goes through su. One place,
# because every install and every check needs it.
install_root() {
    local cmd="$1"
    if [ "${DEVICE_LOCAL:-0}" = 1 ]; then
        device_local_run "$cmd" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
    else
        "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} shell "su -c $(sh_quote "$cmd")" </dev/null 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
    fi
}

# The manager that will take the zip. KernelSU and KSU Next ship ksud; APatch's
# apd takes the same `module install` arguments; Magisk uses --install-module.
# Asked in one root call so the su prompt happens once.
install_manager() {
    local have
    have="$(install_root 'for b in ksud magisk apd; do command -v $b >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "have:$b"; done')"
    case "$have" in
        *have:ksud*) printf 'ksud' ;;
        *have:apd*)  printf 'apd' ;;
        *have:magisk*) printf 'magisk' ;;
        *) printf '' ;;
    esac
}
```

```
- path: gui/app.go
  content: |
      package main
      
      import (
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io/fs"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "runtime"
        "sort"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "time"
      )
      
      const appTitle = "Treble RRO Creator"
      
      // Verb is one command build.sh understands, in the shape the UI draws it.
      type Verb struct {
        Name  string   `json:"name"`
        Label string   `json:"label"`
        Arg   string   `json:"arg"`
        Hint  string   `json:"hint"`
        Flags []string `json:"flags"`
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // The commands the app is allowed to run
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Each entry is one thing `build.sh` already does; the GUI only chooses which
      // one to run. Flags are per verb on purpose: `--all` means "also remove config
      // and device files" and is meaningless on a build, so the UI disables it and
      // the server rejects it. Keeping the table here (not only in the JS) means a
      // hand-written POST cannot widen what the app will execute.
      var verbTable = []Verb{
        {
          Name:  "build",
          Label: "Build",
          Arg:   "build",
          Hint:  "Compile and sign the module, and the submission zips",
          Flags: []string{"--with-vendor-hals", "--xiaomi-fod", "--allow-unknown-resources"},
        },
        {
          Name:  "dryrun",
          Label: "Dry run",
          Arg:   "--dry-run",
          Hint:  "Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing",
          Flags: nil,
        },
        {
          Name:  "check",
          Label: "Check",
          Arg:   "check",
          Hint:  "Validate config.env, build nothing",
          Flags: nil,
        },
        {
          Name:  "doctor",
          Label: "Doctor",
          Arg:   "doctor",
          Hint:  "Check the toolchain, install nothing",
          Flags: nil,
        },
        {
          Name:  "setup",
          Label: "Setup",
          Arg:   "setup",
          Hint:  "Install or repair the build tools",
          Flags: []string{"--force"},
        },
        {
          Name:  "clean",
          Label: "Clean",
          Arg:   "clean",
          Hint:  "Remove build output",
          Flags: []string{"--all"},
        },
      }
      
      func lookupVerb(name string) (Verb, bool) {
        for _, v := range verbTable {
          if v.Name == name {
            return v, true
          }
        }
        return Verb{}, false
      }
      
      // buildArgs turns a verb and its ticked flags into the argv for bash.
      //
      // -y is always appended: the child has no terminal, so anything that would
      // prompt has to take its default instead of blocking forever on stdin. That is
      // also why --with-vendor-hals becomes reachable at all — build.sh only honours
      // it together with --yes.
      func buildArgs(verb string, flags []string) ([]string, error) {
        v, ok := lookupVerb(verb)
        if !ok {
          return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown command %q", verb)
        }
        args := []string{"--noprofile", "--norc", "./build.sh", v.Arg}
        for _, f := range flags {
          if !contains(v.Flags, f) {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is not available with %s", f, v.Name)
          }
          args = append(args, f)
        }
        return append(args, "-y"), nil
      }
      
      func contains(list []string, want string) bool {
        for _, s := range list {
          if s == want {
            return true
          }
        }
        return false

      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Persisted state
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Settings is all the app remembers. It is deliberately two paths and nothing
      // else: config.env belongs to the clone, and the build reads it from there.
      type Settings struct {
        Clone string `json:"clone"`
        Bash  string `json:"bash"`
      }
      
      // App is the whole program state. root and bash can change at runtime from the
      // UI, so both are read through the mutex rather than captured at startup.
      //
      // runner is the Build console and adbRunner the Device one: separate logs, so an
      // adb command cannot appear in the build pane (or the other way round). They
      // share one Gate, so only one of them runs at a time.
      type App struct {
        mu        sync.RWMutex
        settings  Settings
        file      string
        root      string
        bash      string
        runner    *Runner
        adbRunner *Runner
      
        // The update check is cached separately: it can block on the network, and
        // nothing that answers /api/state may wait for a fetch.
        updMu   sync.Mutex
        upd     UpdateInfo
        updWhen time.Time
        updBusy bool
      
        // The native file chooser: pickMu keeps one dialog open at a time, and
        // picker answers it instead in a test (nil means the platform dialog).
        pickMu sync.Mutex
        picker func(pickAsk) (string, error)
      }
      
      func newApp(explicitClone string) (*App, error) {
        gate := NewGate()
        a := &App{
          runner:    NewRunner(gate),
          adbRunner: NewRunner(gate),
          file:      settingsFile(),
        }
        a.settings = loadSettings(a.file)
      
        a.root = chooseClone(explicitClone, a.settings.Clone)
      
        a.bash = a.settings.Bash
        if a.bash == "" || !fileExists(a.bash) {
          if b, err := findBash(); err == nil {
            a.bash = b
          }
        }
        // The first check happens while the window is still drawing.
        go a.watchUpdates()
        return a, nil
      }

      func randomToken() (string, error) {
        b := make([]byte, 16)
        if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
          return "", err
        }

      func (a *App) guard(method string, h http.HandlerFunc) http.HandlerFunc {
        return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
          if r.Method != method {
            w.Header().Set("Allow", method)
            http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
            return
          }
          if r.Header.Get("Sec-Fetch-Site") == "cross-site" {
            http.Error(w, "forbidden", http.StatusForbidden)
            return
          }
          h(w, r)
        }
      }
      
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      // Handlers
      // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      func (a *App) handleState(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, a.State())
      }
      
      // handleSettings remembers the clone and the bash binary. Nothing is run here:
      // a wrong path is stored and reported by /api/state so the field stays visible
      // and editable instead of being rejected on a typo.
      func (a *App) handleSettings(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Clone string `json:"clone"`
          Bash  string `json:"bash"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        if err := a.setPaths(body.Clone, body.Bash); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, a.State())
      }
      
      // handleConfig writes config.env exactly as typed. The file is the interface
      // build.sh reads, comments included, so it is saved verbatim rather than
      // round-tripped through a form.
      func (a *App) handleConfig(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Text string `json:"text"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "no clone selected")
          return
        }
        if len(body.Text) > 1<<20 {
          writeError(w, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, "config.env is limited to 1 MiB")
          return
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "config.env"), []byte(body.Text), 0o644); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"path": filepath.Join(root, "config.env")})
      }
      
      func (a *App) handleRun(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Verb  string   `json:"verb"`
          Flags []string `json:"flags"`
          // Sudo is the password the app collected after the installer said it
          // needed one. It lives in this request, a 0600 file for the duration of
          // the run, and the page's memory — never in a log or the clone.
          Sudo string `json:"sudo"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        args, err := buildArgs(body.Verb, body.Flags)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        // Only these two verbs install anything (see ensure_toolchain). A password
        // for check or clean would be carried for nothing.
        if body.Sudo != "" && body.Verb != "build" && body.Verb != "setup" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "that command does not install anything")
          return
        }
        extraEnv, cleanup, err := a.sudoEnv(body.Sudo)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        if err := a.runner.StartEnv(a.Root(), a.Bash(), args, "build.sh "+body.Verb, false, extraEnv, cleanup); err != nil {
          // start() already ran cleanup on its own failure paths.
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, a.runner.Snapshot())
      }
```

```
      let pendingRun = null;
      let sudoPassword = '';
      let sudoPromptOpen = false;
      let sudoDeclined = false;
      
      // config.env: the form keeps only what the user changed, so a poll that lands
      // mid-edit cannot repaint the row they are typing in.
      let cfgEdits = new Map();
      let cfgRaw = false;
      let cfgRawDirty = false;
      
      // --------------------------------------------------------------------- api --
      async function api(path, opts = {}) {
        const init = { method: opts.method || 'GET', cache: 'no-store' };
        if (opts.form !== undefined) {
          // Multipart upload: the browser owns the Content-Type boundary, so no
          // header is set here.
          init.body = opts.form;
        } else if (opts.body !== undefined) {
          init.headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' };
          init.body = JSON.stringify(opts.body);
        }
        const res = await fetch(path, init);
        const text = await res.text();
        let data = null;
        if (text) {
          try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch (_) { data = null; }
        }
        if (!res.ok) {
          const err = new Error((data && data.error) || text || res.statusText);
          // Some failures come with useful detail (the update clash list), so keep
          // the whole payload on the error instead of only the message.
          err.data = data;
          err.status = res.status;
          throw err;
        }
        return data;
      }
      
      function status(message, ms = 3500) {

      // the scan needs a path the unpacker can open — a 9 GB super.img is not going
      // to be uploaded to find out where it is. An empty answer is the user closing
      // the dialog, so the field keeps whatever was typed.
      async function choosePath(button, field, kind) {
        if (button.disabled) return;
        button.disabled = true;
        try {
          const res = await api('api/pick', { method: 'POST', body: { kind, start: $(field).value.trim() } });
          if (res && res.path) {
            $(field).value = res.path;
            $(field).focus();
          }
        } catch (err) {
          status(err.message, 6000);
        } finally {
          button.disabled = false;

      // ------------------------------------------------------------------ dialog --
      // A dialog grows out of the control that opened it and travels to the middle
      // of the window. Only the browser knows where it will land, so the start point
      // is measured after showModal: the button's centre, relative to the dialog's,
      // and a scale that fits the dialog inside that button. Without a button (a
      // dialog the app opens for itself) the plain centred fade in app.css is used.
      function openDialog(dlg, from) {
        // Focus moves into the dialog on showModal, so the trigger is read first.
        const trigger = from || document.activeElement;
        // Reopened while its exit was still playing: drop the exit and start over.
        if (dlg.classList.contains('is-closing')) {
          dlg.classList.remove('is-closing', 'from-control');
          dlg.close();
        }
        if (dlg.open) return; // showModal() throws on an open dialog; the fields still repaint
        dlg.classList.remove('from-control');
        dlg.showModal();
        const box = trigger && trigger.getBoundingClientRect ? trigger.getBoundingClientRect() : null;
        // A body-sized or empty rect means the dialog was not opened from a control.
        if (!box || !box.width || box.width > window.innerWidth * .8) return;
        const d = dlg.getBoundingClientRect();
        const dx = (box.left + box.width / 2) - (d.left + d.width / 2);
        const dy = (box.top + box.height / 2) - (d.top + d.height / 2);
        const s = Math.min(.8, Math.max(.35, (box.width + box.height) / (d.width + d.height)));
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-x', Math.round(dx) + 'px');
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-y', Math.round(dy) + 'px');
        dlg.style.setProperty('--from-s', s.toFixed(3));
        dlg.classList.add('from-control');
      }
      
      // Leaving: the same measured start point played backwards, so a dialog that
      // flew out of a button goes back into it. The dialog is still open while it
      // animates; closeDialog() calls the real close() once the card has left, which
      // is what the 'close' listeners that reset state wait for.
      const DIALOG_OUT_MS = 260;
      
      function closeDialog(dlg, value) {
        if (!dlg || !dlg.open || dlg.classList.contains('is-closing')) return;
      
        const finish = () => {
          dlg.removeEventListener('animationend', onEnd);
          dlg.classList.remove('is-closing', 'from-control');
          if (dlg.open) dlg.close(value);
        };
        const onEnd = (event) => {
          if (event.target === dlg) finish();
        };
      
        // With motion turned down there is nothing to wait for, and a window that is
        // not painting animations would otherwise leave the dialog stuck open.
        if (window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
          finish();
          return;
        }
        // Closed while it was still flying in: an exit would restart from the middle
        // and jump, so this one just goes.
        const arriving = dlg.getAnimations && dlg.getAnimations().some(
          (a) => a.playState === 'running' &&
            (a.animationName === 'dialog-fly' || a.animationName === 'dialog-in')
        );
        if (arriving) {
          finish();
          return;
        }
        dlg.classList.add('is-closing');
        dlg.addEventListener('animationend', onEnd);
        setTimeout(finish, DIALOG_OUT_MS + 160); // longer than the CSS animation, as a backstop
      }
```

```
      banner() {
          ui_title "$*"
          printf '\n'
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Prompts
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ask <question> <default>   -> answer in $REPLY
      #
      # `read` returns 1 at EOF (stdin redirected, CI, IDE task, no console). Under
      # `set -e` that used to kill the scripts silently right after a menu had been
      # printed. Falling back to a stated default keeps everything runnable
      # unattended, and pressing Enter also takes the default.
      ask() {
          local question="$1" default="${2:-}" answer=""
          printf '%s' "$question"
          if ! read -r answer; then
              echo ""
              info "No terminal input available — using '${default}'."
              answer="$default"
          fi
          [ -z "$answer" ] && answer="$default"
          REPLY="$answer"
      }
      
      # confirm <question> <y|n>   -> returns 0 for yes
      confirm() {
          local question="$1" default="${2:-n}" answer
          ask "$question" "$default"
          answer="$REPLY"
          case "$answer" in
              [Yy]|[Yy][Ee][Ss]) return 0 ;;
              *) return 1 ;;
          esac
      }
```

```
      ui_heading() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_rule [INDENT] — a plain separator.
      ui_rule() {
          local indent="${1:-2}" w; w=$(ui_cols)
          # One short of the window, like ui_heading: a rule that ends in the last
          # column wraps on a terminal that is exactly that wide.
          printf '%s%s%s%s\n' "$(ui_repeat "$indent" ' ')" "$UI_DIM" \
              "$(ui_repeat $((w - indent - 1)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_kv KEY VALUE [KEYWIDTH] — one aligned key and its value.
      # A value wider than the window (a property name, a path) moves under its key
      # and wraps there, instead of running off the edge of a phone.
      ui_kv() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="${3:-10}" pad cols line
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          printf -v pad '%*s' $((keyw - ${#key})) ''
          if [ $(( 3 + keyw + ${#value} )) -lt "$cols" ]; then
              printf '  %s%s%s  %s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$key$pad" "$UI_OFF" "$value"
              return 0
          fi
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$key" "$UI_OFF"
          ui_wrap "$value" 4 | while IFS= read -r line; do
              printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
          done
      }
      
      # ui_pad TEXT WIDTH — TEXT followed by spaces up to WIDTH characters.
      #
      # printf's %-*s pads by bytes, so one `·` (three bytes) would leave a row three
      # columns short and the right border would step in once per glyph. Everything a
      # user typed — a model name, a path, a dotted list — goes through here.
      ui_pad() {
          local text="$1" width="$2" pad=""
          [ "${#text}" -lt "$width" ] && printf -v pad '%*s' $((width - ${#text})) ''
          printf '%s%s' "$text" "$pad"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_line CONTENT INNER — CONTENT padded to INNER and closed off with the
      # right border. CONTENT carries its own leading space, so the row never starts
      # hard against the border.
      ui_panel_line() {
          local content="$1" inner="$2" pad=""
          [ "${#content}" -lt "$inner" ] && printf -v pad '%*s' $((inner - ${#content})) ''
          printf '  %s%s%s%s%s%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF" "$content" "$pad" \
              "$UI_DIM" "$UI_V" "$UI_OFF"
      }
      
      # ui_panel_row KEY VALUE KEYWIDTH INNER — one key/value row.
      # A value too long for the row is wrapped onto its own indented lines rather than
      # cut with an ellipsis: half a property name is worse than two lines.
      ui_panel_row() {
          local key="$1" value="$2" keyw="$3" inner="$4" keypad="" line avail
          local -a parts=()
          printf -v keypad '%*s' $((keyw - ${#key})) ''
          avail=$((inner - keyw - 3))

      #
      # Cutting a table in half is worse than folding it: below the width where the
      # natural columns collide, every row becomes its own two-line entry — the key in
      # bold and the rest joined with a dot — which is the same data, stacked, and
      # still comparable down the page.
      ui_table() {
          local header="$1"; shift
          local avail ncols=0 i k w total cell line first
          local -a rows=("$@") heads=() widths=()
          avail=$(( $(ui_cols) - 4 ))
          ui_split "$header" '|'
          heads=("${UI_SPLIT[@]}")
          ncols=${#heads[@]}
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do widths[$k]=${#heads[$k]}; done
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              for k in "${!UI_SPLIT[@]}"; do
                  [ "$k" -lt "$ncols" ] || continue
                  cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]}"
                  [ "${#cell}" -gt "${widths[$k]}" ] && widths[$k]=${#cell}
              done
          done
          total=$(( 2 * (ncols - 1) ))
          for w in "${widths[@]}"; do total=$(( total + w )); done
      
          if [ "$total" -gt "$avail" ]; then
              for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
                  ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
                  # A size or a zone on its own line means nothing without the column
                  # it came from, so the header word leads it: `Size 12K`.
                  printf '\n  %s%s%s %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "${heads[0]}" "$UI_OFF" \
                      "$UI_BOLD" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}" "$UI_OFF"
                  line=""
                  for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                      cell="${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                      [ -n "$cell" ] || continue
                      if [ -z "$line" ]; then line="$cell"; else line="$line $UI_DOT $cell"; fi
                  done
                  [ -n "$line" ] || continue
                  ui_wrap "$line" 4 | while IFS= read -r cell; do
                      printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$cell" "$UI_OFF"
                  done
              done
              return 0
          fi
      
          # Every column but the last is padded; the last one is printed as it is, so
          # a table does not leave a trail of spaces a terminal will happily select.
          printf '\n  %s' "$UI_BOLD"
          for k in "${!heads[@]}"; do
              if [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ]; then
                  printf '%-*s  ' "${widths[$k]}" "${heads[$k]}"
              else
                  printf '%s' "${heads[$k]}"
              fi
          done
          printf '%s\n' "$UI_OFF"
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat "$total" "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
          for i in "${!rows[@]}"; do
              ui_split "${rows[$i]}" '|'
              printf '  %s' "$UI_DIM"
              printf '%-*s' "${widths[0]}" "${UI_SPLIT[0]}"
              printf '%s  ' "$UI_OFF"
              for ((k = 1; k < ncols; k++)); do
                  if [ "$k" -lt $((ncols - 1)) ]; then
                      printf '%-*s  ' "${widths[$k]}" "${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                  else
                      printf '%s' "${UI_SPLIT[$k]:-}"
                  fi
              done
              printf '\n'
          done
      }
      
      # ui_title "TEXT" [SUBTITLE] — the first line of a report, ruled to the width.
      ui_title() {
          local w; w=$(ui_cols)
          printf '\n  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_BOLD" "$1" "$UI_OFF"
          if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
              ui_wrap "$2" 2 $((w - 2)) | while IFS= read -r line; do
                  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$line" "$UI_OFF"
              done
          fi
          printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$UI_DIM" "$(ui_repeat $((w - 3)) "$UI_H")" "$UI_OFF"
      }
```

```
# Where the zip lives on the phone. /sdcard/Download is the folder every manager
# app browses, and the one the manual instructions in the build summary use.
install_remote_path() {
    printf '/sdcard/Download/%s' "$(basename "$1")"
}

# adb push, but bounded: adb has no timeout and a wedged server would hang the
# script with nothing on screen.
install_push() {
    local local_zip="$1" remote="$2" dir status
    dir="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/install.$$")"
    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null
    "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} shell "mkdir -p /sdcard/Download" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    adb_device_exec 1200 "$dir/push" "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} push "$local_zip" "$remote"
    status=$?
    cat "$dir/push.err" >&2 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -rf "$dir"
    return "$status"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reboot, then wait for the phone to be up again
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Waiting on sys.boot_completed rather than on `adb wait-for-device`: the device
# node comes back long before the framework is ready, and the checks below read
# the overlay service, which only answers after boot_completed.
install_wait_boot() {
    local limit="${1:-240}" waited=0 state
    while [ "$waited" -lt "$limit" ]; do
        sleep 2
        waited=$((waited + 2))
        state="$("$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} shell getprop sys.boot_completed 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r\n')"
        if [ "$state" = 1 ]; then
            return 0
        fi
        if [ $((waited % 20)) -eq 0 ]; then
            info "still booting — ${waited}s of ${limit}s"
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Did it work?
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Three separate answers, because they fail independently: the module may be
# missing (wrong manager), present but disabled (manager's "enabled" switch), or
# present and enabled while the overlay itself did not attach (a bad resource,
# a mount system that did not mount it).
install_verify() {
    local fails=0 mod_dir disable_line overlay_line

    mod_dir="$(install_root "ls -d /data/adb/modules/${module_id} 2>/dev/null | head -n1")"
    if [ -n "$mod_dir" ]; then
        ok "module /data/adb/modules/${module_id} is present"
        disable_line="$(install_root "ls /data/adb/modules/${module_id}/disable 2>/dev/null")"
        if [ -n "$disable_line" ]; then
            warn "the module is disabled in the manager — enable it and reboot"
            fails=$((fails + 1))
        else
            ok "it is enabled (no disable or remove flag)"
        fi
    else
        err "no /data/adb/modules/${module_id} — the install did not land"
        info "Open your root manager and install out/$(basename "$1") by hand, or check that the manager is supported."
        fails=$((fails + 1))
    fi

    if [ -n "$overlay_pkg" ]; then
        overlay_line="$(device_sh "cmd overlay list | grep -F ${overlay_pkg} | head -n1")"
        case "$overlay_line" in
            \[x\]*)
                ok "overlay ${overlay_pkg} is registered and enabled"
                ;;
            \[*\]*)
                warn "overlay ${overlay_pkg} is registered but not enabled:"
                printf '      %s\n' "$overlay_line"
                info "Enable it: adb shell su -c 'cmd overlay enable ${overlay_pkg}'"
                fails=$((fails + 1))
                ;;
            *)
                err "overlay ${overlay_pkg} is not in the overlay list"
                info "The module is installed but did not mount. KernelSU/KSU Next needs Magic Mount (not OverlayFS) — see docs/how-it-works.md."
                fails=$((fails + 1))
                ;;
        esac
    fi

    if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
        ok "the overlay is live — reboot once more after changing values, then hard-reboot if a value sticks at the old one"
        return 0
    fi
    warn "${fails} check(s) did not pass — details above"
    return 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
install_main() {
    local zip local_zip remote manager confirm_reboot

    zip="$(install_find_zip)" || return 1
    [ -f "$zip" ] || return 1
    local_zip="$(cd "$(dirname "$zip")" && pwd)/$(basename "$zip")"

    step "Install the module"
    ui_kv "Module" "$(basename "$local_zip")" 10
    ui_kv "Device" "${module_id:-unknown}" 10
    printf '\n'

    # Termux, not adb: this phone is the machine, so nothing is pushed.
    if device_is_termux && [ -z "$want_serial" ] && ! adb_device_ready_now "${adb:-adb}" 2>/dev/null; then
        if ! device_local_begin "install-module.sh"; then
            die "root is needed to install a module on this phone"
            return 1
        fi
        manager="$(install_manager)"
        if [ -z "$manager" ]; then
            die "no ksud, apd or magisk on this phone — install the zip from your root manager's Modules screen"
            return 1
        fi
        # Root can read Termux's home, so the zip is installed where it sits.
        info "installing with ${manager} (no adb involved)"
        case "$manager" in
            magisk) install_root "magisk --install-module $(sh_quote "$local_zip")" ;;
            *)      install_root "${manager} module install $(sh_quote "$local_zip")" ;;
        esac
        ok "installed — reboot this phone, then open the WebUI or run ./build.sh doctor to check it"
        return 0
    fi

    resolve_adb || { die "adb was not found — install platform-tools (./build.sh doctor says where)"; return 1; }
    adb_pick_device "$adb" "$want_serial" "install-module.sh" || return 1
    # device_sh and install_root read the globals adb-device.sh uses.
    serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
    info "using ${serial}"

    remote="$(install_remote_path "$local_zip")"
    info "copying to ${remote}"
    if ! install_push "$local_zip" "$remote"; then
        die "the copy failed — is the phone still connected? (adb devices)"
        return 1
    fi

    manager="$(install_manager)"
    case "$manager" in
        ksud|apd)
            info "installing with ${manager}"
            if ! install_root "${manager} module install ${remote}" | sed 's/^/    /'; then
                die "${manager} refused the zip"
                return 1
            fi
            ;;
        magisk)
            info "installing with magisk"
            if ! install_root "magisk --install-module ${remote}" | sed 's/^/    /'; then
                die "magisk refused the zip"
                return 1
            fi
            ;;
        *)
            warn "no ksud, apd or magisk on the phone — the zip is at ${remote}"
            info "Open your root manager → Modules → Install from storage and pick it."
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
    ok "installed"

    if [ "$do_reboot" = 0 ]; then
        info "reboot when you are ready, then check: adb shell cmd overlay list | grep ${overlay_pkg}"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
        confirm "Reboot now and check the overlay when it comes back? [Y/n] " y || {
            info "not rebooting — reboot yourself, then verify with: adb shell cmd overlay list | grep ${overlay_pkg}"
            return 0
        }
    fi

    info "rebooting"
    "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} reboot >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    # The phone drops off adb for a few seconds; asking it to come back first
    # keeps the boot wait from reading an empty shell.
    "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} wait-for-device >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    if ! install_wait_boot 240; then
        die "the phone did not finish booting within 240s — plug it in and watch it, then check by hand"
        return 1
    fi
    ok "booted"

    [ "$do_verify" = 1 ] || return 0
    install_verify "$local_zip"
}
if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
    install_main
fi
```

```
---
tools_on_path() {
    case ":$PATH:" in
        *":$TOOLS_DIR:"*) ;;
        *) export PATH="$TOOLS_DIR:$PATH" ;;
    esac

    [ -d "$TOOLS_DIR" ] || return 0
    if ! $IS_WINDOWS; then
        local lib
        for lib in "$TOOLS_DIR"/android-sdk/build-tools/*/lib64; do
            [ -d "$lib" ] && [ -f "$lib/libc++.so" ] || continue
            export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
            break
        done
    fi
    return 0
}
```

```json
  "path": "stuff/scripts/wrap.sh",
  "instructions": "Create the script that packs existing overlay APKs into a flashable test module.",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# =============================================================================\n# wrap.sh — turn overlay APKs you already have into a flashable test module\n# =============================================================================\n# For an overlay that was built somewhere else — a repo zip, a friend's build,\n# an APK you signed by hand — this compiles nothing. It puts the APK(s) in the\n# module's system/product/overlay and zips them with the module files every\n# root manager expects. One APK (a framework overlay) or two (framework +\n# SystemUI) are both fine.\n#\n#   ./build.sh wrap --overlay path/to/overlay.apk\n#   ./build.sh wrap --overlay overlay.apk --systemui overlay-systemui.apk\n#   ./build.sh wrap --overlay overlay.apk --name my-test -y\n#\n#   Standalone: bash stuff/scripts/wrap.sh --overlay ... [the same options]\n#\n# Options\n#   --overlay PATH     the overlay APK (required)\n#   --systemui PATH    a second, SystemUI overlay APK (optional)\n#   --name ID          module id; default wrap-<apk file name>\n#   -y, --yes          no questions, do not offer to install\n#   -h, --help         this help\n#\n# Output: out/wrap/<module-id>.zip — its own folder, so a test module never\n# sits next to the release zips looking like one.\n# =============================================================================\n\nset -uo pipefail\n\nROOT=\"${ROOT:-$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/../..\" && pwd)}\"\n. \"$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh\"\n# aapt2 lives in stuff/tools/ on a machine that has built once; it is used here\n# only to read the APK's own package name, never to compile anything.\ntools_on_path\n\noverlay=\"\"\nsystemui=\"\"\nwant_name=\"\"\nassume_yes=\"${ASSUME_YES:-false}\"\n\nusage() { sed -n '3,25p' \"$0\" | sed 's/^# \\{0,1\\}//'; }\ndie() { err \"$1\"; return 1; }\n\nwhile [ $# -gt 0 ]; do\n    case \"$1\" in\n        --overlay|--apk|--framework) overlay=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --systemui|--system-ui)      systemui=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        --name|--id)                 want_name=\"${2:-}\"; shift 2 ;;\n        -y|--yes)                    assume_yes=true; shift ;;\n        -h|--help)                   usage; exit 0 ;;\n        -*)                          die \"unknown option: $1 (try --help)\"; exit 2 ;;\n        *)\n            # Positional: the first APK is the overlay, the second SystemUI.\n            if [ -z \"$overlay\" ]; then\n                overlay=\"$1\"\n            elif [ -z \"$systemui\" ]; then\n                systemui=\"$1\"\n            else\n                die \"more than two APKs given — use --overlay and --systemui\"; exit 2\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\n# A tty (the menu, or a person typing) gets asked for what was not typed.\nif [ -z \"$overlay\" ] && [ -t 0 ]; then\n    ask \"  Overlay APK to pack: \" \"\"\n    overlay=\"$REPLY\"\nfi\n[ -n \"$overlay\" ] || { die \"no APK given — ./build.sh wrap --overlay path/to/overlay.apk\"; exit 2; }\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Checks — an APK that cannot be an overlay fails here, not after flashing\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# An APK is a zip; two bytes are enough to catch a truncated download or a file\n# renamed to .apk. od instead of grep because this is binary.\nwrap_is_zip() {\n    [ \"$(head -c 2 \"$1\" 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \\n')\" = \"504b\" ]\n}\n\nwrap_check_apk() {\n    local p=\"$1\" label=\"$2\"\n    [ -f \"$p\" ] || { die \"$label: no such file: $p\"; return 1; }\n    [ -r \"$p\" ] || { die \"$label: cannot read: $p\"; return 1; }\n    [ -s \"$p\" ] || { die \"$label: the file is empty: $p\"; return 1; }\n    case \"$(printf '%s' \"$p\" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')\" in\n        *.apk) ;;\n        *) warn \"$label: $p does not end in .apk — packing it anyway\" ;;\n    esac\n    wrap_is_zip \"$p\" || { die \"$label: not a zip, so not an APK: $p\"; return 1; }\n    return 0\n}\n\n# The package name, and the package the APK overrides. Both are read from the\n# APK itself: it is what the summary prints and what the on-phone check greps\n# for, and a typo in a name typed by hand would send the user looking at the\n# wrong line of `cmd overlay list`.\nWRAP_PKG=\"\"\nWRAP_TARGET=\"\"\nWRAP_STATIC=\"\"\nwrap_meta() {\n    local apk=\"$1\" dump\n    WRAP_PKG=\"\"; WRAP_TARGET=\"\"; WRAP_STATIC=\"\"\n    command -v aapt2 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0\n    dump=\"$(aapt2 dump badging \"$apk\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n    WRAP_PKG=\"$(printf '%s\\n' \"$dump\" | sed -n \"s/^package: name='\\([^']*\\)'.*/\\1/p\" | head -n 1)\"\n    dump=\"$(aapt2 dump xmltree --file AndroidManifest.xml \"$apk\" 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n    WRAP_TARGET=\"$(printf '%s\\n' \"$dump\" | sed -n 's/.*:targetPackage([^)]*)=\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n 1)\"\n    if printf '%s\\n' \"$dump\" | grep -Eq ':isStatic\\([^)]*\\)=true'; then\n        WRAP_STATIC=true\n    fi\n    return 0\n}\n\nstep \"Checking the APKs\"\nwrap_check_apk \"$overlay\" \"overlay\" || exit 1\n[ -n \"$systemui\" ] && { wrap_check_apk \"$systemui\" \"SystemUI\" || exit 1; }\n\nfw_name=\"$(basename \"$overlay\")\"\nsu_name=\"\"\nif [ -n \"$systemui\" ]; then\n    su_name=\"$(basename \"$systemui\")\"\n    # Both APKs land in one folder; a shared name would silently pack one and\n    # drop the other.\n    if [ \"$su_name\" = \"$fw_name\" ]; then\n        die \"both APKs are named ${fw_name} — rename one of them\"; exit 1\n    fi\n    if [ \"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$overlay\")\" && pwd)/$fw_name\" = \"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$systemui\")\" && pwd)/$su_name\" ]; then\n        die \"the same file was given twice\"; exit 1\n    fi\nfi\n\nwrap_meta \"$overlay\"\nfw_pkg=\"$WRAP_PKG\"; fw_target=\"$WRAP_TARGET\"; fw_static=\"$WRAP_STATIC\"\nsu_pkg=\"\"; su_target=\"\"; su_static=\"\"\nif [ -n \"$systemui\" ]; then\n    wrap_meta \"$systemui\"\n    su_pkg=\"$WRAP_PKG\"; su_target=\"$WRAP_TARGET\"; su_static=\"$WRAP_STATIC\"\nfi\n\nok \"$(ui_kv_pairs \"$fw_name\" \"${fw_pkg:-package not readable}\")\"\n\nif [ -z \"$fw_pkg\" ] && [ -z \"$su_pkg\" ]; then\n    warn \"aapt2 is not installed, so the package names could not be read — the\"\n    warn \"module is still built, but the on-phone check cannot name the overlay.\"\n    info \"Read them yourself with: aapt2 dump badging \\\"$overlay\\\" | head -n1\"\nfi\nif [ -n \"$fw_pkg\" ] && [ -z \"$fw_target\" ]; then\n    warn \"${fw_pkg} has no <overlay> element in its manifest — it may not be an overlay at all\"\nfi\nif [ \"$fw_static\" != true ] && [ -n \"$fw_pkg\" ]; then\n    warn \"${fw_pkg} is not a static overlay — it is enabled by the module's service.sh, not by the framework\"\nfi\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Module id and output path\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nwrap_slug() {\n    printf '%s' \"$1\" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' \\\n        | sed 's/[^a-z0-9._-]/-/g; s/--*/-/g; s/^[._-]*//; s/[._-]*$//'\n}\n\nwrap_module_id() {\n    local base slug\n    if [ -n \"$want_name\" ]; then\n        # The three managers share this namespace: ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$\n        if printf '%s' \"$want_name\" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'; then\n            printf '%s' \"$want_name\"\n            return 0\n        fi\n        die \"--name must start with a letter; letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    base=\"$(basename \"$overlay\")\"\n    base=\"${base%.*}\"\n    slug=\"$(wrap_slug \"$base\")\"\n    [ -n \"$slug\" ] || slug=\"overlay\"\n    printf 'wrap-%s' \"$slug\"\n}\n\nmodule_id=\"$(wrap_module_id)\" || exit 1\nout_dir=\"$OUT_DIR/wrap\"\ndest=\"$out_dir/${module_id}.zip\"\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Author, from config.env when there is one\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nauthor=\"overlay test\"\nif [ -f \"$ROOT/config.env\" ]; then\n    # shellcheck disable=SC1090\n    . \"$ROOT/config.env\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    if [ -n \"${MODULE_AUTHOR:-}\" ] && [[ \"$MODULE_AUTHOR\" != *\"<\"* ]]; then\n        author=\"$MODULE_AUTHOR\"\n    fi\nfi\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Stage the module\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nstep \"Packing ${module_id}\"\nmkdir -p \"$BUILD_DIR\" \"$out_dir\"\ntmp=\"$(mktemp -d \"$BUILD_DIR/wrap.XXXXXX\" 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d)\"\nmod=\"$tmp/module\"\ncleanup_wrap() { rm -rf \"$tmp\"; }\ntrap cleanup_wrap EXIT INT TERM\n\nmkdir -p \"$mod/system/product/overlay\"\ncp \"$overlay\" \"$mod/system/product/overlay/$fw_name\" || { die \"could not copy $overlay\"; exit 1; }\nok \"framework overlay: $fw_name\"\nif [ -n \"$systemui\" ]; then\n    cp \"$systemui\" \"$mod/system/product/overlay/$su_name\" || { die \"could not copy $systemui\"; exit 1; }\n    ok \"SystemUI overlay:  $su_name\"\nfi\n\npkg_label=\"${fw_pkg:-$fw_name}\"\n[ -n \"$su_pkg\" ] && pkg_label=\"$pkg_label + $su_pkg\"\n\ncat > \"$mod/module.prop\" << PROP\nid=${module_id}\nname=Overlay test - ${pkg_label}\nversion=$(date +%Y.%m.%d)\nversionCode=$(date +%Y%m%d)\nauthor=${author}\ndescription=Packs overlay APKs you already have (${pkg_label}). Nothing was compiled: for testing only, not a submission.\nPROP\n\ncat > \"$mod/customize.sh\" << 'CUSTOMIZE_EOF'\n#!/sbin/sh\n# Test module: the APKs were packed as-is, so this only sets their permissions.\nMODPATH=${MODPATH:-${0%/*}}\nui_print \"  Installing overlay test module...\"\nset_perm_recursive $MODPATH/system/product/overlay 0 0 0755 0644 u:object_r:system_file:s0\nui_print \"  Installed. Reboot, then check: cmd overlay list | grep overlay\"\nCUSTOMIZE_EOF\nchmod 0755 \"$mod/customize.sh\"\n\n# A static overlay is already enabled by the time this runs, so the loop below\n# only reports. A non-static one is enabled here, which is the one case where a\n# test module has to do something at boot.\ncat > \"$mod/service.sh\" << SERVICE_EOF\n#!/sbin/sh\n# Reports whether the packed overlay(s) were accepted by the framework. This is\n# what tells \"the module is mounted\" from \"the framework refused the overlay\".\nPACKAGES=\"${fw_pkg} ${su_pkg}\"\nwhile [ \"\\$(getprop sys.boot_completed)\" != \"1\" ]; do\n    sleep 5\ndone\nfor pkg in \\$PACKAGES; do\n    [ -n \"\\$pkg\" ] || continue\n    cmd overlay enable \"\\$pkg\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    if cmd overlay list 2>/dev/null | grep -q \"\\[x\\] \\$pkg\"; then\n        log -t wrap-overlay \"enabled: \\$pkg\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    else\n        log -t wrap-overlay \"NOT enabled: \\$pkg (wrong target package or priority, or the mount system did not mount the module)\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    fi\ndone\nSERVICE_EOF\nchmod 0755 \"$mod/service.sh\""
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/install-module.sh
  content: |
      # present and enabled while the overlay itself did not attach (a bad resource,
      # a mount system that did not mount it).
      install_verify() {
          local fails=0 mod_dir disable_line overlay_line
      
          mod_dir="$(install_root "ls -d /data/adb/modules/${module_id} 2>/dev/null | head -n1")"
          if [ -n "$mod_dir" ]; then
              ok "module /data/adb/modules/${module_id} is present"
              disable_line="$(install_root "ls /data/adb/modules/${module_id}/disable 2>/dev/null")"
              if [ -n "$disable_line" ]; then
                  warn "the module is disabled in the manager — enable it and reboot"
                  fails=$((fails + 1))
              else
                  ok "it is enabled (no disable or remove flag)"
              fi
          else
              err "no /data/adb/modules/${module_id} — the install did not land"
              info "Open your root manager and install out/$(basename "$1") by hand, or check that the manager is supported."
              fails=$((fails + 1))
          fi
      
          if [ -n "$overlay_pkg" ]; then
              overlay_line="$(device_sh "cmd overlay list | grep -F ${overlay_pkg} | head -n1")"
              case "$overlay_line" in
                  \[x\]*)
                      ok "overlay ${overlay_pkg} is registered and enabled"
                      ;;
                  \[*\]*)
                      warn "overlay ${overlay_pkg} is registered but not enabled:"
                      printf '      %s\n' "$overlay_line"
                      info "Enable it: adb shell su -c 'cmd overlay enable ${overlay_pkg}'"
                      fails=$((fails + 1))
                      ;;
                  *)
                      err "overlay ${overlay_pkg} is not in the overlay list"
                      info "The module is installed but did not mount. KernelSU/KSU Next needs Magic Mount (not OverlayFS) — see docs/how-it-works.md."
                      fails=$((fails + 1))
                      ;;
              esac
          fi
      
          if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
              ok "the overlay is live — reboot once more after changing values, then hard-reboot if a value sticks at the old one"
              return 0
          fi
          warn "${fails} check(s) did not pass — details above"
          return 1
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Main
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      install_main() {
          local zip local_zip remote manager confirm_reboot
      
          zip="$(install_find_zip)" || return 1
          [ -f "$zip" ] || return 1
          local_zip="$(cd "$(dirname "$zip")" && pwd)/$(basename "$zip")"
      
          step "Install the module"
          ui_kv "Module" "$(basename "$local_zip")" 10
          ui_kv "Device" "${module_id:-unknown}" 10
          printf '\n'
      
          # Termux, not adb: this phone is the machine, so nothing is pushed.
          if device_is_termux && [ -z "$want_serial" ] && ! adb_device_ready_now "${adb:-adb}" 2>/dev/null; then
              if ! device_local_begin "install-module.sh"; then
                  die "root is needed to install a module on this phone"
                  return 1
              fi
              manager="$(install_manager)"
              if [ -z "$manager" ]; then
                  die "no ksud, apd or magisk on this phone — install the zip from your root manager's Modules screen"
                  return 1
              fi
              # Root can read Termux's home, so the zip is installed where it sits.
              info "installing with ${manager} (no adb involved)"
              case "$manager" in
                  magisk) install_root "magisk --install-module $(sh_quote "$local_zip")" ;;
                  *)      install_root "${manager} module install $(sh_quote "$local_zip")" ;;
              esac
              ok "installed — reboot this phone, then open the WebUI or run ./build.sh doctor to check it"
              return 0
          fi
      
          resolve_adb || { die "adb was not found — install platform-tools (./build.sh doctor says where)"; return 1; }
          adb_pick_device "$adb" "$want_serial" "install-module.sh" || return 1
          # device_sh and install_root read the globals adb-device.sh uses.
          serial="$DEVICE_SERIAL"
          info "using ${serial}"
      
          remote="$(install_remote_path "$local_zip")"
          info "copying to ${remote}"
          if ! install_push "$local_zip" "$remote"; then
              die "the copy failed — is the phone still connected? (adb devices)"
              return 1
          fi
      
          manager="$(install_manager)"
          case "$manager" in
              ksud|apd)
                  info "installing with ${manager}"
                  if ! install_root "${manager} module install ${remote}" | sed 's/^/    /'; then
                      die "${manager} refused the zip"
                      return 1
                  fi
                  ;;
              magisk)
                  info "installing with magisk"
                  if ! install_root "magisk --install-module ${remote}" | sed 's/^/    /'; then
                      die "magisk refused the zip"
                      return 1
                  fi
                  ;;
              *)
                  warn "no ksud, apd or magisk on the phone — the zip is at ${remote}"
                  info "Open your root manager → Modules → Install from storage and pick it."
                  return 1
                  ;;
          esac
          ok "installed"
      
          if [ "$do_reboot" = 0 ]; then
              info "reboot when you are ready, then check: adb shell cmd overlay list | grep ${overlay_pkg}"
              return 0
          fi
          if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
              confirm "Reboot now and check the overlay when it comes back? [Y/n] " y || {
                  info "not rebooting — reboot yourself, then verify with: adb shell cmd overlay list | grep ${overlay_pkg}"
                  return 0
              }
          fi
      
          info "rebooting"
          "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} reboot >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          # The phone drops off adb for a few seconds; asking it to come back first
          # keeps the boot wait from reading an empty shell.
          "$adb" ${serial:+-s "$serial"} wait-for-device >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          if ! install_wait_boot 240; then
              die "the phone did not finish booting within 240s — plug it in and watch it, then check by hand"
              return 1
          fi
          ok "booted"
      
          [ "$do_verify" = 1 ] || return 0
```

```
- path: stuff/scripts/wrap.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # =============================================================================
      # wrap.sh — turn overlay APKs you already have into a flashable test module
      # =============================================================================
      # For an overlay that was built somewhere else — a repo zip, a friend's build,
      # an APK you signed by hand — this compiles nothing. It puts the APK(s) in the
      # module's system/product/overlay and zips them with the module files every
      # root manager expects. One APK (a framework overlay) or two (framework +
      # SystemUI) are both fine.
      #
      #   ./build.sh wrap --overlay path/to/overlay.apk
      #   ./build.sh wrap --overlay overlay.apk --systemui overlay-systemui.apk
      #   ./build.sh wrap --overlay overlay.apk --name my-test -y
      #
      #   Standalone: bash stuff/scripts/wrap.sh --overlay ... [the same options]
      #
      # Options
      #   --overlay PATH     the overlay APK (required)
      #   --systemui PATH    a second, SystemUI overlay APK (optional)
      #   --name ID          module id; default wrap-<apk file name>
      #   -y, --yes          no questions, do not offer to install
      #   -h, --help         this help
      #
      # Output: out/wrap/<module-id>.zip — its own folder, so a test module never
      # sits next to the release zips looking like one.
      # =============================================================================
      
      set -uo pipefail
      
      ROOT="${ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      # aapt2 lives in stuff/tools/ on a machine that has built once; it is used here
      # only to read the APK's own package name, never to compile anything.
      tools_on_path
      
      overlay=""
      systemui=""
      want_name=""
      assume_yes="${ASSUME_YES:-false}"
      
      usage() { sed -n '3,25p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
      die() { err "$1"; return 1; }
      
      while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
          case "$1" in
              --overlay|--apk|--framework) overlay="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --systemui|--system-ui)      systemui="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              --name|--id)                 want_name="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
              -y|--yes)                    assume_yes=true; shift ;;
              -h|--help)                   usage; exit 0 ;;
              -*)                          die "unknown option: $1 (try --help)"; exit 2 ;;
              *)
                  # Positional: the first APK is the overlay, the second SystemUI.
                  if [ -z "$overlay" ]; then
                      overlay="$1"
                  elif [ -z "$systemui" ]; then
                      systemui="$1"
                  else
                      die "more than two APKs given — use --overlay and --systemui"; exit 2
                  fi
                  shift
                  ;;
          esac
      done
      
      # A tty (the menu, or a person typing) gets asked for what was not typed.
      if [ -z "$overlay" ] && [ -t 0 ]; then
          ask "  Overlay APK to pack: " ""
          overlay="$REPLY"
      fi
      [ -n "$overlay" ] || { die "no APK given — ./build.sh wrap --overlay path/to/overlay.apk"; exit 2; }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Checks — an APK that cannot be an overlay fails here, not after flashing
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # An APK is a zip; two bytes are enough to catch a truncated download or a file
      # renamed to .apk. od instead of grep because this is binary.
      wrap_is_zip() {
          [ "$(head -c 2 "$1" 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')" = "504b" ]
      }
      
      wrap_check_apk() {
          local p="$1" label="$2"
          [ -f "$p" ] || { die "$label: no such file: $p"; return 1; }
          [ -r "$p" ] || { die "$label: cannot read: $p"; return 1; }
          [ -s "$p" ] || { die "$label: the file is empty: $p"; return 1; }
          case "$(printf '%s' "$p" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
              *.apk) ;;
              *) warn "$label: $p does not end in .apk — packing it anyway" ;;
          esac
          wrap_is_zip "$p" || { die "$label: not a zip, so not an APK: $p"; return 1; }
          return 0
      }
      
      # The package name, and the package the APK overrides. Both are read from the
      # APK itself: it is what the summary prints and what the on-phone check greps
      # for, and a typo in a name typed by hand would send the user looking at the
      # wrong line of `cmd overlay list`.
      WRAP_PKG=""
      WRAP_TARGET=""
      WRAP_STATIC=""
      wrap_meta() {
          local apk="$1" dump
          WRAP_PKG=""; WRAP_TARGET=""; WRAP_STATIC=""
          command -v aapt2 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
          dump="$(aapt2 dump badging "$apk" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          WRAP_PKG="$(printf '%s\n' "$dump" | sed -n "s/^package: name='\([^']*\)'.*/\1/p" | head -n 1)"
          dump="$(aapt2 dump xmltree --file AndroidManifest.xml "$apk" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          WRAP_TARGET="$(printf '%s\n' "$dump" | sed -n 's/.*:targetPackage([^)]*)="\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n 1)"
          if printf '%s\n' "$dump" | grep -Eq ':isStatic\([^)]*\)=true'; then
              WRAP_STATIC=true
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      step "Checking the APKs"
      wrap_check_apk "$overlay" "overlay" || exit 1
      [ -n "$systemui" ] && { wrap_check_apk "$systemui" "SystemUI" || exit 1; }
      
      fw_name="$(basename "$overlay")"
      su_name=""
      if [ -n "$systemui" ]; then
          su_name="$(basename "$systemui")"
          # Both APKs land in one folder; a shared name would silently pack one and
          # drop the other.
          if [ "$su_name" = "$fw_name" ]; then
              die "both APKs are named ${fw_name} — rename one of them"; exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$(cd "$(dirname "$overlay")" && pwd)/$fw_name" = "$(cd "$(dirname "$systemui")" && pwd)/$su_name" ]; then
              die "the same file was given twice"; exit 1
          fi
      fi
      
      wrap_meta "$overlay"
      fw_pkg="$WRAP_PKG"; fw_target="$WRAP_TARGET"; fw_static="$WRAP_STATIC"
      su_pkg=""; su_target=""; su_static=""
      if [ -n "$systemui" ]; then
          wrap_meta "$systemui"
          su_pkg="$WRAP_PKG"; su_target="$WRAP_TARGET"; su_static="$WRAP_STATIC"
          ok "${su_name}: ${su_pkg:-package not readable}${su_target:+ → ${su_target}}"
      fi
      
      ok "${fw_name}: ${fw_pkg:-package not readable}${fw_target:+ → ${fw_target}}"
      
      if [ -z "$fw_pkg" ] && [ -z "$su_pkg" ]; then
          warn "aapt2 is not installed, so the package names could not be read — the"
          warn "module is still built, but the on-phone check cannot name the overlay."
          info "Read them yourself with: aapt2 dump badging \"$overlay\" | head -n1"
      fi
      if [ -n "$fw_pkg" ] && [ -z "$fw_target" ]; then
          warn "${fw_pkg} has no <overlay> element in its manifest — it may not be an overlay at all"
      fi
      if [ "$fw_static" != true ] && [ -n "$fw_pkg" ]; then
          warn "${fw_pkg} is not a static overlay — it is enabled by the module's service.sh, not by the framework"
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Module id and output path
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      wrap_slug() {
          printf '%s' "$1" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' \
              | sed 's/[^a-z0-9._-]/-/g; s/--*/-/g; s/^[._-]*//; s/[._-]*$//'
      }
      
      wrap_module_id() {
          local base slug
          if [ -n "$want_name" ]; then
              # The three managers share this namespace: ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$
              if printf '%s' "$want_name" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'; then
                  printf '%s' "$want_name"
                  return 0
              fi
              die "--name must start with a letter; letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only"
              return 1
          fi
          base="$(basename "$overlay")"
          base="${base%.*}"
          slug="$(wrap_slug "$base")"
          [ -n "$slug" ] || slug="overlay"
          printf 'wrap-%s' "$slug"
      }
      
      module_id="$(wrap_module_id)" || exit 1
      out_dir="$OUT_DIR/wrap"
      dest="$out_dir/${module_id}.zip"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Author, from config.env when there is one
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      author="overlay test"
      if [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
          # shellcheck disable=SC1090
          . "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ -n "${MODULE_AUTHOR:-}" ] && [[ "$MODULE_AUTHOR" != *"<"* ]]; then
              author="$MODULE_AUTHOR"
          fi
      fi
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Stage the module
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      step "Packing ${module_id}"
      mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR" "$out_dir"
      tmp="$(mktemp -d "$BUILD_DIR/wrap.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d)"
      mod="$tmp/module"
      cleanup_wrap() { rm -rf "$tmp"; }
      trap cleanup_wrap EXIT INT TERM
      
      mkdir -p "$mod/system/product/overlay"
      cp "$overlay" "$mod/system/product/overlay/$fw_name" || { die "could not copy $overlay"; exit 1; }
      ok "framework overlay: $fw_name"
      if [ -n "$systemui" ]; then
          cp "$systemui" "$mod/system/product/overlay/$su_name" || { die "could not copy $systemui"; exit 1; }
          ok "SystemUI overlay:  $su_name"
      fi
      
      pkg_label="${fw_pkg:-$fw_name}"
      [ -n "$su_pkg" ] && pkg_label="$pkg_label + $su_pkg"
      
      cat > "$mod/module.prop" << PROP
      id=${module_id}
      name=Overlay test - ${pkg_label}
      version=$(date +%Y.%m.%d)
      versionCode=$(date +%Y%m%d)
      author=${author}
      description=Packs overlay APKs you already have (${pkg_label}). Nothing was compiled: for testing only, not a submission.
      PROP
      
      cat > "$mod/customize.sh" << 'CUSTOMIZE_EOF'
      #!/sbin/sh
      # Test module: the APKs were packed as-is, so this only sets their permissions.
      MODPATH=${MODPATH:-${0%/*}}
      ui_print "  Installing overlay test module..."
      set_perm_recursive $MODPATH/system/product/overlay 0 0 0755 0644 u:object_r:system_file:s0
      ui_print "  Installed. Reboot, then check: cmd overlay list | grep overlay"
      CUSTOMIZE_EOF
      chmod 0755 "$mod/customize.sh"
      
      # A static overlay is already enabled by the time this runs, so the loop below
      # only reports. A non-static one is enabled here, which is the one case where a
      # test module has to do something at boot.
      cat > "$mod/service.sh" << SERVICE_EOF
      #!/sbin/sh
      # Reports whether the packed overlay(s) were accepted by the framework. This is
      # what tells "the module is mounted" from "the framework refused the overlay".
      PACKAGES="${fw_pkg} ${su_pkg}"
      while [ "\$(getprop sys.boot_completed)" != "1" ]; do
          sleep 5
      done
      for pkg in \$PACKAGES; do
          [ -n "\$pkg" ] || continue
          cmd overlay enable "\$pkg" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          if cmd overlay list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "\[x\] \$pkg"; then
              log -t wrap-overlay "enabled: \$pkg" 2>/dev/null || true
          else
              log -t wrap-overlay "NOT enabled: \$pkg (wrong target package or priority, or the mount system did not mount the module)" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
      done
      SERVICE_EOF
      chmod 0755 "$mod/service.sh"
      
      # Magisk's recovery installer bootstraps through META-INF; KernelSU, KSU Next
      # and APatch ignore it. Generated by the same function the real build uses, so a
      # test module and a release module install through identical code.
      . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/module.sh"
      generate_magisk_meta "$mod"
      
      create_zip "$mod" "$dest" || { die "could not write ${dest}"; exit 1; }
      zip_size="$(du -sh "$dest" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Summary
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rewrap_rel="out/wrap/$(basename "$dest")"
      ui_panel "Test module ready" \
          "Module|${module_id}" \
          "Overlay|${fw_pkg:-$fw_name}" \
          ${systemui:+"SystemUI|${su_pkg:-$su_name}"} \
          "Zip|${rewrap_rel} (${zip_size:-?})"
      
      echo ""
      info "Install it with your root manager, then reboot."
      info "Verify:  adb shell cmd overlay list | grep -F ${fw_pkg:-${fw_name%.apk}}"
      if [ -n "$fw_target" ]; then
          info "Lookup:  adb shell cmd overlay lookup ${fw_pkg} ${fw_target}:dimen/rounded_corner_radius"
      fi
      echo ""
      echo -e "  ${UI_DIM}This module is a wrapper, not a build: deleting it removes nothing else,"
      echo -e "  and rebuilding the device's real overlay does not replace it.${UI_OFF}"
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Offer to finish the job
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Same shape as a build: with a terminal, ask. -y and a piped run are left
      # alone, so nothing waits for an answer that will not come.
      if [ "$assume_yes" != true ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          if confirm "  Install it on the phone now? [y/N] " n; then
              # The module id and the packages are known here, so the install's own
              # verification checks this zip instead of whatever config.env describes.
              wrap_install_args=(--zip "$dest" --id "$module_id")
              [ -n "$fw_pkg" ] && wrap_install_args+=(--package "$fw_pkg")
              [ -n "$su_pkg" ] && wrap_install_args+=(--package "$su_pkg")
              bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/install-module.sh" "${wrap_install_args[@]}" \
                  || warn "the install did not finish — the zip is in out/wrap/"
          fi
      fi
      exit 0
```
