- path: build.sh
  content: |
      #
      #   -y, --yes                  no questions (also: --with-vendor-hals)
      #   -V, --version              print the version
      #   -h, --help                 this help
      #
      # On Windows use build.cmd (cmd, PowerShell or a double-click). It finds Git
      # Bash and passes the same arguments here. WSL is not supported on a Windows
      # drive — see docs/windows.md.
      # =============================================================================
      
      # pipefail matters here: most build steps run a tool and parse its output in a
      # pipeline (`aapt2 dump ... | sed | awk`). Without it a failed tool still exits
      # 0 through the pipeline and the build carries on with empty input.
      set -eo pipefail
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Project root
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
      # Launched from cmd.exe, PWD can be "C:/..." instead of "/c/..."; MSYS does
      # not recognise that form, so convert it before anything else uses it.
      if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ROOT=$(cygpath -u "$ROOT")
      fi
      export ROOT
      cd "$ROOT"
      
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/common.sh"
      source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/toolchain.sh"
      
      # Put stuff/tools/ on PATH (and its lib64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH on Linux).
      tools_on_path
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Options
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      MODE="build"
      REQUESTED=$#
      CHECK_MODE=false
      DRY_RUN=false
      ASSUME_YES=false
      FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=false
      CLEAN_ALL=false
      FORCE_RES=""
      ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=false
      
      usage() {
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Usage:${NC} ./build.sh [command] [options]"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Commands${NC}"
          echo "    (none)             The menu (on a terminal), otherwise a build"
          echo "    menu               The menu: build, config.env, addons, device probes"
          echo "    build              Build the overlay module (installs tools if needed)"
          echo "    profiles           Saved config.env setups: show, new, switch, rename, delete"
          echo "    setup              Install or repair the build tools"
          echo "    doctor             Check the toolchain, install nothing"
          echo "    check              Validate config.env, build nothing"
          echo "    install            Install out/<name>-ksu.zip on the phone, reboot, verify"
          echo "    fod-build          Rebuild the arm64 UDFPS helper from its Go source"
          echo "    clean              Remove build output"
          echo "    --dry-run          Print the resources config.env emits, build nothing"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Options${NC}"
          echo "    -y, --yes              Accept defaults, skip prompts"
          echo "    --with-vendor-hals     With --yes: include src/vendor/ in the module"
          echo "    --xiaomi-fod           Include the Xiaomi FOD helper (HBM + HIDL touch mode) in the module"
          echo "    --device SERIAL        With install: the phone to use, when more than one is attached"
          echo "    --zip PATH             With install: a module other than the newest build"
          echo "    --no-reboot            With install: hand it over, do not reboot or verify"
          echo "    --all                  With clean: also remove config and device files"
          echo "    --force                With setup: re-pick the resource dictionary"
          echo "    --allow-unknown-resources  Build even if a resource is missing from the target"
          echo "    --no-su                Termux: do not ask for root up front"
          echo "    -V, --version          Print the version"
          echo "    -h, --help             Show this help"
          echo ""
          echo -e "  ${BOLD}Windows:${NC} build.cmd [command] [options]"
          echo ""
      }
      
      # Options that only `install` understands are collected here and handed to
      # install-module.sh, so the entry point keeps one parser.
      INSTALL_EXTRA=()
      
      # Everything after `profiles` belongs to profiles.sh (switch p2, rename p2 "…").
      PROFILES_ARGS=()
      
      while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
          arg="$1"
          case "$arg" in
              build)          MODE="build" ;;
              menu|--menu)    MODE="menu" ;;
              setup|--setup)  MODE="setup" ;;
              doctor|--doctor) MODE="doctor" ;;
              check|--check)  MODE="check" ;;
              install)        MODE="install" ;;
              profiles)
                  MODE="profiles"
                  PROFILES_ARGS=("${@:2}")
                  break
                  ;;
              --device|--adb|--zip)
                  INSTALL_EXTRA+=("$arg" "${2:-}")
                  shift ;;
              --no-reboot|--no-verify)
                  INSTALL_EXTRA+=("$arg") ;;
              fod-build|--fod-build) MODE="fodbuild" ;;
              clean|--clean)  MODE="clean" ;;
              dry-run|--dry-run) MODE="dryrun" ;;
              -y|--yes)       ASSUME_YES=true ;;
              --with-vendor-hals) FORCE_VENDOR_HALS=true ;;
              --xiaomi-fod)   XIAOMI_FOD=true ;;
              --all)          CLEAN_ALL=true ;;
              --force)        FORCE_RES="force" ;;
              --allow-unknown-resources) ALLOW_UNKNOWN_RESOURCES=true ;;
              # Exported, so a menu that shells out for a build does not ask again.
              --no-su)        export TREBLE_NO_SU=1 ;;
              -V|--version)   echo "Treble RRO Creator ${TOOL_VERSION}"; exit 0 ;;
              -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
              *)
                  err "            Unknown option: ${arg}"
      
                  usage
                  exit 2
                  ;;
          esac
          shift
      done
      
      # No arguments and a terminal to talk on: the menu. Everything scripted passes
      # a verb, so nothing that relied on the old no-argument build needs to change.
      if [ "$REQUESTED" -eq 0 ] && [ "${TREBLE_MENU:-1}" != "0" ] && [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then
          MODE="menu"
      fi
      
      # --device, --zip and --no-reboot belong to install; taking them with another
      # verb and quietly ignoring them would look like they had been used.
      if [ "${#INSTALL_EXTRA[@]}" -gt 0 ] && [ "$MODE" != "install" ]; then
          err "            ${INSTALL_EXTRA[0]} only applies to 'install'"
          usage
          exit 2
      fi
      
      # A checkout on a Windows drive cannot be built from WSL (shared stuff/tools/).
      wsl_guard
      
      # Termux: the one root prompt of the session, asked before any screen is drawn.
      # -y means "unattended", and an unattended run must not stop for a tap.
      [ "$ASSUME_YES" = true ] || termux_root_handoff
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Dispatch
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      case "$MODE" in
          menu)
              # The terminal front end. It shells out to this same script for a build,
              # so a build started from the menu is the build a user would type.
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/menu.sh"
              menu_main
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          doctor)
              if run_doctor; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
              ;;
      
          setup)
              banner "Setup — build tools"
              migrate_layout
              # -y means "no questions": the desktop app has no terminal, so the
              # interactive menu would fall back to its default instead of using the
              # packages this machine already has. Auto is the installer a plain
              # build runs; it still asks for a sudo password when it needs one —
              # in a terminal sudo prompts, and the app has its own dialog for it.
              if $ASSUME_YES; then
                  ensure_toolchain auto "$FORCE_RES"
              else
                  ensure_toolchain interactive "$FORCE_RES"
              fi
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          check)
              # Config validation only: no tools, no output.
              CHECK_MODE=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          fodbuild)
              # Maintainers only: the shipped helper is prebuilt on purpose, so no
              # user path reaches Go for it.
              bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/fod-build.sh"
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          install)
              migrate_layout
              # A child, not a source: it parses its own options and can be run on its
              # own (bash stuff/scripts/install-module.sh --zip out/x-ksu.zip).
              bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/install-module.sh" ${INSTALL_EXTRA[@]+"${INSTALL_EXTRA[@]}"}
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          profiles)
              migrate_layout
              . "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/profiles.sh"
              profiles_cli ${PROFILES_ARGS[@]+"${PROFILES_ARGS[@]}"}
              exit $?
              ;;
      
          clean)
              migrate_layout
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/clean.sh"
              ;;
      
          dryrun)
              # Needs config.env and the resource generators, no toolchain: the point
              # is to see the plan in seconds.
              DRY_RUN=true
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      
          build)
              # Move any files left in the old top-level layout into src/.
              migrate_layout
              if $IS_WINDOWS; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Windows"
              elif $IS_TERMUX; then
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Termux"
              else
                  banner "Treble Overlay Builder — Linux"
              fi
              # Installs only what is missing; prints a summary and returns non-zero
              # when the machine still cannot build.
              ensure_toolchain auto
              # The installer may just have created stuff/tools/, so refresh PATH.
              tools_on_path
              source "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/build.sh"
              ;;
      esac

- path: stuff/scripts/menu.sh
  content: |
      menu_header() {
          cfg_counts
          ui_panel "Treble Overlay Creator ${TOOL_VERSION}" \
              "Device|$(cfg_identity)" \
              "config.env|${CFG_ON} set ${UI_DOT} ${CFG_OFF} off" \
              "Output|$(output_summary)"
      }
      
      # 11 is the width of the longest label here, so every description starts in the
      # same column instead of ragging after each label.
      MENU_LW=14
      
      menu_items() {
          ui_item 1 'Build'          'dry run, build, check, doctor, clean' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 2 'config.env'     'browse and edit one key at a time' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 3 'Addons'         'module tweaks: settings and overlay resources' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 4 'Device'         'read manufacturer, model, codename from the phone' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 5 'Auto Detect'    'ROM answers: cutout, corners, refresh rate, VoLTE, 5G' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 6 'UDFPS'          'in-display fingerprint geometry' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 7 'Match property' 'which property the submission should match on' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 8 'Files'          'what was built, and where it is' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item 9 'Docs'           'the guides in docs/' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item p 'Profiles'       'saved config.env setups: switch, rename, delete' "$MENU_LW"
          ui_item q 'Quit' '' "$MENU_LW"
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Build
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The menu never re-implements a build step: it runs the entry point with the
      # verb a user would type, so `build.sh doctor` and 1 → 4 are the same command.
      run_entry() {
          ( cd "$ROOT" && bash "$ROOT/build.sh" "$@" )
      }
      
      # Whether the Xiaomi FOD helper ships in the module. Off by default: it is only
      # useful on Xiaomi optical UDFPS phones, and on anything else it is a binary
      # that never starts. `./build.sh --xiaomi-fod menu` starts it already on.
      MENU_XIAOMI_FOD="${XIAOMI_FOD:-false}"
      
      # The --xiaomi-fod argument for a build started from here, or nothing at all.
      xiaomi_fod_arg() {
          [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ] && printf '%s' '--xiaomi-fod'
      }
      
      menu_build() {
          while :; do
              if [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ]; then
                  fod_state='on'
              else
                  fod_state='off'
              fi
              ui_heading 'Build'
              ui_item 1 'Dry run'     'print the resources config.env emits, build nothing' 11
              ui_item 2 'Build'       'build the module (installs tools if needed)' 11
              ui_item 3 'Check'       'validate config.env without building' 11
              ui_item 4 'Doctor'      'check the toolchain, install nothing' 11
              ui_item 5 'Clean'       'remove build output' 11
              ui_item 6 'Clean --all' 'start over for a different device' 11
              ui_item 7 'Xiaomi FOD' "$fod_state · HBM + touch-panel FOD mode for Xiaomi UDFPS" 11
              ui_item 8 'Install' "copy out/<name>-ksu.zip to the phone, install it, reboot, check" 11
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 11
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) run_entry --dry-run; pause_menu ;;
                  2)
                      # shellcheck disable=SC2046 # the flag is one word or none
                      run_entry build $(xiaomi_fod_arg)
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  3) run_entry check; pause_menu ;;
                  4) run_entry doctor; pause_menu ;;
                  5) run_entry clean; pause_menu ;;
                  6)
                      warn "This removes config.env and the device files too."
                      if confirm "  Start over for a different device? [y/N] " n; then
                          run_entry clean --all
                      fi
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  7)
                      if [ "$MENU_XIAOMI_FOD" = "true" ]; then
                          MENU_XIAOMI_FOD=false
                      else
                          MENU_XIAOMI_FOD=true
                          info "Next build ships fod/xiaomi-fod — use only if your phone is Xiaomi and has a UDFPS sensor."
                      fi
                      ;;
                  8)
                      # A child, so it can ask about the reboot and show the manager's
                      # own output without this screen having to parse it.
                      printf '\n'
                      bash "$ROOT/stuff/scripts/install-module.sh"
                      pause_menu
                      ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Files
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Where a copy lands on the phone. /sdcard is the same folder whether it is this
      # phone (Termux, where ~/storage/shared points at it) or a cabled one (adb), so
      # the path in the message is one a reader can go and look in either way.
      FILES_PHONE_DIR="/sdcard/treble-rro-creator"
      
      # The build's own outputs, one path per line: the flashable zips and the APKs
      # sitting inside them.
      built_files() {
          find "$OUT_DIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.apk' \) 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort
      }
      
      # files_copy_to_phone — put the build on the phone's shared storage.
      #
      # On the phone itself (Termux) that is a plain cp, once Termux has been given
      # access to /sdcard. From a computer it is `adb push`, because the build tree is
      # on the wrong side of the cable; the destination is the same folder, so the
      # instructions afterwards do not depend on which machine ran the build.
      files_copy_to_phone() {
          local -a files=()
          local f base="" dest copied=0 failed=0 src
          while IFS= read -r f; do files+=("$f"); done < <(built_files)
          if [ "${#files[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
              info "Nothing to copy yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
              return 0
          fi
      
          if device_is_termux; then
              # ~/storage/shared only exists after termux-setup-storage; /sdcard is
              # still worth trying because some builds of Termux ship it ready.
              if [ -d "$HOME/storage/shared" ]; then
                  base="$HOME/storage/shared"
              elif [ -d /sdcard ]; then
                  base="/sdcard"
              fi
              if [ -z "$base" ]; then
                  err "Termux cannot see this phone's storage."
                  echo "     Run: termux-setup-storage"
                  echo "     Then: 8 → 1 again"
                  return 1
              fi
              dest="$base/treble-rro-creator"
              if ! mkdir -p "$dest" 2>/dev/null; then
                  err "Cannot create $FILES_PHONE_DIR."
                  echo "     Run: termux-setup-storage   (it asks for the storage permission)"
                  return 1
              fi
              info "Copying ${#files[@]} file(s) to $FILES_PHONE_DIR..."
              for f in "${files[@]}"; do
                  if cp -f "$f" "$dest/" 2>/dev/null; then
                      ui_mark ok "$(basename "$f")  $(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"
                      copied=$((copied + 1))
                  else
                      ui_mark bad "$(basename "$f") — could not be written"
                      failed=$((failed + 1))
                  fi
              done
          else
              # A computer: the phone is only reachable through adb, and a build for a
              # phone that is not plugged in goes nowhere.
              if ! resolve_adb; then
                  err "adb was not found — install platform-tools and try again."
                  return 1
              fi
              adb_pick_device "$adb" "" "files" || return 1
              if ! "$adb" ${DEVICE_SERIAL:+-s "$DEVICE_SERIAL"} shell "mkdir -p $FILES_PHONE_DIR" \
                      >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  err "Could not create $FILES_PHONE_DIR on the phone."
                  echo "     Check that the phone is unlocked and the storage is not full."
                  return 1
              fi
              info "Pushing ${#files[@]} file(s) to $FILES_PHONE_DIR..."
              for f in "${files[@]}"; do
                  # A Windows adb cannot open an MSYS path, so the local half is
                  # converted when cygpath exists (Git Bash) and passed as it is
                  # everywhere else.
                  src="$f"
                  command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1 && src="$(cygpath -w "$f")"
                  if "$adb" ${DEVICE_SERIAL:+-s "$DEVICE_SERIAL"} push "$src" "$FILES_PHONE_DIR/" \
                          >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                      ui_mark ok "$(basename "$f")  $(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)"
                      copied=$((copied + 1))
                  else
                      ui_mark bad "$(basename "$f") — adb push failed"
                      failed=$((failed + 1))
                  fi
              done
          fi
      
          echo ""
          if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
              warn "$copied copied, $failed failed."
              return 1
          fi
          ui_mark ok "$copied file(s) in $FILES_PHONE_DIR"
          ui_mark note "Open Files on the phone, or flash the module from there."
          return 0
      }
      
      menu_files() {
          local -a table=() f
          while :; do
              ui_heading 'Files'
              ui_panel 'Where things are' \
                  "Project|$ROOT" \
                  "config.env|$ROOT/config.env" \
                  "Build tree|${BUILD_DIR#$ROOT/}"
              echo ""
              table=()
              if [ -d "$OUT_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$OUT_DIR" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
                  while IFS= read -r f; do
                      table+=("$(du -h "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)|${f#$ROOT/}")
                  done < <(built_files)
              fi
              if [ "${#table[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
                  info "Nothing built yet — 1 → 2 builds the module."
                  pause_menu
                  return 0
              fi
              ui_table 'Size|Built file' "${table[@]}"
              echo ""
              ui_item 1 'Copy' "to $FILES_PHONE_DIR on the phone" 11
              ui_item 0 'Back' '' 11
              menu_read "  >" || return 0
              case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
                  1) echo ""; files_copy_to_phone; pause_menu ;;
                  0|q|'') return 0 ;;
                  *) warn "Not one of the numbers above." ;;
              esac
          done
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Docs
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      menu_docs() {
          local files=() i
          ui_heading 'Docs'
          [ -d "$ROOT/docs" ] || { warn "docs/ is missing from this checkout."; pause_menu; return 0; }
          while IFS= read -r f; do
              files+=("$f")
          done < <(find "$ROOT/docs" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
          for i in "${!files[@]}"; do
              ui_item "$((i + 1))" "$(basename "${files[$i]}")"
          done
          echo ""
          menu_read "  number to read, Enter to go back >" || return 0
          case "$MENU_ANSWER" in
              ''|q) return 0 ;;
              *[!0-9]*) warn "Not a number."; return 0 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -lt 1 ] || [ "$MENU_ANSWER" -gt "${#files[@]}" ]; then
              warn "No such doc."
              return 0
          fi
          local pick="${files[$((MENU_ANSWER - 1))]}"
          echo ""
          if [ -t 1 ] && command -v less >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              less -R "$pick"
          else
              cat "$pick"
          fi
          return 0
      }
      
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # config.env
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # The file keeps its shape: these helpers rewrite one line and leave the
      # comments, the section headers and the quoting alone. A key that is commented
      # out shows as `off` and can be switched on by number, which is the whole point
      # of listing it — hunting for the '#' in a 240-line file is where mistakes
      # happen.
      cfg_each_row() { # <section> -> `key<TAB>active<TAB>value` rows of that section
          local section="$1"
          cfg_rows 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' -v s="$section" '$4 == s { print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $5 }'
      }
      
      cfg_section_stats() { # -> `section<TAB>set<TAB>off`, in file order
          cfg_rows 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '
              { if (!($4 in seen)) { seen[$4] = 1; order[n++] = $4 }
                if ($2 == 1) on[$4]++ ; else off[$4]++ }
              END { for (i = 0; i < n; i++) printf "%s\t%d\t%d\n", order[i], on[order[i]], off[order[i]] }
          '
      }
      
      # cfg_list_row NUM KEYW KEY ACTIVE VALUE — one line of a config.env section.
      #
      # A key has three things worth seeing at once: whether it is switched on, its
      # name, and its value. They are three aligned columns when the window has room
      # and two lines when it does not — the state keeps its colour either way, so
      # scanning down the page is still "find the green ones".
      cfg_list_row() {
          local num="$1" keyw="$2" key="$3" active="$4" value="$5"
          local cols state statepad color avail vw vcolor
          cols=$(ui_cols)
          if [ "$active" = "1" ]; then state='on'; color="$UI_GREEN"; else state='off'; color="$UI_DIM"; fi

        return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
          if r.Method != method {
            w.Header().Set("Allow", method)
            http.Error(w, "method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
            return
          }
          if r.Header.Get("Sec-Fetch-Site") == "cross-site" {

          h(w, r)

      // a wrong path is stored and reported by /api/state so the field stays visible

      func (a *App) handleSettings(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Clone string `json:"clone"`
          Bash  string `json:"bash"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        if err := a.setPaths(body.Clone, body.Bash); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, a.State())

      // handleConfig writes config.env exactly as typed. The file is the interface
      // build.sh reads, comments included, so it is saved verbatim rather than
      // round-tripped through a form.
      func (a *App) handleConfig(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Text string `json:"text"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        root := a.Root()
        if !isClone(root) {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "no clone selected")
          return
        }
        if len(body.Text) > 1<<20 {
          writeError(w, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, "config.env is limited to 1 MiB")
          return
        }
        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "config.env"), []byte(body.Text), 0o644); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"path": filepath.Join(root, "config.env")})
      }

      func (a *App) handleRun(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Verb  string   `json:"verb"`
          Flags []string `json:"flags"`
          // Sudo is the password the app collected after the installer said it
          // needed one. It lives in this request, a 0600 file for the duration of
          // the run, and the page's memory — never in a log or the clone.
          Sudo string `json:"sudo"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        args, err := buildArgs(body.Verb, body.Flags)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        // Only these two verbs install anything (see ensure_toolchain). A password
        // for check or clean would be carried for nothing.
        if body.Sudo != "" && body.Verb != "build" && body.Verb != "setup" {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "that command does not install anything")
          return
        }
        extraEnv, cleanup, err := a.sudoEnv(body.Sudo)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        if err := a.runner.StartEnv(a.Root(), a.Bash(), args, "build.sh "+body.Verb, false, extraEnv, cleanup); err != nil {
          // start() already ran cleanup on its own failure paths.
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, a.runner.Snapshot())
      }
      
      // sudoEnv turns a password from the dialog into what `sudo -A` needs.
      //
      // The password goes into a 0600 file rather than the child's environment: an
      // environment entry is inherited by everything the build starts, while the file
      // can be removed the moment the run ends (Runner.finish does exactly that).
      func (a *App) sudoEnv(password string) ([]string, func(), error) {
        if password == "" {
          return nil, nil, nil
        }
        helper := filepath.Join(a.Root(), "stuff", "scripts", "sudo-askpass.sh")
        st, err := os.Stat(helper)
        if err != nil {
          return nil, nil, errors.New("the sudo helper is missing — update the clone (git pull) and try again")
        }
        // Windows has no executable bit: every file would fail this check there,
        // and the helper is never run on Windows anyway (no sudo to ask).
        if runtime.GOOS != "windows" && st.Mode()&0o111 == 0 {
          return nil, nil, errors.New("the sudo helper is not executable — update the clone (git pull) and try again")
        }
        dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "rro-sudo-")
        if err != nil {
          return nil, nil, err
        }
        path := filepath.Join(dir, "password")
        if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(password+"\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
          os.RemoveAll(dir)
          return nil, nil, err
        }
        cleanup := func() { os.RemoveAll(dir) }
        return []string{"SUDO_ASKPASS=" + helper, "RRO_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE=" + path}, cleanup, nil
      }
      
      // handleCancel stops whatever is running. There is one Stop button per console
      // but only one job at a time (see Gate), so asking both runners is the same as
      // asking the one that has something to stop.
      func (a *App) handleCancel(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        if err := a.runner.Cancel(); err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
          return
        }
        if a.adbRunner != nil {
          if err := a.adbRunner.Cancel(); err != nil {
            writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
            return
          }
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, a.runner.Snapshot())
      }
      
      // handleLog is the Build console: a server-sent event stream, one JSON LogLine
      // per event, replayed from the buffer first so a reload does not lose the run
      // in progress.
      func (a *App) handleLog(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        a.streamLog(w, r, a.runner)
      }
      
      // handleAdbLog is the same stream for the Device console. It is a separate
      // buffer on a separate Runner, so an adb command no longer appears in the build
      // log and a build no longer wipes the device console.
      func (a *App) handleAdbLog(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        if a.adbRunner == nil {
          http.Error(w, "no device console", http.StatusInternalServerError)
          return
        }
        a.streamLog(w, r, a.adbRunner)
      }
      
      func (a *App) streamLog(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, run *Runner) {
        flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
        if !ok {
          http.Error(w, "streaming unsupported", http.StatusInternalServerError)
          return
        }
        w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")

      func lookupVerb(name string) (Verb, bool) {
        for _, v := range verbTable {
          if v.Name == name {
            return v, true
          }
        }
        return Verb{}, false
      }
      
      // buildArgs turns a verb and its ticked flags into the argv for bash.
      //
      // -y is always appended: the child has no terminal, so anything that would
      // prompt has to take its default instead of blocking forever on stdin. That is
      // also why --with-vendor-hals becomes reachable at all — build.sh only honours
      // it together with --yes.
      func buildArgs(verb string, flags []string) ([]string, error) {
        v, ok := lookupVerb(verb)
        if !ok {
          return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown command %q", verb)
        }
        args := []string{"--noprofile", "--norc", "./build.sh", v.Arg}
        for _, f := range flags {
          if !contains(v.Flags, f) {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is not available with %s", f, v.Name)
          }
          args = append(args, f)
        }
        return append(args, "-y"), nil
      }
      
      func contains(list []string, want string) bool {
        for _, s := range list {
          if s == want {
            return true
          }
        }
        return false
      }

      type Settings struct {
        Clone string `json:"clone"`
        Bash  string `json:"bash"`
      }
      
      // App is the whole program state. root and bash can change at runtime from the
      // UI, so both are read through the mutex rather than captured at startup.
      //
      // runner is the Build console and adbRunner the Device one: separate logs, so an
      // adb command cannot appear in the build pane (or the other way round). They
      // share one Gate, so only one of them runs at a time.
      type App struct {
        mu        sync.RWMutex
        settings  Settings
        file      string
        root      string

        runner    *Runner
        adbRunner *Runner

        pickMu sync.Mutex

  content: |
      package main
      
      // The file chooser behind the path fields.
      //
      // The page cannot offer one itself: a webview's <input type="file"> hands the
      // page a File object, never a path, and the firmware scans need a path the
      // unpacker can open. Uploading a 9 GB super.img just to learn where it is would
      // be absurd, so the dialog is the system's own and the app opens it:
      // PowerShell's WinForms dialogs on Windows, zenity or kdialog on Linux.
      //
      // Nothing here reads or writes the chosen file. The endpoint returns a string,
      // which is exactly what a user could type into the same field, so it adds no
      // power to the page — only a way to answer the question without a path.
      
      import (
        "net/http"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "strings"
      )
      
      // pickerKind is what the dialog is after. A file and a folder need different
      // dialogs on every platform, so the page says which one it wants.
      type pickerKind string
      
      const (
        pickFile   pickerKind = "file"
        pickFolder pickerKind = "folder"
      )
      
      // pickAsk is everything a dialog needs: which kind, and the folder to open at.
      // Start is a directory even when the field holds a file — see startDir.
      type pickAsk struct {
        Kind  pickerKind
        Start string
      }
      
      func (k pickerKind) title() string {
        if k == pickFolder {
          return "Choose the ROM folder or an unpacked tree"
        }
        return "Choose a super.img, a Samsung AP file, or a partition image"
      }
      
      // startDir turns what is already in the field into a folder a dialog can open
      // at: a folder is itself, a file is its parent, and anything that is not there
      // is dropped so the dialog falls back to its own default.
      func startDir(field string) string {
        field = strings.TrimSpace(field)
        if field == "" {
          return ""
        }
        if st, err := os.Stat(field); err == nil && st.IsDir() {
          return field
        }
        dir := filepath.Dir(field)
        if dir == "." || dir == string(filepath.Separator) {
          return ""
        }
        if st, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil && st.IsDir() {
          return dir
        }
        return ""
      }
      
      // handlePick opens the platform's chooser and answers with the path it
      // returned. An empty path is a cancellation, not a failure: the page leaves the
      // field as it was.
      func (a *App) handlePick(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var body struct {
          Kind  string `json:"kind"`
          Start string `json:"start"`
        }
        if !decode(w, r, &body) {
          return
        }
        kind := pickerKind(strings.TrimSpace(body.Kind))
        if kind != pickFile && kind != pickFolder {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, `kind has to be "file" or "folder"`)
          return
        }
        if len(body.Start) > 4096 {
          writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "that path is too long to be one")
          return
        }
        ask := pickAsk{Kind: kind, Start: startDir(body.Start)}
      
        // One dialog at a time: the request blocks until the user answers, and a
        // second click while the first is open would stack a second modal window on
        // top of it.
        a.pickMu.Lock()
        defer a.pickMu.Unlock()
        path, err := a.chosenPath(ask)
        if err != nil {
          writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
          return
        }
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"path": path})
      }
      
      // chosenPath is the dialog, unless a test has replaced it. Going through a
      // method keeps the handler testable without a window and without a global.
      func (a *App) chosenPath(ask pickAsk) (string, error) {
        if a.picker != nil {
          return a.picker(ask)
        }
        return pickPath(ask)
      }

  content: |
      //go:build windows
      
      package main
      
      // The Windows file chooser.
      //
      // It is PowerShell plus WinForms rather than a COM binding in Go: IFileOpenDialog
      // is a hundred lines of vtable work that needs an STA thread and a window owner,
      // and it is the same dialog PowerShell opens here. The cost is a process start
      // (a few hundred milliseconds) on a click that ends in a modal window anyway.
      //
      // The answer travels through a temp file, not stdout: a path can hold any
      // Unicode character, and a redirected PowerShell console would re-encode it
      // through an OEM code page. Nothing is written when the user cancels, so the
      // file existing is the answer.
      
      import (
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "strings"
        "syscall"
      )
      
      // pickScript is the dialog. The inputs arrive as environment variables, so a
      // title or a folder name with quotes in it cannot break the script.
      const pickScript = `
      $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
      Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
      [System.Windows.Forms.Application]::EnableVisualStyles()
      if ($env:RRO_PICK_KIND -eq 'folder') {
          $d = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.FolderBrowserDialog
          $d.Description = $env:RRO_PICK_TITLE
          $d.ShowNewFolderButton = $true
          if ($env:RRO_PICK_START) {
              try { $d.SelectedPath = $env:RRO_PICK_START } catch { }
          }
          $ok = $d.ShowDialog() -eq [System.Windows.Forms.DialogResult]::OK
          $value = $d.SelectedPath
      } else {
          $d = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.OpenFileDialog
          $d.Title = $env:RRO_PICK_TITLE
          $d.Filter = 'Firmware images (*.img;*.bin;*.tar;*.md5;*.lz4)|*.img;*.bin;*.tar;*.md5;*.lz4|All files (*.*)|*.*'
          $d.CheckFileExists = $true
          $d.CheckPathExists = $true
          $d.Multiselect = $false
          if ($env:RRO_PICK_START) {
              try { $d.InitialDirectory = $env:RRO_PICK_START } catch { }
          }
          $ok = $d.ShowDialog() -eq [System.Windows.Forms.DialogResult]::OK
          $value = $d.FileName
      }
      if ($ok -and $value) {
          [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($env:RRO_PICK_OUT, $value, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))
      }
      `
      
      func pickPath(ask pickAsk) (string, error) {
        ps, err := powershellPath()
        if err != nil {
          return "", err
        }
      
        // A file the script has not written yet: CreateTemp gets a unique name, and
        // removing it makes "exists" mean "the user chose something".
        f, err := os.CreateTemp("", "treble-rro-pick-*.txt")
        if err != nil {
          return "", err
        }
        out := f.Name()
        f.Close()
        if err := os.Remove(out); err != nil {
          return "", err
        }
        defer os.Remove(out)
      
        cmd := exec.Command(ps, "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-STA",
          "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-Command", pickScript)
        cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
          "RRO_PICK_KIND="+string(ask.Kind),
          "RRO_PICK_TITLE="+ask.Kind.title(),
          "RRO_PICK_START="+ask.Start,
          "RRO_PICK_OUT="+out,
        )
        // The dialog is its own window; the PowerShell console behind it must not
        // flash on screen.
        cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{HideWindow: true}
        if msg, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
          detail := strings.TrimSpace(string(msg))
          if detail == "" {
            detail = err.Error()
          }
          return "", fmt.Errorf("the file chooser did not open: %s", detail)
        }
      
        raw, err := os.ReadFile(out)
        if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
          return "", nil // closed the dialog
        }
        if err != nil {
          return "", err
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(string(raw), "\ufeff")), nil
      }
      
      // powershellPath finds Windows PowerShell, and then PowerShell 7 for a machine
      // where the built-in one was removed.
      func powershellPath() (string, error) {
        if p, err := exec.LookPath("powershell.exe"); err == nil {
          return p, nil
        }
        if p, err := exec.LookPath("pwsh.exe"); err == nil {
          return p, nil
        }
        if root := os.Getenv("SystemRoot"); root != "" {
          p := filepath.Join(root, "System32", "WindowsPowerShell", "v1.0", "powershell.exe")
          if fileExists(p) {
            return p, nil
          }
        }
        return "", errors.New("Windows PowerShell was not found, so the file chooser cannot open — type the path instead")
      }
      
- path: gui/pick_unix.go
  content: |
      //go:build !windows
      
      package main
      
      // The Linux file chooser.
      //
      // There is no dialog in a bare X session: the desktop's own helper is the only
      // thing that draws one, so zenity is used when it is installed and kdialog for
      // a KDE box. Termux and a headless shell have neither, and the error says so —
      // the path field still takes a typed path.
      
      import (
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "strings"
      )
      
      func pickPath(ask pickAsk) (string, error) {
        if z, err := exec.LookPath("zenity"); err == nil {
          return runChooser(z, zenityArgs(ask)...)
        }
        if k, err := exec.LookPath("kdialog"); err == nil {
          return runChooser(k, kdialogArgs(ask)...)
        }
        return "", errors.New("no file chooser was found (install zenity or kdialog), or type the path instead")
      }
      
      func zenityArgs(ask pickAsk) []string {
        args := []string{"--file-selection", "--title=" + ask.Kind.title()}
        if ask.Kind == pickFolder {
          args = append(args, "--directory")
        } else {
          args = append(args,
            "--file-filter=Firmware images | *.img *.bin *.tar *.md5 *.lz4",
            "--file-filter=All files | *")
        }
        // The trailing separator opens the dialog at that folder instead of
        // selecting the folder itself as the answer.
        if ask.Start != "" {
          args = append(args, "--filename="+strings.TrimRight(ask.Start, string(os.PathSeparator))+string(os.PathSeparator))
        }
        return args
      }
      
      func kdialogArgs(ask pickAsk) []string {
        args := []string{"--title", ask.Kind.title()}
        if ask.Kind == pickFolder {
          args = append(args, "--getexistingdirectory", ask.Start)
          return args
        }
        filter := "Firmware images (*.img *.bin *.tar *.md5 *.lz4)|*.img *.bin *.tar *.md5 *.lz4\\nAll files|*"
        args = append(args, "--getopenfilename", ask.Start, filter)
        return args
      }
      
      // runChooser starts one desktop helper and reads the answer it prints. Both
      // zenity and kdialog use exit status 1 for "the user closed the dialog", which
      // is a cancellation rather than a failure.
      func runChooser(bin string, args ...string) (string, error) {
        out, err := exec.Command(bin, args...).CombinedOutput()
        if err != nil {
          var exit *exec.ExitError
          if errors.As(err, &exit) && exit.ExitCode() == 1 {
            return "", nil
          }
          detail := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
          if detail == "" {
            detail = err.Error()
          }
          return "", fmt.Errorf("the file chooser did not open: %s", detail)
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), nil
      }

        <section class="pane" id="pane-addons" role="tabpanel">

            module writes on the phone at every boot — the overlay APK alone does
            not apply them, and the module's page on the phone can change them later.
            <b>Overlay</b> addons are baked into the APK, so from here they take
            effect at the next build and flash — the phone's WebUI can write the same
            entries into the installed APK without a rebuild. Only what is listed in
            <code>src/module/addons.conf</code> is enforced, so an addon you leave

- path: gui/ui/app.js
  content: |
      // current either way, and a finished build opens it once.
      function renderOut() {
        const box = $('out');
        const summary = $('out-summary');
        box.textContent = '';
      
        const files = state.out || [];
        if (files.length === 0) {
          summary.textContent = state.cloneValid ? 'nothing in out/ yet' : 'no clone selected';
          box.appendChild(el('span', 'muted', summary.textContent));
          return;
        }
      
        let newest = 0;
        let biggest = 0;
        for (const f of files) {
          if (f.mod > newest) newest = f.mod;
          if (f.size > biggest) biggest = f.size;
        }
        const when = ago(newest);

> _Reasoning_
> The log stream is global (connectLog once), and log is rendered into #log in the Build pane. If a wrap run starts from another tab, the user wouldn't see it. Options:
> 1. Put wrap UI in the Build pane (below verbs) — then log is right there. But Build pane gets crowded.
> 2. Put it in its own tab and after clicking "Create module" switch to Build tab automatically (`switchTab('build')`), then the log is visible. That is clean and clear.
